declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_algebraicSpace_over_baseChange
declarations.doc:
The algebraic space representing the 2-fibre product of a 1-morphism representable by
algebraic spaces with a scheme-valued point `y` of its target, viewed over the original base,
comes with its canonical morphism to `U`. The representing equivalence is over the big fppf
category of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebraicSpace_over_baseChange
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj)
    (hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = Over.map U.hom) :
    ∃ (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F)
      (Fy : SpacesOverSmallerBase B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom),
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p y
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
        (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) ∧
      Fy = (spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩ ∧
      ∃ (ι : Fy.1.left ≅ (OverShriek.relocalizePresheafFunctor U.hom).obj F),
        ∀ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (s : Fy.1.left.obj (op W)),
          (Fy.1.hom.app (op W) s).left = (ι.hom.app (op W) s).1.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0402.** The algebraic space `F_y` over `U` representing the 2-fibre product
`(Sch/U)_fppf ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳` of a 1-morphism `f` representable by algebraic spaces along a point
`y` of its target over `U`.

This is a choice of representative; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def baseChangeSpace : AlgebraicSpaces B U.left.1 U.left.2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_equivalenceOver_baseChangeSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0402, the squiggly arrow.** The category of elements of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeSpace` is equivalent, over the big fppf site of `U`, to the
first projection of the 2-fibre product `(Sch/U)_fppf ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_equivalenceOver_baseChangeSpace :
    Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.p 𝒴.p y f.toFunctor)
      (presheafOfCategories ((baseChangeSpace B S hS f hf U y hy).1 ⋙ typeToCat)).p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeStructureMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0402.** The structure morphism `f_y : F_y ⟶ U` of the display, as a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` from `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeSpace` to the representable
algebraic space of `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev baseChangeStructureMap :
    (⟨(baseChangeSpaceOverBase B S hS f hf U y hy).1.left,
      (baseChangeSpaceOverBase B S hS f hf U y hy).property⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
      (schemeSpace (Over.mk U.hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)

declarations.name: isOpenMap_comap_satisfiesGoingDown
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 0407 (Lemma 10.41.2): if the induced map on prime spectra
`φ* = PrimeSpectrum.comap φ : Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is an open map, then `φ`
satisfies going down.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenMap_comap_satisfiesGoingDown
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (h : IsOpenMap (comap φ)) : φ.SatisfiesGoingDown

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CS**, equivalently **Tag 0409 (2)**. A sheaf of `O`-modules is
*invertible* when its tensor functor is an equivalence. The universal property specifies that
tensor functor independently of any chosen construction of sheafification, hence on every
site; so the ringed-space form of the definition and the ringed-site form coincide here.
declarations.statement:
class IsInvertible
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isInvertible_iff_tensorRightFunctor_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0409 (2)**, equivalently **Tag 01CS**, in the source's own form: a
sheaf of `O`-modules `L` is invertible exactly when the functor `F ↦ (F ⊗_O L)^#` of the
source is an equivalence. The invertibility predicate is phrased through the universal
property of tensoring on the *left*, so this is the criterion the source states and the
predicate agreeing, the two tensor functors being identified by `tensorLeftIsoTensorRight`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_tensorRightFunctor_isEquivalence
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)) :
    IsInvertible O hO L ↔ ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) hO⟩).flip.obj
        L).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules on a ringed site is finite locally free of rank `r` if it is, over a
covering family of every object, a coproduct of `r` copies of the structure sheaf. This is the
rank clause of Stacks 0409.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    (F : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) (r : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.unitsSheaf
declarations.doc: The sheaf of units `O_X^*` of the structure sheaf of a ringed site.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def unitsSheaf (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w}) : Sheaf X.J CommGrpCat.{w}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.unitsSheafι_mono
declarations.doc: The canonical inclusion of the units sheaf into the structure sheaf is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement: instance unitsSheafι_mono (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w}) : Mono (unitsSheafι X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_unitsSheaf_iff_exists_mul_eq_one
declarations.doc:
A section belongs to the units subsheaf exactly when it has a right inverse: the units
subsheaf is `U ↦ {f ∈ O(U) | ∃ g ∈ O(U), fg = 1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unitsSheaf_iff_exists_mul_eq_one (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w}) (U : X.Cᵒᵖ)
    (f : X.O.obj.obj U) :
    (∃ x : ((unitsSheaf X).obj.obj U : Type w), (unitsSheafι X).hom.app U x = f) ↔
      ∃ g : X.O.obj.obj U, f * g = 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.unitsSheafι_hom_app_mul
declarations.doc:
The group law on the sheaf of units is multiplication: the subsheaf inclusion
`O_X^* ⟶ O_X` is multiplicative.
declarations.statement:
theorem unitsSheafι_hom_app_mul (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w}) (U : X.Cᵒᵖ)
    (x y : (X.O.obj.obj U)ˣ) :
    (unitsSheafι X).hom.app U (x * y) =
      (x : X.O.obj.obj U) * (y : X.O.obj.obj U)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isIso_evaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040A (2), the evaluation clause.** For an invertible sheaf of
`𝒪`-modules `L` on a ringed site the evaluation pairing `SheafHom(L, 𝒪) ⊗_𝒪 L ⟶ 𝒪` is an
isomorphism.

The dual is a left dual of `L` by `exactPairingDualSheafOfIsInvertible`, and the evaluation of an
exact pairing is an isomorphism whenever tensoring on the right by the first object is an
equivalence, which for an invertible sheaf of modules it is.

A ringed space is a ringed site, so this is also the evaluation clause of Tag 01CT (2); see
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_evaluation_of_isInvertible` for that reading.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_evaluation [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] : IsIso (evaluation 𝒪 h𝒪 L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isIso_tensorSheafBraiding_hom_comp_evaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040A (2) and Tag 01CT (2), the evaluation clause in the order the tags
write it.** The evaluation map `L ⊗_𝒪 SheafHom(L, 𝒪) ⟶ 𝒪` is an isomorphism. It is the canonical
pairing of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluation`, whose factors come in the order Tag 0FNV writes
them, preceded by the braiding of the tensor product sheaf, which is what exchanges the two
factors; in this order it is the trivializing pairing identifying `L^∨` as a tensor inverse of
`L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorSheafBraiding_hom_comp_evaluation [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] :
    IsIso ((tensorSheafBraiding 𝒪 h𝒪 L (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 L)).hom ≫ evaluation 𝒪 h𝒪 L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isInvertible_dualSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040A (2) and Tag 01CT (2), the invertibility clause.** The dual
`L^∨ = SheafHom(L, 𝒪)` of an invertible sheaf of `𝒪`-modules is again invertible: the evaluation
pairing is an isomorphism `L^∨ ⊗_𝒪 L ≅ 𝒪`, which is Tag 0B8K (2) for `L^∨`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_dualSheaf [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] :
    IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorProduct_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CT (1), Tag 040A (1).** The tensor product of two invertible sheaves
of modules is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorProduct_isInvertible
    (L N : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] [IsInvertible O hO N] :
    IsInvertible O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) hO⟩).obj L)).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.essentiallySmall_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 040B.** The invertible sheaves of modules on a ringed site form an essentially
small class: there is a set of invertible modules such that every invertible module is
isomorphic to exactly one of them. Equivalently, the isomorphism classes of invertible
`O`-modules form a set of size `max u v w`.

The two instance hypotheses are the standing hypotheses of the invertible-module API of this
development — they are what makes the sheafified tensor product and the locally bijective
pairing of Tag 0B8N available — and they are satisfied wherever Tag 01CX builds the Picard
group.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallySmall_isInvertible
    (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{w})
    (hO : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureRingPresheaf O)) :
    ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{max u v w} (IsInvertible O hO)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup
declarations.doc:
The Picard group of `O`: the group of isomorphism classes of
invertible sheaves of `O`-modules, as a small type.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def PicardGroup : Type (max (max u v) w)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.instAddCommGroupPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
The abelian group structure on the Picard group; its addition is the tensor product sheaf,
by `classOf_tensor`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instAddCommGroupPicardGroup : AddCommGroup (PicardGroup O hO)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.classOf
declarations.doc: The class in the Picard group of an invertible sheaf of modules.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.classOf_eq_classOf_iff
declarations.doc:
Two invertible sheaves of modules determine the same Picard class exactly when they are
isomorphic, so the elements of the Picard group are the isomorphism classes.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_eq_classOf_iff (L N : SheafOfModules.{w}
  (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    (hL : IsInvertible O hO L) (hN : IsInvertible O hO N) :
    classOf O hO L hL = classOf O hO N hN ↔ Nonempty (L ≅ N)
declarations.comment: elements are isomorphism classes of invertible modules

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.classOf_tensor
declarations.doc: Addition in the Picard group is the tensor product sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_tensor (L N : SheafOfModules.{w}
  (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    (hL : IsInvertible O hO L) (hN : IsInvertible O hO N)
    (hLN : IsInvertible O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (hO)⟩).obj
        (L)).obj (N)))) :
    classOf O hO L hL + classOf O hO N hN =
      classOf O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (hO)⟩).obj
          (L)).obj (N))) hLN

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.SmallEtaleSite.etaleH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040E, at `τ = étale` on the small site.** For a scheme `S` in a big
étale site containing it there is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups
`H¹_{étale}(S, 𝐆_m) = Pic(𝒪_étale)`.
declarations.statement:
def etaleH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup :
    Sheaf.H
        (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.unitsAddSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS)) 1 ≃+
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O).2
declarations.comment: the identification H¹_étale(S, 𝐆_m) = Pic(𝒪_étale), on the small étale site

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.SmallEtaleSite.etaleH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup_symm_classOf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040E at `τ = étale`, the identification is the canonical one.** Its
inverse sends the class of an invertible `𝒪_étale`-module to the first cohomology class of its
torsor of local generators.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup_symm_classOf
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O))
    (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O.obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O).2 L) :
    (etaleH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup B S hS).symm
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.classOf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O.obj
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O).2 L hL) =
      Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesEquivH1
        (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.unitsAddSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS))
        (Quotient.mk (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorSetoid
            (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.unitsAddSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS)))
          (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.generatorTorsor' (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS)
            (smallEtaleRingedSite_isLocallyRinged B S hS) L hL).torsor)
declarations.comment: the étale identification is normalized on invertible modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 040E for an algebraic space.** The first cohomology of the sheaf of units on the
small étale site of an algebraic space `Z` is the Picard group of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
def h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup :
    Sheaf.H.{u + 1} (unitsAddSheafEtale B S hS Z) 1 ≃+ picardGroup Z
declarations.comment: for the small étale site of an algebraic space

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroupOfEssentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040E on an essentially small ringed site.** Let `(C, O)` be a locally
ringed site whose underlying category is essentially small at the universe of the sections of
`O`. There is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups `H^1(C, O^*) = Pic(O)`.

This is `Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup` with the three
universes of the ringed site independent.
declarations.statement:
def h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroupOfEssentiallySmall
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged X) :
    Sheaf.H.{a} (unitsAddSheaf X) 1 ≃+
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.O.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).2
declarations.comment: on an essentially small ringed site, with the universe of the sections of the structure sheaf independent of the universes of the site

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040E.** Let `(C, O)` be a locally ringed site. There is a canonical
isomorphism of abelian groups `H^1(C, O^*) = Pic(O)`.
declarations.statement:
def h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup :
    Sheaf.H (unitsAddSheaf X) 1 ≃+
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.O.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).2

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040E.** Let `(C, O)` be a locally ringed site. There is a canonical
isomorphism of abelian groups `H^1(C, O^*) = Pic(O)`.

This generalizes `Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup`,
stated for `RingedSite.{u, u, u}`, to independent universes.
declarations.statement:
def h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup' :
    Sheaf.H (unitsAddSheaf X) 1 ≃+
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.O.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).2
declarations.comment: with the three universes of the ringed site independent, on a site essentially small at the universe of the sections of the structure sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.liftsGeneralizations_of_isOpenMap
declarations.doc: An open morphism of schemes lifts generalizations of points.
declarations.statement:
public lemma liftsGeneralizations_of_isOpenMap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsOpenMap f) : LiftsGeneralizations f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universally_liftsGeneralizations_of_universallyOpen
declarations.doc: A universally open morphism of schemes lifts generalizations after every base change.
declarations.statement:
public lemma universally_liftsGeneralizations_of_universallyOpen {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [UniversallyOpen f] : universally (topologically @LiftsGeneralizations) f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Submersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 040H, part (1).** A morphism of schemes is *submersive* when the continuous map of
underlying topological spaces is a quotient map, that is submersive in the sense of Stacks 0406,
part (2). This is unrelated to the notion of a submersion of differentiable manifolds.
declarations.statement: def Submersive : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallySubmersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 040H, part (2).** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is *universally submersive*
when the base change `Y' ×_Y X ⟶ Y'` of `f` along every morphism of schemes `Y' ⟶ Y` is
submersive.
declarations.statement: def UniversallySubmersive : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_singleton_sigmaDesc_mem
declarations.doc:
A family of morphisms of schemes is an fpqc covering precisely when the induced
morphism from the disjoint union of the source schemes is an fpqc covering.
declarations.statement:
public lemma ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_singleton_sigmaDesc_mem
    {ι : Type v} [Small.{u} ι] {T : Scheme.{u}} (T' : ι → Scheme.{u})
    (f : ∀ i, T' i ⟶ T) :
    Presieve.ofArrows T' f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T ↔
      Presieve.singleton (Sigma.desc f) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_faithful_of_source_surjective_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040J.** Pullback of descent data along a morphism whose source is
surjective and flat over the base is faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackFunctor_faithful_of_source_surjective_flat
    {S X X' : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S) (a' : X' ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ X') (comm : f ≫ a' = a)
    [Surjective a] [Flat a] :
    (DescentData.pullbackFunctor a' a (𝟙 S) f (by simpa using comm)).functor.Faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_source_fpqc
declarations.doc:
Pullback along a morphism `X ⟶ X'` over `S` is fully
faithful on descent data if `X ⟶ S` is an fpqc covering.
declarations.statement:
lemma pullbackFunctor_fullyFaithful_of_source_fpqc
    {S X X' : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S) (a' : X' ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ X') (comm : f ≫ a' = a)
    (hcover : Presieve.singleton a ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S) :
    Nonempty
      (DescentData.pullbackFunctor a' a (𝟙 S) f
        (by simpa using comm)).functor.FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_relativeHom_fpqc
declarations.doc:
Let `X` and `Y` be schemes over `S`. The relative morphism functor
`Mor_S(X, Y) : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Set`, which sends an `S`-scheme `T` to the set of morphisms
`X_T ⟶ Y_T` over `T`, satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology on the schemes over
`S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_relativeHom_fpqc (X Y : Over S) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u}.over S) (relativeHom X Y)
declarations.comment: the functor `T ↦ Mor_T(X_T, Y_T)` on the schemes over `S` satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040M.** The scheme of `n`-th roots of unity over the integers is
`Spec (ℤ[X] / (Xⁿ - 1))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev rootsOfUnity (n : ℕ) : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnityCanonicallyOver
declarations.doc: The canonical structure morphism from the scheme of roots of unity to the integer base.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance rootsOfUnityCanonicallyOver (n : ℕ) :
    (rootsOfUnity n).CanonicallyOver (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnityBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040M.** The scheme of `n`-th roots of unity over `S` is the base change
of the scheme of roots of unity over the integers along the unique map from `S` to the integer
base.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev rootsOfUnityBaseChange (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnitySections_representableBy_rootsOfUnity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040M.** The functor of units in global sections whose `n`-th power is
one is represented by `Spec (ℤ[X] / (Xⁿ - 1))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnitySections_representableBy_rootsOfUnity (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    Nonempty ((rootsOfUnitySections n).RepresentableBy (rootsOfUnity n : Scheme.{u}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnityGrpObj
declarations.doc:
The group-object structure on the scheme of positive-order roots of unity over the
integers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance rootsOfUnityGrpObj (n : ℕ) [Fact (0 < n)] :
    GrpObj (Over.mk (rootsOfUnity n ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnityGrpObj_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040M.** The scheme of `n`-th roots of unity is a group scheme over
the integers, with multiplication induced by `X ↦ X ⊗ X` on coordinate rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnityGrpObj_mul (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (letI : Fact (0 < n) := ⟨hn⟩
    μ[Over.mk (rootsOfUnity n ↘ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))].left =
      rootsOfUnityMultiplication n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnitySectionsOver_representableBy_rootsOfUnityBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040M.** For every scheme `S`, the base change to `S` of the scheme of
`n`-th roots of unity represents, naturally in an `S`-scheme `T`, the units in `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` whose
`n`-th power is one. The representing universal element is the pullback of the polynomial
coordinate `X` along the base-change projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnitySectionsOver_representableBy_rootsOfUnityBaseChange
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    ((Over.forget S).op ⋙ rootsOfUnitySections n).IsRepresentedBy
      (rootsOfUnityBaseChangeUniversalRoot n hn S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnityGroupOverFunctor
declarations.doc:
The group-valued functor on schemes over `S` whose value on `T` is the group of `n`-th roots
of unity in `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev rootsOfUnityGroupOverFunctor (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnityBaseChangeOverGrpObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040M.** The base change of the group scheme of `n`-th roots of unity
to a scheme `S` is a group scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance rootsOfUnityBaseChangeOverGrpObj (n : ℕ) [Fact (0 < n)]
    (S : Scheme.{u}) : GrpObj (rootsOfUnityBaseChangeOver n S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnityBaseChangeGroupPointsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040M.** For every scheme `S`, the group-valued functor of points of
the group scheme `μₙ,S` of `n`-th roots of unity is naturally isomorphic to the group of `n`-th
roots of unity in the global sections of the varying `S`-scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rootsOfUnityBaseChangeGroupPointsIso (n : ℕ) [Fact (0 < n)] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    yonedaGrpObj (rootsOfUnityBaseChangeOver n S) ≅ rootsOfUnityGroupOverFunctor n S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.kummerSequence_shortExact_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040N (fppf).** The canonical Kummer complex of
abelian sheaves on the big fppf site is short exact.
declarations.statement:

    (kummerSequence (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040N (syntomic).** The canonical Kummer complex of
abelian sheaves on the big syntomic site is short exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem kummerSequence_shortExact_syntomic
    (B : BigSyntomicSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)

      (BigSyntomicOver.toScheme B S hS)
