declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041Q** at the fppf precoverage: surjectivity of morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S` is local at the target for the fppf topology. This is the form in which the relative
properties of Stacks 03YK ask for it; the comparison of precoverages is Stacks 0DFQ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage`.
declarations.statement:
instance surjective_isLocalAtTarget_fppf :
    (surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041R.** Universal injectivity of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local
on the base for the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
instance universallyInjective_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (universallyInjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyOfFiniteType_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
Being locally of finite type is, for morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, local on the
base for the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
instance locallyOfFiniteType_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 041T** (Lemma 74.11.10 of Chapter 74, *Descent and Algebraic
Spaces*). The property `𝒫(f)` = "`f` is locally of finite presentation" of morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S` is fpqc local on the base.

The setting is the source's own. By the conventions of that chapter (**Stacks 041I**, Section
74.2) every scheme lies in a big fppf site `Sch_fppf`, here `B`, and `S` is one of its objects;
algebraic spaces over `S` are the objects of `AlgebraicSpaces B S S_mem`, and local finite
presentation of a morphism of algebraic spaces is that of **Stacks 03XP**, part (1). "Fpqc local
on the base" is Definition 74.10.1 (**Stacks 03YH**) at the fpqc topology: for every fpqc
covering `{Yᵢ → Y}` of algebraic spaces in the sense of **Stacks 03MQ**, indexed by a type in any
universe `v`, and every morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, the morphism `f` is locally of finite presentation
if and only if every base change `Yᵢ ×_Y X → Yᵢ` is. That is the class
`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget` at `Topology.fpqc.precoverage`, whose coverings
are exactly the families `Presieve.ofArrows Yᵢ gᵢ` with `gᵢ` an fpqc covering of `Y`.

The scheme-level statement, for morphisms of schemes, is Descent, Lemma 35.23.13 (**Stacks
02KY**), `Stacks.Descent.locallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc`; the proof of the
source reduces to it, and so does this one.
declarations.statement:
instance isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (S_mem : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S S_mem⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) =>
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S S_mem f.hom)
      (Topology.fpqc.precoverage.{u, v} B S S_mem)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteType_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041U.** Being of finite type, as a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S`, is local on the target for the fpqc topology.

Being of finite type is being locally of finite type and quasi-compact (**Stacks 03XF**, part
(3)); the first conjunct is local on the target for the fpqc topology by **Stacks 041S** and the
second by **Stacks 041L**, so their conjunction is.
declarations.statement:
instance isFiniteType_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (finiteTypeProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.fpqc.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteType_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
Being of finite type is, for morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, local on the base for
the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
instance finiteType_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePresentation_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041V.** Being of finite presentation is, for morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S`, local on the base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH.

Being of finite presentation is being locally of finite presentation (Stacks 041T) together with
quasi-compactness (Stacks 041L) and quasi-separatedness (Stacks 041N).
declarations.statement:
instance finitePresentation_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041W.** Flatness of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the target
for the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
instance isFlat_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) => IsFlat B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.fpqc.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_isLocalAtTarget_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041W** at the fppf precoverage: flatness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
is local at the target for the fppf topology. It follows from the fpqc form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc` through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage`, and it is the form in
which the relative properties of Stacks 03YK ask for it; it is the exact analogue of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocalAtTarget_fppf` and of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_isLocalAtTarget_fppf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_isLocalAtTarget_fppf (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (g : X ⟶ Y) => IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
      (Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.openImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041X.** Being an open immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base
for the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
instance openImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    (openImmersionProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isomorphisms_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 041Y.** Being an isomorphism is, for morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, local
on the base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH: such a morphism is an isomorphism exactly
when its base change to every member of some fpqc covering family of its target is an
isomorphism.

A morphism is an isomorphism exactly when it is a surjective open immersion, surjectivity is
fpqc local on the base by **Stacks 041Q** and being an open immersion by **Stacks 041X**, so
their conjunction is.
declarations.statement:
instance isomorphisms_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (MorphismProperty.isomorphisms (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalAtTarget_isAffineHom_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Affineness of morphisms of algebraic spaces is fpqc local on the base**, which is
[Stacks, Tag 041Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/041Z).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtTarget_isAffineHom_fpqc (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun {X Y} (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom :
        MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
      (Topology.fpqc.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0420** at the fppf precoverage: being a closed immersion is local on the base for
the fppf topology for morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, so such a morphism is a closed
immersion exactly when its base change to every member of some fppf covering of its target is
one.

The fpqc form is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc`, and the two
are compared by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage` (Stacks 0DFQ). This
is the form in which the relative properties of Stacks 03YK ask for it.
declarations.statement:
instance isClosedImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fppf :
    (closedImmersionProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fppf B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0420.** Being a closed immersion is fpqc local on the base for morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S`: such a morphism is a closed immersion exactly when its base change
to every member of some fpqc covering of its target is one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsClosedImmersion B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.separated_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0421.** Separatedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the
base for the fpqc topology: a morphism is separated exactly when its base change to every member
of some fpqc covering of its target is separated.

Separatedness of `f : X ⟶ Y` is the relative diagonal `Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` being a closed
immersion. Pulling a covering `{Y i ⟶ Y}` back along `X ×_Y X ⟶ Y` gives a covering of `X ×_Y X`
whose base changes of `Δ_f` are the relative diagonals of the base changes of `f`, so Stacks
0420 for closed immersions applies.
declarations.statement:
instance separated_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (separatedProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperULift_of_isPullback_uliftYoneda_family
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0422 for a family of morphisms of the site, in the value universe `Type (u + 1)`.**
Let `p : F ⟶ U` be a morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` with values in
`Type (u + 1)` whose source is an algebraic space over `S` and whose target is the
universe-lifted representable sheaf of an object `U` of the site, and let `{qᵢ : Vᵢ ⟶ U}` be a
family of morphisms of the site whose Yoneda images form an fppf covering family of `U` in the
sense of **Stacks 03Y8**. If some base change of `p` along each `qᵢ` is proper, then `p` is
proper.

The source and the base changes are algebraic spaces, hence universe lifts of presheaves in the
value universe of the site; there properness of a lift is properness of the presheaf
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperULift_whiskerRight_iff`) and the covering family generates a
covering family of the fpqc precoverage of Stacks 03YH, at which properness is local on the
base by **Stacks 0422**.
declarations.comment: for a family of morphisms of the site, in the value universe of a formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperULift_of_isPullback_uliftYoneda_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0422 for a single surjective étale morphism of the site, in the value universe
`Type (u + 1)`.** Let `p : F ⟶ U` be a morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` with
values in `Type (u + 1)` whose source is an algebraic space over `S` and whose target is the
universe-lifted representable sheaf of an object `U` of the site, and let `q : U' ⟶ U` be a
morphism of the site which is surjective and étale on underlying schemes. If some base change
of `p` along `q` is proper, then `p` is proper.

The one-member family consisting of the Yoneda image of `q` is an fppf covering family of its
target by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFppfCovering_atlas`, so this is the family statement at
that family.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperULift_of_isPullback_uliftYoneda_map
    {F F' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)} {U U' : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    {p : F ⟶ (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).obj U} {p' : F' ⟶ (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).obj U'}
    {k : F' ⟶ F} (q : U' ⟶ U)
    (sq : IsPullback k p' p ((uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).map q))
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS F)
    (hqs : Surjective ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map q))
    (hqe : Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map q))
    (hp' : IsProperULift.{u + 1} B S hS p') :
    IsProperULift.{u + 1} B S hS p
declarations.comment: for one surjective étale morphism of the site, in the value universe of a formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.proper_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0422.** Properness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base
for the fpqc topology: a morphism is proper exactly when its base change to every member of some
fpqc covering family of its target is proper.

Being proper is being separated, of finite type and universally closed (**Stacks 03ZM**); the
three conjuncts are local on the base for the fpqc topology by **Stacks 0421**, **Stacks 041U**
and **Stacks 041O**, so their conjunction is.
declarations.statement:
instance proper_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (properProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalAtTarget_isQuasiAffineHom_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0423** (Lemma 74.11.20 of Chapter 74, *Descent and Algebraic Spaces*). The
property "`f` is quasi-affine" of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is fpqc local on the
base, in the sense of Definition 74.10.1 (Stacks 03YH): for every fpqc covering
`{Yᵢ ⟶ Y}` of algebraic spaces over `S` (Stacks 03MQ) and every morphism of algebraic spaces
`f : X ⟶ Y`, the morphism `f` is quasi-affine if and only if each base change
`Yᵢ ×_Y X ⟶ Yᵢ` is quasi-affine.

The setting is that of the conventions of Chapter 74 (Stacks 041I): `S` is a scheme of the big
fppf site `B`, algebraic spaces over `S` are sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`, and
quasi-affineness is the notion of Stacks 03WL, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiAffineHom`:
every base change to an affine scheme is represented by a quasi-affine scheme. Locality on the
base is `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget` for the fpqc precoverage
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology.precoverage .fpqc` of the category of algebraic spaces over
`S`, whose covering presieves are those generated by the fpqc coverings, with index sets in any
universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtTarget_isQuasiAffineHom_fpqc (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (contains : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S contains} (g : X ⟶ Y) ↦
          IsQuasiAffineHom B S contains g.hom :
        MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S contains))
      (Topology.fpqc.precoverage.{u, v} B S contains)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersion_inf_quasiCompact_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0424.** Being a quasi-compact immersion is fpqc local on the base for morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S`: such a morphism is a quasi-compact immersion exactly when its base
change to every member of some fpqc covering of its target is a quasi-compact immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem immersion_inf_quasiCompact_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (immersionProperty B S hS ⊓ quasiCompactProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.integralMorphismProperty_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0425.** Integrality of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base
for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH.

An integral morphism is an affine universally closed one (Stacks 0415), affineness is fpqc local
on the base (Stacks 041Z) and so is universal closedness (Stacks 041O), and locality on the base
passes to an infimum of morphism properties.
declarations.statement:
instance integralMorphismProperty_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (integralMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0426.** Finiteness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base
for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH: a morphism is finite exactly when its base change to every
member of some fpqc covering family of its target is finite.

A morphism is finite exactly when it is proper and locally quasi-finite (**Stacks 0A4X**),
properness is fpqc local on the base by **Stacks 0422** and local quasi-finiteness by
**Stacks 0427**, so their conjunction is.
declarations.statement:
instance isFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (finiteMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0427**, the locally quasi-finite case.  Local quasi-finiteness of a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH.
declarations.statement:
instance isLocallyQuasiFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0427**, the quasi-finite case.  Quasi-finiteness of a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` is local on the base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH.

Quasi-finiteness is local quasi-finiteness together with quasi-compactness, and quasi-compactness
is fpqc local on the base by Stacks 041L.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasiFinite_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsQuasiFinite B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.syntomic_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0428.**  Syntomicity of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the
base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH.
declarations.statement:
instance syntomic_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsSyntomic B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_isLocalAtTarget_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0429** at the fppf precoverage: smoothness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S` is local at the target for the fppf topology. The fpqc form is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc`, and the two are compared by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage`. This is the form in which Stacks
03YK's relative properties ask for it.
declarations.statement:
instance smooth_isLocalAtTarget_fppf (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) :
    (smoothMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc: Smoothness of algebraic-space morphisms is fpqc local on the base.
declarations.statement:
instance smooth_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    (smoothMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
Unramifiedness of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the target for the
fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
public instance isUnramified_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) =>
        IsUnramified B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.fpqc.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_iff_forall_pullbackSnd_of_isFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
Let `{gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Y}` be an fpqc covering of algebraic spaces over `S`, indexed by a type `I`
in any universe, and `f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`. Then `f` is unramified
if and only if every base change `pullback.snd f (g i) : Yᵢ ×_Y X ⟶ Yᵢ` of `f` is unramified.
declarations.comment: Definition 03YH unfolded: f unramified iff every Yᵢ ×_Y X → Yᵢ is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042B.**  Étaleness of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base
for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH.
declarations.statement:
instance isEtale_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFree_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042C.** Being finite locally free is, for morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`,
local on the base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH: such a morphism is finite locally free
exactly when its base change to every member of some fpqc covering family of its target is
finite locally free.

A morphism is finite locally free exactly when it is finite, flat and locally of finite
presentation (**Stacks 0416**), finiteness is fpqc local on the base by **Stacks 0426**,
flatness by **Stacks 041W** and local finite presentation by **Stacks 041T**, so their
conjunction is.
declarations.statement:
instance isFiniteLocallyFree_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (finiteLocallyFreeMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042D.** Monomorphy of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base for
the fpqc topology: a morphism is a monomorphism exactly when its base change to every member of
some fpqc covering of its target is a monomorphism.

Stacks 042Q reduces monomorphy to monomorphy of the base changes along the morphisms out of the
affine objects of the site, over such an object the covering is refined by a finite family of
affine objects factoring through its members, and monomorphy descends along the fpqc covering
sieve that family generates because the fibre product is an fpqc sheaf by Stacks 0APL.
declarations.statement:
instance mono_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallySeparated_isLocalAtTarget_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042F.** Local separatedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on
the base for the fppf topology: a morphism is locally separated exactly when its base change to
every member of some fppf covering of its target is locally separated.

Local separatedness of `f : X ⟶ Y` is the relative diagonal `Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` being an
immersion. Pulling a covering `{Y i ⟶ Y}` back along `X ×_Y X ⟶ Y` gives a covering of
`X ×_Y X` whose base changes of `Δ_f` are the relative diagonals of the base changes of `f`, so
Stacks 042U for immersions applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallySeparated_isLocalAtTarget_fppf :
    (locallySeparatedMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fppf B S hS)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.isFibered_iff_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042G (Lemma 4.33.8).** Let `𝒮` be a category and let `𝒳` and `𝒴` be categories
over `𝒮`.  If `𝒳` and `𝒴` are equivalent as categories over `𝒮`, then `𝒳` is a fibred
category over `𝒮` if and only if `𝒴` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem BasedCategory.isFibered_iff_of_equivalence
    {𝒳 : BasedCategory.{v₂, u₂} 𝒮} {𝒴 : BasedCategory.{v₃, u₃} 𝒮}
    (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴) :
    𝒳.p.IsFibered ↔ 𝒴.p.IsFibered

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.absoluteInertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042I.** If `p : S ⥤ C` is fibred in groupoids, then so is the inertia fibred
category `I_S ⥤ C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem absoluteInertia (p : S ⥤ C) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    (relativeInertiaStruct p p).IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: isFiberedInSetoids_iff_π_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042J.** A category fibred in groupoids `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` is fibred in setoids if and
only if the forgetful 1-morphism `π : I_𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮` of the absolute inertia is an equivalence.
Since `π` is always faithful and essentially surjective, the content is that `π` is full
exactly when the fibres of `p` are thin.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedInSetoids_iff_π_isEquivalence (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    p.IsFiberedInSetoids ↔ (RelativeInertia.π p : AbsoluteInertia p ⥤ 𝒮).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_hom_iff_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042M, parts (1) and (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a
monomorphism of the underlying presheaves exactly when it is a monomorphism of the category
of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_hom_iff_mono {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Mono f.hom ↔ Mono f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_iff_isIso_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042M, parts (2) and (3).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a
monomorphism of the category of algebraic spaces over `S` exactly when its relative diagonal
is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_iff_isIso_diagonal {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Mono f ↔ IsIso (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042N.** A monomorphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is a separated
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`: its relative diagonal is an isomorphism, and an
isomorphism is a closed immersion. The statement is made for an arbitrary morphism of presheaves
on the big fppf site of `S`; no algebraic-space hypothesis is used.

This strictly generalises `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_isIso`, which is the same
statement for an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_mono {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (m : F ⟶ G) (hm : Mono m) :
    IsSeparated B S hS m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042N.** A monomorphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is separated: its relative
diagonal is an isomorphism, and an isomorphism is a closed immersion.

The statement is made for an arbitrary morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`; no
algebraic-space hypothesis is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_mono {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (g : F ⟶ G) (hg : Mono g) :
    IsSeparated B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042Q.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` the following are
equivalent: `f` is a monomorphism; every base change of `f` to a scheme of the site is a
monomorphism; every base change of `f` to an affine scheme of the site is a monomorphism; the
base change of `f` along some surjective étale chart of `Y` is a monomorphism; and the base
changes of `f` along the members of some Zariski covering of `Y` are monomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_tfae {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      Mono f,
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y), Mono (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) → Mono (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
        IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧ Mono (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Subfunctor Y),
        IsZariskiCover B S hS I U ∧ ∀ i, Mono (pullback.snd f (U i).ι))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042R.** An immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is a monomorphism: an immersion
of schemes is a monomorphism, and a morphism of presheaves all of whose represented base
changes are monomorphisms is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_of_isImmersion {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : F ⟶ G}
    (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f) : Mono f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042R.** An immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is separated: it is a
monomorphism, so its relative diagonal is an isomorphism, and an isomorphism of presheaves is
a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isImmersion {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : F ⟶ G}
    (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f) : IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyOpen_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A flat morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation is
universally open in the sense of Stacks 03Z2.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f) (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    UniversallyOpen B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_fppfCovering_scheme_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042T.** An fppf covering of an algebraic space over `S` admits a refinement by a
family of schemes which is again an fppf covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fppfCovering_scheme_refinement
    {I : Type v} {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (X : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ F)
    (hf : IsFppfCovering B S hS X f) :
    ∃ (T : I → BigFppfOver B S hS) (h : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (T i) ⟶ X i),
      IsFppfCovering B S hS (fun i => yoneda.obj (T i)) (fun i => h i ≫ f i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fppf
declarations.doc:
Being an immersion is fppf local on the base for morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`: such
a morphism is an immersion exactly when its base change to every member of some fppf covering of
its target is an immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_isLocalAtTarget_fppf
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    (immersionProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fppf B S hS)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.morPresheafMap
declarations.doc:
The map of presheaves `Mor(x, y) ⟶ Mor(F x, F y)` induced by a 1-morphism of fibred categories
over `𝒞`: over `g` it applies `F` to a section and conjugates by the comparison isomorphisms
`IsFibredOneMorphism.mapPullbackFiberIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def morPresheafMap (hF : IsFibredOneMorphism p r₀ F₀) {U : 𝒞} (a b : p.Fiber U) :
    morPresheaf p a b ⟶ morPresheaf r₀ ((fiberFunctorOfCompEq hF.comp_eq U).obj a)
      ((fiberFunctorOfCompEq hF.comp_eq U).obj b)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.isStack_iff_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and let `𝒳`, `𝒴` be categories over `𝒞`. If `𝒳` and `𝒴` are equivalent
as categories over `𝒞`, then `𝒳` is a stack over `𝒞` if and only if `𝒴` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem BasedCategory.isStack_iff_of_equivalence
    (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    𝒳.p.IsStack J ↔ 𝒴.p.IsStack J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.isFiberedInGroupoids_and_isStack_iff_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042X**. Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and let `𝒳`, `𝒴` be categories over `𝒞`. If `𝒳` and
`𝒴` are equivalent as categories over `𝒞`, then `𝒳` is a stack in groupoids over `𝒞` if and only
if `𝒴` is.

"Stack in groupoids" is read as clause (3) of Stacks 02ZJ, fibred in groupoids together with being
a stack, which is the reading 042X's proof uses; the two conjuncts transport by
`BasedCategory.isFiberedInGroupoids_iff_of_equivalence` and by Stacks 042W,
`BasedCategory.isStack_iff_of_equivalence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BasedCategory.isFiberedInGroupoids_and_isStack_iff_of_equivalence
    (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    𝒳.p.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧ 𝒳.p.IsStack J ↔
      𝒴.p.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧ 𝒴.p.IsStack J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStackInSetoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042Z**.
A *stack in setoids* over the site `(𝒞, J)`: a stack over `𝒞` all of whose fibre categories are
setoids, that is groupoids in which there is at most one morphism between any two objects.
declarations.statement: structure Functor.IsStackInSetoids (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStackInSets
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 042Z**.
A *stack in sets*, also called a *stack in discrete categories*, over the site `(𝒞, J)`: a stack
over `𝒞` all of whose fibre categories are discrete.
declarations.statement: structure Functor.IsStackInSets (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStackInSets_iff_isSheaf_objPresheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site. Under the equivalence of Categories, Stacks 02Y2 between presheaves of
sets on `𝒞` and categories fibred in sets over `𝒞`, the stacks in sets correspond precisely to the
sheaves: a category fibred in sets `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` is a stack in sets over `(𝒞, J)` if and only if its
presheaf of objects `U ↦ Ob(𝒮_U)` is a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSets_iff_isSheaf_objPresheaf (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    p.IsStackInSets J ↔ Presheaf.IsSheaf J (objPresheaf p)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.isStackInSetoids_iff_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and let `𝒳`, `𝒴` be categories over `𝒞`. If `𝒳` and `𝒴` are equivalent
as categories over `𝒞`, then `𝒳` is a stack in setoids over `𝒞` if and only if `𝒴` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem BasedCategory.isStackInSetoids_iff_of_equivalence
    (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    𝒳.p.IsStackInSetoids J ↔ 𝒴.p.IsStackInSetoids J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.isStackInSetoids_iff_isStackInSets_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site, let `𝒳` be a category fibred in setoids over `𝒞`, and let `𝒴` be a
category fibred in sets equivalent to `𝒳` as a category over `𝒞`. Then `𝒳` is a stack in setoids if
and only if `𝒴` is a stack in sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem BasedCategory.isStackInSetoids_iff_isStackInSets_of_equivalence
    {𝒞 : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} 𝒞] {𝒳 𝒴 : BasedCategory.{v₂, u₂} 𝒞}
    (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴) [𝒳.p.IsFiberedInSetoids] [𝒴.p.IsFiberedInSets]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    𝒳.p.IsStackInSetoids J ↔ 𝒴.p.IsStackInSets J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.isStackInSetoids_iff_isSheaf_objPresheaf_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site, let `𝒳` be a category fibred in setoids over `𝒞`, and let `𝒴` be a
category fibred in sets equivalent to `𝒳` as a category over `𝒞`. Then `𝒳` is a stack in setoids if
and only if the presheaf of objects `U ↦ Ob(𝒴_U)` of `𝒴` is a sheaf. Its value at `U` is identified
with the set `Ob(𝒳_U)/≅` of isomorphism classes of the fibre of `𝒳` over `U` by
`CategoryTheory.BasedCategory.Equivalence.fiberQuotientEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BasedCategory.isStackInSetoids_iff_isSheaf_objPresheaf_of_equivalence
    {𝒞 : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} 𝒞] {𝒳 𝒴 : BasedCategory.{v₂, u₂} 𝒞}
    (e : BasedCategory.Equivalence 𝒳 𝒴) [𝒳.p.IsFiberedInSetoids] [𝒴.p.IsFiberedInSets]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    𝒳.p.IsStackInSetoids J ↔ Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Functor.objPresheaf 𝒴.p)
declarations.comment: the "in other words" sentence: iff the presheaf `U ↦ Ob(𝒮_U)/≅` is a sheaf

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.StackInSetoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0433**.
An object of the 2-category of stacks in setoids over the site `(𝒞, J)`: a category over `𝒞`
whose structure functor is a stack in setoids.
declarations.statement: structure StackInSetoids (𝒞 : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} 𝒞] (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.StackInSetoids.bicategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0433**.
The 2-category of stacks in setoids over the site `(𝒞, J)`: the full sub-2-category of the
2-category `BasedCategory 𝒞` of categories over `𝒞` spanned by the stacks in setoids. A
1-morphism `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is a functor `G` over `𝒞`, that is with `p' ∘ G = p`, and a 2-morphism
`F ⟶ G` is a morphism of functors `t` with `p'(t_x) = 𝟙 (p x)` for every object `x`.
declarations.statement: instance StackInSetoids.bicategory : Bicategory (StackInSetoids.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} 𝒞 J)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.isStackInSetoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0434.** The 2-fibre product of stacks in setoids over a site `(𝒞, J)` is a stack in
setoids: the construction of Stacks 0040 does not leave the 2-category of stacks in setoids.

Its three conditions are Stacks 026G (`isStack_structureFunctor`), Stacks 0041
(`fiber_isGroupoid`) and thinness of the fibres (`fiber_isThin`). Nothing is asked of `F` and `G`
beyond being strictly over `𝒞`, since a functor over `𝒞` into a category fibred in groupoids
automatically preserves strongly cartesian morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSetoids {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} (h𝒳 : p𝒳.IsStackInSetoids J)
    (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsStackInSetoids J) (h𝒮 : p𝒮.IsStackInSetoids J)
    (hF : F ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒳) (hG : G ⋙ p𝒮 = p𝒴) :
    (structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒮 F G).IsStackInSetoids J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.extend
declarations.doc:
**The functor underlying the extension of `F` along `G`**, Stacks 0435. Its value on an object
`X` of `𝒮'` is the object of `𝒳` to which the images under `F` of a chosen local presentation of
`X` descend, and its value on a morphism is the morphism glued from the transfers along `G` of the
transition morphisms of the chosen presentations.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extend : 𝒮' ⥤ 𝒳

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.extend_isFibredOneMorphism
declarations.doc:
**The extension is a 1-morphism of fibred categories over `𝒞`**: it is strictly over `𝒞` and
preserves strongly cartesian morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem extend_isFibredOneMorphism :
    p'.IsFibredOneMorphism q (extend hG hF hmor hqmor hobj hdesc)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.unit
declarations.doc:
**The 2-isomorphism `G ⋙ H ≅ F` of Stacks 0435.** Its component at `A` compares the object of
`𝒳` that the chosen presentation of `G A` descends to with `F A`, and it is an isomorphism because
both are descents of presentations of one and the same object of `𝒮'`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def unit : G ⋙ extend hG hF hmor hqmor hobj hdesc ≅ F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isHomLift_unit_app
declarations.doc:
Every component of the 2-isomorphism lies over an identity, so it is a 2-morphism of fibred
categories over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isHomLift_unit_app (A : 𝒮) :
    q.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p.obj A)) ((unit hG hF hmor hqmor hobj hdesc).hom.app A)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.extendGroupoid
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site, let `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` be a category fibred in groupoids, let `G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮'`
exhibit the stack in groupoids `p'` as the stackification of `𝒮`, and let `F : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒳` be a
1-morphism of categories over `𝒞` into a stack in groupoids. This is the extension `H : 𝒮' ⥤ 𝒳`
of `F` along `G`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def extendGroupoid : 𝒮' ⥤ 𝒳

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.extendGroupoid_comp_eq
declarations.doc: The extension `H : 𝒮' ⥤ 𝒳` is strictly over `𝒞`: `H ⋙ q = p'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extendGroupoid_comp_eq :
    extendGroupoid hp hp' hsp' hq hsq hG hF hmor hobj ⋙ q = p'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.unitGroupoid
declarations.doc: The 2-isomorphism `G ⋙ H ≅ F` between `F` and the composite of `G` with its extension.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def unitGroupoid :
    G ⋙ extendGroupoid hp hp' hsp' hq hsq hG hF hmor hobj ≅ F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Stackification.isHomLift_unitGroupoid_app
declarations.doc: Every component of the 2-isomorphism `G ⋙ H ≅ F` lies over an identity morphism of `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isHomLift_unitGroupoid_app (A : 𝒮) :
    q.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p.obj A)) ((unitGroupoid hp hp' hsp' hq hsq hG hF hmor hobj).hom.app A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces.hasPullbacks
declarations.doc:
The category of algebraic spaces over a scheme has fibre products: they are the presheaf
fibre products, which are again algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement: instance hasPullbacks : HasPullbacks (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasBinaryProducts_over_algebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
The category of algebraic spaces over `S` equipped with a morphism to a fixed algebraic space
`Z` has binary products, namely the fibre products over `Z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance hasBinaryProducts_over_algebraicSpace
    (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) : HasBinaryProducts (Over Z)
declarations.comment: products over a base algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043C, part (1).** A *pre-relation* from `R` to `U` is a morphism from `R` to
the product `U ⨯ U`.

This is stated for an arbitrary category with binary products because the two bases it is
taken over are different categories. Over a base algebraic space `Z` it is instantiated at
the slice `CategoryTheory.Over Z` of presheaves on the big fppf site, whose categorical
product is the fibre product `U ×_Z U`, which is the notion of the source; over an
algebraic space `B` it is instantiated at the slice `CategoryTheory.Over B` of the category
`AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces`, which is the shape the invariance notions of **Stacks
048E** in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/InvariantMorphisms.lean` are stated at.
declarations.statement: abbrev PreRelation (R U : C)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043C, part (1).** The *target* map of a pre-relation, its composite with the
first projection of the product.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev target : R ⟶ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043C, part (1).** The *source* map of a pre-relation, its composite with the
second projection of the product.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev source : R ⟶ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPreEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043C, part (3).** A pre-relation is a *pre-equivalence relation* when the
relation it induces on the `U`-valued points is an equivalence relation for every test
scheme over the base.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsPreEquivalenceRelation {R U : Over Z} (j : PreRelation R U) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalenceRelation_iff_mono_and_isPreEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043C, parts (2)-(4).** A pre-relation of algebraic spaces over `Z` is an
internal categorical equivalence relation exactly when it is a monomorphism and the
relation it induces on the points of every test scheme over `Z` is an equivalence
relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceRelation_iff_mono_and_isPreEquivalenceRelation
    {R U : Over Z} (j : PreRelation R U) :
    CategoryTheory.IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source ↔
      (CategoryTheory.Mono j ∧ IsPreEquivalenceRelation j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043D.** The restriction of a pre-relation along a morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` over `Z`,
that is the first projection of the pullback defining `restriction`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev restrict (g : U' ⟶ U) : PreRelation (restriction j g) U'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.isPreEquivalenceRelation_restrict
declarations.doc: **Stacks 043D.** Restriction preserves pre-equivalence relations.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPreEquivalenceRelation_restrict (g : U' ⟶ U) (hj : IsPreEquivalenceRelation j) :
    IsPreEquivalenceRelation (restrict j g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.isEquivalenceRelation_restrict
declarations.doc: **Stacks 043D.** Restriction preserves equivalence relations.
declarations.statement:
instance isEquivalenceRelation_restrict (g : U' ⟶ U)
    [hj : IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source] :
    IsEquivalenceRelation (restrict j g).target (restrict j g).source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043D.** The restriction of a pre-relation along a morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` over `Z`,
that is the first projection of the pullback defining `restriction`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev restrict (g : U' ⟶ U) : PreRelation (restriction j g) U'
declarations.comment: the restriction `R|_{U'}` of a pre-relation along `g : U' ⟶ U`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.isPreEquivalenceRelation_sourceTargetRel
declarations.doc:
A pre-equivalence relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` induces an equivalence relation on `|U|`:
`x` is related to `y` when some point `r` of `|R|` has `t(r) = x` and `s(r) = y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPreEquivalenceRelation_sourceTargetRel (hj : IsPreEquivalenceRelation j) :
    Equivalence
      (Function.SourceTargetRel
        (pointsMap B S hS R.left j.source.left)
        (pointsMap B S hS R.left j.target.left))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043H.** Group algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `B`.  An
object is a group object in presheaves over `B` whose underlying presheaf is an algebraic
space; morphisms are group-object morphisms over `B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev GroupAlgebraicSpace (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : 𝒞.Contains S) (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupOverStarGrpObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043I.** `B ×_S G` is a group object of presheaves over `B`, with the
pointwise group law of the given presheaf of groups.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance groupOverStarGrpObj (F : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{u}) :
    GrpObj (groupOverStar 𝒞 S hS B F)
declarations.comment: the group object over `B` attached to a presheaf of groups on the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043I.** The pullback of a group algebraic space over `B` along a
morphism `B' ⟶ B` of algebraic spaces is a group algebraic space over `B'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def GroupAlgebraicSpace.baseChange
    {B B' : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B}
    (hB' : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B') (f : B' ⟶ B)
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) :
    GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B' hB'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace.baseChange_obj_X
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043I.** The algebraic space underlying the pullback of a group
algebraic space is the fibre product of the original one with the new base.
declarations.statement:
theorem GroupAlgebraicSpace.baseChange_obj_X
    {B B' : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B}
    (hB' : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B') (f : B' ⟶ B)
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) :
    (GroupAlgebraicSpace.baseChange 𝒞 S hS hB' f G).obj.X =
      (Over.mk (pullback.snd G.obj.X.hom f) : Over B')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace.ofGroupSchemeInSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043I.** The group algebraic space `G_B = B ×_S G` over an algebraic
space `B` over `S` attached to a group scheme `G` over `S` belonging to the big fppf site: it is
the base change of `G`, regarded as a group algebraic space over the terminal algebraic space,
along the structure morphism of `B`.  Its points over a scheme `T` over `B` are the morphisms
`T ⟶ G` of schemes over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def GroupAlgebraicSpace.ofGroupSchemeInSite
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B)
    (G : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (hG : GrpObj ((toSchemeOver 𝒞 S hS).obj G)) :
    GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB
declarations.comment: the group algebraic space attached to a group scheme over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmooth_prod_fst_multiplicativeGroupULift
declarations.doc:
The structure morphism of the group algebraic space `Gₘ,B = B ×_{Spec ℤ} Gₘ` over an
arbitrary algebraic space `B` over `Spec ℤ` is a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_prod_fst_multiplicativeGroupULift
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) (contains_specULiftZ 𝒞))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) (contains_specULiftZ 𝒞) B) :
    IsSmooth 𝒞 (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) (contains_specULiftZ 𝒞)
      (prod.fst : B ⨯ (pointsOnSite 𝒞 (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) (contains_specULiftZ 𝒞)
        (multiplicativeGroupULiftSiteObject 𝒞)
        (multiplicativeGroupULiftSiteObjectGrpObj 𝒞) ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)
declarations.comment: the structure morphism of the multiplicative group algebraic space is smooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSiteObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043J.** The multiplicative group scheme over `S`, read as an object of
the big fppf site over `S`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def multiplicativeGroupSiteObject : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS
declarations.comment: the multiplicative group scheme as an object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043J.** The multiplicative group algebraic space
`Gₘ,B = B ×_S Gₘ,S` over an algebraic space `B` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def multiplicativeGroupSpace (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSpace_obj_X
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043J.** The algebraic space underlying the multiplicative group
algebraic space is the fibre product `B ×_S Gₘ,S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicativeGroupSpace_obj_X (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) :
    (multiplicativeGroupSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB).obj.X =
      (Over.mk (prod.fst :
        B ⨯ (multiplicativeGroupPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B) : Over B)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043J.** The group of points of the multiplicative group algebraic
space over a scheme `T` over `B` is the group of units in the global sections of `T`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (T : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (b : yoneda.obj T ⟶ B) :
    ((Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶
        Over.mk (prod.fst :
          B ⨯ (multiplicativeGroupPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)) ≃*
      (globalUnits S).obj (Opposite.op ((toSchemeOver 𝒞 S hS).obj T))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints_apply
declarations.doc:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints` reads a point through the second
projection of the fibre product and the canonical identification of **Stacks 022U**.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints_apply (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (T : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (b : yoneda.obj T ⟶ B)
    (x : (Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶
      Over.mk (prod.fst : B ⨯ (multiplicativeGroupPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)) :
    multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints 𝒞 S hS B T b x =
      (baseChangePointsIsoGlobalUnits S).hom.app
        (Opposite.op ((toSchemeOver 𝒞 S hS).obj T))
        (yonedaEquiv (x.left ≫ (prod.snd :
          B ⨯ (multiplicativeGroupPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ _)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints_naturality
declarations.doc:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints` is natural in the scheme over `B`,
so what is asserted is representability of the functor of global units and not a family of
unrelated group isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints_naturality (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (T U : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (f : T ⟶ U) (b : yoneda.obj U ⟶ B)
    (x : (Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶
      Over.mk (prod.fst : B ⨯ (multiplicativeGroupPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)) :
    multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints 𝒞 S hS B T (yoneda.map f ≫ b)
        ((Over.homMk (yoneda.map f) :
          (Over.mk (yoneda.map f ≫ b) : Over B) ⟶ Over.mk b) ≫ x) =
      (globalUnits S ⋙ forget GrpCat).map ((toSchemeOver 𝒞 S hS).map f).op
        (multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints 𝒞 S hS B U b x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySiteObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043K.** The group scheme `μₙ,S` of `n`-th roots of unity over `S`,
read as an object of the big fppf site over `S`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rootsOfUnitySiteObject : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS
declarations.comment: the roots-of-unity group scheme as an object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043K.** The group algebraic space `μₙ,B = B ×_S μₙ,S` of `n`-th roots
of unity over an algebraic space `B` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rootsOfUnitySpace [Fact (0 < n)] (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySpace_obj_X
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043K.** The algebraic space underlying the group algebraic space of
`n`-th roots of unity is the fibre product `B ×_S μₙ,S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnitySpace_obj_X [Fact (0 < n)] (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) :
    (rootsOfUnitySpace 𝒞 S hS n B hB).obj.X =
      (Over.mk (prod.fst :
        B ⨯ (rootsOfUnityPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS n ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B) : Over B)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySpacePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043K.** The group of points of the group algebraic space of `n`-th
roots of unity over a scheme `T` over `B` is the group of `n`-th roots of unity in the global
sections of `T`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rootsOfUnitySpacePoints [Fact (0 < n)]
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (T : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (b : yoneda.obj T ⟶ B) :
    ((Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶
        Over.mk (prod.fst :
          B ⨯ (rootsOfUnityPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS n ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)) ≃*
      (rootsOfUnityGroupOverFunctor n S).obj
        (Opposite.op ((toSchemeOver 𝒞 S hS).obj T))
declarations.comment: the functor of roots of unity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySpacePoints_apply
declarations.doc:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySpacePoints` reads a point through the second
projection of the fibre product and the canonical identification of **Stacks 040M**.
declarations.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnitySpacePoints_apply [Fact (0 < n)]
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (T : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (b : yoneda.obj T ⟶ B)
    (x : (Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶
      Over.mk (prod.fst : B ⨯ (rootsOfUnityPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS n ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)) :
    rootsOfUnitySpacePoints 𝒞 S hS n B T b x =
      (rootsOfUnityBaseChangeGroupPointsIso n S).hom.app
        (Opposite.op ((toSchemeOver 𝒞 S hS).obj T))
        (yonedaEquiv (x.left ≫ (prod.snd :
          B ⨯ (rootsOfUnityPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS n ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ _)))
declarations.comment: the functor of roots of unity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySpacePoints_naturality
declarations.doc:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rootsOfUnitySpacePoints` is natural in the scheme over `B`, so
what is asserted is representability of the functor of roots of unity and not a family of
unrelated group isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnitySpacePoints_naturality [Fact (0 < n)]
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (T U : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (f : T ⟶ U)
    (b : yoneda.obj U ⟶ B)
    (x : (Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶
      Over.mk (prod.fst : B ⨯ (rootsOfUnityPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS n ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)) :
    rootsOfUnitySpacePoints 𝒞 S hS n B T (yoneda.map f ≫ b)
        ((Over.homMk (yoneda.map f) :
          (Over.mk (yoneda.map f ≫ b) : Over B) ⟶ Over.mk b) ≫ x) =
      (rootsOfUnityGroupOverFunctor n S ⋙ forget GrpCat).map
        ((toSchemeOver 𝒞 S hS).map f).op
        (rootsOfUnitySpacePoints 𝒞 S hS n B U b x)
declarations.comment: the functor of roots of unity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.determinantGroupSpaceMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043N.** The determinant, as a morphism of group algebraic spaces
`GLₙ,B ⟶ Gₘ,B` over an algebraic space `B` over `S`.  It is the base change to `B` of the
determinant morphism of group schemes over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def determinantGroupSpaceMorphism (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) :
    generalLinearSpace 𝒞 S hS n B hB ⟶ multiplicativeGroupSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.determinantGroupSpaceMorphism_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043N.** The morphism over `B` underlying the determinant morphism of
group algebraic spaces is the product of the identity of `B` with the determinant morphism of
group schemes over `S`; that is, `det` on `GLₙ,B` is the base change of `det` on `GLₙ,S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantGroupSpaceMorphism_hom (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) :
    (determinantGroupSpaceMorphism 𝒞 S hS n B hB).hom.hom.hom =
      determinantSpaceHom 𝒞 S hS n B
declarations.comment: base change of the determinant morphism over the base scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.determinantSpaceHom_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043N.** On every scheme `T` over `B` the determinant morphism of group
algebraic spaces sends a point of `GLₙ,B`, that is an invertible `n × n` matrix over the global
sections of `T`, to its determinant, viewed as a global unit.  Its underlying morphism over `B`
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.determinantSpaceHom`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.determinantGroupSpaceMorphism_hom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem determinantSpaceHom_apply (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (T : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (b : yoneda.obj T ⟶ B)
    (x : (Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶
      Over.mk (prod.fst : B ⨯ (generalLinearPointsOnSite 𝒞 S hS n ⋙ forget GrpCat) ⟶ B)) :
    multiplicativeGroupSpacePoints 𝒞 S hS B T b (x ≫ determinantSpaceHom 𝒞 S hS n B) =
      Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det (generalLinearSpacePoints 𝒞 S hS n B T b x)

theorem constantGroupSpacePoints_apply (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EquivariantQuasicoherentModule
declarations.doc:
A `G`-equivariant quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module for an action `A` of a group algebraic space
`G` over `B` on an algebraic space `X` over `B`: a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` together with
a morphism `α : a^*ℱ ⟶ pr₁^*ℱ` of `𝒪_{G ×_B X}`-modules which satisfies the action cocycle
condition and is normalized along the unit section.
declarations.statement:
structure EquivariantQuasicoherentModule (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) (X : Over B)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left) (A : ModObj G.obj.X X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.equivariantQuasicoherentPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043U.**  The inverse image along a `G`-equivariant morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces over `B` is a functor from the `G`-equivariant quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-modules to
the `G`-equivariant quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules: it sends `(ℱ, α)` to `f^*ℱ` with the
reindexing of `α` along `1_G × f`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043W, part (1).** A groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `B` over
`S`: algebraic spaces of objects and of arrows, both over `B`, with source, target and
composition over `B`, whose evaluation at every test scheme is a groupoid.
declarations.statement:
structure GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.points_isGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043W, part (1), as a statement about the quintuple.** The defining property of the
quintuple `(U, R, s, t, c)` of a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B`: the source and the target
are morphisms over `B`, and at every test scheme `T` the quintuple of `T`-points is a groupoid
category. The latter is spelled out as: the `T`-points of the object space `U` are the objects of
a groupoid, an arrow `x ⟶ y` of that groupoid is the same thing as a `T`-point `a` of the arrow
space `R` with `s(a) = x` and `t(a) = y`, and the composite of two such arrows is the `T`-point
of `R` produced by the composition morphism `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem points_isGroupoid {C : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {hS : C.Contains S} {B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) (T : (BigFppfOver C S hS)ᵒᵖ) :
    G.source ≫ G.objectsToBase = G.arrowsToBase ∧
      G.target ≫ G.objectsToBase = G.arrowsToBase ∧
      ∀ (x y z : G.toGroupoidInFunctors.Evaluation T) (g : x ⟶ y) (f : y ⟶ z),
        (G.toGroupoidInFunctors.evaluationArrowEquiv T x z (g ≫ f)).1 =
          (composableToPullback G.source.hom G.target.hom ≫ G.comp.hom).app T
            ⟨((G.toGroupoidInFunctors.evaluationArrowEquiv T y z f).1,
                (G.toGroupoidInFunctors.evaluationArrowEquiv T x y g).1),
              (G.toGroupoidInFunctors.evaluationArrowEquiv T y z f).2.1.trans
                (G.toGroupoidInFunctors.evaluationArrowEquiv T x y g).2.2.symm⟩
declarations.comment: part (1): the T-points of the quintuple are a groupoid category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043W, part (2).** A morphism of groupoids in algebraic spaces over the same base: a
morphism of the underlying groupoids in presheaves whose maps on objects and on arrows are
morphisms over the base.
declarations.comment: part (2): morphism of groupoids in algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidPreRelation_isPreEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043X.** The pre-relation cut out by the target and source morphisms of a groupoid
in algebraic spaces is a pre-equivalence relation: on the points of every test scheme over the
base it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, because those points and the arrows between
them form a groupoid.
declarations.statement:
theorem groupoidPreRelation_isPreEquivalenceRelation
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    IsPreEquivalenceRelation (groupoidPreRelation G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_groupoid_of_isEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043Y.** An equivalence relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_B U` of algebraic spaces over an
algebraic space `B` extends to a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B`, and in exactly one way:
the source and the target of the groupoid are the two components of `j`, and its composition
law is then forced, an arrow being determined by its source and its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_groupoid_of_isEquivalenceRelation
    (j : PreRelation (Over.mk qR.hom) (Over.mk qU.hom))
    [IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source] :
    ∃! G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B, ExtendsRelation j G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_comp_source
declarations.doc:
For a groupoid in algebraic spaces, composition and the second projection out of the space of
composable pairs of arrows form a cartesian square with two copies of the source map: a
composable pair is determined by its second arrow together with its composite, and every arrow
and composite with matching sources arise from one, the first arrow of the pair being the
composite preceded by the inverse of the second.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_comp_source {B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    IsPullback G.comp
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd G.source.hom G.target.hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct C S hS G.source G.target ⟶ G.arrows)
      G.source G.source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_fst_comp
declarations.doc:
For a groupoid in algebraic spaces, the first projection out of the space of composable pairs
of arrows and composition form a cartesian square with two copies of the target map: a
composable pair is determined by its first arrow together with its composite, and every arrow
and composite with matching targets arise from one, the second arrow of the pair being the
composite preceded by the inverse of the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_fst_comp {B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    IsPullback
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst G.source.hom G.target.hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct C S hS G.source G.target ⟶ G.arrows)
      G.comp G.target G.target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0441.**  A quasi-coherent module on a groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)`
over `A`: a quasi-coherent `𝒪_U`-module `ℱ` together with a morphism `α : t^*ℱ ⟶ s^*ℱ` of
`𝒪_R`-modules which satisfies the cocycle condition on the space of composable pairs of arrows
and restricts to the identity along the unit.
declarations.statement: structure QuasicoherentModule (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidQuasicoherentPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0442.**  The inverse image along a morphism `f` of groupoids in algebraic spaces is
a functor `QCoh(U', R', s', t', c') ⥤ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)`: it sends a quasi-coherent module
`(ℱ, α)` on the target groupoid to the inverse image `(f^*ℱ, f^*α)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidQuasicoherentPullbackObj`, and a morphism to the inverse image
of the underlying morphism of modules on the spaces of objects.
declarations.statement:
def groupoidQuasicoherentPullback :
    QuasicoherentModule B S hS G' ⥤ QuasicoherentModule B S hS G
declarations.comment: the inverse image functor on quasi-coherent modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidModulePullbackTransition_unit
declarations.doc:
**The unit law for the transition morphism of the inverse image.**  If the transition
morphism `α` of a module on the target groupoid restricts along the unit arrow to the canonical
identification of the two inverse images, then so does the transition morphism of the inverse
image along the unit arrow of the source groupoid.

This is the unit law of Stacks 0441 for the pair `(f^*ℱ, f^*α)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem groupoidModulePullbackTransition_unit (φ : Hom G G')
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS G'.objects.1 G'.objects.2)
    (α : (modulePullback B S hS G'.target).obj F ⟶ (modulePullback B S hS G'.source).obj F)
    (hunit : groupoidPullbackTransition B S hS G' F α (identityArrow G') =
      pullbackTransport F ((identityArrow_comp_target G').trans
        (identityArrow_comp_source G').symm)) :
    groupoidPullbackTransition B S hS G ((modulePullback B S hS φ.objectsMap).obj F)
        (groupoidModulePullbackTransition B S hS φ F α) (identityArrow G) =
      pullbackTransport ((modulePullback B S hS φ.objectsMap).obj F)
        ((identityArrow_comp_target G).trans (identityArrow_comp_source G).symm)
declarations.comment: the unit law for the transition morphism of the inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidModulePullbackTransition_cocycle
declarations.doc:
**The cocycle law for the transition morphism of the inverse image.**  If the transition
morphism `α` of a module on the target groupoid satisfies the cocycle law on the space of
composable pairs of arrows of the target groupoid, then the transition morphism of the inverse
image satisfies it on the space of composable pairs of arrows of the source groupoid.

This is the cocycle law of Stacks 0441 for the pair `(f^*ℱ, f^*α)`.  Flattened along the map on
objects, both sides become the corresponding sides of the law for `α` at the three morphisms the
map on composable pairs carries the composition and the two projections to.
declarations.statement:
theorem groupoidModulePullbackTransition_cocycle (φ : Hom G G')
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS G'.objects.1 G'.objects.2)
    (α : (modulePullback B S hS G'.target).obj F ⟶ (modulePullback B S hS G'.source).obj F)
    (hcocycle : groupoidPullbackTransition B S hS G' F α G'.comp =
      groupoidTransitionComposite B S hS G' F α) :
    groupoidPullbackTransition B S hS G ((modulePullback B S hS φ.objectsMap).obj F)
        (groupoidModulePullbackTransition B S hS φ F α) G.comp =
      groupoidTransitionComposite B S hS G ((modulePullback B S hS φ.objectsMap).obj F)
        (groupoidModulePullbackTransition B S hS φ F α)
declarations.comment: the cocycle law for the transition morphism of the inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.actionGroupoid
declarations.doc:
The action groupoid `(X, G ×_B X, pr₁, a, m)` of an action `A` of a group algebraic space `G`
over `B` on an algebraic space `X` over `B`, with the projection as its source and the action
morphism as its target.

At the trivial action of `G` on the base this groupoid has arrow space `G ×_B B`, not `G`; the
groupoid `(Spec k, G, p, p, m)` of Stacks 06DZ, with arrow space `G` itself, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidOfGroupOverField`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev actionGroupoid (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) (X : Over B)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left) (A : ModObj G.obj.X X) :
    GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces 𝒞 S hS ⟨B, hB⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidOfAction
declarations.doc:
A group action gives the action groupoid,
with the stated object and arrow spaces and all five structure maps.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def groupoidOfAction :
    ActionGroupoidConstruction B G X hG hX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.actionGroupoidModulesComparison
declarations.doc:
The rule `(ℱ, α) ↦ (ℱ, α)` is a fully faithful and essentially surjective functor from the
`G`-equivariant quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules of Stacks 043T to the quasi-coherent modules of
Stacks 0441 on the action groupoid of Stacks 0444, leaving the underlying quasi-coherent module,
the transition morphism and the morphisms unchanged.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionGroupoidModulesComparison (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB)
    (X : Over B) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left) (A : ModObj G.obj.X X) :
    ActionGroupoidModulesComparison (hB := hB) G X hX A (actionGroupoid G X hX A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.actionGroupoidModulesEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The rule `(ℱ, α) ↦ (ℱ, α)` is an equivalence between the category of `G`-equivariant
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules of Stacks 043T and the category of quasi-coherent modules of
Stacks 0441 on the action groupoid of Stacks 0444.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionGroupoidModulesEquivalence (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB)
    (X : Over B) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left) (A : ModObj G.obj.X X) :
    EquivariantQuasicoherentModule (hB := hB) G X hX A ≌
      QuasicoherentModule 𝒞 S hS (actionGroupoid G X hX A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerGroupStructure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0447.** The stabilizer of a groupoid in algebraic spaces is a group object in the
slice over the object space, with groupoid composition as multiplication.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stabilizerGroupStructure (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    { h : GrpObj (stabilizer G) // IsStabilizerGroupStructure G h }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerGroup
declarations.doc:
The stabilizer group algebraic space over the object space of a groupoid in algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stabilizerGroup (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.objects.obj G.objects.property
declarations.comment: the stabilizer as a group algebraic space over the object space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerAction
declarations.doc:
The stabilizer of a groupoid in algebraic spaces acts on its arrow space over the object space,
and the action is groupoid composition on generalized points.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stabilizerAction (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    { h : ModObj (stabilizer G) (arrowsOverTarget G) // IsStabilizerAction G h }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrict_isRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 044B.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B` and let
`g : U' ⟶ U` be a morphism of algebraic spaces. Form the fibre product squares
`P₁ = U' ×_{g, U, t} R` (projections `pU`, `pR`), `P₂ = R ×_{s, U, g} U'` (projections `qR`,
`qU`), and `R' = P₁ ×_{pR, R, qR} P₂` (projections `a`, `b`), and put `t' = a ≫ pU`,
`s' = b ≫ qU`. Then the restriction `(restrict G g).groupoid` is a groupoid in algebraic spaces
over `B` whose space of objects is `U'` (over `B` through `g`), whose space of arrows is `R'`
(over `B` through `R`), whose source and target are `s'` and `t'`, and whose composition law
`c' : R' ×_{s', U', t'} R' ⟶ R'` keeps the target of the first arrow and the source of the second
and composes the two underlying arrows by `c`. The maps `g : U' ⟶ U` and `a ≫ pR : R' ⟶ R` are
the two components of the morphism `(restrict G g).hom` of groupoids in algebraic spaces over `B`.

Moreover, for every scheme `T` of the site, the functor of groupoids
`(U'(T), R'(T), s', t', c') ⟶ (U(T), R(T), s, t, c)` is the restriction of `(U(T), R(T), s, t, c)`
via `U'(T) ⟶ U(T)`: an element of `R'(T)` is exactly a triple `(x, r, y)` with `x, y ∈ U'(T)`,
`r ∈ R(T)`, `t(r) = g(x)` and `s(r) = g(y)`, with `t'` and `s'` the outer projections and the
composite of `(x, r, y)` and `(y, r'', z)` equal to `(x, c(r, r''), z)`; the functor is `g` on
objects and is fully faithful.

The same holds for the `T`-points over `B`, in the source's sense of a scheme `T` over `B`: for a
scheme `T` of the site and a point `b ∈ B(T)`, the groupoid `(U'(T), R'(T), s', t', c')` of
`T`-points of the restriction lying over `b` maps to the groupoid `(U(T), R(T), s, t, c)` of
`T`-points of `G` lying over `b`, and this functor is the restriction along `U'(T) ⟶ U(T)`: an
arrow over `b` is exactly a triple `(x, r, y)` over `b` as above, the composite of two arrows over
`b` lies over `b` and is computed as above, and the functor, which is `g` on objects and the
functor on all `T`-points on arrows, is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restrict_isRestriction
    {C : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : C.Contains S}
    {B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    {U' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) :
    let H := (restrict G g).groupoid
    let φ := (restrict G g).hom
    ∃ (P₁ : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (pU : P₁ ⟶ U') (pR : P₁ ⟶ G.arrows)
      (P₂ : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (qR : P₂ ⟶ G.arrows) (qU : P₂ ⟶ U')
      (a : H.arrows ⟶ P₁) (b : H.arrows ⟶ P₂),
      IsPullback pU pR g G.target ∧ IsPullback qR qU G.source g ∧ IsPullback a b pR qR ∧
      H.objects = U' ∧ H.target = a ≫ pU ∧ H.source = b ≫ qU ∧
      H.objectsToBase = g ≫ G.objectsToBase ∧
      H.arrowsToBase = (a ≫ pR) ≫ G.arrowsToBase ∧
      H.comp ≫ H.target = fiberProductFst H.source H.target ≫ H.target ∧
      H.comp ≫ H.source = fiberProductSnd H.source H.target ≫ H.source ∧
      (∃ m : AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct C S hS H.source H.target ⟶
          AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct C S hS G.source G.target,
        m ≫ fiberProductFst G.source G.target = fiberProductFst H.source H.target ≫ a ≫ pR ∧
        m ≫ fiberProductSnd G.source G.target = fiberProductSnd H.source H.target ≫ a ≫ pR ∧
        H.comp ≫ a ≫ pR = m ≫ G.comp) ∧
      φ.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects = g.hom ∧
      φ.toGroupoidHom.mapArrows = (a ≫ pR).hom ∧
      (∀ T : (BigFppfOver C S hS)ᵒᵖ,
        (∀ (x y : U'.obj.obj T) (r : G.arrows.obj.obj T),
          G.target.hom.app T r = g.hom.app T x → G.source.hom.app T r = g.hom.app T y →
          ∃! z : H.arrows.obj.obj T, H.target.hom.app T z = x ∧
            (a ≫ pR).hom.app T z = r ∧ H.source.hom.app T z = y) ∧
        (∀ (z w : H.arrows.obj.obj T) (h : H.source.hom.app T z = H.target.hom.app T w)
          (h' : G.source.hom.app T ((a ≫ pR).hom.app T z) =
            G.target.hom.app T ((a ≫ pR).hom.app T w)),
          H.target.hom.app T (H.toGroupoidInFunctors.compose T z w h) =
              H.target.hom.app T z ∧
            (a ≫ pR).hom.app T (H.toGroupoidInFunctors.compose T z w h) =
              G.toGroupoidInFunctors.compose T ((a ≫ pR).hom.app T z)
                ((a ≫ pR).hom.app T w) h' ∧
            H.source.hom.app T (H.toGroupoidInFunctors.compose T z w h) =
              H.source.hom.app T w) ∧
        (∀ x : U'.obj.obj T, (φ.toGroupoidHom.evaluation T).obj x = g.hom.app T x) ∧
        Nonempty (φ.toGroupoidHom.evaluation T).FullyFaithful) ∧
      ∀ (T : (BigFppfOver C S hS)ᵒᵖ) (b : B.obj.obj T),
        (∀ (x y : U'.obj.obj T) (r : G.arrows.obj.obj T),
          H.objectsToBase.hom.app T x = b → H.objectsToBase.hom.app T y = b →
          G.arrowsToBase.hom.app T r = b →
          G.target.hom.app T r = g.hom.app T x → G.source.hom.app T r = g.hom.app T y →
          ∃! z : H.arrows.obj.obj T, H.arrowsToBase.hom.app T z = b ∧
            H.target.hom.app T z = x ∧ (a ≫ pR).hom.app T z = r ∧
            H.source.hom.app T z = y) ∧
