declarations.name: Module.Flat.injective_and_flat_quotient_range_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings with `S` essentially of finite presentation
over `R`, let `𝔪` be the maximal ideal of `R`, and let `u : M → N` be a map of `S`-modules with
`M`, `N` of finite presentation over `S` and `N` flat over `R`. If the induced map
`ū : M/𝔪M → N/𝔪N` is injective, then `u` is injective and `N/u(M)` is flat over `R`.

Here `M/𝔪M` is `M ⧸ 𝔪 • ⊤` and `ū` is the canonical `Submodule.mapQ`, which sends the class of `x`
to the class of `u x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.injective_and_flat_quotient_range_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal
    {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S N] [Module.Flat R N]
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) (u : M →ₗ[S] N)
    (hu :
      Function.Injective
        (Submodule.mapQ (maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R M))
          (maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R N)) (u.restrictScalars R)
          (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal R) (u.restrictScalars R)))) :
    Function.Injective u ∧ Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range u)
declarations.comment:
`M/𝔪M` is `M ⧸ 𝔪 • (⊤ : Submodule R M)` and `ū` the canonical `Submodule.mapQ` of
`u`. Hypothesis (1) is `RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation` (Definition 00QM (2)), Mathlib
having no such predicate. The cokernel `N/u(M)` is `N ⧸ LinearMap.range u`, and the two
conclusions are conjoined; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_and_flat_quotient_span_of_isSMulRegular_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 046Z with both quotients taken by ideals.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of
local rings which is essentially of finite presentation and makes `S` flat over `R`. If `a ∈ S`
is a nonzerodivisor on the fibre `S ⧸ 𝔪S`, then `a` is a nonzerodivisor on `S` and `S ⧸ (a)` is
again flat over `R`.

This is the `M = S` case of
`Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_and_flat_quotient_smul_of_isSMulRegular_maximalIdeal`, restated with
the fibre and the quotient written as quotients of the ring by ideals rather than as quotients of
the module `S` by `I • ⊤`. The two agree because extending an ideal to the top submodule of the
ring returns the ideal, and that identification is an equality of submodules, so the hypothesis
and the conclusion are transported along `Submodule.quotEquivOfEq` rather than compared as
types.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_and_flat_quotient_span_of_isSMulRegular_quotient
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [Module.Flat R S]
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) {a : S}
    (ha : IsSMulRegular (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R)) a) :
    IsSMulRegular S a ∧ Module.Flat R (S ⧸ Ideal.span {a})
declarations.comment: the case M := S, spelled with ring quotients by ideals

declarations.name: Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_and_flat_quotient_smul_of_isSMulRegular_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 046Z.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings with `S` essentially of
finite presentation over `R`, let `𝔪` be the maximal ideal of `R`, and let `M` be an `S`-module of
finite presentation which is flat over `R`. If `f ∈ S` is a nonzerodivisor on the fibre `M/𝔪M`,
then `f` is a nonzerodivisor on `M` and `M/fM` is flat over `R`.

The source is the case `M = S`: `f` is a nonzerodivisor in `S` and `S/fS` is flat over `R`. Here
`𝔪M` is `𝔪S • ⊤` and `fM` is `Ideal.span {f} • ⊤`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_and_flat_quotient_smul_of_isSMulRegular_maximalIdeal
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S M] [Module.Flat R M]
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) {f : S}
    (hf :
      IsSMulRegular (M ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S M))) f) :
    IsSMulRegular M f ∧ Module.Flat R (M ⧸ (Ideal.span {f} • (⊤ : Submodule S M)))
declarations.comment:
Stated in module form (the source's case is `M := S`), with `𝔪M` spelled
`Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S M)` and `fM` spelled
`Ideal.span {f} • ⊤`, and "nonzerodivisor" spelled `IsSMulRegular`. Hypothesis (1) is
`RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation` (Definition 00QM (2)), Mathlib having no such predicate.
The two conclusions are conjoined; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.isRegular_and_flat_quotient_ofList_of_isRegular_map_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0470.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings, essentially of finite
presentation and flat, and let `𝔪` be the maximal ideal of `R`. If `f₁, …, f_c ∈ S` are such that
their images `f̄₁, …, f̄_c` form a regular sequence in `S/𝔪S`, then `f₁, …, f_c` is a regular
sequence in `S` and each quotient `S/(f₁, …, f_i)` is flat over `R`.

This is the case `M = S` of
`Module.Flat.isRegular_and_flat_quotient_ofList_smul_of_isRegular_maximalIdeal`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.isRegular_and_flat_quotient_ofList_of_isRegular_map_maximalIdeal
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [Module.Flat R S]
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) (fs : List S)
    (hfs :
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
        (fs.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))))) :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular S fs ∧ ∀ i, Module.Flat R (S ⧸ Ideal.ofList (fs.take i))
declarations.comment:
The sequence is a `List S` and `(f₁, …, f_i)` is `Ideal.ofList (fs.take i)`, for
every `i` (beyond the length `c` the quotient is `S/(f₁, …, f_c)`). "Regular sequence" is
Mathlib's `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, which is Definition 00LF verbatim (nonvanishing clause
included), and the images `f̄_i` in `S/𝔪S` are `fs.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk _)`. Hypothesis (1) is
`RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation`, Definition 00QM (2). The two conclusions are
conjoined.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_rTensor_subtype_injective_of_flat_quotient_of_essentiallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
The local criterion for flatness for local maps essentially of finite presentation.
Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings with `S` essentially of finite presentation over
`R`, let `I ≠ R` be an ideal of `R` and let `M` be an `S`-module of finite presentation. If
`Tor₁^R(R/I, M) = 0` and `M/IM` is flat over `R/I`, then `M` is flat over `R`.

Here the Tor hypothesis appears in the form of Remark 00M6, as the injectivity of
`I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M`, and `M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤` with its canonical `R ⧸ I`-module structure. No ring
is assumed Noetherian; the Noetherian variant is 00ML.
declarations.statement:
public theorem of_rTensor_subtype_injective_of_flat_quotient_of_essentiallyOfFinitePresentation
    {R : Type u} (S : Type v) (M : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M]
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≠ ⊤)
    (hTor : Function.Injective (I.subtype.rTensor M))
    (hflat : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))) :
    Module.Flat R M
declarations.comment:
The hypothesis `Tor_1^R(M, R/I) = 0` is stated in the form Remark 00M6 identifies it
with, the injectivity of `I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M`, as in the Noetherian sibling 00ML; this is the form
the source's proof produces and the form 00ML consumes, and unlike `Tor_1` it puts `R` and `M` in
no common universe. Hypothesis (1) is `RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation` (Definition
00QM (2)), Mathlib having no such predicate. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.Immersion.epi_immersionConormalSheafMap
declarations.doc:
For a cartesian square of schemes whose horizontal maps `i` and `i'` are immersions, the
canonical map `f^* 𝒞_{Z'/X'} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of conormal sheaves is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_immersionConormalSheafMap (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion i']
    (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X') (sq : IsPullback i f g i') :
    Epi (immersionConormalSheafMap i i' f g (toShHom_square sq.w))

declarations.name: Stacks.Immersion.isIso_immersionConormalSheafMap_of_flat
declarations.doc:
For a cartesian square of schemes whose horizontal maps `i` and `i'` are immersions and
whose ambient vertical map `g` is flat, the canonical map `f^* 𝒞_{Z'/X'} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of
[Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_immersionConormalSheafMap_of_flat (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X')
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion i']
    (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X') [Flat g] (sq : IsPullback i f g i') :
    IsIso (Stacks.Immersion.immersionConormalSheafMap i i' f g
      (Stacks.Immersion.toShHom_square sq.w))

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**The flat base change of the target deformation is compatible with the base, along the other
factorisation of the same composite square.** The square carrying the special fibre of `Q` over
the closed point of `Spec A` also factors through `Spec B`: the special-fibre square of `Q`
followed by the square of closed points
`Deformation.Examples.residueSpecMap_naturality`. Reading the canonical map of
[Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] along *that* factorisation makes
`Deformation.Examples.deformationConormalBaseChangeIso` at `Q` the compatible datum, the map
coming from the base being the conormal map
`Deformation.Examples.residueConormalMap` of `φ.base`.

Together with `Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalMap` this is
the naturality of flat base change for the conormal sheaf of a special fibre in the base object
of `𝒞_Λ`: the two statements are the two readings of one canonical map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalBaseChangeIso (φ : P ⟶ Q) :
    IsBaseCompatibleConormalMap Q.specialMap (residueSpecMap Q.base) (residueSpecMap P.base)
      (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (baseSpecMap φ.base) (Q.toBase ≫ baseSpecMap φ.base) X.hom
      (residueSpecMap_comp_baseSpecMap' φ.base)
      (square_comp Q.specialCartesian.w (residueSpecMap_comp_baseSpecMap' φ.base))
      (deformationConormalBaseChangeIso Q).hom
declarations.comment: naturality in the base object: the flat base change for the conormal sheaf of the special fibre of the target of an arrow of deformations is the conormal datum compatible with the base along the factorisation through the spectrum of the source's base object, the map on the base being the conormal map of the morphism of base objects. This is one of the two readings of a single canonical map of Tag 01R4, not a computation of either reading on sections

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.deformationConormalBaseChangeIso_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The flat base change of the conormal sheaf of a special fibre is natural in the base object
of `𝒞_Λ`.** For an arrow `φ : P ⟶ Q` of deformations of `X` the square

`p_X^* 𝒞_{Spec k/Spec A} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/P.scheme}`, `p_X^* 𝒞_{Spec k/Spec B} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/Q.scheme}`

commutes, the horizontal maps being
`Deformation.Examples.deformationConormalBaseChangeIso` and the vertical ones the pullback along
`p_X` of the conormal map of `φ.base` and the conormal map of `φ`. **This is the statement that
the conormal map of an arrow of deformations corresponds, under flat base change, to the conormal
map of the morphism of base objects.**

Both maps of conormal sheaves are written in the unstripped shape [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4]
produces — that is, out of the pullback along the edge on the closed subschemes, which is an
identity — so each composite begins with the comparison
`RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullbackComp` of the pullback along a composite with the
composite of the pullbacks, and the two composites `𝟙_X ≫ p_X` and `p_X ≫ 𝟙_{Spec k}` of those
edges differ by a `CategoryTheory.eqToHom`. The stripped maps are
`Deformation.Examples.deformationConormalMap` and
`Deformation.Examples.residueConormalMap`.

The proof is the two factorisations
`Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalBaseChangeIso` and
`Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalMap` of the one canonical
map, compared by `Stacks.Immersion.immersionConormalSheafMap_congr` along the equality of edges;
the right-hand edges of the two squares over `Spec A` are identified by the cartesian square
`Deformation.Examples.SchemeDeformationCategory.Hom.cartesian` of the arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem deformationConormalBaseChangeIso_naturality (φ : P ⟶ Q) :
    (modulePullbackComp X.hom.toLRSHom.toShHom
            (Scheme.Hom.toLRSHom (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).toShHom).hom.app
          (immersionConormalSheaf (residueSpecMap P.base)) ≫
        (modulePullback X.hom.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
            (immersionConormalSheafMap (residueSpecMap Q.base) (residueSpecMap P.base)
              (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (baseSpecMap φ.base)
              (toShHom_square (residueSpecMap_comp_baseSpecMap' φ.base))) ≫
          (deformationConormalBaseChangeIso Q).hom =
      eqToHom (congrArg (fun p : X.left ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) =>
            (modulePullback p.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
              (immersionConormalSheaf (residueSpecMap P.base)))
            ((Category.id_comp X.hom).trans (Category.comp_id X.hom).symm).symm) ≫
        (modulePullbackComp (Scheme.Hom.toLRSHom (𝟙 X.left)).toShHom
              X.hom.toLRSHom.toShHom).hom.app
            (immersionConormalSheaf (residueSpecMap P.base)) ≫
          (modulePullback (Scheme.Hom.toLRSHom (𝟙 X.left)).toShHom).map
              (deformationConormalBaseChangeIso P).hom ≫
            immersionConormalSheafMap Q.specialMap P.specialMap (𝟙 X.left) φ.map
              (toShHom_square (specialMap_comp_map φ))
declarations.comment: naturality of flat base change for the conormal sheaf of a special fibre in the base object: for an arrow of deformations, the pullback along the structure morphism of the conormal map of the morphism of base objects, followed by the flat base change of the target, is the flat base change of the source followed by the conormal map of the arrow -- up to the eqToHom comparing the two unit composites of the edge on the closed subschemes. Both conormal maps are the canonical maps of Tag 01R4; nothing is computed on sections and the map on the base is NOT identified with the map of maximal ideals

declarations.name: Ideal.bijective_cotangentBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0473], the flat case in the affine picture.** Let `S` be a flat
`R`-algebra, let `I` be an ideal of `R` and let `I S` be the ideal of `S` generated by its image.
Then the canonical map

`I ⧸ I ^ 2 ⊗[R] S ⟶ I S ⧸ (I S) ^ 2`

is an isomorphism.  This is the commutative algebra statement the proof of that tag reduces to;
the sheaf-level statement for a cartesian square of immersions of schemes is not proved here, and
the surjectivity half of the tag is `Stacks.Immersion.epi_immersionConormalSheafMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_cotangentBaseChange [Module.Flat R S] :
    Function.Bijective (I.cotangentBaseChange S)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.isSplitEpi_differentialsMapOver_of_retraction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0474], a left inverse splits the second arrow.**  For an immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of schemes over `S` admitting a left inverse `g : X ⟶ Z` over `S`, the second arrow
`i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S}` of the conormal sequence of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] is a split epimorphism.

Together with `Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.differentialsMapOver_epi` this is the right-hand half
of the source's conclusion. Split exactness of the three-term sequence, which this statement
supplies the section for, is
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.conormalShortComplexSplitting_of_retraction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSplitEpi_differentialsMapOver_of_retraction (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] (p : X ⟶ S)
    (g : X ⟶ Z) (hg : i ≫ g = 𝟙 Z) (hgS : g ≫ (i ≫ p) = p) :
    IsSplitEpi (relativeDifferentialsMap i p (i ≫ p) (𝟙 S) (by simp))
declarations.comment: a left inverse splits the second arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.forall_exists_isSplitEpi_restrict_of_localRetraction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0474], a local left inverse locally splits the second arrow.**  Let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of schemes over `S` which *locally has a left inverse*: every point
`z` of `Z` has an open neighbourhood `V` which `i` maps into an open `U` of `X`, the restricted
morphism `j : V ⟶ U` admitting a left inverse `g : U ⟶ V` over `S`.  Then the second arrow
`i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S}` of the conormal sequence of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] restricts to a split
epimorphism on a neighbourhood of every point of `Z`.

This is the "(locally)" reading of the source's hypothesis and conclusion, on the second arrow.
Local split exactness of the three-term sequence is
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.forall_exists_nonempty_splitting_restrict_of_localRetraction`,
which combines this splitting with the short exactness
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.conormalShortComplex_shortExact_of_localRetraction` proved under
the same hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_exists_isSplitEpi_restrict_of_localRetraction
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] (p : X ⟶ S)
    (hloc : ∀ z : Z, ∃ (V : Z.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (j : V.toScheme ⟶ U.toScheme)
      (g : U.toScheme ⟶ V.toScheme), z ∈ V ∧ V.ι ≫ i = j ≫ U.ι ∧ j ≫ g = 𝟙 V.toScheme ∧
        g ≫ (V.ι ≫ i ≫ p) = U.ι ≫ p) :
    ∀ z : Z, ∃ V : Z.Opens, z ∈ V ∧
      IsSplitEpi ((Scheme.Modules.pullback V.ι).map
        (relativeDifferentialsMap i p (i ≫ p) (𝟙 S) (by simp)))
declarations.comment: a local left inverse locally splits the second arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.conormalShortComplex_shortExact_of_localRetraction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0474], short exactness under a *local* left inverse.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an
immersion of schemes over `p : X ⟶ S` which *locally has a left inverse*: every point `z` of `Z`
has an open neighbourhood `V` which `i` maps into an open `U` of `X`, the restricted morphism
`j : V ⟶ U` admitting a left inverse `g : U ⟶ V` over `S`. Then the conormal sequence
`0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0` of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] is short exact.

This is the exactness half of the source's *locally split exact* under the source's local
hypothesis, and it is global: being a monomorphism is a stalkwise condition, so a left inverse
near each point is enough. The splitting half under the same hypothesis is
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.forall_exists_isSplitEpi_restrict_of_localRetraction`, which
splits the second arrow over a neighbourhood of every point; the two combine into the local
split exactness
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.forall_exists_nonempty_splitting_restrict_of_localRetraction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalShortComplex_shortExact_of_localRetraction {Z X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] (p : X ⟶ S)
    (hloc : ∀ z : Z, ∃ (V : Z.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (j : V.toScheme ⟶ U.toScheme)
      (g : U.toScheme ⟶ V.toScheme), z ∈ V ∧ V.ι ≫ i = j ≫ U.ι ∧ j ≫ g = 𝟙 V.toScheme ∧
        g ≫ (V.ι ≫ i ≫ p) = U.ι ≫ p) :
    (conormalShortComplex i p).ShortExact
declarations.comment:
the local clause: under a local left inverse — every point of Z has a
neighbourhood V mapping into an open U of X with the restricted morphism admitting a left
inverse over S — the sequence 0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0 of Tag 01UZ is short
exact. This is exactness, globally; the local splitting under the same hypothesis is
forall_exists_nonempty_splitting_restrict_of_localRetraction

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.conormalShortComplexSplitting_of_retraction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0474], a left inverse splits the sequence.** For an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of
schemes over `p : X ⟶ S` admitting a left inverse `g : X ⟶ Z` over `S`, the conormal sequence
`0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0` of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] is *split* short exact: a
splitting is produced, consisting of a retraction of the first arrow and a section of the second
whose composites add up to the identity of `i^*Ω_{X/S}`.

The section of the second arrow is the source's `i^*c_g`, through
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.isSplitEpi_differentialsMapOver_of_retraction`; the sequence is
short exact by `Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.conormalShortComplex_shortExact_of_retraction`, and
a short exact sequence whose epimorphism has a section is split.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalShortComplexSplitting_of_retraction {Z X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] (p : X ⟶ S) (g : X ⟶ Z) (hg : i ≫ g = 𝟙 Z) (hgS : g ≫ (i ≫ p) = p) :
    (conormalShortComplex i p).Splitting
declarations.comment:
a left inverse over S splits the sequence 0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0
of Tag 01UZ: a splitting is produced, so in particular the sequence is short exact. The
hypothesis is a global left inverse g : X ⟶ Z with i ≫ g = 𝟙 Z and g ≫ (i ≫ p) = p; the
source's parenthetical local clause is
forall_exists_nonempty_splitting_restrict_of_localRetraction

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.forall_exists_nonempty_splitting_restrict_of_localRetraction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0474], a local left inverse makes the conormal sequence locally split
exact.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of schemes over `p : X ⟶ S` which *locally has a left
inverse*: every point `z` of `Z` has an open neighbourhood `V` which `i` maps into an open `U` of
`X`, the restricted morphism `j : V ⟶ U` admitting a left inverse `g : U ⟶ V` over `S`. Then
every point of `Z` has an open neighbourhood `V` over which the conormal sequence
`0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0` of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] is *split* short exact: the
sequence restricted to `V` carries a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`.

This is the source's *(locally) split exact* under the source's *(locally) has a left inverse*.
The neighbourhood produced is the one the hypothesis supplies, and the splitting over it is
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.conormalShortComplexRestrictSplitting_of_localRetraction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_exists_nonempty_splitting_restrict_of_localRetraction
    {Z X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] (p : X ⟶ S)
    (hloc : ∀ z : Z, ∃ (V : Z.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (j : V.toScheme ⟶ U.toScheme)
      (g : U.toScheme ⟶ V.toScheme), z ∈ V ∧ V.ι ≫ i = j ≫ U.ι ∧ j ≫ g = 𝟙 V.toScheme ∧
        g ≫ (V.ι ≫ i ≫ p) = U.ι ≫ p) :
    ∀ z : Z, ∃ V : Z.Opens, z ∈ V ∧
      Nonempty (((conormalShortComplex i p).map
        (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι)).Splitting)
declarations.comment:
the parenthetical local clause: under a local left inverse — every point of Z has
a neighbourhood V mapping into an open U of X with the restricted morphism j : V ⟶ U admitting a
left inverse over S — the sequence 0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0 of Tag 01UZ is
*locally split exact*: every point of Z has an open neighbourhood V over which the restricted
sequence carries a ShortComplex.Splitting, so both a retraction of the first arrow and a section
of the second are produced over V. This is the full (locally) reading of the source's hypothesis
and conclusion; the global reading is conormalShortComplexSplitting_of_retraction

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceSplit.isIso_conormalDifferential_of_section
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0474], the conormal sheaf of a section.** For a section `s : S ⟶ X` of
`p : X ⟶ S` the first arrow `𝒞_{S/X} ⟶ s^*Ω_{X/S}` of the conormal sequence of
[Stacks, Tag 01UZ] is an isomorphism.

A section is an immersion whose left inverse over `S` is `p` itself, so the sequence of `s` is
short exact; and `Ω_{S/S}` is a zero object by [Stacks, Tag 01UY], `s ≫ p = 𝟙 S` being a
monomorphism. The first arrow is therefore both a monomorphism and, the sequence being exact at
the middle term with zero on the right, an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conormalDifferential_of_section {X S : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) (s : S ⟶ X)
    (hs : s ≫ p = 𝟙 S) :
    haveI := isImmersion_of_section p s hs
    IsIso (conormalDifferential s p)
declarations.comment:
the source's final assertion: for a section s of p, the first arrow
𝒞_{S/X} ⟶ s^*Ω_{X/S} of the sequence of Tag 01UZ, which is induced by d_{X/S}, is an
isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramifiedAt_iff_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0475, the base-change half, pointwise.** Let
```
X' → X
↓    ↓
Y' → Y
```
be a cartesian diagram of schemes with `f : X ⟶ Y` locally of finite type, and let
`f' : X' ⟶ Y'` be the base change of `f` along `g : Y' ⟶ Y`. A point `x'` of `X'` is a point of
unramifiedness of `f'` if and only if its image `g' x'` in `X` is a point of unramifiedness
of `f`.
declarations.comment: base change of the unramified locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setOf_unramifiedAt_fiber_eq_setOf_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0475, the equality of the two descriptions of `T`.** For a morphism of
schemes locally of finite type, the set of points at which the scheme-theoretic fibre is
unramified over the residue field of its image is the set of points at which the morphism itself
is unramified.
declarations.comment: the two descriptions of `T` agree, locally-of-finite-type reading

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setOf_unramifiedAt_fiber_eq_setOf_gUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0475, the equality of the two descriptions of `T`, G-unramified
reading.** For a morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation, the set of points at which
the scheme-theoretic fibre is unramified over the residue field of its image is the set of points
at which the morphism itself is G-unramified. Hence that set is the open G-unramified locus, which
is what makes the second half of the tag follow from the first.
declarations.comment:
the two descriptions of `T` agree in the locally-of-finite-presentation reading,
identifying `T` with the G-unramified locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setOf_unramifiedAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0475, the base-change half in set form.** Let
```
X' → X
↓    ↓
S' → S
```
be a cartesian diagram of schemes with `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type and `f' : X' ⟶ S'` the
base change of `f` along `g : S' ⟶ S`. Then the unramified locus `T'` of `f'` is the inverse
image under `g' : X' ⟶ X` of the unramified locus `T` of `f`.
declarations.comment: `T' = (g')⁻¹ T` in set form, for the unramified locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0475, the base-change half for the G-unramified locus, pointwise.** Let
```
X' → X
↓    ↓
S' → S
```
be a cartesian diagram of schemes with `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite presentation and
`f' : X' ⟶ S'` the base change of `f` along `g : S' ⟶ S`. A point `x'` of `X'` is a point of
G-unramifiedness of `f'` if and only if its image `g' x'` in `X` is a point of G-unramifiedness
of `f`.
declarations.comment: base change of the G-unramified locus, pointwise

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setOf_gUnramifiedAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0475, the second half in set form.** For a cartesian diagram of schemes
with `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite presentation, the G-unramified locus of the base change
`f' : X' ⟶ S'` is the inverse image under `g' : X' ⟶ X` of the G-unramified locus of `f`.
declarations.comment:
`T' = (g')⁻¹ T` in set form, for the G-unramified locus, under local finite
presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_setOf_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0475.** The locus where a morphism of schemes is unramified is open.
declarations.statement: theorem isOpen_setOf_unramifiedAt (f : X ⟶ Y) : IsOpen {x : X | UnramifiedAt f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_setOf_gUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0475.** The locus where a morphism of schemes is G-unramified is
open.
declarations.statement: theorem isOpen_setOf_gUnramifiedAt (f : X ⟶ Y) : IsOpen {x : X | GUnramifiedAt f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setOf_etaleAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0476.** Let
```
X' → X
↓    ↓
S' → S
```
be a cartesian diagram of schemes, and let `W ⊆ X`, respectively `W' ⊆ X'`, be the open
subscheme of points where `f : X ⟶ S`, respectively the base-changed morphism `f' : X' ⟶ S'`, is
étale. Then `W' = (g')⁻¹(W)` provided `f` is locally of finite presentation and, in addition,
either `f` is flat — the source's case (1) — or `g : S' ⟶ S` is flat — the source's case (2).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraic_residueField_and_jacobsonSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme locally of finite type over a field `k`. Then (1) for every closed point
`x` of `X` the extension `κ(x)/k` is algebraic, and (2) `X` is a Jacobson scheme, that is, its
underlying space is a Jacobson space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAlgebraic_residueField_and_jacobsonSpace (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] :
    (∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) →
        letI : Algebra k (X.residueField x) :=
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ p.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation x).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsAlgebraic k (X.residueField x)) ∧ JacobsonSpace X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_pullback_of_large_cardinality
declarations.doc:
The base change of a scheme to every sufficiently large extension of its ground field is a
Jacobson scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_pullback_of_large_cardinality
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K],
      κ ≤ Cardinal.mk K →
        JacobsonSpace ↑(pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K))))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ClosedPointResidue.exists_cardinal_isAlgebraic_residueField_of_mem_closedPoints_baseChange
declarations.doc:
For every scheme over a field, after extending the field to one of sufficiently large
cardinality, the residue field of every closed point of the base change is algebraic over the
extended field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cardinal_isAlgebraic_residueField_of_mem_closedPoints_baseChange
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K], κ ≤ Cardinal.mk K →
      ∀ x : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}),
        x ∈ closedPoints
            (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}) →
          let p := pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))
          letI : (p x).asIdeal.IsPrime := (p x).isPrime
          letI := ((CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (p x).asIdeal.ResidueField)) ≫
            (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of K) (p x)).inv ≫
            p.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
          Algebra.IsAlgebraic K
            ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) :
              Scheme.{u}).residueField x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.closure_product
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047B.** The set-theoretic fibre product of the closures of two
subsets of schemes over a field is the closure of their set-theoretic fibre product.
declarations.statement:
theorem closure_product {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (A : Set X) (B : Set Y) :
    (pullback.fst f g).base ⁻¹' closure A ∩ (pullback.snd f g).base ⁻¹' closure B =
      closure ((pullback.fst f g).base ⁻¹' A ∩ (pullback.snd f g).base ⁻¹' B)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.modulePullback_isFlatOverAt_of_isFlatOverAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047C (1).** For a cartesian square of schemes a quasi-coherent module
which is flat over the base at the image of a point pulls back to a module which is flat over the
new base at that point. Nothing is assumed of the base morphism, so this holds for an arbitrary
base change. This is a restatement of `AlgebraicGeometry.modulePullback_isFlatOverAt`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma modulePullback_isFlatOverAt_of_isFlatOverAt
    {X S S' X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'} (h : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (x' : X') (hF : IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (g' x')) :
    IsFlatOverAt f'.toLRSHom.toShHom ((modulePullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F) x'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_of_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047C (2).** Relative flatness of the pullback of a quasi-coherent
module along a cartesian square descends at a point at which the base morphism is flat.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isFlatOverAt_of_modulePullback
    {X S S' X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'} (h : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (x' : X') (hg : IsFlatAt g.toLRSHom.toShHom (f' x'))
    (hF : IsFlatOverAt f'.toLRSHom.toShHom
      ((modulePullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F) x') :
    IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (g' x')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setOf_isFlatOverAt_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047C (flat locus).** Under flat base change the relative flat locus
of a quasi-coherent module is the preimage of the relative flat locus of the module itself.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setOf_isFlatOverAt_modulePullback
    {X S S' X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'} (h : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [Flat g] :
    {x' : X' | IsFlatOverAt f'.toLRSHom.toShHom
      ((modulePullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F) x'} =
      g' ⁻¹' {x : X | IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_setOf_isFlatOverAt_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047C (open locus).** The relative flat locus of the pullback of a
finitely presented quasi-coherent module along any base change of a morphism locally of finite
presentation is open. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.setOf_isFlatOverAt_modulePullback` this says that the open subset of
[Stacks, Tag 0399] commutes with flat base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_setOf_isFlatOverAt_modulePullback
    {X S S' X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'} (h : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    IsOpen {x' : X' | IsFlatOverAt f'.toLRSHom.toShHom
      ((modulePullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F) x'}

declarations.statement: structure ClosedSubgroupScheme {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Grp (Over S))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_iff_isClosedImmersion_one
declarations.doc:
A group scheme is separated over its base if and only if its identity section is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_iff_isClosedImmersion_one {S G : Scheme.{u}} (f : G ⟶ S)
    [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] :
    IsSeparated f ↔ IsClosedImmersion (η[Over.mk f]).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparated_iff_quasiCompact_one
declarations.doc:
A group scheme is quasi-separated over its base if and only if its identity section is
quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSeparated_iff_quasiCompact_one {S G : Scheme.{u}} (f : G ⟶ S)
    [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] :
    QuasiSeparated f ↔ QuasiCompact η[Over.mk f].left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_mul_after_map
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 047H.** Left translation parametrized by a flat scheme is flat.
declarations.statement:
lemma flat_mul_after_map {S : Scheme.{u}} (G T : Over S) [GrpObj G]
    (ψ : T ⟶ G) [Flat T.hom] :
    Flat (lift (fst T G ≫ ψ) (snd T G) ≫ μ[G]).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_mul
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 047H.** Multiplication on a flat group scheme is flat.
declarations.statement:
lemma flat_mul {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Over S) [GrpObj G] [Flat G.hom] :
    Flat μ[G].left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeDifferentials.relativeDifferentialsIsoPullbackIdentity
declarations.doc:
**The canonical isomorphism `Ω_{G/S} ≅ f^*e^*Ω_{G/S}`.**  The sheaf of relative
differentials of a group scheme is the inverse image of its restriction along the identity
section.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeDifferentialsIsoPullbackIdentity :
    relativeDifferentials f ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (identity f)).obj (relativeDifferentials f))
declarations.comment: the composite Ω_{G/S} ≅ f^*e^*Ω_{G/S} of the chain of isomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeDifferentials.pullbackConormalIsoPullbackIdentity
declarations.doc:
**The second isomorphism of the chain**, `f^*𝒞_{S/G} ≅ f^*e^*Ω_{G/S}`,
where `𝒞_{S/G}` is the conormal sheaf of the identity section `e`: the inverse image along `f`
of `conormalIsoPullbackIdentity`, that is, of the first arrow `𝒞_{S/G} ⟶ e^*Ω_{G/S}` of the
conormal sequence of `e`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackConormalIsoPullbackIdentity :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.conormalSheaf (identity f) : S.Modules) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (identity f)).obj (relativeDifferentials f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeDifferentials.relativeDifferentialsIsoPullbackConormal
declarations.doc:
**The first isomorphism of the chain**, `Ω_{G/S} ≅ f^*𝒞_{S/G}`, where
`𝒞_{S/G}` is the conormal sheaf of the identity section `e`: the shearing isomorphism
`Ω_{G/S} ≅ f^*e^*Ω_{G/S}` followed by the inverse of `pullbackConormalIsoPullbackIdentity`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeDifferentialsIsoPullbackConormal :
    relativeDifferentials f ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.conormalSheaf (identity f) : S.Modules)
declarations.comment:
the first isomorphism of the chain, Ω_{G/S} ≅ f^*𝒞_{S/G}, where 𝒞_{S/G} is the
conormal sheaf of the identity section e

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupSchemeDifferentials.exists_free_iso_relativeDifferentials_of_field
declarations.doc:
**Freeness over a field.**  If the base is the spectrum of a field, the sheaf of relative
differentials of a group scheme is a free `𝒪_G`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_free_iso_relativeDifferentials_of_field (k : Type u) [Field k] (G : Scheme.{u})
    (f : G ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] :
    ∃ I : Type u,
      Nonempty (relativeDifferentials f ≅
        SheafOfModules.free (R := G.ringCatSheaf) I)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenMap_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047K.** The multiplication morphism of a group scheme over a field is
open.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOpenMap_mul {K : Type u} [Field K] (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] :
    IsOpenMap μ[G].left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_groupScheme_over_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047L.** The underlying scheme of a group scheme over a field is
separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_groupScheme_over_field {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) : G.X.left.IsSeparated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_irreducibleComponent_containing_identity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047M.** A group scheme over a field has a unique irreducible
component containing its identity point.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_irreducibleComponent_containing_identity
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {G : Scheme.{u}} (f : G ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] :
    ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents G,
      (η[Over.mk f]).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k) ∈ (Z : Set G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_irreducibleComponent_of_identity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047M.** An irreducible component of a group scheme over a field
which contains the identity is geometrically irreducible over that field.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyIrreducible_irreducibleComponent_of_identity
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (G : Scheme.{u}) (f : G ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] (Z : irreducibleComponents G)
    (he : Set.range (η[Over.mk f]).left ⊆ Z.1) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible
      ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        (⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩ :
          TopologicalSpace.Closeds G)).subschemeι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_minimalPrime_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047M.** Every local ring of a group scheme over a field has a
unique minimal prime ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_minimalPrime_stalk (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))) (g : G.X.left) :
    ∃! p : Ideal (G.X.left.presheaf.stalk g),
      p ∈ minimalPrimes (G.X.left.presheaf.stalk g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_groupScheme_of_charZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047N.**  Let `k` be a field of characteristic `0` and let `G` be a
locally algebraic group scheme over `k`, i.e. a scheme whose structure morphism
`f : G ⟶ Spec k` is locally of finite type and which is a group object over `Spec k`.  Then `f`
is smooth, i.e. `G` is a smooth group scheme.

By [Stacks, Tag 047I] the sheaf of relative differentials of `f` is free, hence locally free,
and [Stacks, Tag 04QN] turns that into smoothness over a field of characteristic `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_of_groupScheme_of_charZero (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (G : Scheme.{u})
    (f : G ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    Smooth f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace.isSmooth_of_charZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047N.** Let `k` be a field of characteristic `0` and let `G` be a group algebraic
space over `Spec k` which is a scheme locally of finite type over `k`. Then the structure
morphism `G ⟶ Spec k` is smooth.

The group scheme structure on the representing scheme is obtained from the group structure of
`G` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.grpObjOfIsoYoneda`, and the smoothness of the scheme is
`AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_groupScheme_of_charZero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem GroupAlgebraicSpace.isSmooth_of_charZero
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk (terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).obj
      (terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).property)
    [G.obj.X.left.IsRepresentable]
    (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.hom) :
    IsSmooth C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.hom
declarations.comment: group algebraic spaces over `Spec k` which are schemes locally of finite type over `k`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_grpObj_of_charZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047O.**  Any group scheme over a field of characteristic `0` is
reduced (Perrin, thèse I 1.1, I 3.9, II 2.4; Bull. SMF 104, Prop. 4.2.8): a scheme `G` with a
group object structure on `f : G ⟶ Spec k` over `Spec k`, for `k` a field of characteristic
`0`, is reduced.  No finiteness assumption on `f` is made; the locally finite type case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_groupScheme_of_charZero` ([Stacks, Tag 047N]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_grpObj_of_charZero (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (G : Scheme.{u})
    (f : G ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] : IsReduced G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_groupScheme_of_charZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047O**, the case the source proves.  A locally algebraic group scheme
over a field `k` of characteristic `0` is reduced: it is smooth over `k` by [Stacks, Tag 047N],
`Spec k` is a reduced affine scheme, and a scheme smooth over a reduced affine scheme is
reduced.

The source states reducedness for an arbitrary group scheme over a field of characteristic `0`,
citing Perrin for that generality, and records that the locally finite type case is the
consequence of [Stacks, Tag 047N] proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_groupScheme_of_charZero (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (G : Scheme.{u})
    (f : G ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    IsReduced G
declarations.comment: locally of finite type case; the general case is cited to Perrin

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_groupScheme_of_charZero_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047O**, for affine group schemes.  An affine group scheme over a field
of characteristic `0` is reduced, with no finiteness hypothesis: its ring of global sections is a
commutative Hopf algebra, reduced by `HopfAlgebra.isReduced_of_charZero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_groupScheme_of_charZero_of_isAffine (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k]
    (G : Scheme.{u}) (f : G ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] [IsAffine G] :
    IsReduced G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_isReduced_groupScheme_of_perfectField
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a perfect field and let `G` be a reduced locally algebraic group scheme over `k`,
that is, a reduced scheme whose structure morphism `f : G ⟶ Spec k` is locally of finite type and
which is a group object over `Spec k`. Then `f` is smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_of_isReduced_groupScheme_of_perfectField (k : Type u) [Field k] [PerfectField k]
    (G : Scheme.{u}) (f : G ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [GrpObj (Over.mk f)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsReduced G] :
    Smooth f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closedSubgroupScheme_reduction
declarations.doc: The reduction of a group scheme over a perfect field is a closed subgroup scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedSubgroupScheme_reduction
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k]
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) :
    let I := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds G.X.left)
    ∃ H : ClosedSubgroupScheme G,
      ∃ e : Over.mk (I.subschemeι ≫ G.X.hom) ≅ H.carrier.X,
        Over.homMk I.subschemeι = e.hom ≫ H.ι.hom.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_range_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047S.** An open image of a homomorphism of group schemes over a
field is closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_range_of_isOpen {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {G' G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))} (ψ : G' ⟶ G)
    (hopen : IsOpen (Set.range ψ.hom.hom.left.base)) :
    IsClosed (Set.range ψ.hom.hom.left.base)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047T.** Every immersion of group schemes over a field is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_isImmersion {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {G' G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))} (i : G' ⟶ G)
    [IsImmersion i.hom.hom.left] : IsClosedImmersion i.hom.hom.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_openSubgroupScheme_isClosed_iUnion_affineOpens
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047U.** A group scheme over a field has an open and closed subscheme
which is a countable union of affine opens; it can be taken to be an open subgroup scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubgroupScheme_isClosed_iUnion_affineOpens
    (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) :
    ∃ (H : OpenSubgroupScheme G) (V : ℕ → G.X.left.Opens),
      IsOpen (Set.range H.ι.hom.hom.left.base) ∧
      IsClosed (Set.range H.ι.hom.hom.left.base) ∧
      Set.range η[G.X].left.base ⊆ Set.range H.ι.hom.hom.left.base ∧
      (∀ n, IsAffineOpen (V n)) ∧
      Set.range H.ι.hom.hom.left.base = ⋃ n, (V n : Set G.X.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_cohenMacaulayLocus
declarations.doc:
The maximal Cohen–Macaulay locus of `h : U' ×_{g,U,t} R ⟶ U` is the
inverse image of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_cohenMacaulayLocus
    (D : FlatLocallyFinitelyPresentedGroupoidSituation) :
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest
        {V : D.fiberProduct.Opens |
          ∃ hf : ∀ y : D.groupoid.objects.left,
              IsLocallyNoetherian ((V.ι ≫ D.h).fiber y),
            Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay (V.ι ≫ D.h) hf}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_etaleLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047W, case (8).**  In the flat, locally finitely presented groupoid
situation the largest open of `U' ×_{g, U, t} R` on which `h` is étale is the inverse image
along the projection of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_etaleLocus
    (D : FlatLocallyFinitelyPresentedGroupoidSituation.{u}) :
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest {V : D.fiberProduct.Opens | Etale (V.ι ≫ D.h)}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047W, case (4).**  In the flat, locally finitely presented groupoid
situation the largest open of `U' ×_{g, U, t} R` on which `h` is flat is the inverse image along
the projection of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_flatLocus
    (D : FlatLocallyFinitelyPresentedGroupoidSituation.{u}) :
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest {V : D.fiberProduct.Opens | Flat (V.ι ≫ D.h)}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_quasiFiniteLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047W, case (2).**  In the groupoid situation with structure maps
locally of finite type, the largest open of `U' ×_{g, U, t} R` on which `h` is locally
quasi-finite is the inverse image along the projection of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_quasiFiniteLocus
    (D : LocallyOfFiniteTypeGroupoidSituation.{u}) :
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest
        {V : D.fiberProduct.Opens |
          LocallyOfFiniteType (V.ι ≫ D.h) ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite (V.ι ≫ D.h)}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_relativeDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
In the locally finite type groupoid situation, the relative-dimension-at-most-`d` locus of
`h : U' ×_{g, U, t} R ⟶ U` is the inverse image of an open of `U'`, and it is the greatest open
on which the restriction of `h` has that dimension bound.

This is **Stacks Project, Tag 047W, case (1)**.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_relativeDimensionLE
    (D : LocallyOfFiniteTypeGroupoidSituation) (d : ℕ) :
    let _ : LocallyOfFiniteType
        (pullback.snd D.g D.groupoid.target.left ≫ D.groupoid.source.left) := inferInstance
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest
        {V : (pullback D.g D.groupoid.target.left).Opens |
          RelativeDimensionLE
            (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd D.g D.groupoid.target.left ≫ D.groupoid.source.left) d}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_smoothLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047W, case (7).**  In the flat, locally finitely presented groupoid
situation the largest open of `U' ×_{g, U, t} R` on which `h` is smooth is the inverse image
along the projection of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_smoothLocus
    (D : FlatLocallyFinitelyPresentedGroupoidSituation.{u}) :
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest {V : D.fiberProduct.Opens | Smooth (V.ι ≫ D.h)}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_syntomicLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047W, case (6).**  In the flat, locally finitely presented groupoid
situation the largest open of `U' ×_{g, U, t} R` on which `h` is syntomic is the inverse image
along the projection of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_syntomicLocus
    (D : FlatLocallyFinitelyPresentedGroupoidSituation.{u}) :
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest {V : D.fiberProduct.Opens | Syntomic (V.ι ≫ D.h)}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_unramifiedLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 047W, case (3).**  In the groupoid situation with structure maps
locally of finite type, the largest open of `U' ×_{g, U, t} R` on which `h` is unramified is the
inverse image along the projection of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_unramifiedLocus
    (D : LocallyOfFiniteTypeGroupoidSituation.{u}) :
    ∃ W : D.U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest {V : D.fiberProduct.Opens | Unramified (V.ι ≫ D.h)}
        ((pullback.fst D.g D.groupoid.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceStructure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047X.** An *algebraic space structure* on a closed set `Z` of points of an
algebraic space `X` over `S` is a closed subspace of `X` whose set of points is `Z`.
declarations.statement:
def IsAlgebraicSpaceStructure {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (Z : Set (points B S hS X)) (Z' : Subfunctor X) : Prop
declarations.comment: algebraic space structure on a closed set of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpaceStructure_reducedClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047X, the reduced induced structure.** The subspace of Stacks 03IQ on a closed set
of points is an algebraic space structure on that set. That it is moreover reduced is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced_reducedClosedSubspace`, and that it is
the only reduced one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_isAlgebraicSpaceStructure_isReduced`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpaceStructure_reducedClosedSubspace
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (Z : Set (points B S hS X)) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    IsAlgebraicSpaceStructure B S hS Z (reducedClosedSubspace B S hS X hX Z hZ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_isAlgebraicSpaceStructure_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047X, the reduced induced structure characterized.** A closed set of points of an
algebraic space carries exactly one reduced algebraic space structure, namely the subspace of
Stacks 03IQ. This is what makes *the* reduced induced structure well defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isAlgebraicSpaceStructure_isReduced
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (Z : Set (points B S hS X)) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    ∃! Z' : Subfunctor X,
      IsAlgebraicSpaceStructure B S hS Z Z' ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z'.toFunctor (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)
declarations.comment: the reduced induced structure is the unique reduced one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047X, the reduction.** The *reduction* `X_red` of an algebraic space `X` over `S` is
the reduced induced algebraic space structure on the whole of its space of points: the subspace
of Stacks 03IQ at the closed set `Set.univ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reduction (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) : Subfunctor X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047X, the reduction characterized.** The reduction is the unique reduced algebraic
space structure on the whole space of points.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_reduction (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃! Z' : Subfunctor X,
      IsAlgebraicSpaceStructure B S hS (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS X)) Z' ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z'.toFunctor (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)
declarations.comment: the reduction is the unique reduced structure on the whole point set

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_subsingleton_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047Z, part (1).** A decent algebraic space over `S` whose point set is a singleton
is a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_subsingleton_points (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hne : Nonempty (points B S hS X))
    (hsub : Subsingleton (points B S hS X)) : X.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_yoneda_spec_of_subsingleton_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 047Z, part (2).** A reduced decent algebraic space over `S` whose point set is a
singleton is the spectrum of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_yoneda_spec_of_subsingleton_points (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hne : Nonempty (points B S hS X))
    (hsub : Subsingleton (points B S hS X))
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsReduced Y)) :
    ∃ (M : BigFppfOver B S hS) (k : Type u) (_ : Field k),
      Nonempty ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj M ≅ Spec (.of k)) ∧
        Nonempty (X ≅ yoneda.obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRadicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0481.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *radicial* if for every
field `k` in the chosen site and every `k`-valued point of the target, the reduction of the
fibre is either empty or is represented, over `Spec(k)`, by the spectrum of a purely
inseparable extension of `k`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_of_isRadicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0482.** A radicial morphism of algebraic spaces is universally injective.

On a field-valued point of the target the fibre's reduction is either empty, excluding the
point, or the spectrum of a purely inseparable extension, and a scheme-theoretic section of
such a spectrum over the base field is unique; two points of the fibre therefore agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_isRadicial
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsRadicial B S hS hX hY f) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.universallyInjective_galoisQuotientToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0483.** The Galois quotient of `Spec ℚ̄` is universally injective over `Spec ℚ`,
although it is not radicial.

Universal injectivity is tested on field-valued points, so it suffices to make two sections
of the quotient over the spectrum of a field agree over a further field spectrum. The
projection of `Spec ℚ̄` onto the quotient is locally surjective, so after two successive
restrictions both sections come from morphisms to `Spec ℚ̄`, that is from two `ℚ`-embeddings
of `ℚ̄` into the field of the second restriction; those differ by an element of the Galois
group, which is exactly what the quotient divides out.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_galoisQuotientToBase :
    Space.UniversallyInjective B base hS (galoisQuotientToBase B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.not_isRadicial_galoisQuotientToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0483.** The structure morphism of the Galois quotient of `Spec ℚ̄` to `Spec ℚ` is
*not* radicial.

Radicialness is tested at the field `ℚ` itself, on the terminal object of the site with the
identity point of the base, so that the fibre is the quotient itself. Its reduction is not
pointless, because the `ℚ̄`-valued point coming from the projection of `Spec ℚ̄` survives to
the reduction; and it is not the spectrum of a purely inseparable extension `L` of `ℚ`
either: `ℚ` is perfect, so the structure map `ℚ → L` is surjective, while a field algebraic
over `ℚ` carrying a point of the quotient is a copy of `ℚ̄` or of the real algebraic numbers
by `AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.fieldPoint_algEquiv_algebraicClosure_or_real`,
and the structure map of `ℚ` into either of those is not surjective, both fields containing
a square root of two.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isRadicial_galoisQuotientToBase :
    ¬ Space.IsRadicial B base hS (isAlgebraicSpace_galoisQuotient B hS hU)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B base hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS))))
      (galoisQuotientToBase B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.universallyInjective_and_not_isRadicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0483.** The structure morphism of the Galois quotient of `Spec ℚ̄` to `Spec ℚ` is
universally injective but is not radicial: for algebraic spaces, unlike for schemes,
universal injectivity is strictly weaker than radicialness.

This is the conjunction over a fixed big fppf site containing the two spectra;
`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.exists_universallyInjective_not_isRadicial`
exhibits such a site and so asserts the non-equivalence outright.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_and_not_isRadicial :
    Space.UniversallyInjective B base hS (galoisQuotientToBase B hS hU) ∧
      ¬ Space.IsRadicial B base hS (isAlgebraicSpace_galoisQuotient B hS hU)
        (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B base hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS))))
        (galoisQuotientToBase B hS hU)
declarations.comment: the two halves together, over a big fppf site containing the two spectra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.exists_universallyInjective_not_isRadicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0483.** Universal injectivity is not equivalent to radicialness for morphisms of
algebraic spaces: there are a big fppf site over `Spec ℚ`, an algebraic space over `Spec ℚ` in
it, and a structure morphism of that space to `Spec ℚ` which is universally injective and is
not radicial.

Nothing is assumed: the site is the one
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.exists_containing` supplies for the two schemes `Spec ℚ` and
`Spec ℚ̄`, and the space is the Galois quotient of `Spec ℚ̄`, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.universallyInjective_and_not_isRadicial` with its
site hypotheses discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_universallyInjective_not_isRadicial :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{0}) (hS : B.Contains base)
      (X : (BigFppfOver B base hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 0) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B base hS X)
      (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))),
      Space.UniversallyInjective B base hS f ∧
        ¬ Space.IsRadicial B base hS hX
          (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B base hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))) f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_isDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0484, part (1).** A universally injective decent morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` is radicial.

Over a field-valued point of the target the reduction of the fibre is a reduced decent algebraic
space whose point set is a subsingleton, hence empty or the spectrum of a field by Stacks 047Z,
and the resulting extension is purely inseparable because its spectrum map is again universally
injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_isDecent
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hinj : UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hdecent : IsDecent B S hS f) :
    IsRadicial B S hS hX hY f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0484, part (2).** A universally injective quasi-separated morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` is radicial: a quasi-separated morphism is very reasonable, hence reasonable,
hence decent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_isQuasiSeparated
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hinj : UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsRadicial B S hS hX hY f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_isLocallySeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0484, part (3).** A universally injective locally separated morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` is radicial.

Universal injectivity makes the relative diagonal surjective and local separatedness makes it an
immersion, so it is a closed immersion; the morphism is therefore separated, in particular
quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_isLocallySeparated
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hinj : UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hls : IsLocallySeparated B S hS f) :
    IsRadicial B S hS hX hY f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.geometricPointOfSpecHom
declarations.doc:
For an object `U` of the big fppf site over `S`, an algebraically closed field `Ω` whose
spectrum the site contains, a morphism `tb : Spec Ω ⟶ S` and a morphism of schemes
`σ : Spec Ω ⟶ U` over `tb`, the geometric point of `yoneda.obj U` whose field is `Ω`, whose
structure morphism to `S` is `tb` and whose section is `σ`.
declarations.statement:
def geometricPointOfSpecHom (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (hΩ : B.Contains (Spec (.of Ω))) (tb : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S)
    (σ : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
    (hσ : σ ≫ B.inclusion.map U.hom = tb) :
    GeometricPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U)
declarations.comment: part (1): a geometric point of a representable algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
A morphism from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field to a presheaf over a scheme.
For an algebraic space this is a geometric point.
declarations.statement:
abbrev GeometricPoint (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Type (u + 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GeometricPoint.image
declarations.doc: The point of the algebraic space represented by a geometric point.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GeometricPoint.LiesOver
declarations.doc: A geometric point lies over its image point in the underlying point set.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_iff_surjective_app_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0487.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type is
surjective exactly when, for every algebraically closed field `k` of the working universe whose
spectrum lies in the chosen site and every structure morphism `Spec k ⟶ S`, the induced map
`X(k) ⟶ Y(k)` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_iff_surjective_app_isAlgClosed
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsSurjective B S hS f ↔
      ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
        (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S),
        Function.Surjective
          (f.app (Opposite.op (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.geometricPoints_large_enough
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0488.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `X`, `Y` be algebraic spaces over `S`.

1. As `k` ranges over all algebraically closed fields over `S` the geometric points
   `ȳ ∈ Y(k)` cover all of `|Y|`.
2. As `k` ranges over all algebraically closed fields over `S` with `|k| ≥ λ(Y)` and
   `|k| > λ(X)` the geometric points `ȳ ∈ Y(k)` cover all of `|Y|`.
3. For any geometric point `s̄ : Spec k → S` where `k` has cardinality `> λ(X)` the map
   `X(k) → |X_s|` is surjective.
4. For a morphism `X → Y` and any geometric point `s̄ : Spec k → S` where `k` has
   cardinality `> λ(X)`, the map `X(k) → |X| ×_{|Y|} Y(k)` is surjective.
5. A morphism `X → Y` is surjective if and only if `X(k) → Y(k)` is surjective for all
   algebraically closed fields `k` over `S` with `|k| > λ(X)` and `|k| ≥ λ(Y)`.

Following the source, `λ(X)` and `λ(Y)` are the cardinals `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.lambdaCard`
of schemes carrying a surjective étale morphism onto `X` and onto `Y`; the clauses quantify
over all such atlases.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricPoints_large_enough
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    -- (1) geometric points cover the point set
    (∀ y : points B S hS Y, ∃ p : GeometricPoint B S hS Y, p.image = y) ∧
    -- (2) geometric points over large enough fields cover the point set
    (∀ (UX UY : BigFppfOver B S hS) (fX : yoneda.obj UX ⟶ X) (fY : yoneda.obj UY ⟶ Y),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fX →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fX →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fY →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fY →
      ∀ y : points B S hS Y, ∃ p : GeometricPoint B S hS Y, p.LiesOver y ∧
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj UY).lambdaCard ≤ Cardinal.mk p.val.carrier ∧
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj UX).lambdaCard < Cardinal.mk p.val.carrier) ∧
    -- (3) `X(k) → |X_s|` is surjective
    (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f →
      ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
        (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S),
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).lambdaCard < Cardinal.mk k →
      ∀ (s : S) (hs : ∀ t, b t = s) (Xs : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (pr : Xs ⟶ X) (pr' : Xs ⟶ yoneda.obj (residueSiteObject B S hS s))
        (hpb : IsPullback pr pr' (toBaseSiteMap B S hS X)
          (yoneda.map (toBaseSiteObject B S hS (residueSiteObject B S hS s)))),
        Function.Surjective (fibrePointOfFieldPoint B S hS hk b s hs pr pr' hpb)) ∧
    -- (4) `X(k) → |X| ×_{|Y|} Y(k)` is surjective
    (∀ (a : X ⟶ Y) (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f →
      ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
        (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S),
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).lambdaCard < Cardinal.mk k →
      ∀ (x : points B S hS X)
        (y : Y.obj (Opposite.op (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)))),
        pointsMap B S hS X a x =
            (⟨k, hk, b, y⟩ : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y).class B S hS Y →
        ∃ z : X.obj (Opposite.op (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS))),
          a.app (Opposite.op (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS))) z = y ∧
          (⟨k, hk, b, z⟩ : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X).class B S hS X = x) ∧
    -- (5) surjectivity is tested on the field-valued points over large enough fields
    (∀ (a : X ⟶ Y) (UX UY : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (fX : yoneda.obj UX ⟶ X) (fY : yoneda.obj UY ⟶ Y),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fX →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fX →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fY →
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) fY →
      (IsSurjective B S hS a ↔
        ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
          (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S),
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj UX).lambdaCard < Cardinal.mk k →
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj UY).lambdaCard ≤ Cardinal.mk k →
          Function.Surjective
            (a.app (Opposite.op (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS))))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_restriction_locallyQuasiFinite_isIso_quotientMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0489**, conditional on Steps 1 to 3 of its proof.

Let `R` be a groupoid scheme over `S` whose target and source are an equivalence relation.
Given a refinement in the sense of
`Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.QuasiFiniteRefinement` — a morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` whose reach
map is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite and is a singleton covering
of the site — the restriction `R' = R|_{U'}` is again an equivalence relation, its source and
target are flat, locally of finite presentation, locally of finite type and locally
quasi-finite, and the induced map `U'/R' ⟶ U/R` of quotient sheaves is an isomorphism.

The conclusion is stated for *every* groupoid scheme realizing the restriction, which is
stronger than producing one and avoids any appeal to the realization
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict` built by `Classical.choice`.  The morphism
`U' ⟶ U` carrying `R'` into `R` is the one recorded by
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction.hom`, so the clause of the tag that the
isomorphism of quotient sheaves is induced by a morphism `U' ⟶ U` mapping `R'` into `R` is part
of the statement rather than an afterthought.

The flatness and local finite presentation hypotheses which the tag places on `s` and `t` are
not assumed; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_restriction_locallyQuasiFinite_isIso_quotientMap
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify J (Type u)] (F : C ⥤ Over S) (hF : F.Full)
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source]
    (N : QuasiFiniteRefinement J F G) :
    ∃ (U' : Over S) (g : U' ⟶ G.objects),
      ∀ R' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction G g,
      IsEquivalenceRelation R'.groupoid.target R'.groupoid.source ∧
      Flat R'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation R'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType R'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite R'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      Flat R'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation R'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType R'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite R'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      IsIso (restrictionQuotientMap J F G g R')
declarations.comment: the refinement with locally quasi-finite source and target and the same quotient sheaf, given the refinement data as `QuasiFiniteRefinement`. The tag itself, with nothing carried, is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_groupoid_quotientSheaf_iso` of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Groupoids/CohenMacaulayQuotientUnchanged.lean`, which builds that data from the Cohen-Macaulay restriction and the reach map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_refinement_isIso_quotientMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0489.**

Let `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` be a groupoid scheme over `S` whose target and source maps form an
equivalence relation and are flat and locally of finite presentation.  Then there are a scheme
`U'` over `S`, a morphism `U' ⟶ U`, and an equivalence relation `R'` on `U'` mapping into `R`
over it, whose source and target maps are flat, locally of finite presentation, locally of finite
type and locally quasi-finite, and for which the induced map `U'/R' ⟶ U/R` of quotient sheaves on
the big fppf site over `S` is an isomorphism.

The refinement is produced in the two stages of the source proof: `g₁ : U₁ ⟶ U` is the inclusion
of the Cohen-Macaulay open of Stacks 0460, `H₁` is the restriction of `R` along it,
`g' : U' ⟶ U₁` is the disjoint union of the affine slices of Stacks 04N0 over the finite type
points of `U₁`, and `R'` is the restriction `H'` of `H₁` along `g'`.  The morphism `U' ⟶ U` is the
composite `g`, and the morphism of `R'` into `R` is the composite of the two restrictions'
canonical morphisms, which lies over `g` by the second conclusion below.

The last conclusion is more than the tag asks: the map of quotient sheaves induced by the
restriction of `R` along the single morphism `g` is an isomorphism for *every* groupoid scheme
realizing that restriction.  Together with the isomorphism for `R'` it says that the two
descriptions of the refined relation — the restriction of the restriction, and the restriction
along the composite — have the same quotient; that they are the same relation is Stacks 04MW,
which is not used here.

The last two conclusions are the size estimates of the two stages, also more than the tag asks:
the first stage is an open of `U`, and the second is a disjoint union of affine immersions
locally of finite presentation indexed by the points of the first, so
`size U₁ ≤ size U` and `size U' ≤ 2 ^ size U`.  They are not used for the isomorphism of
quotient sheaves — that needs no cardinality hypothesis at all, see the implementation notes —
but they are what a later consumer needs in order to exhibit `U'` and the arrow scheme of `R'`
