as *objects of the site*, which the engine of Stacks 02WW requires and which the existential
form of this statement would otherwise destroy.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_locallyQuasiFinite_refinement_isIso_quotientMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source]
    [Flat G.source.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left] :
    letI := BigFppfOver.hasSheafify_type B S hS
    ∃ (U₁ : Over S) (g₁ : U₁ ⟶ G.objects) (H₁ : Restriction G g₁) (U' : Over S)
      (g' : U' ⟶ H₁.groupoid.objects) (H' : Restriction H₁.groupoid g')
      (g : U' ⟶ G.objects),
      g = g' ≫ H₁.hom.mapObjects ∧
      H'.hom.mapObjects ≫ H₁.hom.mapObjects = eqToHom H'.objects_eq ≫ g ∧
      IsEquivalenceRelation H'.groupoid.target H'.groupoid.source ∧
      Flat H'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation H'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType H'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite H'.groupoid.source.left ∧
      Flat H'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation H'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType H'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite H'.groupoid.target.left ∧
      IsIso (restrictionQuotientMap (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Over.post B.inclusion)
          H₁.groupoid g' H' ≫
        restrictionQuotientMap (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Over.post B.inclusion) G g₁ H₁) ∧
      (∀ H : Restriction G g,
        IsIso (restrictionQuotientMap (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
          (Over.post B.inclusion) G g H)) ∧
      U₁.left.size ≤ G.objects.left.size ∧
      U'.left.size ≤ 2 ^ G.objects.left.size
declarations.comment:
unconditionally, with no assumed input: the hypotheses are exactly the tag's, that
the source and target of the groupoid scheme are an equivalence relation and are flat and locally
of finite presentation. The refined equivalence relation R' is the restriction H' along the second
stage g' of the restriction H₁ along the first stage g₁ of the two-stage refinement that
`exists_cohenMacaulay_and_quasiFinite_refinement` produces -- the Cohen-Macaulay open of
Stacks 0460, then the disjoint union of the affine slices of Stacks 04N0 over the finite type
points -- and the morphism U' ⟶ U of the tag is the composite g, over which the composite of the
two restrictions' canonical morphisms carries R' into R. Its source and target are flat, locally
of finite presentation, locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite, being base changes of the
second stage's reach map by Stacks 04MV; it is an equivalence relation by
`restriction_isEquivalenceRelation`; and U'/R' ⟶ U/R, the composite of the two stages' maps of
quotient sheaves, is an isomorphism because each stage's reach map is flat, locally of finite
presentation and surjective and therefore locally surjective on the functors of points of the big
fppf site by `isLocallySurjective_points_map_of_fppf`, which Stacks 02VH turns into an
isomorphism of quotient sheaves. No covering datum is assumed: on this site a flat, locally
finitely presented, surjective morphism of Over S is locally surjective on points whatever the
sizes of its source and target, so neither the disjoint union of Step 3 nor the source of either
reach map has to be exhibited as an object of the site. The two stages are not collapsed into one
morphism whose reach map is a covering, because the reach map of the composite factors through the
base change of an immersion and so is not flat; the final conclusion instead gives the
isomorphism of quotient sheaves for the restriction along the composite as well, by
`isIso_restrictionQuotientMap_of_comp_reach`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_slice_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
An equivalence relation on schemes over `S` with flat, locally finitely
presented source and target maps admits a slice: an equivalence relation whose
source and target maps are flat, locally of finite presentation and locally
quasi-finite, together with a morphism `g` of object schemes and a morphism `r`
of arrow schemes over it, inducing an isomorphism of fppf quotient sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_slice_locallyQuasiFinite
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [HasSheafify (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)]
    {R U : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (j : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation (S := S) ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj R)
      ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj U))
    [IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source]
    [Flat j.source.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation j.source.left]
    [Flat j.target.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation j.target.left] :
    ∃ (U' R' : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (j' : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation (S := S) ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj R')
        ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj U'))
      (g : U' ⟶ U) (r : R' ⟶ R)
      (hs : (Over.post B.inclusion).map r ≫ j.source =
        j'.source ≫ (Over.post B.inclusion).map g)
      (ht : (Over.post B.inclusion).map r ≫ j.target =
        j'.target ≫ (Over.post B.inclusion).map g),
      IsEquivalenceRelation j'.target j'.source ∧
        Flat j'.source.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j'.source.left ∧
        LocallyQuasiFinite j'.source.left ∧
        Flat j'.target.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j'.target.left ∧
        LocallyQuasiFinite j'.target.left ∧
      IsIso (Stacks.Groupoids.quotientSheafMap
          (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Over.post B.inclusion) j' j
          ((Over.post B.inclusion).map r) ((Over.post B.inclusion).map g)
          hs ht)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsInvariant
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ` out of `U` is *invariant* under a pre-relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` when it
identifies the target and the source of every arrow of `j`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGroupInvariant
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ` out of an object `U` carrying an action of a group algebraic space `G` is
*invariant* when acting does not change its value.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsGroupInvariant
    (G : Over B.obj) {U X : Over B.obj} [GrpObj G] [ModObj G U]
    (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.invariant_iff_factors_through_quotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048F.** A morphism from `U` to a sheaf is invariant under a pre-relation `j` if
and only if it factors through the canonical projection of `U` onto the quotient sheaf
`U/R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invariant_iff_factors_through_quotientSheaf (j : PreRelation R U)
    (hX : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology site S hS) X) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) :
    IsInvariant j φ ↔
      ∃ d : quotientSheaf j ⟶ baseSheaf hX, toQuotientSheaf j ≫ d.hom = φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.overInvariantTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048G.** A morphism out of the object space of a groupoid in algebraic spaces
which is invariant under the pre-relation of the groupoid makes the groupoid a groupoid over
its target: the object and arrow spaces, the source, the target and the composition are
unchanged, and the new structure morphism on objects is the invariant morphism itself.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def overInvariantTarget (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS} (XtoB : X ⟶ B) (φ : G.objects ⟶ X)
    (_hφB : φ ≫ XtoB = G.objectsToBase)
    (hφ : Space.IsInvariant (Space.groupoidPreRelation G) φ.hom) :
    { H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS X //
      H.toGroupoidInFunctors = G.toGroupoidInFunctors ∧
      ∃ hobj : H.objects = G.objects, eqToHom hobj.symm ≫ H.objectsToBase = φ }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.baseChangedPreRelation_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048G.** The base change of the pre-relation of a groupoid in algebraic spaces
along a morphism to an invariant target is the pre-relation of the base change of the
groupoid over that target: the object and the arrow spaces agree, canonically through the two
projections of the pullbacks, and the identifications intertwine the source and the target
maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangedPreRelation_isBaseChange (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS} (XtoB : X ⟶ B) (φ : G.objects ⟶ X)
    (hφB : φ ≫ XtoB = G.objectsToBase)
    (hφ : Space.IsInvariant (Space.groupoidPreRelation G) φ.hom)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) :
    let H := (overInvariantTarget G XtoB φ hφB hφ).val
    let bc := Space.baseChange H f
    let j := Space.groupoidPreRelation G
    let j' := (Space.baseChangedPreRelation j φ.hom f.hom hφ).val
    ∃ (hobj : H.objects = G.objects) (harr : H.arrows = G.arrows)
      (α : (Space.baseChangedObject (U := Over.mk G.objectsToBase.hom) φ.hom f.hom).left ≅
          bc.groupoid.objects.obj)
      (β : (Space.baseChangedArrows j φ.hom f.hom).left ≅ bc.groupoid.arrows.obj),
      (α.hom ≫ bc.groupoid.objectsToBase.hom = pullback.fst f.hom φ.hom) ∧
      (β.hom ≫ bc.groupoid.arrowsToBase.hom =
        pullback.fst f.hom (j.target.left ≫ φ.hom)) ∧
      (α.hom ≫ bc.projection.mapObjects ≫ (eqToHom hobj).hom =
        pullback.snd f.hom φ.hom) ∧
      (β.hom ≫ bc.projection.mapArrows ≫ (eqToHom harr).hom =
        pullback.snd f.hom (j.target.left ≫ φ.hom)) ∧
      (j'.source.left ≫ α.hom = β.hom ≫ bc.groupoid.source.hom) ∧
      (j'.target.left ≫ α.hom = β.hom ≫ bc.groupoid.target.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_inducedAction_of_baseChangedPreRelation
declarations.doc:
An invariant base change of an action pre-relation is again an action
pre-relation. The comparison of arrow spaces respects the original arrows and
both endpoints, while the induced action fixes the new-base coordinate.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_inducedAction_of_baseChangedPreRelation
    (hsource : j.source = snd G U) (htarget : j.target = γ[G,U])
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) :
    ∃ action : ModObj G (baseChangedObject φ f),
      letI : ModObj G (baseChangedObject φ f) := action
      let U' := baseChangedObject φ f
      let R' := baseChangedArrows j φ f
      let j' := (baseChangedPreRelation j φ f hφ).val
      let q : U' ⟶ U := Over.homMk (pullback.snd f φ) (by rfl)
      let toOriginal : G ⊗ U' ⟶ G ⊗ U :=
        lift (fst G U') (snd G U' ≫ q)
      ((γ[G, U']).left ≫ pullback.fst f φ =
        (snd G U').left ≫ pullback.fst f φ) ∧
      (γ[G, U'] ≫ q = toOriginal ≫ γ[G,U]) ∧
    ∃ e : G ⊗ U' ≅ R',
        (e.hom.left ≫ pullback.snd f (j.target.left ≫ φ) = toOriginal.left) ∧
        (e.hom ≫ j'.source = snd G U') ∧
        (e.hom ≫ j'.target = γ[G, U'])

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChangedPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048G** and **Stacks 048H.** The canonical pre-relation on the base changes of the
object and of the arrow space of an invariant pre-relation. Its target and source maps are
fixed by their composites with the two projections of the pullbacks: both preserve the
component in `X'`, and on the component in `U` they are the target and the source of `j`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangedPreRelation (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) :
    { j' : PreRelation (baseChangedArrows j φ f) (baseChangedObject φ f) //
      ((j'.target.left ≫ pullback.fst f φ =
          pullback.fst f (j.target.left ≫ φ)) ∧
        (j'.target.left ≫ pullback.snd f φ =
          pullback.snd f (j.target.left ≫ φ) ≫ j.target.left)) ∧
      ((j'.source.left ≫ pullback.fst f φ =
          pullback.fst f (j.target.left ≫ φ)) ∧
        (j'.source.left ≫ pullback.snd f φ =
          pullback.snd f (j.target.left ≫ φ) ≫ j.source.left)) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPreEquivalenceRelation_baseChangedPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048G.** Base change along an invariant morphism preserves the pointwise
equivalence property of a pre-relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPreEquivalenceRelation_baseChangedPreRelation (j : PreRelation R U)
    (φ : U.left ⟶ X) (f : X' ⟶ X) (hφ : IsInvariant j φ)
    (hj : IsPreEquivalenceRelation j) :
    IsPreEquivalenceRelation (baseChangedPreRelation j φ f hφ).val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_baseChangedPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048G.** Base change along an invariant morphism preserves relations, that is
monomorphy of the map to the product.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_baseChangedPreRelation (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) [Mono j] :
    Mono (baseChangedPreRelation j φ f hφ).val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalenceRelation_baseChangedPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048G.** Base change along an invariant morphism preserves equivalence relations:
the base-changed pre-relation of an invariant equivalence relation is again an internal
categorical equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
instance isEquivalenceRelation_baseChangedPreRelation (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (hφ : IsInvariant j φ)
    [IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source] :
    IsEquivalenceRelation
      (PreRelation.target (baseChangedPreRelation j φ f hφ).val)
      (PreRelation.source (baseChangedPreRelation j φ f hφ).val)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChangedPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048G** and **Stacks 048H.** The canonical pre-relation on the base changes of the
object and of the arrow space of an invariant pre-relation. Its target and source maps are
fixed by their composites with the two projections of the pullbacks: both preserve the
component in `X'`, and on the component in `U` they are the target and the source of `j`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangedPreRelation (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) :
    { j' : PreRelation (baseChangedArrows j φ f) (baseChangedObject φ f) //
      ((j'.target.left ≫ pullback.fst f φ =
          pullback.fst f (j.target.left ≫ φ)) ∧
        (j'.target.left ≫ pullback.snd f φ =
          pullback.snd f (j.target.left ≫ φ) ≫ j.target.left)) ∧
      ((j'.source.left ≫ pullback.fst f φ =
          pullback.fst f (j.target.left ≫ φ)) ∧
        (j'.source.left ≫ pullback.snd f φ =
          pullback.snd f (j.target.left ≫ φ) ≫ j.source.left)) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCategoricalQuotient
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` is a *categorical quotient* of a
pre-relation `j` when it is invariant under `j` and every invariant morphism out of `U` factors
uniquely through it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCategoricalQuotient {R U X : Over B} (j : PreRelation R U)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCategoricalQuotientIn
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` is a *categorical quotient in the full subcategory* cut out by an object
property `P` when `R`, `U` and `X` lie in it and the universal property of a categorical quotient
holds against the objects of `P`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCategoricalQuotientIn (P : ObjectProperty (Over B)) {R U X : Over B}
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCategoricalQuotientInSchemes
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of schemes over `T` is a *categorical quotient* of a pre-relation of
schemes when it equalizes the target and the source of the pre-relation and every morphism out of
`U` which does so factors uniquely through it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCategoricalQuotientInSchemes {T : Scheme.{u}} {R U X : Over T}
    (j : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.categoricalQuotient_unique
declarations.doc:
Two categorical quotients of a pre-relation of algebraic spaces over `B` are uniquely
isomorphic over `B`, compatibly with their quotient maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem categoricalQuotient_unique {R U X Y : Over B} (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (ψ : U ⟶ Y) (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotient j φ) (hψ : IsCategoricalQuotient j ψ) :
    ∃! e : X ≅ Y, φ ≫ e.hom = ψ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.categoricalQuotientIn_unique
declarations.doc:
Two categorical quotients of a pre-relation in the full subcategory cut out by an object
property are uniquely isomorphic within that subcategory, compatibly with their quotient maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem categoricalQuotientIn_unique (P : ObjectProperty (Over B)) {R U X Y : Over B}
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) (ψ : U ⟶ Y)
    (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotientIn P j φ) (hψ : IsCategoricalQuotientIn P j ψ) :
    ∃! e : X ≅ Y, φ ≫ e.hom = ψ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversalCategoricalQuotientIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048L, part (1).** An `R`-invariant morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` is a *universal
categorical quotient* in a full subcategory `P` of the algebraic spaces over `B`, closed
under fibre products, when `R`, `U` and `X` lie in `P` and for every morphism `f : X' ⟶ X`
of `P` the projection `X' ×_X U ⟶ X'` is the categorical quotient in `P` of the base change
of `j` along `f`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniformCategoricalQuotientIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048L, part (2).** An `R`-invariant morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` is a *uniform
categorical quotient* in a full subcategory `P` of the algebraic spaces over `B`, closed
under fibre products, when `R`, `U` and `X` lie in `P` and for every flat morphism
`f : X' ⟶ X` of `P` the projection `X' ×_X U ⟶ X'` is the categorical quotient in `P` of the
base change of `j` along `f`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.pointOrbit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048N.** The *orbit* of a point of `|U|` under a pre-relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U`:
the set of points joined to it by a finite chain of arrows of `j`, traversed in either
direction, with stationary steps allowed.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev PreRelation.pointOrbit (j : PreRelation R U)
    (u : points B S hS U.left) : Set (points B S hS U.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.pointOrbit_eq_targets_of_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048O.** For a pre-equivalence relation an orbit is cut out by a single arrow: it
consists of the targets of the arrows of the pre-relation whose source is the given point.
declarations.statement:
theorem PreRelation.pointOrbit_eq_targets_of_source (j : PreRelation R U)
    (hj : IsPreEquivalenceRelation j) (u : points B S hS U.left) :
    j.pointOrbit u =
      {u' | ∃ r : points B S hS R.left,
        pointsMap B S hS R.left j.source.left r = u ∧
          pointsMap B S hS R.left j.target.left r = u'}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap_eq_of_mem_pointOrbit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048P.** A morphism out of `U` which is invariant under a pre-relation takes the
same value at any two points in one orbit.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointsMap_eq_of_mem_pointOrbit (j : PreRelation R U)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (φ : U.left ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ)
    {x y : points B S hS U.left} (hy : y ∈ j.pointOrbit x) :
    pointsMap B S hS U.left φ x = pointsMap B S hS U.left φ y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.WeaklyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
Two points of `U` over a field-valued point `p` of `Z` are
*weakly equivalent* when they are joined by a finite chain of arrows of the pre-relation over
the field of `p`, traversed in either direction and with stationary steps allowed.
declarations.statement:
abbrev WeaklyEquivalent (j : PreRelation R U) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z)
    (x y : TestPoint (p.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) U) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.Equivalent
declarations.doc:
Two points of `U` over a field-valued point `p` of `Z` are
*equivalent* when their restrictions to some extension of the field of `p` are weakly
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Equivalent (j : PreRelation R U) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z)
    (x y : TestPoint (p.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) U) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.weakOrbit
declarations.doc:
The *weak orbit* of a point of `U` over a geometric point of
`Z`: its class for weak equivalence over the given algebraically closed field.
declarations.statement:
abbrev weakOrbit (j : PreRelation R U) (p : GeometricPoint B S hS Z)
    (x : TestPoint (p.val.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) U) :
    Set (TestPoint (p.val.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.orbit
declarations.doc:
The *orbit* of a point of `U` over a geometric point of `Z`:
its class for equivalence, that is after allowing one extension of the field.
declarations.statement:
abbrev orbit (j : PreRelation R U) (p : GeometricPoint B S hS Z)
    (x : TestPoint (p.val.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) U) :
    Set (TestPoint (p.val.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.weakOrbit_eq_targets
declarations.doc:
For a pre-equivalence relation the weak orbit of a point is cut out by a
single arrow: it consists of the targets of the arrows whose source is that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakOrbit_eq_targets (j : PreRelation R U) (hj : IsPreEquivalenceRelation j)
    (p : GeometricPoint B S hS Z)
    (x : TestPoint (p.val.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) U) :
    j.weakOrbit p x = {y | j.Rel (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) y x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.orbit_eq_targets_after_extension
declarations.doc:
For a pre-equivalence relation the orbit of a point is cut out by a
single arrow over some extension of the field of the geometric point.
declarations.statement:
theorem orbit_eq_targets_after_extension (j : PreRelation R U)
    (hj : IsPreEquivalenceRelation j) (p : GeometricPoint B S hS Z)
    (x : TestPoint (p.val.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) U) :
    j.orbit p x =
      {y | ∃ (q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z)
          (f : q.siteObject B S hS Z ⟶ p.val.siteObject B S hS Z),
          Z.map f.op p.val.value = q.value ∧
            ∃ x' y' : TestPoint (q.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm q.value) U,
              x'.1 = yoneda.map f ≫ x.1 ∧ y'.1 = yoneda.map f ≫ y.1 ∧
                j.Rel (yonedaEquiv.symm q.value) y' x'}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flippedRelation
declarations.doc:
The *flipped* arrow of a pre-relation, `r ↦ (s(r), t(r))`: the map to `U ×_B U` that
reverses each arrow of `j`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def flippedRelation {R U : Over B} (j : PreRelation R U) : R ⟶ U ⨯ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.composedRelation
declarations.doc:
The endpoint map on composable pairs, `(r, r') ↦ (t(r), s(r'))`: the map to `U ×_B U`
recording the outer endpoints of a pair of arrows of `j` that compose.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def composedRelation {R U : Over B} (j : PreRelation R U) :
    pullback j.source j.target ⟶ U ⨯ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.allPathsRelation_source_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048T, part (5).** The source map of the relation of all finite paths is locally of
finite type when both endpoint maps of the original pre-relation are.
declarations.statement:
theorem allPathsRelation_source_locallyOfFiniteType (P : PathConstruction j)
    (hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.source.left.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.target.left.hom) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS P.allPathsRelation.source.left.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.allPathsRelation_target_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048T, part (5).** The target map of the relation of all finite paths is locally of
finite type when both endpoint maps of the original pre-relation are.
declarations.statement:
theorem allPathsRelation_target_locallyOfFiniteType (P : PathConstruction j)
    (hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.source.left.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.target.left.hom) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS P.allPathsRelation.target.left.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInvariant_allPathsRelation_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048T, part (1).** A morphism out of `U` is invariant under a pre-relation exactly
when it is invariant under the relation of all finite paths that the pre-relation generates.

The codomain is an arbitrary algebraic space over `S`; for a morphism `φ` of algebraic spaces
over `B` take `φ.left`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvariant_allPathsRelation_iff (P : PathConstruction j) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) :
    IsInvariant P.allPathsRelation φ ↔ IsInvariant j φ
declarations.comment: part (1): invariance under the generated relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weakOrbit_allPathsRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048T, part (3).** The weak orbit of a point of `U` at a geometric point of `B` is
unchanged when the pre-relation is replaced by the relation of all finite paths it
generates.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakOrbit_allPathsRelation (p : GeometricPoint site S hS B.obj)
    (x : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) ((overForgetSpace B).obj U)) :
    (presheafPreRelation P.allPathsRelation).weakOrbit p x =
      (presheafPreRelation j).weakOrbit p x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.orbit_allPathsRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048T, part (4).** The orbit of a point of `U` at a geometric point of `B` is
unchanged when the pre-relation is replaced by the relation of all finite paths it
generates.
declarations.statement:
theorem orbit_allPathsRelation (p : GeometricPoint site S hS B.obj)
    (x : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) ((overForgetSpace B).obj U)) :
    (presheafPreRelation P.allPathsRelation).orbit p x =
      (presheafPreRelation j).orbit p x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPreEquivalenceRelation_allPathsRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048T.** The relation generated by a pre-relation of algebraic spaces over `B`,
whose arrows are the finite composable paths of original, identity and reversed arrows, is a
pre-equivalence relation over `B`: on the points of every test scheme over `B` it induces an
equivalence relation.

Reflexivity is witnessed by the identity arrow of a point, symmetry by the reverse of a path,
and transitivity by the concatenation of two paths.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPreEquivalenceRelation_allPathsRelation (P : PathConstruction j) :
    IsPreEquivalenceRelation (presheafPreRelation P.allPathsRelation)
declarations.comment: the generated relation is a pre-equivalence relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_quotientSheafToAllPaths
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048T**, part (2). The canonical map of quotient sheaves `U/R ⟶ U/R_∞`, from the
quotient by a pre-relation to the quotient by the relation of all the finite paths it generates,
is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_quotientSheafToAllPaths (P : PathConstruction j) :
    IsIso (quotientSheafToAllPaths P)
declarations.comment: part (2): the quotient sheaf is unchanged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.equivalent_iff_weaklyEquivalent_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048U.** For a pre-relation whose source and target are locally of finite type,
two points of `U` over a geometric point of `B` are equivalent exactly when they are already
weakly equivalent over the field of that geometric point: no extension of the field is
needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem equivalent_iff_weaklyEquivalent_of_locallyOfFiniteType (j : PreRelation R U)
    (hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.source.left.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.target.left.hom)
    (p : GeometricPoint site S hS B.obj)
    (x y : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value)
      ((overForgetSpace B).obj U)) :
    (presheafPreRelation j).Equivalent p.val x y ↔
      (presheafPreRelation j).WeaklyEquivalent p.val x y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.orbit_eq_weakOrbit_of_large_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048U, part (2).** Over a sufficiently large algebraically closed field the orbit
of a point of `U` under a pre-relation is its weak orbit over the same field: no extension of
the field is needed. The bound is on the relation generated by the pre-relation, and is
uniform in the geometric point and in the point whose orbit is taken.
declarations.statement:
theorem orbit_eq_weakOrbit_of_large_field {j : PreRelation R U} (P : PathConstruction j)
    (p : GeometricPoint site S hS B.obj)
    (hp : IsLargeField site S hS P.allPaths.left.obj p.val.carrier)
    (x : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value)
      ((overForgetSpace B).obj U)) :
    (presheafPreRelation j).orbit p x = (presheafPreRelation j).weakOrbit p x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.equivalent_iff_weaklyEquivalent_of_large_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048U, part (2).** Over a sufficiently large algebraically closed field,
equivalence of two points of `U` under a pre-relation is their weak equivalence over the same
field. The bound is on the relation generated by the pre-relation, and is uniform in the
geometric point and in the pair of points.
declarations.statement:
theorem equivalent_iff_weaklyEquivalent_of_large_field {j : PreRelation R U}
    (P : PathConstruction j) (p : GeometricPoint site S hS B.obj)
    (hp : IsLargeField site S hS P.allPaths.left.obj p.val.carrier)
    (x y : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value)
      ((overForgetSpace B).obj U)) :
    (presheafPreRelation j).Equivalent p.val x y ↔
      (presheafPreRelation j).WeaklyEquivalent p.val x y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant
declarations.doc:
A morphism out of `U` is *set-theoretically invariant* under a
pre-relation when it takes the same value at the two endpoints of every arrow of the
pre-relation between points over an algebraically closed field.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SeparatesOrbits
declarations.doc:
A morphism out of `U` *separates the orbits* of a pre-relation
when it is set-theoretically invariant and two points over an algebraically closed field with
the same image lie in one orbit.
declarations.statement: abbrev SeparatesOrbits (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_iff_eq_of_mem_orbit
declarations.doc:
A morphism from `U` to an algebraic space is set-theoretically invariant under a
pre-relation if and only if, for every algebraically closed field over the base, the induced map
on the points of `U` over that field is constant on the orbits of the pre-relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_iff_eq_of_mem_orbit (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) :
    IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant j φ ↔
      ∀ (p : GeometricPoint B S hS Z)
        (x y : TestPoint (p.val.siteObject B S hS Z) (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value) U),
        y ∈ j.orbit p x → x.1 ≫ φ = y.1 ≫ φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_of_isInvariant
declarations.doc: A morphism which is invariant under a pre-relation is set-theoretically invariant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_of_isInvariant (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) :
    IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant j φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInvariant_of_isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_of_reduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Y.** On a reduced relation space, set-theoretic invariance of a morphism to a
locally separated target implies that the morphism is invariant under the pre-relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvariant_of_isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_of_reduced {R U X : Over Z}
    (j : PreRelation R U)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) (hφ : IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant j φ.left)
    (hR : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS R.left (fun Y : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsReduced Y))
    (hX : IsLocallySeparated B S hS X.hom)
    (hXsheaf : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) X.left) :
    IsInvariant j φ.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.diskToInvolutionQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Z.** The morphism from the formal disk to the quotient of the affine line by
the involution relation given by the power-series variable.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def diskToInvolutionQuotient
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    yoneda.obj (siteFormalDisk k B hS hD) ⟶ (involutionQuotient k B hS).obj
declarations.comment: the coordinate map to the quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.diskToInvolutionQuotientNeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Z.** The morphism from the formal disk to the quotient of the affine line by
the involution relation given by the negative of the power-series variable.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def diskToInvolutionQuotientNeg
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    yoneda.obj (siteFormalDisk k B hS hD) ⟶ (involutionQuotient k B hS).obj
declarations.comment: the negated coordinate map to the quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.diskMaps_agree_on_fieldPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Z.** The two morphisms from the formal disk to the quotient agree after
every field-valued point of the disk.
declarations.statement:
theorem diskMaps_agree_on_fieldPoints
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)]
    (K : Type u) [Field K] (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
    (β : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (g : (Over.mk (ObjectProperty.homMk β : B.obj hK ⟶ B.obj hS) :
      BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS) ⟶ siteFormalDisk k B hS hD) :
    yoneda.map g ≫ diskToInvolutionQuotient k B hS hD =
      yoneda.map g ≫ diskToInvolutionQuotientNeg k B hS hD

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.diskMaps_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Z.** Away from characteristic two, the two morphisms from the formal disk to
the quotient are nevertheless distinct.
declarations.statement:
theorem diskMaps_ne (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    diskToInvolutionQuotient k B hS hD ≠ diskToInvolutionQuotientNeg k B hS hD

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_algebraicSpaces_setTheoreticallyInvariant_not_invariant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Z.** Quasi-separatedness of the target cannot replace local separatedness in
the criterion `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInvariant_of_isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_of_reduced`
(**Stacks 048Y**): over a field in which two is invertible there are an algebraic space `Z`
and algebraic spaces `R`, `U`, `X` over `Z`, a pre-relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` and a morphism
`φ : U ⟶ X` over `Z` such that `φ` is set-theoretically invariant, `R` is reduced, `X` is
quasi-separated over `Z` (and an fppf sheaf), and yet `φ` is not invariant.

The base `Z` is `Spec k`, the relation is the formal disk `Spec k[[x]]` acting on itself by
the identity and by negation of the coordinate, and the morphism is the coordinate map to the
quotient of the affine line by the involution relation of **Stacks 02Z1**, whose
quasi-separatedness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_involutionQuotient`,
converted to quasi-separatedness of the structure morphism by **Stacks 073B** part (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebraicSpaces_setTheoreticallyInvariant_not_invariant (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    ∃ (Z : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (R U X : Over Z)
      (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS Z ∧
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS R.left ∧
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS U.left ∧
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS X.left ∧
        IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant j φ.left ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS R.left (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsReduced T) ∧
        IsQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS X.hom ∧
        Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) X.left ∧
        ¬ IsInvariant j φ.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isInvariant_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Z.** **Stacks 048Y** fails with local separatedness of the target replaced by
quasi-separatedness: over a field in which two is invertible it is not true that for every
algebraic space `Z`, all algebraic spaces `R`, `U`, `X` over `Z`, every pre-relation
`j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` and every morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` over `Z`, set-theoretic invariance of `φ`,
reducedness of `R`, quasi-separatedness of `X` over `Z` and the sheaf condition on `X` imply
that `φ` is invariant.  This is the hypothesis list of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInvariant_of_isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_of_reduced` with
`IsLocallySeparated` replaced by `IsQuasiSeparated`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isInvariant_of_isQuasiSeparated (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    ¬ ∀ (Z : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (R U X : Over Z)
      (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS Z →
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS R.left →
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS U.left →
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS X.left →
        IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant j φ.left →
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS R.left (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsReduced T) →
        IsQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS X.hom →
        Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) X.left →
        IsInvariant j φ.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_agree_on_fieldPoints_ne_and_algebraicSpaces_not_invariant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 048Z.** Over a field in which two is invertible there are reduced
quasi-separated algebraic spaces `X`, `Y` and two morphisms `a, b : Y ⟶ X` which agree on
every field-valued point of `Y` yet are not equal; consequently **Stacks 048Y**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInvariant_of_isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_of_reduced`) does not
hold with local separatedness of the target replaced by quasi-separatedness: there are an
algebraic space `Z`, algebraic spaces `R`, `U`, `X` over `Z`, a pre-relation
`j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` with `R` reduced and `X` quasi-separated over `Z`, and a set-theoretically
invariant morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` over `Z` which is not invariant.

The spaces are `Y = Spec k[[x]]` and `X = 𝔸¹_k/(Δ ⨿ {(x, -x) | x ≠ 0})`, the algebraic space
of **Stacks 02Z1**, and the two morphisms are the coordinate and its negative followed by the
projection to the quotient.  For the second assertion `Z = Spec k`, `R = U = Y` with
`s = 1`, `t = -1`, and `φ = a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_agree_on_fieldPoints_ne_and_algebraicSpaces_not_invariant
    (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    (∃ (X Y : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (a b : Y ⟶ X),
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS X ∧
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS Y ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsReduced T) ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsReduced T) ∧
        IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ X ∧
        IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ Y ∧
        (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
            (β : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of k))
            (g : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (ObjectProperty.homMk β : B.obj hK ⟶ B.obj hS) :
              BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS) ⟶ Y),
          g ≫ a = g ≫ b) ∧
        a ≠ b) ∧
      ∃ (Z : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (R U X : Over Z)
        (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X),
        IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS Z ∧
          IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS R.left ∧
          IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS U.left ∧
          IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS X.left ∧
          IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant j φ.left ∧
          HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS R.left
            (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsReduced T) ∧
          IsQuasiSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hS X.hom ∧
          Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) X.left ∧
          ¬ IsInvariant j φ.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0490, part (1).** A pre-relation is a *set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation*
when the relation it induces on the fibres of the points over every algebraically closed
field in the site is an equivalence relation, arrows being allowed to appear only after a
field extension.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation (j : PreRelation R U) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0490, part (2).** A *set-theoretic equivalence relation* is a universally
injective set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation (j : PreRelation R U) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PreRelation.ContainsRelationImages
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0491, part (2).** A pre-relation *contains the relation images* when its image on
topological points contains the images of the diagonal of `U`, of the flip of the pre-relation
and of the endpoint map on composable pairs of arrows.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev PreRelation.ContainsRelationImages (j : PreRelation R U) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_iff_containsRelationImages
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0491, parts (1) and (2).** A pre-relation is a set-theoretic pre-equivalence
relation exactly when its image on points contains the images of the diagonal, of the flip and
of the endpoint map on composable pairs.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_iff_containsRelationImages
    (j : PreRelation R U) :
    IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation (presheafPreRelation j) ↔
      j.ContainsRelationImages

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.containsRelationImages_iff_exists_geometricRel_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0491, parts (2) and (3).** The three image containments hold exactly when the
relation cut out by the arrows already present over `k` is an equivalence relation for every
algebraically closed field `k` in the site above one cardinal strictly below the size cutoff
of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem containsRelationImages_iff_exists_geometricRel_equivalence (j : PreRelation R U) :
    j.ContainsRelationImages ↔
      ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, κ < site.cutoff ∧ ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
        (hk : site.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
        (β : B.obj.obj (Opposite.op (fieldObject (hS := hS) k hk b))),
        κ < Cardinal.mk k → Equivalence ((presheafPreRelation j).GeometricRel k hk b β)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_iff_geometricRel_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0491, part (4).** For a pre-relation whose source and target are locally of
finite type no cardinal bound is needed: the set-theoretic pre-equivalence condition is
equivalent to the relation of actual arrows being an equivalence relation over *every*
algebraically closed field in the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_iff_geometricRel_equivalence
    (j : PreRelation R U) (_hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.source.left.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS j.target.left.hom) :
    IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation (presheafPreRelation j) ↔
      ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hk : site.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
        (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
        (β : B.obj.obj (Opposite.op (fieldObject (hS := hS) k hk b))),
        Equivalence ((presheafPreRelation j).GeometricRel k hk b β)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_of_isPreEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0492, part (1).** A pre-equivalence relation is a set-theoretic pre-equivalence
relation: over every algebraically closed field over the base, the relation its arrows induce
on the points of `U` — arrows being allowed to appear after an extension of the field — is an
equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_of_isPreEquivalenceRelation
    (j : PreRelation R U) (hj : IsPreEquivalenceRelation j) :
    IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_groupoidPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0492, part (1).** The pre-relation of a groupoid in algebraic spaces is a
set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_groupoidPreRelation
    {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS A) :
    IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation (groupoidPreRelation G)
declarations.comment: part (1): a groupoid in algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_groupoidOfAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0492, part (1).** The pre-relation of the groupoid of an action of a group
algebraic space on an algebraic space is a set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_groupoidOfAction
    (A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (G W : Over A.obj) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G W]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.left) (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W.left) :
    IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation
      (groupoidPreRelation (groupoidOfAction A G W hG hW).groupoid)
declarations.comment: part (1): an action of a group algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_of_isEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0492, part (2).** An equivalence relation is a set-theoretic equivalence
relation: it is a monomorphism, hence universally injective, and a pre-equivalence relation,
hence set-theoretically one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_of_isEquivalenceRelation (j : PreRelation R U)
    (hj : CategoryTheory.IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source) :
    IsSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsPseudoTorsor
declarations.doc:
An action is a pseudo-torsor if its shear map `(g, x) ↦ (g • x, x)` is an

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPseudoTorsor_iff_forall_existsUnique_smul
declarations.doc:
An action is a pseudo-torsor exactly when it is pointwise simply transitive: for every test
object `T`, any two `T`-points of `X` differ by a unique `T`-point of `G`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPseudoTorsor_iff_forall_existsUnique_smul
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C]
    (G X : C) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X] :
    IsPseudoTorsor G X ↔ ∀ (T : C) (x y : T ⟶ X), ∃! g : T ⟶ G, g • x = y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTrivial_iff_exists_globalSection

declarations.statement:

    (G X : C) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X] (hX : IsPseudoTorsor G X) :
    IsTrivialPseudoTorsor G X ↔ Nonempty (𝟙_ C ⟶ X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace.isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049D, Stacks 07VU.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be an algebraic space over
`S`. If `X_red` is a scheme, then `X` is a scheme.

The inclusion of the reduction is a closed immersion bijective on points, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_isClosedImmersion_of_bijective` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_isRepresentable_reduction {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hred : (reduction B S hS X hX).toFunctor.IsRepresentable) :
    X.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isWeaklyRadicial_galoisQuotientBaseChangeToCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049E.** The base change `X_ℚ̄ ⟶ Spec ℚ̄` of the morphism of Stacks 0483 is weakly
radicial.

Over a field-valued point `Spec(K) ⟶ Spec ℚ̄` the fibre has a section, through the projection
of `Spec ℚ̄` onto the Galois quotient; a section is a monomorphism, and it exhibits the trivial,
purely inseparable, extension `K ⊂ K`. The point set of the fibre is a singleton because it
receives the point of the section and because the base change of the universally injective
morphism of Stacks 0483 is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyRadicial_galoisQuotientBaseChangeToCover :
    Space.IsWeaklyRadicial B base hS (isAlgebraicSpace_galoisQuotientBaseChange B hS hU)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B base hS _) (galoisQuotientBaseChangeToCover B hS hU)
declarations.comment: the base change of Example 0483 to ℚ̄ is weakly radicial

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.not_isRadicial_galoisQuotientBaseChangeToCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049E.** The base change `X_ℚ̄ ⟶ Spec ℚ̄` of the morphism of Stacks 0483 is not
radicial.

Were it radicial, the two projections `Spec ℚ̄ ×_ℚ Spec ℚ̄ ⟶ Spec ℚ̄`, which are morphisms from
the reduced scheme `Spec(ℚ̄ ⊗_ℚ ℚ̄)`, would have the same image in the Galois quotient
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.galoisChart_eq_of_isRadicial`). The graph of the
Galois action is the kernel pair of the projection of `Spec ℚ̄` onto its quotient, so the two
projections would be related by a morphism `Spec(ℚ̄ ⊗_ℚ ℚ̄) ⟶ ∐_{g} Spec ℚ̄`, which by
quasi-compactness forces the absolute Galois group of `ℚ` to be finite
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.finite_galoisGroup_of_rel`); it is not
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.infinite_galoisGroup`).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isRadicial_galoisQuotientBaseChangeToCover :
    ¬ Space.IsRadicial B base hS (isAlgebraicSpace_galoisQuotientBaseChange B hS hU)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B base hS _) (galoisQuotientBaseChangeToCover B hS hU)
declarations.comment: the base change of Example 0483 to ℚ̄ is not radicial

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsWeaklyRadicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049E.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *weakly radicial* if for every
field `K` in the chosen site and every `K`-valued point of the target, the point set of the fibre
is a singleton and the fibre admits, over `Spec(K)`, a monomorphism from the spectrum of a purely
inseparable extension of `K`.
declarations.comment: the definition of a weakly radicial morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_app_of_isWeaklyRadicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049E.** A weakly radicial morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is surjective on
`k`-valued points for every algebraically closed field `k` in the chosen site.

The fibre over a `k`-valued point of the target receives a monomorphism from the spectrum of a
purely inseparable extension of `k`, and such an extension of an algebraically closed field is
trivial; the induced morphism of field spectra is therefore an isomorphism, and inverting it
produces a section of the fibre's projection, hence a `k`-valued point of the source over the
given one.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_app_of_isWeaklyRadicial
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsWeaklyRadicial B S hS hX hY f)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (s : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) :
    Function.Surjective (f.app (Opposite.op
      (Over.mk (⟨s⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS) : BigFppfOver B S hS)))
declarations.comment: surjectivity on k-points for k algebraically closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isWeaklyRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_hasPropertyBeta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049E, the analogue of Stacks 0484.** A surjective, universally injective morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` with property `(β)` is weakly radicial.

The source states this without the surjectivity hypothesis, and in that form it is false: a weakly
radicial morphism is surjective (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_of_isWeaklyRadicial`),
while the inclusion of the empty scheme is universally injective and has property `(β)`, see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_universallyInjective_hasPropertyBeta_not_isWeaklyRadicial`.

Over a field-valued point `Spec(K) ⟶ Y` the fibre has a subsingleton point set by universal
injectivity and a nonempty one by surjectivity. Property `(β)` at its unique point is
condition (1) of Stacks 03JU, which is equivalent to condition (4): a monomorphism from the
spectrum of a field `L` representing the point. The composite `Spec(L) ⟶ Spec(K)` is
universally injective, a monomorphism being universally injective, so `K ⊂ L` is purely
inseparable, exactly as in the proof of Stacks 0484.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_hasPropertyBeta
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hinj : UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hbeta : HasPropertyBeta B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    IsWeaklyRadicial B S hS hX hY f
declarations.comment: corrected form of the analogue of 0484, with surjectivity added

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_universallyInjective_hasPropertyBeta_not_isWeaklyRadicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049E, the analogue of Stacks 0484 as stated is false.** As soon as the site
contains the spectrum of a field, there is a universally injective morphism of algebraic
spaces with property `(β)` which is not weakly radicial: the inclusion into `Spec(K)` of the
empty scheme. Its fibre over `Spec(K)` has no point, whereas a weakly radicial morphism has a
one-point fibre over every field-valued point.

The corrected statement, with surjectivity added, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isWeaklyRadicial_of_universallyInjective_of_hasPropertyBeta`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_universallyInjective_hasPropertyBeta_not_isWeaklyRadicial
    (K : Type u) [Field K] (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K))) (s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S) :
    ∃ (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
      (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y),
      UniversallyInjective B S hS f ∧ HasPropertyBeta B S hS f ∧
        ¬ IsWeaklyRadicial B S hS hX hY f
declarations.comment: the analogue of Lemma 0484 without surjectivity is false: a counterexample

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 049J.** A presheaf of sets preserves inverse limits of affine
schemes as filtered colimits of sets, relative to its underlying-scheme functor.
declarations.statement:
abbrev LimitPreserving {C : Type z} [Category C]
    (toScheme : C ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativelyLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 049J.** A transformation is relatively limit preserving when the
presheaf of lifts of every target section is limit preserving over that section's base.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_sectionFiberι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 049K.** The presheaf of lifts of a section `y` of `G` over `X` through
a transformation `a : F ⟶ G` of presheaves of sets on the big fppf site over `S` is the fibre
product

```text
  F_y = F|_{(Sch/X)_fppf} ×_{G|_{(Sch/X)_fppf}} *
```

of presheaves on the big fppf site over `X`, where `*` is the final presheaf and the morphism
`* ⟶ G|_{(Sch/X)_fppf}` is the point named by `y`. That is, the inclusion of the fibre into the
restriction of `F` along the localization functor and its structural morphism to the final
presheaf exhibit it as the fibre product of the restriction of `a` and of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_sectionFiberι :
    IsPullback (sectionFiberι B S hS a X y) (sectionFiberToFinal B S hS a X y)
      (Functor.whiskerLeft (Over.forget X).op a) (pointOfSection B S hS G X y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyLimitPreserving_comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of two relatively limit-preserving transformations is
relatively limit preserving.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyLimitPreserving_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
    (a : F ⟶ G) (b : G ⟶ H)
    (ha : RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, v, max w w', w'} B S hS a)
    (hb : RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, v, max w w', w'} B S hS b) :
    RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, v, max w w', w'} B S hS (a ≫ b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyLimitPreserving_pullback_fst
declarations.doc:
A relatively limit-preserving transformation of presheaves remains so
after pullback along any transformation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyLimitPreserving_pullback_fst
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
    (a : F ⟶ G) (b : H ⟶ G)
    (ha : RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, w'} B S hS a) :
    RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, w'} B S hS
      (pullback.fst b a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isStandardCovering_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049N (1), uniformly in the topology.** Let `T = lim Tᵢ` be an affine scheme written
as an inverse limit of a cofiltered system of affine schemes. A standard `τ`-covering of `T` is,
member by member, the base change along `T ⟶ Tᵢ` of a standard `τ`-covering of `Tᵢ` for some
stage `i`, for each of the five topologies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isStandardCovering_of_isLimit (τ : CoveringTopology)
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [IsAffine c.pt] [∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)]
    {J : Type w} (U : J → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ j, U j ⟶ c.pt)
    (h : IsStandardCovering τ U f) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Uᵢ : J → Scheme.{u}) (fᵢ : ∀ j, Uᵢ j ⟶ D.obj i),
      IsStandardCovering τ Uᵢ fᵢ ∧
        ∀ j : J, Nonempty ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (fᵢ j)) ≅
          Over.mk (f j))
declarations.comment: covering_existence, stated once for AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering rather than separately in the idiom native to each of the five topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardZariskiCovering_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
A finite standard Zariski covering of an affine inverse limit descends to a
standard Zariski covering at some stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardZariskiCovering_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [IsAffine c.pt] [∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)]
    (𝒰 : c.pt.Cover.{w} Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage)
    (h𝒰 : AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardZariskiCovering 𝒰) :
    ∃ (i : I) (𝒰ᵢ : (D.obj i).Cover.{w} Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage)
      (_h𝒰ᵢ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardZariskiCovering 𝒰ᵢ)
      (e : 𝒰.I₀ ≃ 𝒰ᵢ.I₀),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀,
        Nonempty ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (𝒰ᵢ.f (e j))) ≅
          Over.mk (𝒰.f j))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardEtaleCovering_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
A finite standard étale covering of an affine inverse limit descends to a
standard étale covering at some stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardEtaleCovering_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [IsAffine c.pt] [∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)]
    (𝒰 : c.pt.AffineCover.{w} @Etale) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] :
    ∃ (i : I) (𝒰ᵢ : (D.obj i).AffineCover.{w} @Etale)
      (_ : Finite 𝒰ᵢ.I₀) (e : 𝒰.I₀ ≃ 𝒰ᵢ.I₀),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀,
        Nonempty ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (𝒰ᵢ.f (e j))) ≅
          Over.mk (𝒰.f j))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardSmoothCovering_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
A finite standard smooth covering of an affine inverse limit descends to a
standard smooth covering at some stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardSmoothCovering_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [IsAffine c.pt] [∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)]
    {J : Type w} [Finite J]
    (U : J → Scheme.{u}) [∀ j, IsAffine (U j)]
    (f : ∀ j, U j ⟶ c.pt)
    (hf : IsStandardSmoothCovering U f) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Uᵢ : J → Scheme.{u})
      (hUᵢ : ∀ j, IsAffine (Uᵢ j)) (fᵢ : ∀ j, Uᵢ j ⟶ D.obj i),
      (letI : ∀ j, IsAffine (Uᵢ j) := hUᵢ
       IsStandardSmoothCovering Uᵢ fᵢ) ∧
        ∀ j : J,
          Nonempty ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (fᵢ j)) ≅
            Over.mk (f j))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardSyntomicCovering_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
A finite standard syntomic covering of an affine inverse limit descends to a
standard syntomic covering at some stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardSyntomicCovering_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)]
    {J : Type w} (U : J → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ j, U j ⟶ c.pt)
    (hf : IsStandardSyntomicCovering U f) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Uᵢ : J → Scheme.{u}) (fᵢ : ∀ j, Uᵢ j ⟶ D.obj i),
      IsStandardSyntomicCovering Uᵢ fᵢ ∧
        ∀ j : J,
          Nonempty ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (fᵢ j)) ≅
            Over.mk (f j))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardFppfCovering_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
A finite standard fppf covering of an affine inverse limit descends to a
standard fppf covering at some stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardFppfCovering_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)]
    {J : Type w} (U : J → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ j, U j ⟶ c.pt)
    (hf : IsStandardFppfCovering U f) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Uᵢ : J → Scheme.{u}) (fᵢ : ∀ j, Uᵢ j ⟶ D.obj i),
      IsStandardFppfCovering Uᵢ fᵢ ∧
        ∀ j : J,
          Nonempty ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (fᵢ j)) ≅
            Over.mk (f j))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_familyHom_eq_of_baseChange_eq
declarations.doc:
Equality of morphisms of finite families of affine, flat, finitely presented
schemes over a limit holds already at some finite stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_familyHom_eq_of_baseChange_eq
    {I : Type v} [Category.{a} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) (i : I)
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} (D.obj i))
    (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} (D.obj i)) [Finite E.I₀]
    (hE : ∀ j, IsAffineFlatOfFinitePresentation (Over.mk (E.f j)))
    (hF : ∀ j, IsAffineFlatOfFinitePresentation (Over.mk (F.f j)))
    (f g : E.Hom F) (hfg : FamilyHom.BaseChangeEq (c.π.app i) E F f g) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i), FamilyHom.BaseChangeEq (D.map e) E F f g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_familyHom_after_baseChange
declarations.doc:
A morphism of finite standard covering families of an affine inverse limit
descends to a morphism at a finite stage, with its given index map unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_familyHom_after_baseChange
    {I : Type v} [Category.{a} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) (i : I)
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} (D.obj i))
    (F : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} (D.obj i))
    [Finite E.I₀]
    (hE : ∀ k, IsAffineFlatOfFinitePresentation (Over.mk (E.f k)))
    (hF : ∀ k, IsAffineFlatOfFinitePresentation (Over.mk (F.f k)))
    (f : (E.pullback₂ (c.π.app i)).Hom (F.pullback₂ (c.π.app i))) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i)
      (g : (E.pullback₂ (D.map e)).Hom (F.pullback₂ (D.map e))),
      g.s₀ = f.s₀ ∧ ∀ k : E.I₀,
        ∃ (α : (Over.pullback (c.π.app j)).obj
            ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj (Over.mk (E.f k))) ≅
              (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (E.f k)))
          (β : (Over.pullback (c.π.app j)).obj
            ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj (Over.mk (F.f (g.s₀ k)))) ≅
              (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj (Over.mk (F.f (g.s₀ k)))),
          (α.hom.left ≫ pullback.fst (E.f k) (c.π.app i) =
            pullback.fst ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj (Over.mk (E.f k))).hom
              (c.π.app j) ≫ pullback.fst (E.f k) (D.map e)) ∧
          (β.hom.left ≫ pullback.fst (F.f (g.s₀ k)) (c.π.app i) =
            pullback.fst ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj
              (Over.mk (F.f (g.s₀ k)))).hom (c.π.app j) ≫
                pullback.fst (F.f (g.s₀ k)) (D.map e)) ∧
          HEq (α.hom.left ≫ f.h₀ k)
            (((Over.pullback (c.π.app j)).map
              (show Over.mk ((E.pullback₂ (D.map e)).f k) ⟶
                  Over.mk ((F.pullback₂ (D.map e)).f (g.s₀ k)) from
                Over.homMk (g.h₀ k) (g.w₀ k))).left ≫ β.hom.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.limitPreserving_of_isLocallyBijective
declarations.doc:
An fppf sheaf receiving a locally bijective map from a limit-preserving presheaf is
limit preserving. Local injectivity makes sections that agree at the limit agree at a later
stage, and local surjectivity puts every section of the sheaf at a finite stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem limitPreserving_of_isLocallyBijective [UnivLE.{max w w', u}]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (η : F ⟶ G)
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) η]
    [Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) η]
    (hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) G)
    (hF : LimitPreserving.{u, v, w, w', u + 1} (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) F) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, v, w, w', u + 1} (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.limitPreserving_sheafify
declarations.doc: Fppf sheafification of a limit-preserving presheaf is limit preserving.
declarations.statement:
public theorem limitPreserving_sheafify [UnivLE.{max w w', u}]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) v))
    (hF : LimitPreserving.{u, max (u + 1) v, w, w', u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) F) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, max (u + 1) v, w, w', u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)
      ((BigFppfOver.topology B S hS).sheafify F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.limitPreserving_of_fppfCover
declarations.doc:
Limit preservation for an fppf sheaf can be checked on an fppf cover of
the base scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem limitPreserving_of_fppfCover
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} (B.obj hS))
    (hE : IsFppfCovering ⟨B.obj hS, E⟩)
    (hlocal : ∀ i : E.I₀,
      LimitPreserving.{u, v, w, w', u + 1}
        (Over.forget (E.X i) ⋙ B.inclusion)
        ((Over.map (E.f i)).op ⋙ F)) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, v, w, w', u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyLimitPreserving_sheafifyMap
declarations.doc:
Sheafification preserves relative limit preservation of a transformation
of presheaves on the big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyLimitPreserving_sheafifyMap [UnivLE.{max w w', u}]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) v)}
    (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, max (u + 1) v, w, w'}
      B S hS a) :
    RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, max (u + 1) v, w, w'} B S hS
      (sheafifyMap (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) a)
