declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCategoricalQuotient
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` is a *categorical quotient* of a
pre-relation `j` when it is invariant under `j` and every invariant morphism out of `U` factors
uniquely through it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCategoricalQuotient {R U X : Over B} (j : PreRelation R U)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop
declarations.comment: items (2)-(5): the separated, quasi-separated, locally separated and decent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCategoricalQuotientIn
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` is a *categorical quotient in the full subcategory* cut out by an object
property `P` when `R`, `U` and `X` lie in it and the universal property of a categorical quotient
holds against the objects of `P`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCategoricalQuotientIn (P : ObjectProperty (Over B)) {R U X : Over B}
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop
declarations.comment: items (2)-(5): the separated, quasi-separated, locally separated and decent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCategoricalQuotientInSchemes
declarations.doc:
A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of schemes over `T` is a *categorical quotient* of a pre-relation of
schemes when it equalizes the target and the source of the pre-relation and every morphism out of
`U` which does so factors uniquely through it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCategoricalQuotientInSchemes {T : Scheme.{u}} {R U X : Over T}
    (j : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop
declarations.comment: items (2)-(5): the separated, quasi-separated, locally separated and decent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049W**, for algebraic spaces over the base. A categorical quotient of a reduced
algebraic space is reduced. Unconditional.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotient
    {R U X : Over Base} (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotient j φ)
    (hU : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS U.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049W**, for separated algebraic spaces. A categorical quotient in the full
subcategory of separated algebraic spaces, of a reduced algebraic space, is reduced.

The reduction of the target is separated because its inclusion is a closed immersion, hence a
separated morphism by Stacks 04CH, and the target is separated — Stacks 04ZH, part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInSeparated
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {R U X : Over Base} (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotientIn
      (fun Y : Over Base => IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Y.left.obj) j φ)
    (hU : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS U.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049W**, for quasi-separated algebraic spaces. A categorical quotient in the full
subcategory of quasi-separated algebraic spaces, of a reduced algebraic space, is reduced.

The inclusion of the reduction of the target is a closed immersion, hence separated by Stacks
04CH and so quasi-separated by Stacks 03KK; Stacks 04ZH, part (2) then transfers
quasi-separatedness from the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInQuasiSeparated
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {R U X : Over Base} (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotientIn
      (fun Y : Over Base => IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.left.obj) j φ)
    (hU : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS U.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInLocallySeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049W**, for locally separated algebraic spaces. A categorical quotient in the full
subcategory of locally separated algebraic spaces, of a reduced algebraic space, is reduced.

The inclusion of the reduction of the target is a closed immersion, hence separated by Stacks
04CH and so locally separated by Stacks 03KK; Stacks 04ZH, part (3) then transfers local
separatedness from the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInLocallySeparated
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {R U X : Over Base} (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotientIn
      (fun Y : Over Base => IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated B S hS hZ Y.left.obj) j φ)
    (hU : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS U.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049W**, for decent algebraic spaces. A categorical quotient in the full
subcategory of decent algebraic spaces, of a reduced algebraic space, is reduced.

The reduction of the target is decent because the inclusion of a closed subspace is
representable and decency passes to the source of a representable morphism — Stacks 03KF for
property `(γ)`, which is condition (4) of Stacks 03JV.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInDecent
    {R U X : Over Base} (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotientIn
      (fun Y : Over Base => IsDecentSpace B S hS Y.left.obj) j φ)
    (hU : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS U.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.left.obj (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInSchemes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049W**, for schemes. A categorical quotient in the category of schemes over a base
scheme, of a reduced scheme, is reduced.

Unconditional: the reduction of a scheme is its closed subscheme cut out by the nilradical, and
a morphism from a reduced scheme factors uniquely through it by Stacks 0356.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_isCategoricalQuotientInSchemes
    {T : Scheme.{u}} {R U X : Over T} (j : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation R U)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) (hφ : IsCategoricalQuotientInSchemes j φ)
    (hU : IsReduced U.left) : IsReduced X.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_iff_containsRelationImages
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049X, conditions (1) and (2).** A pre-relation of algebraic spaces is a
set-theoretic equivalence relation exactly when it is universally injective and its image on
topological points contains the images of the diagonal of `U`, of its flip, and of the endpoint
map on composable pairs of its arrows.

Universal injectivity is one of the two conditions on either side, and the other two are
equivalent by **Stacks 0491**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_iff_containsRelationImages (j : PreRelation R U) :
    IsSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation (presheafPreRelation j) ↔
      UniversallyInjective site S hS (presheafPreRelation j).left ∧
        j.ContainsRelationImages

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_iff_exists_hasGeometricEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049X, conditions (1) and (3).** A pre-relation of algebraic spaces is a
set-theoretic equivalence relation exactly when, over every algebraically closed field in the
site above one cardinal strictly below the size cutoff of the site, its map on arrows is
injective and the relation its arrows cut out is an equivalence relation.

The equivalence-relation half is **Stacks 0491**. Universal injectivity gives the injectivity
over every sufficiently large field through the descent of a point of `R` along the relative
diagonal of `j`, and conversely injectivity over all sufficiently large fields makes that
diagonal surjective on points, which is universal injectivity by **Stacks 040X**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_iff_exists_hasGeometricEquivalence
    (j : PreRelation R U) :
    IsSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation (presheafPreRelation j) ↔
      ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, κ < site.cutoff ∧ ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
        (hk : site.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
        (β : B.obj.obj (Opposite.op (fieldObject (hS := hS) k hk b))),
        κ < Cardinal.mk k → j.HasGeometricEquivalence k hk b β

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_iff_hasGeometricEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049X, condition (4).** For a pre-relation of algebraic spaces which is decent,
locally separated or quasi-separated the cardinality restriction can be dropped: it is a
set-theoretic equivalence relation exactly when over *every* algebraically closed field in the
site its map on arrows is injective and the relation its arrows cut out is an equivalence
relation.

Under any of the three hypotheses a universally injective pre-relation is radicial by
**Stacks 0484**, and over an algebraically closed field a fibre of a radicial morphism has
exactly one section as soon as it has a point: this gives the injectivity on arrows, and makes
the relation cut out by the arrows present over the field agree with the one of
**Stacks 0490**, where arrows are allowed to appear after a field extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation_iff_hasGeometricEquivalence
    (j : PreRelation R U)
    (hsep : IsDecent site S hS (presheafPreRelation j).left ∨
      IsLocallySeparated site S hS (presheafPreRelation j).left ∨
      IsQuasiSeparated site S hS (presheafPreRelation j).left) :
    IsSetTheoreticEquivalenceRelation (presheafPreRelation j) ↔
      ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hk : site.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
        (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
        (β : B.obj.obj (Opposite.op (fieldObject (hS := hS) k hk b))),
        j.HasGeometricEquivalence k hk b β

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_iff_isSurjective_invarianceToRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049Y, part (1).** A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` over the base, with `X` an algebraic
space, is set-theoretically invariant under a pre-relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` if and only if
the projection `p : (U ×_X U) ×_{U ×_Z U} R ⟶ R` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticallyInvariant_iff_isSurjective_invarianceToRelation
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left) (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) :
    IsSetTheoreticallyInvariant j φ.left ↔
      IsSurjective B S hS (j.invarianceToRelation φ).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.separatesOrbits_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049Y, part (3).** If both projections of the square are surjective, then the
morphism `φ` separates the orbits of the pre-relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem separatesOrbits_of_isSurjective (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left)
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hp : IsSurjective B S hS (j.invarianceToRelation φ).left)
    (hq : IsSurjective B S hS (j.invarianceToSelfFibreProduct φ).left) :
    SeparatesOrbits j φ.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049Y, part (3).** If both projections of the square are surjective, then the
pre-relation is a set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation_of_isSurjective
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left) (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hp : IsSurjective B S hS (j.invarianceToRelation φ).left)
    (hq : IsSurjective B S hS (j.invarianceToSelfFibreProduct φ).left) :
    IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.separatesOrbits_iff_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049Y, part (2).** For a set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation, a morphism
`φ : U ⟶ X` over the base, with `X` an algebraic space, separates the orbits of the
pre-relation if and only if both projections `p` and `q` of the square are surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem separatesOrbits_iff_isSurjective (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left)
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) (hj : IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation j) :
    SeparatesOrbits j φ.left ↔
      (IsSurjective B S hS (j.invarianceToRelation φ).left ∧
        IsSurjective B S hS (j.invarianceToSelfFibreProduct φ).left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.separatesOrbits_iff_isSurjective_toSelfFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049Y, part (4).** If `φ : U ⟶ X` is invariant under a set-theoretic
pre-equivalence relation `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U`, with `X` an algebraic space, then `φ` separates
the orbits of `j` if and only if the induced morphism `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_X U` is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem separatesOrbits_iff_isSurjective_toSelfFibreProduct
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left) (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ.left) (hj : IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation j) :
    SeparatesOrbits j φ.left ↔
      IsSurjective B S hS (j.toSelfFibreProduct φ hφ).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOrbitSpace_iff_isSurjective_toSelfFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 049Z.** Let `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` be a set-theoretic pre-equivalence relation and
let `φ : U ⟶ X` be a morphism over the base whose target is an algebraic space. Then `φ` is
an orbit space for `j` if and only if

1. `φ` is invariant, `t ≫ φ = s ≫ φ`,
2. the induced morphism `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_X U` is surjective, and
3. the morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` is surjective.

Condition (2) is stated for the morphism `(t, s)` built from the proof of condition (1), so
the three conditions appear as an existential over that proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOrbitSpace_iff_isSurjective_toSelfFibreProduct
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left) (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hj : IsSetTheoreticPreEquivalenceRelation j) :
    IsOrbitSpace j φ.left ↔
      ∃ hφ : IsInvariant j φ.left,
        IsSurjective B S hS (j.toSelfFibreProduct φ hφ).left ∧
          IsSurjective B S hS φ.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOrbitSpace_iff_geometricPoints_quotient_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A0.** For a pre-relation whose relation space and whose source are locally of
finite type over the base, an invariant morphism out of `U` is an orbit space for the
pre-relation exactly when, over every algebraically closed field-valued point of the base, it
induces a bijection from the quotient of the points of `U` by the relation generated by the
pre-relation onto the points of the target: every point of the target over that point of the
base lifts, and two points of `U` have the same image precisely when they are weakly
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOrbitSpace_iff_geometricPoints_quotient_bijective {X : Over B}
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hR : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS R.hom.hom)
    (hU : IsLocallyOfFiniteType site S hS U.hom.hom)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ.left) :
    IsOrbitSpace (presheafPreRelation j) φ.left.hom ↔
      ∀ p : GeometricPoint site S hS B.obj,
        (∀ y : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value)
            ((overForgetSpace B).obj X),
          ∃ x : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value)
            ((overForgetSpace B).obj U), x.1 ≫ φ.left.hom = y.1) ∧
        (∀ x y : TestPoint p.val.siteObject (yonedaEquiv.symm p.val.value)
            ((overForgetSpace B).obj U),
          x.1 ≫ φ.left.hom = y.1 ≫ φ.left.hom ↔
            (presheafPreRelation j).WeaklyEquivalent p.val x y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCoarseQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A2.** A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` is a *coarse
quotient* of a pre-relation `j` when it is a categorical quotient of `j` and an orbit space
for it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCoarseQuotient {R U X : Over B} (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) :
    Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCoarseQuotientInSchemes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A2.** A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of schemes over the base scheme `S`, with `R`,
`U` and `X` contained in the big fppf site, is a *coarse quotient in schemes* of a
pre-relation `j` of schemes over `S` when it is a categorical quotient in schemes of `j`
and an orbit space for it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCoarseQuotientInSchemes {R U X : Over S} (hR : site.Contains R.left)
    (hU : site.Contains U.left) (hX : site.Contains X.left)
    (j : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsInvariantClosedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, condition (2).** An invariant morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` has *closed invariant
images* when for every `R`-invariant closed subset `Z ⊆ |U|` the image `φ(Z)` is closed in
`|X|`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsInvariantClosedMap (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) : Prop
declarations.comment: condition (2): invariant closed subsets have closed image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsInvariantClosedMapInter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, condition (3).** Condition (2) holds, and moreover for every pair of
`R`-invariant closed subsets `Z₁, Z₂ ⊆ |U|` one has `φ(Z₁ ∩ Z₂) = φ(Z₁) ∩ φ(Z₂)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsInvariantClosedMapInter (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) : Prop
declarations.comment: condition (3): intersections of invariant closed subsets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsStronglySubmersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, condition (4).** An invariant morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` is *strongly
submersive* when the morphism `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_X U` assembled from the target and the source
of `j` is universally submersive.

Invariance of `φ` is exactly the commutation `t ≫ φ = s ≫ φ` needed to form that morphism,
so it is taken as an argument.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsStronglySubmersive (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniformlySubmersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, uniform condition (1).** Condition (1) holds after every flat base
change.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsUniformlySubmersive : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniformlyInvariantClosedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, uniform condition (2).** Condition (2) holds after every flat base
change.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsUniformlyInvariantClosedMap : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversallyInvariantClosedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, universal condition (2).** Condition (2) holds after every base
change.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsUniversallyInvariantClosedMap : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniformlyInvariantClosedMapInter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, uniform condition (3).** Condition (3) holds after every flat base
change.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsUniformlyInvariantClosedMapInter : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversallyInvariantClosedMapInter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, universal condition (3).** Condition (3) holds after every base
change.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsUniversallyInvariantClosedMapInter : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniformlyStronglySubmersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, uniform condition (4).** Condition (4) holds after every flat base
change.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev IsUniformlyStronglySubmersive : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversallyStronglySubmersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04A4, universal condition (4).** Condition (4) holds after every base
change.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev IsUniversallyStronglySubmersive : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.invariantFunctionSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AA**, part (1).  The *sheaf of `R`-invariant functions* `(φ_*O_U)^R` of an
`R`-invariant morphism `φ : U ⟶ X`: the equalizer, on the small étale site of `X`, of the two
maps `φ_*t^♯, φ_*s^♯ : φ_*O_U ⟶ φ'_*O_R` given by pulling functions back along the target and
the source of the pre-relation.

Its inclusion into `φ_*O_U` as an `O_X`-subalgebra is `CategoryTheory.Limits.equalizer.ι`,
which is a monomorphism.
declarations.comment: part (1): the sheaf of invariant functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasInvariantFunctions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AA**, part (2).  *The functions on `X` are the `R`-invariant functions on `U`*
when the natural map `O_X ⟶ (φ_*O_U)^R` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev HasInvariantFunctions {R U : Over B} {X : AlgebraicSpaces site S hS}
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U.left ⟶ X) (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2): the functions on X are the invariant functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGoodQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AC.** A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` is a *good quotient*
of a pre-relation `j` when it is `R`-invariant, affine and surjective, condition (3) of
**Stacks 04A4** holds for it universally, and the functions on `X` are the `R`-invariant
functions on `U`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsGoodQuotient {B : AlgebraicSpaces site S hS} {R U X : Over B} (j : PreRelation R U)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGeometricQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AE.** A morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` is a *geometric
quotient* of a pre-relation `j` when it is an orbit space for `j`, universally submersive,
and the functions on `X` are the `R`-invariant functions on `U`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsGeometricQuotient {B : AlgebraicSpaces site S hS} {R U X : Over B}
    (j : PreRelation R U) (φ : U ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFiniteType_classifyingStack_of_smoothSchemeCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AH.** Let `k` be a field and let `G` be an affine group scheme over `k`. If the
classifying stack `[Spec(k)/G]` has a smooth surjective covering by a scheme, then `G` is of
finite type over `k`.

The covering hypothesis is the third clause of Stacks 026O for the classifying stack. By
Stacks 04WZ the classifying stack is then algebraic, and by the half of Stacks 06PL going from
algebraicity to flatness and local finite presentation, the group is locally of finite
presentation over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_classifyingStack_of_smoothSchemeCovering
    (G : Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk
      (Space.terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).obj
      (Space.terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).property)
    (hAffine : Space.IsAffineHom C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.hom)
    (hcov :
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver C (Spec (.of k)) hk)
        (f : (schemeFibredCategory C (Spec (.of k)) hk U).val ⥤ᵇ
          (classifyingStack C hk G).val),
        IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C (Spec (.of k)) hk f ∧
          ∀ (V : BigFppfOver C (Spec (.of k)) hk)
            (y : BigFppfOver C V.left.1 V.left.2 ⥤ (classifyingStack C hk G).val.obj)
            (_hy : y ⋙ (classifyingStack C hk G).val.p = Over.map V.hom)
            (F : (BigFppfOver C V.left.1 V.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
            (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace C V.left.1 V.left.2 F),
            Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
              (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map V.hom)
                (schemeFibredCategory C (Spec (.of k)) hk U).val.p
                (classifyingStack C hk G).val.p y f.toFunctor)
              (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
              (let g := (algebraicSpaceMap C (Spec (.of k)) hk V
                ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor C V.left.1 (Spec (.of k)) V.left.2 hk
                  V.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom
               Space.IsSurjective C (Spec (.of k)) hk g ∧
                 Space.IsSmooth C (Spec (.of k)) hk g)) :
    Space.IsFiniteType C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_flat_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04AI.** A locally finitely presented morphism over a stage which
becomes flat over the inverse limit is flat at some later stage.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_flat_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : Functor I Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [IsCofiltered I]
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    (hc : IsLimit c)
    [Flat ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀), Flat ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AJ.** A smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isSmooth
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : F ⟶ G}
    (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_relativelyLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AK.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` is locally of finite
presentation if and only if it is relatively limit preserving as a transformation of functors
on the big fppf site of `S`.

Both conditions are read at index categories in the universe of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_relativelyLimitPreserving
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f ↔
      RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyLimitPreserving_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation is relatively
limit preserving, for index categories in the universe of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyLimitPreserving_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    {a : F ⟶ G} (ha : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS a) :
    RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} B S hS a
declarations.comment: locally of finite presentation implies relatively limit preserving

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_relativelyLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AK, the implication from relative limit preservation towards local finite
presentation.** A relatively limit-preserving transformation of presheaves on the big fppf site
of `S` is locally of finite presentation as a morphism of algebraic spaces.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_relativelyLimitPreserving` with its
scheme-level input discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_relativelyLimitPreserving_yoneda_map` — the
implication (2) ⇒ (1) of Stacks 01ZC for a morphism of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_relativelyLimitPreserving
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} B S hS f) :
    Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f
declarations.comment:
the implication from relatively limit preserving to locally of finite
presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallyEtale_of_etale
declarations.doc: An étale representable transformation on the big fppf site is formally étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallyEtale_of_etale
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a) :
    FormallyEtale a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_of_etale
declarations.doc: An étale representable transformation on the big fppf site is formally smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallySmooth_of_etale
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a) :
    FormallySmooth a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AL, part (1).** A smooth representable transformation on the big fppf site is
formally smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallySmooth_of_smooth
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Smooth.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a) :
    FormallySmooth a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_formallyEtale_formallyUnramified_of_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AL.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` and `G` be set-valued functors on the big
fppf site over `S`, and let `a : F ⟶ G` be a representable transformation of functors.  Then

1. if `a` is smooth it is formally smooth;
2. if `a` is étale it is formally étale;
3. if `a` is unramified it is formally unramified.

Each part is proved by turning the lifting problem into one for the scheme representing the
base change of `a` along a point of the target, where the corresponding implication for
morphisms of schemes applies; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_of_smooth`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallyEtale_of_etale` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallyUnramified_of_unramified`, which this statement assembles.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallySmooth_formallyEtale_formallyUnramified_of_representable
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (a : F ⟶ G) :
    ((MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Smooth.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a → FormallySmooth a) ∧
      ((MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a → FormallyEtale a) ∧
      ((MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Unramified.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a → FormallyUnramified a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallyUnramified_of_unramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04AL.** An unramified representable transformation is
formally unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallyUnramified_of_unramified
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Unramified.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a) :
    FormallyUnramified a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmooth_iff_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AM.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is smooth exactly when it is locally
of finite presentation and formally smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_iff_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsSmooth B S hS f ↔ IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f ∧ FormallySmooth f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmooth_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_formallySmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AM, the implication towards smoothness.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` which is locally of finite presentation and formally smooth is smooth.

Smoothness of `f` is a property of its étale charts, so there is nothing to descend: a chart
`h : U ⟶ V` is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_lift_scheme_of_formallySmooth` solves every lifting problem for
it along a first-order thickening of affine schemes *contained in the site*. That is exactly
the hypothesis of `Stacks.Smooth.smooth_of_exists_lift_of_size_lt`, which upgrades it to
smoothness: the only thickening the criterion needs is the spectrum of a polynomial
presentation of the sections over an affine chart, and the site contains it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_formallySmooth
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) (hf : FormallySmooth f) :
    IsSmooth B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AM, the implication from smoothness, for a representable morphism.** A smooth
representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite presentation and
formally smooth.

Local finite presentation is Tag 04AJ. For formal smoothness, smoothness of a representable
morphism is smoothness of each of its base changes to an object of the site by Tag 03MJ, so the
base change of `f` along a section `y` of the target over the thickened test object is a smooth
morphism of schemes; the scheme case Tag 02H6 extends the section of that base change cut out
by the given section of `X` over the test object, and the extension is a morphism of the site
because the inclusion of the site into schemes is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth_of_isSmooth
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f ∧ FormallySmooth f
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (2), for a representable morphism

registrations.name: BinaryCofan
registrations.comment:
A coproduct is a limiting binary cofan, so this in combination with `IsColimit`
  covers binary coproducts. API specific to binary coproducts is provided in the namespace
  `BinaryCofan.IsColimit`, while API that holds more generally (like uniqueness up to isomorphism)
  is provided in the namespace `IsColimit`.

registrations.name: BinaryCofan.IsColimit.mk
registrations.comment: A constructor for `IsColimit` using the usual data of a binary coproduct

registrations.name: HasBinaryCoproduct
registrations.comment: Prop-valued typeclass stating that two objects have a product

registrations.name: coprod
registrations.comment: A choice of coproduct, when one exists

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.hasLimitsOfShape_isConnected_iff_hasEqualizers_and_hasPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AT.** A category `C` admits limits over every finite connected shape
if and only if it has equalizers and pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLimitsOfShape_isConnected_iff_hasEqualizers_and_hasPullbacks
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] :
    (∀ (J : Type) [SmallCategory J] [FinCategory J] [IsConnected J], HasLimitsOfShape J C) ↔
      (HasEqualizers C ∧ HasPullbacks C)

declarations.name: nonempty_finite_limits_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AU**. For a category `C`, having every limit indexed by a finite nonempty shape is
equivalent to having binary products together with equalizers, and equivalent to having binary
products together with pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_finite_limits_tfae :
    List.TFAE
      [ HasNonemptyFiniteLimits C,
        HasBinaryProducts C ∧ HasEqualizers C,
        HasBinaryProducts C ∧ HasPullbacks C ]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimitsOfShape_isConnected_iff_hasCoequalizers_and_hasPushouts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AV.** A category `C` admits colimits over every finite connected shape
if and only if it has coequalizers and pushouts.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimitsOfShape_isConnected_iff_hasCoequalizers_and_hasPushouts
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] :
    (∀ (J : Type) [SmallCategory J] [FinCategory J] [IsConnected J], HasColimitsOfShape J C) ↔
      (HasCoequalizers C ∧ HasPushouts C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.HasNonemptyFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
`HasNonemptyFiniteColimits C` says that `C` has all colimits of shape `J` for `J` a
small, finite, *nonempty* category; equivalently, every nonempty finite diagram in `C`
has a colimit. Unlike Mathlib's `HasFiniteColimits` this deliberately omits the empty
shape, so it does not require an initial object.
declarations.statement: class HasNonemptyFiniteColimits : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.hasNonemptyFiniteColimits_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNonemptyFiniteColimits_tfae :
    List.TFAE
      [ HasNonemptyFiniteColimits C
      , HasBinaryCoproducts C ∧ HasCoequalizers C
      , HasBinaryCoproducts C ∧ HasPushouts C ]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCofiltered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AZ.** A diagram `M : I ⥤ C` is *cofiltered* (or *codirected*) if
`I` is nonempty, every pair of objects of `I` admits morphisms from a common
object, and every pair of parallel morphisms of `I` is equalized, after applying
`M`, by precomposition with a further morphism.
declarations.statement:
structure Functor.IsCofiltered {I : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} I] {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} C]
    (M : I ⥤ C) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isCofiltered_id_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04AZ.** An index category `I` is cofiltered in the sense of Stacks —
the identity diagram `𝟭 I` is a cofiltered diagram — exactly when it is
cofiltered in the sense of Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`. Since
`(𝟭 I).map f = f`, condition (3) for `𝟭 I` reads `c ≫ a = c ≫ b` in `I`, so both
directions are a repackaging of the same data.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isCofiltered_id_iff (I : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} I] :
    (𝟭 I).IsCofiltered ↔ _root_.CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered I

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasExactColimitsOfShape_of_isPseudofiltered
declarations.doc:
Let `J` be an index category satisfying the assumptions of Stacks 002X: every span
`y ← x → z` is completed by some commutative square, and every pair of parallel morphisms
`a b : x ⟶ y` is coequalized by some `c : y ⟶ z`. Then taking colimits of diagrams over `J` in an
abelian category with exact filtered colimits is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem CategoryTheory.hasExactColimitsOfShape_of_isPseudofiltered {C : Type u}
    [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [Limits.HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} C] [AB5OfSize.{w, w} C]
    {J : Type w} [Category.{w} J]
    (hspan : ∀ ⦃x y z : J⦄ (a : x ⟶ y) (b : x ⟶ z), ∃ (t : J) (c : y ⟶ t) (d : z ⟶ t),
      a ≫ c = b ≫ d)
    (hpar : ∀ ⦃x y : J⦄ (a b : x ⟶ y), ∃ (z : J) (c : y ⟶ z), a ≫ c = b ≫ c) :
    HasExactColimitsOfShape J C
declarations.comment:
Stated as `HasExactColimitsOfShape J C`, i.e. `colim : (J ⥤ C) ⥤ C` preserves
finite limits, which for a left adjoint is exactness and is the form of `Stacks 00DB` the source
asks for. The assumptions of `Stacks 002X` are spelled out because Mathlib has no predicate for
a pseudofiltered category. Stated for an arbitrary abelian category with colimits of size `w`
whose filtered colimits are exact, instead of the source's abelian groups, since the source's
proof uses only that; AB4 is derived from AB5 rather than assumed.

declarations.name: Algebra.Smooth.exists_span_eq_top_isStandardSmooth_algEquiv_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `R → R'` be a surjective ring map (for instance `R' = R ⧸ I`) and let `R' → S'` be
smooth. Then there are elements `g ∈ S'` generating the unit ideal of `S'` such that each `S'_g` is
isomorphic as an `R'`-algebra to `R' ⊗[R] S` for some standard smooth `R`-algebra `S`; that is,
`S'` is, locally on `Spec S'`, a base change of a standard smooth `R`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Smooth.exists_span_eq_top_isStandardSmooth_algEquiv_tensorProduct
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (R' : Type v) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R R'))
    (S' : Type w) [CommRing S'] [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra.Smooth R' S'] :
    ∃ s : Set S', Ideal.span s = ⊤ ∧ ∀ g ∈ s,
      ∃ (S : Type u) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : Algebra R S) (_ : Algebra.IsStandardSmooth R S),
        Nonempty (Localization.Away g ≃ₐ[R'] R' ⊗[R] S)
declarations.comment:
The source's `R/I → S̄` is stated for an arbitrary surjection `R → R'`, which is
what the proof uses (it lifts the relations along `R[x] → R'[x]`); the source's form is the case
`R' = R ⧸ I`, by `Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective`. The source's `S_i/I S_i` is the base change
`R' ⊗[R] S`, identified with that quotient over `R ⧸ I` by
`Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor`. The parenthetical `(standard)` is taken as
the assertion. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange_injective
declarations.doc:
**The sequence of differentials of a tower is exact on the left**: let `R → A → B` be ring
maps such that `H₁(L_{B/A}) = 0`, for instance with `A → B` smooth. Then the canonical map
`B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} → Ω_{B/R}` is injective, so that `0 → B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} → Ω_{B/R} → Ω_{B/A} → 0` is
a short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange_injective (R : Type*) [CommRing R]
    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B]
    [IsScalarTower R A B] [Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent A B)] :
    Function.Injective (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange R A B)
declarations.comment:
Exactness at `C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A}`, the one node of the sequence that is not already
in Mathlib; the other two are `KaehlerDifferential.exact_mapBaseChange_map` and
`KaehlerDifferential.map_surjective`. Stated under `H₁(L_{C/B}) = 0`, the hypothesis the
source's second proof uses, which the tag's smoothness gives by instance inference. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: SheafTheoreticallyEmpty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04B5.** An object `U` of a site is *sheaf theoretically empty* if the
sheafification of the canonical map `∅ ⟶ h_U` from the initial presheaf to the presheaf
represented by `U` is an isomorphism of sheaves.
declarations.statement: def SheafTheoreticallyEmpty [HasWeakSheafify J (Type v)] (U : C) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksSheafTheoreticallyEmpty.tfae_sheafTheoreticallyEmpty
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_sheafTheoreticallyEmpty [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] (U : C) :
    TFAE [IsIso ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).map (emptyPresheafTo (yoneda.obj U))),
      ∀ F : Sheaf J (Type u), Subsingleton (F.obj.obj (op U)) ∧ Nonempty (F.obj.obj (op U)),
      Subsingleton ((sheafify J (emptyPresheaf (C := C))).obj (op U)) ∧
        Nonempty ((sheafify J (emptyPresheaf (C := C))).obj (op U)),
      Nonempty ((sheafify J (emptyPresheaf (C := C))).obj (op U)),
      (⊥ : Sieve U) ∈ J U]

declarations.name: StacksSheafTheoreticallyEmpty.isIso_map_emptyPresheafTo_of_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04B6**, final assertion.  If `U` is sheaf theoretically empty, then so is `U'` for
every morphism `U' ⟶ U` of `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_map_emptyPresheafTo_of_hom [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] {U U' : C} (f : U' ⟶ U)
    (h : IsIso ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).map (emptyPresheafTo (yoneda.obj U)))) :
    IsIso ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).map (emptyPresheafTo (yoneda.obj U')))

declarations.name: IsAlmostCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04B7.** A functor `u : C ⥤ D` between sites `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` is *almost
cocontinuous* if for every object `U` of `C` and every covering sieve `S` of `u U` there is a
covering sieve `T` of `U` such that each arrow `f : V ⟶ U` in `T` either has `u V` sheaf
theoretically empty, or has `u f` in `S`.
declarations.statement:
def IsAlmostCocontinuous (u : C ⥤ D) (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (K : GrothendieckTopology D) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_homEquiv_symm_whiskerLeft_toSheafify_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04B8.** Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites and let `u : C ⥤ D` be continuous and
almost cocontinuous (Stacks 04B7). Let `G` be a presheaf of sets on `D` such that `G(V)` is a
singleton whenever `V` is sheaf theoretically empty. Then `(u^p G)^# = u^p(G^#)`: the canonical
morphism of sheaves `(u^p G)^# ⟶ u^s(G^#)`, the transpose under the sheafification adjunction of
`u^p` of the unit `G ⟶ G^#`, is an isomorphism.

Sheaves are of sets in the universe `max u₁ v₁` of a site whose objects lie in `Type u₁` and whose
morphisms lie in `Type v₁`, as for Mathlib's sheafification of presheaves of types; in particular
this covers small sites with sheaves of sets. In that setting sheafification exists on both sites
and inverts exactly the locally bijective morphisms
(`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.WEqualsLocallyBijective`), both by instances.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_homEquiv_symm_whiskerLeft_toSheafify_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) [u.IsContinuous J K]
    (hu : IsAlmostCocontinuous u J K) (G : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u₁ v₁))
    (hG : ∀ V : D, SheafTheoreticallyEmptySite K V → Nonempty (Unique (G.obj (op V)))) :
    IsIso (((sheafificationAdjunction J (Type (max u₁ v₁))).homEquiv (u.op ⋙ G)
      ((u.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (max u₁ v₁)) J K).obj
        ((presheafToSheaf K (Type (max u₁ v₁))).obj G))).symm
      (Functor.whiskerLeft u.op (toSheafify K G)))
declarations.comment:
For `u` continuous and almost cocontinuous and `G` a presheaf of sets on `D` with
  `G(V)` a singleton for every sheaf theoretically empty `V`, the canonical morphism
  `(u^p G)^# ⟶ u^p(G^#)` is an isomorphism.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesColimitsOfShape_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04B9.** Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites and let `u : C ⥤ D` be continuous and
almost cocontinuous, and assume sheafification of `Type w`-valued presheaves on `(D, K)` inverts
exactly the locally bijective morphisms. Then `u^s = u^p : Sh(D) ⥤ Sh(C)`, restriction of sheaves
of sets along `u.op`, preserves colimits of every connected shape `I` for which `I`-shaped colimits
of sets exist — in particular pushouts (`WalkingSpan`) and coequalizers (`WalkingParallelPair`),
and more generally every finite connected shape.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) [u.IsContinuous J K]
    (hu : IsAlmostCocontinuous u J K) [HasWeakSheafify J (Type w)] [HasWeakSheafify K (Type w)]
    [K.WEqualsLocallyBijective (Type w)] (I : Type t) [Category.{t'} I] [IsConnected I]
    [HasColimitsOfShape I (Type w)] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape I (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type w) J K)
declarations.comment:
For `u` continuous and almost cocontinuous, `u^s = u^p : Sh(D) → Sh(C)` commutes
  with pushouts and coequalizers, and more generally with finite connected colimits.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites.preservesColimitsOfShape_pushforward_morphismOfTopoi_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BA.** Let `f : D → C` be a morphism of sites (Stacks 00X1) associated to the
continuous functor `u : C ⥤ D`, so that `f_* : Sh(D) ⥤ Sh(C)` is the pushforward of the morphism
of topoi attached to `f` (Stacks 00XC), namely restriction of sheaves of sets along `u.op`. If `u`
is almost cocontinuous (Stacks 04B7), then `f_*` preserves colimits of every connected shape whose
colimits exist — in particular pushouts and coequalizers, which are connected shapes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_pushforward_morphismOfTopoi_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
    {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type w} [SmallCategory D] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {u : C ⥤ D} (hf : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K)
    (hu : IsAlmostCocontinuous u J K) (I : Type t) [Category.{t'} I] [IsConnected I]
    [HasColimitsOfShape I (Type w)] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape I hf.morphismOfTopoi.pushforward
declarations.comment:
For a morphism of sites `f : D → C` whose continuous functor `u : C → D` is almost
  cocontinuous, `f_*` commutes with pushouts and coequalizers, and more generally with finite
  connected colimits.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.preservesLimitsOfShape_of_isConnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BB.** Let `C` be a site and let `U` be an object of `C`. Let `L` be a left adjoint
of the restriction functor `j_U^{-1} = J.overPullback : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh(C/U)`, i.e. let `L` be
`j_{U!}`. Then `L` commutes with limits of every connected shape `K`; in particular it commutes
with fibre products (`K = WalkingCospan`) and equalizers (`K = WalkingParallelPair`), and hence
carries subsheaf inclusions to subsheaf inclusions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesLimitsOfShape_of_isConnected {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (U : C) [HasWeakSheafify J (Type v)]
    [HasWeakSheafify (J.over U) (Type v)] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (Type v)]
    {L : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type v) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type v)} (adj : L ⊣ J.overPullback (Type v) U)
    {K : Type w} [Category.{w'} K] [IsConnected K] :
    Limits.PreservesLimitsOfShape K L
declarations.comment:
j_{U!} commutes with fibre products and equalizers, and more generally with
connected limits; in particular it preserves subsheaf inclusions.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exactFunctor_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BD (1).** Let `f : D → C` be a morphism of sites associated to the continuous
functor `v : C ⥤ D`, and assume `v` is almost cocontinuous. Then the direct image
`f_* = v^s : Ab(D) ⥤ Ab(C)`, restriction of sheaves of abelian groups along `v.op`, is exact.

The four site universes are unrelated and there is no hypothesis beyond the source's. Both
sheafification facts the right exact half needs — existence, and that sheafification inverts
exactly the locally bijective morphisms, which is what makes `Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat` abelian —
are available at the universe `max uC vC uD vD` that a statement about two sites at once is
forced to use, because that universe dominates each site's own `max u v`; see
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hasSheafify_addCommGrpCat` and
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.wEqualsLocallyBijective_addCommGrpCat`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exactFunctor_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {v : C ⥤ D}
    (hv : IsMorphismOfSites.{max uC vC uD vD} v J K)
    (ha : IsAlmostCocontinuous v J K) :
    letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
    exactFunctor (Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD})
      (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD})
      (v.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC uD vD} J K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exactFunctor_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_isAlmostCocontinuous_of_smallCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BD (1)** for sites that are small categories, with sheaves of abelian groups in the
site's own universe: the setting of the source, in which the hypotheses are exactly the source's,
namely a morphism of sites whose continuous functor is almost cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exactFunctor_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_isAlmostCocontinuous_of_smallCategory
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {v : C ⥤ D}
    (hv : IsMorphismOfSites.{u} v J K) (ha : IsAlmostCocontinuous v J K) :
    letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
    exactFunctor (Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (v.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u} J K)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.PushforwardRightExact.exactFunctor_pushforward_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BD (2).** Let `f : D → C` be a morphism of sites associated to the continuous
functor `v : C ⥤ D` with `v` almost cocontinuous, and let `f^♯ : S ⟶ f_* R` make `f` a morphism of
ringed sites. Then the direct image `f_* : Mod(R) ⥤ Mod(S)` is exact.

As in part (1) this additionally assumes that sheafification of `AddCommGrpCat.{m}`-valued
presheaves exists and inverts exactly the locally bijective morphisms, for both topologies; that is
what makes the two categories of sheaves of modules abelian, and it holds automatically in the
setting of the source, as recorded by
`exactFunctor_pushforward_of_isAlmostCocontinuous_of_smallCategory`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exactFunctor_pushforward_of_isAlmostCocontinuous
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {v : C ⥤ D}
    (hv : IsMorphismOfSites.{max uC vC uD vD} v J K)
    (ha : IsAlmostCocontinuous v J K)
    {S : Sheaf J RingCat.{r}} {R : Sheaf K RingCat.{r}}
    (φ : letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
      S ⟶ (v.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{r} J K).obj R)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{m}] [HasSheafify K AddCommGrpCat.{m}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{m}]
    [K.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{m}] :
    letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
    exactFunctor (SheafOfModules.{m} R) (SheafOfModules.{m} S)
      (SheafOfModules.pushforward φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.PushforwardRightExact.exactFunctor_pushforward_of_isAlmostCocontinuous_of_univLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BD (2)** with the four sheafification hypotheses replaced by the single universe
inequality they follow from: the module universe `m` dominates both sites. This is the sharpest
form the statement takes with `m` still a variable — at `m = max uC vC uD vD` the inequality is
an instance, so there the statement holds with no hypothesis beyond the source's.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exactFunctor_pushforward_of_isAlmostCocontinuous_of_univLE
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {v : C ⥤ D}
    (hv : IsMorphismOfSites.{max uC vC uD vD} v J K)
    (ha : IsAlmostCocontinuous v J K)
    {S : Sheaf J RingCat.{r}} {R : Sheaf K RingCat.{r}}
    (φ : letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
      S ⟶ (v.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{r} J K).obj R)
    [UnivLE.{max uC vC uD vD, m}] :
    letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
    exactFunctor (SheafOfModules.{m} R) (SheafOfModules.{m} S)
      (SheafOfModules.pushforward φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.PushforwardRightExact.exactFunctor_pushforward_of_isAlmostCocontinuous_of_smallCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BD (2)** for sites that are small categories, with the sheaf of rings and the
sheaves of modules in the site's own universe: the setting of the source, in which the hypotheses
are exactly the source's.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exactFunctor_pushforward_of_isAlmostCocontinuous_of_smallCategory
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {v : C ⥤ D}
    (hv : IsMorphismOfSites.{u} v J K) (ha : IsAlmostCocontinuous v J K)
    {S : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} {R : Sheaf K RingCat.{u}}
    (φ : letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
      S ⟶ (v.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R) :
    letI : v.IsContinuous J K := hv.toIsContinuous
    exactFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} R) (SheafOfModules.{u} S)
      (SheafOfModules.pushforward φ)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.lan

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.LowerShriek.gShriek_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
If a continuous functor between sites has a source with fibre products and equalizers which
it preserves, then lower shriek on abelian sheaves preserves finite limits.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gShriek_preservesFiniteLimits
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    (u : C ⥤ D) (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsContinuous J K]
    [HasPullbacks C] [HasEqualizers C]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair u]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{w}, u.op.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension F]
    [HasSheafify K Ab.{w}] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
      (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback u Ab.{w} J K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.LowerShriek.gShriek_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
Lower shriek along a continuous functor `u` preserves finite colimits, for sheaves valued in
any category `A` for which the left Kan extensions along `u.op` and weak sheafification on the
target site exist.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gShriek_preservesFiniteColimits
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    (A : Type uA) [Category.{vA} A]
    (u : C ⥤ D) (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsContinuous J K]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasLeftKanExtension F]
    [HasWeakSheafify K A] :
    PreservesFiniteColimits
      (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback u A J K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.LowerShriek.gShriek_preservesFiniteLimits_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BH for module coefficients.** If a continuous functor between sites has a source
with fibre products and equalizers which it preserves, then lower shriek on sheaves of
`R`-modules preserves finite limits. Being a left adjoint it preserves finite colimits, so it is
exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem gShriek_preservesFiniteLimits_module
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    (u : C ⥤ D) (R : Type r) [Ring R]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsContinuous J K]
    [UnivLE.{max uC uD, w}] [UnivLE.{max vC vD, w}] [UnivLE.{max uC vD, w}]
    [HasPullbacks C] [HasEqualizers C]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair u]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} R, u.op.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension F]
    [HasSheafify K (ModuleCat.{w} R)] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
      (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback u (ModuleCat.{w} R) J K)
declarations.comment: preservation of finite limits, module coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.ChangeOfRings.hasRightAdjoint_extendScalars

If base change `M ↦ S ⊗_R M` along a ring map `f : R →+* S` has a left adjoint, then `f` is

theorem flat_of_isRightAdjoint_extendScalars [Small.{v} R]
