declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.Differentials.universalDerivation_isUniversal
declarations.doc:
Every relative derivation with values in a sheaf of modules factors through the universal
derivation by a unique morphism of sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalDerivation_isUniversal
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (underlyingRingSheaf O₂))
    (D : SheafDerivation O₁ O₂ φ F) :
    ∃! f : moduleOfDifferentials O₁ O₂ φ ⟶ F,
      (universalDerivation O₁ O₂ φ).postcomp f.val = D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.existsUnique_descDerivation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BL**, in unique-factorization form: every relative derivation with values in a
sheaf of modules factors through the universal derivation by a unique morphism of sheaves of
modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_descDerivation
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O₂))
    (D : PresheafOfModulesOfCommRing.Derivation' F.val φ.hom) :
    ∃! f : moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, m} O₁ O₂ φ ⟶ F,
      (universalDerivationOfSite.{v, u, w, m} O₁ O₂ φ).postcomp f.val = D
declarations.comment: unique-factorization form, on an arbitrary site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.derivationsFunctor_isCorepresentable
declarations.doc:
For a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings, the functor
sending a sheaf of modules to the type of relative derivations is represented by a sheaf
of modules.
declarations.statement:
instance derivationsFunctor_isCorepresentable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})]
    (O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂) :
    (derivationsFunctor.{v} O₁ O₂ φ).IsCorepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleDifferentialsRelationMap
declarations.doc:
The map
`O₂[O₂ × O₂] ⊕ O₂[O₂ × O₂] ⊕ O₂[O₁] ⟶ O₂[O₂]`
whose three components send generators respectively to
`[a+b]-[a]-[b]`, `[fg]-g[f]-f[g]`, and `[φ(h)]`.

Here every free module presheaf and the displayed morphism have been sheafified.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleDifferentialsRelationMap
    (O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}] :
    (sheafification (𝟙 O₂.obj)).obj
      ((freeObj (R := O₂.obj) (ringElementPairs O₂) ⨿
        freeObj (R := O₂.obj) (ringElementPairs O₂)) ⨿
        freeObj (R := O₂.obj) (ringElements O₁)) ⟶
    (sheafification (𝟙 O₂.obj)).obj
      (freeObj (R := O₂.obj) (ringElements O₂))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleDifferentialsRelationMap_additive
declarations.doc: The additive summand sends `[(a,b)]` to `[a+b]-[a]-[b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleDifferentialsRelationMap_additive
    (O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (X : Cᵒᵖ) (a b : O₂.obj.obj X) :
    ((sheafificationHomEquiv (𝟙 O₂.obj)
      ((sheafification (𝟙 O₂.obj)).map (coprod.inl ≫ coprod.inl) ≫
        moduleDifferentialsRelationMap O₁ O₂ φ)).app X) (ModuleCat.freeMk (a, b)) =
      sheafifiedFreeGenerator O₂ (ringElements O₂) X (a + b) -
        sheafifiedFreeGenerator O₂ (ringElements O₂) X a -
        sheafifiedFreeGenerator O₂ (ringElements O₂) X b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleDifferentialsRelationMap_leibniz
declarations.doc: The multiplicative summand sends `[(f,g)]` to `[fg]-g[f]-f[g]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleDifferentialsRelationMap_leibniz
    (O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (X : Cᵒᵖ) (f g : O₂.obj.obj X) :
    ((sheafificationHomEquiv (𝟙 O₂.obj)
      ((sheafification (𝟙 O₂.obj)).map (coprod.inr ≫ coprod.inl) ≫
        moduleDifferentialsRelationMap O₁ O₂ φ)).app X) (ModuleCat.freeMk (f, g)) =
      sheafifiedFreeGenerator O₂ (ringElements O₂) X (f * g) -
        g • sheafifiedFreeGenerator O₂ (ringElements O₂) X f -
        f • sheafifiedFreeGenerator O₂ (ringElements O₂) X g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleDifferentialsRelationMap_base
declarations.doc: The base-ring summand sends `[h]` to `[φ(h)]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleDifferentialsRelationMap_base
    (O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (X : Cᵒᵖ) (h : O₁.obj.obj X) :
    ((sheafificationHomEquiv (𝟙 O₂.obj)
      ((sheafification (𝟙 O₂.obj)).map coprod.inr ≫
        moduleDifferentialsRelationMap O₁ O₂ φ)).app X) (ModuleCat.freeMk h) =
      sheafifiedFreeGenerator O₂ (ringElements O₂) X (φ.hom.app X h)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite
declarations.doc:
The sheaf of relative differentials `Ω_{O₂/O₁}`: the sheaf of modules corepresenting the
functor of relative derivations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.universalDerivationOfSite
declarations.doc: The universal relative derivation with values in `Ω_{O₂/O₁}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def universalDerivationOfSite :
    PresheafOfModulesOfCommRing.Derivation' (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, w, m} O₁ O₂ φ).val
      φ.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.overDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BO.** For a homomorphism `φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂` of sheaves of commutative rings on a site
and an object `U` of that site, the restriction of the sheaf of relative differentials to the
slice site over `U` is the sheaf of relative differentials of the restrictions:
`Ω_{O₂/O₁}|_U ≅ Ω_{(O₂|_U)/(O₁|_U)}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def overDifferentialsIso :
    (moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, u, max u v w, max u v w} O₁ O₂ φ).over U ≅
      moduleOfDifferentialsOfSite.{v, max u v, max u v w, max u v w}
        (O₁.over U) (O₂.over U) ((J.overPullback CommRingCat.{max u v w} U).map φ)
declarations.comment:
the canonical isomorphism, with the object, arrow and section universes of the
site independent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.homEquiv_overDifferentialsIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BO.** The identification is the one carrying the restriction of the universal
derivation of `Ω_{O₂/O₁}` to the universal derivation of `Ω_{(O₂|_U)/(O₁|_U)}`: transposing it
along the corepresentation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.overDifferentialsCorepresentableBy` returns that universal
derivation.
declarations.statement:
lemma homEquiv_overDifferentialsIso_hom :
    (overDifferentialsCorepresentableBy.{w} J U φ).homEquiv
        (overDifferentialsIso.{w} J U φ).hom =
      universalDerivationOfSite.{v, max u v, max u v w, max u v w}
        (O₁.over U) (O₂.over U) ((J.overPullback CommRingCat.{max u v w} U).map φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.SquareZeroExtension.statement₁
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.** For every `φ`-derivation `D`, the map `s + D : O₂ → A`
(Definition 5) is again a section of `π`: it underlies a homomorphism of sheaves of
`O₁`-algebras with `π ∘ (s + D) = id`.

We express this by producing a `Section` whose objectwise function is `s + D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement₁ (s : E.Section) (D : E.Derivation) :
    ∃ s' : E.Section, ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a : E.O₂.obj U), s'.app U a = E.addDeriv s D U a

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.SquareZeroExtension.statement₂_bijection
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (the bijection / torsor).** Fixing a section `s`, the map
`D ↦ s + D` is a bijection from `φ`-derivations to sections of `π`, with inverse
`s' ↦ s' - s`.  We package the bijection as an explicit `Equiv` between
`Der_{O₁}(O₂, F)` and the sections of `π`, characterized on underlying objectwise
functions by `s + D` and `s' - s`.  This exhibits the set of sections of `π` as a
torsor under (an affine space over) `Der_{O₁}(O₂, F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement₂_bijection (s : E.Section) :
    ∃ e : E.Derivation ≃ E.Section,
      (∀ (D : E.Derivation) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a : E.O₂.obj U),
        (e D).app U a = E.addDeriv s D U a) ∧
      (∀ (s' : E.Section) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a : E.O₂.obj U),
        (e.symm s').toFun U a = E.subSection s s' U a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.Derivation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BQ, part (1).** A `Y`-derivation `D : 𝒪_C ⟶ F` with values in a sheaf `F` of
`𝒪_C`-modules, for a morphism of ringed topoi `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), 𝒪_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), 𝒪_D)`: by
definition an `f♯`-derivation, that is, a derivation of `𝒪_C` relative to the inverse-image
form `f♯ : f⁻¹𝒪_D ⟶ 𝒪_C` of the structure map.
declarations.statement: abbrev Derivation (F : Sheaf.targetModules.{u, v, w} X.J X.O)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.differentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BQ, part (2).** The sheaf of differentials `Ω_{X/Y} = Ω_f = Ω_{𝒪_C/f⁻¹𝒪_D}` of a
morphism of ringed topoi `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), 𝒪_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), 𝒪_D)`: the sheaf of differentials of
the inverse-image form `f⁻¹𝒪_D ⟶ 𝒪_C` of its structure map, a sheaf of `𝒪_C`-modules on the
source site.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev differentials : Sheaf.targetModules.{u, v, w} X.J X.O

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.universalDerivation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BQ.** The universal `Y`-derivation `d_{X/Y} : 𝒪_C ⟶ Ω_{X/Y}` that the sheaf of
differentials comes equipped with: the universal derivation of the inverse-image form of the
structure map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def universalDerivation : f.Derivation f.differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.existsUnique_descDerivation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BQ.** `d_{X/Y}` is universal among `Y`-derivations: every `Y`-derivation with
values in a sheaf of `𝒪_C`-modules factors through it by a unique morphism of sheaves of
modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_descDerivation (F : Sheaf.targetModules.{u, v, w} X.J X.O)
    (D : f.Derivation F) :
    ∃! g : f.differentials ⟶ F, (f.universalDerivation).postcomp g.val = D

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.Differentials.RingedSiteOverBase.Hom.comparison_differentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04BR.** For a commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi, `f : X' ⟶ X` over
`Y' ⟶ Y`:

1. the composite `f_* d_{X'/Y'} ∘ f♯ : O_X ⟶ f_* Ω_{X'/Y'}`, `a ↦ d_{X'/Y'}(f♯ a)`, is a
   `Y`-derivation;
2. hence there is a unique `O_X`-linear map `c'_f : Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ f_* Ω_{X'/Y'}` with
   `c'_f(d_{X/Y} t) = d_{X'/Y'}(f♯ t)` for every local section `t`;
3. the comparison map `c_f : f^* Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ Ω_{X'/Y'}` is the unique `O_{X'}`-linear map sending
   `f^* d_{X/Y}(t)` to `d_{X'/Y'}(f^* t)` for every local section `t` of `O_X`;
4. and this `c_f` is the map obtained from `c'_f` by the adjunction `f^* ⊣ f_*`.

Here `Ω_{X/Y}` and `Ω_{X'/Y'}` are the sheaves of differentials of Stacks 04BQ, universal among
derivations into sheaves of modules. A local section `t ∈ O_X(U)` is pulled back to the section
`f♯ t` over `Ff U`, and `f^* d_{X/Y}(t)` is the image of `d_{X/Y}(t)` under the unit of the
adjunction, a section of `f^* Ω_{X/Y}` over `Ff U` (`pullbackDiff`); the source's equation of
maps out of `f⁻¹h_U^#` is the equation of these sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem comparison_differentials :
    (∃ D : PresheafOfModulesOfCommRing.Derivation' f.pushΩ.val X.φ.hom,
      ∀ (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (a : (ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj U),
        (D.app U).d a = (X'.universalDerivation.app (f.Ff.op.obj U)).d (f.fsharpApp U a)) ∧
    (∃! cf' : X.differentials ⟶ f.pushΩ,
      ∀ (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (t : (ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj U),
        (cf'.val.app U).hom (X.universalDerivation.d t)
          = (X'.universalDerivation.app (f.Ff.op.obj U)).d (f.fsharpApp U t)) ∧
    (∃! cf : f.pullΩ ⟶ X'.differentials,
      ∀ (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (t : (ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj U),
        (cf.val.app (f.Ff.op.obj U)).hom (f.pullbackDiff U t)
          = (X'.universalDerivation.app (f.Ff.op.obj U)).d (f.fsharpApp U t)) ∧
    ∀ (cf : f.pullΩ ⟶ X'.differentials) (cf' : X.differentials ⟶ f.pushΩ),
      (∀ (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (t : (ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj U),
        (cf'.val.app U).hom (X.universalDerivation.d t)
          = (X'.universalDerivation.app (f.Ff.op.obj U)).d (f.fsharpApp U t)) →
      (∀ (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (t : (ringSheaf X.O).obj.obj U),
        (cf.val.app (f.Ff.op.obj U)).hom (f.pullbackDiff U t)
          = (X'.universalDerivation.app (f.Ff.op.obj U)).d (f.fsharpApp U t)) →
      (f.adj).homEquiv X.differentials X'.differentials cf = cf'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiProjection
declarations.doc: The projection `π_S` from the big Zariski topos to the small one.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallZariskiProjection :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (BigZariskiOver.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (SmallZariski.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: restriction to the small Zariski site is its direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inclusionInverseImageIsoProjectionPushforward
declarations.doc:
Inverse image along `i_S` is naturally restriction to the small étale
site, equivalently direct image along `π_S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def inclusionInverseImageIsoProjectionPushforward :
    (smallEtaleToBigEtaleMorphism B (B.obj S hS) (B.obj S hS)
        (𝟙 (B.obj S hS))).inverseImage ≅
      (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S hS).pushforward
declarations.comment: restriction to the small étale site, i.e. `i_S^{-1} = π_{S,*}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.derivationDirectImageEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Equation (04BV).**  For `a : X ⟶ Y`, `b : Y ⟶ Z` morphisms of schemes and an
`𝒪_X`-module `C`, the `𝒪_X`-linear maps `θ : a^*Ω_{Y/Z} ⟶ C` correspond bijectively to the
`Z`-derivations `D : 𝒪_Y ⟶ a_*C`, by `D = d_{Y/Z} ∘ θ` with `θ` transposed along the
adjunction `a^* ⊣ a_*`.
declarations.statement:
def derivationDirectImageEquiv (a : X ⟶ Y) (b : Y ⟶ Z) (C : X.Modules) :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback a).obj (relativeDifferentials b) ⟶ C) ≃
      SheafOfModules.SheafDerivation (inverseImageStructureMap b)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward a).obj C)
declarations.comment: the bijection `θ ↔ D = d_{Y/S} ∘ θ` at scheme level on the Zariski site, stated at a general target module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.derivationDirectImageEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Equation (04BV) itself.**  The derivation attached to `θ : a^*Ω_{Y/Z} ⟶ C` is the
universal derivation `d_{Y/Z}` followed by the transpose of `θ` along `a^* ⊣ a_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivationDirectImageEquiv_apply (a : X ⟶ Y) (b : Y ⟶ Z) (C : X.Modules)
    (θ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback a).obj (relativeDifferentials b) ⟶ C) :
    derivationDirectImageEquiv a b C θ =
      (universalRelativeDerivation b).postcomp
        (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction a).homEquiv
          (relativeDifferentials b) C) θ).val
declarations.comment: the equation `D = d_{Y/S} ∘ θ` at scheme level on the Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.universalDerivation_isUniversal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08RM.** Postcomposition with the universal
derivation gives the unique morphism from the module of relative
differentials to any coefficient sheaf.
declarations.comment: the factorization D = d o theta of a derivation through the universal derivation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isIso_relativeDifferentialsMap_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04BX.** In a commutative square of schemes whose two horizontal
arrows `f : X₂ ⟶ X₁` and `g : S₂ ⟶ S₁` are étale, the canonical map
`f^* Ω_{X₁/S₁} ⟶ Ω_{X₂/S₂}` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_relativeDifferentialsMap_of_etale {X₁ X₂ S₁ S₂ : Scheme.{u}} (f : X₂ ⟶ X₁)
    (p₁ : X₁ ⟶ S₁) (p₂ : X₂ ⟶ S₂) (g : S₂ ⟶ S₁) (hcomm : f ≫ p₁ = p₂ ≫ g)
    [Etale f] [Etale g] :
    IsIso (relativeDifferentialsMap f p₁ p₂ g hcomm)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.derivationActionSheaf_comp_etaleLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Acting by a derivation commutes with an étale localization.** Let
`(h, h') : (T₂ ⊂ T₂') ⟶ (T₁ ⊂ T₁')` be a morphism of first-order thickenings, let
`(f, f') : (X₂ ⟶ X₂') ⟶ (X₁ ⟶ X₁')` be a morphism of the right-hand pairs, let `(a₁, a₁')` and
`(a₂, a₂')` be morphisms of thickenings compatible with them, and let `p₁ : X₁' ⟶ S₁`,
`p₂ : X₂' ⟶ S₂` and `k : S₂ ⟶ S₁` form a commutative square with `f`. Assume `f` and `k` are étale.
Then for every `𝒪_{T₁}`-linear `θ₁ : a₁^*Ω_{X₁/S₁} ⟶ 𝒞_{T₁/T₁'}`, the lifts `θ₁ ⬝ a₁'` and
`θ₂ ⬝ a₂'` of [Stacks Project, Tag 0CK1] — for `θ₂` the transported datum
`Stacks.Thickenings.localizedDerivationSheaf` — give a commutative square:
```
(θ₂ ⬝ a₂') ≫ f' = h' ≫ (θ₁ ⬝ a₁').
```

Nothing is assumed affine, and both actions are the ones constructed by
`Stacks.Thickenings.derivationActionSheaf`, not morphisms assumed to satisfy a relation.

`j₁` and `j₂` are not assumed to be first-order thickenings, and the commutativity of the square
of bases is assumed only as the square `f ≫ (j₁ ≫ p₁) = (j₂ ≫ p₂) ≫ k` of the closed subschemes,
which the ambient square `f' ≫ p₁ = p₂ ≫ k` implies.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivationActionSheaf_comp_etaleLocalization
    (hi₁ : i₁.ker ^ 2 = ⊥) (hi₂ : i₂.ker ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (ca₁ : i₁ ≫ a₁' = a₁ ≫ j₁) (ca₂ : i₂ ≫ a₂' = a₂ ≫ j₂)
    (cT : i₂ ≫ h' = h ≫ i₁) (cj : j₂ ≫ f' = f ≫ j₁) (cX : a₂ ≫ f = h ≫ a₁)
    (cA : a₂' ≫ f' = h' ≫ a₁') (cS : f ≫ (j₁ ≫ p₁) = (j₂ ≫ p₂) ≫ k)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale f] [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale k]
    (θ₁ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback a₁).obj (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials (j₁ ≫ p₁)) ⟶
      Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf i₁) :
    derivationActionSheaf hi₂ p₂ ca₂ (localizedDerivationSheaf cT cX cS θ₁) ≫ f' =
      h' ≫ derivationActionSheaf hi₁ p₁ ca₁ θ₁

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.derivationAction_comp_of_derivation_comm
declarations.doc:
**Acting by compatible derivation data commutes with the vertical maps**, the affine case of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04BZ]. Let `(h, h')` and `(f, f')` be the vertical maps of a diagram of
first-order thickenings with affine ambient schemes as in [Stacks Project, Tag 04BY], let
`(a₁, a₁')` and `(a₂, a₂')` be morphisms of thickenings compatible with them, and let
`p₁ : X₁' ⟶ S₁` and `p₂ : X₂' ⟶ S₂` be the structure morphisms. Nothing is assumed étale.
Given `Γ(X₁, ⊤)`-linear `θ₁ : Ω[Γ(X₁, ⊤)⁄Γ(S₁, ⊤)] ⟶ 𝒞_{T₁/T₁'}` and `Γ(X₂, ⊤)`-linear
`θ₂ : Ω[Γ(X₂, ⊤)⁄Γ(S₂, ⊤)] ⟶ 𝒞_{T₂/T₂'}` whose derivations `D_n = θ_n ∘ d_{X_n/S_n}` of
Equation [Stacks Project, Tag 04BV] satisfy `D₂ (f^♯ y) = (h')^♯ (D₁ y)` — the commuting square
of the source — acting by `θ₁` on `a₁'` and by `θ₂` on `a₂'` gives a commutative square:
```
(θ₂ ⬝ a₂') ≫ f' = h' ≫ (θ₁ ⬝ a₁').
```

In [Stacks Project, Tag 04BY] the second datum is built from the first out of the étale
hypotheses, and the hypothesis `hθ` here is then its defining property
`Stacks.Thickenings.localizedDerivation_apply`; see
`Stacks.Thickenings.derivationAction_comp_localizedDerivation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivationAction_comp_of_derivation_comm [IsAffine T₁'] [IsAffine T₂'] [IsAffine X₁']
    [IsAffine X₂'] (hi₁ : IsFirstOrderThickening i₁) (hi₂ : IsFirstOrderThickening i₂)
    (ca₁ : i₁ ≫ a₁' = a₁ ≫ j₁) (ca₂ : i₂ ≫ a₂' = a₂ ≫ j₂) (cj : j₂ ≫ f' = f ≫ j₁)
    (cA : a₂' ≫ f' = h' ≫ a₁') :
    letI := appTopAlgebra (j₁ ≫ p₁)
    letI := conormalModuleAlong hi₁ a₁
    letI := appTopAlgebra (j₂ ≫ p₂)
    letI := conormalModuleAlong hi₂ a₂
    ∀ (θ₁ : Ω[Γ(X₁, (⊤ : X₁.Opens))⁄Γ(S₁, (⊤ : S₁.Opens))] →ₗ[Γ(X₁, (⊤ : X₁.Opens))]
        RingHom.ker i₁.appTop.hom)
      (θ₂ : Ω[Γ(X₂, (⊤ : X₂.Opens))⁄Γ(S₂, (⊤ : S₂.Opens))] →ₗ[Γ(X₂, (⊤ : X₂.Opens))]
        RingHom.ker i₂.appTop.hom),
      (∀ y : Γ(X₁, (⊤ : X₁.Opens)),
          ((θ₂ (KaehlerDifferential.D _ _ (f.appTop.hom y)) : RingHom.ker i₂.appTop.hom) :
              Γ(T₂', (⊤ : T₂'.Opens)))
            = h'.appTop.hom ((θ₁ (KaehlerDifferential.D _ _ y) : RingHom.ker i₁.appTop.hom) :
              Γ(T₁', (⊤ : T₁'.Opens)))) →
        derivationAction hi₂ ca₂ p₂ θ₂ ≫ f' = h' ≫ derivationAction hi₁ ca₁ p₁ θ₁
declarations.comment: affine case, with the two actions of Tag 0CK1 constructed by Stacks.Thickenings.derivationAction; the remark for arbitrary schemes is Stacks.Thickenings.derivationActionSheaf_comp_of_derivationSection_comm

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.derivationActionSheaf_comp_of_derivationSection_comm
declarations.doc:
**Acting by compatible derivation data commutes with the vertical maps**,
[Stacks Project, Tag 04BZ] for arbitrary schemes, with both actions *constructed*. Let `(h, h')`
and `(f, f')` be the vertical maps of a diagram of first-order thickenings as in
[Stacks Project, Tag 04BY], let `(a₁, a₁')` and `(a₂, a₂')` be morphisms of thickenings
compatible with them, and let `p₁ : X₁' ⟶ S₁` and `p₂ : X₂' ⟶ S₂` be the structure morphisms.
Nothing is assumed étale and nothing is assumed affine. Given
`θ₁ : a₁^*Ω_{X₁/S₁} ⟶ 𝒞_{T₁/T₁'}` and `θ₂ : a₂^*Ω_{X₂/S₂} ⟶ 𝒞_{T₂/T₂'}` whose derivations
`D_n = θ_n ∘ d_{X_n/S_n}` of Equation [Stacks Project, Tag 04BV] satisfy
`D₂ (f^♯ y) = (h')^♯ (D₁ y)` — the commuting square of the source, read inside the ambient
structure sheaves — the lifts `θ₁ ⬝ a₁'` and `θ₂ ⬝ a₂'` of [Stacks Project, Tag 0CK1] give a
commutative square:
```
(θ₂ ⬝ a₂') ≫ f' = h' ≫ (θ₁ ⬝ a₁').
```

This is `Stacks.Thickenings.derivationAction_comp_of_derivationSection_comm` with its two
hypotheses `Stacks.Thickenings.IsDerivationAction` discharged by
`Stacks.Thickenings.isDerivationAction_derivationActionSheaf`: the lifts are the morphisms
constructed by `Stacks.Thickenings.derivationActionSheaf`, not morphisms assumed to satisfy a
relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivationActionSheaf_comp_of_derivationSection_comm
    (hi₁ : i₁.ker ^ 2 = ⊥) (hi₂ : i₂.ker ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (p₁ : X₁' ⟶ S₁) (p₂ : X₂' ⟶ S₂)
    (ca₁ : i₁ ≫ a₁' = a₁ ≫ j₁) (ca₂ : i₂ ≫ a₂' = a₂ ≫ j₂)
    (cT : i₂ ≫ h' = h ≫ i₁) (cj : j₂ ≫ f' = f ≫ j₁) (cX : a₂ ≫ f = h ≫ a₁)
    (cA : a₂' ≫ f' = h' ≫ a₁')
    {θ₁ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback a₁).obj (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials (j₁ ≫ p₁)) ⟶
      Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf i₁}
    {θ₂ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback a₂).obj (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials (j₂ ≫ p₂)) ⟶
      Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf i₂}
    (hθ : ∀ (V : X₁'.Opens) (s : Γ(X₁', V)),
      (T₂'.presheaf.map (eqToHom (preimage_comp_eq cA V)).op).hom
          ((h'.app (a₁' ⁻¹ᵁ V)).hom (derivationSectionι hi₁ p₁ ca₁ θ₁ V ((j₁.app V).hom s)))
        = derivationSectionι hi₂ p₂ ca₂ θ₂ (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V)
            ((j₂.app (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V)).hom ((f'.app V).hom s))) :
    derivationActionSheaf hi₂ p₂ ca₂ θ₂ ≫ f' = h' ≫ derivationActionSheaf hi₁ p₁ ca₁ θ₁
declarations.comment: the two actions of Tag 0CK1 constructed by Stacks.Thickenings.derivationActionSheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePushforwardAb_properties_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04C2.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an integral morphism of schemes — a finite
morphism, for instance. Then

1. `f_{small, *}` transforms surjections into surjections, on sheaves of sets and on abelian
   sheaves,
2. the counit `f^{-1} f_* F ⟶ F` is surjective for every abelian sheaf `F` on `X_étale`,
3. `f_{small, *} : Ab(X_étale) ⥤ Ab(Y_étale)` is faithful and reflects injections and
   surjections, and
4. `f_{small, *} : Ab(X_étale) ⥤ Ab(Y_étale)` is exact.

The seven conjuncts are, in order: part (1) on sheaves of sets, part (1) on abelian sheaves,
part (2), the three assertions of part (3), and part (4).
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtalePushforwardAb_properties_of_isIntegralHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegralHom f] :
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1)) (smallEtaleTopology Y)
        (smallEtaleTopology X)).PreservesEpimorphisms ∧
      (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).PreservesEpimorphisms ∧
      (∀ F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1},
          Epi ((smallEtaleAdjunctionAb f).counit.app F)) ∧
        (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).Faithful ∧
          (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).ReflectsMonomorphisms ∧
            (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).ReflectsEpimorphisms ∧
              exactFunctor (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1})
                (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology Y) Ab.{u + 1}) (smallEtalePushforwardAb f)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleAbelianDirectImage_preservesEpimorphisms_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04C2, part (1), at the coefficients of the proper base change development.** For an
integral morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` — a finite morphism, for instance — direct image
`f_* : Ab(X_étale) ⥤ Ab(Y_étale)` carries surjections of abelian sheaves with values in
`AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}` to surjections.

A morphism of abelian sheaves is epimorphic exactly when it is locally surjective, and local
surjectivity is a property of the underlying morphism of sheaves of sets. Since the underlying
sheaf of sets of a direct image is the direct image of the underlying sheaf of sets, the
statement reduces to its set-valued counterpart, which is stated for an arbitrary coefficient
universe.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAbelianDirectImage_preservesEpimorphisms_of_isIntegralHom
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegralHom f] :
    (etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, v} f).PreservesEpimorphisms
declarations.comment: part (1) for abelian sheaves, at the coefficients of proper base change

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesFiniteColimits_etaleAbelianDirectImage_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04C2, part (2), at the coefficients of the proper base change development.** For an
integral morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, direct image of abelian sheaves on the small étale sites
preserves finite colimits.

Direct image is a right adjoint, so it preserves finite limits and is therefore additive; it
preserves epimorphisms because `f` is integral; and an additive functor between abelian
categories which preserves kernels and epimorphisms preserves homology, hence finite colimits
as well.
declarations.statement:
public instance preservesFiniteColimits_etaleAbelianDirectImage_of_isIntegralHom
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegralHom f] :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, v} f)
declarations.comment: part (2) for abelian sheaves, at the coefficients of proper base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePushforward_preservesEpimorphisms_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04C2, part (1), for an integral morphism of algebraic spaces.** The small étale
direct image of sheaves of sets along an integral morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
transforms surjections into surjections.

A scheme atlas `a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y` of the target is chosen, and the base change of `f` along
it is taken from the representability witness that Stacks 03ZQ attaches to an integral
morphism: that produces an object `P` of the site, a morphism `s : P ⟶ T` and a Cartesian
square exhibiting `yoneda.map s` as the base change. Its underlying morphism of schemes is
integral, so `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representedSmallEtalePushforward_preservesEpimorphisms`
applies, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePushforward_preservesEpimorphisms_of_etaleCover` carries the
conclusion back to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtalePushforward_preservesEpimorphisms_of_isIntegralHom
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f.hom) :
    Functor.PreservesEpimorphisms (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).pushforward
declarations.comment: part (1), for an integral morphism of algebraic spaces

of big syntomic sites preserves colimits of every connected shape whose colimits of sets exist.

This is Stacks Project, Tag 04B9 — the general form of the Tag 04BA that the source cites — fed
the almost cocontinuity of base change supplied by Stacks Project, Tag 04C3. No passage to an
equivalent small site is needed, Tag 04B9 being stated for an arbitrary pair of sites.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePushforwardAb_properties_of_isIntegralHom_or_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes which is either integral, or separated and locally
quasi-finite. Then the counit `f^{-1} f_* F ⟶ F` is surjective for every abelian sheaf `F` on the
small étale site of `X`, direct image of abelian sheaves along the small étale sites is faithful,
and it reflects injections and surjections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtalePushforwardAb_properties_of_isIntegralHom_or_locallyQuasiFinite
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsIntegralHom f ∨ (IsSeparated f ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite f)) :
    (∀ F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1},
        Epi ((smallEtaleAdjunctionAb f).counit.app F)) ∧
      (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).Faithful ∧
      (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).ReflectsMonomorphisms ∧
      (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).ReflectsEpimorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleAdjunction_counit_isIso_abelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CA.** The counit of the inverse image/direct image adjunction along a closed
immersion is an isomorphism on every abelian sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleAdjunction_counit_isIso_abelian
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B Z.1 Z.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    IsIso (((smallEtaleBaseChange B i).sheafAdjunctionContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B Z.1 Z.property)).counit.app F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePushforwardCompPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CA.** Inverse image along a closed immersion is a left inverse to direct image
on abelian sheaves: the counit of the adjunction is a natural isomorphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePushforward_essImage_iff_abelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CA, part (2).** An abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `X` lies in the
essential image of direct image along a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` exactly when its support
is contained in `Z`, that is, exactly when its stalk vanishes at every geometric point of `X`
whose image misses `Z`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtalePushforward_essImage_iff_abelian
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange B i).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B Z.1 Z.property)).essImage F ↔
      SmallEtale.supportSheaf B X.1 X.property F ⊆
        Set.range (B.inclusion.map i).base

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePushforwardFullyFaithful
declarations.doc: Direct image of sheaves of sets along a closed immersion is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtalePushforwardFullyFaithful {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange i).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (max (u + 1) v))
      (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X) (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology Z)).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePushforwardCompInverseImageIso
declarations.doc: The counit `i^{-1} i_* ⟶ 𝟭` of the adjunction is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtalePushforwardCompInverseImageIso {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange i).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (max (u + 1) v))
        (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X) (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology Z) ⋙
      smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} i ≅
      𝟭 (Sheaf (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology Z) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePushforward_essImage_iff
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of sets on `X_étale` lies in the essential image of direct image along a closed
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` exactly when its restriction to the open complement of `Z` is the
singleton sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtalePushforward_essImage_iff {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange i).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (max (u + 1) v))
        (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X) (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology Z)).essImage F ↔
      Nonempty (IsTerminal ((smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} (openComplement i).ι).obj F))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePushforwardAb_essImage_iff_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
An abelian sheaf on `W_étale` is a direct image along a closed immersion `j : Z ⟶ W` exactly
when its restriction to an open subscheme `U` complementary to the image of `j` vanishes, that
is, exactly when its support is contained in `j(Z)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_iff_isClosed_range_pointsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CD.** An immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed immersion exactly
when the image of its point set is a closed subset of the point space of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_isClosed_range_pointsMap (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS i ↔ IsClosed (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_ι_boundarySubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CE.** The point set of the boundary subspace of an immersion is the boundary
of the image of that immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_ι_boundarySubspace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (boundarySubspace B S hS hX i hi).toFunctor
        (boundarySubspace B S hS hX i hi).ι) =
      closure (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i)) \ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i)
declarations.comment: the points of the boundary subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced_boundarySubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CE.** The boundary subspace of an immersion is reduced, in the étale-local
sense of Stacks 03E6.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced_boundarySubspace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS (boundarySubspace B S hS hX i hi).toFunctor
      (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_ι_boundaryComplement_eq_compl
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CE.** The open subspace through which an immersion is to be factored is the
complement of its boundary subspace: the two have complementary point sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_ι_boundaryComplement_eq_compl (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS
        (boundaryComplement B S hS X (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))).toFunctor
        (boundaryComplement B S hS X (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))).ι) =
      (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (boundarySubspace B S hS hX i hi).toFunctor
        (boundarySubspace B S hS hX i hi).ι))ᶜ
declarations.comment: the open subspace is the complement of the boundary subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_range_pointsMap_of_comp_ι_boundaryComplement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CE.** The image of an immersion is closed in the complement of its boundary:
any factorisation of the immersion through that open subspace has closed image on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_range_pointsMap_of_comp_ι_boundaryComplement (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (g : Z ⟶ (boundaryComplement B S hS X (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))).toFunctor)
    (hg : g ≫ (boundaryComplement B S hS X (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))).ι = i) :
    IsClosed (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z g))
declarations.comment: the image is closed away from the boundary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedImmersion_comp_ι_boundaryComplement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CE.** Every immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` factors as a closed
immersion into the complement of its boundary, followed by the open immersion of that open
subspace into the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedImmersion_comp_ι_boundaryComplement
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    ∃ g : Z ⟶ (boundaryComplement B S hS X (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))).toFunctor,
      IsClosedImmersion B S hS g ∧
        g ≫ (boundaryComplement B S hS X (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))).ι = i
declarations.comment: an immersion is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforward_comp_overFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CF, for an arbitrary morphism of algebraic spaces.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `V` be an étale scheme chart of `Y`.  Write
`U = V ×_Y X` for the base change of the chart, an étale algebraic space over `X`, and
`f' : U ⟶ V` for the base change of `f`.  Then for every `𝒪_X`-module `F`

`f'_*(F|_U) = (f_*F)|_V`.

The restriction `(-)|_V` is restriction to the slice of the small étale site of `Y` at `V`, the
restriction `(-)|_U` is restriction to the slice of the *spaces-étale* site of `X` at `U` — both
readings of Stacks' Equation 03LW — and `f'_*` is the direct image along the localized
base-change functor of Stacks 03CF with the localized structure map
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartLocalizedStructureSharp` of Stacks 04J0, part (1).

No representability hypothesis is made on `f`; this is the form in which the proof of
Stacks 03M9 invokes the identity.  It is an isomorphism rather than an equality of functors
because `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleDirectImage` is conjugated by the comparison
equivalence of Stacks 03G1; for a representable `f` an equality is available in the reading of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.overFunctor_comp_smallBaseChangeModulePushforward`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforward_comp_overFunctorIso (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1) :
    modulePushforward B S hS f ⋙
        SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS Y) V ≅
      moduleChartBaseChangeRestriction B S hS f V ⋙
        chartLocalizedModulePushforward B S hS f V
declarations.comment:
for an arbitrary morphism of algebraic spaces, with the restriction to the
  base-changed chart taken on the slice of the spaces-étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: A closed immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_of_isClosedImmersion {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G)
    (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (_hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CH.** A closed immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is separated. Its
relative diagonal is an isomorphism, because the morphism is a monomorphism, and an
isomorphism of presheaves is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kerIdealSmulQuotientUnitIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (1).**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over
`S` and let `𝓘 = ker(i♯) ⊆ 𝒪_X` be the ideal cutting out `Z`.  For every `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` the
unit `𝓕 ⟶ i_*i^*𝓕` of the adjunction of Stacks 03LU induces an isomorphism `𝓕/𝓘𝓕 ≅ i_*i^*𝓕`.

The isomorphism is the one the adjunction gives: `cokernel.π ≫ e.hom` is the unit, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cokernel_π_comp_kerIdealSmulQuotientUnitMap`.
declarations.statement:
def kerIdealSmulQuotientUnitIso (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    kerIdealSmulQuotient B S hS i F ≅
      (modulePushforward B S hS i).obj ((modulePullback B S hS i).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (1): the unit identifies the quotient by the defining ideal with the direct image of the inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cokernel_π_comp_kerIdealSmulQuotientUnitIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (1)**, the normalisation of the isomorphism: it is induced by the unit of
the adjunction of Stacks 03LU, that is, composing the projection `𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕/𝓘𝓕` with it gives the
unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem cokernel_π_comp_kerIdealSmulQuotientUnitIso_hom (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    cokernel.π (kerIdealSmul B S hS i F).ι ≫
        (kerIdealSmulQuotientUnitIso B S hS i hi F).hom =
      (modulePullbackAdjunction B S hS i).unit.app F
declarations.comment: part (1): the isomorphism is the one induced by the unit of the adjunction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_modulePullbackAdjunction_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (2)** for the modules of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Modules`: for a closed
immersion `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces and any sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `G`, the adjunction map
`f^*f_*G ⟶ G` is an isomorphism.

This is full faithfulness of the direct image read through the adjunction of Stacks 03LU: the
counit of an adjunction is an isomorphism exactly when its right adjoint is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_modulePullbackAdjunction_counit (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f.hom)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    IsIso ((modulePullbackAdjunction B S hS f).counit.app G)
declarations.comment: part (2): inverse image is a left inverse of direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackCounitIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (2)**, functorially: inverse image along a closed immersion of algebraic
spaces is a left inverse of direct image, the counit of the adjunction of Stacks 03LU being a
natural isomorphism `f_* ⋙ f^* ≅ 𝟭`. This is the functorial form of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_modulePullbackAdjunction_counit`.
declarations.comment: part (2): inverse image is a left inverse of direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.annihilatedByKerIdeal_modulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (3)**, half of the essential-image assertion: the ideal cutting out the
closed subspace annihilates every direct image `f_*G`.

Restriction of scalars along `f♯` makes a section `a` of `𝒪_Y` act on `f_*G` as `f♯(a)`, so a
section killed by `f♯` acts as zero. Neither the closed-immersion hypothesis on `f` nor
surjectivity of `f♯` is used.

This is also one inclusion of the essential-image clause of Stacks 08KS for algebraic spaces; the
containment form of it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_modulePushforward_le_annihilatedByKerIdeal` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ClosedImmersionModulePushforwardExactness.lean`, which
carries no tag of its own, and the reverse inclusion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_modulePushforward_of_annihilatedByKerIdeal`, proved with no
hypothesis beyond the closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilatedByKerIdeal_modulePushforward (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    AnnihilatedByKerIdeal B S hS f ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (3): the essential image is annihilated by the defining ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.annihilatedByKerIdeal_of_essImage_modulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (3)**, half of the essential-image assertion, in essential-image form:
every `𝒪_Y`-module isomorphic to a direct image along `f` is annihilated by the ideal cutting out
the closed subspace. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.annihilatedByKerIdeal_modulePushforward` transported along an
isomorphism, and is the inclusion `essImage f_* ⊆ {𝓕 | 𝓘𝓕 = 0}` of the essential-image clause of
Stacks 08KS for algebraic spaces, whose tag is carried by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_modulePushforward_le_annihilatedByKerIdeal` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ClosedImmersionModulePushforwardExactness.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilatedByKerIdeal_of_essImage_modulePushforward (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2} (hG : (modulePushforward B S hS f).essImage G) :
    AnnihilatedByKerIdeal B S hS f G
declarations.comment: part (3): the essential image is annihilated by the defining ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulQuasicoherentModulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (3)**, the full-faithfulness assertion: direct image along a closed
immersion of algebraic spaces is fully faithful on quasi-coherent modules.

It is fully faithful on *all* modules by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulModulePushforward`, and a full subcategory inclusion is
fully faithful.
declarations.comment: part (3): the direct image is fully faithful on quasi-coherent modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDirectImageEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of Stacks 04CJ in the form Stacks 04CL consumes.**  For a closed immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces the direct image carries quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-modules to
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, and every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module annihilated by `𝓘 = ker(i♯)`
is the direct image of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module.

The first clause is the closed-immersion case of Stacks 03M9,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion`.  For the
second, an annihilated `𝒪_X`-module is a direct image by the unconditional essential-image clause
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_modulePushforward_iff`, so the unit `𝓕 ⟶ i_*i^*𝓕` is an
isomorphism, and the witness `i^*𝓕` is quasi-coherent by the closed-immersion case of
Stacks 03GA.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentDirectImageEquivalence (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    QuasicoherentDirectImageEquivalence B S hS i
declarations.comment: part (3): quasi-coherence of the direct image, and quasi-coherence of the module whose direct image an annihilated quasi-coherent module is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDirectImageOfClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**The functor `i_* : QCoh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` of Stacks 04CJ, part (3)**, for a closed
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentPushforwardOfEquivalence` with its hypothesis
discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDirectImageEquivalence`; composing it with
the inclusion of the quasi-coherent modules gives back the direct image of all modules, so it is
the functor the source names and not another one of the same type.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentDirectImageOfClosedImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2 ⥤ QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2
declarations.comment: part (3): the induced functor on quasi-coherent modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulQuasicoherentDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (3), the full-faithfulness clause.**  The direct image
`i_* : QCoh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces is fully faithful.

The direct image is fully faithful on all modules by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulModulePushforward` (part (2)), and a lift along a full
subcategory inclusion inherits that.
declarations.statement:
def fullyFaithfulQuasicoherentDirectImage (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    (quasicoherentDirectImageOfClosedImmersion B S hS i hi).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: part (3): the direct image on quasi-coherent modules is fully faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_quasicoherentDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (3), the exactness clause.**  The direct image
`i_* : QCoh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces is an exact
functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_quasicoherentDirectImage (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    exactFunctor (QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2)
      (QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
      (quasicoherentDirectImageOfClosedImmersion B S hS i hi)
declarations.comment: part (3): the direct image on quasi-coherent modules is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essImage_quasicoherentDirectImage_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CJ, part (3), the essential-image clause.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module is the
direct image of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module along the closed immersion `i` exactly when the
ideal `𝓘 = ker(i♯)` cutting out `Z` annihilates it.

The forward implication is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.annihilatedByKerIdeal_of_essImage_modulePushforward`, applied to the
underlying `𝒪_X`-module.  The converse is the second clause of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDirectImageEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_quasicoherentDirectImage_iff (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (F : QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    (quasicoherentDirectImageOfClosedImmersion B S hS i hi).essImage F ↔
      AnnihilatedByKerIdeal B S hS i F.obj
declarations.comment: part (3): the essential image is the quasi-coherent modules annihilated by the defining ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_largestQuasicoherentSubobject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CK.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `𝓕` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `𝒢 ⊆ 𝓕` be an `𝒪_X`-submodule.  There is a unique
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-submodule `𝒢' ⊆ 𝒢` for which composition with the inclusion `𝒢' ⊆ 𝒢` is a
bijection `Hom(𝓗, 𝒢') ⟶ Hom(𝓗, 𝒢)` for every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓗`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_quasicoherentSubobject_of_isClosedUnderKernels`
with its kernel hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderKernels`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_largestQuasicoherentSubobject (M : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF)
    [M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (G : Subobject M) :
    ∃! G' : { G' : Subobject (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) //
        (G' : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF).IsQuasicoherentOnSite },
      ∀ (H : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) [H.IsQuasicoherentOnSite],
        Function.Bijective
          (fun f : H ⟶ (G'.1 : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) ↦ f ≫ G'.1.arrow)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_greatest_quasicoherentSubobject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CK, the maximality clause.**  The quasi-coherent submodule of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_largestQuasicoherentSubobject` is the largest
quasi-coherent submodule of `𝓕` contained in `𝒢`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_greatest_quasicoherentSubobject_of_isClosedUnderKernels`
with its kernel hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderKernels`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_greatest_quasicoherentSubobject (M : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF)
    [M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (G : Subobject M) :
    ∃ G' : Subobject (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF),
      (G' : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF).IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
        ∀ K : Subobject (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF),
          (K : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF).IsQuasicoherentOnSite → K ≤ G'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLeftAdjoint_quasicoherentDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CL.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of algebraic
spaces over `S`.  Then the direct image `i_* : QCoh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` has a right adjoint, the
functor `i^!` of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_quasicoherentDirectImage (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    (quasicoherentDirectImageOfClosedImmersion B S hS i hi).IsLeftAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentRightAdjointOfClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CL**, the functor `i^!`: the right adjoint of the direct image
`i_* : QCoh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` along a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces. For a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓖`, the direct image of `i^! 𝓖` is the largest quasi-coherent
submodule of `𝓖` annihilated by the ideal cutting out `Z`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDirectImageAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CL**, the adjunction `i_* ⊣ i^!` exhibiting
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentRightAdjointOfClosedImmersion` as a right adjoint of the
direct image of quasi-coherent modules along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CN for an immersion.**  The conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of an immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces: the inverse image along the closed factorisation
`Z ⟶ X ∖ ∂Z` of the defining ideal sheaf of the image of that factorisation.

Stacks 76.5 defines the conormal sheaf of an immersion to be the conormal sheaf of the closed
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X ∖ ∂Z` of Stacks 04CE, which is what this is.  Unlike
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModule`, which returns a module on the closed subspace's own
functor, this is a module on `Z` itself, as the source asks; the two are related by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersion_eq_conormalAlgebraOfImmersion_piece_one`
below, which identifies this module with the degree-one piece of the conormal algebra
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersion`.

The source describes the module as `𝓘/𝓘²`, which is `i_*i^*𝓘`; the module documentation of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.ConormalModule` records why `i^*𝓘` is that module
and that the identification is not formalized, and the "What is not proved" section of this
file records that quasi-coherence is not established either.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalModuleOfImmersion (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z₀ hZ
declarations.comment: construction as the pullback of the ideal sheaf, via the closed factorisation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CN for a closed immersion.**  The conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of a closed subspace
`Z` of an algebraic space `X`: the inverse image along the inclusion `i : Z ⟶ X` of the defining
ideal sheaf `𝓘_Z ⊆ 𝒪_X` of Stacks 03MB.

Stacks 76.5 describes this `𝒪_Z`-module as `𝓘/𝓘²`, which is `i_*i^*𝓘`; the implementation notes
of this file record why `i^*𝓘` is that module and that the identification is not formalized
here, and that this is the convention of the scheme-level `Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalModule (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.2.1
declarations.comment: construction as the pullback of the ideal sheaf, closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalIdealQuotientIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CN, the identification with `𝓘/𝓘²`.**  For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of
algebraic spaces the canonical map induced by the unit of `i^* ⊣ i_*` is an isomorphism

`𝓘/𝓘² ≅ i_*𝒞_{Z/X}`,

so the `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒞_{Z/X} = i^*𝓘` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfHom` is the one
Stacks 76.5 describes as `𝓘/𝓘²`.  The characterising property is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalIdealQuotientπ_comp_toPushforward`: composed with the
projection `𝓘 ⟶ 𝓘/𝓘²` it is the unit.
declarations.comment: the identification of the conormal module with 𝓘/𝓘², for a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_conormalModuleOfImmersion
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-coherence clause of Stacks 04CN for an arbitrary immersion**, unconditionally:
the closed factorisation of Stacks 04CE is a closed immersion, where
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_conormalModuleOfHom` applies.

The definition of the source calls `𝒞_{Z/X}` *the quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module* `𝓘/𝓘²`; this is
that clause of the definition, which `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersion` — being
a definition — cannot itself state.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_conormalModuleOfImmersion (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    (conormalModuleOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the conormal sheaf is a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_and_nonempty_conormalIdealQuotientIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04CN.**  The *conormal sheaf* `𝒞_{Z/X}` of an immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S`, constructed as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersion` through the closed immersion of `Z` into the
complement `X ∖ ∂Z` of the boundary of its image (Stacks 04CE), is the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_Z`-module `𝓘/𝓘²` of the source: it is quasi-coherent, and for `𝓘` the ideal sheaf of `Z` in
`X ∖ ∂Z` its direct image along that closed immersion is `𝓘/𝓘²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_and_nonempty_conormalIdealQuotientIso
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    (conormalModuleOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi).IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
      Nonempty (conormalIdealQuotient B S hS (immersionClosedFactorization B S hS hX hZ i hi) ≅
        (modulePushforward B S hS (immersionClosedFactorization B S hS hX hZ i hi)).obj
          (conormalModuleOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO for the conormal module.**  Let `φ : U ⟶ X` be an étale morphism of algebraic
spaces and `Z ⊆ X` a closed subspace, with inverse image `Z_U = U ×_X Z` and projection
`p : Z_U ⟶ Z`.  Then the inverse image along `p` of the conormal module of `Z` in `X` is the
conormal module of `Z_U` in `U`:

`𝒞_{Z/X}|_{Z_U} = p^*𝒞_{Z/X} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_U/U}`.

The isomorphism is the square comparison `p^*i^* ≅ i_U^*φ^*` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalPullbackCompIso`, then the inverse image along `i_U` of the
identification of `φ^*` with étale restriction of [Stacks Project, Tag 03LW], then the equality
`𝓘_Z|_U = 𝓘_{Z_U}` of defining ideal sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso (φ : U ⟶ X) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    (modulePullback B S hS
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (Z.1.fromPreimage φ.hom) :
            (⟨(Z.1.preimage φ.hom).toFunctor,
                (isClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2).1⟩ :
              AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
            (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))).obj
        (conormalModule B S hS X Z) ≅
      conormalModule B S hS U (⟨Z.1.preimage φ.hom,
        isClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2⟩ :
        ClosedSubspaces B S hS U.1)
declarations.comment: the conormal module commutes with etale base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO.**  Let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S`, let
`g : X' ⟶ X` be étale — written `φ : U ⟶ X` in the source — and let

```
Z_U --f--> Z
|          |
U  --g-->  X
```

be a cartesian square, so that `Z_U = U ×_X Z` is the inverse image of `Z`.  Then the inverse
image along `f` of the conormal module of `Z` in `X` is the conormal module of `Z_U` in `U`:

`𝒞_{Z/X}|_{Z_U} = f^*𝒞_{Z/X} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_U/U}`.

The identification is the canonical map of Stacks 04CP itself, which is invertible by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalMap_of_isPullback_of_isEtale`; it is therefore canonical by
construction, and functorial in the étale source by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso_comp`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X'.1) (g : X ⟶ X')
    (f : (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
      (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z ≫ g = f ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z')
    (hcart : IsPullback Z.1.ι f.hom g.hom Z'.1.ι)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    (modulePullback B S hS f).obj (conormalModule B S hS X' Z') ≅
      conormalModule B S hS X Z
declarations.comment: the identification, as the canonical map of 04CP, for an etale source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO, the functoriality in the étale source `U`.**  Let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed
subspace, let `g' : X' ⟶ X''` and `g : X ⟶ X'` be étale — written `φ : U ⟶ X` and `ψ : V ⟶ U` in
the source — and let the two squares

```
Z   --f--> Z'  --f'--> Z''
|          |           |
X   --g--> X'  --g'--> X''
```

both be cartesian.  Then the identification of Stacks 04CO for the composite `g ≫ g'` is the
composition comparison of Stacks 03LU for `f` and `f'`, followed by the inverse image along `f`
of the identification for `g'`, followed by the identification for `g`.

The étaleness of the composite and the cartesianness of the outer rectangle are derived from the
hypotheses, so what is assumed is exactly what the tag assumes.  The proof is the composition law
for the canonical map, part (3) of Stacks 04G2
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp`), together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso_hom`: because the
identification *is* the canonical map, its functoriality is that law and needs nothing further.
In particular the composition law for the identification of Stacks 03LW is not needed, which is
what blocks the functoriality of the separately built isomorphism of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ConormalModuleEtaleRestriction.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso_comp
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X'.1)
    (Z'' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X''.1) (g : X ⟶ X') (g' : X' ⟶ X'')
    (f : (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
      (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (f' : (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
      (⟨Z''.1.toFunctor, Z''.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z ≫ g = f ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z')
    (hsq' : subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z' ≫ g' = f' ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X'' Z'')
    (hcart : IsPullback Z.1.ι f.hom g.hom Z'.1.ι)
    (hcart' : IsPullback Z'.1.ι f'.hom g'.hom Z''.1.ι)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) (hg' : IsEtale B S hS g'.hom) :
    (conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso B S hS Z Z'' (g ≫ g') (f ≫ f')
          (by rw [← Category.assoc, hsq, Category.assoc, hsq', Category.assoc])
          ((hcart.flip.paste_horiz hcart'.flip).flip)
          (isEtale_comp B S hS hg hg')).hom =
      (modulePullbackCompIso B S hS f f').inv.app (conormalModule B S hS X'' Z'') ≫
        (modulePullback B S hS f).map
            (conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso B S hS Z' Z'' g' f' hsq' hcart' hg').hom ≫
          (conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionCanonicalIso B S hS Z Z' g f hsq hcart hg).hom
declarations.comment: functoriality in the etale source U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyClosedSubspace_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO, the locally closed clause.**  The inverse image of a locally closed subspace
of an algebraic space along a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a locally closed subspace
of the source.

For an étale `f` this is the clause of Stacks 04CO that `Z_U = U ×_X Z` is a locally closed
subspace of `U`; no étaleness is needed, the inverse image being the fibre product by
Stacks 083Q and immersions being stable under base change by Stacks 02YW.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyClosedSubspace_preimage
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (Z : Subfunctor X)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyClosedSubspace B S hS Z) :
    IsLocallyClosedSubspace B S hS (Z.preimage f)
declarations.comment: Z_U = U ×_X Z is a locally closed subspace of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`φ : U ⟶ X` be étale and let `Z_U = U ×_X Z` with projections `p : Z_U ⟶ Z` and `i_U : Z_U ⟶ U`.
Then the inverse image along `p` of the conormal module of `Z` in `X` is the conormal module of
`Z_U` in `U`:

`𝒞_{Z/X}|_{Z_U} = p^*𝒞_{Z/X} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_U/U}`.

Both conormal modules are taken through the closed factorisation of Stacks 04CE, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionConormalModule`; `i_U` is an immersion because immersions are
stable under base change.  The isomorphism is the degree-one instance of the conormal-algebra
isomorphism of Stacks 09RR, conjugated by the bridge
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionPieceIso` at `i` and at `i_U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalModuleOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso (p : ZU ⟶ Z) (iU : ZU ⟶ U)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (φ : U ⟶ X) (sq : IsPullback p iU i φ) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) :
    (modulePullback B S hS p).obj (immersionConormalModule B S hS i hi) ≅
      immersionConormalModule B S hS iU (isImmersion_of_isPullback B S hS sq hi)
declarations.comment: the conormal module of an immersion commutes with etale localisation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleSubspaceEtaleRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO in the shape the source states it.**  Let `Z` be a locally closed subspace of
an algebraic space `X` over `S`, let `φ : U ⟶ X` be étale and let `Z_U = U ×_X Z` be the inverse
image of `Z`, a locally closed subspace of `U` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyClosedSubspace_preimage`.  Then the inverse image along the
projection `p : Z_U ⟶ Z` of the conormal module of `Z` in `X` is the conormal module of `Z_U` in
`U`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso` at the cartesian
square of Stacks 083Q, the inverse image being the fibre product by
`CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.isPullback_preimage`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalModuleSubspaceEtaleRestrictionIso (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) (Z : Subfunctor X.1)
    (hZ : IsLocallyClosedSubspace B S hS Z) :
    (modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk (Z.fromPreimage φ.hom) :
          (⟨(Z.preimage φ.hom).toFunctor,
              (isLocallyClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS φ.hom Z X.2 U.2 hZ).1⟩ :
            AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
          (⟨Z.toFunctor, hZ.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))).obj
        (immersionConormalModule B S hS
          (ObjectProperty.homMk Z.ι : (⟨Z.toFunctor, hZ.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ X)
          hZ.2) ≅
      immersionConormalModule B S hS
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (Z.preimage φ.hom).ι :
          (⟨(Z.preimage φ.hom).toFunctor,
              (isLocallyClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS φ.hom Z X.2 U.2 hZ).1⟩ :
            AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ U)
        (isLocallyClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS φ.hom Z X.2 U.2 hZ).2
declarations.comment: the conormal module of a locally closed subspace commutes with etale localisation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleSchemeEtaleRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `U` be a
scheme of the site and `φ : U ⟶ X` étale.  Then

* the fibre product `Z_U = U ×_X Z` is a scheme `R` of the site, and for every presentation of
  it by a cartesian square with `j : R ⟶ U` and `p : Z_U ⟶ Z`:
* `j` is an immersion of schemes, so `Z_U` is a locally closed subscheme of `U`;
* the canonical map `𝒞_{Z/X}|_{Z_U} = p^*𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z_U/U}` — the canonical map of
  [Stacks Project, Tag 04CP] of the square followed by part (1) of [Stacks Project, Tag 04G2],
  whose target is the conormal sheaf `Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf` of the immersion of schemes
  `j` of Morphisms, Definition [Stacks Project, Tag 01R2] read on the small étale site — is an
  isomorphism;
* this identification is functorial in `U`: for a morphism `ψ : U' ⟶ U` of schemes over `X`
  with induced `b : Z_{U'} ⟶ Z_U`, the identification for `U'` is the restriction along `b` of
  the identification for `U` followed by the canonical map of Morphisms, Lemma
  [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalModuleSchemeEtaleRestriction (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (φ : (⟨yoneda.obj V, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS V⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) :
    (∃ (R : BigFppfOver B S hS) (j : R ⟶ V)
      (p : (⟨yoneda.obj R, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS R⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ Z),
      IsPullback p (representedSpaceMap B S hS j) i φ) ∧
    ∀ {R : BigFppfOver B S hS} (j : R ⟶ V)
      (p : (⟨yoneda.obj R, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS R⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ Z)
      (sq : IsPullback p (representedSpaceMap B S hS j) i φ),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map j) ∧
      (haveI := isImmersion_toScheme_of_isPullback B S hS sq hi
      IsIso (conormalMapOfImmersions B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS j) i
        p φ
        (isImmersion_representedSpaceMap B S hS j) hi sq.w.symm ≫
        (conormalModuleOfImmersionRepresentedIso B S hS j).hom)) ∧
      ∀ {R' V' : BigFppfOver B S hS} (ψ : V' ⟶ V) (j' : R' ⟶ V') (b : R' ⟶ R)
        (hb : j' ≫ ψ = b ≫ j)
        (sq' : IsPullback (representedSpaceMap B S hS b ≫ p) (representedSpaceMap B S hS j') i
          (representedSpaceMap B S hS ψ ≫ φ)),
        haveI := isImmersion_toScheme_of_isPullback B S hS sq hi
        haveI := isImmersion_toScheme_of_isPullback B S hS sq' hi
        conormalMapOfImmersions B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS j') i
            (representedSpaceMap B S hS b ≫ p) (representedSpaceMap B S hS ψ ≫ φ)
            (isImmersion_representedSpaceMap B S hS j') hi sq'.w.symm ≫
          (conormalModuleOfImmersionRepresentedIso B S hS j').hom =
          (modulePullbackCompIso B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS b) p).inv.app
              (immersionConormalModule B S hS i hi) ≫
            (modulePullback B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS b)).map
              (conormalMapOfImmersions B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS j) i
            p φ
            (isImmersion_representedSpaceMap B S hS j) hi sq.w.symm ≫
                (conormalModuleOfImmersionRepresentedIso B S hS j).hom) ≫
            (representedAssociatedModulePullbackIso B S hS b
                (relativelyRepresentable_yoneda_map B S hS b)
                (Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map j))).hom ≫
            (representedSmallEtaleModuleEquivalence B S hS R').functor.map
              ((_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule (associatedBigEtaleSite B)
                  ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj R') R'.left.property).map
                (Stacks.Immersion.immersionConormalSheafMap
                  ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map j')
                  ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map j)
                  ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map b)
                  ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ψ)
                  (toShHom_square_of_comp_eq B S hS j' j b ψ hb)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleIdealSheafRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CO.** The étale restriction of the defining ideal sheaf of a closed subspace
`Z ⊆ X` along an étale `φ : U ⟶ X` is the defining ideal sheaf of the inverse image `φ⁻¹(Z)`.

Over every étale chart of `U` the two sheaves have the same sections, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealAt_preimage_eq_definingIdealAt_postcomp`, and this
isomorphism is the identity on the underlying regular functions there.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleIdealSheafRestrictionIso (φ : U ⟶ X) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS φ hφ).obj
        (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z).toSheafOfModules ≅
      (definingIdealSheaf B S hS U (⟨Z.1.preimage φ.hom,
        isClosedSubspace_preimage B S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2⟩ :
        ClosedSubspaces B S hS U.1)).toSheafOfModules
declarations.comment: the ideal sheaf of the inverse image is the restriction of the ideal sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
**The functoriality of Stacks 04CO in the étale source.**  For étale morphisms
`ψ : V ⟶ U` and `φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces with étale composite and a closed subspace
`Z ⊆ X`, the identification `p^*𝒞_{Z/X} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_V/V}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CO] taken in two
steps — the comparison of the inverse images along the two projections of [Stacks Project,
Tag 03LU], then the inverse image along `q : ψ⁻¹(φ⁻¹Z) ⟶ φ⁻¹Z` of the identification for `φ`,
then the identification for `ψ` over `φ⁻¹(Z)` — is the identification for `ψ ≫ φ` taken in one
step.  This is the "functorially in `U`" of the source.

The route is the one of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CP]: both sides are read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_eq_conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso_hom`, which identifies
the canonical map of that tag at an étale restriction square with the forward map constructed by
[Stacks Project, Tag 04CO], and the clause becomes part (3) of [Stacks Project, Tag 04G2] at the
two stacked étale restriction squares, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp_of_spaces`.  The one-step identification for `ψ ≫ φ` is
read at the *iterated* spelling `ψ⁻¹(φ⁻¹Z)` of the upper closed subspace and with the projection
written as the composite `q ≫ p`, which costs nothing: an iota-crossing in a first-order argument
position of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap` is free, so neither
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspacePreimage_comp` nor
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.subspaceProjection_comp` has to be rewritten.

The two-step composite is written out here rather than quoted as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalEtaleRestrictionTwoStep`; the implementation notes of this file
record why, and that the difference is one of spelling and not of content.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso_hom_comp (ψ : V ⟶ U) (φ : U ⟶ X)
    (hψ : IsEtale C S hS ψ.hom) (hφ : IsEtale C S hS φ.hom)
    (hψφ : IsEtale C S hS (ψ ≫ φ).hom) (Z : ClosedSubspaces C S hS X.1) :
    (modulePullbackCompIso C S hS
          (ObjectProperty.homMk ((Z.1.preimage φ.hom).fromPreimage ψ.hom) :
        (⟨((Z.1.preimage φ.hom).preimage ψ.hom).toFunctor,
          (isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS ψ.hom (Z.1.preimage φ.hom) U.2 V.2
            (isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2)).1⟩ :
        AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) ⟶
        (⟨(Z.1.preimage φ.hom).toFunctor,
          (isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2).1⟩ :
        AlgebraicSpaces C S hS))
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (Z.1.fromPreimage φ.hom) :
        (⟨(Z.1.preimage φ.hom).toFunctor,
          (isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2).1⟩ :
        AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) ⟶
        (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS))).inv.app (conormalModule C S hS X Z) ≫
        (modulePullback C S hS
            (ObjectProperty.homMk ((Z.1.preimage φ.hom).fromPreimage ψ.hom) :
        (⟨((Z.1.preimage φ.hom).preimage ψ.hom).toFunctor,
          (isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS ψ.hom (Z.1.preimage φ.hom) U.2 V.2
            (isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2)).1⟩ :
        AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) ⟶
        (⟨(Z.1.preimage φ.hom).toFunctor,
          (isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2).1⟩ :
        AlgebraicSpaces C S hS))).map
          (conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso C S hS φ hφ Z).hom ≫
          (conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso C S hS ψ hψ
            (⟨Z.1.preimage φ.hom,
          isClosedSubspace_preimage C S hS φ.hom Z.1 X.2 U.2 Z.2⟩ :
          ClosedSubspaces C S hS U.1)).hom =
      (conormalModuleEtaleRestrictionIso C S hS (ψ ≫ φ) hψφ Z).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CP for closed immersions.**  The canonical map of `𝒪_Z`-modules
`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X'} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` attached to a commutative square of algebraic spaces in which `Z` is a
closed subspace of `X` and `Z'` a closed subspace of `X'`: the inverse image along the inclusion
of `Z` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealSheafMap`, read through the identification
`f^*(i')^* ≅ i^*g^*` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalPullbackCompIso`.

The source states the lemma for immersions and reduces it to closed immersions at the start of
its proof; the lemma for arbitrary immersions is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMapOfImmersions`, and the implementation notes of this file say
why the closed case is the one carried here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalMap
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z ≫ g = f ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z') :
    (modulePullback B S hS f).obj (conormalModule B S hS X' Z') ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS X Z
declarations.comment: the canonical map, for closed immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMapOfImmersions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04CP.**  Let
```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```
be a commutative square of algebraic spaces over `S` in which `i` and `i'` are immersions.  Then
there is a canonical map of `𝒪_Z`-modules

`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X'} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}`

between the conormal modules of the two immersions.

The conormal modules are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionConormalModule`, the conormal
modules taken through the canonical closed factorisation of Stacks 04CE, which is how the
source's reduction of an immersion to a closed immersion into an open subspace is carried.  The
map is the degree-one canonical map `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraSquarePieceMap` of
the square, conjugated by the bridge `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionPieceIso`
at `i'` and at `i`; the module documentation of this file explains why that construction needs no
choice of ambient open subspaces and no hypothesis beyond the commutativity of the square.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalMapOfImmersions (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom) (hi' : IsImmersion B S hS i'.hom)
    (hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i') :
    (modulePullback B S hS f).obj (immersionConormalModule B S hS i' hi') ⟶
      immersionConormalModule B S hS i hi
declarations.comment: the canonical map, for arbitrary immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalMap_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
