declarations.name: HenselianLocalRing.isLocalHom_indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue
declarations.doc: `HenselianLocalRing.indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue` is a local ring map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem HenselianLocalRing.isLocalHom_indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue
    (hind : (CommAlgCat.etale.{max u v} R).ind.{max u v}
      (CommAlgCat.of R (ULift.{u} Rsh)))
    (φ : ResidueField Rsh →+* ResidueField Ssh)
    (hφ : φ.comp ((residue Rsh).comp (algebraMap R Rsh))
      = (residue Ssh).comp (algebraMap R Ssh)) :
    IsLocalHom (HenselianLocalRing.indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue hind φ hφ)
declarations.comment: `indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue` is local, which the source asserts

declarations.name: HenselianLocalRing.indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue_unique
declarations.doc:
`HenselianLocalRing.indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue` is the only local `R`-algebra map `Rsh → Ssh`
inducing `φ` on residue fields.
declarations.statement:
public theorem HenselianLocalRing.indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue_unique
    (hind : (CommAlgCat.etale.{max u v} R).ind.{max u v}
      (CommAlgCat.of R (ULift.{u} Rsh)))
    (φ : ResidueField Rsh →+* ResidueField Ssh)
    (hφ : φ.comp ((residue Rsh).comp (algebraMap R Rsh))
      = (residue Ssh).comp (algebraMap R Ssh))
    (f : Rsh →ₐ[R] Ssh) (hfloc : IsLocalHom f)
    (hf : (residue Ssh).comp (f : Rsh →+* Ssh) = φ.comp (residue Rsh)) :
    f = HenselianLocalRing.indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue hind φ hφ

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization.existsUnique_algHom
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of the strict henselization against a henselian local algebra**
(Stacks 04GU). Let `A` be a local ring, let `κ^sep` be a separable algebraic closure of its
residue field and let `R` be a strict henselization of `A` with respect to it. Let `C` be a
henselian local `A`-algebra, and let `χ : κ^sep → κ(C)` be a ring map compatible with the residue
maps of `A → R` and `A → C` (the square of fields of the source). Then there is exactly one local
`A`-algebra map `R → C` inducing `χ` on residue fields.

The source states this for `C` a strict henselization of a local ring `S` receiving a local map
from `A`; Lemma 04GU uses of `C` only that it is a henselian local `A`-algebra, and that is the
form taken here, since the target that this is applied to is known to be strictly henselian before
it is known to be a strict henselization.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStrictHenselization.existsUnique_algHom (hR : IsStrictHenselization A κsep R)
    {C : Type*} [CommRing C] [HenselianLocalRing C] [Algebra A C]
    (χ : κsep →+* ResidueField C)
    (hχ : ∀ a : A, χ (algebraMap (maximalIdeal A).ResidueField κsep
        (algebraMap A (maximalIdeal A).ResidueField a))
      = residue C (algebraMap A C a)) :
    ∃! f : R →ₐ[A] C, IsLocalHom f ∧
      (residue C).comp (f : R →+* C) = (χ.comp hR.residueFieldHom).comp (residue R)
declarations.comment:
The universal property read off `IsStrictHenselization`: the residue datum is a map
out of the chosen separable closure `κ^sep` rather than out of `IsLocalRing.ResidueField R`, the
convention `HenselianLocalRing.indEtaleAlgHomOfResidue` is phrased in, and the target is an
arbitrary henselian local `A`-algebra as there. Existence and uniqueness among local `A`-algebra
maps are the source's two assertions.

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization.exists_algHom_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**A strictly henselian local algebra receives a local map from the strict henselization.**
Let `A` be a local ring, let `κ^sep` be a separable algebraic closure of its residue field and let
`R` be a strict henselization of `A` with respect to it. Let `C` be a henselian local `A`-algebra
with separably closed residue field whose structure map is local. Then there is a local
`A`-algebra map `R → C`.

No residue datum has to be supplied: `κ^sep` is separable over `κ_A` and `κ(C)` is a separably
closed field over `κ_A` through the residue map of `A → C`, so `IsSepClosed.lift` produces one,
and `existsUnique_algHom` turns it into the map. Uniqueness is *not* asserted, and genuinely
fails: the local maps `R → C` over `A` are permuted by the automorphisms of `κ^sep` over `κ_A`,
and it is the residue datum that singles one out.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStrictHenselization.exists_algHom_of_isSepClosed (hR : IsStrictHenselization A κsep R)
    (C : Type*) [CommRing C] [HenselianLocalRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A C)] (hC : IsSepClosed (ResidueField C)) :
    ∃ f : R →ₐ[A] C, IsLocalHom f
declarations.comment:
The source's map, in the case where the target's residue field is only known to be
separably closed rather than identified with a chosen separable closure: the residue datum is then
not part of the input but produced by `IsSepClosed.lift`, and only existence survives.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isFiltered_etaleNeighborhood_and_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**The henselization as a colimit of étale neighborhoods** (Stacks 04GV). Let `p` be a prime of
`R` and let `Rh` be a henselization of `R_p`. The category of étale neighborhoods `(S, q)` of `p`
with `κ(q) = κ(p)` is filtered, and `Rh` is canonically the colimit of the algebras `S` and also of
the local rings `S_q`. The canonical maps `S → Rh` are the unique `R`-algebra maps inducing
`κ(q) = κ(p) ≅ κ(Rh)` on residue fields, and the maps `S_q → Rh` extend them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_etaleNeighborhood_and_isColimit :
    IsFiltered (EtaleNeighborhood p) ∧
      ∃ ι : EtaleNeighborhood.forget p ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of R Rh),
        (∀ A x, residue Rh ((ι.app A).hom x) =
          ResidueField.map (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p) Rh) (A.hom.hom x)) ∧
        (∀ ι' : EtaleNeighborhood.forget p ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of R Rh),
          (∀ A x, residue Rh ((ι'.app A).hom x) =
            ResidueField.map (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p) Rh) (A.hom.hom x)) → ι' = ι) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ ι)) ∧
        ∃ ιLoc : EtaleNeighborhood.localization p ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of R Rh),
          (∀ A, (EtaleNeighborhood.toLocalization p).app A ≫ ιLoc.app A = ι.app A) ∧
          Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ ιLoc))
declarations.comment:
Étale neighborhoods `(S, q)` with `κ(p) = κ(q)` are étale `R`-algebras with an
augmentation to `κ(p)`, whose kernel is `q`. `canonically` is the characterization of the colimit
maps `S → (R_p)^h`: the unique family inducing the identity of `κ(p) = κ((R_p)^h)` on residue
fields; the maps `S_q → (R_p)^h` are pinned by extending them along `S → S_q`. The henselization is
`IsHenselization` with residue field `κ(p)`.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isFiltered_augmentedEtale_and_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**The strict henselization as a colimit of étale algebras** (Stacks 04GW). Let `p` be a prime
of `R`, let `L` be an extension of `κ(p)` (a separable algebraic closure `κ^sep`, in the source),
let `Rsh` be a henselization of `R_p` with residue field `L` (the strict henselization
`(R_p)^{sh}`), and fix an isomorphism `e : L ≅ κ(Rsh)` compatible with the maps from `R`. The
category of étale `R`-algebras `S` with an `R`-algebra map `S → L` — the triples `(S, q, φ)` — is
filtered, and `Rsh` is canonically the colimit of the algebras `S` and also of the local rings
`S_q`, where `q` is the kernel of `S → L`. The canonical maps `S → Rsh` are the unique `R`-algebra
maps whose reduction is `S → L ≅ κ(Rsh)`, and the maps `S_q → Rsh` extend them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_augmentedEtale_and_isColimit [IsScalarTower R (Localization.AtPrime p) Rsh] :
    IsFiltered (AugmentedEtale R L) ∧
      ∃ ι : forget R L ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of R Rsh),
        (∀ A x, residue Rsh ((ι.app A).hom x) = e (A.hom.hom x)) ∧
        (∀ ι' : forget R L ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of R Rsh),
          (∀ A x, residue Rsh ((ι'.app A).hom x) = e (A.hom.hom x)) → ι' = ι) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ ι)) ∧
        ∃ ιLoc : localization R L ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommAlgCat.of R Rsh),
          (∀ A, (toLocalization R L).app A ≫ ιLoc.app A = ι.app A) ∧
          Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ ιLoc))
declarations.comment:
A triple `(S, q, φ)` is an étale `R`-algebra with an `R`-algebra map to `κ^sep`,
whose kernel is `q`. The strict henselization of `R_p` with respect to `κ^sep` is
`IsHenselization (Localization.AtPrime p) κsep Rsh`; the statement is proved for any extension `L`
of `κ(p)`. `canonically` is the characterization of the colimit maps `S → Rsh`: given the
identification `e : κ^sep ≅ κ(Rsh)`, they are the unique maps reducing to `S → κ^sep ≅ κ(Rsh)`;
the maps `S_q → Rsh` extend them along `S → S_q`.

declarations.name: bijOn_solutions_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 04GX.**
Let `φ : R → S` be a local homomorphism of strictly henselian local rings and let
`P_1, …, P_n ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n]` be polynomials such that `R[x_1, …, x_n]/(P_1, …, P_n)` is
étale over `R`. Then the coordinatewise map `r ↦ (fun i => φ (r i))` induces a bijection
between the solutions of the `P_i` over `R` and the solutions of their images `P_i^φ` over
`S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_solutions_of_etale
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [HenselianLocalRing R] [HenselianLocalRing S]
    [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)] [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField S)]
    (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : IsLocalHom φ)
    (n : ℕ) (P : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
    [Algebra.Etale R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range P))] :
    Set.BijOn (fun r : Fin n → R => (fun i => φ (r i) : Fin n → S))
      {r : Fin n → R | ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval r (P i) = 0}
      {s : Fin n → S | ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval s (MvPolynomial.map φ (P i)) = 0}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.exists_over_equiv_sheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04GZ: `Sh(C)/F` is a topos.** For a sheaf `F` on a site `(C, J)`, the slice
`Sh(C)/F` is equivalent to the category of sheaves of sets on a site, namely the site `C/F` of
`sheafOverEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.exists_over_equiv_sheaf (F : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    ∃ (D : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory D) (K : GrothendieckTopology D),
      Nonempty (Over F ≌ Sheaf K (Type u))
declarations.comment:
the category Sh(C)/F is a topos: it is equivalent to Sh(C/F), sheaves on the site
  of pairs (U, s) with s ∈ F(U)

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafOverLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04GZ.** Let `(C, J)` be a site and `F` a sheaf on it. The localization morphism
`j_F : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)` is the morphism of topoi with inverse image `j_F⁻¹ = toOver F`, i.e.
`H ↦ (H × F ⟶ F)`, and pushforward `j_{F,*} = overLocalizationPushforward J F`, its right
adjoint.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafOverLocalization (F : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Over F) (Sheaf J (Type u))
declarations.comment:
the canonical morphism of topoi j_F : Sh(C)/F → Sh(C), with j_F^{-1} = toOver F
  and j_{F,*} its right adjoint, constructed through Sh(C)/F ≌ Sh(C/F)

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafOverLocalization_inverseImage_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04GZ (1).** The inverse image of `j_F : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)` is
`H ↦ (H × F ⟶ F)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sheafOverLocalization_inverseImage_obj (F H : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    (sheafOverLocalization J F).inverseImage.obj H = Over.mk (snd H F)
declarations.comment: (1): the functor j_F^{-1} is H ↦ H × F / F

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafOverLocalizationShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04GZ (2).** The functor `j_{F!}` of `j_F : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)` is the forgetful functor
`(G ⟶ F) ↦ G`: it is left adjoint to `j_F⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafOverLocalizationShriek (F : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    Over.forget F ⊣ (sheafOverLocalization J F).inverseImage
declarations.comment: (2): the functor j_{F!} is the forgetful functor G/F ↦ G

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafOverLocalization_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04GZ: `j_F` is a localization.** The triple of adjoints
`j_{F!} ⊣ j_F⁻¹ ⊣ j_{F,*}` of `j_F : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)`, with `j_{F!} = Over.forget F` and
`j_F⁻¹ = toOver F`, as in Section 7.25 (tag 00XZ).
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafOverLocalization_isLocalization (F : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    Nonempty (Over.forget F ⊣ (sheafOverLocalization J F).inverseImage) ∧
      Nonempty ((sheafOverLocalization J F).inverseImage ⊣
        (sheafOverLocalization J F).pushforward) ∧
      (sheafOverLocalization J F).inverseImage = toOver F
declarations.comment:
j_F is a localization: the triple of adjoints j_{F!} ⊣ j_F^{-1} ⊣ j_{F,*}, with
  j_{F!} the forgetful functor and j_F^{-1} = H ↦ H × F / F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.homPushforwardEquivRightInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H0.** Let `E` be a topos, `F` an object of `E` and `j_{F,*} = p` a pushforward
for the localization `j_F : E/F ⟶ E`, i.e. a right adjoint of `j_F⁻¹ = toOver F`.  For an object
`φ : G ⟶ F` of `E/F` and any object `A` of `E`, the maps `A ⟶ j_{F,*}(G/F)` are in bijection
with the morphisms `α : F|_A ⟶ G|_A` of `E/A` that are right inverse to `φ|_A`, restriction to
`A` being `(-)|_A = j_A⁻¹ = toOver A`.

Taking `A = h_U^#` and using `Γ(U, -) = Hom(h_U^#, -)` this is Stacks 04H0: the sections of
`j_{F,*}(G/F)` over `U` are the right inverses of `φ|_U`.  The proof follows the Stacks one: the
adjunction defining `p` identifies `Hom(A, j_{F,*}(G/F))` with the fibre of `φ ∘ (-)` over the
projection `A ⊗ F ⟶ F`, and interchanging the two factors turns that fibre into the set of right
inverses of `φ|_A`.

Two things are *not* covered: the bijection is stated pointwise in `A`, its naturality in `A`
(which is what makes the right-inverse description a description of the sheaf rather than of its
individual section sets) being left implicit; and `F|_A` is read in the slice `E/A`, whereas
Stacks reads it in `Sh(C/U)` via the equivalence `Sh(C/U) ≃ Sh(C)/h_U^#` of Stacks 00Y1, which
is not yet available.

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H1.** Let `f : E ⟶ D` be a morphism of topoi and `G` an object of `D`.  Localizing
`E` at `F = f⁻¹G` and `D` at `G` gives a morphism of topoi `f' : E/F ⟶ D/G` whose inverse image
is `Over.post f⁻¹`, i.e.
```
(f')⁻¹(H ⟶ G) = (f⁻¹H ⟶ f⁻¹G) ,
```
which is the property characterizing `f'`.  Its pushforward is
`(K ⟶ F) ↦ (f_*K ×_{f_*f⁻¹G} G ⟶ G)`, the right adjoint supplied by
`CategoryTheory.Over.postAdjunctionLeft`, and its inverse image is left exact because `f⁻¹` is.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def over : MorphismOfTopoi (Over (f.inverseImage.obj G)) (Over G)
declarations.comment: the morphism f' and the description of (f')⁻¹

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.inverseImageCompToOverIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H1**, commutativity of the square on inverse images: `j_F⁻¹ ∘ f⁻¹ = (f')⁻¹ ∘ j_G⁻¹`,
where `j_G⁻¹ = toOver G` and `j_F⁻¹ = toOver (f⁻¹G)`.  Concretely, `f⁻¹` carries the product
`H ⊗ G` over `G` to the product `f⁻¹H ⊗ f⁻¹G` over `f⁻¹G`; this is where the left exactness of
`f⁻¹` enters.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageCompToOverIso :
    f.inverseImage ⋙ toOver (f.inverseImage.obj G) ≅ toOver G ⋙ (f.over G).inverseImage
declarations.comment: commutativity of the square, on inverse images

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.toOverCompPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H1**: `f'_* ∘ j_F⁻¹ = j_G⁻¹ ∘ f_*`.

Both sides are right adjoints — of `(f')⁻¹ ⋙ j_{F!}` and of `j_{G!} ⋙ f⁻¹` respectively — and
those two left adjoints are equal on the nose by `Over.post_forget_eq_forget_comp`, so the
identity follows from uniqueness of right adjoints.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toOverCompPushforwardIso :
    toOver (f.inverseImage.obj G) ⋙ (f.over G).pushforward ≅ f.pushforward ⋙ toOver G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiberOverIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H2.** The point `q = Φ.over x` of the localized site `C/U` lies above the point
`Φ` of `C`: for every sheaf `F` on `C` the stalk of `F` at `Φ` agrees with the stalk of its
restriction `j_U⁻¹F = F.over U` at `q`.  In other words the triangle formed by `q`, `Φ` and the
localization morphism `j_U : Sh(C/U) ⟶ Sh(C)` commutes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafFiberOverIso :
    J.overPullback A X ⋙ (Φ.over x).sheafFiber ≅ Φ.sheafFiber

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.OverPoint.existsUnique_nonempty_iso_ofFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H3.** Let `p` be a point of the site `C` with fibre functor `u`, and `U` an object
of `C`.  Every point `q` of `C/U` lying over `p` (a point of `C/U` with an identification
`j_U ∘ q = p`) is isomorphic over `p` to the point `q_x` of Stacks 04H2 for exactly one
`x ∈ u(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_nonempty_iso_ofFiber (q : OverPoint Φ U) :
    ∃! x : Φ.fiber.obj U, Nonempty (q ≅ ofFiber x)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.OverPoint.fiberEquivOverPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H3.** Let `p` be a point of the site `C` with fibre functor `u`, and `U` an object
of `C`.  The construction `x ↦ q_x` of Stacks 04H2 is a one to one correspondence between the
elements `x ∈ u(U)` and the points `q` of `C/U` lying over `p`, up to isomorphism of points over
`p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fiberEquivOverPoint :
    Φ.fiber.obj U ≃ _root_.Quotient (isIsomorphicSetoid (OverPoint Φ U))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafFiberSigmaEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H4.** Let `C` be a site, `p` a point of `C` given by `u : C ⥤ Set`, and `U` an
object of `C`.  For any sheaf `F` on `C/U`,
```
  (j_{U!}F)_p = ∐_x F_{q_x} ,
```
the coproduct being over the points `q_x` of `C/U` attached to the elements `x` of `u(U)` as in
Stacks 04H2.

Here `j_{U!}` is `(Over.forget U).sheafPullback`, the left adjoint of the restriction
`j_U⁻¹ = GrothendieckTopology.overPullback`, and the coproduct is the sigma type, which is the
coproduct in `Type v`.  The proof combines the presheaf-level statement
`presheafFiberSigmaEquiv` with Stacks 03CD (`OverShriek.sheafifyIso`: `j_{U!}` of a sheafification
is the sheafification of the coproduct presheaf) and Stacks 00Y8 (`Point.presheafFiber` and
`Point.sheafFiber` agree across sheafification).

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsConservativeFamily.over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H6.** Let `{p_i}_{i ∈ I}` be a conservative family of points of a site `(C, J)`,
with fibre functors `u_i`, and let `X` be an object of `C`. Then the points
`q_{i,x} = (p i).over x` of the localized site `C/X` of Stacks 04H2, for `i ∈ I` and
`x ∈ u_i(X)`, form a conservative family of points of `C/X`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H6**, the "in particular": if a site `(C, J)` has enough points, i.e. a
conservative family of points (Stacks 00YK (2)), then so does every localization `C/X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasConservativeFamily.over (h : HasConservativeFamily.{w} J) (X : C)
    [HasSheafify (J.over X) (Type w)] : HasConservativeFamily.{w} (J.over X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isLocallyRinged_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04H7, part (1).** The inverse image of a locally ringed site by a
morphism of topoi is locally ringed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyRinged_inverseImage (hY : IsLocallyRinged Y) :
    IsLocallyRinged
      ({ C := C, J := J, O := (inverseImageCommRingFunctor f).obj Y.O } :
        RingedSite.{u, u, u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isLocallyRinged_iff_of_ringedToposEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04H7, part (2).** An equivalence of ringed topoi preserves and
reflects local ringedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyRinged_iff_of_ringedToposEquivalence (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    [f.toToposHom.inverseImage.IsEquivalence] [IsIso f.fSharp] :
    RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged ({ C := Y.C, J := Y.J, O := Y.O } : RingedSite.{v, v, v}) ↔
      RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged ({ C := X.C, J := X.J, O := X.O } : RingedSite.{u, u, u})

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.isLocallyRingedSite_iff
declarations.doc:
Definition 18.40.4 in the source's own spelling (the morphism of Tag 05D7 is an isomorphism,
and the equivalent conditions of Tag 04ES hold) is equivalent to the sections-level predicate
`IsLocallyRingedSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyRingedSite_iff :
    IsIso (oneIsNeverZero X.J X.O) ∧ Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.Condition1 X.O ↔
      LocalizedRingedTopos.IsLocallyRingedSite X
declarations.comment: a ringed topos is locally ringed exactly when its underlying ringed site is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.IsLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04H8.** A ringed topos is locally ringed when the ringed site
presenting it is a locally ringed site.
declarations.statement: abbrev RingedTopos.IsLocallyRinged (X : RingedTopos.{v, u, w}) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.isLocallyRinged_iff_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04H8**, well-posedness. Being locally ringed is a property of a ringed
topos and not of a site presenting it: by Stacks 04H7 part (2) an equivalence of ringed topoi
preserves and reflects it.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingedTopos.isLocallyRinged_iff_of_equivalence {X : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}}
    {Y : RingedTopos.{v, v, v}} (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    [f.toToposHom.inverseImage.IsEquivalence] [IsIso f.fSharp] :
    Y.IsLocallyRinged ↔ X.IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment: well-posedness: invariance under an equivalence of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.HomGeneral.reflectsUnitsObj_of_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H9, (1) ⇒ (3) at independent universes.** If a morphism of ringed sites is
locally ringed, then every left exact functor to sets reflects units for the induced morphism
`f⁻¹O_Y ⟶ O_X`; at a stalk functor this is locality of the induced map of stalk rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem reflectsUnitsObj_of_isLocallyRinged (hf : f.IsLocallyRinged)
    (P : Sheaf X.J (Type w) ⥤ Type t) [PreservesFiniteLimits P] :
    RingedTopos.ReflectsUnitsObj P f.fSharpRingMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.HomGeneral.isLocallyRinged_iff_reflectsUnitsObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H9, (1) ⇔ (3) at independent universes.** For a family of left exact functors to
sets which detects isomorphisms — in practice the stalk functors at a conservative family of
points — a morphism of ringed sites is locally ringed exactly when each member reflects units
for `f⁻¹O_Y ⟶ O_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyRinged_iff_reflectsUnitsObj {ι : Type*}
    (P : ι → Sheaf X.J (Type w) ⥤ Type t) (hP : ∀ i, PreservesFiniteLimits (P i))
    [HasPullback (RingedTopos.unitsιOf X.O)
      (RingedTopos.forgetRingMap f.fSharpRingMap)]
    (hcons : ∀ {F G : Sheaf X.J (Type w)} (ψ : F ⟶ G), (∀ i, IsIso ((P i).map ψ)) → IsIso ψ) :
    f.IsLocallyRinged ↔ ∀ i, RingedTopos.ReflectsUnitsObj (P i) f.fSharpRingMap
declarations.comment: (1)⇔(3) at a conservative family, independent universes

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedTopos.condition1_imp_condition2
declarations.doc:
**Theorem, part 1: (1) ⇒ (2) always holds** (no hypotheses beyond Definition 1).

Each stalk functor `(.)_p = p^{-1}` is exact, hence preserves the cartesian square of
condition (1); together with the identifications `(f^{-1} O_D)_p = O_{D,q}` and
`(f^{-1} O_D^*)_p = O_{D,q}^*`, this yields condition (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem condition1_imp_condition2 (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (h : Condition1 f) : Condition2 f

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedTopos.condition1_of_condition2OnFamily
declarations.doc:
**Theorem, part 4 (general case): (2) on a conservative family implies (1).**

If condition (2) holds for every point of a conservative family of points of `C`, then
condition (1) holds (the family detects cartesianness of the sheaf square).
declarations.statement:
theorem condition1_of_condition2OnFamily (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (P : ConservativeFamily X) (h : Condition2OnFamily f P) :
    Condition1 f

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedTopos.condition1_iff_condition2_of_enoughPoints
declarations.doc:
**Theorem, part 2: if `C` has enough points, then (1) ⇔ (2).**

Forward is part 1. Conversely a conservative family of points detects whether a square
of sheaves is cartesian (cartesianness is preserved and reflected by the exact,
jointly-conservative stalk functors), so condition (2) forces condition (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem condition1_iff_condition2_of_enoughPoints (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (hC : HasEnoughPoints X) :
    Condition1 f ↔ Condition2 f

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedTopos.condition2_iff_condition3_of_locallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Theorem, part 3: in the locally ringed case, (2) ⇔ (3).**

When both topoi are locally ringed, every stalk `O_{C,p}` and `O_{D,q}` is a local ring
(via `IsLocallyRinged.isLocalRing_stalk`, with no enough-points assumption on either
`C` or `D`), so condition (2) at `p` — the cartesianness of the stalk-of-units-sheaves
square — is, via the identifications `(O^*)_p = (O_p)^*` (`stalkUnitsIso`), exactly the
statement that the unit-inclusion square of `phi_p` is cartesian, which by the
algebraic core lemma is equivalent to `phi_p` being a local ring map.
declarations.statement:
theorem condition2_iff_condition3_of_locallyRinged (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (hlrC : IsLocallyRinged X) (hlrD : IsLocallyRinged Y) :
    Condition2 f ↔ Condition3 f

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedTopos.condition1_of_condition3OnFamily_of_locallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Theorem, part 4 (locally ringed case): (3) on a conservative family implies (1).**

If both topoi are locally ringed and `phi_p` is a local ring map for every point `p` of
a conservative family of points of `C`, then condition (1) holds. No enough-points
assumption on `D` is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem condition1_of_condition3OnFamily_of_locallyRinged (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (hlrC : IsLocallyRinged X) (hlrD : IsLocallyRinged Y)
    (P : ConservativeFamily X) (h : Condition3OnFamily f P) :
    Condition1 f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.isLocalHom_sheafFiber_iff_reflectsUnitsObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04H9, reflection of units and locality of the stalk map are equivalent, at
independent universes.**  The fibre functor of `Φ` on sheaves of sets reflects units for `φ`
exactly when the fibre of `φ` at `Φ` taken in commutative rings is a local ring
homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalHom_sheafFiber_iff_reflectsUnitsObj {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} (Φ : J.Point.{w}) {O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    [LocallySmall.{w} C] [J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w})]
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})] :
    IsLocalHom ((Φ.sheafFiber (A := CommRingCat.{w})).map φ).hom ↔
      ReflectsUnitsObj (Φ.sheafFiber (A := Type w)) φ
declarations.comment: that the two spellings of condition (3) at a single point of the site agree, at independent universes: reflection of units by the set-valued fibre functor is locality of the fibre ring map. Neither implication between conditions (1), (2) and (3) is proved here — the forward half of this equivalence is proved in this file and the converse alongside it; what the statement supplies is the bridge at a site with `C : Type u`, `Category.{v} C` and sections at `w` all independent, which the collapsed formulation of StalkCriterion.lean cannot state

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.IsLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
A morphism of ringed topoi is locally ringed when its square of units subsheaves, over the
structure map `fSharpSet f`, is cartesian.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyRinged (f : RingedToposHom X Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.exists_associatedRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of ringed sites induces a morphism of ringed topoi whose underlying morphism of
topoi and whose structure map on underlying sheaves of sets are the given ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_associatedRingedToposHom (f : RingedSite.Hom X Y) :
    ∃ g : RingedToposHom (toRingedTopos X) (toRingedTopos Y),
      (g.toToposHom = f.isMorphismOfSites.morphismOfTopoi) ∧
      HEq (RingedToposHom.fSharpSet g) (fSharpSet f)
declarations.comment: associated ringed-topos morphism of a ringed-site morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.IsLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
A morphism of ringed sites is locally ringed when the units square for its associated morphism
of ringed topoi is cartesian.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyRinged (f : RingedSite.Hom X Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.HomGeneral.IsLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04HA** at independent universes.  A morphism of ringed sites is *locally ringed*
when its square

```
  f⁻¹(O_Y^*) ---> O_X^*
      |             |
      v             v
  f⁻¹(O_Y)  ---> O_X
```

of units subsheaves is cartesian, the bottom arrow being the structure map on underlying sheaves
of sets.  The top arrow is not part of the data: the inclusion of units is a monomorphism, so an
arrow making the square commute is unique if it exists, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.HomGeneral.isLocallyRinged_iff_existsUnique`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyRinged (f : HomGeneral X Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: morphisms of locally ringed sites, independent universes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.HomGeneral.exists_associatedRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04HA** at independent universes.  A morphism of ringed sites induces a morphism of
ringed topoi whose underlying morphism of topoi is `HomGeneral.toposHom` and whose structure map
on underlying sheaves of sets is `HomGeneral.fSharpSet`.

As in `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.exists_associatedRingedToposHom`, the statement is
existential rather than a construction: the structure map of a morphism of ringed sites lands in
the *restriction* `u^s O_X` along the site functor, whereas a morphism of ringed topoi needs it
in the direct image `f_* O_X` along the induced morphism of topoi, and those agree only up to
`Stacks.Sheaves.ToposPullback.restrictionCommRingIso`, which is the identity on underlying
sheaves of sets but not the identity map of sheaves of commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem HomGeneral.exists_associatedRingedToposHom (f : HomGeneral X Y) :
    ∃ g : RingedToposHom (toRingedTopos X) (toRingedTopos Y),
      (g.toToposHom = f.toposHom) ∧ HEq (RingedToposHom.fSharpSet g) f.fSharpSet

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_eq_of_residueFieldMap_eq
declarations.doc:
Two morphisms over `S` to a scheme unramified over `S` which have the same value and
induce the same residue-field map at `x` agree on an open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_eq_of_residueFieldMap_eq {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : Over S}
    (f g : X ⟶ Y) (x : X.left) [Unramified Y.hom]
    (hfg : f.left x = g.left x)
    (hκ : f.left.residueFieldMap x =
      (Y.left.residueFieldCongr hfg).hom ≫ g.left.residueFieldMap x) :
    ∃ U : X.left.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ U.ι ≫ f.left = U.ι ≫ g.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothOverMap_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
The functor `V / T ↦ V / S` between the big smooth sites over `T` and over `S`, given by
composing the structure morphism with `f`, is cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
public instance bigSmoothOverMap_isCocontinuous
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (Over.map f).IsCocontinuous
      (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
      (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothOverMap_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
The functor `V / T ↦ V / S` between the big smooth sites over `T` and over `S` is
continuous.
declarations.statement:
public instance bigSmoothOverMap_isContinuous
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (Over.map f).IsContinuous
      (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
      (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothOverMapPullbackAdj
declarations.doc:
Base change along `f`, the functor `(U → S) ↦ (U ×_S T → T)` between the big smooth sites
over `S` and over `T`, is right adjoint to composition with `f`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmoothOverMapPullbackAdj
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (Over.map f : BigSmoothOver B T.obj T.property ⥤ BigSmoothOver B S.obj S.property) ⊣
      Over.pullback f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothOverPullback_isContinuous
declarations.doc: Base change along `f` is continuous for the two localized big smooth topologies.
declarations.statement:
public instance bigSmoothOverPullback_isContinuous
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (Over.pullback f).IsContinuous
      (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
      (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi
declarations.doc:
The big smooth morphism of topoi associated to a morphism `f : T ⟶ S` in a big smooth site,
induced by the cocontinuous functor sending `V ⟶ T` to the composite `V ⟶ T ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoiPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
The direct image of the big smooth morphism of topoi attached to postcomposition along `f`
is isomorphic to the direct image along the continuous base-change functor `Over.pullback f`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoiPushforwardIso
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).pushforward ≅
      (Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoiPullbackAdjunction
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of the big smooth morphism of topoi is left adjoint to restriction along
base change.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoiPullbackAdjunction
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).inverseImage ⊣
      (Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoiInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of the big smooth morphism of topoi is isomorphic to the left adjoint of
restriction along base change.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoiInverseImageIso
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).inverseImage ≅
      ((Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property)).leftAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothInverseImageObjIso
declarations.doc:
The sections of an inverse image on `U / T` are the sections of the sheaf on `U / S`:
`f⁻¹(G)(U / T) = G(U / S)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmoothInverseImageObjIso
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S)
    (G : Sheaf (BigSmoothOver.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1))) (U : Over T) :
    ((bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).inverseImage.obj G).obj.obj (Opposite.op U) ≅
      G.obj.obj (Opposite.op (Over.mk (U.hom ≫ f)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothPushforwardObjIso
declarations.doc:
The sections of a direct image on `U / S` are the sections of the sheaf on the base change
`U ×_S T / T`: `f_*(F)(U / S) = F(U ×_S T / T)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmoothPushforwardObjIso
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S)
    (F : Sheaf (BigSmoothOver.topology B T.obj T.property) (Type (u + 1))) (U : Over S) :
    ((bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).pushforward.obj F).obj.obj (Opposite.op U) ≅
      F.obj.obj (Opposite.op (Over.mk (pullback.snd U.hom f)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothInverseImage_isRightAdjoint
declarations.doc: The inverse image of a big smooth morphism of topoi has a left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance bigSmoothInverseImage_isRightAdjoint
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).inverseImage.IsRightAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc: The lower shriek of a big smooth morphism of topoi preserves fibre products.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance bigSmoothLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan
      (bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).inverseImage.leftAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmoothLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers
declarations.doc: The lower shriek of a big smooth morphism of topoi preserves equalizers.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance bigSmoothLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers
    (B : BigSmoothSite.{u}) {T S : B.category} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair
      (bigSmoothMorphismOfTopoi B f).inverseImage.leftAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSyntomicMorphismOfTopoi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HD.** The big syntomic morphism of topoi attached
to `f : T ⟶ S` in a chosen big syntomic site. Its defining functor sends
`V ⟶ T` to the composite `V ⟶ T ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSyntomicMorphismOfTopoi : MorphismOfTopoi
    (Sheaf (BigSyntomicOver.topology B T.obj T.property) (Type (u + 1)))
    (Sheaf (BigSyntomicOver.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSyntomicMorphismPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HD.** The big syntomic morphism of topoi defined by postcomposition
along `f` is the morphism of topoi induced by the continuous base-change functor
`Over.pullback f`: their direct images are canonically isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSyntomicMorphismPushforwardIso :
    (bigSyntomicMorphismOfTopoi B f).pushforward ≅
      (Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (BigSyntomicOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (BigSyntomicOver.topology B T.obj T.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSyntomicLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HD.** The lower shriek on big syntomic sheaves is left adjoint to
inverse image.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSyntomicLowerShriekAdjunction :
    (Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
      (BigSyntomicOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
      (BigSyntomicOver.topology B S.obj S.property) ⊣
        (bigSyntomicMorphismOfTopoi B f).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSyntomicLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 04HD.** The lower shriek preserves fibre products.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bigSyntomicLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan
      ((Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (BigSyntomicOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
        (BigSyntomicOver.topology B S.obj S.property))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSyntomicLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 04HD.** The lower shriek preserves equalizers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bigSyntomicLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair
      ((Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (BigSyntomicOver.topology B T.obj T.property)
        (BigSyntomicOver.topology B S.obj S.property))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_isClosedImmersion_opens_of_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HH.** After a single étale base change, finitely many distinct points
of one fibre at which a morphism of schemes is unramified are covered, in that fibre, by open
subschemes which are closed immersions over the new base, pass through the distinguished point,
and pairwise avoid one another there.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_isClosedImmersion_opens_of_unramifiedAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (s : S)
    (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s) (hx_injective : Function.Injective x)
    (hunramified : ∀ i, UnramifiedAt f (x i)) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (m : Fin n → ℕ)
      (V : (Σ i, Fin (m i)) → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens),
      (∀ a, IsClosedImmersion ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) ∧
        ∃ y : (pullback f U.toBase : Scheme.{u}),
          y ∈ V a ∧ (pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point) ∧
      (∀ a b, a ≠ b → ∀ y : (pullback f U.toBase : Scheme.{u}),
        y ∈ V a → y ∈ V b → (pullback.snd f U.toBase) y ≠ U.point) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (y : (pullback f U.toBase : Scheme.{u})),
        (pullback.snd f U.toBase) y = U.point →
        (pullback.fst f U.toBase) y = x i →
        ∃ j : Fin (m i), y ∈ V ⟨i, j⟩)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_closed_decomposition_of_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HI.** A separated morphism of schemes which is unramified at finitely
many points of one fibre becomes, after a single étale base change around the image point, the
disjoint union of finitely many closed subschemes of the new base passing through the
distinguished point and a remainder whose distinguished fibre avoids the chosen points. The
remainder has empty distinguished fibre when the chosen points exhaust the original fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_closed_decomposition_of_unramifiedAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (s : S)
    (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s) (hunramified : ∀ i, UnramifiedAt f (x i)) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s)
      (W : (pullback f U.toBase).Opens) (m : Fin n → ℕ)
      (V : (Σ i, Fin (m i)) → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens),
      (sSup (Set.range V) ⊔ W = ⊤) ∧
        (Pairwise (Disjoint on V)) ∧
        (∀ a, Disjoint (V a) W) ∧
        (∀ a, IsClosedImmersion ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase)) ∧
        (∀ a, ∃ z : (V a).toScheme,
          ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase) z = U.point) ∧
        (∀ (z : (W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiber U.point) (i : Fin n),
          ((W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiberι U.point ≫ W.ι ≫
            pullback.fst f U.toBase) z ≠ x i) ∧
    ((∀ y : X, f y = s → ∃ i, y = x i) →
          IsEmpty ((W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiber U.point))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_closed_decomposition_of_finite_unramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HJ.** A finite unramified morphism of schemes becomes a finite
disjoint union of closed immersions after an étale base change around any chosen point of the
target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_closed_decomposition_of_finite_unramified
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsFinite f] [Unramified f] (s : S) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (n : ℕ) (V : Fin n → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens),
      (sSup (Set.range V) = ⊤) ∧
        (Pairwise (Disjoint on V)) ∧
        (∀ j, IsClosedImmersion ((V j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_openCopies_cover_fibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HL.** A morphism which is étale at finitely many distinct points of
one fibre admits, after an étale base change, open subschemes of the base change which map
isomorphically onto the new base, meet one another nowhere over the distinguished point, and
together contain every point of that fibre lying over one of the given points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_openCopies_cover_fibers
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (s : S)
    (hinj : Function.Injective x) (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s) (hetale : ∀ i, EtaleAt f (x i)) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (m : Fin n → ℕ)
      (V : (Σ i, Fin (m i)) → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens),
      (∀ a, IsIso ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase)) ∧
      (∀ a b, a ≠ b → ∀ z : (pullback f U.toBase : Scheme.{u}),
        z ∈ (V a).1 → z ∈ (V b).1 → pullback.snd f U.toBase z ≠ U.point) ∧
      (∀ i (z : (pullback f U.toBase : Scheme.{u})),
        pullback.snd f U.toBase z = U.point → pullback.fst f U.toBase z = x i →
          ∃ j : Fin (m i), z ∈ (V ⟨i, j⟩).1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_openCopies_decomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04HM.** After an étale base change, a separated morphism which is étale
at finitely many points over one point of the base is the disjoint union of copies of the new
base together with a remainder whose distinguished fibre contains none of those points. If the
given points exhaust the original fibre, that remaining fibre is empty.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_openCopies_decomposition
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X) (s : S)
    (hx : ∀ i, f (x i) = s) (hetale : ∀ i, EtaleAt f (x i)) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (W : (pullback f U.toBase).Opens) (m : Fin n → ℕ)
      (V : (Σ i, Fin (m i)) → (pullback f U.toBase).Opens),
      sSup (Set.range V) ⊔ W = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (Disjoint on V) ∧ (∀ a, Disjoint (V a) W) ∧
        (∀ a, IsIso ((V a).ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase)) ∧
        (∀ (z : (W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiber U.point) (i : Fin n),
          ((W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiberι U.point ≫ W.ι ≫
            pullback.fst f U.toBase) z ≠ x i) ∧
        ((∀ y : X, f y = s → ∃ i, y = x i) →
          IsEmpty ((W.ι ≫ pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiber U.point))

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_etale_pullback_iso_sigma
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a finite étale morphism of schemes and let `s : S`. There is an étale
neighbourhood `g : U ⟶ S` of `s`, a finite index type `ι` and an isomorphism
`X ×_S U ≅ ∐_{i : ι} U` over `U`; that is, `X` becomes a finite disjoint union of copies of the
base, each mapping isomorphically onto it, after an étale base change near `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_pullback_iso_sigma {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (s : S) :
    ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (g : U ⟶ S) (_ : Etale g) (u : U) (_ : g u = s) (ι : Type u)
      (_ : Finite ι) (e : pullback f g ≅ ∐ fun _ : ι ↦ U),
      e.hom ≫ Limits.Sigma.desc (fun _ ↦ 𝟙 U) = pullback.snd f g

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_etaleCover_pullback_iso_sigma
declarations.doc:
A finite étale morphism `f : X ⟶ S` admits an étale covering `𝒰` of `S` together with, for
each member `i`, a finite index type `ι i` and an isomorphism `X ×_S 𝒰.X i ≅ ∐_{ι i} 𝒰.X i` over
`𝒰.X i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleCover_pullback_iso_sigma {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFinite f] [Etale f] :
    ∃ (𝒰 : S.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @Etale)) (ι : 𝒰.I₀ → Type u)
      (_ : ∀ i, Finite (ι i)) (e : ∀ i, pullback f (𝒰.f i) ≅ ∐ fun _ : ι i ↦ 𝒰.X i),
      ∀ i, (e i).hom ≫ Limits.Sigma.desc (fun _ ↦ 𝟙 (𝒰.X i)) = pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_isSplitOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04HN**, in terms of sheets. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be finite étale and let `q : V ⟶ S`
be any scheme over `S`. Every point of `V` has an étale neighbourhood `g : W ⟶ V` over which
`f` has sheet data.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isSplitOver {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (q : V ⟶ S) (v : V) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (g : W ⟶ V) (_ : Etale g) (w : W) (_ : g w = v),
      Nonempty (IsSplitOver f (g ≫ q))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricPoint.EtaleNeighborhood.geometricPoint_liesOver_iff

declarations.statement:
theorem geometricPoint_liesOver_iff (U : σ.EtaleNeighborhood) (h : σ.LiesOver s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_geometricPoint_fiber_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04HU, part (1).** Every point of the small étale site of `S` is given by a geometric
point of `S`: its fibre functor is naturally isomorphic to the functor of lifts of that geometric
point, which is the fibre functor of
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricPointSitePoint`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_geometricPoint_fiber_iso
    (p : (SmallEtale.topology B S hS).Point.{u}) :
    ∃ s : GeometricPoint S, Nonempty (p.fiber ≅ geometricPointFiber B S hS s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_geometricPoint_inverseImage_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04HU, part (2).** Every point of the small étale topos of `S` has the geometric
stalk functor of a geometric point of `S` as its inverse image: the stalk of a sheaf `F` at the
point is the colimit of `F` over the category of étale neighbourhoods of that geometric point.

The point of the topos is first reconstructed as a point of the site
(`PointOfTopos.exists_sitePoint_fiber_eq`, Stacks 00YA (2)); that point of the site is then a
geometric point by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_geometricPoint_fiber_iso`, part (1), and the
canonical comparison identifies the two inverse images
(`PointOfTopos.isIso_sheafFiberComparison`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_geometricPoint_inverseImage_iso
    (p : PointOfTopos.{u + 1} (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)) :
    ∃ s : GeometricPoint S,
      Nonempty (p.inverseImage ≅
        sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
          (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj
            (Functor.Elements.π (geometricPointFiber B S hS s)).op ⋙
          colim)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_open_of_isSubterminal_topos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04HV for a subterminal object of the topos of the small étale ringed site.** A
subsheaf of the final object of `(Sh(S_étale), 𝒪_S)` is represented by exactly one open
subscheme of `S`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_open_of_isSubterminal` with its free sections universe
instantiated at the universe `u` of the sections of
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleRingedSite`, a `RingedSite.{u + 1, u, u}`.  Nothing is transported:
`CategoryTheory.IsSubterminal` is a condition in the sheaf category and the representability
conclusion is about the same sheaf, and the two sides are the same category, because
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.Topos` of that ringed site *is*
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type u)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_open_of_isSubterminal_topos (X : B.Scheme)
    (F : (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B X.obj X.property)).Topos)
    (hF : IsSubterminal F) :
    ∃! W : X.obj.Opens,
      Nonempty (F ≅
        (presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type u)).obj
          ((SmallEtale.inclusion B X.obj X.property ⋙
            Over.post (X := B.obj X.obj X.property) B.inclusion).op ⋙
            uliftYoneda.{u}.obj (Over.mk W.ι)))
declarations.comment:
the case of a subterminal object of the topos of
  `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleRingedSite`, whose sections are of `Type u`; this is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_open_of_isSubterminal`, which carries the tag in its own
  generality `Type (max u v)`, instantiated at `v := u` with no transport in between

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_open_of_isSubterminal
declarations.doc:
A subterminal sheaf on the small étale site is represented by a unique open
subscheme of the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_open_of_isSubterminal
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : smallEtaleTopos.{u, max (u + 1) v} B S hS)
    (hF : IsSubterminal F) :
    ∃! W : S.Opens,
      Nonempty (F ≅
        (presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
          (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj
          ((SmallEtale.inclusion B S hS ⋙
            Over.post (X := B.obj S hS) B.inclusion).op ⋙
            uliftYoneda.{max (u + 1) v}.obj (Over.mk W.ι)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the ordinary local ring to the stalk of the
ring-valued étale structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S) :
    S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)) →+*
      ↥(etaleStalk B S hS s
        (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B S hS).obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.structureSheafStalkToGeometricField
declarations.doc: Evaluation of a structure-sheaf stalk germ in the geometric residue field.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def structureSheafStalkToGeometricField
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S) :
    ↥(etaleStalk B S hS s
      (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B S hS).obj) →+* s.residueField

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing_germ
declarations.doc:
The canonical ordinary-to-étale germ map is characterized at every
étale neighborhood by ordinary restriction of sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing_germ
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (U : (geometricPointFiber B S hS s).Elementsᵒᵖ)
    (r : S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))
    (a : Γ((SmallEtale.toScheme B S hS).obj U.unop.1, ⊤)) :
    let f : ((SmallEtale.toScheme B S hS).obj U.unop.1) ⟶ S :=
      B.inclusion.map U.unop.1.obj.hom
    let p := U.unop.2.1
    let x := p (closedPoint s.residueField)
    let h : f x = s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField) :=
      (Scheme.Hom.comp_apply p f (closedPoint s.residueField)).symm.trans
        (congrArg (fun q : s.source ⟶ S => q (closedPoint s.residueField)) U.unop.2.2)
    (f.stalkMap x).hom (h.symm ▸ r) =
        ((SmallEtale.toScheme B S hS).obj U.unop.1).presheaf.germ
          ⊤ x trivial a →
      structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing B S hS s r = (colimit.ι
        ((Functor.Elements.π (geometricPointFiber B S hS s)).op ⋙
          (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B S hS).obj) U).hom a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.structureSheafStalkToGeometricField_ι
declarations.doc:
Evaluation of a germ of the structure sheaf is its value at the chosen
geometric lift on every étale neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
public theorem structureSheafStalkToGeometricField_ι
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (U : (geometricPointFiber B S hS s).Elementsᵒᵖ) :
    (structureSheafStalkToGeometricField B S hS s).comp ((colimit.ι
      ((Functor.Elements.π (geometricPointFiber B S hS s)).op ⋙
        (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B S hS).obj) U).hom) =
      ((U.unop.2.1).appTop ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of s.residueField)).hom).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleLocalRing_strictHenselization_canonical
declarations.doc:
The étale stalk is canonically the strict henselization of the ordinary
local ring, with its residue field identified with the separable subextension
of the geometric point's field.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def etaleLocalRing_strictHenselization_canonical
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (T : IsLocalRing.HenselizationTower
        (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))
        (separableClosure (ResidueField
          (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField))))
          s.residueField)) :
    { e : T.strictHenselization ≃+*
        ↥(etaleStalk B S hS s
          (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B S hS).obj) //
      (∀ r, e (algebraMap
        (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))
        T.strictHenselization r) = structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing B S hS s r) ∧
      (∀ a, structureSheafStalkToGeometricField B S hS s (e a) =
        ((T.strictHenselizationResidueEquiv.symm
          (residue T.strictHenselization a) :
            separableClosure (ResidueField
              (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField))))
              s.residueField) : s.residueField)) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleLocalRing_strictHenselization_unique
declarations.doc:
The comparison is uniquely determined by the map from the ordinary local
ring and by the inclusion of the relative separable closure in the geometric
point's field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleLocalRing_strictHenselization_unique
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (T : IsLocalRing.HenselizationTower
      (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))
      (separableClosure (ResidueField
        (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))) s.residueField))
    (e : T.strictHenselization ≃+*
      ↥(etaleStalk B S hS s
        (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B S hS).obj))
    (hbase : ∀ r, e (algebraMap
      (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))
      T.strictHenselization r) = structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing B S hS s r)
    (hres : ∀ a, structureSheafStalkToGeometricField B S hS s (e a) =
      ((T.strictHenselizationResidueEquiv.symm
        (residue T.strictHenselization a) :
          separableClosure (ResidueField
            (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField))))
            s.residueField) : s.residueField)) :
    e = (etaleLocalRing_strictHenselization_canonical B S hS s T).val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstant_smallEtalePullbackAb_strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
**A locally constant abelian étale sheaf has constant inverse image on the strict
henselization.** The inverse image is locally constant by Tag 093R, and over the spectrum of the
strictly henselian local ring `𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` a locally constant sheaf is constant, because the
canonical geometric point there has the final object of the small étale site as an initial étale
neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConstant_smallEtalePullbackAb_strictHenselization
    (G : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hG : Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant (smallEtaleTopology X) G) :
    Sheaf.IsConstant (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselization B X hX x))
      ((smallEtalePullbackAb (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).obj G)
declarations.comment: a locally constant abelian étale sheaf becomes constant on the strict henselization, because every étale covering of a strictly henselian local scheme splits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.geometricEval
declarations.doc:
**Evaluation of germs at a geometric point.**  The homomorphism from the étale local ring of
`F` at `x̄` to the field of `x̄` sending the germ of a regular function on a small étale
neighbourhood to its value at the chosen lift of `x̄`.
declarations.statement:
def geometricEval (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) :
    ↥(etaleLocalRing B S hS F x) →+* x.val.carrier
declarations.comment: the geometric evaluation map, for an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.instIsFilteredOppositeElementaryEtaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KS.** The opposite of the category of elementary
étale neighborhoods of a point is filtered.
declarations.statement:
instance instIsFilteredOppositeElementaryEtaleNeighborhood
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S) :
    IsFiltered (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood S s)ᵒᵖ
declarations.comment: the henselization is the colimit of O(U) over the étale neighbourhoods with κ(s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isColimit_globalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KS.** A henselization of the local ring of a
scheme at a point is a colimit of the rings of global sections of its
elementary étale neighborhoods.
declarations.statement:
lemma isColimit_globalSections (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S)
    (Rh : Type u) [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh]
    [Algebra (S.presheaf.stalk s) Rh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (S.presheaf.stalk s)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (S.presheaf.stalk s)) Rh] :
    ∃ ι : globalSections S s ⟶
        (Functor.const _).obj (CommRingCat.of Rh),
      (∀ U x, IsLocalRing.residue Rh ((ι.app U).hom x) =
        henselizationResidueFieldMap S s Rh
          (elementaryEtaleAugmentation S s U.unop x)) ∧
      (∀ U : (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood S s)ᵒᵖ,
        IsOverStalk S s Rh U.unop (ι.app U).hom) ∧
      (∀ ι' : globalSections S s ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommRingCat.of Rh),
        (∀ U x, IsLocalRing.residue Rh ((ι'.app U).hom x) =
          henselizationResidueFieldMap S s Rh
            (elementaryEtaleAugmentation S s U.unop x)) →
        (∀ U : (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood S s)ᵒᵖ,
          IsOverStalk S s Rh U.unop (ι'.app U).hom) → ι' = ι) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ ι))
declarations.comment: the henselization is the colimit of O(U) over the étale neighbourhoods with κ(s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleRingedSite_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
The small étale site of a scheme, endowed with its structure sheaf, is a
locally ringed site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleRingedSite_isLocallyRinged :
    RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Base change along `f : X ⟶ Y`, as a functor from the small étale site of `Y` to that of
`X`: an étale scheme `W` over `Y` is sent to the fibre product `W ×_Y X`, which is étale over
`X` because étale morphisms are stable under base change. This is the functor
`u : Y_étale → X_étale, V/Y ↦ X ×_Y V/X` of Tag 04I1, with the fibre product written in the
other order (see `smallEtaleBaseChangeObjIso`).
declarations.statement: public def smallEtaleBaseChange {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.Etale ⥤ X.Etale

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleBaseChangeObjIso_hom_fst
declarations.doc:
The object formula `V/Y ↦ X ×_Y V/X` for the base-change functor `u : Y_étale → X_étale`:
under `smallEtaleBaseChangeObjIso`, the structure morphism of the base change of `V` to `X` is
the first projection `X ×_Y V ⟶ X`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleAbelianHigherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**The higher direct images `R^p f_*` along `f : X ⟶ Y`**: the right derived functors of the
direct image `f_* : Ab(X_étale) ⥤ Ab(Y_étale)` on abelian sheaves of the small étale sites. The
family with `p ≥ 1` is what the source calls the higher direct images.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.inverseImageIsoSheafifyColimitPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04I3.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and let `f⁻¹` be any left adjoint
of the direct image `f_*` on sheaves of sets of the small étale sites (Stacks 03Q0). Then for
every sheaf `G` on `Y_étale`, `f⁻¹ G` is the sheaf associated to the presheaf
`U ↦ colim_{(V, φ : U ⟶ X ×_Y V)} G(V)`, namely `smallEtaleColimitPresheaf f G`. The isomorphism
is natural, being the composite of the uniqueness of left adjoints with the uniqueness of left
Kan extensions.
declarations.statement:
def inverseImageIsoSheafifyColimitPresheaf
    {L : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology Y) (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ⥤
      Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v))}
    (adj : L ⊣ (smallEtaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      (Type (max (u + 1) v)) (smallEtaleTopology Y) (smallEtaleTopology X))
    (G : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology Y) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    L.obj G ≅
      (presheafToSheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj
        (smallEtaleColimitPresheaf.{u, v} f G)
declarations.comment:
for any left adjoint `f⁻¹` of `f_*` on sheaves of sets of the small étale sites,
  `f⁻¹ G` is the sheafification of `U ↦ colim G(V)` over the pairs `(V, U ⟶ X ×_Y V)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleRingedSiteHom_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04I5.** The morphism of ringed sites `(a_small, a_small^♯)` associated to a
morphism of schemes `a : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of locally ringed sites: its square of units
subsheaves is cartesian.

The geometric points of `X` are a conservative family of points of its small étale site, and at
each of them the stalk of `a⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` is the map of étale local rings
`(𝒪_Y)_ȳ ⟶ (𝒪_X)_x̄`, which is a local ring map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleRingedSiteHom_isLocallyRinged :
    (smallEtaleRingedSiteHom B a).IsLocallyRinged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**The existence half of [Stacks Project, Tag 04I6].**  Let `X` and `Y` be schemes of a big
étale site with `Y` affine, and let

`(g, g^♯) : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), 𝒪_Y)`

be a morphism of *locally* ringed topoi.  Then there is a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` such
that `(g, g^♯)` is 2-isomorphic to `(f_{small}, f_{small}^♯)` in the sense of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04IC].

This is the half of the tag that has content; uniqueness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom`, i.e. [Stacks Project, Tag 04LW], and
needs no hypothesis, so it upgrades this to the `∃!` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_schemeHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged` for free.  The affineness of
`X`, which the tag assumes, is not needed; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_schemeHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged (hg : g.IsLocallyRinged) :
    ∃ a : X ⟶ Y,
      Nonempty (RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B a))
declarations.comment: the existence clause: 2-isomorphic to some (f_small, f_small^sharp)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_schemeHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 04I6].**  Let `X` and `Y` be schemes of a big étale site with `Y`
affine, and let

`(g, g^♯) : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), 𝒪_Y)`

be a morphism of *locally* ringed topoi.  Then there is a **unique** morphism of schemes
`f : X ⟶ Y` such that `(g, g^♯)` is 2-isomorphic to `(f_{small}, f_{small}^♯)` in the sense of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04IC].

Existence is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged`, whose content is the
whole of the source's proof: the ring map on global functions and the morphism `f = Spec φ` it
names, the comparison `g⁻¹h_V ≅ h_{X ×_Y V}` at the affine étale charts of `Y` with its stalk
computation through [Stacks Project, Tag 04GX], the transport to all charts along
[Stacks Project, Tag 04HR], and the agreement of the two structure maps.  Uniqueness is
[Stacks Project, Tag 04LW], `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom`.

The tag assumes `X` affine as well; that hypothesis is not needed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_schemeHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged (hg : g.IsLocallyRinged) :
    ∃! a : X ⟶ Y,
      Nonempty (RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B a))

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
registrations.comment:
the uniqueness clause: for two affine schemes and a morphism of locally
  ringed topoi, which this statement covers since it assumes neither

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_schemeHom_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
Let `X` and `Y` be schemes (of a big étale site) and let
`(g, g^♯) : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), 𝒪_Y)` be a morphism of locally ringed topoi.  Then
there is a unique morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` such that `(g, g^♯)` is 2-isomorphic to
`(f_small, f_small^♯)`.

Existence: `f` is glued from the morphisms `f_V : W_V ⟶ V` over the affine opens `V` of `Y`
determined by `g` on global sections (`AlgebraicGeometry.glueHom`), and the 2-isomorphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.twoIsoGlueHom`.  Uniqueness is Stacks 04LW
(`AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom`).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_schemeHom_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    {X Y : B.Scheme}
    (g : RingedToposHom (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B X.obj X.property))
      (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B Y.obj Y.property)))
    (hg : g.IsLocallyRinged) :
    ∃! f : X ⟶ Y, Nonempty (RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B f))

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
registrations.comment:
the uniqueness clause, i.e. the faithfulness half of the full faithfulness
  asserted by the theorem

declarations.name: TwoMorphismOfTopoi.hcomp
declarations.doc:
Horizontal composition `s ⋆ t` of 2-morphisms of topoi: a 2-morphism from `f' ∘ f` to
`g' ∘ g`, given on `ℱ` by either of the two composites `f'_*f_*ℱ ⟶ g'_*g_*ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
def hcomp (s : TwoMorphismOfTopoi f' g') (t : TwoMorphismOfTopoi f g) :
    TwoMorphismOfTopoi (f'.comp f) (g'.comp g)
declarations.comment: horizontal composition s ⋆ t of 2-morphisms of topoi, and its two descriptions

declarations.name: TwoMorphismOfTopoi
declarations.doc:
A *2-morphism* from a morphism of topoi `f : E → F` to a morphism of topoi `g : E → F` is a
transformation of functors `t : f_* ⟶ g_*`.
declarations.statement:
def TwoMorphismOfTopoi {E : Type u} [Category.{v} E] {F : Type u'} [Category.{v'} F]
    (f g : MorphismOfTopoi E F) : Type _
declarations.comment: a 2-morphism f ⇒ g of morphisms of topoi is a transformation f_* ⟶ g_*

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.TwoMorphismOfRingedTopoi
declarations.doc:
A 2-morphism of ringed topoi: a natural transformation `f_* ⟶ g_*` of the underlying
direct-image functors commuting with the two maps from the target structure sheaf.
declarations.statement: structure TwoMorphismOfRingedTopoi (f g : RingedToposHom X Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IC for the canonical morphism of ringed topoi.** A 2-morphism between two
morphisms of ringed topoi `f, g : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` in the sense of Stacks 01D3
part (2): a transformation `t : f_* ⟶ g_*` of the underlying direct image functors — which is
exactly a `TwoMorphismOfTopoi` of the underlying morphisms of topoi — whose value at the
structure sheaf of the source carries the structure map of `f` to the structure map of `g`.
declarations.statement: structure TwoMorphism (f g : RingedToposHom A B)
declarations.comment:
2-morphisms of the canonical two-field morphisms of ringed topoi of 01D3 part (2),
  which are the ones that compose

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.sliceEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE**, the equivalence with the slice topos: sheaves on the site of elements of `F`
are the same thing as sheaves on `C` over `F`. This is the sheaf-level restriction of the
canonical equivalence of Tag 0791, taken from
`CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.exists_sheafEquivalence_costructuredArrow_yoneda`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sliceEquivalence (X : RingedTopos.{u}) (F : X.Topos) :
    (localizedRingedTopos X F).Topos ≌ Over F

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.shriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE**, part (3): the lower shriek of the localization morphism on sheaves of sets is
the forgetful functor of the slice. Concretely, `Sh(C/F) ≌ Sh(C)/F` followed by `Over.forget F` is
left adjoint to the inverse image of the localization morphism, which is restriction along the
projection from the site of elements.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def shriekAdjunction (X : RingedTopos.{u}) (F : X.Topos) :
    (sliceEquivalence X F).functor ⋙ Over.forget F ⊣
      (localizationToposMorphism X F).inverseImage

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.sliceEquivalenceFibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE**: the equivalence with the slice topos is the canonical fibre construction and
not merely an abstract equivalence. On underlying presheaves, the inverse of `sliceEquivalence`
sends an object `φ : A ⟶ F` of `Sh(C)/F` to the presheaf `(U, t) ↦ {x ∈ A(U) | φ(x) = t}` on the
site of elements of `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sliceEquivalenceFibers (X : RingedTopos.{u}) (F : X.Topos) :
    (sliceEquivalence X F).inverse ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (elementTopology X F) (Type u) ≅
      Over.post (X := F) (sheafToPresheaf X.J (Type u)) ⋙
        (overEquivPresheafCostructuredArrow F.obj).functor
declarations.comment: canonical identification with the slice topos

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedToposEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE for the small étale site: the small étale topos of an object `U` of the small
étale site of `S` is the localization of the small étale topos of `S` at the sheaf `h_U^#`.**

The three steps of the identification are each proved elsewhere and none of them is rebuilt here.
The small étale site of the scheme of `U` is the slice `(S_étale)/U`, so their topoi agree
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizationSheafEquivalence`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizationEquivalence` read on sheaves); the topos of a slice
site is the slice of the topos at the represented sheaf, which is Stacks 00Y1
(`CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafEquivalence`); and the slice of a topos at a sheaf is the
localization of the ringed topos at that sheaf, which is Stacks 04IE in the generality it is
formalized in (`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationEquivalence`).

What this is *not*: an identification of **ringed** topoi. It identifies the two topoi only.
Upgrading it needs the comparison of the two structure sheaves — the structure sheaf of the
localization is the restriction of `𝒪_S` along the projection from the site of elements of
`h_U^#`, and the structure sheaf of the small étale site of the scheme of `U` is its own sheaf
of global functions — and that comparison is not carried here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizedToposEquivalence :
    Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B U.obj.left.obj U.obj.left.property) (Type u) ≌
      (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos
        (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS))
        ((presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type u)).obj (yoneda.obj U))).Topos
declarations.comment:
for the small étale site: the topos of the small étale site of an object `U` of
  the small étale site of `S` is the topos of the localization of the small étale ringed topos
  of `S` at the sheaf represented by `U`.  This form identifies the two topoi; the identification
  of the two RINGED topoi, structure sheaves included, is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedRingedToposHom`.  It is the composite of three
  equivalences: the equivalence of sites
  between the small étale site of the scheme of `U` and the slice of the small étale site of `S`
  at `U`, read on sheaves; Stacks 00Y1 for the slice site; and the equivalence of the
  localization at a sheaf with the slice of the topos

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openLocalizedToposEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE for an open subscheme: the small étale topos of an open subscheme `V` of `S`
is the localization of the small étale topos of `S` at the sheaf represented by `V`.**

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedToposEquivalence` at the object
`AlgebraicGeometry.opensToBoundedEtale B S hS V` of the small étale site, the open subscheme `V`
regarded as étale over `S` — the composite of that functor with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizationEquivalence`, which is the identification the Zariski
gluing of Stacks 04I7 restricts along.

The sheaf it localizes at is `h_V^#` for `V` read in the small étale site. It is **not** stated
here to agree with `AlgebraicGeometry.openRepresentable'`, which spells the same idea as the
restriction to the small étale site of the presheaf `V` represents in the big étale slice, with
its sections raised by `CategoryTheory.uliftYoneda`; identifying the two is a separate
comparison and is not carried.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def openLocalizedToposEquivalence (V : S.Opens) :
    Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B V.toScheme
        (Scheme.size_lt_of_isOpenImmersion V.ι hS)) (Type u) ≌
      (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos
        (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS))
        ((presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type u)).obj
          (yoneda.obj ((opensToBoundedEtale B S hS).obj V)))).Topos
declarations.comment:
for an open subscheme: the topos of the small étale site of an open subscheme `V`
  of `S` is the topos of the localization of the small étale ringed topos of `S` at the sheaf
  represented by `V` regarded as étale over `S`.  This is the composite of
  `AlgebraicGeometry.opensToBoundedEtale` with the identification of the small étale site of an
  object with the slice over it.  The sheaf localized at is the one `V` represents in the small
  étale site; that it agrees with `AlgebraicGeometry.openRepresentable'` is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openRepresentableSheafIsoYoneda`, and the identification of the
  two RINGED topoi at that spelling is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openLocalizedRingedToposHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openRepresentableLocalizedToposEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE for an open subscheme, at the `AlgebraicGeometry.openRepresentable'`
spelling of the sheaf it localizes at.**

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openLocalizedToposEquivalence` moved along
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openRepresentableSheafIsoYoneda` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizedToposEquivalenceOfIso`, and it is the form in which
Stacks 04IE meets Stacks 04IF: the target of `AlgebraicGeometry.localizedOverOpen` and the
source `AlgebraicGeometry.inverseImageOpenLocalizedToposEquivalence` produces are both
localizations at the sheafification of `AlgebraicGeometry.openRepresentable'`.

Still the two **topoi** only.  The morphism of ringed topoi of Stacks 04IF therefore composes
with these as a morphism of topoi and not yet as one of ringed topoi; what is missing is the
comparison of the two structure sheaves, and this module's implementation notes record what that
needs.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def openRepresentableLocalizedToposEquivalence (V : S.Opens) :
    Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B V.toScheme
        (Scheme.size_lt_of_isOpenImmersion V.ι hS)) (Type u) ≌
      (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos
        (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS))
        ((presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type u)).obj
          (openRepresentable'.{u, u} B S hS V))).Topos
declarations.comment:
