for an open subscheme `V` of `S`, with the sheaf localized at spelled as the
  sheafification of `AlgebraicGeometry.openRepresentable'`: the topos of the small étale site of
  `V` is the topos of the localization of the small étale ringed topos of `S` at that sheaf.
  This is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openLocalizedToposEquivalence` transported along the
  comparison of the two spellings of the represented sheaf; the identification of the two RINGED
  topoi at this spelling, structure sheaves included, is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openLocalizedRingedToposHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openLocalizedRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE for an open subscheme, as a morphism of ringed topoi, at the
`AlgebraicGeometry.openRepresentable'` spelling.** The small étale ringed topos of an open
subscheme `V` of `S` is the localization of the small étale ringed topos of `S` at the sheaf
`V` represents — structure sheaves included, and at the spelling of that sheaf which Stacks
04IF's half of input (1) of the Zariski gluing of Stacks 04I7 localizes at.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedRingedToposHom`, which is Stacks 04IE at the
representable spelling, followed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizedRingedToposHomOfIso` along
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.openRepresentableSheafIso`.  With it, the target of
`AlgebraicGeometry.localizedOverOpen` and the source
`AlgebraicGeometry.inverseImageOpenLocalizedToposEquivalence` produces are both identified with
small étale ringed topoi of opens, as morphisms of ringed topoi, and input (1) is closed.

**Universes.** `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp` elaborates its own nine universe
parameters before its arguments, and the three belonging to the source default to zero if left
to be inferred; they are supplied positionally, in the order
`comp.{Xv, Xu, Xw, Yv, Yu, Yw, Zv, Zu, Zw}` that `pp.universes` reports, with the two
localizations' object universe written `max (u + 1) u`.  Annotating the argument, `let`-binding
it with its type written out, and `by exact` all come too late.
declarations.statement:
def openLocalizedRingedToposHom (V : S.Opens) :
    RingedToposHom (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B V.toScheme
        (Scheme.size_lt_of_isOpenImmersion V.ι hS)))
      (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos.{u, u + 1}
        (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS))
        ((presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type u)).obj
          (openRepresentable'.{u, u} B S hS V)))
declarations.comment:
for an open subscheme `V` of `S`, as a morphism of RINGED topoi and at the
  `AlgebraicGeometry.openRepresentable'` spelling of the sheaf: the small étale ringed topos of
  `V` IS the localization of the small étale ringed topos of `S` at the sheaf `V` represents,
  structure sheaves included.  It is 04IE at the representable spelling
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedRingedToposHom`, whose identification of the topoi is a
  restriction along a functor of sites, which is what makes the structure sheaves comparable)
  followed by the transport of a localization along an isomorphism of sheaves
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizedRingedToposHomOfIso`).  This is the spelling Stacks
  04IF's half of input (1) of the Zariski gluing of 04I7 localizes at, so with it that input is
  closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.elementSiteSheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE for the small étale site, on the topoi, by restriction along a functor of
sites.** The small étale topos of the scheme of `U` is the topos of the localization of the small
étale ringed topos of `S` at the sheaf `U` represents, and the identification is restriction
along `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.toElementSite`.

That it is a restriction, and not merely an equivalence, is the whole point: the three
topos-level forms in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/EtaleCohomology/RecoveringMorphisms/OpenLocalization.lean` factor
through Stacks 00Y1, whose functor is a lower shriek, and so carry no comparison of structure
sheaves; this one does, and the comparison is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.sheafPushforward_localizedRingedTopos_O`.
declarations.comment:
for the small étale site of an object `U` of the small étale site of `S`, with the
  identification given as restriction along a functor of sites: the small étale topos of the
  scheme of `U` is the topos of the localization of the small étale ringed topos of `S` at the
  sheaf `U` represents.  The functor of sites is the equivalence of the small étale site of the
  scheme of `U` with the slice at `U`, followed by the identification of that slice with the site
  of elements of the represented sheaf, which is available because the small étale topology is
  subcanonical; the comparison of the two topologies is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.functorPushforward_mem_elementTopology_iff`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.sheafPushforward_localizedRingedTopos_O
declarations.doc:
**The structure sheaf of the localization, restricted to the small étale site of the scheme
of `U`, is its structure sheaf.** This is the cheap presheaf identity, and it is an *equality*:
the structure sheaf of the localization is the restriction of `𝒪_S` along the projection from
the site of elements, restricting that along `toElementSite` restricts along the composite
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.toElementSite_comp_elementProjection`), the composite is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.postcompose`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.commRingStructurePresheaf` is
`(SmallEtale.toScheme B S hS).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ`, which `postcompose` leaves alone.

This is the comparison that the topos-level forms of Stacks 04IE do not carry, and the reason
this route was taken.
declarations.comment:
the comparison of the two structure sheaves, for the small étale site: the
  structure sheaf of the localization of the small étale ringed topos of `S` at the sheaf an
  object `U` represents, restricted along the functor of sites identifying the small étale site
  of the scheme of `U` with the site of elements, IS the structure sheaf of the small étale site
  of the scheme of `U`.  An equality of sheaves of commutative rings, both being the restriction
  of the structure sheaf of `S` along post-composition with the structure morphism of `U`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE for the small étale site, as a morphism of ringed topoi.** The small étale
ringed topos of the scheme of an object `U` of the small étale site of `S` is the localization of
the small étale ringed topos of `S` at the sheaf `U` represents — structure sheaves included.

The morphism of topoi is the identification of the two topoi, an equivalence; the structure map
is the adjunct of `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedStructureSheafIso`, so it is an
isomorphism, and the two ringed topoi are identified and not merely compared.
declarations.comment:
for the small étale site, as a morphism of RINGED topoi: the small étale ringed
  topos of the scheme of an object `U` of the small étale site of `S` is the localization of the
  small étale ringed topos of `S` at the sheaf `U` represents, structure sheaves included.  The
  morphism of topoi is restriction along the functor of sites identifying the small étale site of
  the scheme of `U` with the site of elements of that sheaf, and the structure map is the adjunct
  of the comparison of the two structure sheaves, which is an isomorphism because the comparison
  is — the two structure sheaves being equal, both the restriction of the structure sheaf of `S`
  along post-composition with the structure morphism of `U`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE, part (4): the direct-sum formula.** The sections over `V` of the
presheaf-level lower shriek of `G` along the localization of `X` at `F` are the direct sum,
over the sections `s` of `F` over `V`, of the sections of `G` at the element `(V, s)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (localizedRingSheaf X F)) (V : X.C) :
    ((PresheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
      (F := elementProjection X F)
      (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj)
      (S := (localizedRingSheaf X F).obj)
      (elementModuleRingPresheafHom X F)).obj G.val).obj (Opposite.op V) ≅
      (∐ extensionByZeroSummands X F G V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso_inv_ι
declarations.doc:
**The direct-sum comparison is the canonical one.** On the summand indexed by a section `s`
of `F` over `V` it is the component, at the element `(V, s)`, of the unit of the adjunction
between the presheaf-level lower shriek and restriction to the site of elements.
declarations.statement:
theorem extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso_inv_ι
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (localizedRingSheaf X F)) (V : X.C)
    (s : F.obj.obj (Opposite.op V)) :
    HEq (Limits.Sigma.ι (extensionByZeroSummands X F G V) s ≫
      (extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso X F G V).inv)
      (((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{u}
        (F := elementProjection X F)
        (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj)
        (S := (localizedRingSheaf X F).obj)
        (elementModuleRingPresheafHom X F)).unit.app G.val).app
          (Opposite.op
            (CostructuredArrow.mk (yonedaEquiv.symm s) : elementSite X F)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.moduleRestriction_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE, part (2): module sections.** At an element `(V, s)` of `F`, the restriction
of a sheaf of `O`-modules to the site of elements has precisely the sections of the original
module over `V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleRestriction_obj (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (V : (elementSite X F)ᵒᵖ) :
    (((SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := elementProjection X F)
      (J := elementTopology X F) (K := X.J)
      (elementModuleRingHom X F)).obj G).val.obj V : Type u) =
      (G.val.obj (Opposite.op ((elementProjection X F).obj V.unop)) : Type u)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationModulePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE, part (2): the inverse image on modules.** Pullback of sheaves of modules
along the localization morphism — the inverse image of Stacks 03D2 followed by extension of
scalars along the structure map — is restriction to the site of elements of `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationModulePullbackIso :
    (localizationMorphism X F).toRingedToposModulesHom.pullbackModules ≅
      SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := elementProjection X F)
        (J := elementTopology X F) (K := X.J) (elementModuleRingHom X F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.extensionByZeroModules_adjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IE, parts (2) and (4): the module adjunction.** On sheaves of modules the lower
shriek of the localization is left adjoint to pullback along the localization morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionByZeroModules_adjunction :
    SheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
      (F := elementProjection X F) (J := elementTopology X F) (K := X.J)
      (elementModuleRingHom X F) ⊣
      (localizationMorphism X F).toRingedToposModulesHom.pullbackModules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The **canonical equivalence between the localization of `X` at `F` and the slice topos**
`Sh(C)/F`: the equivalence supplied by Stacks 0791, whose inverse is the fibre construction
recorded in `localizationEquivalence_fibers`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def localizationEquivalence : (localizedRingedTopos X F).Topos ≌ Over F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationEquivalence_fibers
declarations.doc:
The equivalence with the slice topos is the canonical fibre construction: on underlying
presheaves its inverse sends an object `φ : G ⟶ F` of `Sh(C)/F` to the presheaf
`(U, s) ↦ {t ∈ G(U) | φ(t) = s}` on the site of elements of `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationEquivalence_fibers :
    (localizationEquivalence X F).inverse ⋙
      sheafToPresheaf (elementTopology X F) (Type v) ≅
      Over.post (X := F) (sheafToPresheaf X.J (Type v)) ⋙
        (overEquivPresheafCostructuredArrow F.obj).functor
declarations.comment: canonical identification with the slice topos

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The lower shriek of the localization on sheaves of sets is `Over.forget F`**: read
through the equivalence with the slice topos, the left adjoint of the inverse image of the
localization morphism is the forgetful functor from `Sh(C)/F`.

This is the adjunction of Stacks 0791 for the same equivalence as
`localizationEquivalence_fibers`, which is what pins the comparisons built from it down.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationShriekAdjunction :
    (localizationEquivalence X F).functor ⋙ Over.forget F ⊣
      (localizationMorphism X F).toToposHom.inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of the localization is product with `F`**: read through the
equivalence with the slice topos, the inverse image of the localization morphism is
`toOver F`, which sends a sheaf `G` to the product `G × F` viewed as an object over `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationInverseImageIso :
    (localizationMorphism X F).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
      (localizationEquivalence X F).functor ≅ toOver F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.forget_localizationInverseImageIso_hom_app
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of the inverse image with `toOver F` is the one the lower shriek
prescribes**: the component of `localizationInverseImageIso` at a sheaf `G`, followed by the
projection `G × F ⟶ G`, is the counit of the lower shriek adjunction at `G`.

This is what `localizationInverseImageIso` means, and it is a statement only because the
equivalence and the adjunction come from one package: for an unrelated adjunction the two sides
are morphisms that nothing relates. With `localizationInverseImageIso_eq` it pins the comparison
down completely.
declarations.statement:
theorem forget_localizationInverseImageIso_hom_app (G : X.Topos) :
    (Over.forget F).map ((localizationInverseImageIso X F).hom.app G) ≫
        (forgetAdjToOver F).counit.app G =
      (localizationShriekAdjunction X F).counit.app G
declarations.comment: part (1): the comparison is the one the lower shriek prescribes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationInverseImageIso_eq
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of the inverse image with `toOver F` is unique**: an isomorphism of
`j⁻¹ ⋙ E.functor` with `toOver F` whose components are, after the projection `G × F ⟶ G`, the
counit of the lower shriek adjunction is `localizationInverseImageIso`.

A morphism into `toOver F` over `F` is determined by its composite with that projection, its
composite with the other one being its structure morphism — which is
`CategoryTheory.Iso.ext_of_left_comp_forgetAdjToOver_counit`. Together with
`forget_localizationInverseImageIso_hom_app` this is what makes the comparison of a relocalization
with base change computable: it is enough to exhibit one isomorphism with the right counits.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationInverseImageIso_eq
    (Ψ : (localizationMorphism X F).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
      (localizationEquivalence X F).functor ≅ toOver F)
    (h : ∀ G : X.Topos, (Over.forget F).map (Ψ.hom.app G) ≫ (forgetAdjToOver F).counit.app G =
      (localizationShriekAdjunction X F).counit.app G) :
    Ψ = localizationInverseImageIso X F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.fibreTranspose_shriek_counit
declarations.doc:
**The fibre transpose of the lower shriek counit is the unit of the equivalence.** Both
morphisms `E⁻¹(E(j⁻¹G)) ⟶ j⁻¹G` agree on fibre sections, by
`CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.app_fibers_inv_comp_homEquiv_shriek` and by
`CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.app_fibers_inv_comp_unitInv`; the fibre identification is an
isomorphism, so they are equal.

This is the functor-level form of Stacks 0791's bridge between the fibre description of the
equivalence and the counit of `j_!`, and it is what lets a comparison built from fibres be
compared with the counit.
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreTranspose_shriek_counit (G : X.Topos) :
    fibreTranspose X F ((localizationEquivalence X F).functor.obj
          ((X.localizationMorphism F).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)) G
        ((X.localizationShriekAdjunction F).counit.app G) =
      (localizationEquivalence X F).unitInv.app
        ((X.localizationMorphism F).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)
declarations.comment: part (1): the fibre transpose of the lower shriek counit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos
declarations.doc:
The **localization of the ringed topos `X` at the sheaf `F`**: the site of elements of `F`,
with the restricted topology, and with the restriction of `O` along the projection as structure
sheaf.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev localizedRingedTopos : RingedTopos.{v, max u v, v}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationMorphism
declarations.doc:
The localization as a morphism of ringed topoi: the morphism of topoi above, with the
identification of the inverse image of `O` with the localized structure sheaf as structure
map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationMorphism :
    RingedToposHom (localizedRingedTopos X F) X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.localizedSmallModelMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF for the small étale ringed topoi of schemes.**  Let
`ψ : (S_étale, 𝒪_S) ⟶ (T_étale, 𝒪_T)` be a morphism of the small étale ringed topoi of two
schemes of a big étale site and let `G` be a sheaf of sets on the equi-universe model of the
target.  This is the localized morphism of ringed topoi `ψ'` of Stacks 04IF, from the
localization of the model of the source at the inverse image of `G` to the localization of the
model of the target at `G`.

It is obtained by transport: `ψ` is conjugated by the comparisons of the two small étale ringed
topoi with their equi-universe models — an equivalence of ringed topoi on each side, so nothing
is lost — and Stacks 04IF is applied to the conjugate, whose two ringed topoi are
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.{u, u, u}`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedSmallModelMorphism
    (ψ : RingedToposHom (ringedTopos B S hS) (ringedTopos B T hT))
    (G : (smallModelRingedTopos B T hT).Topos) :
    RingedToposHom
      ((smallModelRingedTopos B S hS).localizedRingedTopos
        (letI : EssentiallySmall.{u} (ringedTopos B S hS).C := essentiallySmall B S hS
         letI : EssentiallySmall.{u} (ringedTopos B T hT).C := essentiallySmall B T hT
         (RingedToposHom.smallModelTransport.{u} ψ).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G))
      ((smallModelRingedTopos B T hT).localizedRingedTopos G)
declarations.comment:
the localized morphism of ringed topoi of a morphism of the small étale ringed
  topoi of two schemes, obtained by transporting the morphism through the `Type u` equi-universe
  models of the two small étale ringed topoi, to which the statement at `RingedTopos.{u, u, u}`
  applies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.localizedOverOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF for the small étale ringed topoi: the restriction of a morphism of ringed
topoi to a pair of opens.**

For schemes `X` and `Y` of a big étale site, a morphism of ringed topoi
`g : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), 𝒪_Y)` and an open subscheme `V` of `Y`, this is the
localization of `g` at the sheaf `h_V^#` represented by `V`: the morphism of ringed topoi
```
  (Sh(X_étale)/g⁻¹h_V^#, (𝒪_X)_{g⁻¹h_V^#}) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale)/h_V^#, (𝒪_Y)_{h_V^#})
```
of Stacks 04IF, whose inverse image is `(H ⟶ h_V^#) ↦ (g⁻¹H ⟶ g⁻¹h_V^#)`.

It carries no hypothesis beyond `g` and `V`: the essential smallness of the small étale site
that Stacks 04IF's localization needs is the instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.essentiallySmall`.  This is the first input of the Zariski gluing
in the proof of Stacks 04I7; the identification of the source with the small étale ringed topos
of the open subscheme of `X` representing `g⁻¹h_V^#` is Stacks 04IE for the étale site and is
not carried here, so this is not yet that gluing's input in full.
declarations.statement:
def localizedOverOpen (X Y : B.Scheme)
    (g : RingedToposHom (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B X.obj X.property))
      (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B Y.obj Y.property)))
    (V : Y.obj.Opens) :
    RingedToposHom
      ((RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B X.obj X.property)).localizedRingedTopos
        (g.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj
          ((presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property) (Type u)).obj
            (openRepresentable'.{u, u} B Y.obj Y.property V))))
      ((RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B Y.obj Y.property)).localizedRingedTopos
        ((presheafToSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property) (Type u)).obj
          (openRepresentable'.{u, u} B Y.obj Y.property V)))
declarations.comment:
the localization of a morphism of ringed topoi at the sheaf represented by an
  open subscheme `V` of the target, for the small étale ringed topoi of two schemes: the
  morphism of ringed topoi from the localization of the source at the inverse image of that
  sheaf to the localization of the target at it, with the structure map of 04IF.  This is the
  instance of 04IF at `RingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u}`, the universes of the small étale ringed
  topos, which is what the Zariski gluing of 04I7 restricts along; it is *not* a morphism
  between the small étale ringed topoi of two open subschemes, that identification being 04IE
  for the étale site, which is not carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localizedSmallModelMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF for the small étale ringed topoi of algebraic spaces.**  Let
`ψ : (X_étale, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y_étale, 𝒪_Y)` be a morphism of the small étale ringed topoi of two
algebraic spaces and let `G` be a sheaf of sets on the equi-universe model of the target.  This is
the localized morphism of ringed topoi `ψ'` of Stacks 04IF, from the localization of the model of
the source at the inverse image of `G` to the localization of the model of the target at `G`.

It is obtained by transport: `ψ` is conjugated by the comparisons of the two small étale ringed
topoi with their equi-universe models — an equivalence of ringed topoi on each side, so nothing is
lost — and the library's Stacks 04IF is applied to the conjugate, whose two ringed topoi are
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.{u, u, u}`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedSmallModelMorphism
    (ψ : RingedToposHom (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X) (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Y))
    (G : (RingedTopos.smallModel.{u} (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1)
      (structureSheaf B S hS Y.1 Y.2)).Topos) :
    RingedToposHom
      ((RingedTopos.smallModel.{u} (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1)
          (structureSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2)).localizedRingedTopos
        ((RingedToposHom.smallModelTransport.{u} ψ).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G))
      ((RingedTopos.smallModel.{u} (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1)
        (structureSheaf B S hS Y.1 Y.2)).localizedRingedTopos G)
declarations.comment:
the localized morphism of ringed topoi of a morphism of the small étale ringed
  topoi of two algebraic spaces, obtained by transporting the morphism through the `Type u`
  equi-universe models of the two small étale ringed topoi, to which the statement at
  `RingedTopos.{u, u, u}` applies

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.localizationCompPushforwardModulesIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF, the clause `f'_* j_F^* = j_G^* f_*` on sheaves of modules.** For a morphism
of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), O) ⟶ (Sh(D), O')`, a sheaf of sets `G` on `D` and `F = f^{-1}G`,
pulling a sheaf of `O`-modules back along the localization `j_F` and pushing it forward along
the localized morphism `f'` is pushing it forward along `f` and pulling back along the
localization `j_G`, naturally in the sheaf of modules.

Both pullbacks are the pullbacks of sheaves of modules of Stacks 03D6 part (2) along the
localization morphisms, which Stacks 04IE part (2)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationModulePullbackIso`) identifies with restriction to
the site of elements; the comparison is therefore
`elementRestrictionCompPushforwardModulesIso` conjugated by those two identifications.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationCompPushforwardModulesIso :
    RingedToposHom.pullbackModules.{uu, uu, uu, uu, uu, uu}
          (X := X.localizedRingedTopos (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)) (Y := X)
          (X.localizationMorphism
            (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)).toRingedToposModulesHom ⋙
        pushforwardModules.{uu, uu, uu, uu, uu, uu}
          (f.localized G).toRingedToposModulesHom ≅
      pushforwardModules.{uu, uu, uu, uu, uu, uu} f.toRingedToposModulesHom ⋙
        RingedToposHom.pullbackModules.{uu, uu, uu, uu, uu, uu}
          (X := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Y := Y)
          (Y.localizationMorphism G).toRingedToposModulesHom
declarations.comment: f'_* j_F^* = j_G^* f_*, on sheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localizedRingedToposSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF**: the square of Stacks 04IF as a 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi.

The comparison of inverse images is `inverseImageCompLocalizationIso`, and the compatibility of
the three structure maps that it needs is `localized_fSharpInverseImage_forget`; the structure
maps of the two localization morphisms are identities on underlying sheaves of sets, so they
drop out of the two composites.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizedRingedToposSquare (G : Y.Topos) :
    TwoIso (A := X.localizedRingedTopos (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)) (B := Y)
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G))
        (Y := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Z := Y)
        (Y.localizationMorphism G) (f.localized G))
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)) (Y := X) (Z := Y)
        f (X.localizationMorphism (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)))
declarations.comment: the square of 04IF as a 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localizedInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF**, the rule characterizing `f'`: read through the identifications of the two
localizations with their slice topoi, the inverse image of `f'` is `Over.post f⁻¹`, that is
```
(f')⁻¹(H ⟶ G) = (f⁻¹H ⟶ f⁻¹G) .
```
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizedInverseImageIso :
    (localizedToposMorphism f G).inverseImage ⋙
        (X.localizationEquivalence (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)).functor ≅
      (Y.localizationEquivalence G).functor ⋙ Over.post f.toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment: the characterization (f')^{-1}(H → G) = (f^{-1}H → F) of f'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.inverseImageCompLocalizationIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF**, commutativity of the square on inverse images: `f⁻¹ ⋙ j_F⁻¹ = j_G⁻¹ ⋙
(f')⁻¹`. Concretely, the inverse image of a sheaf `H` on `D`, localized at `F`, is the inverse
image under `f'` of `H` localized at `G`; this is Stacks 04H1's version of the same square,
transported across the identifications of the localizations with their slice topoi.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageCompLocalizationIso :
    f.toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (X.localizationMorphism (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)).toToposHom.inverseImage ≅
      (Y.localizationMorphism G).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (localizedToposMorphism f G).inverseImage
declarations.comment: commutativity of the square, on inverse images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localizationCompPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF**: `f'_* j_F⁻¹ = j_G⁻¹ f_*`, on sheaves of sets.

This is Stacks 04H1's identity `f'_* ∘ toOver F = toOver G ∘ f_*` for the slice topoi, read
through the identification of the inverse image of each localization morphism with `toOver`
(Stacks 04IE part (1)) and through the two identifications of the localizations with their
slice topoi.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationCompPushforwardIso :
    (X.localizationMorphism (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (localizedToposMorphism f G).pushforward ≅
      f.toToposHom.pushforward ⋙ (Y.localizationMorphism G).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment: f'_* j_F^{-1} = j_G^{-1} f_*, on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localized
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF.** The **localized morphism of ringed topoi**
`(f', (f')♯) : (Sh(C)/F, O_F) ⟶ (Sh(D)/G, O'_G)`, with `F = f⁻¹G`.

Its structure map is the restriction `j_G⁻¹(f♯)` of the structure map of `f`: the localized
structure sheaf `O'_G` is the inverse image `j_G⁻¹O'`, applying `j_G⁻¹` to `f♯ : O' ⟶ f_*O` lands
in `j_G⁻¹f_*O`, and that is `f'_*j_F⁻¹O = f'_*O_F` by
`localizedPushforwardCommRingIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localized :
    RingedToposHom (X.localizedRingedTopos (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G))
      (Y.localizedRingedTopos G)
declarations.comment: the localized morphism of ringed topoi (f', (f')^sharp)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localized_fSharpInverseImage_forget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IF**: the square of Stacks 04IF is a square of *ringed* topoi — the comparison of
inverse images carries the structure map of `f` restricted to the site of elements of `f⁻¹G` to
the structure map of the localized morphism.

This is the compatibility that commutativity of 04IF's square as a square of ringed topoi needs,
in inverse-image form and on underlying sheaves of sets, and with it
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoIso.ofInverseImageIso` turns 04IF's comparison of inverse
images into a 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi.

The proof is the adjointness the source omits. Both structure maps are adjunct to their
direct-image forms (`fSharpInverseImage_forget`), the direct-image form of `(f')♯` is `j_G⁻¹(f♯)`
followed by the comparison of direct images (`localized_fSharp_forget`), and
`inverseImageCompLocalizationIso_hom_app_comp_counit` says that 04IF's two comparisons are mates
of each other; naturality of the comparison of inverse images at `f♯` matches the two up.
declarations.statement:
theorem localized_fSharpInverseImage_forget :
    (f.inverseImageCompLocalizationIso G).hom.app (Y.forgetRing.obj Y.O) ≫
        (X.localizedRingedTopos (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)).forgetRing.map
          (f.localized G).fSharpInverseImage =
      (X.localizationMorphism (f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj G)).toToposHom.inverseImage.map
        (X.forgetRing.map f.fSharpInverseImage)
declarations.comment:
commutativity of the square as a square of ringed topoi: the comparison of
  inverse images is compatible with the structure maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isLocallyRinged_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IG.** A composite of locally ringed morphisms of ringed topoi is locally
ringed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyRinged_comp (g : RingedToposHom Y Z) (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (hg : IsLocallyRinged g) (hf : IsLocallyRinged f) :
    IsLocallyRinged (g.comp f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.isLocallyRingedSite_localizedRingedTopos
declarations.doc: The localization of a locally ringed topos at a sheaf is again a locally ringed topos.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyRingedSite_localizedRingedTopos (X :
  Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedTopos.RingedTopos.{u})
    (F : X.Topos) (hX : IsLocallyRingedSite X) :
    IsLocallyRingedSite (localizedRingedTopos X F)
declarations.comment: (5), first assertion: the localization at a sheaf is again locally ringed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.localizationRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (1), second assertion.** The localization morphism `(j_U, j_U♯)` of a ringed
site at an object `U` is a morphism of locally ringed topoi: its structure map is the identity
on underlying sheaves of sets, and the inverse image of the units subsheaf is the units
subsheaf, so the units square is a square of identities.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged (U : X.C) :
    (X.localizationRingedToposHom U).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment:
(1), second assertion: the localization morphism `(j_U, j_U♯)` is a morphism of
locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.relocalizationRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (2).** The morphism `(j, j♯) : (Sh(C/V), O_V) → (Sh(C/U), O_U)` of Stacks 04IY,
the relocalization of a ringed site along a morphism `f : V ⟶ U` of its underlying category, is
a morphism of locally ringed topoi. As for the localization morphism, the units square is a
square of identities.
declarations.statement:
theorem relocalizationRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged (f : V ⟶ U) :
    (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment: (2): the morphism `(j, j♯)` of 04IY is a morphism of locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationMorphism_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (5), second assertion.** The localization morphism
`(j_F, j_F♯) : (Sh(C)/F, O_F) → (Sh(C), O)` of a ringed topos at a sheaf is a morphism of
locally ringed topoi: the site of elements carries the restriction of the structure sheaf, so
the structure map is the identity on underlying sheaves of sets and the units square is a
square of identities.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationMorphism_isLocallyRinged :
    (localizationMorphism X F).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment:
(5), second assertion: the localization morphism `(j_F, j_F♯)` is a morphism of
locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localized_isLocallyRinged_sites
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of *locally ringed* sites `(f, f^#)` and an
object `V` of the target, the two localized sites `(C/U, O_U)` and `(D/V, O'_V)` are locally
ringed sites and the localized morphism `(f', (f')^#)` of Stacks 04J0 is a locally ringed
morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem localized_isLocallyRinged_sites (hX : RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged X)
    (hY : RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged Y) (hf : f.IsLocallyRinged) :
    RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged (X.over (f.u.obj V)) ∧
      RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged (Y.over V) ∧ (f.localized V).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment: part (3): the localization of a morphism of locally ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (3).** The localized morphism `(f', (f')♯)` of Stacks 04J0 is a morphism of
locally ringed sites as soon as `(f, f♯)` is: its units square is the image under the exact
functor `j_U^{-1}` of the units square of `f`, with the two bottom edges matched by Stacks 03CF's
clause (b).

The units subsheaf of a localization, and its inclusion, are the restrictions of those of the
original ringed site on the nose, so the only comparison entering is clause (b), whose two
components form a square of isomorphisms on the left of the pasting.
declarations.statement:
theorem Hom.localizedRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged (V : Y.C)
    (hf : f.ringedToposHom.IsLocallyRinged) :
    (f.localizedRingedToposHom V).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment: (3): the localized morphism `f'` of 04J0 is a morphism of locally ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.relocalized_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (4).** The relocalized morphism `(f_c, f_c♯)` of Stacks 04J1 is a morphism of
locally ringed topoi as soon as `(f, f♯)` is a morphism of locally ringed sites.

This is Stacks' "follows formally on combining (2) and (3)": `f_c` is by definition the localized
morphism of Stacks 04J0 composed with the relocalization morphism of Stacks 04IY along `c`, the
first locally ringed by clause (3) and the second by clause (2), and a composite of locally ringed
morphisms is locally ringed by Stacks 04IG.
declarations.statement:
theorem Hom.relocalized_isLocallyRinged {U : X.C} {V : Y.C} (c : U ⟶ f.u.obj V)
    (hf : f.ringedToposHom.IsLocallyRinged) :
    (f.relocalized c).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment: (4): the relocalized morphism `f_c` of 04J1 is a morphism of locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localized_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (7).** The localized morphism `(f', (f')♯)` of Stacks 04IF is a morphism of
locally ringed topoi as soon as `(f, f♯)` is: its units square is the image under the exact
functor `j_{f⁻¹G}⁻¹` of the units square of `f`, with the two bottom edges matched by 04IF's
comparison of inverse images.

The units subsheaf of a localization, and its inclusion, are the inverse image of those of the
original ringed topos on the nose, so the only comparison entering is 04IF's, whose two
components form a square of isomorphisms on the left of the pasting.
declarations.statement:
theorem localized_isLocallyRinged (hf : f.IsLocallyRinged) :
    (f.localized G).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment: (7): the localized morphism `f'` of 04IF is a morphism of locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalized_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (8).** The relocalized morphism `(f_s, f_s♯)` of Stacks 04J8 is a morphism of
locally ringed topoi as soon as `(f, f♯)` is.

Stacks 04J8 defines `f_s` as the morphism of 04IF composed with the relocalization morphism of
04J4 along `s`, the first locally ringed by clause (7) and the second by clause (6), and a
composite of locally ringed morphisms is locally ringed by Stacks 04IG.
declarations.comment: (8): the relocalized morphism `f_s` of 04J8 is a morphism of locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (5), first assertion.** The localization `(Sh(C)/F, O_F)` of a locally ringed
topos at a sheaf of sets is again a locally ringed topos: its structure sheaf is the inverse
image of `O` along the localization morphism of topoi, and local ringedness passes to an inverse
image.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedRingedTopos_isLocallyRinged (X : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}) (F : X.Topos)
    (hX : RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged (toRingedSite X)) :
    RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged (toRingedSite (localizedRingedTopos X F))
declarations.comment:
(5), first assertion: the localization `(Sh(C)/F, O_F)` of a locally ringed topos
at a sheaf is again a locally ringed topos, in the categorical spelling of local ringedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.relocalizationMorphism_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (6).** The morphism
`(j, j♯) : (Sh(C)/G, O_G) → (Sh(C)/F, O_F)` of Stacks 04J4, the relocalization of a ringed topos
along a morphism `s : G ⟶ F` of sheaves, is a morphism of locally ringed topoi: its structure
map is the identity on underlying sheaves of sets and the inverse image of the units subsheaf is
the units subsheaf, so the units square is a square of identities.
declarations.statement:
theorem relocalizationMorphism_isLocallyRinged (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (X.relocalizationMorphism s).IsLocallyRinged
declarations.comment: (6): the morphism `(j, j♯)` of 04J4 is a morphism of locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isLocallyRinged_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IH (1), first assertion.** A localization `(C/U, O_U)` of a locally ringed site
is again a locally ringed site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyRinged_over (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w}) (U : X.C)
    (hX : IsLocallyRinged X) : IsLocallyRinged (X.over U)
declarations.comment:
(1), first assertion: the localization `(C/U, O_U)` of a locally ringed site is
again a locally ringed site

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.localizedRingedTopos_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
If the morphism of Tag 05D7 is an isomorphism for `X` and the conditions of Tag 04ES hold, then
both hold for the localization of `X` at a sheaf `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedRingedTopos_isLocallyRinged (F : X.Topos)
    (hX : IsIso (oneIsNeverZero X.J X.O) ∧ Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.Condition1 X.O) :
    IsIso (oneIsNeverZero (LocalizedRingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X F).J
        (LocalizedRingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X F).O) ∧
      Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.Condition1 (LocalizedRingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X F).O
declarations.comment:
(5), first assertion, with condition (1) in the source's sheaf-level spelling of
05D7

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_immersion_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04II.** A quasi-affine scheme locally of finite type over `S` admits,
over `S`, an immersion into a finite-dimensional relative affine space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_immersion_affineSpace
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [X.IsQuasiAffine] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S),
      IsImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S ↘ S) = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeSmallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoMorphism_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IJ.** A 2-morphism from the morphism of small étale ringed topoi induced by a
morphism of schemes to itself is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeSmallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoMorphism_eq_id
    (t : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoMorphism.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u}
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (schemeSpaceMap g))
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (schemeSpaceMap g))) :
    t = AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoMorphism.id
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (schemeSpaceMap g))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeSmallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoMorphismOfRingedTopoi_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IJ** for a 2-morphism over the four-field morphism of ringed topoi: a 2-morphism
from the morphism of small étale ringed topoi induced by a morphism of schemes to itself is the
identity.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.shriekCompSheafFunctorToOverIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IL (2).**  Under the identification of Stacks 00Y1, used in the forward direction
`Φ_U = sheafFunctorToOver J : Sh(C/U) ⥤ Sh(C)/h_U^#`, the relocalization lower shriek `j_!` becomes
postcomposition with `h_f^# : h_V^# ⟶ h_U^#`:
```
  j_!(H --φ--> h_V^#) = (H --φ ≫ h_f^#--> h_U^#) .
```

This is Stacks' proof of (2): the identification sends `G` to `j_{V!}G ⟶ j_{V!}(*) = h_V^#`, so
`j_!G` is sent to `j_{U!}j_!G ⟶ j_{U!}(*) = h_U^#`, and `j_{U!}j_! = j_{V!}` — carried out here at
the presheaf level, where the two structural maps to `h_U` are literally the same
(`relocalizePresheafFunctorToOverIso`), and then transported through sheafification.
declarations.statement:
def shriekCompSheafFunctorToOverIso :
    (Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type v) (J.over V) (J.over U) ⋙ sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ≅
      sheafFunctorToOver (U := V) J ⋙
        Over.map ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))
declarations.comment: (2): under the identification of 00Y1, j_! is postcomposition with h_f^#

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IL (1).**  Under the identification of Stacks 00Y1, used in the forward direction
`Φ_U = sheafFunctorToOver J`, the relocalization inverse image `j^{-1}` becomes base change along
`h_f^# : h_V^# ⟶ h_U^#`:
```
  j^{-1}(H --φ--> h_U^#) = (H ×_{φ, h_U^#, h_f^#} h_V^# ⟶ h_V^#) .
```

This is the proof Stacks suggests: "the reader can now prove (1) by using that `j^{-1}` is the
right adjoint to `j_!` and using that the rule in (1) is the right adjoint to the rule in (2)".
Concretely, `Over.map h_f^# ⋙ Φ_U^{-1}` — which is `j_!` transported, by (2) — is left adjoint both
to `j^{-1} ⋙ Φ_V` and to `Φ_U ⋙ Over.pullback h_f^#`, so the two agree by uniqueness of right
adjoints.
declarations.statement:
def inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso :
    (Over.map f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type v) (J.over V) (J.over U) ⋙
        sheafFunctorToOver (U := V) J ≅
      sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ⋙
        Over.pullback ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))
declarations.comment: (1): under the identification of 00Y1, j^{-1} is base change along h_f^#

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.homEquiv_symm_inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso_inv_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IL (1) is the comparison its counit prescribes.**  Transposing the inverse of the
comparison across the adjunction `Φ_V^{-1} ⋙ j_! ⊣ j^{-1} ⋙ Φ_V` — the one whose left adjoint
Stacks 04IL (2) identifies with `Over.map h_f^# ⋙ Φ_U^{-1}` — returns, up to that identification,
the counit of base change along `h_f^#` read through Stacks 00Y1 at `U`.

Both sides are morphisms out of `Φ_V^{-1}(Φ_U(j^{-1}... ) ×_{h_U^#} h_V^#)`, and the comparison is
an `Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq`, so this is `Adjunction.homEquiv_symm_rightAdjointUniq_hom_app`
for the two adjunctions it is built from, read in the inverse direction by
`Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq_inv_app` and corrected by `Adjunction.ofNatIsoLeft` for the
identification of the two left adjoints.

This is the form in which the comparison enters an equation that has been transposed across a
lower shriek: on one side of such an equation the base change of Stacks 03EH appears, on the
other the relocalization counit, and nothing but this lemma relates them.
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_symm_inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso_inv_app
    (Z : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type v)) :
    (((sheafEquivalence (U := V) J).symm.toAdjunction.comp
          ((Over.map f).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type v) (J.over V) (J.over U))).homEquiv
        ((sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ⋙
          Over.pullback ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))).obj Z) Z).symm
        ((inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso f J).inv.app Z) =
      (inverseCompShriekRelocalizeIso f J).hom.app
          ((sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ⋙
            Over.pullback ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))).obj Z) ≫
        ((Over.mapPullbackAdj ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))).comp
          (sheafEquivalence (U := U) J).symm.toAdjunction).counit.app Z
declarations.comment: (1): the comparison of inverse images is the one its counit prescribes

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.left_inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso_inv_app_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IL (1) carries the counit of `j_{V!} ⊣ j_V^{-1}` to that of
`j_{U!} ⊣ j_U^{-1}`.**  The inverse of Stacks 04IL (1) at a restricted sheaf `j_U^{-1}A`, read
through `Over.forget h_V^#` and followed by Stacks 00Y1's identification at `V` and the counit
`ε^V`, is the first projection of the base change along `h_f^#` followed by Stacks 00Y1's
identification at `U` and the counit `ε^U`.

The two counits belong to two different localizations of the site, and Stacks 04IL (1) is what
relates them.
declarations.statement:
theorem left_inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso_inv_app_comp_counit
    (A : Sheaf J (Type v)) :
    ((inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso f J).inv.app
            ((J.overPullback (Type v) U).obj A)).left ≫
        (sheafFunctorToOverForgetIso (U := V) J).hom.app ((J.overPullback (Type v) V).obj A) ≫
          ((Over.forget V).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type v) (J.over V) J).counit.app A =
      pullback.fst
            ((sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J).obj ((J.overPullback (Type v) U).obj A)).hom
            ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f)) ≫
          (sheafFunctorToOverForgetIso (U := U) J).hom.app ((J.overPullback (Type v) U).obj A) ≫
            ((Over.forget U).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type v) (J.over U) J).counit.app A
declarations.comment: (1) carries the counit of j_{V!} to the counit of j_{U!}

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.relocalize
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IN.** Let `f : E ⟶ D` be a morphism of topoi, `V` an object of `D`, `U` an object
of `E` and `c : U ⟶ f⁻¹V`.  The morphism of topoi `f_c : E/U ⟶ D/V` is the composition
```
  f_c = f' ∘ j_{U/f⁻¹V}
```
of the relocalization morphism `j_{U/f⁻¹V} : E/U ⟶ E/f⁻¹V` of Stacks 03EH with the morphism
`f' : E/f⁻¹V ⟶ D/V` of Stacks 04H1 (03CF); this factorization is Stacks 04IN's second
assertion, and holds here by construction.  Consequently
```
  (f_c)⁻¹ = Over.post f⁻¹ ⋙ Over.pullback c ,
```
see `relocalize_inverseImage_obj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalize {V : D} {U : E} (c : U ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj V)
    {p : Over U ⥤ Over (f.inverseImage.obj V)} (adj : Over.pullback c ⊣ p) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Over U) (Over V)
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi f_c and the factorization f_c = f' ∘ j_{U/u(V)}

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.relocalize_inverseImage_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IN**, the description of `(f_c)⁻¹`: an object `φ : H ⟶ V` of `D/V` is sent to the
fibre product
```
  (f⁻¹H ×_{f⁻¹φ, f⁻¹V, c} U ⟶ U) ,
```
the base change along `c` of `f⁻¹φ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma relocalize_inverseImage_obj {V : D} {U : E} (c : U ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj V)
    {p : Over U ⥤ Over (f.inverseImage.obj V)} (adj : Over.pullback c ⊣ p) (H : Over V) :
    (f.relocalize c adj).inverseImage.obj H =
      Over.mk (pullback.snd (f.inverseImage.map H.hom) c)
declarations.comment: the description of (f_c)^{-1} as a fibre product

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.relocalizeInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IN**, commutativity of the first square: `j_U⁻¹ ∘ f⁻¹ = (f_c)⁻¹ ∘ j_V⁻¹`, where
`j_U⁻¹ = toOver U` and `j_V⁻¹ = toOver V`.

The proof is the one Stacks gives: the square of Stacks 04H1 for `f'`, namely
`f⁻¹ ⋙ toOver (f⁻¹V) ≅ toOver V ⋙ (f')⁻¹`, is whiskered with the base change
`j_{U/f⁻¹V}⁻¹ = Over.pullback c`, and the left-hand side collapses by
`toOverCompPullbackIso`, the identity `j_{U/f⁻¹V}⁻¹ ∘ j_{f⁻¹V}⁻¹ = j_U⁻¹` of Stacks 03EH.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizeInverseImageIso {V : D} {U : E} (c : U ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj V)
    {p : Over U ⥤ Over (f.inverseImage.obj V)} (adj : Over.pullback c ⊣ p) :
    f.inverseImage ⋙ toOver U ≅ toOver V ⋙ (f.relocalize c adj).inverseImage
declarations.comment: commutativity of the first square, on inverse images

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.relocalizeCompPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IN**, commutativity of the last square: given `b : V' ⟶ V`, `a : U' ⟶ U` and
`c' : U' ⟶ f⁻¹V'` with `c' ≫ f⁻¹b = a ≫ c`, the square
```
  E/U' --j_{U'/U}--> E/U
   |f_{c'}            |f_c
  D/V' --j_{V'/V}--> D/V
```
commutes, i.e. `(f_c)⁻¹ ∘ j_{U'/U}⁻¹ = j_{V'/V}⁻¹ ∘ (f_{c'})⁻¹` on inverse images.

This is Stacks' equality
```
  f⁻¹H ×_{f⁻¹V, c} U ×_U U' = f⁻¹(H ×_V V') ×_{f⁻¹V', c'} U' ,
```
obtained here by Beck–Chevalley for `Over.post f⁻¹` (`Over.postPullbackIso`, which uses that
`f⁻¹` is left exact), the composition rule `Over.pullbackComp` for base change, and the
hypothesis `c' ≫ f⁻¹b = a ≫ c`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizeCompPullbackIso {V V' : D} (b : V' ⟶ V) {U U' : E} (a : U' ⟶ U)
    (c : U ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj V) (c' : U' ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj V')
    (hc : c' ≫ f.inverseImage.map b = a ≫ c)
    {p : Over U ⥤ Over (f.inverseImage.obj V)} (adj : Over.pullback c ⊣ p)
    {p' : Over U' ⥤ Over (f.inverseImage.obj V')} (adj' : Over.pullback c' ⊣ p') :
    Over.pullback b ⋙ (f.relocalize c' adj').inverseImage ≅
      (f.relocalize c adj).inverseImage ⋙ Over.pullback a
declarations.comment: commutativity of the last square, on inverse images

declarations.name: localizationMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IP (2).** The *localization morphism* of the topos `Sh(C, J)` at a sheaf `F` is the
morphism of topoi `j_F : Sh(C, J)/F ⟶ Sh(C, J)` of Stacks 04GZ: its inverse image `j_F⁻¹` is
`H ↦ (H × F ⟶ F)`, which is left exact, and its pushforward `j_{F,*}` is the right adjoint of
`j_F⁻¹` given by sections over `F`. Its source is `toposLocalization J F`, the localization of the
topos `Sh(C, J)` at `F` (Stacks 04IP (1)).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationMorphism (F : Sheaf J (Type (max u v))) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (toposLocalization J F) (Sheaf J (Type (max u v)))
declarations.comment: (2): the localization morphism j_F : Sh(C)/F → Sh(C)

declarations.name: toposLocalization
declarations.doc:
The localization of the topos of sheaves `Sh(C, J)` at a sheaf `F` is the
slice (over) category `Sh(C, J) / F`. Objects are pairs `(G, φ)` where `G` is a
sheaf on `C` and `φ : G ⟶ F` is a morphism of sheaves, and morphisms are
commuting triangles over `F`.
declarations.statement: abbrev toposLocalization (F : Sheaf J (Type (max u v)))
declarations.comment: (1): the localization Sh(C)/F of the topos Sh(C) at F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafFunctorToOverCompForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IQ**, on lower shrieks: `j_{F!} ∘ Φ_U = j_{U!}` for `F = h_U^#`.

The lower shriek of the localization morphism `j_F` of Stacks 04GZ is the forgetful functor
`Over.forget F` (`MorphismOfTopoi.overLocalizationShriek`), so this says that the sheaf underlying
`Φ_U G` is `j_{U!}G`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafFunctorToOverCompForgetIso :
    sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ⋙
        Over.forget ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).obj (yoneda.obj U)) ≅
      (Over.forget U).sheafPullback (Type v) (J.over U) J
declarations.comment: j_{F!} = j_{U!} for F = h_U^#: the lower shrieks agree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.overPullbackCompSheafFunctorToOverIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IQ**, on inverse images: `j_F^{-1} = j_U^{-1}` for `F = h_U^#`, i.e.
`j_U^{-1} ⋙ Φ_U ≅ toOver F`.
declarations.comment: j_F^{-1} = j_U^{-1} for F = h_U^#: the inverse images agree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafFunctorToOverCompPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IQ**, on pushforwards: `j_{F,*} = j_{U,*}` for `F = h_U^#`, i.e.
`Φ_U ⋙ j_{F,*} ≅ j_{U,*}`.

Both pushforwards are taken as data, as in `MorphismOfTopoi.overLocalization` and Stacks 04H0 and
04IR: `p` is a right adjoint of `j_F^{-1} = toOver F` and `q` a right adjoint of `j_U^{-1}`.
declarations.comment: j_{F,*} = j_{U,*} for F = h_U^#: the pushforwards agree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.starIteratedSliceForwardIsoPullback
declarations.doc:
Let `s : G ⟶ F` be a morphism of a topos `E` and write `G/F` for the corresponding object of
the slice topos `E/F`.  Localizing `E/F` at `G/F` produces the morphism of topoi whose inverse
image is `Over.star (Over.mk s)`; transporting it along the iterated slice equivalence
`(E/F)/(G/F) ≌ E/G` identifies it with base change along `s`:
```
j⁻¹(H ⟶ F) = (H ×_F G ⟶ G).
```
Together with `map_eq_forget_iteratedSlice` (Stacks 03EH), which identifies the corresponding
lower shriek with `Over.map s`, this is the assertion that `j` is the localization of `E/F` at
`G/F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def starIteratedSliceForwardIsoPullback [HasPullbacks E] :
    Over.star (Over.mk s) ⋙ (Over.mk s).iteratedSliceForward ≅ Over.pullback s
declarations.comment: j = j_{G/F} and j^{-1}(H → F) = (H ×_F G → G)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.pushforwardIsoCompPushforward
declarations.doc:
The pushforwards of the localizations satisfy `j_{G,*} = j_{F,*} ∘ j_*`.

The inverse images satisfy `j_G⁻¹ = j⁻¹ ∘ j_F⁻¹`, which is `Over.starPullbackIsoStar`; passing
to right adjoints turns this into the stated identity between the pushforwards.  The three
pushforwards are given as data, since a general category with pullbacks and binary products
need not have them (in a topos they exist, by Stacks 04GZ).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardIsoCompPushforward [HasPullbacks E] [HasBinaryProducts E]
    {pF : Over F ⥤ E} {pG : Over G ⥤ E} {p : Over G ⥤ Over F}
    (adjF : Over.star F ⊣ pF) (adjG : Over.star G ⊣ pG) (adj : Over.pullback s ⊣ p) :
    pG ≅ p ⋙ pF

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.relocalizeToposInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IS**, on inverse images.  Under the identification of Stacks 00Y1, used in the
forward direction `Φ_U = sheafFunctorToOver J`, the inverse image `j^{-1}` of the relocalization
functor `j = Over.map f` of diagram (04IK) is the inverse image
`Over.star (h_V^#/h_U^#) ⋙ iteratedSliceForward` of the localization of the topos `Sh(C)/h_U^#` at
the object `h_V^#/h_U^#` of Stacks 04IR.

This is Stacks' proof: by Stacks 04IL the left-hand side is base change along `h_f^#`, and by
Stacks 04IR so is the right-hand side.
declarations.statement:
def relocalizeToposInverseImageIso :
    (Over.map f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type v) (J.over V) (J.over U) ⋙
        sheafFunctorToOver (U := V) J ≅
      sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ⋙
        Over.star (Over.mk ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))) ⋙
          (Over.mk ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))).iteratedSliceForward
declarations.comment: the inverse images of the two relocalizations agree, via 00Y1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.relocalizeToposShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IS**, on lower shrieks.  Under the identification of Stacks 00Y1, used in the
forward direction `Φ_U = sheafFunctorToOver J`, the lower shriek `j_!` of the relocalization
functor `j = Over.map f` of diagram (04IK) is the lower shriek
`iteratedSliceBackward ⋙ Over.forget (h_V^#/h_U^#)` of the localization of the topos `Sh(C)/h_U^#`
at the object `h_V^#/h_U^#` of Stacks 04IR.

By Stacks 04IL the left-hand side is postcomposition with `h_f^#`, and by
`Over.iteratedSliceBackward_forget` — the identity underlying Stacks 04IR's description of `j_!` —
so is the right-hand side.
declarations.statement:
def relocalizeToposShriekIso :
    (Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type v) (J.over V) (J.over U) ⋙ sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) J ≅
      sheafFunctorToOver (U := V) J ⋙
        (Over.mk ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f))).iteratedSliceBackward ⋙
          Over.forget (Over.mk ((presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).map (yoneda.map f)))
declarations.comment: the lower shrieks of the two relocalizations agree, via 00Y1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SliceTopos.underlyingIso_hom_app_comp_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IU.**  Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between sites defining a morphism of
sites, with induced morphism of topoi `f : Sh(D) ⟶ Sh(C)`, let `V` be an object of `C` and put
`U = u V`.  Localizing the morphism of sites at `V` (Stacks 03CF) gives
`f' : Sh(D/U) ⟶ Sh(C/V)` with `(f')⁻¹ = u'_s` for `u' = Over.post u`; localizing the morphism of
topoi at the sheaf `h_V^#` (Stacks 04H1) gives `f'' : Sh(D)/f⁻¹h_V^# ⟶ Sh(C)/h_V^#` with
`(f'')⁻¹ = Over.post f⁻¹`.  Through the equivalences `Φ_V, Φ_U` of Stacks 00Y1 and the
identification `f⁻¹h_V^# ≅ h_U^#` of Stacks 04D3 the two agree:
```
  (f')⁻¹ ⋙ Φ_U  ≅  Φ_V ⋙ (f'')⁻¹ ⋙ Over.map (04D3) .
```
Both sides become `j_{U!}(f')⁻¹ ≅ f⁻¹j_{V!}` after `Over.forget h_U^#`, canonically and for free,
by `underlyingIso`; the content of the lemma, stated here, is that that canonical isomorphism
respects the structure maps to `h_U^#`, the one on the right being computed with Stacks 04D3's
identification.  Feeding this equation to `Over.natIsoOfForgetIso` produces the displayed
isomorphism of functors, hence the agreement of the diagram of Stacks 04H1 with the diagram of
Stacks 03CF via the identifications `j_F = j_U`, `j_G = j_V` of Stacks 04IQ.
declarations.statement:
public theorem underlyingIso_hom_app_comp_hom {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u}
    [SmallCategory D] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {u : C ⥤ D}
    [u.IsContinuous J K]
    (hu : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K) (V : C) (H : Sheaf (J.over V) (Type u)) :
    (underlyingIso J K u V).hom.app H ≫
        ((sheafFunctorToOver (U := V) J ⋙
            (hu.morphismOfTopoi.over
                ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).obj (yoneda.obj V))).inverseImage ⋙
            Over.map (sheafPullbackSheafifyYonedaIso u J K V).hom).obj H).hom =
      (((Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback (Type u) (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V)) ⋙
          sheafFunctorToOver (U := u.obj V) K).obj H).hom

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafRelocalize
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IV**, the morphism of topoi `f_s`.  Let `f : Sh(C) ⟶ Sh(D)` be a morphism of
topoi, `G` a sheaf on `D`, `F` a sheaf on `C` and `s : F ⟶ f⁻¹G`.  The morphism of topoi
`f_s : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(D)/G` is
```
  f_s = f' ∘ j_{F/f⁻¹G} ,
```
the composite of the relocalization morphism `j_{F/f⁻¹G}` (Stacks 04IR,
`sheafOverRelocalization s`) with the morphism `f'` of Stacks 04H1 (`f.over G`).  Both
pushforwards are constructed: that of `f'` from `f_*`, that of `j_{F/f⁻¹G}` as the right adjoint
of base change along `s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafRelocalize {G : Sheaf K (Type u')} {F : Sheaf J (Type u)}
    (s : F ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj G) : MorphismOfTopoi (Over F) (Over G)
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi f_s : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(D)/G

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafRelocalize_eq_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IV**, the factorization `f_s = f' ∘ j_{F/f⁻¹G}`, where `f' = f.over G` is the
morphism of Stacks 04H1 and `j_{F/f⁻¹G} = sheafOverRelocalization s` is the relocalization
morphism of Stacks 04IR.

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafRelocalize_inverseImage_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IV**, the description of `(f_s)⁻¹`: an object `φ : H ⟶ G` of `Sh(D)/G` is sent to
```
  (f⁻¹H ×_{f⁻¹φ, f⁻¹G, s} F ⟶ F) .
```
declarations.statement:
lemma sheafRelocalize_inverseImage_obj {G : Sheaf K (Type u')} {F : Sheaf J (Type u)}
    (s : F ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj G) (H : Over G) :
    (f.sheafRelocalize s).inverseImage.obj H =
      Over.mk (pullback.snd (f.inverseImage.map H.hom) s)
declarations.comment: the description of (f_s)⁻¹ as a fibre product

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafRelocalizeInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IV**, commutativity of the first square `j_G ∘ f_s = f ∘ j_F`, on inverse images:
`j_F⁻¹ ∘ f⁻¹ ≅ (f_s)⁻¹ ∘ j_G⁻¹`, where `j_F⁻¹ = toOver F` and `j_G⁻¹ = toOver G`.
declarations.comment: commutativity of the square j_G ∘ f_s = f ∘ j_F, on inverse images

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.sheafRelocalizeCompPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IV**, commutativity of the last square: given `b : G' ⟶ G`, `a : F' ⟶ F` and
`s' : F' ⟶ f⁻¹G'` with `s ∘ a = f⁻¹b ∘ s'`, the square of topoi
```
  Sh(C)/F' --j_{F'/F}--> Sh(C)/F
     |f_{s'}                |f_s
  Sh(D)/G' --j_{G'/G}--> Sh(D)/G
```
commutes: the inverse images of `j_{G'/G} ∘ f_{s'}` and of `f_s ∘ j_{F'/F}` are isomorphic.
This is the formal identity `f⁻¹H ×_{f⁻¹G} F ×_F F' = f⁻¹(H ×_G G') ×_{f⁻¹G'} F'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafRelocalizeCompPullbackIso {G G' : Sheaf K (Type u')} (b : G' ⟶ G)
    {F F' : Sheaf J (Type u)} (a : F' ⟶ F) (s : F ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj G)
    (s' : F' ⟶ f.inverseImage.obj G') (hs : a ≫ s = s' ≫ f.inverseImage.map b) :
    ((sheafOverRelocalization b).comp (f.sheafRelocalize s')).inverseImage ≅
      ((f.sheafRelocalize s).comp (sheafOverRelocalization a)).inverseImage
declarations.comment: commutativity of the last square j_{G'/G} ∘ f_{s'} = f_s ∘ j_{F'/F}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SliceTopos.isPullback_sheafFunctorToOver_overMap_overPost_of_isMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IW.**  Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between sites defining a morphism of
sites (`hu`), with induced morphism of topoi `f : Sh(D) ⟶ Sh(C)`, let `V` be an object of `C`, `U`
an object of `D` and `c : U ⟶ u V`.  Localizing the morphism of sites at `c` (Stacks 04IN) gives
`f_c : Sh(D/U) ⟶ Sh(C/V)` with `(f_c)⁻¹ = (Over.post u)_s ⋙ (Over.map c)^s`; localizing the
morphism of topoi at `s : h_U^# ⟶ f⁻¹h_V^#`, the morphism induced by `c` (Stacks 04IV), gives
`f_s : Sh(D)/h_U^# ⟶ Sh(C)/h_V^#`, characterised by
`(f_s)⁻¹(H ⟶ h_V^#) = (f⁻¹H ×_{f⁻¹h_V^#, s} h_U^# ⟶ h_U^#)`.

Through the equivalences `Φ_V, Φ_U` of Stacks 00Y1 — the identifications `j_G = j_V`, `j_F = j_U`
of Stacks 04IQ — the two agree: for every sheaf `H` on `C/V` the square
```
    Φ_U((f_c)⁻¹H) ---------> f⁻¹(j_{V!}H)
        |                          |
        |                          | f⁻¹(structure map)
        v                          v
      h_U^# ---------s---------> f⁻¹h_V^#
```
is cartesian, the top edge being the canonical comparison map assembled from Stacks 04IL (1)
(Stacks 04IS), which identifies `j_{U/u(V)}⁻¹ ⋙ Φ_U` with `Φ_{u(V)} ⋙ Over.pullback h_c^#`, and
`underlyingIso` (Stacks 04IU, Stacks 03CF), which identifies `j_{u(V)!}(f')⁻¹H` with `f⁻¹j_{V!}H`.
Equivalently: `Φ_U((f_c)⁻¹H) ≅ (f_s)⁻¹(Φ_V H)` in `Sh(D)/h_U^#`, i.e. the diagram of topoi of
Stacks 04IN agrees with the diagram of topoi of Stacks 04IV.

The hypotheses are exactly the source's: `u` continuous and `hu : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K`; no
finite limits in `C` and no exactness of `u` are assumed.  `hu` is used through Stacks 04IU, whose
statement involves the morphism of topoi `f` it defines.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPullback_sheafFunctorToOver_overMap_overPost_of_isMorphismOfSites
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {u : C ⥤ D} [u.IsContinuous J K]
    (hu : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K) (V : C) {U : D} (c : U ⟶ u.obj V)
    (H : Sheaf (J.over V) (Type u)) :
    IsPullback
      (((inverseImageCompSheafFunctorToOverIso c K).hom.app
            (((Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback (Type u) (J.over V)
              (K.over (u.obj V))).obj H)).left ≫
          pullback.fst
              ((sheafFunctorToOver (U := u.obj V) K).obj
                (((Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback (Type u) (J.over V)
                  (K.over (u.obj V))).obj H)).hom
              ((presheafToSheaf K (Type u)).map (yoneda.map c)) ≫
            (underlyingIso J K u V).hom.app H)
      (((sheafFunctorToOver (U := U) K).obj
        (((Over.map c).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) (K.over U) (K.over (u.obj V))).obj
          (((Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback (Type u) (J.over V)
            (K.over (u.obj V))).obj H))).hom)
      ((u.sheafPullback (Type u) J K).map ((sheafFunctorToOver (U := V) J).obj H).hom)
      ((presheafToSheaf K (Type u)).map (yoneda.map c) ≫
        (sheafPullbackSheafifyYonedaIso u J K V).inv)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.moduleRestriction_obj
declarations.doc:
The sections of a restricted sheaf of modules over an object `V ⟶ U` of the localized site
are the sections of the original sheaf over `V`: restriction is reindexing along
`Over.forget U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleRestriction_obj {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{w}} (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R) (U : C) (V : (Over U)ᵒᵖ) :
    ((F.over U).val.presheaf.obj V : Type w) =
      (F.val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op V.unop.left) : Type w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.localizationPullbackIsoRestriction_exists
declarations.doc:
Pullback of sheaves of modules along the localization morphism of ringed topoi at `U` is
isomorphic to restriction to the localized site.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationPullbackIsoRestriction_exists :
    Nonempty ((X.localizationMorphism U).pullbackModules ≅
      SheafOfModules.overFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.relocalizationRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04IY.** The structure map of the relocalization along `f : V ⟶ U`, in
inverse-image form and on sheaves of commutative rings, is the canonical comparison of the
inverse image of `O|_U` with its restriction along `Over.map f`, followed by the change-of-slice
identification of that restriction with `O|_V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relocalizationRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage :
    (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f).fSharpInverseImage =
      (restrictionCommRingIso (X.J.over V) (X.J.over U) (Over.map f) (X.O.over U)).hom ≫
        (X.O.pushforwardOverMapIso f).hom
declarations.comment: structure map of localization at V/U

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.pushforwardTopos_comp_overFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J0, the identity `f'_* j_U^* = j_V^* f_*` on sheaves of modules**, which is also
the underived identity behind Stacks 0D6G: the direct image of a sheaf of modules along a morphism
of ringed sites, restricted to the site localized at an object `V` of the target, is the direct
image along the localized morphism `f.localized V` of the restriction to the localization at
`U = u(V)`. As in the source this is an equality of functors, not merely an isomorphism: the
functor identity `u' ∘ j_V = j_U ∘ u` of Stacks 03CF is strict.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardTopos_comp_overFunctor :
    f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pushforwardTopos ⋙
        SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) V =
      SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) (f.u.obj V) ⋙
        localizedPushforward f V
declarations.comment: (3): the identity `f'_* j_U^* = j_V^* f_*` on sheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localized
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J0.** The localization of a morphism of ringed sites at an object `V` of the
target: the underlying functor is `Over.post u`, a morphism of sites by Stacks 03CF clause (a),
and the structure map is the restriction `j_V^{-1}(f^♯)` of the structure map of `f`.

That this typechecks is the content of the choice: the target of `j_V^{-1}(f^♯)` is
`j_V^{-1}f_*O`, which is `f'_*j_U^{-1}O = f'_*O_U` by the strict identity of Stacks 03CF, so no
comparison isomorphism intervenes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localized :
    RingedSite.Hom (X.over (f.u.obj V)) (Y.over V)
declarations.comment:
(1): the localized morphism of ringed sites, with its canonical structure map
  `(f')♯ = j_V^{-1}(f♯)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
The localized morphism of ringed *topoi* `(f', (f')♯) : (Sh(C/U), O_U) ⟶ (Sh(D/V), O'_V)`,
with `U = u(V)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.localizedRingedToposHom (V : Y.C) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom (ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V)))
      (ringedTopos (Y.over V))
declarations.comment: (1): the localized morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.overPullback_comp_localizedPushforward
declarations.doc:
The identity `f'_* j_U^{-1} = j_V^{-1} f_*`, as a strict equality of functors
`Sh(C) ⥤ Sh(D/V)`. This is Stacks 03CF's clause (d) read on the assembled morphisms of ringed
topoi: the localizations contribute their inverse images and `f`, `f'` their direct images.
declarations.statement:
theorem Hom.overPullback_comp_localizedPushforward (V : Y.C) :
    (X.localizationRingedToposHom (f.u.obj V)).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (f.localizedRingedToposHom V).toToposHom.pushforward =
      f.ringedToposHom.toToposHom.pushforward ⋙
        (Y.localizationRingedToposHom V).toToposHom.inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRingedSquare
declarations.doc:
With `U = u(V)`, the square
```
  (Sh(C/U), O_U)   --j_U-->  (Sh(C), O)
       | f'                     | f
  (Sh(D/V), O'_V)  --j_V-->  (Sh(D), O')
```
commutes, as a square of ringed topoi: the two composites `j_V ∘ f'` and `f ∘ j_U` are
2-isomorphic in the sense of Stacks 04IC, which is what Stacks means by a commutative diagram of
ringed topoi. The 2-isomorphism is an isomorphism of the two direct images (from Stacks 03CF's
clause (b)) carrying the structure map of `j_V ∘ f'` to that of `f ∘ j_U`, where `j_U♯` and `j_V♯`
are the units of `j^{-1} ⊣ j_*` at the structure sheaves and `(f')♯` is the structure map of
`localizedRingedToposHom`. No hypothesis beyond `f` being a morphism of ringed sites is used.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.localizedRingedSquare (V : Y.C) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoIso
      (A := ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V))) (B := ringedTopos Y)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V)))
        (Y := ringedTopos (Y.over V)) (Z := ringedTopos Y)
        (Y.localizationRingedToposHom V) (f.localizedRingedToposHom V))
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V)))
        (Y := ringedTopos X) (Z := ringedTopos Y)
        f.ringedToposHom (X.localizationRingedToposHom (f.u.obj V)))
declarations.comment:
(2): the commutative diagram of ringed topoi `(f, f♯) ∘ (j_U, j_U♯) ≅
  (j_V, j_V♯) ∘ (f', (f')♯)`, as a 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.relocalized
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J1.** The morphism of ringed topoi
`(f_c, f_c♯) : (Sh(C/U), O_U) ⟶ (Sh(D/V), O'_V)` attached to a morphism of ringed sites
`(f, f♯)` and a morphism `c : U ⟶ u(V)` of the source site: the composition of the localized
morphism of Stacks 04J0, from the localization at `u(V)`, with the relocalization morphism of
Stacks 04IY along `c`.

The factorization that Stacks 04J1 asserts is this definition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.relocalized :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom (ringedTopos (X.over U)) (ringedTopos (Y.over V))
declarations.comment:
the morphism `f_c` and its factorization as the morphism of 04J0 after the
  relocalization morphism of 04IY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.relocalizedLocalizationSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J1**, the localization square: the square

```
  (Sh(C/U), O_U)   --j_U-->  (Sh(C), O)
       | f_c                     | f
  (Sh(D/V), O'_V)  --j_V-->  (Sh(D), O')
```

commutes, as a square of ringed topoi.

This is the square of Stacks 04J0 for the localized morphism `f'`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRingedSquare`), pasted with the relocalization
triangle of Stacks 04IY for `c : U ⟶ u(V)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.relocalizedLocalizationSquare :
    TwoIso (A := ringedTopos (X.over U)) (B := ringedTopos Y)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over U))
        (Y := ringedTopos (Y.over V)) (Z := ringedTopos Y)
        (Y.localizationRingedToposHom V) (f.relocalized c))
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over U))
        (Y := ringedTopos X) (Z := ringedTopos Y)
        f.ringedToposHom (X.localizationRingedToposHom U))
declarations.comment:
commutativity of the localization square, pasted from 04IY's triangle and the
  square of 04J0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.relocalizedNaturalitySquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J1**, the last assertion: for `a ≫ c = c' ≫ u(b)` the square

```
  (Sh(C/U'), O_{U'})  --j_{U'/U}-->  (Sh(C/U), O_U)
        | f_{c'}                          | f_c
  (Sh(D/V'), O'_{V'}) --j_{V'/V}-->  (Sh(D/V), O'_V)
```

commutes, as a square of ringed topoi.

Both `f_c` and `f_{c'}` are, by definition, the localized morphism of Stacks 04J0 after a
relocalization of Stacks 04IY. Reassociating, the two relocalizations of the source site compose
by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.relocalizationComp`, and the hypothesis says that the two
composites are the relocalization along one and the same morphism `a ≫ c = c' ≫ u(b)`; what is
left is `Hom.localizedNaturalitySquare`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.relocalizedNaturalitySquare (h : a ≫ c = c' ≫ f.u.map b) :
    TwoIso (A := (X.over U').ringedTopos) (B := (Y.over V).ringedTopos)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp
        (X := (X.over U').ringedTopos) (Y := (Y.over V').ringedTopos)
        (Z := (Y.over V).ringedTopos)
        (Y.relocalizationRingedToposHom b) (f.relocalized c'))
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp
        (X := (X.over U').ringedTopos) (Y := (X.over U).ringedTopos)
        (Z := (Y.over V).ringedTopos)
        (f.relocalized c) (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom a))
declarations.comment: the final assertion: for `b : V' ⟶ V`, `a : U' ⟶ U` and `c'` with `a ≫ c = c' ≫ u(b)`, the induced square of ringed topoi on the slices commutes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos
declarations.doc:
The **localization of the ringed topos `X` at the sheaf `F`**: the site of elements of `F`,
with the restricted topology, and with the restriction of `O` along the projection as structure
sheaf.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev localizedRingedTopos : RingedTopos.{v, max u v, v}
declarations.comment: part (1): the localization of the ringed topos at F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationMorphism
declarations.doc:
The localization as a morphism of ringed topoi: the morphism of topoi above, with the
identification of the inverse image of `O` with the localized structure sheaf as structure
map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationMorphism :
    RingedToposHom (localizedRingedTopos X F) X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.left_representableLocalizationForwardInverseImageIso_hom_app_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J3's comparison of inverse images, read through the lower shriek.** The
comparison of the two inverse images in the direction of the slice topos, read through
`Over.forget` and followed by the lower shriek counit of the localization at `h_U^#`, is Stacks
00Y1's identification of `Φ_U ⋙ Over.forget` with `j_{U!}` followed by the lower shriek counit
of the localization at `U`.

This is the statement that connects the two lower shrieks the comparison of Stacks 04J3 sits
between — that of the slice site `C/U` and that of the localization of the ringed topos at
`h_U^#` — and it is what lets an equation built from one be compared with an equation built
from the other after transposing across `j_{U!}`.

Each of the two factors of `representableLocalizationForwardInverseImageIso` contributes one
step, and each step is already proved: Stacks 04IQ's comparison read through `Over.forget` and
followed by the first projection is Stacks 00Y1's identification followed by the slice-site
counit (`CategoryTheory.OverShriek.left_overPullbackCompSheafFunctorToOverIso_hom_app_comp_fst`);
and Stacks 04IE's comparison carries the projection to the localization counit
(`RingedTopos.forget_localizationInverseImageIso_inv_app`), whose right-hand side is that first
projection.

The step that replaces a factor *inside* the composite is taken by `rw` rather than by an
explicit `congrArg`: a `congrArg` against a hand-written `fun z => z ≫ _` has to have its own
spelling of the composite identified with the goal's, and that identification unfolds the body of
`localizationShriekAdjunction` — the equation is the same, and the proof is five times the
elaborator's budget. `rw` substitutes into the goal's own term, so no such identification
arises.
declarations.statement:
theorem left_representableLocalizationForwardInverseImageIso_hom_app_comp_counit
    (A : Sheaf X.J (Type u)) :
