    ((representableLocalizationForwardInverseImageIso X U).hom.app A).left ≫
        (X.ringedTopos.localizationShriekAdjunction (representableSheaf X U)).counit.app A =
      (CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafFunctorToOverForgetIso X.J).hom.app
          ((X.J.overPullback (Type u) U).obj A) ≫
        ((Over.forget U).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type u) (X.J.over U) X.J).counit.app A
declarations.comment: part (2): the comparison of inverse images, read through the lower shriek

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableLocalizationInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison of the two inverse images**: the inverse image of the
localization at `h_U^#`, read through the identification of the two localized topoi, is the
inverse image of the localization at `U`. This is the previous comparison transported across
the unit of Stacks 00Y1's equivalence, so it is not an arbitrary isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableLocalizationInverseImageIso :
    (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism X.ringedTopos
          (representableSheaf X U)).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (representableLocalizationEquivalence X U).inverse ≅
      (X.localizationCommRingedToposHom U).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment: part (2): canonical comparison of inverse images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.shriek_representableLocalizationInverseImageIso_hom_app_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J3's comparison of inverse images, read through the lower shriek.** Applying
`j_{U!}` to the comparison and following it by the counit of `j_{U!} ⊣ j_U^{-1}` is Stacks 00Y1's
identification of `j_{U!}Phi_U^{-1}` with `Over.forget` followed by the counit of the lower
shriek of the localization at `h_U^#`.

This is the form of Stacks 04J3's comparison that an equation transposed across `j_{U!}`
consumes: on one side of such an equation the lower shriek is the slice site's, on the other it
is the localization's, and nothing but this lemma relates them. It is the comparison *after* the
cancellation of Stacks 00Y1's unit, so it applies to
`representableLocalizationInverseImageIso` itself rather than to the comparison in the slice
direction that it is built from.

The three steps are `shriek_sheafEquivalence_unitInv` for the cancelled unit, the naturality of
`CategoryTheory.OverShriek.inverseCompShriekIso`, and
`left_representableLocalizationForwardInverseImageIso_inv_app_comp_counit` for the comparison in
the slice direction.

The last of those is whiskered on by `CategoryTheory.whisker_eq` with the whiskering morphism left
to unification: written as a `congrArg` against an explicit `fun z => _ ≫ z`, the step alone takes
the whole of the elaborator's budget, because the lambda's spelling of the comparison has to be
identified with the goal's and that unfolds the body of `localizationShriekAdjunction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shriek_representableLocalizationInverseImageIso_hom_app_comp_counit
    (A : Sheaf X.J (Type u)) :
    ((Over.forget U).sheafPullback (Type u) (X.J.over U) X.J).map
          ((representableLocalizationInverseImageIso X U).hom.app A) ≫
        ((Over.forget U).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type u) (X.J.over U) X.J).counit.app A =
      (CategoryTheory.OverShriek.inverseCompShriekIso X.J).hom.app
          ((X.ringedTopos.localizationEquivalence (representableSheaf X U)).functor.obj
            ((X.ringedTopos.localizationMorphism
              (representableSheaf X U)).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj A)) ≫
        (X.ringedTopos.localizationShriekAdjunction (representableSheaf X U)).counit.app A
declarations.comment:
part (2): the comparison of inverse images after the unit cancellation, read
  through the lower shriek

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableLocalizationStructureSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison of the two structure sheaves.** Read through the identification
of the two localized topoi, the structure sheaf of the localization at `h_U^#` is the structure
sheaf `O|_U` of the localization at `U`: the inverse image of the former along the
identification is the inverse image of `O` along the composite, which the lift above identifies
with the inverse image of `O` along the localization at `U`, which is `O|_U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableLocalizationStructureSheafIso :
    (inverseImageCommRingFunctor (representableLocalizationToposMorphism X U)).obj
        (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U)).O ≅
      (X.over U).ringedTopos.O

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableLocalizationRingInverseImageIso_existsUnique
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of inverse images lifts uniquely to sheaves of commutative rings.** For
the composite of the localization at `h_U^#` with the identification of the two localized
topoi, and for the localization at `U`, there is exactly one isomorphism of their inverse
images of sheaves of commutative rings whose underlying map of sheaves of sets is the canonical
comparison.
declarations.statement:
theorem representableLocalizationRingInverseImageIso_existsUnique :
    ∃! β : inverseImageCommRingFunctor.{u, u, u, u, u, u}
        ((RingedTopos.localizationMorphism X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U)).comp
          (representableLocalizationRingedMorphism X U)).toToposHom ≅
        inverseImageCommRingFunctor.{u, u, u, u, u, u}
          (X.localizationCommRingedToposHom U).toToposHom,
      ∀ R : Sheaf X.J CommRingCat.{u},
        (sheafCompose (X.J.over U) (forget CommRingCat.{u})).map (β.hom.app R) =
          (representableLocalizationInverseImageIso X U).hom.app
            ((sheafCompose X.J (forget CommRingCat.{u})).obj R)
declarations.comment: part (2): canonical comparison on ring sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableLocalizationMorphism_compare
declarations.doc:
**The two localizations have the same structure map**, under the canonical comparison of
their inverse images of sheaves of commutative rings. This is the last compatibility of Stacks
04J3: the identification of the two localized ringed topoi is compatible with their structure
maps, so it is an identification of localizations and not merely of topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem representableLocalizationMorphism_compare :
    (representableLocalizationRingInverseImageIso X U).inv.app X.O ≫
        ((RingedTopos.localizationMorphism X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U)).comp
          (representableLocalizationRingedMorphism X U)).fSharpInverseImage =
      (X.localizationCommRingedToposHom U).fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment: part (2): compatibility of localization structure maps

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.OverSite.elementPostcomp_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04J4, cocontinuity of postcomposition.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem elementPostcomp_isCocontinuous (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (elementPostcomp s).IsCocontinuous (elementTopology G) (elementTopology F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.OverSite.elementPostcomp_isContinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04J4, continuity of postcomposition.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem elementPostcomp_isContinuous (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (elementPostcomp s).IsContinuous (elementTopology G) (elementTopology F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.elementPostcomp_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4, cocontinuity of postcomposition.** The tag is registered on
`OverSite.elementPostcomp_isCocontinuous`, which states the same thing over a bare site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem elementPostcomp_isCocontinuous (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (elementPostcomp s).IsCocontinuous (elementTopology X G) (elementTopology X F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.elementPostcomp_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4, continuity of postcomposition.** The tag is registered on
`OverSite.elementPostcomp_isContinuous`, which states the same thing over a bare site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem elementPostcomp_isContinuous (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (elementPostcomp s).IsContinuous (elementTopology X G) (elementTopology X F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, left exactness of relocalization: restriction of sheaves along a
continuous functor of sites is left exact. For the relocalization of a topos at a morphism of
sheaves `G ⟶ F` the continuous functor is postcomposition with that morphism on the sites of
elements, and this is the left exactness that makes the relocalization a morphism of topoi.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance preservesFiniteLimits_sheafPushforwardContinuous [HasFiniteLimits A] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.relocalizationToposMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, the geometric morphism of the relocalization. A morphism of sheaves
`s : G ⟶ F` postcomposes sections, giving a functor between the sites of elements which is
continuous and cocontinuous and whose restriction functor is left exact; those three facts are
exactly the data of a morphism of topoi `Sh(C/G) ⟶ Sh(C/F)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationToposMorphism (s : G ⟶ F) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (localizedRingedTopos X G).Topos (localizedRingedTopos X F).Topos

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.comp_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, the inverse-image half of the relocalization triangle: localizing at `F`
and then relocalizing along `s : G ⟶ F` has the same inverse image as localizing at `G`
directly, on the nose. Postcomposition with `s` leaves the underlying object of the site
unchanged, so the two functors of sites to `C` are equal, and restriction along a composite is
the composite of the restrictions.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_inverseImage (s : G ⟶ F) :
    ((localizationToposMorphism X F).comp (relocalizationToposMorphism s)).inverseImage =
      (localizationToposMorphism X G).inverseImage
declarations.comment: the relocalization triangle of topoi, on inverse images

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.relocalizationRingIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, the identification of the localized structure sheaves: restricting the
structure sheaf of the localization at `F` along postcomposition with `s : G ⟶ F` gives the
structure sheaf of the localization at `G`. Both are the restriction of `O` along a projection
from a site of elements and the two projections agree, so the identification is the identity
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationRingIso (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (relocalizationRingInverseImage s).obj (localizedRingedTopos X F).O ≅
      (localizedRingedTopos X G).O
declarations.comment: identification of the localized structure sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.relocalizationRingAdjunction_homEquiv_symm_fSharp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, the canonical structure-sheaf map: the structure map of the relocalization
morphism, read in its inverse-image form `f⁻¹O_F ⟶ O_G` through the ring-level adjunction, is
the canonical identification of the restriction of `O_F` with `O_G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relocalizationRingAdjunction_homEquiv_symm_fSharp (s : G ⟶ F) :
    ((relocalizationRingAdjunction s).homEquiv _ _).symm (relocalizationFSharp s) =
      (relocalizationRingIso s).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.relocalization_inverseImage_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, the uniqueness half of the identification of the relocalization inverse image
with base change. Fix an identification `eF` of the localization of `X` at `F` with the slice topos
`Sh(C)/F` whose composite with `Over.forget F` is the lower shriek, i.e. is left adjoint to the
inverse image of the localization morphism (the canonical such identification is
`sliceEquivalence`, with `shriekAdjunction`). Then two isomorphisms of a functor `P` with
`eF ⋙ (base change along s)` which agree after whiskering with the inverse image of the
localization at `F` are equal.

`P` is arbitrary; the case of interest is `P = (relocalization inverse image) ⋙ eG`, for an
identification `eG` of the localization at `G` with `Sh(C)/G`. The hypothesis on `eF` is used only
through the faithfulness of the lower shriek.
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the comparison with base change on slice topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.relocalization_inverseImage_unique_of_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, the uniqueness half in the shape of the source's `∃!`: a comparison of the
relocalization inverse image with base change is determined by a compatibility equation with the
localization comparisons. Here `Φ` is the isomorphism against which the compatibility is stated
and `Ψ` is the prescribed value; both are arbitrary, so this covers any choice of the comparison
isomorphisms for the localizations at `F` and at `G`.
declarations.comment: the comparison with base change is pinned down by the localization comparisons

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.relocalizationMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4.** The relocalization morphism of ringed topoi attached to a morphism
`s : G ⟶ F` of sheaves on a ringed topos: the morphism of topoi is restriction along
postcomposition of sections, and the structure map is the canonical identification of the
inverse image of the structure sheaf of the localization at `F` with that of the localization
at `G`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationMorphism (s : G ⟶ F) :
    RingedToposHom (localizedRingedTopos X G) (localizedRingedTopos X F)
declarations.comment: the upper edge `(j, j♯)` of the relocalization triangle

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.relocalizationInverseImageSliceIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4.** The inverse image of the relocalization morphism along a morphism
`a : H ⟶ K` of sheaves of sets, read through Stacks 04IE's identifications of the localization
of `X` at `H` and at `K` with the slice topoi `Sh(C)/H` and `Sh(C)/K`, is base change along
`a`.

This is `relocalizationFibreIso` transported across the two equivalences.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationInverseImageSliceIso (a : H ⟶ K) :
    (X.relocalizationMorphism a).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (localizationEquivalence X H).functor ≅
      (localizationEquivalence X K).functor ⋙ Over.pullback a
declarations.comment: the inverse image of the relocalization is base change on slice topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationInverseImageIso_eq_relocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4: the comparison with base change is the one the localization comparisons
prescribe.** Stacks 04IE identifies the inverse image of the localization at `H` with
`toOver H`; that identification is `localizationInverseImageIso X H`, and this says it is the
comparison with base change along `a`, whiskered with the inverse image of the localization at
`K`, followed by Stacks 04IE at `K` and by the identification
`toOver K ⋙ Over.pullback a ≅ toOver H` of Stacks 03EH.

With `Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedRingedTopos.relocalization_inverseImage_unique` this is the full
`∃!` of the source: uniqueness holds for every choice of the two identifications, and here is the
one solution for the canonical choice. The proof is
`localizationInverseImageIso_eq` — the comparison is determined by its lower shriek counits —
fed with `forget_map_relocalizationInverseImageSliceIso_hom_app` for the relocalization half,
`CategoryTheory.forget_map_toOverCompPullbackIso_hom_app` for the Stacks 03EH half, and
`localizationInverseImageIso`'s own counit description at `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationInverseImageIso_eq_relocalization (a : H ⟶ K) :
    localizationInverseImageIso X H =
      Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (X.localizationMorphism K).toToposHom.inverseImage
          (X.relocalizationInverseImageSliceIso a) ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerRight (localizationInverseImageIso X K) (Over.pullback a) ≪≫
          toOverCompPullbackIso a
declarations.comment:
the comparison with base change is the one the localization comparisons of 04IE
  prescribe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.localizationAtRelocalizationObjectInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of the localization at `G/F`.** Read through the identification of
Stacks 04IE of the localization of `X` at `F` with `Sh(C)/F`, and through the identification of
the slice at `G/F` with `Sh(C)/G`, the inverse image of the localization morphism of
`(Sh(C)/F, O_F)` at the object `G/F` is base change along `s`.

This is Stacks 04IR for the slice topos `Sh(C)/F`: the inverse image of a localization at an
object is the product with that object (`localizationInverseImageIso`), and the product with
`G/F` is base change along `s` (`relocalizationStarIso`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationAtRelocalizationObjectInverseImageIso (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (localizationMorphism (X.localizedRingedTopos F)
            (X.relocalizationObject s)).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        ((localizationEquivalence (X.localizedRingedTopos F)
            (X.relocalizationObject s)).functor ⋙
          (X.relocalizationSliceEquivalence s).functor) ≅
      (localizationEquivalence X F).functor ⋙ Over.pullback s
declarations.comment: the localization at `G/F` has base change along `s` as its inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.relocalizationObjectTriangleInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
The relocalization triangle with the localization at `G/F` as its upper edge, on inverse
images: the composite of the localization of `(Sh(C)/F, O_F)` at the object
`G/F` with the localization morphism `j_F`, read through `relocalizationObjectEquivalence`, is
the localization morphism `j_G`.

The inverse image of `j_F` is the product with `F` and that of `j_G` the product with `G`, both
by Stacks 04IE; the inverse image of the localization at `G/F` is base change along `s`; and the
product with `F` followed by base change along `s` is the product with `G`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationObjectTriangleInverseImageIso (s : G ⟶ F) :
    ((X.localizationMorphism F).comp
          (localizationMorphism (X.localizedRingedTopos F)
            (X.relocalizationObject s))).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (X.relocalizationObjectEquivalence s).functor ≅
      (X.localizationMorphism G).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment:
the triangle whose upper edge is the localization at `G/F` commutes on inverse
  images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.relocalizationObjectTriangle_fSharpInverseImage
declarations.doc:
The relocalization triangle with the localization at `G/F` as its upper edge, on structure
maps: both edges from the localization at `G/F` to `X` have the identity as
their structure map on underlying sheaves of sets, so the triangle commutes as a triangle of
*ringed* topoi and not merely of topoi.

Each of the three localization morphisms in the triangle has the identity as its structure map
on underlying sheaves of sets, and the structure map of a composite is the restriction of the
first factor's followed by the second factor's.
declarations.statement:
theorem relocalizationObjectTriangle_fSharpInverseImage (s : G ⟶ F) :
    ((X.localizedRingedTopos F).localizedRingedTopos
          (X.relocalizationObject s)).forgetRing.map
        ((X.localizationMorphism F).comp (localizationMorphism (X.localizedRingedTopos F)
          (X.relocalizationObject s))).fSharpInverseImage =
      𝟙 (((X.localizedRingedTopos F).localizedRingedTopos
            (X.relocalizationObject s)).forgetRing.obj
          ((X.localizedRingedTopos F).localizedRingedTopos (X.relocalizationObject s)).O) ∧
      (X.localizedRingedTopos G).forgetRing.map (X.localizationMorphism G).fSharpInverseImage =
        𝟙 ((X.localizedRingedTopos G).forgetRing.obj (X.localizedRingedTopos G).O)
declarations.comment: the triangle commutes on structure maps, both of them being the identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.relocalizationObjectInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**The two relocalizations have the same inverse image.** Read through
`relocalizationObjectEquivalence`, the inverse image of the localization of `(Sh(C)/F, O_F)` at
the object `G/F` is the inverse image of the relocalization morphism along `s`.

Both are base change along `s` on slice topoi — the first by
`localizationAtRelocalizationObjectInverseImageIso`, the second by
`relocalizationInverseImageSliceIso` — so the two agree once the equivalence at `G` is
cancelled.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationObjectInverseImageIso (s : G ⟶ F) :
    (localizationMorphism (X.localizedRingedTopos F)
          (X.relocalizationObject s)).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (X.relocalizationObjectEquivalence s).functor ≅
      (X.relocalizationMorphism s).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment: the localization at `G/F` and the relocalization have the same inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.toposRelocalizationTriangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4**, commutativity of the relocalization triangle as a triangle of ringed topoi:
`(j_G, j_G♯)` is `(j_F, j_F♯)` composed with the relocalization `(j, j♯)` along `s`.

The two inverse images are equal on the nose — restriction along postcomposition followed by
restriction along the projection from the site of elements of `F` is restriction along the
projection from the site of elements of `G` — and all three structure maps are identities on
underlying sheaves of sets, so there is nothing left to check.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toposRelocalizationTriangle (W : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}) {H K : W.Topos}
    (a : H ⟶ K) :
    TwoIso (A := W.localizedRingedTopos H) (B := W)
      (W.localizationMorphism H)
      (comp (X := W.localizedRingedTopos H) (Y := W.localizedRingedTopos K) (Z := W)
        (W.localizationMorphism K) (W.relocalizationMorphism a))
declarations.comment: the relocalization triangle commutes as a triangle of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizationCompTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4: the relocalization morphisms of ringed topoi compose.** Relocalizing along
`s : F ⟶ H` after relocalizing along `a : F' ⟶ F` is relocalizing along `a ≫ s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationCompTwoIso (W : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}) {F' F H : W.Topos}
    (a : F' ⟶ F) (s : F ⟶ H) :
    TwoIso (A := W.localizedRingedTopos F') (B := W.localizedRingedTopos H)
      (comp (X := W.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := W.localizedRingedTopos F)
        (Z := W.localizedRingedTopos H) (W.relocalizationMorphism s) (W.relocalizationMorphism a))
      (W.relocalizationMorphism (a ≫ s))
declarations.comment: the relocalization morphisms of ringed topoi compose

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizationSquareTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J4: a commuting square of sheaves gives a commuting square of relocalizations.** For
`a ≫ s = s' ≫ c`, relocalizing along `s'` and then along `c` agrees with relocalizing along `a` and
then along `s`, as morphisms of ringed topoi.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizationSquareTwoIso (W : RingedTopos.{u, u, u})
    {F' F H' H : W.Topos} (a : F' ⟶ F) (s : F ⟶ H) (s' : F' ⟶ H') (c : H' ⟶ H)
    (h : a ≫ s = s' ≫ c) :
    TwoIso (A := W.localizedRingedTopos F') (B := W.localizedRingedTopos H)
      (comp (X := W.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := W.localizedRingedTopos H')
        (Z := W.localizedRingedTopos H) (W.relocalizationMorphism c)
        (W.relocalizationMorphism s'))
      (comp (X := W.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := W.localizedRingedTopos F)
        (Z := W.localizedRingedTopos H) (W.relocalizationMorphism s)
        (W.relocalizationMorphism a))
declarations.comment:
a commuting square of sheaves gives a commuting square of relocalization
  morphisms of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableRelocalizationInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J5**, on inverse images. Read through the identification of Stacks 04J3 of
`Sh(C/U)` with the localization of the ringed topos at `h_U^#`, and through the identification
of the localization at `h_V^#/h_U^#` with `Sh(C/V)`, the inverse image of the localization of
`(Sh(C)/h_U^#, O_{h_U^#})` at the object `h_V^#/h_U^#` is the inverse image of the
relocalization of the ringed site along `f : V ⟶ U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableRelocalizationInverseImageIso {U V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    (X.representableLocalizationEquivalence U).functor ⋙
        (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism
            (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U))
            (representableRelocalizationObject X f)).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
          (representableRelocalizationEquivalence X f).functor ≅
      (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment:
the two relocalizations have the same inverse image, via the identifications
  of 04J3

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableRelocalizationPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J5**, on direct images. Read through the same two identifications, the direct
image of the localization of `(Sh(C)/h_U^#, O_{h_U^#})` at `h_V^#/h_U^#` is the direct image of
the relocalization of the ringed site along `f : V ⟶ U`. The two inverse images agree, so the
two direct images agree by uniqueness of right adjoints.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableRelocalizationPushforwardIso {U V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    ((representableRelocalizationEquivalence X f).inverse ⋙
          (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism
            (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U))
            (representableRelocalizationObject X f)).toToposHom.pushforward) ⋙
        (X.representableLocalizationEquivalence U).inverse ≅
      (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f).toToposHom.pushforward
declarations.comment: the two relocalizations have the same direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableRelocalization_fSharpSet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J5**, on structure maps: the two relocalizations have the same structure map
`j^♯`, both being the identity on underlying sheaves of sets. For the localization of the ringed
topos at `h_V^#/h_U^#` the structure sheaf is the restriction of `O_{h_U^#}` along the
projection from the site of elements, and for the relocalization of the ringed site it is the
restriction of `O|_U` along `Over.map f`; in both cases the structure map is the comparison of
an inverse image with that restriction, which is the identity on sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem representableRelocalization_fSharpSet {U V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    RingedToposHom.fSharpSet
          (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism
            (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U))
            (representableRelocalizationObject X f)) =
        𝟙 ((RingedTopos.localizationMorphism
              (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U))
              (representableRelocalizationObject X f)).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj
            ((RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos
              (representableSheaf X U)).forgetRing.obj
                (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U)).O)) ∧
      RingedToposHom.fSharpSet (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f) =
        𝟙 ((X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj
          ((ringedTopos (X.over U)).forgetRing.obj (X.over U).O))
declarations.comment: the two maps j^sharp agree, both being the identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableRelocalizationTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**The two upper edges agree**, as a 2-isomorphism of morphisms of ringed topoi: the
localization of `(Sh(C)/h_U^#, O_{h_U^#})` at the object `h_V^#/h_U^#`, read through the
identification of the localization at `h_V^#/h_U^#` with `Sh(C/V)`, *is* the relocalization of
the ringed site along `f : V ⟶ U`, read through the identification of Stacks 04J3 at `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableRelocalizationTwoIso :
    TwoIso (A := ringedTopos (X.over V)) (B := representableLocalizedRingedTopos X U)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over V))
        (Y := representableRelocalizedRingedTopos X f)
        (Z := representableLocalizedRingedTopos X U)
        (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism (representableLocalizedRingedTopos X U)
          (representableRelocalizationObject X f))
        (representableRelocalizationRingedMorphism X f))
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over V))
        (Y := ringedTopos (X.over U)) (Z := representableLocalizedRingedTopos X U)
        (representableLocalizationRingedMorphism X U) (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f))
declarations.comment: the diagrams of 04IY and 04J4 agree via the identifications of 04J3, as a 2-isomorphism of morphisms of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableRelocalizationTriangleCompare
declarations.doc:
**The two relocalization triangles agree**: the relocalization triangle of Stacks 04J4 at the
morphism `h_f^# : h_V^# ⟶ h_U^#` of representable sheaves, read through the identifications of
Stacks 04J3 at `U` and the identification of the localization at `h_V^#/h_U^#` with `Sh(C/V)`,
*is* the relocalization triangle of Stacks 04IY along `f : V ⟶ U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def representableRelocalizationTriangleCompare :
    TwoIso (A := ringedTopos (X.over V)) (B := ringedTopos X)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over V))
        (Y := representableLocalizedRingedTopos X U) (Z := ringedTopos X)
        (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U))
        (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over V))
          (Y := representableRelocalizedRingedTopos X f)
          (Z := representableLocalizedRingedTopos X U)
          (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism (representableLocalizedRingedTopos X U)
            (representableRelocalizationObject X f))
          (representableRelocalizationRingedMorphism X f)))
      (X.localizationRingedToposHom V)
declarations.comment: the triangle of 04J4 at a representable is the triangle of 04IY, via the identifications of 04J3

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedComparisonTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J7.** The diagrams of Stacks 04J0 and Stacks 04IF agree, via the identifications of
Stacks 04J3: the square commutes: the composite
`j_V ∘ f'_{04J0}` of the localization of the source at `V` with Stacks 04J0's localized morphism
is 2-isomorphic to the composite `f'_{04IF} ∘ compareMid` of Stacks 04IF's localized morphism
with Stacks 04D3's identification of the two localizations of the source.

The 2-isomorphism is `Hom.localizedRepresentableCompInverseImageIso` on inverse images; what
makes it a 2-isomorphism of morphisms of ringed topoi is `Hom.key`, its compatibility with the
two structure maps.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.localizedComparisonTwoIso :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoIso
      (A := ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V)))
      (B := RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos Y.ringedTopos (representableSheaf Y V))
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp.{u, u, u, u, u, u, u, u, u}
        (X := ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V)))
        (Y := ringedTopos (Y.over V))
        (Z := RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos Y.ringedTopos (representableSheaf Y V))
        (representableLocalizationRingedMorphism Y V)
        (f.localizedRingedToposHom V))
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp.{u, u, u, u, u, u, u, u, u}
        (X := ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V)))
        (Y := RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos
          (f.inverseImageRepresentableSheaf V))
        (Z := RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos Y.ringedTopos (representableSheaf Y V))
        (f.ringedToposHom.localized (representableSheaf Y V))
        (f.compareMid V))
declarations.comment: the diagrams of 04J0 and 04IF agree via the identifications of 04J3, as a 2-isomorphism of morphisms of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRepresentableInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J7**, on inverse images.  Read through the identifications of Stacks 04J3 of
`Sh(D/V)` with the localization of the ringed topos at `h_V^#` and of `Sh(C/U)` with the
localization at `h_U^#`, and through Stacks 04D3's identification of `F = f^{-1}h_V^#` with
`h_U^#`, the inverse image of the morphism of ringed topoi that Stacks 04IF obtains by localizing
at `F` and `G = h_V^#` is the inverse image of the morphism of ringed topoi that Stacks 04J0
obtains by localizing the morphism of ringed sites at `V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.localizedRepresentableInverseImageIso :
    (Y.representableLocalizationEquivalence V).functor ⋙
        (RingedToposHom.localizedToposMorphism f.ringedToposHom
            (representableSheaf Y V)).inverseImage ⋙
          (f.localizedSourceEquivalence V).functor ≅
      (f.localizedRingedToposHom V).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (X.representableLocalizationEquivalence (f.u.obj V)).functor
declarations.comment:
the two localized morphisms have the same inverse image, via the identifications
  of 04J3

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRepresentablePushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J7**, on direct images.  Read through the same identifications, the direct image
of Stacks 04IF's localized morphism is the direct image of Stacks 04J0's localized morphism.  The
two inverse images agree, so the two direct images agree by uniqueness of right adjoints.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.localizedRepresentablePushforwardIso :
    ((f.localizedSourceEquivalence V).inverse ⋙
          (RingedToposHom.localizedToposMorphism f.ringedToposHom
            (representableSheaf Y V)).pushforward) ⋙
        (Y.representableLocalizationEquivalence V).inverse ≅
      (X.representableLocalizationEquivalence (f.u.obj V)).inverse ⋙
        (f.localizedRingedToposHom V).toToposHom.pushforward
declarations.comment: the two localized morphisms have the same direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRepresentable_forgetFSharp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J7**, on structure maps: the two `(f')^♯` are the same formula, each being the
restriction `j^{-1}(f^♯)` of the structure map of `f` along its own localization morphism — along
`j_V` for Stacks 04J0 and along `j_G` for Stacks 04IF — and Stacks 04J3 identifies
`(j_G, j_G^♯)` with `(j_V, j_V^♯)`.

For Stacks 04J0 the restriction is the whole formula, because Stacks 03CF's clause (d) is a
strict equality of functors `f'_*j_U^{-1} = j_V^{-1}f_*`.  For Stacks 04IF, where `G` is an
arbitrary sheaf, that identity is only an isomorphism, and the formula is the restriction followed
by it; the identifications of sheaves of commutative rings that Stacks 04IF's definition inserts
contribute nothing, being the identity on underlying sheaves of sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem Hom.localizedRepresentable_forgetFSharp :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.forgetFSharp (f.localizedRingedToposHom V) =
        (Y.overMorphismOfTopoi V).inverseImage.map
          (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.forgetFSharp f.ringedToposHom) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.forgetFSharp
          (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localized f.ringedToposHom
            (representableSheaf Y V)) =
        (RingedTopos.localizationMorphism Y.ringedTopos
              (representableSheaf Y V)).toToposHom.inverseImage.map
            (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.forgetFSharp f.ringedToposHom) ≫
          (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos Y.ringedTopos
              (representableSheaf Y V)).forgetRing.map
            (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localizedStructureIso f.ringedToposHom
              (representableSheaf Y V)).hom
declarations.comment:
the two maps (f')^sharp agree, each being the restriction j^{-1}(f^sharp) of the
  structure map of f along its own localization morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizedNaturalityInverseImageSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J8**, the naturality square on inverse images:
`(j_{F'/F})⁻¹ ∘ (f_s)⁻¹ ≅ (f_{s'})⁻¹ ∘ (j_{G'/G})⁻¹`.

Along the factorization `f_s = f'_G ∘ j_s` this is the relocalization square
`relocalizationInverseImage_square` for `a ≫ s = s' ≫ f⁻¹b`, whiskered by the inverse image of
`f'_G`, pasted with the comparison `localizedCompRelocalizationIso` of the localized morphism
of Stacks 04IF at `G` with the one at `G'`, whiskered by the inverse image of the relocalization
along `s'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizedNaturalityInverseImageSquare
    (hs : a ≫ s = s' ≫ f.toToposHom.inverseImage.map b) :
    (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := X.localizedRingedTopos F)
        (Z := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (f.relocalized s)
        (X.relocalizationMorphism a)).toToposHom.inverseImage ≅
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := Y.localizedRingedTopos G')
        (Z := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Y.relocalizationMorphism b)
        (f.relocalized s')).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment: the naturality square of the last assertion, on inverse images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizedNaturalityToposSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J8**, the naturality square as a square of *topoi*: the comparison of the two direct
images conjugate to `relocalizedNaturalityInverseImageSquare`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizedNaturalityToposSquare
    (hs : a ≫ s = s' ≫ f.toToposHom.inverseImage.map b) :
    (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := Y.localizedRingedTopos G')
        (Z := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Y.relocalizationMorphism b)
        (f.relocalized s')).toToposHom.pushforward ≅
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := X.localizedRingedTopos F)
        (Z := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (f.relocalized s)
        (X.relocalizationMorphism a)).toToposHom.pushforward
declarations.comment: the naturality square of the last assertion, as a square of topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizedNaturalitySquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J8**, the naturality square of the last assertion as a square of *ringed* topoi:
```
  (j_{G'/G}, …) ∘ (f_{s'}, f_{s'}♯) ≅ (f_s, f_s♯) ∘ (j_{F'/F}, …) .
```
This is the pasting of `relocalizationSquareTwoIso` for `a ≫ s = s' ≫ f⁻¹b` with
`localizedCompRelocalizationRingedSquare` along the factorization `f_s = f'_G ∘ j_s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizedNaturalitySquare
    (hs : a ≫ s = s' ≫ f.toToposHom.inverseImage.map b) :
    TwoIso (A := X.localizedRingedTopos F') (B := Y.localizedRingedTopos G)
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := Y.localizedRingedTopos G')
        (Z := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Y.relocalizationMorphism b) (f.relocalized s'))
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F') (Y := X.localizedRingedTopos F)
        (Z := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (f.relocalized s) (X.relocalizationMorphism a))
declarations.comment: the final assertion: for `b`, `a`, `s'` with the compatibility square, the induced square of ringed topoi on the slices commutes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalized
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J8.** The morphism of ringed topoi
`(f_s, f_s♯) : (Sh(C)/F, O_F) ⟶ (Sh(D)/G, O'_G)` attached to a morphism of ringed topoi
`(f, f♯)`, a sheaf `G` on the target, a sheaf `F` on the source and a morphism
`s : F ⟶ f⁻¹G`: the composition of the localized morphism of Stacks 04IF, from the localization
at `f⁻¹G`, with the relocalization morphism of Stacks 04J4 along `s`.

The factorization that Stacks 04J8 asserts is this definition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalized :
    RingedToposHom (X.localizedRingedTopos F) (Y.localizedRingedTopos G)
declarations.comment:
the morphism (f_s, f_s^sharp), and its factorization as the morphism of 04IF
  after the relocalization morphism of 04J4

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizedInverseImageSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J8**, commutativity of the localization square on inverse images:
`f⁻¹ ⋙ j_F⁻¹ ≅ j_G⁻¹ ⋙ (f_s)⁻¹`.

Since `j_F⁻¹` is `j_{f⁻¹G}⁻¹` followed by the inverse image of the relocalization along `s` on
the nose, this is Stacks 04IF's inverse-image square whiskered by that relocalization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizedInverseImageSquare :
    (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F) (Y := X) (Z := Y) f
        (X.localizationMorphism F)).toToposHom.inverseImage ≅
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F) (Y := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Z := Y)
        (Y.localizationMorphism G) (f.relocalized s)).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment: commutativity of the localization square, on inverse images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizedToposSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J8**, commutativity of the localization square as a square of *topoi*: the
comparison of the two direct images conjugate to `relocalizedInverseImageSquare`.

This is the underlying morphism-of-topoi content of the square; its compatibility with the
structure sheaves is `relocalizedRingedSquare`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizedToposSquare :
    (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F) (Y := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Z := Y)
        (Y.localizationMorphism G) (f.relocalized s)).toToposHom.pushforward ≅
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F) (Y := X) (Z := Y) f
        (X.localizationMorphism F)).toToposHom.pushforward
declarations.comment: commutativity of the localization square, as a square of topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.relocalizedRingedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J8**, commutativity of the localization square as a square of *ringed* topoi.

The structure-map compatibility of Stacks 04IF's own square is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.localized_fSharpInverseImage_forget`: the inverse-image form of
`(f')♯` for the morphism `f'` of Stacks 04IF, read through 04IF's inverse-image square, is the
restriction of the inverse-image form of `f♯` to the site of elements of `f⁻¹G`. It is the one
thing beyond the inverse-image and pushforward squares of Stacks 04IF that commutativity of 04J8's
square as a square of ringed topoi needs; see the implementation notes of this file.

Given it, the square for `f_s` follows with no further geometry: the structure map of the
relocalization along `s` and that of the two localization morphisms are identities on
underlying sheaves of sets, and `j_F⁻¹` is `j_{f⁻¹G}⁻¹` followed by the inverse image of the
relocalization on the nose.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relocalizedRingedSquare :
    TwoIso (A := X.localizedRingedTopos F) (B := Y)
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F) (Y := Y.localizedRingedTopos G) (Z := Y)
          (Y.localizationMorphism G) (f.relocalized s))
      (comp (X := X.localizedRingedTopos F) (Y := X) (Z := Y) f
        (X.localizationMorphism F))
declarations.comment: commutativity of the localization square as a square of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.relocalized_fSharpInverseImage_forget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J9**, on structure maps: the two relocalized morphisms have the same structure
map, each being the structure map of its own localized morphism `f'` restricted along its own
relocalization.

Read in inverse-image form and on underlying sheaves of sets, the structure map of `f_c` is
`j_c^{-1}` applied to the structure map of the morphism of Stacks 04J0, and the structure map of
`f_s` is `j_s^{-1}` applied to the structure map of the morphism of Stacks 04IF; the structure
maps of the two relocalizations themselves are identities and drop out. Stacks 04J7
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.localizedRepresentable_forgetFSharp`) says that the two
structure maps so restricted are the same formula, namely the structure map of `f` restricted
along the localization morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem Hom.relocalized_fSharpInverseImage_forget :
    (ringedTopos (X.over U)).forgetRing.map (f.relocalized c).fSharpInverseImage =
      (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom c).toToposHom.inverseImage.map
        ((ringedTopos (X.over (f.u.obj V))).forgetRing.map
          (f.localizedRingedToposHom V).fSharpInverseImage) ∧
    (RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U)).forgetRing.map
        (f.ringedToposHom.relocalized (f.relocalizationSheafMap c)).fSharpInverseImage =
      (X.ringedTopos.relocalizationMorphismOfTopoi (f.relocalizationSheafMap c)).inverseImage.map
        ((RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos
            (f.ringedToposHom.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj
              (representableSheaf Y V))).forgetRing.map
          (f.ringedToposHom.localized (representableSheaf Y V)).fSharpInverseImage)
declarations.comment:
the relocalized morphism of 04J1 and the relocalized morphism of 04J8 have the
  same structure map: each is the structure map of its own `f'` restricted along its own
  relocalization, the relocalization contributing the identity, so that the assertion reduces
  to the one of 04J7

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.relocalizedCompInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
The relocalized morphism of Stacks 04J1 followed by the identification of Stacks 04J3 at `V`,
and the relocalized morphism of Stacks 04J8 preceded by the identification of Stacks 04J3 at `U`,
have the same inverse image.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Hom.relocalizedCompInverseImageIso :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over U))
        (Y := ringedTopos (Y.over V))
        (Z := RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos Y.ringedTopos (representableSheaf Y V))
        (representableLocalizationRingedMorphism Y V)
        (f.relocalized c)).toToposHom.inverseImage ≅
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp (X := ringedTopos (X.over U))
        (Y := RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos X.ringedTopos (representableSheaf X U))
        (Z := RingedTopos.localizedRingedTopos Y.ringedTopos (representableSheaf Y V))
        (f.ringedToposHom.relocalized (f.relocalizationSheafMap c))
        (representableLocalizationRingedMorphism X U)).toToposHom.inverseImage
declarations.comment:
on inverse images: the relocalized morphism of 04J1 and the relocalized morphism
  of 04J8 have the same inverse image, through the identifications of 04J3 at `U` and at `V`,
  the comparison being pasted from 04J5 and 04J7 on inverse images. The upgrade of this
  comparison to a 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi, and the agreement of the two localization
  squares under it, are not established here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.Hom.relocalizedComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J9.** The commutative diagram of Stacks 04J1 and the commutative diagram of
Stacks 04J8 agree via the identifications of Stacks 04J3: there is a 2-isomorphism
`β : ι_V ∘ f_c ≅ f_s ∘ ι_U` of morphisms of ringed topoi under which the localization square of
Stacks 04J1 *is* the localization square of Stacks 04J8.
declarations.statement: theorem Hom.relocalizedComparison : f.RelocalizedComparisonStatement c
declarations.comment:
the commutative diagrams of 04J1 and of 04J8 agree via the identifications of
  04J3

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.representableRelocalizationSheafMapCompInverseImageIso_hom_app_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04J5's comparison of inverse images is the one Stacks 04J3 prescribes.** The
component of the comparison of the relocalization of the ringed topos along `h_f^#` with the
relocalization of the ringed site along `f`, taken at an object `j_{h_U^#}^{-1}A` and followed by
Stacks 04J3's comparison at `U` restricted along `Over.map f`, is Stacks 04J3's comparison at
`V`.

The two strictness facts the statement uses hold on the nose: the inverse image of the
relocalization of the ringed topos composed with that of the localization at `h_U^#` *is* the
inverse image of the localization at `h_V^#`, because
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.toposRelocalizationTriangle` is built from `Iso.refl` on
inverse images, and `Over.forget V = Over.map f ⋙ Over.forget U`.

Both sides are morphisms into `j_V^{-1}A`, so the equation is equivalent to its transpose across
`j_{V!} ⊣ j_V^{-1}`, which is
`shriek_representableRelocalizationSheafMapCompInverseImageIso_hom_app_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem representableRelocalizationSheafMapCompInverseImageIso_hom_app_comp
    (A : Sheaf X.J (Type u)) :
    (representableRelocalizationSheafMapCompInverseImageIso X f).hom.app
          ((RingedTopos.localizationMorphism X.ringedTopos
            (representableSheaf X U)).toToposHom.inverseImage.obj A) ≫
        (X.relocalizationRingedToposHom f).toToposHom.inverseImage.map
          ((X.representableLocalizationInverseImageIso U).hom.app A) =
      (X.representableLocalizationInverseImageIso V).hom.app A
declarations.comment:
the comparison of 04J5 on inverse images is the one determined by 04J3 at U and
  at V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.IsFlat
declarations.doc: A morphism of ringed topoi is flat when its inverse-image structure map is flat.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFlat {X : RingedTopos.{v, u, w}} {Y : RingedTopos.{v', u', w'}}
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w})]
    [Y.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w'})]
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [Y.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w'} RingCat.{w'})]
    (f : RingedToposHom X Y) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.preservesFiniteLimits_ringedSitePullback_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04JC for a morphism of ringed sites.** If `f` is flat — that is, if `O_C` is flat
as an `f⁻¹O_D`-module — then the pullback `f^* : Mod(O_D) ⥤ Mod(O_C)` of sheaves of modules
preserves finite limits.

This is `Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.pullbackModules_exact_of_isFlatMap` at the morphism
of ringed topoi of `f`. That result is stated for the pullback built over the four-field
morphism of ringed topoi of the modules development, whereas `ringedSitePullback` is built over
the two-field morphism of Stacks 01D3; the two are left adjoints of one and the same direct
image, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackAdjPushforwardModulesViaComparison` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackAdjPushforwardModules`, so they are identified by
uniqueness of left adjoints and left exactness transfers along that isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_ringedSitePullback_of_isFlat
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatMapULift
      f.ringedToposHom.fSharpInverseImage) :
    Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits (ringedSitePullback f)
declarations.comment: left exactness of the flat pullback, for a morphism of ringed sites

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.abelianInverseImage_exact
declarations.doc: The inverse image of a morphism of topoi is exact on ordinary abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianInverseImage_exact :
    exactFunctor (Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{w'}) (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w})
      (abelianInverseImage f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.pullbackModules_exact_of_isFlatMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04JC**, second assertion. Pullback of sheaves of modules along a *flat* morphism
of ringed topoi is exact: it preserves finite limits and finite colimits. The first assertion,
exactness of the inverse image of abelian sheaves, is
`CategoryTheory.Sites.abelianInverseImage_exact`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackModules_exact_of_isFlatMap (f : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom X Y)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatMapULift.{w, u, v} f.fSharpInverseImage) :
    exactFunctor (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
      (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
      (f.toRingedToposModulesHom.pullbackModules)

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.continuousModule_hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04JF.** The category of `R`-modules with continuous
`G`-action has functorial injective embeddings. In particular, taking
`R = ℤ` gives this result for discrete `G`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuousModule_hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings
    (R : Type u) [Ring R]
    (G : Type v) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
    HasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings (ContinuousModule.{u, v, max u v w} R G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ContinuousGSet.ofMulAction
declarations.doc:
A `G`-set, or discrete `G`-set: a set with a left action of `G` which is continuous when the
set is given the discrete topology and `G × X` the product topology.
declarations.statement:
public def ofMulAction (X : Type v) [MulAction G X]
    (h : (Action.ofMulAction G X).IsContinuous) : ContinuousGSet.{u, v} G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ContinuousGSet.homEquiv
declarations.doc:
A morphism of `G`-sets is precisely a `G`-equivariant map of the underlying sets: no
continuity condition is imposed on it.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricPointStalkMap_germ
declarations.doc:
The canonical map takes the germ of `(U, u', σ)` to the germ of
`(U, u' ∘ a, σ)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricPointStalkMap_germ
    (F : (SmallEtale B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (U : (geometricPointFiber B S hS t).Elementsᵒᵖ)
    (σ : F.obj (Opposite.op U.unop.1)) :
    (geometricPointStalkMap B S hS a (Type u)).app F
        ((colimit.ι
          ((Functor.Elements.π (geometricPointFiber B S hS t)).op ⋙ F) U) σ) =
      (colimit.ι
        ((Functor.Elements.π (geometricPointFiber B S hS s)).op ⋙ F)
        ((neighborhoodFunctor B S hS a).op.obj U)) σ
declarations.comment: the displayed rule: the germ of (U, u, t) goes to that of (U, u ∘ Spec σ, t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_etaleGlobalSectionGerm
declarations.doc:
For a geometric point of the spectrum of a field, taking the germ at that point is a bijection
from the global sections of a sheaf of sets on the small étale site onto the elements of its stalk
fixed by the absolute Galois group.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_etaleGlobalSectionGerm
    (F : smallEtaleTopos.{u, max u v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun t : ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F).obj
          (op (SmallEtale.final B (Spec (.of K)) hK)) ↦
        (⟨etaleGlobalSectionGerm.{u, v} B K hK sbar F t,
            fun σ ↦ etaleStalkSmul_etaleGlobalSectionGerm.{u, v} B K hK sbar F σ t⟩ :
          etaleStalkGaloisFixedPoints.{u, v} B K hK sbar F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleGlobalSectionsEquivGaloisFixedPoints
declarations.doc:
The bijection between the global sections of a sheaf of sets on the small étale site of the
spectrum of a field and the Galois-fixed elements of its stalk at a geometric point.
declarations.statement:
def etaleGlobalSectionsEquivGaloisFixedPoints
    (F : smallEtaleTopos.{u, max u v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK) :
    ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F).obj (op (SmallEtale.final B (Spec (.of K)) hK)) ≃
      etaleStalkGaloisFixedPoints.{u, v} B K hK sbar F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleGlobalSectionGerm_map
declarations.doc:
The bijection between global sections and Galois-fixed stalk elements is functorial: a
morphism of sheaves carries the germ of a global section to the germ of its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleGlobalSectionGerm_map
    {F F' : smallEtaleTopos.{u, max u v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK} (φ : F ⟶ F')
    (t : ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F).obj (op (SmallEtale.final B (Spec (.of K)) hK))) :
    etaleGlobalSectionGerm.{u, v} B K hK sbar F'
        (ConcreteCategory.hom (((sheafToPresheaf _ _).map φ).app
          (op (SmallEtale.final B (Spec (.of K)) hK))) t) =
      ConcreteCategory.hom ((etaleStalkFunctor.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar).map φ)
        (etaleGlobalSectionGerm.{u, v} B K hK sbar F t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricPoint.subsingleton_absoluteGaloisGroup_of_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04JN.** An algebraically closed field has trivial absolute Galois
group at every geometric point of its spectrum.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_absoluteGaloisGroup_of_isAlgClosed :
    Subsingleton (absoluteGaloisGroup s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.globalSections_isEquivalence_of_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04JN.** Over an algebraically closed field, taking global sections is
an equivalence from the small étale topos to the category of sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem globalSections_isEquivalence_of_isAlgClosed :
    (Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) (Type (u + 1))).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkIsoPullbackGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04JN.** The alternative description of the stalk functor at a
geometric point `sbar` of `S`: it is the functor sending a sheaf to the global sections of its
pullback along `sbar`.
declarations.statement:
def etaleStalkIsoPullbackGlobalSections (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of s.residueField))) :
    letI : (smallEtaleBaseChange B (⟨s.hom⟩ :
        (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶ (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))).IsContinuous
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
        (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK) :=
      smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B
        (⟨s.hom⟩ : (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶ (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B (⟨s.hom⟩ : (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
            (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1)) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
          (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK) ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK) (Type (u + 1)) ≅
      etaleStalkFunctor.{u, u + 1} B S hS s
declarations.comment: the stalk as global sections of the pullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkIsoPullbackGlobalSections_inv_app_etaleStalkGerm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04JN.** The alternative description of the stalk functor is the
canonical comparison: it carries the germ at `sbar` of a section over a pointed étale
neighbourhood to the section of the pullback obtained by restricting along the corresponding
morphism from the final étale object over `sbar`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleStalkIsoPullbackGlobalSections_inv_app_etaleStalkGerm (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of s.residueField)))
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (V : (geometricPointFiber B S hS s).Elements)
    (a : SmallEtale.final B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK ⟶
      (smallEtaleBaseChange B (⟨s.hom⟩ : (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
        (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))).obj V.1)
    (ha : (SmallEtale.toScheme B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK).map a ≫
      B.inclusion.map (pullback.fst V.1.obj.hom
        (⟨s.hom⟩ : (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
          (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))) = V.2.1)
    (t : F.obj.obj (op V.1)) :
    letI : (smallEtaleBaseChange B (⟨s.hom⟩ :
        (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶ (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))).IsContinuous
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
        (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK) :=
      smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B
        (⟨s.hom⟩ : (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶ (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))
    (Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK)
          (Type (u + 1))
          (SmallEtale.finalIsTerminal B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK)).hom.app
        (((smallEtaleBaseChange B (⟨s.hom⟩ :
            (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
              (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme))).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
              (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
              (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK)).obj F)
        ((etaleStalkIsoPullbackGlobalSections B S hS s hK).inv.app F
          (etaleStalkGerm.{u, u + 1} B S hS s F V t)) =
      pullbackSectionAlong B (⟨s.hom⟩ : (⟨Spec (.of s.residueField), hK⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
          (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme)) F V.1
        (SmallEtale.final B (Spec (.of s.residueField)) hK) a t

together with a left action of `G` on `M` by group homomorphisms which is continuous when `M` is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.abelianEtaleSheafStalkEquivalence
declarations.doc:
For a geometric point of the spectrum of a field, taking stalks is an equivalence from abelian
sheaves on the small étale site to discrete modules over the absolute Galois group at that point,
naturally identified with the abelian-group-valued stalk functor, and the Galois action on a germ
changes the geometric lift of the étale neighbourhood by precomposition.
declarations.statement:
def abelianEtaleSheafStalkEquivalence :
    Σ e : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} ≌
        ContinuousGAddCommGrp.{u, max u v} (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar),
      { α : e.functor ⋙
            ContinuousGAddCommGrp.forget (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) ≅
          abelianEtaleStalkFunctor.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar //
        ∀ (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})
          (σ : GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar),
          letI := GeometricPoint.residueFieldAlgebra sbar
          ∀ (τ : Gal(sbar.residueField /
              (Spec (.of K)).residueField (sbar.hom default)))
            (_hτ : ∀ a : GeometricPoint.separableClosure sbar,
              (σ a : sbar.residueField) = τ (a : sbar.residueField))
            (U : (geometricPointFiber B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar).Elements)
            (q : (geometricPointFiber B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar).obj U.1)
            (_hq : q.1 = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom τ.toRingHom) ≫ U.2.1)
            (t : ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F).obj (op U.1)),
            let V : (geometricPointFiber B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar).Elements := ⟨q⟩
            ConcreteCategory.hom (α.app F).hom
                (ConcreteCategory.hom ((e.functor.obj F).obj.obj.ρ σ).asHom
                  (ConcreteCategory.hom (α.app F).inv
                    (abelianEtaleStalkGerm.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar F U t))) =
              abelianEtaleStalkGerm.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar F V t }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AffineEtale.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the affine étale charts of an algebraic space into all its étale charts is
a special cocontinuous functor; in particular it is a dense subsite inclusion, and so induces an
equivalence between the affine étale topos and the small étale topos.
declarations.statement:
theorem AffineEtale.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous
      (AffineEtale.topology B S hS F)
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS F)
      (AffineEtale.inclusion B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleTopos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04JT.** The category of sheaves of sets on the small étale site of a presheaf
`F` on the big fppf site of `S`; for an algebraic space, its small étale topos.
declarations.statement:
abbrev smallEtaleTopos (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EtaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
An étale neighbourhood of a geometric point of an algebraic space, with a chosen lift from
the same field spectrum as the given geometric point.
declarations.statement:
structure EtaleNeighborhood (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EtaleNeighborhood.Hom
declarations.doc:
A map of étale neighbourhoods over the fixed algebraic space which carries the chosen lift
to the chosen lift.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (U V : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EtaleNeighborhood.exists_common_refinement
declarations.doc: Two étale neighbourhoods of a geometric point have a common refinement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_common_refinement (U V : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x) :
    ∃ W : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x, Nonempty ((W ⟶ U) × (W ⟶ V))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EtaleNeighborhood.exists_equalizing_refinement
declarations.doc:
Two parallel morphisms of étale neighbourhoods of a geometric point are equalized by a
further étale neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equalizing_refinement {U V : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x} (h₁ h₂ : U ⟶ V) :
    ∃ (W : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x) (h : W ⟶ U), h ≫ h₁ = h ≫ h₂

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EtaleNeighborhood.exists_smallEtaleNeighborhood_refinement
declarations.doc:
Every étale neighbourhood of a geometric point is refined by one coming from the small étale
site, i.e. by one in the image of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EtaleNeighborhood.ofSmallEtale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smallEtaleNeighborhood_refinement (U : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x) :
    ∃ V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x, Nonempty ((ofSmallEtale hF x).obj V ⟶ U)
declarations.comment: scheme_refinement, in the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_scheme_refinement
declarations.doc: Every étale neighbourhood of a geometric point admits a refinement by a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_refinement (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    (U : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x) :
    ∃ (U' : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS F hF x),
      ∃ (_f : U' ⟶ U), U'.space.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_lift_to_etaleCovering
declarations.doc:
A covering of an étale neighbourhood `U` of a geometric point `x` of an algebraic space `X`,
taken in the spaces-étale site of `X`, has a member to which `x` lifts; that member, with the
lift, is again an étale neighbourhood of `x`, and the covering arrow is a morphism of étale
neighbourhoods.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_to_etaleCovering (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (U : EtaleNeighborhood B S hS X.1 X.2 x)
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} (etaleSiteObjectOfNeighborhood B S hS X x U))
    (hE : SpacesEtale.IsCovering B S hS X
      ⟨etaleSiteObjectOfNeighborhood B S hS X x U, E⟩) :
    ∃ i : E.I₀,
      ∃ uiBar : ((SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS X).obj (E.X i)).1.obj
        (Opposite.op x.val.siteObject),
      ∃ huiBar : (((SpacesEtale.inclusion B S hS X).obj (E.X i)).hom.hom).app
          (Opposite.op x.val.siteObject) uiBar = x.val.value,
      ∃ φ : etaleNeighborhoodOfSitePoint B S hS X x (E.X i) uiBar huiBar ⟶ U,
        EtaleNeighborhood.Hom.hom φ =
          ((SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS X).map (E.f i)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.yonedaIdentityNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
**A representable algebraic space is its own pointed étale chart.** The identity of
`yoneda.obj X` is an étale chart, and it is a small étale neighbourhood of *every* geometric
point of `yoneda.obj X`: the section defining the point is itself the required lift.
declarations.statement:
abbrev yonedaIdentityNeighborhood (X : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (w : GeometricPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj X)) : SmallEtaleNeighborhood w
declarations.comment: the identity chart of a representable algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalk
declarations.doc:
The stalk of a presheaf on the small étale site at a geometric point,
formed as the colimit of its sections over the small étale neighbourhoods of that point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev stalk {C : Type w} [Category.{v} C] (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    (P : (SmallEtale B S hS F)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C)
    [HasColimit (SmallEtaleNeighborhood.sections (x := x) P)] : C

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkFunctor
declarations.doc: The stalk at a geometric point, as a functor of the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkFunctor (C : Type w) [Category.{v} C] (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    [HasColimitsOfShape (SmallEtaleNeighborhood x)ᵒᵖ C] :
    ((SmallEtale B S hS F)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C) ⥤ C

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkSet
declarations.doc:
The set-valued stalk at a geometric point, formed as the quotient colimit
`CategoryTheory.Functor.ColimitType`, with no smallness assumption on the neighbourhood
category.
declarations.statement:
abbrev stalkSet (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) (P : (SmallEtale B S hS F)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) :
    Type _

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkSetFunctor
declarations.doc: The set-valued stalk at a geometric point, as a functor of the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
def stalkSetFunctor (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) :
    ((SmallEtale B S hS F)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkSpacesEtaleIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04JZ.** The small-site stalk at a geometric point is the colimit of sections
over all étale algebraic-space neighbourhoods of that point, naturally in the presheaf on the
spaces-étale site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkSpacesEtaleIso :
    ((Functor.whiskeringLeft (SmallEtale B S hS X.1)ᵒᵖ (SpacesEtale B S hS X)ᵒᵖ
        (Type w)).obj (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).op ⋙ stalkSetFunctor x) ≅
      spacesStalkSetFunctor x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleSitePoint
declarations.doc:
The point of the small étale site of an algebraic space determined by
a geometric point of it: its fibre functor is the functor of lifts of the geometric point
into the étale scheme charts.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleSitePoint (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) : (SmallEtale.topology B S hS F).Point.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleSitePoint_fiber
declarations.doc:
The fibre functor of the point of the small étale site determined by a geometric point is
the geometric fibre functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleSitePoint_fiber (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (etaleSitePoint B S hS F x hF).fiber = geometricFiber B S hS F x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleSitePointStalkIso
declarations.doc:
The stalk at the point of the small étale site determined by a geometric point is
isomorphic to the geometric stalk, naturally in the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleSitePointStalkIso (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (etaleSitePoint B S hS F x hF).presheafFiber (A := Type (u + 1)) ≅
      stalkSetFunctor x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (1).** The geometric stalk of a presheaf of abelian groups on the
small étale site is left exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteLimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (1).** The geometric stalk of a presheaf of abelian groups on the
small étale site is right exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteColimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkSetMap_toSheafify_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (2).** Sheafification does not change the geometric stalk of a
presheaf of sets: the comparison induced by the unit of sheafification is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkSetMap_toSheafify_isIso (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X)
    (P : (SmallEtale B S hS X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) w)) :
    IsIso ((stalkSetFunctor x).map
      ((SmallEtale.topology B S hS X).toSheafify P))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (3).** The geometric stalk of a sheaf of abelian groups on the small
étale site is left exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteLimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
      (sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} ⋙
        stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (3).** The geometric stalk of a sheaf of abelian groups on the small
étale site is right exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafAbelianStalk_preservesFiniteColimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits
      (sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} ⋙
        stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (4).** The geometric stalk of a presheaf of sets on the small étale
site preserves finite limits.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteLimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
      (stalkSetFunctor x : ((SmallEtale B S hS X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) w))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (4).** The geometric stalk of a presheaf of sets on the small étale
site preserves finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteColimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits
      (stalkSetFunctor x : ((SmallEtale B S hS X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) w))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafSetStalk_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (4).** The geometric stalk of a presheaf of sets on the small étale
site commutes with arbitrary colimits of presheaves.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (4).** The geometric stalk of a sheaf of sets on the small étale site
preserves finite limits.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteLimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
      (sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) (Type w) ⋙ stalkSetFunctor x)
declarations.comment: part (4): sheaves of sets, finite limits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (4).** The geometric stalk of a sheaf of sets on the small étale site
preserves finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafSetStalk_preservesFiniteColimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits
      (sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) (Type (max (u + 1) w)) ⋙
        stalkSetFunctor x)
declarations.comment: part (4): sheaves of sets, finite colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafSetStalk_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K1, part (4).** The geometric stalk of a sheaf of sets on the small étale site
commutes with arbitrary colimits of sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafSetStalk_preservesColimits (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X) :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{max (u + 1) w, max (u + 1) w}
      (sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) (Type (max (u + 1) w)) ⋙
        stalkSetFunctor x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.abelianPullback_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K2.** Pullback of sheaves of abelian groups along a morphism of algebraic
spaces is exact on the small étale sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianPullback_exact :
    exactFunctor
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (abelianPullback B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePullbackRepresentableNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K2.** The inverse image of the small étale sheaf represented by an algebraic
space `V` étale over `Y` is the sheaf represented by the cartesian base change `X ×_Y V`,
naturally in `V`.

An algebraic space étale over `Y` need not be a scheme, so the sheaf it represents on the
small étale site is its sheafified Yoneda presheaf on the spaces-étale site, restricted along
the comparison functor of Stacks 03G1.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallEtalePullbackRepresentableNatIso :
    (yoneda ⋙ presheafToSheaf (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS Y) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
      (comparisonFunctor B S hS Y).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS Y) ⋙
      (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage) ≅
    ((spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor ⋙ yoneda ⋙
      presheafToSheaf (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
      (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInverseImage_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K2.** Pullback of sheaves of sets along a morphism of algebraic spaces is exact
on the small étale sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleInverseImage_exact :
    exactFunctor _ _ (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInverseImageFiberIso
declarations.doc:
The fibre at a geometric point `x` of `X` of the inverse image along the canonical morphism
of small étale topoi of Stacks 03G8 of a sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `Y` is the
fibre of that sheaf at the image point `f ∘ x`, naturally in the sheaf.

It is the right-adjoint transpose of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleSkyscraperIso`.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleInverseImageFiberIso :
    (etaleSitePoint B S hS Y.1 (geometricPointMap f.hom x) Y.2).sheafFiber (A := Type u) ≅
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).toToposHom.inverseImage ⋙
        (etaleSitePoint B S hS X.1 x X.2).sheafFiber (A := Type u)
declarations.comment: part (4), for sheaves of sets at the universe of the structure rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInverseImageStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K2, part (4).** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` and a
