geometric point `x` of `X`, the stalk at `x` of the small étale inverse image of a sheaf on `Y`
is the stalk of that sheaf at the image geometric point `f ∘ x`, naturally in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleInverseImageStalkIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage ⋙
        sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙ stalkSetFunctor x ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
        stalkSetFunctor (geometricPointMap f.hom x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleAbelianInverseImageStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K2, part (4), for abelian sheaves.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces over `S` with representable underlying morphism and a geometric point `x` of `X`, the
stalk at `x` of the inverse image of an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `Y` is the
stalk of that sheaf at the image geometric point `f ∘ x`, naturally in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleAbelianInverseImageStalkIso (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    letI := isContinuous_smallBaseChange B S hS f hf
    (smallBaseChange B S hS f hf).sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
          (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) ⋙
        sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
          stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} x ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
        stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (geometricPointMap f.hom x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_smallEtaleAbelianInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K2, part (1).** The inverse image of abelian sheaves along a morphism of
algebraic spaces with representable underlying morphism is left exact.

Base change of scheme charts is not representably flat, for want of a terminal object on the
small étale site; left exactness is instead inherited from base change of étale algebraic
spaces through the equivalences of Stacks 03G1.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_smallEtaleAbelianInverseImage :
    letI := isContinuous_smallBaseChange B S hS f hf
    PreservesFiniteLimits ((smallBaseChange B S hS f hf).sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.globalSections_isEquivalence_of_geometricPoint
declarations.doc:
Global sections is an equivalence from sheaves of sets on the small étale site of the
algebraic space represented by the field spectrum of a geometric point onto sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem globalSections_isEquivalence_of_geometricPoint (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) :
    (Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B S hS (yoneda.obj x.val.siteObject))
      (Type (u + 1))).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleStalkIsoPullbackGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
The stalk functor at a geometric point `x` of an algebraic space `X` is the inverse image
along `x` — viewed as a morphism of algebraic spaces from the space represented by its field
spectrum, hence as a morphism of small étale topoi — followed by global sections on the source.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleStalkIsoPullbackGlobalSections (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.obj) :
    sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.obj) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙ stalkSetFunctor x ≅
      (smallToposMorphism B S hS
            (ObjectProperty.homMk (fieldMorphism B S hS X.obj x.val) :
              (⟨yoneda.obj x.val.siteObject,
                  isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS x.val.siteObject⟩ :
                AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ X)).inverseImage ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B S hS (yoneda.obj x.val.siteObject))
          (Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the stalk as global sections of the pullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkFunctor_iso_of_liesOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K4.** The stalk functors on the small étale site at two geometric points
lying over the same point of the algebraic space are isomorphic, naturally in the presheaf.
The isomorphism is not canonical: the two points are compared through a common dominating
geometric point.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkFunctor_iso_of_liesOver (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (C : Type w)
    [Category.{v} C] {x : points B S hS F} (p q : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    [HasColimitsOfShape (SmallEtaleNeighborhood p)ᵒᵖ C]
    [HasColimitsOfShape (SmallEtaleNeighborhood q)ᵒᵖ C]
    (hp : p.LiesOver x) (hq : q.LiesOver x) :
    Nonempty (stalkFunctor C p ≅ stalkFunctor C q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.injective_iff_stalkSetMap_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K5.** A map of sheaves of sets on the small étale site of an algebraic space
is injective on sections over every étale chart exactly when it is injective on every
geometric stalk.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_iff_stalkSetMap_injective
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) (Type w)} (a : F ⟶ G) :
    (∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, Function.Injective (a.hom.app (Opposite.op U))) ↔
      ∀ x : GeometricPoint B S hS X, Function.Injective (stalkSetMap x a.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_iff_stalkSetMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K5.** A map of sheaves of sets on the small étale site of an algebraic space
is locally surjective exactly when it is surjective on every geometric stalk.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_iff_stalkSetMap_surjective
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) (Type w)} (a : F ⟶ G) :
    Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective a ↔
      ∀ x : GeometricPoint B S hS X, Function.Surjective (stalkSetMap x a.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_iff_stalk_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K5.** A short complex of sheaves of abelian groups on the small étale site of
an algebraic space is exact exactly when its sequence of geometric stalks is exact at every
geometric point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_stalk_exact
    (T : ShortComplex (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X)
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w})) :
    T.Exact ↔ ∀ x : GeometricPoint B S hS X,
      let Φ := sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X)
        AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} ⋙ stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w} x
      ∀ b : Φ.obj T.X₂,
        ((Φ.map T.g).hom b = 0 ↔ ∃ a : Φ.obj T.X₁, (Φ.map T.f).hom a = b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_geometricPoint_stalkFunctor_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K6.** Every point of the small étale topos of an algebraic space is
represented, at the level of stalk functors, by a geometric point of the space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_geometricPoint_stalkFunctor_iso (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (p : PointOfTopos.{u + 1} (SmallEtale.topology B S hS F)) :
    ∃ x : GeometricPoint B S hS F,
      Nonempty (p.inverseImage ≅
        sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS F) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
          stalkSetFunctor x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_openSubspace_of_subterminalSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K8.** Every subsheaf of the terminal sheaf on the spaces-étale site of an
algebraic space is the sheaf of a unique open subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_openSubspace_of_subterminalSheaf
    (F : Subfunctor (spacesEtaleTerminalSheaf B S hS X))
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X) F.toFunctor) :
    ∃! W : {W : Subfunctor X.1 // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      F = openSubspaceSheaf B S hS X W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.largestOpenZeroSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K9, part (1).** The largest open subspace of the algebraic space underlying an
object `U` of the spaces-étale site of `X` on which a section of an abelian sheaf over `U`
vanishes: the open subspace whose point set is the zero images of the section.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def largestOpenZeroSubspace
    (F : Sheaf (topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    {W : Subfunctor (underlying B S hS X U).1 // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.largestOpenZeroSubspace_restrict_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K9, part (2).** A section restricts to zero on an object of the spaces-étale
site over `U` exactly when the image of the points of that object lies in the largest open
zero subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem largestOpenZeroSubspace_restrict_iff
    (F : Sheaf (topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U))
    (V : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (f : V ⟶ U) :
    F.obj.map f.op σ = 0 ↔
      ImageInOpen B S hS X
        (openPoints B S hS X U (largestOpenZeroSubspace B S hS X F U σ)) f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.restrict_largestOpenZeroSubspace_eq_zero
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04K9, part (1).** A section vanishes on its largest open zero subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrict_largestOpenZeroSubspace_eq_zero
    (F : Sheaf (topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    F.obj.map (openSubspaceInclusion B S hS X U
      (largestOpenZeroSubspace B S hS X F U σ)).op σ = 0
declarations.comment: part (1): the section vanishes on the open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.largestOpenZeroSubspace_maximal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K9, part (1).** Every open subspace on which a section vanishes is contained in
its largest open zero subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem largestOpenZeroSubspace_maximal
    (F : Sheaf (topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U))
    (W : {W : Subfunctor (underlying B S hS X U).1 // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W})
    (hW : F.obj.map (openSubspaceInclusion B S hS X U W).op σ = 0) :
    W.1 ≤ (largestOpenZeroSubspace B S hS X F U σ).1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.germ_eq_zero_iff_mem_largestOpenZeroSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K9, part (3).** The germ of a section at a geometric point of the algebraic
space underlying an object `U` of the spaces-étale site of `X` vanishes in the spaces-étale
stalk at the image of that point in `X` exactly when the point lies in the largest open zero
subspace of the section.

The colimit defining the stalk is filtered, so the germ vanishes exactly when the section
already vanishes on some étale neighbourhood refining `U`; one direction is then the
restriction criterion applied to such a refinement, and the other is the restriction
criterion applied to the largest open zero subspace itself, which the field-valued point
factors through by Tag 03IE.
declarations.statement:
theorem germ_eq_zero_iff_mem_largestOpenZeroSubspace
    (F : Sheaf (topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U))
    (p : GeometricPoint B S hS (underlying B S hS X U).1) :
    (spacesNeighborhoodSections (imageGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)
        (F.obj ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{v})).ιColimitType
      (op (neighborhoodOfGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)) σ =
    (spacesNeighborhoodSections (imageGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)
        (F.obj ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{v})).ιColimitType
      (op (neighborhoodOfGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)) (0 : F.obj.obj (op U)) ↔
      p.image ∈ openPoints B S hS X U (largestOpenZeroSubspace B S hS X F U σ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.exists_largestOpenZeroSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04K9.** A section `σ` of an abelian sheaf on the spaces-étale site of an
algebraic space `X`, over an object `U` of that site, has an open subspace `W` of the
algebraic space underlying `U` such that: `σ` vanishes on `W` and `W` contains every open
subspace on which `σ` vanishes; `σ` restricts to zero on an object of the site over `U`
exactly when the image of its points lies in `W`; and the germ of `σ` at a geometric point of
`U` vanishes in the spaces-étale stalk at its image in `X` exactly when that point lies in
`W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_largestOpenZeroSubspace
    (F : Sheaf (topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    ∃ W : {W : Subfunctor (underlying B S hS X U).1 // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      F.obj.map (openSubspaceInclusion B S hS X U W).op σ = 0 ∧
      (∀ W' : {W : Subfunctor (underlying B S hS X U).1 // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
        F.obj.map (openSubspaceInclusion B S hS X U W').op σ = 0 → W'.1 ≤ W.1) ∧
      (∀ (V : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (f : V ⟶ U),
        F.obj.map f.op σ = 0 ↔ ImageInOpen B S hS X (openPoints B S hS X U W) f) ∧
      (∀ p : GeometricPoint B S hS (underlying B S hS X U).1,
        (spacesNeighborhoodSections (imageGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)
            (F.obj ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{v})).ιColimitType
          (op (neighborhoodOfGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)) σ =
        (spacesNeighborhoodSections (imageGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)
            (F.obj ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{v})).ιColimitType
          (op (neighborhoodOfGeometricPoint B S hS X U p)) (0 : F.obj.obj (op U)) ↔
          p.image ∈ openPoints B S hS X U W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSection
declarations.doc:
The *support* of a section of an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of an algebraic
space over an étale chart: the complement of the largest open on which the section restricts
to zero.
declarations.statement:
abbrev supportOfSection (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    Set (points B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf
declarations.doc:
The *support* of an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of an algebraic space: the set
of points at which the stalk at some geometric point lying over that point is nonzero, that is,
at which the set-valued stalk is not a subsingleton.
declarations.statement:
def supportOfSheaf (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}) :
    Set (points B S hS X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_supportOfSection
declarations.doc: The support of a section is closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_supportOfSection
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    IsClosed (supportOfSection B S hS X F U σ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSection_add_subset
declarations.doc: The support of a sum is contained in the union of the supports.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSection_add_subset
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v})
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (σ τ : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    supportOfSection B S hS X F U (σ + τ) ⊆
      supportOfSection B S hS X F U σ ∪ supportOfSection B S hS X F U τ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSection_map_subset
declarations.doc:
A morphism of abelian sheaves cannot enlarge the support of a section: the support of the
image of `σ` under `φ` is contained in the support of `σ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSection_map_subset
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (σ : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    supportOfSection B S hS X G U (φ.hom.app (op U) σ) ⊆
      supportOfSection B S hS X F U σ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_subset_of_mono
declarations.doc:
The support of an abelian subsheaf is contained in the support of the ambient sheaf: a
monomorphism `f : F ⟶ G` of abelian sheaves on the small étale site cannot enlarge the support
of its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_subset_of_mono (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}} (f : F ⟶ G) [Mono f] :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS X F ⊆ supportOfSheaf B S hS X G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_subset_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KB, part (6).** If a map of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of an
algebraic space is injective on sections over every étale chart, then the support of its source
is contained in the support of its target.

Such a map is injective on every geometric stalk by Stacks 04K5, and an injection into a
subsingleton has subsingleton source.

The hypothesis is the sectionwise one, which is what a splitting of sheaves supplies.
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_subset_of_mono` draws the same conclusion from a `Mono`
instance in the sheaf category; neither hypothesis is the other, the passage between them being
full faithfulness of `CategoryTheory.sheafToPresheaf` together with
`CategoryTheory.NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app`, so both forms are stated.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_subset_of_injective (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hφ : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, Function.Injective (φ.hom.app (op U))) :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS X F ⊆ supportOfSheaf B S hS X G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_eq_iUnion_image_supportOfSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KB, part (4).** The support of an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of an
algebraic space is the union, over all étale charts and all sections on them, of the images of
the supports of those sections.

A point of the support carries a geometric point with a nonzero stalk, hence a neighbourhood
and a section whose germ there is nonzero, and that section has the point of the chart in its
support. Conversely a point in the support of a section is the image of a geometric point of
the chart, whose germ there is then nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_eq_iUnion_image_supportOfSection
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}) :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS X F =
      ⋃ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, ⋃ σ : F.obj.obj (op U),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U)) U.obj.hom ''
          supportOfSection B S hS X F U σ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_eq_iUnion_image_supportOfSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KB, part (4).** The support of an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of an
algebraic space is the union, over all étale charts and all sections on them, of the images of
the supports of those sections.

A point of the support carries a geometric point with a nonzero stalk, hence a neighbourhood
and a section whose germ there is nonzero, and that section has the point of the chart in its
support. Conversely a point in the support of a section is the image of a geometric point of
the chart, whose germ there is then nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_eq_iUnion_image_supportOfSection
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}) :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS X F =
      ⋃ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, ⋃ σ : F.obj.obj (op U),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U)) U.obj.hom ''
          supportOfSection B S hS X F U σ
declarations.comment: part (4): the support of a sheaf is the union of the section supports

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_subset_of_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KB.** A surjection of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of an algebraic
space does not enlarge the support: the support of the target is contained in the support of
the source.

A surjection of sheaves is surjective on every geometric stalk by Stacks 04K5, so a point at
which the stalk of the source is a subsingleton is one at which the stalk of the target is one
too.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_subset_of_isLocallySurjective
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X) AddCommGrpCat.{v}} (a : F ⟶ G)
    [Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective a] :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS X G ⊆ supportOfSheaf B S hS X F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_supportOfSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KC.** The support of a sheaf of rings on the small étale site of an algebraic
space is closed.

The support is the set of points of the space at which the stalk of the underlying abelian
sheaf at some geometric point is nonzero; for a sheaf of rings that is the set of points at
which the ring of germs is not the zero ring, since a ring vanishes exactly when its unit
does. Its complement is exhibited as the image of the maximal open zero locus of the unit
section of a surjective étale atlas, which is open because an étale chart is open on points
by clause (3) of Stacks 03BX.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_supportOfSheaf (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    IsClosed (supportOfSheaf B S hS X (toAddCommGrp B S hS X R))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isHenselization_chartLocalRingToEtaleLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KF, with the structure map named.** The étale local ring of an algebraic space at
a geometric point `x̄` is a strict henselization of the local ring `𝒪_{U, u}` of a scheme chart
at the point under the chosen lift, *along the canonical map of Stacks 05VP*
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartLocalRingToEtaleLocalRing`, with the separable closure of the
residue field of `𝒪_{U, u}` inside the residue field of the geometric point as the residue
extension.

This is the form `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_algebra_isHenselization_etaleLocalRing_chart`
is proved from: there the algebra structure is produced existentially and an arbitrary chosen
separable closure is matched to this one by uniqueness of separable closures, which is all the
residue extension is used for. Naming the structure map is what lets a statement about
`𝒪_{U, u} → 𝒪_{X, x̄}` — flatness, locality, lengths, orders of vanishing — be read off the
henselization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHenselization_chartLocalRingToEtaleLocalRing {x : GeometricPoint B S hS X}
    (V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x) :
    @IsHenselization ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS X V) _ _
      (separableClosure (ResidueField ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS X V))
        (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField) _ _
      (etaleLocalRing B S hS X x : Type (u + 1)) _
      (isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X hX x)
      (chartLocalRingToEtaleLocalRing B S hS X hX V).toAlgebra
declarations.comment:
the étale local ring is a strict henselization of a neighborhood stalk along the
canonical map of Stacks 05VP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_algebra_isHenselization_etaleLocalRing_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KF.** The étale local ring of an algebraic space at a geometric point is a strict
henselization of the local ring of a scheme chart at the point under the chosen lift, for every
chosen separable algebraic closure of the residue field of that local ring. The algebra
structure is the canonical map of Stacks 05VP.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebra_isHenselization_etaleLocalRing_chart {x : GeometricPoint B S hS X}
    (V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x) (p : chartScheme V.chart)
    (hp : chartPoint B S hS X V = p)
    (κsep : Type u) [Field κsep]
    [Algebra (ResidueField ((chartScheme V.chart).presheaf.stalk p : Type u)) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField ((chartScheme V.chart).presheaf.stalk p : Type u)) κsep] :
    letI : IsLocalRing (etaleLocalRing B S hS X x : Type (u + 1)) :=
      isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X hX x
    ∃ alg : Algebra ((chartScheme V.chart).presheaf.stalk p : Type u)
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X x : Type (u + 1)),
      @IsHenselization ((chartScheme V.chart).presheaf.stalk p : Type u) _ _ κsep _ _
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X x : Type (u + 1)) _
        (isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X hX x) alg
declarations.comment: the étale local ring is a strict henselization of a neighborhood stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_algebra_isHenselization_etaleLocalRing_elementary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KF.** The étale local ring of an algebraic space at a geometric point `x̄` is a
strict henselization of the local ring of an elementary étale neighborhood of the point below
`x̄`, at its distinguished point, for every chosen separable algebraic closure of the residue
field of that local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebra_isHenselization_etaleLocalRing_elementary (hxbar : xbar.LiesOver x)
    (κsep : Type u) [Field κsep]
    [instAlg : Algebra (ResidueField (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u)) κsep]
    [instSep : IsSepClosure (ResidueField (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u))
      κsep] :
    letI : IsLocalRing (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)) :=
      isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X hX xbar
    ∃ alg : Algebra (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u)
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)),
      @IsHenselization (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u) _ _ κsep _ _
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)) _
        (isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X hX xbar) alg
declarations.comment:
the étale local ring is a strict henselization of an elementary neighborhood
stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleLocalRingEquivChart
declarations.doc:
The stalk of the structure sheaf of an algebraic space is canonically
the étale local ring of a scheme étale neighborhood. The comparison sends
ordinary chart germs and all common pointed étale-refinement germs to their
scheme-side germs.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleLocalRingEquivChart
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x)
    (E : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (hV : E.Contains (neighborhoodChartScheme V)) :
    { e : etaleLocalRing B S hS F x ≃+*
        _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.etaleLocalRing E (neighborhoodChartScheme V) hV
          (chartGeometricPoint V) //
      (∀ a : Γ(neighborhoodChartScheme V, ⊤),
        e (etaleLocalRingGerm B S hS F x (Opposite.op V) a) =
          structureSheafStalkFromLocalRing E (neighborhoodChartScheme V) hV
            (chartGeometricPoint V)
            ((neighborhoodChartScheme V).presheaf.germ ⊤
              ((chartGeometricPoint V).hom
                (closedPoint (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField)) trivial a)) ∧
      (∀ (W : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x) (f : W ⟶ V)
          (U : (geometricPointFiber E (neighborhoodChartScheme V) hV
            (chartGeometricPoint V)).Elementsᵒᵖ)
          (a : Γ(neighborhoodChartScheme W, ⊤))
          (hs : neighborhoodChartScheme W =
            (_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.toScheme E
              (neighborhoodChartScheme V) hV).obj U.unop.1)
          (_hp : HEq (chartGeometricPoint W).hom U.unop.2.1)
          (_hf : HEq (neighborhoodChartMap f)
            (E.inclusion.map U.unop.1.obj.hom)),
        e (etaleLocalRingGerm B S hS F x (Opposite.op W) a) =
          (colimit.ι
            ((Functor.Elements.π
              (geometricPointFiber E (neighborhoodChartScheme V) hV
                (chartGeometricPoint V))).op ⋙
              (_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.structureSheaf E
                (neighborhoodChartScheme V) hV).obj)
            U).hom (show Γ((_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.toScheme E
              (neighborhoodChartScheme V) hV).obj U.unop.1, ⊤) from hs ▸ a)) }
declarations.comment: identification of the two étale stalks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictHenselizationEquivEtaleLocalRing
declarations.doc:
The étale local ring of the algebraic space is the strict henselization
of the local ring of a scheme étale neighborhood at the selected point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def strictHenselizationEquivEtaleLocalRing
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x)
    (E : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (hV : E.Contains (neighborhoodChartScheme V))
    (T : IsLocalRing.HenselizationTower
      ((neighborhoodChartScheme V).presheaf.stalk
        ((chartGeometricPoint V).hom
          (closedPoint (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField)))
      (separableClosure (ResidueField
        ((neighborhoodChartScheme V).presheaf.stalk
          ((chartGeometricPoint V).hom
            (closedPoint (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField))))
        (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField)) :
    T.strictHenselization ≃+* etaleLocalRing B S hS F x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictHenselizationEquivEtaleLocalRing_germ
declarations.doc:
The strict-henselization comparison sends the ordinary germ of a chart
section to its germ in the algebraic-space structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictHenselizationEquivEtaleLocalRing_germ
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x)
    (E : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (hV : E.Contains (neighborhoodChartScheme V))
    (T : IsLocalRing.HenselizationTower
      ((neighborhoodChartScheme V).presheaf.stalk
        ((chartGeometricPoint V).hom
          (closedPoint (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField)))
      (separableClosure (ResidueField
        ((neighborhoodChartScheme V).presheaf.stalk
          ((chartGeometricPoint V).hom
            (closedPoint (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField))))
        (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField))
    (a : Γ(neighborhoodChartScheme V, ⊤)) :
    (strictHenselizationEquivEtaleLocalRing hF V E hV T)
      (algebraMap _ T.strictHenselization
        ((neighborhoodChartScheme V).presheaf.germ ⊤
          ((chartGeometricPoint V).hom
            (closedPoint (chartGeometricPoint V).residueField)) trivial a)) =
      etaleLocalRingGerm B S hS F x (Opposite.op V) a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleLocalRingChartIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KF, first equality.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `x̄` be a
geometric point of `X` and let `(U, ū)` be an étale neighbourhood of `x̄` with `U` a scheme.
Then the étale local ring of `U` at `ū` is the étale local ring of `X` at `x̄`.

Only the first of the two equalities of Stacks 04KF is proved here.  The second,
`𝒪_{U, ū} = 𝒪_{U, u}^{sh}`, is Étale Cohomology, Lemma 04HX, which is not in the library.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleLocalRingChartIso {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    (N : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x) :
    etaleLocalRing B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F).obj N.chart))
        (chartPresheafGeometricPoint B S hS x N) ≅ etaleLocalRing B S hS F x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleLocalRing
declarations.doc:
The *étale local ring* of an algebraic space at a geometric point: the
stalk of the structure sheaf on the small étale site, i.e. the ring of germs at that point of
regular functions on étale neighbourhoods.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev etaleLocalRing (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) : CommRingCat.{u + 1}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
The *strict henselization* of an algebraic space at a geometric point is
the spectrum of its étale local ring.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev strictHenselization (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) : Scheme.{u + 1}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedSite_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KH.** The small étale site of an algebraic space, endowed with its
structure sheaf, is a locally ringed site.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleRingedSite_isLocallyRinged (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    RingedSite.IsLocallyRinged (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, the morphism of small
étale ringed topoi `(f_small, f♯)` attached to `f` is a morphism of locally ringed topoi: its
square of units subsheaves is cartesian.

The geometric points of `X` are a conservative family of points of its small étale site, and at
each of them the fibre of `f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` is the map of étale local rings
`𝒪_{Y, f(x̄)} ⟶ 𝒪_{X, x̄}`, which is a local ring map.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged :
    (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).IsLocallyRinged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoMorphism_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KK.** A 2-endomorphism of the morphism of small étale ringed topoi induced by a
morphism of algebraic spaces is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoMorphism_eq_id
    (t : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoMorphism.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u}
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f)
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f)) :
    t = AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.TwoMorphism.id
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoMorphismOfRingedTopoi_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KK.**  A 2-morphism from the morphism of small étale ringed topoi induced by a
morphism of algebraic spaces to itself is the identity.

The 2-morphism is taken over `(smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).toRingedToposModulesHom`,
since `Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.TwoMorphismOfRingedTopoi` (Stacks 04IC) is defined for
the four-field `Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom`; the two structures are
equivalent.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_spaceHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KL.** Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over `Spec ℤ` (here `Spec (ULift ℤ)`, the
terminal scheme at the universe of the site) and let
`(g, g♯) : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), 𝒪_Y)` be a morphism of locally ringed topoi.
Then there is a unique morphism of algebraic spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` such that `(g, g♯)` is
2-isomorphic to `(f_small, f♯)` (Stacks 04IC, 03G8).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_spaceHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) hZ}
    (g : RingedToposHom (smallEtaleRingedTopos B _ hZ X) (smallEtaleRingedTopos B _ hZ Y))
    (hg : g.IsLocallyRinged) :
    ∃! f : X ⟶ Y, Nonempty (RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B _ hZ f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_smallEtaleLocallyRingedClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KL, in the form of full faithfulness.** Over `Spec ℤ`, the construction
`X ↦ (X_étale, 𝒪_X)` is fully faithful from algebraic spaces to locally ringed topoi, morphisms of
the latter being taken up to 2-isomorphism: `f ↦ [(f_small, f♯)]` is a bijection from the
morphisms `X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces onto the 2-isomorphism classes of morphisms of locally ringed
topoi `(Sh(X_étale), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), 𝒪_Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_smallEtaleLocallyRingedClass (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
    (X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) hZ) :
    Function.Bijective (smallEtaleLocallyRingedClass B _ hZ X Y)
declarations.comment:
the reformulation: X ↦ (X_étale, 𝒪_X) is fully faithful, morphisms of locally
  ringed topoi being taken up to 2-isomorphism

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
registrations.comment:
the uniqueness clause over a base: at most one morphism of algebraic spaces
  over S induces a given morphism of the small étale ringed topoi. This is the faithfulness half
  of the asserted full faithfulness, and it needs neither of the theorem's hypotheses — not
  local ringedness of the morphism of topoi, and not 2-compatibility with structure morphisms to
  a further base

declarations.name: exists_isPurelyInseparable_and_isSeparablyGenerated_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KM.** Let `K/k` be a finitely generated field extension and let `Ω/K` be a perfect
field extension. Then inside `Ω` there is a diagram
```
K  →  K'
↑     ↑
k  →  k'
```
with `k'/k` and `K'/K` finite purely inseparable and `K'/k'` separably generated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_and_isSeparablyGenerated_of_essFiniteType
    (k K Ω : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Field Ω] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k Ω] [Algebra K Ω]
    [IsScalarTower k K Ω] [PerfectField Ω] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K] :
    ∃ (K' : IntermediateField K Ω) (k' : IntermediateField k ↥K'),
      Module.Finite K ↥K' ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K ↥K' ∧
      Module.Finite k ↥k' ∧ IsPurelyInseparable k ↥k' ∧
      Algebra.IsSeparablyGenerated ↥k' ↥K'

declarations.name: geometricallyReduced_localization
declarations.doc:
If `R` is geometrically reduced over the field `k` and `A` is a localization of `R` at a
multiplicative subset `M ⊆ R`, carrying the induced `k`-algebra structure, then `A` is
geometrically reduced over `k`.

Fix a field extension `K/k`; then `K ⊗[k] R` is reduced. The key base-change fact is that
`K ⊗[k] A` is isomorphic to a localization of `K ⊗[k] R`: viewing `K ⊗[k] R` as an
`R`-algebra, `(K ⊗[k] R) ⊗[R] A` is a localization of `K ⊗[k] R` at the image submonoid
`Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (K ⊗[k] R) M`, and cancelling the base change gives a
`K`-algebra isomorphism `(K ⊗[k] R) ⊗[R] A ≃ₐ[K] K ⊗[k] A`. A localization of a reduced ring
is reduced, so `(K ⊗[k] R) ⊗[R] A` is reduced and reducedness transfers back to `K ⊗[k] A`
along that isomorphism. As `K/k` was arbitrary, `A` is geometrically reduced over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyReduced_localization
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    (M : Submonoid R) (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization M A]
    [Algebra k A] [IsScalarTower k R A]
    (hR : GeometricallyReduced.{u, v, w} k R) :
    GeometricallyReduced.{u, v, w} k A

declarations.name: geometricallyReduced_polynomial
declarations.doc:
If `R` is geometrically reduced over the field `k`, then so is the polynomial ring `R[x]`
in one variable.

Fix a field extension `K/k`. Then `K ⊗[k] R` is reduced, hence so is the polynomial ring
`(K ⊗[k] R)[X]`, and transferring reducedness backward along the ring isomorphism
`K ⊗[k] R[X] ≃+* (K ⊗[k] R)[X]` shows `K ⊗[k] R[X]` is reduced. As `K/k` was arbitrary,
`R[X]` is geometrically reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyReduced_polynomial
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    (hR : GeometricallyReduced.{u, v, w} k R) :
    GeometricallyReduced.{u, v, w} k (Polynomial R)

declarations.name: gal_acts_transitively_on_primes_of_isGalois
declarations.doc:
Statement 1 (Stacks Tag 04KP). The Galois group `Gal(kbar/k)` of a Galois extension
`kbar/k` acts transitively on the primes of `kbar ⊗[k] K`: for every pair of prime ideals
`P, Q` there exists `σ ∈ Gal(kbar/k)` whose induced map on the prime spectrum
(via `comap` of `σ ⊗ id_K`) carries `Q` to `P`. A separable algebraic closure of `k`, the case
the source states, is Galois over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gal_acts_transitively_on_primes_of_isGalois
    {k K kbar : Type*}
    [Field k] [Field K] [Field kbar]
    [Algebra k K] [Algebra k kbar] [IsGalois k kbar] :
    ∀ (P Q : PrimeSpectrum (kbar ⊗[k] K)),
      ∃ σ : kbar ≃ₐ[k] kbar,
        PrimeSpectrum.comap
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.congr σ (AlgEquiv.refl (R := k) (A₁ :=
              K))).toAlgHom.toRingHom Q = P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inverseImage_units_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KR: the inverse image of the units subsheaf.** There is exactly one isomorphism
of the inverse image of the units subsheaf of `Y` with the units subsheaf of the inverse-image
ringed topos compatible with the inclusions into the structure sheaves; it is therefore the
canonical one.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImage_units_iso :
    ∃! e : f.inverseImage.obj (RingedTopos.units Y) ≅
        RingedTopos.units (inverseImageRingedTopos C J Y f),
      e.hom ≫ RingedTopos.unitsι (inverseImageRingedTopos C J Y f) =
        f.inverseImage.map (RingedTopos.unitsι Y) ≫ (inverseImageForgetIso J Y f).hom
declarations.comment: inverse image of the units subsheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inverseImageRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04KR: the canonical morphism is a morphism of locally ringed topoi.** Its structure
map on underlying sheaves of sets is an isomorphism, so its square of units subsheaves is
cartesian as soon as the comparison of units subsheaves exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImageRingedToposHom_isLocallyRinged :
    RingedToposHom.IsLocallyRinged (inverseImageRingedToposHom C J Y f)
declarations.comment: canonical morphism of locally ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyReducedAt_of_specializes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KS.** Geometric reducedness at a point of a scheme over a field is
preserved on passing to a generalization of that point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyReducedAt_of_specializes
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) {x' x : X}
    (hsp : x' ⤳ x) (hx : IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x) :
    IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyReducedAt_of_isReduced_stalk_of_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KS.** A scheme over a field is geometrically reduced at a point
whose local ring is reduced if it is geometrically reduced at every generic point of an
irreducible component specializing to that point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyReducedAt_of_isReduced_stalk_of_genericPoints
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X)
    (hx : _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hgeneric : ∀ x' : X, x' ∈ genericPoints X → x' ⤳ x →
      IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x') :
    IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_of_isGeometricallyReducedAt_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
A reduced scheme over a field which is geometrically reduced at the generic points of all
its irreducible components is geometrically reduced.
declarations.statement:
public lemma geometricallyReduced_of_isGeometricallyReducedAt_genericPoints
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsReduced X]
    (h : ∀ x : X, x ∈ genericPoints X → IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x) :
    GeometricallyReduced f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_iff_isSeparableExtension_functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KS.** An integral scheme over a field is geometrically reduced if and
only if its function field is a separable extension of the base field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyReduced_iff_isSeparableExtension_functionField
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X] :
    letI : Nonempty (⊤ : X.Opens) := ⟨⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩⟩
    letI : Algebra k X.functionField :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
        X.germToFunctionField ⊤).hom.toAlgebra
    GeometricallyReduced f ↔ Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k X.functionField

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_purelyInseparable_extension_geometricallyReduced_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KT.** After a finite purely inseparable extension of the ground
field, the reduction of the base change of a scheme with finitely many irreducible components
is geometrically reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_purelyInseparable_extension_geometricallyReduced_reduction
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hX : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k')
      (_ : Module.Finite k k') (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k k'),
      let g : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))
      let p : pullback f g ⟶ Spec (.of k') := pullback.snd f g
      let I := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        (X := (pullback f g : Scheme.{u})) (⊤ : Closeds (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}))
      GeometricallyReduced (I.subschemeι ≫ p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_subextension_descending_isCompact_open
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact open in the base change of a scheme to an algebraic extension is pulled back
from a quasi-compact open after a finite intermediate extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_subextension_descending_isCompact_open
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (V : (pullback f (spectrumMap k K)).Opens) (hV : IsCompact V.1) :
    ∃ (E : IntermediateField k K) (_ : FiniteDimensional k E)
      (V' : (pullback f (spectrumMap k E)).Opens),
      IsCompact V'.1 ∧
        ∃ p : pullback f (spectrumMap k K) ⟶ pullback f (spectrumMap k E),
          p ≫ pullback.fst f (spectrumMap k E) = pullback.fst f (spectrumMap k K) ∧
          p ≫ pullback.snd f (spectrumMap k E) =
            pullback.snd f (spectrumMap k K) ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom E.val) ∧
          V = p ⁻¹ᵁ V'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_subgroup_fixing_isCompact_open
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact open in the base change of a scheme to a Galois extension is fixed by an open
subgroup of the Galois group.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_subgroup_fixing_isCompact_open
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsGalois k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (V : (pullback f (spectrumMap k K)).Opens) (hV : IsCompact V.1) :
    ∃ H : Subgroup Gal(K/k), IsOpen (H : Set Gal(K/k)) ∧
      ∀ σ : Gal(K/k), σ ∈ H →
        ∃ a : pullback f (spectrumMap k K) ≅ pullback f (spectrumMap k K),
          a.hom ≫ pullback.fst f (spectrumMap k K) = pullback.fst f (spectrumMap k K) ∧
          a.hom ≫ pullback.snd f (spectrumMap k K) =
            pullback.snd f (spectrumMap k K) ≫
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ.toRingEquiv.toRingHom) ∧
      V = a.hom ⁻¹ᵁ V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_of_connectedSpace_of_algebraicClosure_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KV.** A connected scheme over a field is geometrically
connected if the field is algebraically closed in the residue field of one of
its points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_of_connectedSpace_of_algebraicClosure_eq_bot
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [ConnectedSpace X] (x : X)
    (h : let : (f x).asIdeal.IsPrime := (f x).isPrime
      let := ((CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (f x).asIdeal.ResidueField)) ≫
        (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of k) (f x)).inv ≫
        f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      IsAlgClosedIn k (X.residueField x)) :
    GeometricallyConnected f
declarations.comment: point with algebraically closed base field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_of_connectedSpace_of_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KV, rational-point consequence.** A connected scheme
over a field with a rational point is geometrically connected.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_of_connectedSpace_of_section
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [ConnectedSpace X] (s : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = 𝟙 _) :
    GeometricallyConnected f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_irreducibleComponent_eq_sUnion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KW.** After extension of the base field, the inverse image
of an irreducible component is a union of irreducible components.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mapsTo_irreducibleComponents_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KX.** Let `K/k` be an extension of fields and let `X` be a scheme
over `k`. The image of every irreducible component of `X ×_{Spec k} Spec K` under the projection
to `X` is an irreducible component of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mapsTo_irreducibleComponents_baseChange
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    Set.MapsTo
      (fun Z ↦ (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base '' Z)
      (irreducibleComponents
        (pullback (C := Scheme) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))))
      (irreducibleComponents X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjOn_irreducibleComponents_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KX.** Let `K/k` be an extension of fields and let `X` be a scheme
over `k`. Every irreducible component of `X` is the image of an irreducible component of
`X ×_{ Spec k} Spec K` under the projection to `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjOn_irreducibleComponents_baseChange
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    Set.SurjOn
      (fun Z ↦ (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base '' Z)
      (irreducibleComponents
        (pullback (C := Scheme) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))))
      (irreducibleComponents X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fiber_irreducibleComponentsBaseChangeMap_eq_orbit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KY.** For a scheme over a field `k` and a normal extension `K/k`,
for instance a separable closure of `k`, the fibre through each geometric irreducible component
of the canonical map to the irreducible components downstairs is its orbit under the group
`K ≃ₐ[k] K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fiber_irreducibleComponentsBaseChangeMap_eq_orbit
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Normal k K]
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (Z : (galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k K X).V) :
    (irreducibleComponentsBaseChangeMap k K X) ⁻¹'
        {irreducibleComponentsBaseChangeMap k K X Z} =
      Set.range (fun σ : MulOpposite (K ≃ₐ[k] K) ↦
        ConcreteCategory.hom
          ((galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k K X).ρ σ).asHom Z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_subextension_defining_component
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KZ.** Every irreducible component after extension to a separable
closure is defined over a finite intermediate extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_subextension_defining_component
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsSepClosure k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (Z : irreducibleComponents
      (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) :
    ∃ (E : IntermediateField k K) (_ : FiniteDimensional k E)
      (T : irreducibleComponents
        (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E)))))
      (p : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) ⟶
        pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E)))),
      p ≫ pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))) =
          pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) ∧
        p ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))) =
          pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) ≫
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom E.val) ∧
        p.base ⁻¹' (T : Set _) = (Z : Set _)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.continuous_galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KZ.** The Galois action on the geometric irreducible components
of a locally finite-type scheme is continuous when the component set is discrete.
declarations.statement:
public theorem continuous_galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsSepClosure k K]
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] :
    letI : TopologicalSpace (galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k K X).V := ⊥
    Continuous (fun p : MulOpposite (K ≃ₐ[k] K) ×
        (galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k K X).V =>
      ConcreteCategory.hom
        ((galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k K X).ρ p.1).asHom p.2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_single_orbit_decomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04KZ.** Over a separable closure, the inverse image of an irreducible
component is a finite union of irreducible components forming a single Galois orbit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_single_orbit_decomposition
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsSepClosure k K]
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom]
    (T : irreducibleComponents X.left) :
    ∃ s : Finset (galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k K X).V,
      s.Nonempty ∧
        ((pullback.fst X.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base ⁻¹'
              (T : Set X.left) =
            ⋃ Z ∈ s, Z.1) ∧
          ∀ Z ∈ s, ∀ Z' ∈ s,
            ∃ σ : MulOpposite (K ≃ₐ[k] K),
              ConcreteCategory.hom
                  ((galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k K X).ρ σ).asHom Z = Z'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProperVariety
declarations.doc:
A variety over a field is proper when its structure morphism to the spectrum of the field
is proper.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSmoothVariety
declarations.doc:
A variety over a field is smooth when its structure morphism to the spectrum of the field
is smooth.
declarations.statement:
class IsSmoothVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop extends IsVariety k f, Smooth f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjectiveVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L1.** A variety over a field is projective when its structure
morphism to the spectrum of the field is H-projective, equivalently projective.
declarations.statement:
class IsProjectiveVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop extends IsVariety k f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjectiveVariety_iff_isProjectiveMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L1, clause (2), the form cited to [Stacks, Tag 01WB].** For a
variety, being a projective variety is equivalent to H-projectivity of its structure morphism,
that is, to `X` being isomorphic over `k` to a closed subscheme of `ℙⁿ_k` for some `n`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjectiveVariety_iff_isProjective'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L1, clause (2).** A projective variety is exactly a variety whose
structure morphism to the spectrum of the field is projective.

The source defines the notion by projectivity of the structure morphism and observes, citing
[Stacks, Tag 01WB], that it amounts to `X` being isomorphic to a closed subscheme of `ℙⁿ_k` for
some `n`, which is the H-projectivity carried by the class. The two agree over the affine base
`Spec k` by `AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_iff_isProjectiveMorphism_of_isAffine`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjectiveVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L1.** A variety over a field is quasi-projective when its structure
morphism to the spectrum of the field is quasi-projective.
declarations.statement:
class IsQuasiProjectiveVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop extends IsVariety k f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjectiveVariety_iff_isHQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L1, clause (3).** A quasi-projective variety is exactly a variety
whose structure morphism is H-quasi-projective, that is, admits a quasi-compact immersion into
`ℙⁿ_k` over `k` for some `n`, which realizes `X` as a locally closed subscheme of `ℙⁿ_k`.

This is the identification the source records by citing [Stacks, Tag 01VZ]; over the affine base
`Spec k` it is `AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_iff_isHQuasiProjective_of_isAffine`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparable_globalSections_of_isProperVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L2, part (2).** For a geometrically reduced proper variety over a
field `k`, the field of global functions is separable over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparable_globalSections_of_isProperVariety
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k f] [GeometricallyReduced f] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsSeparable k Γ(X, ⊤)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPurelyInseparable_globalSections_of_isProperVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L2, part (3).** For a geometrically irreducible proper variety over a
field `k`, the field of global functions is purely inseparable over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPurelyInseparable_globalSections_of_isProperVariety
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k f] [GeometricallyIrreducible f] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    IsPurelyInseparable k Γ(X, ⊤)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_isOpenImmersion_into_properVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L4.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field, let `Xbar` be a
proper variety over `k`, and let `X` be a normal open subscheme of `Xbar`. Then the group of
invertible global functions on `X`, modulo the constants coming from `k`, is finitely generated.

The ambient proper variety may be replaced by its normalization, which is again a proper variety
over `k` and is normal, and over the normal open `X` the normalization morphism is an
isomorphism; so the statement follows from the case of a normal ambient variety.
declarations.statement:
theorem fg_units_quotient_of_isOpenImmersion_into_properVariety
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X Xbar : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Xbar ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProperVariety k f]
    (i : X ⟶ Xbar) [IsOpenImmersion i] [IsNormal X] :
    let φ : k →+* Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (i ≫ f).appTop).hom
    Group.FG (Units Γ(X, ⊤) ⧸ (Units.map φ.toMonoidHom).range)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L5.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field and let `X` be an
integral scheme locally of finite type over `k`.  Then the group of invertible global functions on
`X` modulo the constants coming from `k` is a finitely generated abelian group.

The normalization `ν : X^ν ⟶ X` is finite, `X^ν` is a normal integral scheme locally of finite
type over `k`, and `ν` is dominant, hence injective on global sections; so the statement follows
from the normal case.
declarations.statement:
theorem fg_units_quotient_of_locallyOfFiniteType (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    let φ : k →+* Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom
    Group.FG (Γ(X, ⊤)ˣ ⧸ (Units.map φ.toMonoidHom).range)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_connectedSpace_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be an algebraically closed field and let `X` be a connected reduced scheme which is
locally of finite type over `k` and has finitely many irreducible components.  Then `𝒪^*(X)/k^*`,
the group of invertible global functions on `X` modulo the constants coming from `k`, is a finitely
generated abelian group.
declarations.statement:
theorem fg_units_quotient_of_connectedSpace_of_isReduced (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [ConnectedSpace X] [IsReduced X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hX : (irreducibleComponents (X : Type u)).Finite) :
    Group.FG (Γ(X, ⊤)ˣ ⧸ (Units.map
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).toMonoidHom).range)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_integrallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L7 under its condition (1).** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a
connected reduced scheme, locally of finite type over `k`, with finitely many irreducible
components, and assume that every global section of `X` integral over `k` is a constant — that is,
that the integral closure of `k` in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is `k`.  Then the group of invertible global
functions on `X` modulo the constants coming from `k` is a finitely generated abelian group.

The base change `X̄ = X ×_k \bar k` is surjective over `X` and has finitely many irreducible
components; each of them with its reduced induced structure is integral and locally of finite type
over `\bar k`, so Tag 04L5 applies to it.  A unit of `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` which is a constant from
`\bar k` on every component of `X̄` is killed by the product of the minimal polynomials of those
constants over `k`, hence is integral over `k`, hence is a constant from `k` by the hypothesis.

Connectedness of `X` is one of the source's hypotheses and is kept here, but this proof does not
use it: in the source connectedness is what forces the constants on the components to agree,
whereas here condition (1) does that work.
declarations.statement:
theorem fg_units_quotient_of_integrallyClosed (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [ConnectedSpace X] [IsReduced X] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hX : (irreducibleComponents (X : Type u)).Finite)
    (h1 : ∀ a : Γ(X, ⊤), (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).IsIntegralElem a →
      a ∈ Set.range ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom) :
    Group.FG (Γ(X, ⊤)ˣ ⧸ (Units.map
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).toMonoidHom).range)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_rationalPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L7 under its condition (2).** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a
connected reduced scheme, locally of finite type over `k`, with finitely many irreducible
components, and suppose `X` has a `k`-rational point.  Then the group of invertible global
functions on `X` modulo the constants coming from `k` is a finitely generated abelian group.

Condition (2) implies condition (1) by `mem_range_of_isIntegralElem_of_rationalPoint`, which is
the source's own argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem fg_units_quotient_of_rationalPoint (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [ConnectedSpace X] [IsReduced X] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hX : (irreducibleComponents (X : Type u)).Finite) (e : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X)
    (he : e ≫ f = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    Group.FG (Γ(X, ⊤)ˣ ⧸ (Units.map
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).toMonoidHom).range)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_geometricallyIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L7 under its condition (3).** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a
connected reduced scheme, locally of finite type over `k`, with finitely many irreducible
components, and suppose `X` is geometrically integral over `k`.  Then the group of invertible
global functions on `X` modulo the constants coming from `k` is a finitely generated abelian
group.

Condition (3) implies condition (1) by `mem_range_of_isIntegralElem_of_geometricallyIntegral`, and
`fg_units_quotient_of_integrallyClosed` is the proposition under condition (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem fg_units_quotient_of_geometricallyIntegral (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [ConnectedSpace X] [IsReduced X] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hX : (irreducibleComponents (X : Type u)).Finite) (hgi : GeometricallyIntegral f) :
    Group.FG (Γ(X, ⊤)ˣ ⧸ (Units.map
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).toMonoidHom).range)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.integralClosure_globalSections_eq_bot_of_isAlgClosedIn_functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L8, condition (2) implies condition (1).** Let `k` be a field and let
`X` be an integral scheme over `k`.  If `k` is algebraically closed in the function field of `X`,
then the integral closure of `k` in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is `k`.

The germ map from the global sections to the stalk at the generic point is injective on an
integral scheme, so this is the field-theoretic statement
`integralClosure_eq_bot_of_isAlgClosedIn_of_injective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_globalSections_eq_bot_of_isAlgClosedIn_functionField
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra k X.functionField :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
        X.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint X) trivial).hom.toAlgebra
    IsAlgClosedIn k X.functionField → integralClosure k Γ(X, ⊤) = ⊥
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1); the source omits this verification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.integralClosure_globalSections_eq_bot_of_closedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L8, condition (4) implies condition (1).** Let `k` be a field and let
`X` be a connected reduced scheme over `k`.  Suppose that every field extension `L` of `k` which
admits at each closed point `x` of `X` a ring map to the residue field `κ(x)` compatible with the
maps out of `k` is already equal to `k`.  Then the integral closure of `k` in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is `k`.

The integral closure is a field by Tag 04MI, and evaluation at a point restricts to a ring map
from it to the residue field there which is compatible with the maps out of `k`.  So the
hypothesis applies to it and makes it `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_globalSections_eq_bot_of_closedPoints
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [ConnectedSpace X] [IsReduced X] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    (∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L],
      (∀ x ∈ closedPoints X, ∃ ι : L →+* X.residueField x,
        ∀ a : k, ι (algebraMap k L a) = X.Γevaluation x (algebraMap k Γ(X, ⊤) a)) →
      Function.Surjective (algebraMap k L)) →
    integralClosure k Γ(X, ⊤) = ⊥
declarations.comment: condition (4) implies condition (1); the source omits this verification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.integralClosure_globalSections_eq_bot_of_geometricallyIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L8, condition (3) implies condition (1).** Let `k` be a field and let
`X` be an integral scheme over `k` which is geometrically integral.  Then the integral closure of
`k` in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is `k`.

Geometric integrality is geometric reducedness together with geometric irreducibility.  The first
says the function field is a separable extension of `k` (Tag 04KS) and the second says `k` is
separably closed in the residue field at the generic point (Tag 054Q), which is the same field;
so `k` is algebraically closed in the function field, which is condition (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_globalSections_eq_bot_of_geometricallyIntegral
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X]
    (hgi : GeometricallyIntegral f) :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    integralClosure k Γ(X, ⊤) = ⊥
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (1); the source omits this verification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_isVariety_of_field_conditions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04L8.** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a variety over `k`.  Then the
group of invertible global functions on `X` modulo the constants coming from `k` is finitely
generated as soon as one of the following holds: the integral closure of `k` in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is
`k`; `k` is algebraically closed in the function field of `X`; `X` is geometrically integral over
`k`; or no field extension of `k` other than `k` itself admits at every closed point a map to the
residue field there compatible with the maps out of `k`.

A variety is integral, hence connected and reduced with a single irreducible component, and its
structure morphism is locally of finite type, so Proposition 04L7 under its condition (1) —
`AlgebraicGeometry.fg_units_quotient_of_integrallyClosed` — applies.  Each of the other three
conditions is turned into condition (1) by the three lemmas above.
declarations.statement:
theorem fg_units_quotient_of_isVariety_of_field_conditions
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    (integralClosure k Γ(X, ⊤) = ⊥ ∨
      (letI : Algebra k X.functionField :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
          X.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint X) trivial).hom.toAlgebra
       IsAlgClosedIn k X.functionField) ∨
      GeometricallyIntegral f ∨
      (∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L],
        (∀ x ∈ closedPoints X, ∃ ι : L →+* X.residueField x,
          ∀ a : k, ι (algebraMap k L a) = X.Γevaluation x (algebraMap k Γ(X, ⊤) a)) →
        Function.Surjective (algebraMap k L))) →
    Group.FG (Γ(X, ⊤)ˣ ⧸ (Units.map
      (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).toMonoidHom).range)

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.fst_snd_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The lower-left square of the composition diagram, formed by the two projections out of the
scheme of composable arrows, the source map and the target map, is a pullback square: it is the
defining square of the fibre product `R ×_{s, U, t} R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fst_snd_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback (pullback.fst G.source G.target) (pullback.snd G.source G.target) G.source
      G.target
declarations.comment: diagram (04LF): the lower-left square (projections `pr₀`, `pr₁`, source and target) is cartesian

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.comp_source_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The square formed by composition, the second projection, and two copies of the source map
is a pullback square: a composable pair of arrows is determined by its first member together
with its composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_source_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback G.comp (pullback.snd G.source G.target) G.source G.source
declarations.comment: diagram (04LF): the lower-right square is cartesian

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.target_comp_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The upper triangle in the composition diagram, viewed as a square with two copies of its
apex, is a pullback square: a pair of arrows with the same target is the same thing as a
composable pair together with its composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem target_comp_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback (pullback.fst G.source G.target) G.comp G.target G.target
declarations.comment: diagram (04LF): the top triangle, read as a square with two copies of its apex `U` (maps `pr₀`, `c`, and the target map twice), is cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable
declarations.doc:
The vertical map in the top left of the diagram: it sends a pair `(α, β)` with equal
targets to the composable pair `(α, α⁻¹ ∘ β)`.
declarations.comment: the vertical map `(pr₀, c ∘ (i, 1))` of the displayed diagram

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.fst_source_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The square formed by the two projections of the scheme of composable pairs together with
the source and the target maps is a pullback square.  This is the lower-left square of the
diagram taken with the lower horizontal maps, and it is cartesian because the scheme of
composable pairs is by definition the fibre product of the source and the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem fst_source_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback (pullback.fst G.source G.target) (pullback.snd G.source G.target)
      G.source G.target
declarations.comment: cartesianness: the lower of the two lower left squares, the one taken with the first projection on top and the target along the bottom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.id_target_comm
declarations.doc:
The upper-right square of the diagram commutes.  Both of its vertical maps are
identities, of the arrow scheme and of the object scheme respectively, and both of its
horizontal maps are the target map.
declarations.statement:
theorem id_target_comm {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) :
    𝟙 G.arrows ≫ G.target = G.target ≫ 𝟙 G.objects
declarations.comment: commutativity: the right-hand square between the two top rows, whose vertical maps are the identities

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable_fst
declarations.doc:
The comparison map preserves the first projection.  This is the lower of the two
commutative triangles in the top left of the diagram.
declarations.statement:
theorem targetPullbackToComposable_fst {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) :
    targetPullbackToComposable G ≫ pullback.fst G.source G.target =
      pullback.fst G.target G.target
declarations.comment: commutativity: the left square between the two top rows taken with the first projections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable_comp
declarations.doc:
Composing a pair after the change of coordinates recovers its second member.  This is
the upper of the two commutative triangles in the top left of the diagram.
declarations.comment: commutativity: the left square between the two top rows taken with the second projection on top and the composition along the bottom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable_isIso
declarations.doc:
The vertical comparison between pairs with the same target and composable pairs is an
isomorphism.
declarations.comment: the two top rows are isomorphic via the vertical maps given

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.diagram_pull
declarations.doc:
Every assertion made about the displayed diagram, in one statement.

Each square is written as `left ≫ bottom = top ≫ right`, so that the vertical maps which are
identities are displayed rather than suppressed.  The first three conjuncts are the
commutativity of the three squares between the two top rows: the two on the left, one for each
of the two parallel arrows, and the right-hand one whose vertical maps are the identity of the
arrow scheme and the identity of the object scheme.  Together with the fourth conjunct, which
says that the remaining vertical map is an isomorphism, they say that the two top rows are
isomorphic through the vertical maps given.  The last two conjuncts say that the two lower left
squares, again one for each of the two parallel arrows, are cartesian; the commutativity of
those two squares is part of the same assertions.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagram_pull {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) :
    targetPullbackToComposable G ≫ G.comp =
          pullback.snd G.target G.target ≫ 𝟙 G.arrows ∧
      targetPullbackToComposable G ≫ pullback.fst G.source G.target =
          pullback.fst G.target G.target ≫ 𝟙 G.arrows ∧
      𝟙 G.arrows ≫ G.target = G.target ≫ 𝟙 G.objects ∧
      IsIso (targetPullbackToComposable G) ∧
      IsPullback G.comp (pullback.snd G.source G.target) G.source G.source ∧
      IsPullback (pullback.fst G.source G.target) (pullback.snd G.source G.target)
        G.source G.target
declarations.comment: the whole diagram: it is commutative, its two top rows are isomorphic via the vertical maps given, and its two lower left squares are cartesian

registrations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.comp_source_isPullback
registrations.comment: cartesianness: the upper of the two lower left squares, the one taken with the composition on top and the source along the bottom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_locus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LH.** Suppose `P`, `Q`, and `R` are properties of morphisms of
schemes, `R` implies `Q`, `Q` is stable under composition and base change, and maximal open
`P`-loci exist for `Q`-morphisms and commute with base change by `R`-morphisms.  For a groupoid
scheme whose source and target have `R`, the maximal `P`-locus of the indicated map from the
pullback of its arrow scheme is the inverse image of an open of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_with_preimage_maximal_locus
    (P Q R : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hRQ : R ≤ Q) [Q.IsStableUnderComposition] [Q.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hmax : ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), Q f →
      ∃ V : X.Opens, IsGreatest {W : X.Opens | P (W.ι ≫ f)} V)
    (hbase : ∀ {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
      {p : X' ⟶ X} {q : Y' ⟶ Y}, Q f → R q → IsPullback p f' f q →
      ∀ {V : X.Opens}, IsGreatest {W : X.Opens | P (W.ι ≫ f)} V →
        IsGreatest {W' : X'.Opens | P (W'.ι ≫ f')} (p ⁻¹ᵁ V))
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) {U' : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : U' ⟶ G.objects.left) (hs : R G.source.left) (ht : R G.target.left) (hg : Q g) :
    ∃ W : U'.Opens,
      IsGreatest
        {V : (pullback g G.target.left).Opens |
          P (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd g G.target.left ≫ G.source.left)}
        ((pullback.fst g G.target.left) ⁻¹ᵁ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_maximal_locus_warning
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LI.** Stacks Tag 04LH applies to `P =` flat, `Q =` every morphism
(the empty condition) and `R =` flat and locally of finite presentation: `R` implies `Q`, `Q` is
stable under composition and base change, every morphism of schemes has a largest open of its
source on which it is flat, and that open commutes with base change along a morphism which is
flat and locally of finite presentation. But this largest flat open is not the set of points at
which the morphism is flat: for some morphism of schemes it is strictly smaller.

The largest flat open is `AlgebraicGeometry.maximalFlatOpen`, the interior of the pointwise flat
locus. The counterexample is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_flat_locus_not_open`; openness of the
universally open map `p` (Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyOpen.of_flat`, Stacks 01UA)
gives the base change compatibility.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_maximal_locus_warning :
    ((fun _ _ q => Flat q ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation q : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ≤ ⊤) ∧
    (⊤ : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).IsStableUnderComposition ∧
    (⊤ : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).IsStableUnderBaseChange ∧
    (∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), ∃ V : X.Opens,
      IsGreatest {W : X.Opens | Flat (W.ι ≫ f)} V) ∧
    (∀ {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {p : X' ⟶ X} {q : Y' ⟶ Y},
      Flat q → LocallyOfFinitePresentation q → IsPullback p f' f q → ∀ {V : X.Opens},
        IsGreatest {W : X.Opens | Flat (W.ι ≫ f)} V →
          IsGreatest {W' : X'.Opens | Flat (W'.ι ≫ f')} (p ⁻¹ᵁ V)) ∧
    ∃ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (W : X.Opens),
      IsGreatest {V : X.Opens | Flat (V.ι ≫ f)} W ∧
        (W.1 : Set X) ⊂ {x : X | IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x}
