declarations.comment: hypotheses (1)-(4) of 04LH for P = flat, Q = empty, R = flat and locally of finite presentation, and a morphism whose largest flat open is not its flat locus; the base change hypothesis uses Mathlib's UniversallyOpen.of_flat (01UA)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isOpenMap_comp_of_objects_isFieldSpectrum
declarations.doc:
Composition in a groupoid scheme is an open map when the scheme of objects is the
spectrum of a field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenMap_comp_of_objects_isFieldSpectrum
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (e : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k)) :
    IsOpenMap G.comp.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_arrows_of_objects_isSpec_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LN.** The arrow scheme of a groupoid scheme with object scheme the
spectrum of a field is separated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparated_arrows_of_objects_isSpec_field
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (_ : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k)) : G.arrows.left.IsSeparated

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_fieldExtension_sourceFiber_iso_mapping_points
declarations.doc:
If the object scheme of a groupoid scheme is the spectrum of a field `k`, then any two
points of its arrow scheme lift, after a field extension `k'/k`, to points of two base changes
of the arrow scheme along the source map which are carried to one another by an isomorphism
over `Spec k'`.

The two base changes are taken along the two `k`-algebra structures on `k'` that Tag 02YF
produces, namely the ones induced by the target and by the source of a chosen arrow.  This is
the corrected form of Tag 04LP: the printed form, an automorphism of a single base change, is
false (`Stacks.Groupoids.not_groupoidOnFieldHomogeneousStatement`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fieldExtension_sourceFiber_iso_mapping_points
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (e : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k))
    (r r' : G.arrows.left) :
    let s : G.arrows.left ⟶ Spec (.of k) := G.source.left ≫ e.hom
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (α β : Algebra k k'),
      let gt : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (@algebraMap k k' _ _ α))
      let gs : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (@algebraMap k k' _ _ β))
      let P : Scheme.{u} := pullback s gt
      let P' : Scheme.{u} := pullback s gs
      let POver : Over (Spec (.of k')) := Over.mk (pullback.snd s gt)
      let POver' : Over (Spec (.of k')) := Over.mk (pullback.snd s gs)
      ∃ (r₁ : P) (r₂ : P') (φ : POver ≅ POver'),
        φ.hom.left.base r₁ = r₂ ∧
          (pullback.fst s gt).base r₁ = r ∧
          (pullback.fst s gs).base r₂ = r'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_restrictionDiagramMorphisms
declarations.doc:
Every morphism in the defining restriction diagram over a field extension is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
public lemma surjective_restrictionDiagramMorphisms {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    {U' : Over S} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k']
    (_ : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k)) (_ : U'.left ≅ Spec (.of k'))
    (i : Fin 12) :
    Surjective ((restrictionDiagramMorphisms G g i).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_restrictionDiagramMorphisms
declarations.doc: Every morphism in the defining restriction diagram over a field extension is flat.
declarations.statement:
public lemma flat_restrictionDiagramMorphisms {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    {U' : Over S} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k']
    (_ : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k)) (_ : U'.left ≅ Spec (.of k'))
    (i : Fin 12) :
    Flat ((restrictionDiagramMorphisms G g i).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_restrictionDiagramMorphisms
declarations.doc:
Every morphism in the defining restriction diagram over a field extension is universally
open.
declarations.statement:
public lemma universallyOpen_restrictionDiagramMorphisms {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) {U' : Over S} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects)
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k']
    (_ : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k)) (_ : U'.left ≅ Spec (.of k'))
    (i : Fin 12) :
    UniversallyOpen ((restrictionDiagramMorphisms G g i).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_restrictionArrowsToArrows
declarations.doc:
The dotted morphism from the arrow scheme of a restriction to the original arrow scheme
is affine.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isAffineHom_restrictionArrowsToArrows {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    {U' : Over S} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k']
    (_ : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k)) (_ : U'.left ≅ Spec (.of k')) :
    IsAffineHom (restrictionArrowsToArrows G g).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_isIso_source_target_over_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
An arrow over a point of a groupoid scheme on `Spec k` can be lifted after an algebraically
closed extension of `k` so that both its source and target induce isomorphisms from the
extending field to the residue field of the lifted point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isIso_source_target_over_isAlgClosed {S : Scheme.{u}} {k : Type u}
    [Field k] (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (objects_eq : G.objects = Over.mk structureMap) (r : G.arrows.left) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : IsAlgClosed k') (i : k →+* k'),
      let g : Over.mk (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i).op ≫ structureMap) ⟶ G.objects :=
        extensionMap structureMap i ≫ eqToHom objects_eq.symm
      ∃ (r' : Spec (.of k') ⟶ (restrictionArrows G g).left),
      let rPoint := r' (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k')
      (restrictionArrowsToArrows G g).left rPoint = r ∧
        IsIso ((restrictionSource G g).left.residueFieldMap rPoint) ∧
        IsIso ((restrictionTarget G g).left.residueFieldMap rPoint)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.translationByPoint_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LS.** Translation by a point whose source and target induce
isomorphisms on residue fields is an automorphism of the arrow scheme.
declarations.statement:
public lemma translationByPoint_isIso {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hU : G.objects.left = Spec (.of k))
    (r : G.arrows.left) [IsIso (G.source.left.residueFieldMap r)]
    [IsIso (G.target.left.residueFieldMap r)] :
    IsIso (translationByPoint G k hU r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.identity_image_translationByPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LS.** Translation by `r` maps the identity arrow at the source of
`r` to `r`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma identity_image_translationByPoint {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hU : G.objects.left = Spec (.of k))
    (r : G.arrows.left) [IsIso (G.source.left.residueFieldMap r)] :
    (G.identity ≫ translationByPoint G k hU r).left (G.source.left r) = r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.existsUnique_minimalPrime_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LT.** Every local ring of the arrows of a groupoid scheme over a
field has a unique minimal prime ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_minimalPrime_stalk {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hU : G.objects.left = Spec (.of k))
    (r : G.arrows.left) :
    ∃! p : Ideal (G.arrows.left.presheaf.stalk r),
      p ∈ minimalPrimes (G.arrows.left.presheaf.stalk r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.existsUnique_irreducibleComponent_containing_identity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LT.** There is exactly one irreducible component of the arrow scheme
containing the identity section.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_irreducibleComponent_containing_identity
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hU : G.objects.left = Spec (.of k)) :
    ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents G.arrows.left,
      Set.range G.identity.left ⊆ (Z : Set G.arrows.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.geometricallyIrreducible_irreducibleComponent_of_identity_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LT.** The component containing the identity is geometrically
irreducible over the field via the source morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_irreducibleComponent_of_identity_source
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hU : G.objects.left = Spec (.of k)) (Z : irreducibleComponents G.arrows.left)
    (he : Set.range G.identity.left ⊆ (Z : Set G.arrows.left)) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible
      ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        (⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩ :
          Closeds G.arrows.left)).subschemeι ≫ G.source.left ≫ eqToHom hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.geometricallyIrreducible_irreducibleComponent_of_identity_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LT.** The component containing the identity is geometrically
irreducible over the field via the target morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_irreducibleComponent_of_identity_target
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hU : G.objects.left = Spec (.of k)) (Z : irreducibleComponents G.arrows.left)
    (he : Set.range G.identity.left ⊆ (Z : Set G.arrows.left)) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible
      ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        (⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩ :
          Closeds G.arrows.left)).subschemeι ≫ G.target.left ≫ eqToHom hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.trdeg_residueField_eq_of_target_isSpec_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LU.** The transcendence degree of the residue field at a point of a
scheme over the residue field of its image does not depend on which morphism locally of finite
type to the spectrum of a field is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem trdeg_residueField_eq_of_target_isSpec_field {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (e : Y ≅ Spec (.of k)) (f g : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (Y.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) :=
      (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra (Y.residueField (g x)) (X.residueField x) :=
      (g.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.trdeg (Y.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) =
      Algebra.trdeg (Y.residueField (g x)) (X.residueField x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_topologicalKrullDimAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LU.** The dimension of the arrow scheme of a groupoid scheme whose
object scheme is the spectrum of a field is its local dimension at every point, provided both
structure morphisms are locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_topologicalKrullDimAt {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) {k : Type u} [Field k] (e : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.source.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.target.left]
    (r : G.arrows.left) :
    topologicalKrullDim G.arrows.left = topologicalKrullDimAt G.arrows.left r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LU.** At a closed point of the arrow scheme of a groupoid scheme
whose object scheme is the spectrum of a field, the dimension of the arrow scheme is the Krull
dimension of the local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_ringKrullDim_stalk {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) {k : Type u} [Field k] (e : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.source.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.target.left]
    (r : G.arrows.left) (hr : IsClosed ({r} : Set G.arrows.left)) :
    topologicalKrullDim G.arrows.left = ringKrullDim (G.arrows.left.presheaf.stalk r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.equidimensional_arrows
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04LU.** The arrow scheme of a groupoid scheme whose object scheme is
the spectrum of a field is equidimensional, provided both structure morphisms are locally of
finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem equidimensional_arrows {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (e : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType G.source.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.target.left] :
    Equidimensional G.arrows.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_smallEtale_twoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LW.** Let `X` and `Y` be schemes. Two morphisms `a, b : X ⟶ Y` for which there
is a 2-isomorphism `(a_small, a_small^♯) ≅ (b_small, b_small^♯)` in the 2-category of ringed
topoi are equal.

The hypotheses are the data of such a 2-isomorphism: an isomorphism `t` of the direct images,
and the commutation of `t` with the two structure maps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eq_of_smallEtale_twoIso {X Y : B.Scheme} (a b : X ⟶ Y)
    (t : (smallEtaleBaseChange B a).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≅
      (smallEtaleBaseChange B b).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property))
    (hsharp : ∀ (V : SmallEtale B Y.obj Y.property)
        (s : (SmallEtale.commRingStructureSheaf B Y.obj Y.property).obj.obj (op V)),
      (t.hom.app (setStructureSheaf B X.obj X.property)).hom.app (op V)
          ((structureSharp B a).hom.app (op V) s) =
        (structureSharp B b).hom.app (op V) s) :
    a = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_smallEtale_twoIso_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LW**, with the compatibility with the structure maps written as the commuting
triangle of a 2-morphism of ringed topoi: the composite of `a_small^♯` with `t`, evaluated at
the structure sheaf of `X`, is `b_small^♯`, after forgetting the ring structure of the two
structure sheaves, which is what a 2-morphism of topoi acts on.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eq_of_smallEtale_twoIso_comm {X Y : B.Scheme} (a b : X ⟶ Y)
    (t : (smallEtaleBaseChange B a).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≅
      (smallEtaleBaseChange B b).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property))
    (hsharp : (sheafCompose (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
            (forget CommRingCat.{u})).map (structureSharp B a) ≫
          t.hom.app ((sheafCompose (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
            (forget CommRingCat.{u})).obj
            (SmallEtale.commRingStructureSheaf B X.obj X.property)) =
        (sheafCompose (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
          (forget CommRingCat.{u})).map (structureSharp B b)) :
    a = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_smallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LW**, in the 2-category of ringed topoi.  Two morphisms of schemes `a, b : X ⟶ Y`
for which `(a_small, a_small^♯)` and `(b_small, b_small^♯)` are 2-isomorphic are equal.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_smallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoIso (a b : X ⟶ Y)
    (t : RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B a)
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B b)) :
    a = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**The uniqueness half of Stacks 04I6.**  A morphism of ringed topoi between the small étale
ringed topoi of two schemes is 2-isomorphic to `(f_small, f_small^♯)` for at most one morphism
of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_twoIso_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
    (g : RingedToposHom
      (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B X.obj X.property))
      (RingedSite.toRingedTopos (smallEtaleRingedSite B Y.obj Y.property)))
    (a b : X ⟶ Y)
    (ta : RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B a))
    (tb : RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B b)) :
    a = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LY.** For an étale morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces, the spaces-étale
site of `X` is equivalent to the localization of the spaces-étale site of `Y` at the object
`f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spacesEtaleLocalization :
    SpacesEtale B S hS X ≌ Over (etaleObject B S hS f hf)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleLocalization_forget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LY.** Under the localization equivalence an algebraic space étale over `X` is
unchanged, and its structure morphism to `Y` is the composite with `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesEtaleLocalization_forget :
    (spacesEtaleLocalization B S hS f hf).functor ⋙
        Over.forget (etaleObject B S hS f hf) ⋙ SpacesEtale.inclusion B S hS Y =
      SpacesEtale.inclusion B S hS X ⋙ Over.map f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleLocalization_slice
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LY.** The localization equivalence preserves the whole arrow to `X`, not only
its composite with `f`; this is what makes it canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesEtaleLocalization_slice :
    (spacesEtaleLocalization B S hS f hf).functor ⋙
        Over.post (SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS Y) =
      SpacesEtale.inclusion B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleLocalization_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LY.** The localization equivalence carries covering sieves of the spaces-étale
site of `X` to covering sieves of the slice topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesEtaleLocalization_isContinuous :
    (spacesEtaleLocalization B S hS f hf).functor.IsContinuous
      (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X)
      ((SpacesEtale.topology B S hS Y).over (etaleObject B S hS f hf))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleLocalization_inverse_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LY.** The inverse of the localization equivalence carries covering sieves of
the slice topology to covering sieves of the spaces-étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesEtaleLocalization_inverse_isContinuous :
    (spacesEtaleLocalization B S hS f hf).inverse.IsContinuous
      ((SpacesEtale.topology B S hS Y).over (etaleObject B S hS f hf))
      (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleLocalization_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LZ.** For an étale morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces, the structure sheaf
of the spaces-étale site of `X` is the restriction of the structure sheaf of `Y` along the
localization equivalence of Stacks 04LY: `𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y|_{Y_{spaces,étale}/X}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesEtaleLocalization_structureSheaf :
    ((spacesEtaleLocalization B S hS f hf).functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous
          CommRingCat.{u + 1} (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X)
          ((SpacesEtale.topology B S hS Y).over (etaleObject B S hS f hf))).obj
        ((SpacesEtale.structureSheaf B S hS Y).over (etaleObject B S hS f hf)) =
      SpacesEtale.structureSheaf B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleLocalizationRingedHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04LZ.** For an étale morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces, the ringed site
`(X_{spaces,étale}, 𝒪_X)` is the localized ringed site
`(Y_{spaces,étale}/X, 𝒪_Y|_{Y_{spaces,étale}/X})`: the identification of sites of Stacks 04LY
matches the two structure sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spacesEtaleLocalizationRingedHom :
    RingedToposSiteHom (spacesEtaleRingedToposOver B S hS f hf)
      (spacesEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleEquivalenceOverChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04M0.** The small étale site of an étale scheme chart `X → F` is canonically the
localization of the small étale site of `F` at that chart. The equivalence preserves the entire
arrow to `X`, not just the underlying scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleEquivalenceOverChart
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (X : SmallEtale B S hS F) :
    ∃ e : SmallEtale B S hS
        (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F).obj X)) ≌ Over X,
      e.functor.inducedTopology ((SmallEtale.topology B S hS F).over X) =
        SmallEtale.topology B S hS
          (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F).obj X)) ∧
      e.functor ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F =
        SmallEtale.toOver B S hS
          (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F).obj X)) ∧
      e.functor ⋙ Over.post (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ yoneda) =
        SmallEtale.inclusion B S hS
            (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F).obj X)) ⋙
          CostructuredArrow.toOver yoneda
            (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F).obj X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedEquivalenceOverChart
declarations.doc:
The small étale ringed site of an étale scheme chart `X → Y` of an
algebraic space is the localization of the ringed small étale site of `Y` at that chart: the
localization equivalence of Tag 04M0 matches the two structure presheaves, naturally in the
chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleRingedEquivalenceOverChart
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (X : SmallEtale B S hS Y) :
    ∃ e : SmallEtale B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)) ≌ Over X,
      e.functor.inducedTopology ((SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y).over X) =
        SmallEtale.topology B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)) ∧
      (e.functor ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y =
        SmallEtale.toOver B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X))) ∧
      (e.functor.op ⋙ (Over.forget X).op ⋙ structurePresheaf B S hS Y =
        structurePresheaf B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleEquivalenceOverChart
declarations.doc:
The affine étale site of an affine étale chart `X → Y` of an algebraic
space is the localization of the affine étale site of `Y` at that chart, by an equivalence
preserving both the topology and the underlying objects of the big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineEtaleEquivalenceOverChart
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (X : AffineEtale B S hS Y) :
    ∃ e : AffineEtale B S hS (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)) ≌ Over X,
      e.functor.inducedTopology ((AffineEtale.topology B S hS Y).over X) =
        AffineEtale.topology B S hS (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)) ∧
      e.functor ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y =
        AffineEtale.toOver B S hS (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleRingedEquivalenceOverChart
declarations.doc:
The affine étale ringed site of an affine étale chart `X → Y` of an
algebraic space is the localization of the ringed affine étale site of `Y` at that chart: the
equivalence of Tag 04M2 matches the two structure presheaves, naturally under restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineEtaleRingedEquivalenceOverChart
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (X : AffineEtale B S hS Y) :
    ∃ e : AffineEtale B S hS (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)) ≌ Over X,
      e.functor.inducedTopology ((AffineEtale.topology B S hS Y).over X) =
        AffineEtale.topology B S hS (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)) ∧
      (e.functor ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y =
        AffineEtale.toOver B S hS (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X))) ∧
      (e.functor.op ⋙ (Over.forget X).op ⋙ (AffineEtale.inclusion B S hS Y).op ⋙
          structurePresheaf B S hS Y =
        (AffineEtale.inclusion B S hS
          (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X))).op ⋙
          structurePresheaf B S hS
            (yoneda.obj ((AffineEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj X)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleComparisonMap
declarations.doc:
The map `c : U ⟶ V ×_Y X` corresponding to `g`, as an arrow of the spaces-étale site of
`X` from `U` to the cartesian base change of `V` along `f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spacesEtaleComparisonMap (hsq : g ≫ q = p ≫ f) :
    etaleObject B S hS p hp ⟶
      (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.obj (etaleObject B S hS q hq)
declarations.comment: the map `c : U ⟶ V ×_Y X` corresponding to `g`, and nothing else

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtaleRelocalizedTwoIso
declarations.doc:
Via the identifications of Stacks 04LZ for `U ⟶ X` and for `V ⟶ Y`, the morphism of ringed
topoi `(g_{spaces,étale}, g^♯)` is 2-isomorphic to the morphism `(f_{spaces,étale,c}, f_c^♯)` of
Stacks 04J1 built from `(f_{spaces,étale}, f^♯)` and the map `c : U ⟶ V ×_Y X` corresponding to
`g`: the square of ringed topoi whose vertical arrows are the two identifications commutes, up
to an invertible 2-morphism.
declarations.comment:
the two morphisms of ringed topoi are 2-isomorphic, via the identifications of
  04LZ read as the two vertical arrows of a commuting square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartRelocalizedTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04M5.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `U ⟶ X` and
`V ⟶ Y` be étale morphisms from schemes (objects of the small étale sites of `X` and `Y`) and let
`g : U ⟶ V` be a morphism of schemes with `q ∘ g = f ∘ p`. Via the identifications of Stacks 04M1
of the small étale ringed topoi of `U` and `V` with the localizations of those of `X` at `h_U` and
of `Y` at `h_V` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartLocalizationHom`, an equivalence of topoi), the
morphism of small étale ringed topoi `(g_small, g♯)` is 2-isomorphic to the morphism
`(f_{small,s}, f_s♯)` of Stacks 04J8 built from `(f_small, f♯)` and the map
`s : h_U ⟶ f_small⁻¹h_V` corresponding to `g`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartRelocalizationSheafMap`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartRelocalizedTwoIso :
    RingedToposHom.TwoIso (A := 𝒰) (B := 𝒴ᵥ) (chartRelocalizedHom B S hS f U V g hg)
      (chartMorphismHom B S hS U V g)
declarations.comment:
via the identifications of 04M1 at U and V, the morphism (g_small, g^sharp) is
  2-isomorphic to the morphism (f_{small,s}, f_s^sharp) of 04J8 for the map s : h_U -> f^{-1}h_V
  corresponding to g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_smallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04M6.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `X, Y` be algebraic spaces over `S`. Two
morphisms `a, b : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` for which there exists a 2-isomorphism
`(a_small, a^♯) ≅ (b_small, b^♯)` in the 2-category of ringed topoi are equal.

No representability is assumed: the general case is reduced to a scheme source by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_twoIso_of_schemeSource`, where the two morphisms are
automatically representable because the diagonal of an algebraic space is.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_smallEtaleRingedToposHom_twoIso (a b : X ⟶ Y)
    (t : RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u}
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS a) (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS b)) :
    a = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_smallBaseChange_iso_of_twoIso
declarations.doc:
**The étale-chart comparison of Stacks 04M6.** Let `a, b : X ⟶ Y` be two representable
morphisms of algebraic spaces whose morphisms of small étale ringed topoi are 2-isomorphic.
Through the Stacks 03G8 identification of the two direct images with base change of étale scheme
charts, the 2-isomorphism is restriction along an isomorphism `V ×_{Y,b} X ≅ V ×_{Y,a} X` of the
chart base-change functors, natural in the étale chart `V` of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smallBaseChange_iso_of_twoIso {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (a b : X ⟶ Y)
    (ha : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable a.hom) (hb : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable b.hom)
    (t : RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u}
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS a) (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS b)) :
    letI := (smallBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites B S hS a ha).toIsContinuous
    letI := (smallBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites B S hS b hb).toIsContinuous
    ∃ e : smallBaseChange B S hS b hb ≅ smallBaseChange B S hS a ha,
      ∀ (H : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.obj) (Type u))
        (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.obj)
        (x : (((smallBaseChange B S hS a ha).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
          (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.obj)
          (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.obj)).obj H).obj.obj (op V)),
        ((((smallEtaleRingedToposHom_representable B S hS a ha).symm ≪≫ t.e ≪≫
            smallEtaleRingedToposHom_representable B S hS b hb).hom.app H).hom.app (op V)) x =
          H.obj.map (op (e.hom.app V)) x
declarations.comment:
the étale-chart comparison of the proof: for two representable morphisms the
  2-isomorphism of the morphisms of small étale ringed topoi is, through the 03G8 identification
  of the direct images with étale-chart base change, restriction along an isomorphism of the
  chart base-change functors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackTwoArrow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 044S.** The canonical 2-morphism between the source and target maps to a quotient
stack, making the square of Stacks 044R 2-commutative. Its components are the images of the
groupoid arrows.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientStackTwoArrow
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    BasedFunctor.comp (associatedMap C S hS G.source.hom).1.hom
        (quotientStackProjection G) ⟶
      BasedFunctor.comp (associatedMap C S hS G.target.hom).1.hom
        (quotientStackProjection G)
declarations.comment: remark restating the 2-commutative square in the X-for-S_X notation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
The canonical square of the quotient stack is a two-fibre product of
stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientStack_twoFibreProduct
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (quotientStackSquare G)

declarations.name: hasBasis_isConnected_nhds_open_and_isOpen_connectedComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04ME.** Let `X` be a topological space in which every point has a fundamental
system of connected neighbourhoods (locally connected in the sense of Stacks 04MD). Then
(1) every open subset `U` of `X` has the same property, (2) the connected components of `X` are
open, (3) the connected components of an open subset `U` are open (as subsets of `X`), and
(4) every point has a fundamental system of open connected neighbourhoods.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasBasis_isConnected_nhds_open_and_isOpen_connectedComponent
    (h : ∀ x : X, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun s : Set X => s ∈ 𝓝 x ∧ IsConnected s) id) :
    (∀ U : Set X, IsOpen U →
        ∀ x : U, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun s : Set U => s ∈ 𝓝 x ∧ IsConnected s) id) ∧
      (∀ x : X, IsOpen (connectedComponent x)) ∧
      (∀ U : Set X, IsOpen U → ∀ x : U, IsOpen (Subtype.val '' connectedComponent x)) ∧
      ∀ x : X, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun s : Set X => IsOpen s ∧ x ∈ s ∧ IsConnected s) id
declarations.comment:
The complete lemma under the Stacks definition 04MD of local connectedness
(a fundamental system of connected, not necessarily open, neighbourhoods): open subsets are
locally connected, connected components of the space and of its open subsets are open, and
every point has a fundamental system of open connected neighbourhoods.

registrations.name: IsOpen.locallyConnectedSpace
registrations.comment: (1) an open subset of a locally connected space is locally connected

registrations.name: LocallyConnectedSpace.open_connected_basis
registrations.comment: in particular, a fundamental system of open connected neighbourhoods

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.IsLocallyNoetherianSpace.locallyConnectedSpace
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04MF.** A locally Noetherian topological space is locally connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyNoetherianSpace.locallyConnectedSpace
    (α : Type*) [TopologicalSpace α] (hα : IsLocallyNoetherianSpace α) :
    LocallyConnectedSpace α

declarations.name: spec_profinite_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a ring `R` the following are equivalent: `Spec R` is profinite;
`Spec R` is Hausdorff; `Spec R` is totally disconnected; every quasi-compact open of
`Spec R` is closed; there are no nontrivial inclusions between primes of `R`; every prime
of `R` is maximal; every prime of `R` is a minimal prime; every basic open `D(f)` is
closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem spec_profinite_tfae (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    [ -- (1) X is profinite: compact, Hausdorff, and totally disconnected
      CompactSpace (PrimeSpectrum R) ∧ T2Space (PrimeSpectrum R) ∧
        TotallyDisconnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R),
      -- (2) X is Hausdorff
      T2Space (PrimeSpectrum R),
      -- (3) X is totally disconnected
      TotallyDisconnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R),
      -- (4) every quasi-compact open subset of X is closed
      ∀ U : Set (PrimeSpectrum R), IsOpen U → IsCompact U → IsClosed U,
      -- (5) no nontrivial inclusions between prime ideals
      ∀ p q : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → q.IsPrime → p ≤ q → p = q,
      -- (6) every prime ideal is maximal
      ∀ p : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → p.IsMaximal,
      -- (7) every prime ideal is a minimal prime
      ∀ p : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → p ∈ minimalPrimes R,
      -- (8) every standard open D(f) is closed
      ∀ f : R, IsClosed (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ].TFAE

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.exists_isClosed_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_decomposition
declarations.doc:
The base of a finite locally free morphism decomposes as a disjoint union of open and closed
subschemes indexed by the degree, over the `d`-th of which the morphism is finite locally free of
degree `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosed_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_decomposition {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree f] :
    ∃ Z : ℕ → S.Opens, (∀ d, IsClosed (Z d : Set S)) ∧
      (∀ d e, d ≠ e → Disjoint (Z d) (Z e)) ∧ (⨆ d : ℕ, Z d) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ d, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (f ∣_ Z d) d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.integralClosure_globalSections_isField
declarations.doc:
The integral closure of the ground field in the global sections of a
connected reduced scheme over that field is a field.
declarations.statement:
public lemma integralClosure_globalSections_isField
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [ConnectedSpace X] [IsReduced X] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    IsField (integralClosure k Γ(X, ⊤))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.integralClosure_baseField_toSubring_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04MK (Uniqueness of base field).**  Let `X` be a reduced connected
scheme which is locally of finite type over a field `k₁` and also over a field `k₂`.  Then the
integral closure of `k₁` in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and the integral closure of `k₂` in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` are the
same subring of `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.

Each inclusion is `isIntegralElem_of_isIntegralElem`: locally of finite type over a field makes
`X` locally Noetherian, hence covered by quasi-compact connected opens, and on such an open the
two closures agree because Tag 04L7 makes the invertible global functions modulo either closure
finitely generated, which by the Hilbert Nullstellensatz forces each closure to be finite over
their intersection.  A monic polynomial over `k₂` killing a section on one such open then kills it
globally, since its value is everywhere locally zero or a unit — the closures are fields by Tag
04MI — so its nonvanishing locus is clopen and `X` is connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_baseField_toSubring_eq (k₁ k₂ : Type u) [Field k₁] [Field k₂]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (a : X ⟶ Spec (.of k₁)) (b : X ⟶ Spec (.of k₂))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [LocallyOfFiniteType b] [IsReduced X] [ConnectedSpace X] :
    letI : Algebra k₁ Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k₁)).inv ≫ a.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra k₂ Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k₂)).inv ≫ b.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    (integralClosure k₁ Γ(X, ⊤)).toSubring = (integralClosure k₂ Γ(X, ⊤)).toSubring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restrictStabilizerIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04ML.** The stabilizer of a restricted groupoid scheme is canonically
the base change of the original stabilizer.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictStabilizerIso {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    {U' : Scheme.{u}} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects.left) :
    let U'_S : Over S := Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom)
    let g' : U'_S ⟶ G.objects := Over.homMk g
    Over.mk ((stabilizer (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g').groupoid).hom ≫
      eqToHom (congrArg Over.left (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g').objects_eq)) ≅
      Over.mk (pullback.fst g (stabilizer G).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict
declarations.doc: Restriction of a groupoid scheme along a morphism to its scheme of objects.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restrictionSource_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
The source map of a restriction is locally of finite type if the original source map
and the restricting morphism are locally of finite type.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restrictionTarget_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
The target map of a restriction is locally of finite type if the original target map
and the restricting morphism are locally of finite type.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restrictionSource_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
The source map of a restriction is locally of finite presentation if the original source map
and the restricting morphism are locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restrictionSource_locallyOfFinitePresentation {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) {U' : Scheme.{u}} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects.left)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g] :
    let U'_S : Over S := Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom)
    let g' : U'_S ⟶ G.objects := Over.homMk g
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation
      (GroupoidScheme.restrict G g').groupoid.source.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restrictionTarget_locallyOfFinitePresentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04MQ.** The arrow scheme of a groupoid scheme whose object scheme is
the spectrum of a field has the same dimension as its stabilizer group scheme, provided both
structure morphisms are locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_stabilizer
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (e : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.source.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.target.left] :
    topologicalKrullDim G.arrows.left = topologicalKrullDim (stabilizer G).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.groupoid
declarations.doc:
**The groupoid scheme of the warning.**  The restriction of the groupoid scheme of the
multiplicative action of `𝐆_{m,𝐐}` on `𝐀¹_𝐐` to the generic point of `𝐀¹_𝐐`, presented as the
pair groupoid of `Spec 𝐐(x) → Spec 𝐐`: its object scheme is `Spec 𝐐(x)`, the spectrum of a
field, and its arrow scheme is `Spec 𝐐(x) ×_{Spec 𝐐} Spec 𝐐(x)`, whose ring of functions is
the arrow ring `𝐐(x)[Y][1/P(Y)]` of the source.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def groupoid : GroupoidScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℚ))
declarations.comment: the groupoid scheme of the warning, as the pair groupoid of Spec Q(x) over Q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.topologicalKrullDim_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
The stabilizer group scheme has dimension zero: the second projection of its defining
square carries it isomorphically onto `Spec 𝐐(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_stabilizer :
    topologicalKrullDim (stabilizer groupoid).left = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_one
declarations.doc: The arrow scheme has dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_arrows_eq_one :
    topologicalKrullDim groupoid.arrows.left = 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.topologicalKrullDim_arrows_ne_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
**The conclusion of Tag 04MQ fails for this groupoid scheme.**  Its object scheme is the
spectrum of a field, yet the dimension of its arrow scheme is not the dimension of its
stabilizer group scheme: the stabilizer has dimension zero and the arrows have dimension one.
The source and target morphisms are not locally of finite type, which is the hypothesis of
Tag 04MQ that this example drops.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_arrows_ne_stabilizer :
    topologicalKrullDim groupoid.arrows.left
      ≠ topologicalKrullDim (stabilizer groupoid).left
declarations.comment: dim R = 1 ≠ 0 = dim G there, so the conclusion of Tag 04MQ fails for this groupoid scheme; that its source and target are not locally of finite type, which is the hypothesis of Tag 04MQ the example drops, is proved below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.not_locallyOfFiniteType_source
declarations.doc:
**The source of the groupoid scheme is not locally of finite type.**  On rings it is the
inclusion of `𝐐(x)` into `𝐐(x) ⊗_𝐐 𝐐(x)` as the right factor, which is not of finite type.
declarations.statement: theorem not_locallyOfFiniteType_source : ¬ LocallyOfFiniteType groupoid.source.left
declarations.comment: s is not locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.not_locallyOfFiniteType_target
declarations.doc:
**The target of the groupoid scheme is not locally of finite type.**  On rings it is the
inclusion of `𝐐(x)` into `𝐐(x) ⊗_𝐐 𝐐(x)` as the left factor, which is not of finite type.
declarations.statement: theorem not_locallyOfFiniteType_target : ¬ LocallyOfFiniteType groupoid.target.left
declarations.comment: t is not locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.exists_dim_arrows_eq_one_dim_stabilizer_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The example of Tag 04MR, in full.**  There is a groupoid scheme whose object scheme is
the spectrum of a field — here `𝐐(x)` — whose arrow scheme is `Spec (𝐐(x)[y][1/P(xy)])`, whose
source and target morphisms are not locally of finite type, and for which the dimension of the
arrow scheme is one while the dimension of the stabilizer group scheme is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dim_arrows_eq_one_dim_stabilizer_eq_zero :
    ∃ (k : Type) (_ : Field k) (G : GroupoidScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℚ))),
      G.objects.left = Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ∧
        Nonempty (G.arrows.left ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of sourceArrowRing)) ∧
        ¬ LocallyOfFiniteType G.source.left ∧
        ¬ LocallyOfFiniteType G.target.left ∧
        topologicalKrullDim G.arrows.left = 1 ∧
        topologicalKrullDim (stabilizer G).left = 0
declarations.comment: the example in full: U = Spec Q(x) with Q(x) a field, R = Spec (Q(x)[y][1/P(xy)]), s and t are not locally of finite type, dim R = 1 and dim G = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalFunctionPairGroupoid.not_forall_dim_arrows_eq_dim_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
**The warning of Tag 04MR.**  Tag 04MQ is wrong without the condition that `s` and `t` are
locally of finite type: for a groupoid scheme whose object scheme is the spectrum of a field,
the dimension of the arrow scheme need not be the dimension of the stabilizer group scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_dim_arrows_eq_dim_stabilizer :
    ¬ ∀ (S : Scheme.{0}) (G : GroupoidScheme S) (k : Type) (_ : Field k),
        G.objects.left = Spec (CommRingCat.of k) →
          topologicalKrullDim G.arrows.left = topologicalKrullDim (stabilizer G).left
declarations.comment: Tag 04MQ is wrong without the condition that s and t are locally of finite type

**Stacks Project, Tag 04MW.** Restricting a groupoid scheme successively

the comparison arrow is given by composing the second arrow with the inverse of

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restrictionSource_mem_of_composite
declarations.doc:
A property of the source map over a composite restriction descends to the
source map over the second restriction when the original target map covers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restrictionSource_mem_of_composite {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    {U' U'' : Over S} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) (g' : U'' ⟶ U')
    (K : Precoverage Scheme.{u}) [K.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget K]
    (ht : Presieve.singleton G.target.left ∈ K G.objects.left)
    (hP : P ((pullback.snd (g' ≫ g) G.target ≫ G.source).left)) :
    P ((pullback.snd g' (restrictionTarget G g) ≫ restrictionSource G g).left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.descent_to_open_image
declarations.doc:
A morphism property local on the target descends from the source map of a
restriction to the source map after a further restriction, viewed over the
open image of the first source map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem descent_to_open_image {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    {U' U'' : Over S} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) (g' : U'' ⟶ U')
    (K : Precoverage Scheme.{u}) (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [P.IsLocalAtTarget K]
    (V : G.objects.left.Opens)
    (hV : (firstArrowSource G g).left ⟶ V.toScheme)
    (hV_fac : hV ≫ V.ι = (firstSourceMap G g).left)
    (_hV_range : Set.range (firstSourceMap G g).left = (V : Set G.objects.left))
    (hV_cover : Presieve.singleton hV ∈ K V.toScheme)
    (hP : P (secondSourceMap G g g').left) :
    ∃ hV' : (compositeArrowSource G g g').left ⟶ V.toScheme,
      hV' ≫ V.ι = (compositeSourceMap G g g').left ∧ P hV'

declarations.doc:

locally closed subscheme of its arrow scheme.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_slice_dim_eq_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04MZ.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` be a groupoid scheme whose source
and target maps are Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation, and let `u` be a finite
type point of `U`. Then there are an affine scheme `U'` and a morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` which is an
immersion through `u` and locally of finite presentation, such that `h : U' ×_{g,U,t} R ⟶ U`
and the source and target maps of the restricted groupoid are again Cohen--Macaulay and locally
of finite presentation, and the restricted source fibre `F'_u` has at the identity arrow exactly
the dimension of the restricted stabilizer fibre `G'_u`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affine_slice_dim_eq_stabilizer {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) (u : G.objects.left)
    (hu : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left]
    (hs : ∃ hf : ∀ y : G.objects.left,
      IsLocallyNoetherian (G.source.left.fiber y),
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay G.source.left hf)
    (_ht : ∃ hf : ∀ y : G.objects.left,
      IsLocallyNoetherian (G.target.left.fiber y),
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay G.target.left hf) :
    ∃ (U' : Over S) (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) (u' : U'.left)
      (hgu : g.left u' = u),
      let D : SliceSituation :=
        { S := S, groupoid := G, U' := U', g := g,
          u := u, u' := u', mapsTo := hgu }
      IsAffine U'.left ∧
      IsImmersion g.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation g.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.sourceMap.left ∧
      (∃ hf : ∀ y : G.objects.left,
        IsLocallyNoetherian (D.sourceMap.left.fiber y),
        Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay D.sourceMap.left hf) ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.restrictedGroupoid.source.left ∧
      (∃ hf : ∀ y : D.restrictedGroupoid.objects.left,
        IsLocallyNoetherian (D.restrictedGroupoid.source.left.fiber y),
        Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay D.restrictedGroupoid.source.left hf) ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.restrictedGroupoid.target.left ∧
      (∃ hf : ∀ y : D.restrictedGroupoid.objects.left,
        IsLocallyNoetherian (D.restrictedGroupoid.target.left.fiber y),
        Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay D.restrictedGroupoid.target.left hf) ∧
      topologicalKrullDimAt D.restrictedSourceFiber
          D.sliceIdentityPoints.restrictedSourceIdentity =
        topologicalKrullDim D.restrictedStabilizerFiber

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_slice_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04N0.** A finite type point of a groupoid scheme whose source and
target maps are Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation and whose stabilizer group
scheme is locally quasi-finite has an affine slice `g : U' ⟶ U`, an immersion locally of finite
presentation, for which `h : U' ×_{g, U, t} R ⟶ U` and the source and target maps of the
restricted groupoid are flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affine_slice_locallyQuasiFinite {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) (u : G.objects.left)
    (hu : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left]
    (hs : ∃ hf : ∀ y : G.objects.left, IsLocallyNoetherian (G.source.left.fiber y),
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay G.source.left hf)
    (ht : ∃ hf : ∀ y : G.objects.left, IsLocallyNoetherian (G.target.left.fiber y),
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay G.target.left hf)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite (stabilizer G).hom] :
    ∃ (U' : Scheme.{u}) (g : U' ⟶ G.objects.left) (u' : U'),
      g u' = u ∧ IsAffine U' ∧ IsImmersion g ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g ∧
      Flat (pullback.snd g G.target.left ≫ G.source.left) ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation (pullback.snd g G.target.left ≫ G.source.left) ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite (pullback.snd g G.target.left ≫ G.source.left) ∧
      Flat (GroupoidScheme.restrict G
        (Over.homMk g : Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects)).groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation (GroupoidScheme.restrict G
        (Over.homMk g : Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects)).groupoid.source.left ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite (GroupoidScheme.restrict G
        (Over.homMk g : Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects)).groupoid.source.left ∧
      Flat (GroupoidScheme.restrict G
        (Over.homMk g : Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects)).groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation (GroupoidScheme.restrict G
        (Over.homMk g : Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects)).groupoid.target.left ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite (GroupoidScheme.restrict G
        (Over.homMk g : Over.mk (g ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects)).groupoid.target.left
declarations.comment: conclusions (1)-(5) with the fibre products of schemes: `g` an affine immersion locally of finite presentation, `h`, `s'`, `t'` flat, locally finitely presented, quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_slice_locallyQuasiFinite_of_isFiniteTypePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04N0.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` be a groupoid scheme with `s` and
`t` Cohen-Macaulay and locally of finite presentation, let `u` be a finite type point of `U`,
and assume the stabilizer group scheme is locally quasi-finite.  Then there are an affine scheme
`U'` and a morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` such that `g` is an immersion, `u` lies in `U'`, `g` is locally
of finite presentation, the morphism `h : U' ×_{g, U, t} R ⟶ U` is flat, locally of finite
presentation and locally quasi-finite, and the structure maps `s', t' : R' ⟶ U'` of the
restricted groupoid are flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affine_slice_locallyQuasiFinite_of_isFiniteTypePoint {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) (u : G.objects.left)
    (hu : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left]
    (hs : ∃ hf : ∀ y : G.objects.left, IsLocallyNoetherian (G.source.left.fiber y),
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay G.source.left hf)
    (ht : ∃ hf : ∀ y : G.objects.left, IsLocallyNoetherian (G.target.left.fiber y),
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay G.target.left hf)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite (stabilizer G).hom] :
    ∃ (U' : Over S) (g : U' ⟶ G.objects) (u' : U'.left) (hgu : g.left u' = u),
      let D : SliceSituation :=
        { S := S, groupoid := G, U' := U', g := g, u := u, u' := u', mapsTo := hgu }
      IsAffine U'.left ∧ IsImmersion g.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g.left ∧
        (Flat D.sourceMap.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.sourceMap.left ∧
          LocallyQuasiFinite D.sourceMap.left) ∧
        (Flat D.restrictedGroupoid.source.left ∧
          LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.restrictedGroupoid.source.left ∧
          LocallyQuasiFinite D.restrictedGroupoid.source.left) ∧
        (Flat D.restrictedGroupoid.target.left ∧
          LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.restrictedGroupoid.target.left ∧
          LocallyQuasiFinite D.restrictedGroupoid.target.left)
declarations.comment: conclusions (1)-(5): an affine immersion locally of finite presentation whose `h`, `s'` and `t'` are flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite
