declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_etale_chart_iff_exists_etale_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04N2, conditions (1) and (2).** An étale-local property of germs of schemes
holds at every étale scheme chart over a point of an algebraic space exactly when it holds at
some such chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_etale_chart_iff_exists_etale_chart (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F)
    (P : GermOfScheme.{u} → Prop) (hP : GermOfScheme.IsEtaleLocal P) :
    (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a →
      ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) a (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) = x →
        P ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U, schemePoint B S hS U p⟩) ↔
    (∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) a (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) = x ∧
        P ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U, schemePoint B S hS U p⟩)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_etale_chart_iff_of_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04N2, the representable case.** For a represented algebraic space the
every-chart condition is the property of the germ of its representing scheme at the
corresponding scheme point.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_etale_chart_iff_of_representable (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (X : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : yoneda.obj X ≅ F) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj X))
    (P : GermOfScheme.{u} → Prop) (hP : GermOfScheme.IsEtaleLocal P) :
    (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a →
      ∀ q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) a (q.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) =
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X) e.hom (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj X)) →
        P ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U, schemePoint B S hS U q⟩) ↔
      P ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X, schemePoint B S hS X p⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etale_chart_iff_of_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04N2, the representable case.** For a represented algebraic space the one-chart
condition is the property of the germ of its representing scheme at the corresponding scheme
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_chart_iff_of_representable (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (X : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : yoneda.obj X ≅ F) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj X))
    (P : GermOfScheme.{u} → Prop) (hP : GermOfScheme.IsEtaleLocal P) :
    (∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      ∃ q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) a (q.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) =
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X) e.hom (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj X)) ∧
        P ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U, schemePoint B S hS U q⟩) ↔
      P ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X, schemePoint B S hS X p⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_eq_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04N4.** An étale morphism preserves the local Krull dimension at
corresponding points.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_eq_of_etale
    {U V : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V) [Etale f] (u : U) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt U u = topologicalKrullDimAt V (f u)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimensionAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04N5.** The dimension of an algebraic space at one of its points: the infimum of
the local dimensions of the étale scheme charts at a point above it. By
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimensionAtPoint_eq_of_etale_chart` every one of those local
dimensions equals this infimum.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dimensionAtPoint (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : points B S hS F) : WithBot ℕ∞

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etale_chart_at_point
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04N5.** Every point of an algebraic space has an étale scheme chart above it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_chart_at_point (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a ∧
      ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U),
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) a (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) = x
declarations.comment: existence of a chart at the point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimensionAtPoint_eq_of_etale_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04N5.** The dimension of an algebraic space at a point equals the local
dimension of every étale scheme chart at a point above it; this is the property the source
uses to define the dimension at a point.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimensionAtPoint_eq_of_etale_chart (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F) (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F)
    (ha : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) a)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U))
    (hp : pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) a (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) = x) :
    dimensionAtPoint B S hS F hF x =
      topologicalKrullDimAt ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
        (schemePoint B S hS U p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04N6.** The dimension of an algebraic space: the supremum of its dimensions at
its points.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev dimension (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) : WithBot ℕ∞

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04N8.** An étale morphism preserves the Krull dimension of local
rings at corresponding points.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_of_etale {U V : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V) [Etale f] (u : U) :
    ringKrullDim (U.presheaf.stalk u) = ringKrullDim (V.presheaf.stalk (f u))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04N9.** For a point `x` of an algebraic space and `d` in `ℕ∞`, the dimension of
the local ring of the space at `x` is `d` exactly when the stalk at some geometric point
above `x` has Krull dimension `d`, and exactly when the stalk at every geometric point above
`x` does.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_eq_tfae (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : points B S hS F) (d : ℕ∞) :
    List.TFAE
      [localRingDimension B S hS x = d,
        ∃ xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS F, xbar.LiesOver x ∧
          ringKrullDim (etaleLocalRing B S hS F xbar) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞),
        ∀ xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS F, xbar.LiesOver x →
          ringKrullDim (etaleLocalRing B S hS F xbar) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NA.** The Krull dimension of the local ring of an algebraic space at a point,
measured on an étale scheme chart at a point above it.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_iff_hasChartLocalRingDimension` exactly one
value is realized by such a chart, and it is this infimum.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def localRingDimension (x : points B S hS F) : ℕ∞

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_iff_hasChartLocalRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NA.** The dimension of the local ring of an algebraic space at a point is the
value measured on any étale scheme chart at a point above it.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_eq_iff_hasChartLocalRingDimension (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : points B S hS F) (d : ℕ∞) :
    localRingDimension B S hS x = d ↔ HasChartLocalRingDimension B S hS x d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfGerms.IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
A property of morphisms of germs of schemes is étale local on the source and target if it
is invariant under commutative squares with étale vertical arrows.
declarations.statement:
structure MorphismOfGerms.IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget
    (Q : ∀ {X Y : GermOfScheme.{u}}, MorphismOfGerms X Y → Prop) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChartAtPoint_iff_some
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NC, equivalence of conditions (1) and (2).** An étale-local property of germ
morphisms holds in every pointed chart if and only if it holds in one pointed chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem holdsOnEveryEtaleChartAtPoint_iff_some
    (Q : ∀ {X Y : GermOfScheme.{u}}, MorphismOfGerms X Y → Prop)
    (hQ : MorphismOfGerms.IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget Q)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (f : F ⟶ G) (x : points B S hS F) :
    HoldsOnEveryEtaleChartAtPoint B S hS Q f x ↔
      HoldsOnSomeEtaleChartAtPoint B S hS Q f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChartAtPoint_iff_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NC, representable source and target.** For representable algebraic spaces the
chart condition is the property of the induced morphism of scheme germs at the corresponding
scheme point.
declarations.statement:
theorem holdsOnEveryEtaleChartAtPoint_iff_representable
    (Q : ∀ {X Y : GermOfScheme.{u}}, MorphismOfGerms X Y → Prop)
    (hQ : MorphismOfGerms.IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget Q)
    [F.IsRepresentable] [G.IsRepresentable] (f : F ⟶ G) (x : points B S hS F)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj F.reprX)) (t : Spec (.of p.carrier))
    (hx : pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj F.reprX) F.reprW.hom
      (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj F.reprX)) = x) :
    HoldsOnEveryEtaleChartAtPoint B S hS Q f x ↔
      Q (MorphismOfGerms.ofSchemeHom
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
          (yoneda.preimage (F.reprW.hom ≫ f ≫ G.reprW.inv)))
        (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p.value) t))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfGerms.isEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget_isFlat
declarations.doc:
Flatness of the map on local rings of a morphism of germs is étale local on
both source and target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget_isFlat :
    IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget (@IsFlat.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_etaleLocalRingMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NG.** A morphism `f` of algebraic spaces over `S` induces at a geometric point
`x` of its source a unique homomorphism of étale local rings
`𝒪_{G, f ∘ x} ⟶ 𝒪_{F, x}` compatible with the germ maps in every commuting diagram of pointed
étale scheme charts over `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_etaleLocalRingMap (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (f : F ⟶ G)
    (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) :
    ∃! φ : etaleLocalRing B S hS G (geometricPointMap f x) →+* etaleLocalRing B S hS F x,
      IsEtaleLocalRingMap f x φ
declarations.comment: the canonical homomorphism of étale local rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatAt_iff_etaleLocalRingMap_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NG.** A morphism `f` of algebraic spaces over `S` is flat at the image of a
geometric point `x` of its source exactly when the canonical homomorphism of étale local rings
`𝒪_{G, f ∘ x} ⟶ 𝒪_{F, x}` is flat.

For a point `x₀` of `F` with `x.LiesOver x₀` the statement for `x₀` follows by rewriting along
that equality.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatAt_iff_etaleLocalRingMap_flat (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) :
    IsFlatAt B S hS f x.image ↔ (etaleLocalRingMap hF f x).Flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_fiberMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04NI.** The morphism between corresponding fibres in
a commutative square with étale vertical arrows is étale.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLocalRingDimension_isEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
The dimension of the local ring of the fibre of a morphism of germs at its distinguished
point is étale local on the source and target germs.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MorphismOfGerms.residueFieldTranscendenceDegree_isEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04NK.** Residue-field transcendence degree at a
point is étale local on the source and target of a morphism of germs.
declarations.statement:
public theorem residueFieldTranscendenceDegree_isEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget
    (r : ℕ∞) :
    IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget
      (@HasResidueFieldTranscendenceDegree.{u} r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fiberDimensionAt_isEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04NL.** Dimension at a point of a fibre is étale
local on the source and target of a morphism of germs.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fiberDimensionAt_isEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget (d : ℕ∞) :
    MorphismOfGerms.IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget (@HasFiberDimensionAt.{u} d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFiberLocalRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NM, dimension of the local ring of a fibre.** The local ring of the fibre of
`f` has dimension `d` at `x`, tested on every étale chart at `x`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasFiberLocalRingDimension (d : ℕ∞) (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (_hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (f : F ⟶ G) (x : points B S hS F) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasRelativeDimensionAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NM, relative dimension at a point.** A morphism of algebraic spaces has
relative dimension `d` at `x` if its fibre has dimension `d` at the corresponding point in
every étale chart.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasTranscendenceDegreeAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NM, transcendence degree at a point.** The transcendence degree of `x` over
its image under `f` is `r`. For algebraic spaces this is equivalently tested on one or every
étale scheme chart at `x`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasTranscendenceDegreeAt (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G) (x : points B S hS F) (r : ℕ∞) :
    Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasBasis_nhds_isOpen_isCompact
declarations.doc:
The quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of a point of an algebraic space over `S` are a
fundamental system of neighbourhoods of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasBasis_nhds_isOpen_isCompact (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F) :
    (nhds x).HasBasis
      (fun W : Set (points B S hS F) ↦ IsOpen W ∧ IsCompact W ∧ x ∈ W) id
declarations.comment: fundamental system of open quasi-compact neighbourhoods

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyCompactSpace
declarations.doc: The space of points of an algebraic space over `S` is locally quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyCompactSpace (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) : LocallyCompactSpace (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeDimensionAt_eq_fiberLocalRingDimension_add_transcendenceDegreeAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NQ.** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
type, the relative dimension at a point is the dimension of the local ring of the fibre there
plus the transcendence degree of the point over its image.

The three invariants of Stacks 04NM are chart conditions, so all three are read off one pointed
étale chart at the point (Stacks 04NC); on the resulting morphism of schemes the identity is
the dimension formula of Stacks 02FX.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimensionAt_eq_fiberLocalRingDimension_add_transcendenceDegreeAt
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (f : F ⟶ G) (x : points B S hS F) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (d e r : ℕ∞) (hd : HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x)
    (he : HasFiberLocalRingDimension e B S hS hF hG f x)
    (hr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x r) : d = e + r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_comp
declarations.doc:
**Additivity of the transcendence degree at a point**, part (3) of Stacks 04NR. For
composable morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` of algebraic spaces over `S` and a point `x`
of `X`, the transcendence degree of `x` over its image under `f ≫ g` is the sum of the
transcendence degree of `x` over `f x` and of `f x` over `g (f x)`.

Compatible étale charts for the composite
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_compatible_etale_charts_comp`) read all three transcendence
degrees on a single commuting pair of chart morphisms `α` and `β` of the site; on the resulting
morphisms of schemes the three residue fields form a tower and the transcendence degree of a
tower is additive.

The source assumes `f` and `g` locally of finite type; that is not needed, neither for the
chart comparison nor for the tower identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_comp {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : points B S hS X)
    (r s : ℕ∞) (hr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x r)
    (hs : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS g (pointsMap B S hS X f x) s) :
    HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS (f ≫ g) x (r + s)
declarations.comment: part (3): additivity of the transcendence degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_le_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NR, part (1).** For composable morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which are
locally of finite type, the relative dimension of the composite at a point is at most the sum of
the relative dimension of the first morphism there and of the second morphism at the image
point.

Compatible étale charts for the composite read all three relative dimensions as fibre
dimensions of a pair of composable morphisms of schemes at one point, where the inequality is
part of Stacks 02JS.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_le_add {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (d e n : ℕ∞)
    (hd : HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x)
    (he : HasRelativeDimensionAt e B S hS g (pointsMap B S hS X f x))
    (hn : HasRelativeDimensionAt n B S hS (f ≫ g) x) : n ≤ d + e
declarations.comment: part (1): the relative dimension of a composite is at most the sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_le_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NR, part (1).** The composite of two morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which
are locally of finite type has a relative dimension at every point of its source, and that
dimension is at most the sum of the relative dimensions of the two factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_le_add {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (d e : ℕ∞)
    (hd : HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x)
    (he : HasRelativeDimensionAt e B S hS g (pointsMap B S hS X f x)) :
    ∃ n : ℕ∞, HasRelativeDimensionAt n B S hS (f ≫ g) x ∧ n ≤ d + e
declarations.comment: part (1): the relative dimension of a composite is at most the sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NR, part (2), special case.** The inequality of part (1) is an equality as soon as
the first morphism is flat at the point.

On compatible étale charts for the composite this is the corresponding part of Stacks 02JS,
flatness of `f` at `x` becoming flatness of the first chart morphism at the selected scheme
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_of_isFlatAt {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (d e : ℕ∞)
    (hd : HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x)
    (he : HasRelativeDimensionAt e B S hS g (pointsMap B S hS X f x))
    (hflat : IsFlatAt B S hS f x) :
    HasRelativeDimensionAt (d + e) B S hS (f ≫ g) x
declarations.comment: part (2): equality when the first morphism is flat at the point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_of_isFlatAt_fibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NR, part (2).** The inequality of part (1) is an equality as soon as the morphism
of field-valued fibres over the image point is flat at a point above `x`: here `Xk` and `Yk` are
the fibres of `X` and `Y` over a field-valued representative `p` of the image of `x` in `Z`,
presented by the two cartesian squares, `x'` is a point of `Xk` above `x`, and `Xk ⟶ Yk` is flat
at `x'`.

Relative dimension is invariant under base change (part (1) of Stacks 04NS), so all three
relative dimensions may be read on the fibres over `p`, where the first morphism is flat at the
chosen point and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_of_isFlatAt` applies. The
fibres are algebraic because they are fibre products of algebraic spaces (Stacks 02X2), and the
two morphisms between them are locally of finite type because being so is stable under base
change (Stacks 03XH).

No chosen fibre-product objects are imposed: the two squares are cartesian squares of arbitrary
presheaves, which is why neither fibre is assumed algebraic.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeDimensionAt_comp_of_isFlatAt_fibre
    {X Y Z Xk Yk : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (d e : ℕ∞)
    (hd : HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x)
    (he : HasRelativeDimensionAt e B S hS g (pointsMap B S hS X f x))
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z) (px : Xk ⟶ X) (py : Yk ⟶ Y)
    (qy : Yk ⟶ yoneda.obj (p.siteObject B S hS Z)) (fk : Xk ⟶ Yk) (x' : points B S hS Xk)
    (hpx : IsPullback px fk f py)
    (hpy : IsPullback py qy g (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value))
    (hx : pointsMap B S hS Xk px x' = x) (hflat : IsFlatAt B S hS fk x') :
    HasRelativeDimensionAt (d + e) B S hS (f ≫ g) x
declarations.comment: part (2): equality when the morphism of field-valued fibres is flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeDimensionAt_iff_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Invariance of relative dimension under base change**, part (1) of Stacks 04NS. In a
cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f` is locally of
finite type, the relative dimension of the base change `f'` at a point `x'` of its source is
the relative dimension of `f` at the image of `x'`.

Read on the compatible pointed charts of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleChartAtPoint_pair_of_isPullback`, each side is the
dimension of the fibre of a morphism of schemes at corresponding points of a cartesian square,
which is part (1) of Stacks 02FY.

The source assumes all four corners of the square algebraic; the fourth corner `X'` need not
be, because the two chart conditions are compared on charts supplied as data rather than on
charts produced from an atlas.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeDimensionAt_iff_of_isPullback {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y')
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x' : points B S hS X') (d : ℕ∞) :
    HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x') ↔
      HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f' x'
declarations.comment: part (1): invariance of the relative dimension under base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_fiberLocalRingDimension_add_eq_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks 04NS.** In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right
vertical arrow `f` is locally of finite type, the dimension gained by the local ring of the
fibre at a point `x'` of the source of the base change, over its value for `f` at the image of
`x'`, is the transcendence degree lost there; in particular the common difference is
nonnegative, which is why it is recorded as a summand `n` rather than as a difference.

The transcendence degrees are compared on the compatible pointed charts of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleChartAtPoint_pair_of_isPullback`, where the drop is part
(2) of Stacks 02FY for the resulting cartesian square of schemes; the sum of the two invariants
is the relative dimension (Stacks 04NQ) and so agrees on the two sides by part (1) of Stacks
04NS, which turns that drop into the gain of the other invariant. The transcendence degree at
`x'` is finite, so it cancels.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fiberLocalRingDimension_add_eq_of_isPullback
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x' : points B S hS X') (e r e' r' : ℕ∞)
    (he : HasFiberLocalRingDimension e B S hS hX hY f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x'))
    (hr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x') r)
    (he' : HasFiberLocalRingDimension e' B S hS hX' hY' f' x')
    (hr' : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f' x' r') :
    ∃ n : ℕ∞, e + n = e' ∧ r' + n = r
declarations.comment: part (2): the gain in the dimension of the local ring of the fibre is the loss in transcendence degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fiberLocalRingDimension_le_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks 04NS.** Base change does not decrease the dimension of the local ring
of the fibre at a point.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberLocalRingDimension_le_of_isPullback
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x' : points B S hS X') (e r e' r' : ℕ∞)
    (he : HasFiberLocalRingDimension e B S hS hX hY f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x'))
    (hr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x') r)
    (he' : HasFiberLocalRingDimension e' B S hS hX' hY' f' x')
    (hr' : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f' x' r') : e ≤ e'
declarations.comment: part (2): the dimension of the local ring of the fibre does not decrease

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.transcendenceDegreeAt_le_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks 04NS.** Base change does not increase the transcendence degree of a
point over its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem transcendenceDegreeAt_le_of_isPullback
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x' : points B S hS X') (e r e' r' : ℕ∞)
    (he : HasFiberLocalRingDimension e B S hS hX hY f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x'))
    (hr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x') r)
    (he' : HasFiberLocalRingDimension e' B S hS hX' hY' f' x')
    (hr' : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f' x' r') : r' ≤ r
declarations.comment: part (2): the transcendence degree does not increase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_point_preserving_fiberLocalRingDimension_and_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of Stacks 04NS.** In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right
vertical arrow `f` is locally of finite type, a point `x` of `X` and a point `y'` of `Y'` with
the same image in `Y` have a common lift `x'` to `X'` at which the dimension of the local ring
of the fibre and the transcendence degree both take the value they take at `x` — that is, at
which the common difference of part (2) vanishes.

Some common lift exists because the point set of a fibre product surjects onto the fibre product
of the point sets (Stacks 03H4). On the compatible pointed charts at such a lift
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleChartAtPoint_pair_of_isPullback`) part (3) of Stacks 02FY
replaces the scheme point selected by the chart of the base change by one lying over the same
two points at which both invariants are preserved; the same chart with that point as its
representative is a pointed chart at its image in `X'`, and that image is the required lift,
because the two source charts commute with the horizontal arrow of the square.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_point_preserving_fiberLocalRingDimension_and_trdeg
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x : points B S hS X) (y' : points B S hS Y')
    (hxy : pointsMap B S hS X f x = pointsMap B S hS Y' g y') :
    ∃ x' : points B S hS X', pointsMap B S hS X' g' x' = x ∧
      pointsMap B S hS X' f' x' = y' ∧
      (∀ d : ℕ∞, HasFiberLocalRingDimension d B S hS hX hY f x ↔
        HasFiberLocalRingDimension d B S hS hX' hY' f' x') ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ∞, HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x r ↔
        HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f' x' r)
declarations.comment: part (3): a common lift at which both invariants are preserved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeDimensionAt_iff_of_isPullback'
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` with `f` locally of finite type, the
relative dimension of the base change of `f` at a point of its source is the relative dimension of
`f` at the image of that point.

The square is the one with `p` over `f` and `q` over `g`, so `p : W ⟶ Z` is the base change of
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `q : W ⟶ X` is the projection. Only `X`, `Y` and `Z` are assumed to be algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeDimensionAt_iff_of_isPullback' (d : ℕ∞)
    {W X Z Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (x' : points B S hS W) :
    HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS p x' ↔
      HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f (pointsMap B S hS W q x')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_hasRelativeDimensionAt_le
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type, the set of
points of the source at which the relative dimension is at most `n` is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_hasRelativeDimensionAt_le (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (n : ℕ) :
    IsOpen {x : points B S hS F |
      ∃ d : ℕ∞, d ≤ (n : ℕ∞) ∧ HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRetrocompact_setOf_exists_hasRelativeDimensionAt_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NU.** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
presentation and a natural number `n`, the open set of Stacks 04NT — the points of the source
at which the relative dimension is at most `n` — is retrocompact in the point space of Tag
03BU.

As for Stacks 04NT, a surjective étale chart `a` of the source lifted from an atlas of the
target reads the locus, point by point, as the bounded-fibre-dimension locus `Wₙ` of the
induced morphism of schemes, which is retrocompact by Stacks 02G0. Points of a represented
presheaf are homeomorphic to points of the representing scheme (Tag 03BX), so the preimage of
the locus under `|a|` is retrocompact; transporting that to the locus itself uses that `|a|` is
a continuous open surjection: a compact open `K` of the target is covered by the images of the
preimages of finitely many affine opens of the chart contained in the open `|a| ⁻¹' K`, and on
each of them the intersection with the locus is the image of a compact set.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRetrocompact_setOf_exists_hasRelativeDimensionAt_le (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) (n : ℕ) :
    IsRetrocompact {x : points B S hS F |
      ∃ d : ℕ∞, d ≤ (n : ℕ∞) ∧ HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff_forall_hasRelativeDimensionAt_zero
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : F ⟶ G` of presheaves over `S` on the big fppf site which is locally of finite
type is locally quasi-finite exactly when it has relative dimension `0` at every point of its
source. In particular this holds for a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff_forall_hasRelativeDimensionAt_zero (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f ↔
      ∀ x : points B S hS F, HasRelativeDimensionAt 0 B S hS f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NW, the canonical open subspace.** The open subspace of the source of a morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type cut out by the points of relative
dimension `0`; it is an open subspace by Stacks 04NT and Stacks 03BZ.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_range_pointsMap_locallyQuasiFinitePart_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NW, the points of the canonical open subspace.** A point of the source lies in
the point set of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart` exactly when the relative
dimension there is `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_range_pointsMap_locallyQuasiFinitePart_iff (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (x : points B S hS F) :
    x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hF hG f hf).1.toFunctor
        (locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hF hG f hf).1.ι) ↔
      HasRelativeDimensionAt 0 B S hS f x
declarations.comment: the points of the canonical open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_locallyQuasiFinitePart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NW, local quasi-finiteness of the restriction.** The restriction of the morphism
to `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart` is locally quasi-finite.

Every point of the open subspace has relative dimension `0` for the restricted morphism,
because relative dimension is unchanged by restricting the source to an open subspace, so this
is Stacks 04NV for the restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_locallyQuasiFinitePart (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS ((locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hF hG f hf).1.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_one_le_hasRelativeDimensionAt_of_not_mem_locallyQuasiFinitePart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NW, positive relative dimension outside the canonical open subspace.** At a point
of the source which is not in the point set of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart` the relative dimension is at least `1`: a
relative dimension exists there, and were it `0` the point would lie in that point set.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_one_le_hasRelativeDimensionAt_of_not_mem_locallyQuasiFinitePart
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x : points B S hS F)
    (hx : x ∉ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS
      (locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hF hG f hf).1.toFunctor
      (locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hF hG f hf).1.ι)) :
    ∃ d : ℕ∞, 1 ≤ d ∧ HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x
declarations.comment: positive relative dimension outside the canonical open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.le_locallyQuasiFinitePart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NW, maximality.** Every open subspace of the source over which the morphism is
locally quasi-finite is contained in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart`; together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_locallyQuasiFinitePart` this is what makes it
canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_locallyQuasiFinitePart (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (U : {U : Subfunctor F // IsOpenSubspace B S hS U})
    (hU : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (U.1.ι ≫ f)) :
    U ≤ locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hF hG f hf
declarations.comment: maximality of the canonical open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NW, compatibility with arbitrary base change.** In a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow is locally of finite type, the base change
is locally of finite type and its locally quasi-finite part is the inverse image of the locally
quasi-finite part of the morphism.

On points both sides are the relative-dimension-zero locus, and relative dimension at a point
is invariant under base change by part (1) of Stacks 04NS.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinitePart_preimage_of_isPullback
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    ∃ hf' : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f',
      (locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hX' hY' f' hf').1 =
        (locallyQuasiFinitePart B S hS hX hY f hf).1.preimage g'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_relativeDimensionZeroLocus
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type, the locus where
the relative dimension is zero is an open subspace of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_relativeDimensionZeroLocus (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (relativeDimensionZeroLocus B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeDimensionZeroLocus
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type is locally
quasi-finite on the open subspace of its source where its relative dimension is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeDimensionZeroLocus (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS ((relativeDimensionZeroLocus B S hS f).ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.one_le_of_hasRelativeDimensionAt_of_notMem_relativeDimensionZeroLocus
declarations.doc:
At a point of the source which is not in the relative-dimension-zero locus, every value of
the relative dimension of the morphism is at least `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_le_of_hasRelativeDimensionAt_of_notMem_relativeDimensionZeroLocus (f : F ⟶ G)
    (x : points B S hS F)
    (hx : x ∉ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (relativeDimensionZeroLocus B S hS f).toFunctor
      (relativeDimensionZeroLocus B S hS f).ι))
    (d : ℕ∞) (hd : HasRelativeDimensionAt d B S hS f x) : 1 ≤ d
declarations.comment: relative dimension at least one outside the subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NX, part (2).** If a composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is proper
and its second factor is separated, then its first factor is proper.

Properness is separatedness, finite type and universal closedness (**Stacks 03ZM**). The first
cancels by **Stacks 03KR** and the universal closedness by part (1) of Stacks 04NX; finite type
is local finite type, which cancels by **Stacks 0462**, together with quasi-compactness, which
cancels by **Stacks 03KS** against a quasi-separated second factor — and the second factor is
quasi-separated, being separated (**Stacks 03KK**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_comp_of_isSeparated {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hfg : IsProper B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    IsProper B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NX, part (1).** Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`. If
the composite `X ⟶ Z` is universally closed and `Y ⟶ Z` is separated, then `X ⟶ Y` is
universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_comp_of_isSeparated {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hfg : UniversallyClosed B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_range_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04NX, part (1).** Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_of_comp_of_isSeparated`, the image of `|X|` in
`|Y|` is closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_range_of_comp_of_isSeparated {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hfg : UniversallyClosed B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    _root_.IsClosed (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiFinite_of_isFinite
declarations.doc: A finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFinite_of_isFinite (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hf : IsFinite B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiFinite B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_iff_isAffineHom_and_isProper
declarations.doc: A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is finite exactly when it is affine and proper.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_openSubspace_of_fpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
A family of open subspaces `Wᵢ i` of the members of an fpqc covering `f i : Tᵢ i ⟶ T` whose
two pullbacks to each `Tᵢ i ×_T Tᵢ j` agree is the family of preimages of a unique open subspace
of `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_openSubspace_of_fpqcCovering
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type v} {T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {Tᵢ : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : ∀ i, Tᵢ i ⟶ T)
    (hf : IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun i => (f i).hom))
    (Wᵢ : ∀ i, {W : Subfunctor (Tᵢ i).1 // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W})
    (hW : ∀ i j,
      (Wᵢ i).1.preimage (pullback.fst (f i).hom (f j).hom) =
        (Wᵢ j).1.preimage (pullback.snd (f i).hom (f j).hom)) :
    ∃! W : {W : Subfunctor T.1 // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      ∀ i, W.1.preimage (f i).hom = (Wᵢ i).1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_desc_of_fpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04P2.** For an fpqc covering `{X i ⟶ Y}` of algebraic spaces over `S` and an
algebraic space `Z` over `S`, the diagram
`Mor(Y, Z) ⟶ ∏ i, Mor(X i, Z) ⇉ ∏ (i, j), Mor(X i ×_Y X j, Z)` is an equalizer: a family of
morphisms `X i ⟶ Z` agreeing on the fibre products `X i ×_Y X j` descends uniquely to `Y ⟶ Z`.

The input is Stacks 0APL, that an algebraic space is a sheaf for the fpqc topology; the rest is
formal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_desc_of_fpqcCovering
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type v} {X : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun i => (f i).hom))
    (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (g : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Z)
    (hg : ∀ i j,
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst (f i).hom (f j).hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS (f i) (f j) ⟶ X i) ≫ g i =
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd (f i).hom (f j).hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS (f i) (f j) ⟶ X j) ≫ g j) :
    ∃! h : Y ⟶ Z, ∀ i, f i ≫ h = g i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackSquare
declarations.doc: The canonical source-target square over the quotient stack.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientStackSquare
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    let J := BigFppfOver.topology C S hS
    let U : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨liftedFibredCategory G.objects,
        isStackInGroupoids_liftedFibredCategory G.objects⟩
    let Q : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨quotientStack G,
        isStackInGroupoids_quotientStack G⟩
    Bicategory.TwoCommSq
      (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom
        (liftedQuotientStackProjection G) : U ⟶ Q)
      (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom
        (liftedQuotientStackProjection G) : U ⟶ Q)
declarations.comment: the displayed square of a groupoid over its quotient stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_twoCartesian_source_target
declarations.doc:
**The 2-cartesian square `R ⇉ U → [U/R]`.** Take the square whose apex is the arrow space
`R`, whose two legs `R ⟶ U` are the source `s` and the target `t`, whose two maps `U ⟶ [U/R]` are
both the projection `π`, and whose filler is the canonical 2-arrow `π ∘ s ⟶ π ∘ t` of
Stacks 044S. That 2-arrow is invertible, so the square 2-commutes through it, and the square is
2-cartesian. Here `R` and `U` stand for the stacks in groupoids attached to the two spaces.
declarations.comment: the 2-cartesian square R ⇉ U → [U/R]: legs s, t, π twice, 2-arrow of 044S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fst_snd_source_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0450**, the lower-left square for the projections. The two projections out of the
space of composable pairs of arrows of a groupoid in algebraic spaces form a cartesian square
with the source and the target morphisms: a composable pair is exactly a pair of arrows whose
first arrow has as its source the target of the second.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_fst_snd_source_target (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    IsPullback
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst G.source.hom G.target.hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct C S hS G.source G.target ⟶ G.arrows)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd G.source.hom G.target.hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct C S hS G.source G.target ⟶ G.arrows)
      G.source G.target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FiniteOpenSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PC.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` and an algebraic
space `T`, a morphism `T ⟶ Y` together with an open subspace of `T ×_Y X` which is finite
over `T`.
declarations.statement:
structure FiniteOpenSubspace (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PD.** The finite part `(X/Y)_fin` of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces
over `S`: the presheaf whose sections over a scheme `T` are the pairs consisting of a morphism
`T ⟶ Y` and an open subspace of `T ×_Y X` finite over `T`, with restriction given by base
change.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    FinitePartPresheaf B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheaf_finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PE, part (1).** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over a scheme
`S`, the finite part `(X/Y)_fin` of `f` satisfies the sheaf condition for the fppf topology of
the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
      (finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspaceEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PE, part (2).** For an algebraic space `T` over `S`, the morphisms of sheaves
from `T` to the finite part `(X/Y)_fin` of `f : X ⟶ Y` are in canonical bijection with the
pairs `(a, Z)` of Stacks 04PC over `T`: the pair attached to a morphism restricts, along every
morphism from a scheme of the site, to the pair that the morphism names there.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finiteOpenSubspaceEquiv
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    { e : (T.obj ⟶ (finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).toFunctor) ≃
        FiniteOpenSubspace B S hS f T //
      ∀ (v : T.obj ⟶ (finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).toFunctor)
        (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (g : yoneda.obj U ⟶ T.obj),
        let p := e v
        let q := (finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).sections U
          (v.app (op U) (yonedaEquiv g))
        (q.toBase.hom = g ≫ p.toBase.hom) ∧
          ∃ j : q.subspace.toFunctor ⟶ p.subspace.toFunctor,
            (IsPullback
              (q.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.fst q.toBase.hom f.hom)
              j g
              (p.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.fst p.toBase.hom f.hom)) ∧
            (j ≫ p.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.snd p.toBase.hom f.hom =
              q.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.snd q.toBase.hom f.hom) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspaceMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical injective map `(X'/Y)₍fin₎ ⟶ (X/Y)₍fin₎` induced by an
open immersion `X' ⟶ X` over `Y`. Its specification identifies each image
finite open pair over a test scheme.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finiteOpenSubspaceMap
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X' X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (j : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hj : j ≫ f = f') (hjOpen : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenImmersion B S hS j.hom) :
    { m : (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f').toFunctor ⟶
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).toFunctor //
      Mono m ∧
        ∀ (T : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
          (s : (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f').toFunctor.obj (op T)),
          let p := (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f').sections T s
          let q := (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).sections T
            (m.app (op T) s)
          (p.toBase = q.toBase) ∧
            ∃ k : p.subspace.toFunctor ⟶ q.subspace.toFunctor,
              IsIso k ∧
                (k ≫ q.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.fst q.toBase.hom f.hom =
                  p.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.fst p.toBase.hom f'.hom) ∧
                (k ≫ q.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.snd q.toBase.hom f.hom =
                  p.subspace.ι ≫ pullback.snd p.toBase.hom f'.hom ≫ j.hom) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_finiteOpenSubspaceMap_locallyQuasiFinitePart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PG.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` which
is locally of finite type and let `X' ⊆ X` be the maximal open subspace over which `f` is
locally quasi-finite, Stacks 04NW. Then `(X/Y)_fin = (X'/Y)_fin`, in the sense that the
canonical injection `(X'/Y)_fin ⟶ (X/Y)_fin` of Stacks 04PF is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_finiteOpenSubspaceMap_locallyQuasiFinitePart {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) :
    IsIso (finiteOpenSubspaceMap B S hS (locallyQuasiFinitePartInclusion B S hS f hf)
      (locallyQuasiFinitePartInclusion B S hS f hf ≫ f) f rfl
      (isOpenImmersion_locallyQuasiFinitePartInclusion B S hS f hf)).1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FiniteOpenSubspace.isClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PH.** An open subspace of `T ×_Y X` which is finite over `T` is a closed
subspace of `T ×_Y X`, provided `f : X ⟶ Y` is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem FiniteOpenSubspace.isClosedSubspace (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (Z : FiniteOpenSubspace B S hS f T)
    (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z.subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.zeroFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the zero of the `F₂`-algebra.** The section `0 = (a, ∅)` cut out by no
point at all, whose projection to `T` is finite because the empty open subspace is the
coproduct of the empty family.
declarations.statement: def zeroFibre (a : T ⟶ Y) : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.zeroSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI.** The zero section `0 = (1_Y, ∅)` of the `F₂`-algebra, as a section of the
finite part over `Y`.
declarations.statement: def zeroSection : Y.obj ⟶ P.toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.sections_zeroSection
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** On sections, the zero is the empty open subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem sections_zeroSection (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : Y.obj.obj (op T)) :
    P.sections T ((zeroSection P).app (op T) y) =
      (FinitePartFibre.zeroFibre
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (yonedaEquiv.symm y) : schemeSpace T ⟶ Y)).toPair

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.zeroSection_comp_baseMap
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** The zero is a section of the projection to `Y`.
declarations.statement: theorem zeroSection_comp_baseMap : zeroSection P ≫ P.baseMap = 𝟙 Y.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.oneSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the finite case.** The unit `1 = (1_Y, X)` of the `F₂`-algebra, as a section
of the finite part over `Y`.
declarations.statement: def oneSection (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom) : Y.obj ⟶ P.toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.sections_oneSection
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI, the finite case.** On sections, the unit is the whole fibre product.
declarations.statement:
theorem sections_oneSection (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom) (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (y : Y.obj.obj (op T)) :
    P.sections T ((oneSection P hfin).app (op T) y) =
      (FinitePartFibre.one (a := (ObjectProperty.homMk (yonedaEquiv.symm y) :
        schemeSpace T ⟶ Y)) hfin).toPair

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.oneSection_comp_baseMap
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI, the finite case.** The unit is a section of the projection to `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem oneSection_comp_baseMap (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom) :
    oneSection P hfin ≫ P.baseMap = 𝟙 Y.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.nonUnitalCommRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI.** The sections of the finite part over `T` lying over a fixed `a : T ⟶ Y`
form a commutative ring without unit: the multiplication is the intersection `⋆₂`, the addition
is the symmetric difference `⋆₁(⋆₃(s, s'), ⋆₄(s, s'))` and the zero is `(a, ∅)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def nonUnitalCommRing (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (a : T ⟶ Y) :
    NonUnitalCommRing (FinitePartFibre B S hS f a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.zmodModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI.** Every section is its own additive inverse, so the ring of sections over a
fixed `a : T ⟶ Y` is an algebra over `F₂`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zmodModule (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (a : T ⟶ Y) :
    letI := nonUnitalCommRing hf a
    Module (ZMod 2) (FinitePartFibre B S hS f a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.commRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the finite case.** When `f` is finite the sections of the finite part over a
fixed `a : T ⟶ Y` form a commutative ring, the unit being the section `(a, T ×_Y X)` and the
remaining structure that of the `F₂`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def commRing (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    (a : T ⟶ Y) : CommRing (FinitePartFibre B S hS f a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₃_eq_mul_one_add
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI, the finite case.** `⋆₃(s, s') = s (1 + s')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem star₃_eq_mul_one_add (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    {a : T ⟶ Y} (Z₁ Z₂ : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a) :
    letI := commRing hf hfin a
    star₃ hf Z₁ Z₂ = Z₁ * (1 + Z₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₄_eq_one_add_mul
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI, the finite case.** `⋆₄(s, s') = (1 + s) s'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem star₄_eq_one_add_mul (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    {a : T ⟶ Y} (Z₁ Z₂ : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a) :
    letI := commRing hf hfin a
    star₄ hf Z₁ Z₂ = (1 + Z₁) * Z₂

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₂`.** The intersection `(a, Z₁ ∩ Z₂)` of two sections of
the finite part lying over the same morphism to `Y`.
declarations.statement: def star₂ : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₃`.** The difference `(a, Z₁ ∖ Z₂)` of two sections of the
finite part lying over the same morphism to `Y`.
declarations.statement: def star₃ : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₄
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₄`.** The difference `(a, Z₂ ∖ Z₁)` of two sections of the
finite part lying over the same morphism to `Y`.
declarations.statement: def star₄ : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.pointSet_star₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₂`.** On points, `⋆₂(s, s')` is the intersection
`Z₁ ∩ Z₂`.
declarations.statement: theorem pointSet_star₂ : (star₂ hf Z₁ Z₂).pointSet = Z₁.pointSet ∩ Z₂.pointSet

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.pointSet_star₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₃`.** On points, `⋆₃(s, s')` is the difference
`Z₁ ∖ Z₂`.
declarations.statement: theorem pointSet_star₃ : (star₃ hf Z₁ Z₂).pointSet = Z₁.pointSet \ Z₂.pointSet

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.pointSet_star₄
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₄`.** On points, `⋆₄(s, s')` is the difference
`Z₂ ∖ Z₁`.
declarations.statement: theorem pointSet_star₄ : (star₄ hf Z₁ Z₂).pointSet = Z₂.pointSet \ Z₁.pointSet

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.isOpenImmersion_star₂_le_left
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** `Z₁ ∩ Z₂` is open inside `Z₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_star₂_le_left :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (Subfunctor.homOfLe (star₂_le_left hf Z₁ Z₂))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.isClosedImmersion_star₂_le_left
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** `Z₁ ∩ Z₂` is closed inside `Z₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_star₂_le_left :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS (Subfunctor.homOfLe (star₂_le_left hf Z₁ Z₂))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.isOpenImmersion_star₂_le_right
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** `Z₁ ∩ Z₂` is open inside `Z₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_star₂_le_right :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (Subfunctor.homOfLe (star₂_le_right hf Z₁ Z₂))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.isClosedImmersion_star₂_le_right
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** `Z₁ ∩ Z₂` is closed inside `Z₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_star₂_le_right :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS (Subfunctor.homOfLe (star₂_le_right hf Z₁ Z₂))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI.** The zero section `0 = (a, ∅)` of the `F₂`-algebra: the empty open
subspace, which is finite over `T`.
declarations.statement: def zero : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.subspace_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI.** The open subspace of the zero section is the empty one, so `0 = (a, ∅)`.

The empty open subspace of an algebraic space is the sheafification of the bottom subfunctor
and not the bottom subfunctor itself, whose sections over an object of the site with no points
are not those of a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem subspace_zero : (zero Z₁).subspace =
    (⊥ : Subfunctor (pullback a.hom f.hom)).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the unit of the finite case.** When `f` is finite the section
`1 = (a, T ×_Y X)` cut out by all of the points of `T ×_Y X`, which is the restriction along
`a` of the pair `(1_Y, X)`.
declarations.statement: def one (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom) : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.subspace_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the unit of the finite case.** The open subspace of the unit is the whole
of `T ×_Y X`, so `1` is the restriction along `a` of the pair `(1_Y, X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subspace_one (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom) :
    (one (a := a) hfin).subspace = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₂_one
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI, the unit of the finite case.** `1 s = s`.
declarations.statement: theorem star₂_one (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f.hom) : star₂ hf (one hfin) Z₁ = Z₁

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₂_comm
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** The multiplication `s s' = ⋆₂(s, s')` is commutative.
declarations.statement: theorem star₂_comm : star₂ hf Z₁ Z₂ = star₂ hf Z₂ Z₁

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₂_assoc
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI.** The multiplication `s s' = ⋆₂(s, s')` is associative.
declarations.statement:
theorem star₂_assoc (Z₃ : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a) :
    star₂ hf (star₂ hf Z₁ Z₂) Z₃ = star₂ hf Z₁ (star₂ hf Z₂ Z₃)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.existsUnique_projection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI.** The component rule sending a finite open pair to its morphism to `Y`
determines a unique morphism of presheaves to `Y`, namely the projection
`FinitePartPresheaf.baseMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_projection (P : FinitePartPresheaf B S hS f) :
    ∃! π : P.toFunctor ⟶ Y.obj,
      ∀ T (p : P.toFunctor.obj (op T)),
        yonedaEquiv.symm (π.app (op T) p) = (P.sections T p).toBase.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.star₁Map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₁`.** The morphism of presheaves
`⋆₁ : (X/Y)_fin ×_Y (X/Y)_fin ⟶ (X/Y)_fin` sending a pair of sections over a common morphism
to `Y` to the union `Z₁ ∪ Z₂`.
declarations.statement: def star₁Map : Limits.pullback P.baseMap P.baseMap ⟶ P.toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartPresheaf.sections_star₁Map
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₁`.** On sections, `⋆₁` is the union `Z₁ ∪ Z₂`.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartFibre.star₁
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PI, the operation `⋆₁`.** The union `(a, Z₁ ∪ Z₂)` of two sections of the finite
part lying over the same morphism to `Y`.

Its projection to `T` is finite because `Z₁ ∪ Z₂` is the disjoint union of the open and closed
pieces `Z₁` and `Z₂ ∖ Z₁`, hence their coproduct as a sheaf, and a morphism out of a finite
coproduct whose restriction to each summand is finite is finite.
declarations.statement: def star₁ : FinitePartFibre B S hS f a

declarations.statement: theorem pointSet_star₁ : (star₁ hf Z₁ Z₂).pointSet = Z₁.pointSet ∪ Z₂.pointSet

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_diagonal_finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf

over `S`, the diagonal `(X/Y)_fin ⟶ (X/Y)_fin ×_Y (X/Y)_fin` is representable by schemes and

declarations.name: main_theorem04PL
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04PL**.
If `X` is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens, and the intersection of two
quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, then a subset `T ⊆ X` is an intersection of clopen
subsets if and only if `T` is closed and is a union of connected components of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem04PL
    [CompactSpace X]
    (hbasis : PrespectralSpace X)
    (hinter : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (T : Set X) :
    IsIntersectionOfClopens T ↔ (IsClosed T ∧ IsUnionOfConnectedComponents T)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_and_biUnion_connectedComponent_eq_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and `T ⊆ Spec R`. The following are equivalent:
`T` is closed and a union of connected components of `Spec R`; `T` is an intersection of open and
closed subsets of `Spec R`; `T = V I` for some ideal `I` generated by idempotents; there is a
unique such ideal `I`; and `T` is the zero locus of the ideal generated by all idempotents
vanishing on `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_and_biUnion_connectedComponent_eq_tfae (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) :
    [IsClosed T ∧ (⋃ x ∈ T, connectedComponent x) = T,
      ∃ S : Set (Set (PrimeSpectrum R)), (∀ U ∈ S, IsClopen U) ∧ T = ⋂₀ S,
      ∃ I : Ideal R, (∃ s : Set R, (∀ e ∈ s, IsIdempotentElem e) ∧ I = Ideal.span s) ∧
        T = zeroLocus (I : Set R),
      ∃! I : Ideal R, (∃ s : Set R, (∀ e ∈ s, IsIdempotentElem e) ∧ I = Ideal.span s) ∧
        T = zeroLocus (I : Set R),
      T = zeroLocus
        (Ideal.span {e : R | IsIdempotentElem e ∧ T ⊆ zeroLocus {e}} : Set R)].TFAE

declarations.name: Ideal.pure_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Characterizations of pure ideals.** For an ideal `I` of a commutative ring `R` the following
are equivalent: (1) `I` is pure, i.e. `R ⧸ I` is flat over `R`; (2) `I ⊓ J = I * J` for every
ideal `J`; (3) the same for every finitely generated `J`; (4) the same for every principal `J`;
(5) every `x ∈ I` satisfies `x = x * y` for some `y ∈ I`; (6) finitely many elements of `I` admit
a common such `y`; (7) `I` localizes to `⊥` or to `⊤` at every prime; (8) the support of `I` is the
complement of `V(I)`; (9) `I` is the kernel of `R → (1 + I)⁻¹R`; (10) `R ⧸ I` is `R`-algebra
isomorphic to a localization of `R`; (11) `R ⧸ I` is `R`-algebra isomorphic to `(1 + I)⁻¹R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.pure_tfae {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) :
    List.TFAE
      [I.Pure,
       ∀ J : Ideal R, I ⊓ J = I * J,
       ∀ J : Ideal R, J.FG → I ⊓ J = I * J,
       ∀ x : R, I ⊓ Ideal.span {x} = I * Ideal.span {x},
       ∀ x ∈ I, ∃ y ∈ I, x = x * y,
       ∀ s : Finset R, (s : Set R) ⊆ I → ∃ y ∈ I, ∀ x ∈ s, x = x * y,
       ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
         I.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)) = ⊥ ∨
           I.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)) = ⊤,
       Module.support R I = (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R))ᶜ,
       RingHom.ker (algebraMap R
         (Localization (Submonoid.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I).toMonoidHom ⊥))) = I,
       ∃ S : Submonoid R, Nonempty ((R ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[R] Localization S),
       Nonempty ((R ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[R]
         Localization (Submonoid.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I).toMonoidHom ⊥))]

declarations.name: bijOn_zeroLocus_isPure
declarations.doc:
(Stacks 04PU) The map `I ↦ V(I)` is a bijection between the set of pure
ideals of `R` and the set of closed subsets of `Spec(R)` that are closed under
generalizations. This packages the three claims above as a single `Set.BijOn`
statement.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.support_bijOn_flat_closedImmersions
declarations.doc:
Taking the support is a bijection from the flat closed subschemes of a scheme to the closed
subsets stable under generalization.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_lift_of_flat_closedImmersion
declarations.doc:
A morphism whose set-theoretic image lies in a flat closed subscheme factors uniquely
through it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_lift_of_flat_closedImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) [Flat I.subschemeι] (g : Y ⟶ X)
    (hg : Set.range g ⊆ (I.support : Set X)) :
    ∃! h : Y ⟶ I.subscheme, h ≫ I.subschemeι = g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedComponentIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
The canonical closed subscheme structure on the connected component of a point `x` of a
scheme `X`: the closed subscheme cut out by `connectedComponent x`, which is closed and stable
under generalization. It is the unique closed subscheme structure on that component whose closed
immersion into `X` is flat.

public noncomputable def connectedComponentIdealSheaf {X : Scheme.{u}} (x : X) :
    X.IdealSheafData

registrations.name: Continuous.preimage_connectedComponent
registrations.comment: for the continuous map X_K → X; stated for any continuous map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.image_connectedComponent_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04PZ** (Gabber). Let `K/k` be an extension of fields -- not assumed
finite, algebraic or separable -- and let `X` be a scheme over `k`. The projection `X_K ⟶ X`
sends every connected component of `X_K` onto a connected component of `X`: the image of the
connected component of a point `x` is the connected component of its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_connectedComponent_baseChange
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (x : ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))) :
    (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base ''
        connectedComponent x =
      connectedComponent
        ((pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.closure_range_pullback_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04Q0.** For morphisms `f : A ⟶ X` and `g : B ⟶ Y` of schemes over a
field, the closure of the image of the induced morphism `A ×ₖ B ⟶ X ×ₖ Y` is the
set-theoretic fibre product of the closures of the two images.
declarations.statement:
theorem closure_range_pullback_map {k : Type u} [Field k] {A B X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pA : A ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pB : B ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (f : A ⟶ X) (g : B ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pX = pA) (hg : g ≫ pY = pB) :
    (pullback.fst pX pY).base ⁻¹' closure (Set.range f.base) ∩
        (pullback.snd pX pY).base ⁻¹' closure (Set.range g.base) =
      closure (Set.range
        (pullback.map pA pB pX pY f g (𝟙 _)
          (by simpa using hf.symm) (by simpa using hg.symm)).base)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_imageProductMapIso
declarations.doc:
The image of the product of two quasi-compact maps over a field is canonically isomorphic,
over the product of their targets, to the product of their scheme-theoretic images.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_imageProductMapIso
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {A B X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (f : A ⟶ X) (g : B ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiCompact g] :
    ∃! e : (productMap pX pY f g).image ≅
        pullback (f.imageι ≫ pX) (g.imageι ≫ pY),
      e.hom ≫ productMap pX pY f.imageι g.imageι =
        (productMap pX pY f g).imageι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fiber_isFpqcTorsor
declarations.doc:
A nonempty fibre of the arrows over a pair is a torsor under the corresponding
stabilizer group over the residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiber_isFpqcTorsor {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (p : (G.objects ⊗ G.objects).left) (h : Nonempty (fiberArrows G p).left) :
    IsFpqcTorsor
      (Scheme.Spec.obj (.op ((G.objects ⊗ G.objects).left.residueField p)))
      (fiberGroup G p) (fiberArrows G p)
