      (finitePartWithSection B S hS f σ hσ).toSubfunctor.ι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_finitePartWithSection
declarations.doc:
For separated `f`, the same transformation is representable by closed
immersions as well as open immersions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedImmersion_finitePartWithSection
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (σ : Y ⟶ X) (hσ : σ.hom ≫ f.hom = 𝟙 Y.obj)
    (hf : Space.IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) :
    Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
      (finitePartWithSection B S hS f σ hσ).toSubfunctor.ι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_finitePartWithSection
declarations.doc:
If the finite-part functor is an algebraic space, the section-containing
subfunctor is an open algebraic subspace of it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenSubspace_finitePartWithSection
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (σ : Y ⟶ X) (hσ : σ.hom ≫ f.hom = 𝟙 Y.obj)
    (hfin : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).toFunctor) :
    Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS
      (finitePartWithSection B S hS f σ hσ).toSubfunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.openSubscheme_finitePartWithSection
declarations.doc:
A scheme representing the finite-part functor contains the
section-containing functor as a compatible open subscheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem openSubscheme_finitePartWithSection
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (σ : Y ⟶ X) (hσ : σ.hom ≫ f.hom = 𝟙 Y.obj)
    (V : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : yoneda.obj V ≅
      (Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf B S hS f).toFunctor) :
    ∃ (U : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : U ⟶ V)
      (e' : yoneda.obj U ≅
        (finitePartWithSection B S hS f σ hσ).toSubfunctor.toFunctor),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map i) ∧
      yoneda.map i ≫ e.hom =
        e'.hom ≫ (finitePartWithSection B S hS f σ hσ).toSubfunctor.ι

declarations.name: Deformation.PointwiseGroupoid.finiteArrows
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RS.** The septuple of finite collections of arrows of a groupoid is a groupoid:
its objects are the finite subsets `Z` of the arrows with `s(Z)` a singleton `{u}` and
`e(u) ∈ Z`, its arrows are the pairs `(Z, z)` with `z ∈ Z`, the source of `(Z, z)` is `Z`, its
target is `{z' ∘ z⁻¹ : z' ∈ Z}`, and the composite of `(Z₁, z₁)` with `(Z₂, z₂)` is
`(Z₂, z₁ ∘ z₂)`.

The verification is a reflection along the faithful pair of maps `Z ↦ u` and `(Z, z) ↦ z`, which
carries the unit, the composition and the inverse of `C_fin` to those of the original groupoid.
declarations.statement:
def finiteArrows (P : PointwiseGroupoid source target comp) :
    PointwiseGroupoid (FiniteArrows.src P) (FiniteArrows.tgt P) (FiniteArrows.compose P)
declarations.comment: the groupoid of finite collections of arrows

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.finitePartGroupoid_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RT, the finite part of a groupoid.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` be a groupoid in
algebraic spaces over `B` whose source morphism `s` is separated and locally of finite type. The
construction of Stacks 04RT produces the following, all of which are recorded here for the finite
part `fp = finitePart G hsep hft`, its groupoid `finitePartGroupoid hsep hft` and the canonical
morphism `finitePartGroupoidHom hsep hft`.

* The object space `U'` is `(R_s/U, e)_fin`: the inclusion of `U'` into `(R_s/U)_fin` is an open
  immersion whose range is the subfunctor of pairs containing the unit.
* The morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` is the projection of `(R_s/U)_fin` restricted to `U'`, and is étale.
* `Z_univ` is the universal open subspace of the fibre product of `g` and `s`, finite over `U'`,
  namely the pair which the inclusion of `U'` names under Stacks 04PE; it is closed as well as
  open, and the base change of the unit factors through it.
* The groupoid has object space `U'` and arrow space `Z_univ`, with
  - `s' : (u, Z, z) ↦ (u, Z)`, the first projection;
  - `t' : (u, Z, z) ↦ (t ∘ z, c(Z, i ∘ z))`: the pair that `t'` names is the translate of the
    tautological pair by the tautological arrow, and its base morphism is `t ∘ z`;
  - `e' : (u, Z) ↦ (u, Z, e ∘ u)`, the unit of the groupoid;
  - `i' : (u, Z, z) ↦ (t ∘ z, c(Z, i ∘ z), i ∘ z)`, the inverse of the groupoid;
  - `c' : ((u₁, Z₁, z₁), (u₂, Z₂, z₂)) ↦ (u₂, Z₂, z₁ ∘ z₂)`, the composition of the groupoid.
* The canonical morphism of groupoids over `B` to `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` is `g` on objects and
  `(u, Z, z) ↦ z` on arrows.

The hypotheses are on `s` alone; the source also assumes `t` separated and locally of finite type,
which the construction does not use. As in the rest of the formalization, the ambient fibre
product of `Z_univ` is `U' ×_{g, U, s} R` rather than `R ×_{s, U, g} U'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePartGroupoid_spec (hsep : Space.IsSeparated C S hS G.source.hom)
    (hft : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS G.source.hom) :
    -- `U' = (R_s/U, e)_fin`, an open subspace of `(R_s/U)_fin`
    Subfunctor.range (finitePart G hsep hft).inclusion =
        (Space.finitePartWithSection C S hS G.source (identityHom G)
          (identityHom_comp_source G)).toSubfunctor ∧
      Space.IsOpenImmersion C S hS (finitePart G hsep hft).inclusion ∧
      -- `g : U' ⟶ U` is the projection of the finite part, and is étale
      (finitePart G hsep hft).pair.toBase.hom =
        (finitePart G hsep hft).inclusion ≫
          (Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf C S hS G.source).baseMap ∧
      Space.IsEtale C S hS (finitePart G hsep hft).pair.toBase.hom ∧
      -- `Z_univ` is universal, closed, and contains the base change of the unit
      (finitePart G hsep hft).pair =
        (Space.finiteOpenSubspaceEquiv C S hS G.source (finitePart G hsep hft).objects).1
          (finitePart G hsep hft).inclusion ∧
      Space.IsClosedSubspace C S hS (finitePart G hsep hft).pair.subspace ∧
      Space.ContainsSection C S hS G.source (identityHom G) (identityHom_comp_source G)
        (finitePart G hsep hft).pair ∧
      -- the groupoid has object space `U'` and arrow space `Z_univ`
      (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft).objects = (finitePart G hsep hft).objects ∧
      (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft).arrows = FinitePart.arrowSpace (finitePart G hsep hft) ∧
      -- `s' : (u, Z, z) ↦ (u, Z)`
      (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft).source.hom = FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft) ∧
      -- `t' : (u, Z, z) ↦ (t ∘ z, c(Z, i ∘ z))`
      (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft).target.hom = targetHom hsep hft ∧
      (Space.finiteOpenSubspaceEquiv C S hS G.source
          (FinitePart.arrowSpace (finitePart G hsep hft))).1
          (targetHom hsep hft ≫ (finitePart G hsep hft).inclusion) =
        translatePair (FinitePart.sourcePair (finitePart G hsep hft))
          (FinitePart.arrowMap (finitePart G hsep hft))
          (FinitePart.arrowMap_comp_source (finitePart G hsep hft)) ∧
      targetHom hsep hft ≫ (finitePart G hsep hft).pair.toBase.hom =
        (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom ≫ G.target.hom ∧
      -- `e' : (u, Z) ↦ (u, Z, e ∘ u)`
      (identityHom (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft)).hom = unitHom hsep hft ∧
      unitHom hsep hft ≫ FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft) =
        𝟙 (finitePart G hsep hft).objects.obj ∧
      unitHom hsep hft ≫ (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom =
        (finitePart G hsep hft).pair.toBase.hom ≫ (identityHom G).hom ∧
      -- `i' : (u, Z, z) ↦ (t ∘ z, c(Z, i ∘ z), i ∘ z)`
      (inverseHom (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft)).hom = invHom hsep hft ∧
      invHom hsep hft ≫ FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft) = targetHom hsep hft ∧
      invHom hsep hft ≫ (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom =
        (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom ≫ (inverseHom G).hom ∧
      -- `c' : ((u₁, Z₁, z₁), (u₂, Z₂, z₂)) ↦ (u₂, Z₂, z₁ ∘ z₂)`
      (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft).comp.hom = compHom hsep hft ∧
      compHom hsep hft ≫ FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft) =
        pullback.snd (FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft)) (targetHom hsep hft) ≫
          FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft) ∧
      compHom hsep hft ≫ (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom =
        composeHom
          (pullback.fst (FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft)) (targetHom hsep hft) ≫
            (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom)
          (pullback.snd (FinitePart.sourceHom (finitePart G hsep hft)) (targetHom hsep hft) ≫
            (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom)
          (FinitePart.composable_compose (finitePart G hsep hft) (targetHom hsep hft)
            (targetHom_comp_inclusion hsep hft)) ∧
      -- the canonical morphism of groupoids: `g` on objects, `(u, Z, z) ↦ z` on arrows
      (finitePartGroupoidHom hsep hft).toGroupoidHom.mapObjects =
        (finitePart G hsep hft).pair.toBase.hom ∧
      (finitePartGroupoidHom hsep hft).toGroupoidHom.mapArrows =
        (finitePart G hsep hft).arrowHom
declarations.comment: the finite part (U', Z_univ, s', t', c', e', i') of the groupoid, with the rules for its structure morphisms and its morphism of groupoids to (U, R, s, t, c, e, i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartUniversalOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clauses (1) and (2).** The two structure spaces of the finite part of a
groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B`: the object space `U'` with its étale projection
`g : U' ⟶ U`, identified with `(R_s/U, e)_fin ⟶ U`, and the universal open and closed subspace
`Z_univ ⊂ R ×_{s, U, g} U'` finite over `U'` which contains the base change of the unit.
declarations.comment: clauses (1) and (2) stated; not the groupoid structure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartUniversalOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clauses (1) and (2).** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B` whose
source and target are separated and locally of finite type, the object space `(R_s/U, e)_fin`
with its étale projection to `U` and the universal open and closed subspace of
`R ×_{s, U, g} U'` finite over `U'` containing the base change of the unit.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finitePartUniversalOpen
    {C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : C.Contains S}
    {B : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (hs_sep : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_ht_sep : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated C S hS G.target.hom)
    (hs_lft : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_ht_lft : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS G.target.hom) :
    FinitePartUniversalOpen G
declarations.comment: clauses (1) and (2); not the groupoid structure or its morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clause (3).** The groupoid in algebraic spaces
`(U', Z_univ, s', t', c')` carried by the finite part of `(U, R, s, t, c)`, together with its
canonical morphism of groupoids to `(U, R, s, t, c)` over `B`.
declarations.comment: clause (3), the groupoid structure on the finite part and its morphism to R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_finitePartGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clause (3).** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B` whose source and
target are separated and locally of finite type, the finite part carries a groupoid
`(U', Z_univ, s', t', c')` together with a morphism of groupoids to `(U, R, s, t, c)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_finitePartGroupoid
    {C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : C.Contains S}
    {B : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (hs_sep : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_ht_sep : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated C S hS G.target.hom)
    (hs_lft : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_ht_lft : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS G.target.hom) :
    Nonempty (FinitePartGroupoid G)
declarations.comment: clause (3), the groupoid structure on the finite part and its morphism to R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU.** The groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U', Z_univ, s', t', c', e', i')` over `B`
carried by the finite part of `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finitePartGroupoid :
    AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B
declarations.comment: the groupoid (U', Z_univ, s', t', c', e', i') on the finite part

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoidHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU.** The canonical morphism of groupoids in algebraic spaces over `B`
`(U', Z_univ, s', t', c', e', i') ⟶ (U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` whose existence the lemma asserts.
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism of groupoids over B to (U, R, s, t, c, e, i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoid_objectProjection_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clause (1).** Under the identification of `U'` with `(R_s/U, e)_fin` the
projection `g : U' ⟶ U` is the projection of the finite part.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePartGroupoid_objectProjection_spec :
    (finitePartGroupoidObjectProjection G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft).hom =
      (finitePartGroupoidObjectsEquiv G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft).hom ≫
        (finitePartWithSection C S hS G.source
          (finitePartGroupoidUnit G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft)
          (finitePartGroupoidUnit_source G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft)).toSubfunctor.ι ≫
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteOpenSubspacePresheaf C S hS G.source).baseMap
declarations.comment: clause (1), g : U' ⟶ U is identified with (R_s/U, e)_fin ⟶ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clause (2), universality.** `Z_univ` is the finite open subspace of
`R ×_{s, U, g} U'` classified by the inclusion of `U'` into the finite part of `s`; this is what
makes it the universal such subspace.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen_spec :
    (finiteOpenSubspaceEquiv C S hS G.source
        (finitePartGroupoid G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft).objects).1
      ((finitePartGroupoidObjectsEquiv G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft).hom ≫
        (finitePartWithSection C S hS G.source
          (finitePartGroupoidUnit G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft)
          (finitePartGroupoidUnit_source G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft)).toSubfunctor.ι) =
      finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft
declarations.comment: clause (2), Z_univ is the universal finite open subspace of R ×_{s, U, g} U'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen_containsUnit
declarations.doc: **Stacks 04RU, clause (2), the unit.** `Z_univ` contains the base change of the unit `e`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen_containsUnit :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ContainsSection C S hS G.source
      (finitePartGroupoidUnit G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft)
      (finitePartGroupoidUnit_source G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft)
      (finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft)
declarations.comment: clause (2), Z_univ contains the base change of the unit e

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clause (2), closedness.** `Z_univ` is closed in `R ×_{s, U, g} U'` as well as
open.
declarations.comment: clause (2), Z_univ is closed in R ×_{s, U, g} U' as well as open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoid_arrows
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, clause (2), the arrow space.** The space of arrows of the groupoid on the
finite part *is* the universal finite open subspace `Z_univ`.
declarations.comment: clause (2), the arrow space of the finite part is Z_univ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finitePartGroupoidHom_mapArrows
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU.** Under the identification of the arrow space with `Z_univ`, the canonical
morphism of groupoids sends an arrow of the finite part to its underlying arrow of `R`, i.e. it is
the second projection of `R ×_{s, U, g} U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePartGroupoidHom_mapArrows :
    (finitePartGroupoidHom G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft).toGroupoidHom.mapArrows =
      eqToHom (finitePartGroupoid_arrows G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft) ≫
        (finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft).subspace.ι ≫
        pullback.snd
          (finitePartGroupoidUniversalOpen G hs_sep ht_sep hs_lft ht_lft).toBase.hom
          G.source.hom
declarations.comment: the arrow map of the canonical morphism is Z_univ ⊂ R ×_{s, U, g} U' ⟶ R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.finitePartGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, the groupoid structure.** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B` whose
source morphism is separated and locally of finite type, the finite part
`(U', Z_univ, s', t', c', e', i')` is a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finitePartGroupoid (hsep : Space.IsSeparated C S hS G.source.hom)
    (hft : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS G.source.hom) :
    GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B
declarations.comment: the groupoid structure on the finite part

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.finitePartGroupoidHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04RU, the canonical morphism of groupoids.** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces over
`B` whose source morphism is separated and locally of finite type, the canonical morphism of
groupoids in algebraic spaces over `B` from the finite part to the given groupoid: on objects it
is the étale projection `g : U' ⟶ U` of Stacks 04RU, clause (1), and on arrows it is the rule
`(u, Z, z) ↦ z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finitePartGroupoidHom (hsep : Space.IsSeparated C S hS G.source.hom)
    (hft : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C S hS G.source.hom) :
    Hom (finitePartGroupoid hsep hft) G
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism of groupoids from the finite part to the given groupoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasiSplittingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04RV.** The standing quasi-splitting situation: a point `u` of
the object scheme of a groupoid scheme whose source and target are separated and locally of
finite type, with the source quasi-finite at the identity arrow `e(u)`.
declarations.statement: structure QuasiSplittingSituation

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_etale_quasiSplitting_of_quasiSplittingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04RW.**

In the quasi-splitting situation of Stacks 04RV there are an algebraic space `U'`, an étale
morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` of algebraic spaces and a point `u' : Spec κ(u) ⟶ U'` lying over `u` such
that the restriction `R|_{U'}` is quasi-split over `u'`.

`U'` is the finite part `(R_s/U, e)_fin` of Stacks 04RU and `g` its étale projection; `u'` is
the pair `(u, Z_u)` with `Z_u = {e(u)}`, which is an open and closed piece of the fibre
`F_u = R ×_{s, U} Spec κ(u)` finite over `κ(u)` because the source is quasi-finite at `e(u)`;
and the quasi-splitting is the universal open `Z_univ` of Stacks 04RU read inside `R|_{U'}`,
which is a quasi-splitting at every point of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_quasiSplitting_of_quasiSplittingSituation
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasiSplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left)
    (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u))) :
    ∃ (U' : AlgebraicSpaces C D.S hS)
      (g : U' ⟶ (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP).objects),
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      ∃ v : U'.obj.obj (Opposite.op
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.residueFieldSiteObject C hS
            (X := D.groupoid.objects) D.u hK)),
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.yonedaSchemePointEquiv C hS hU
            (Opposite.op (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.residueFieldSiteObject C hS
              (X := D.groupoid.objects) D.u hK))
            (g.hom.app _ v)).left =
              D.groupoid.objects.left.fromSpecResidueField D.u ∧
        IsQuasiSplitAt (restrict (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP) g).groupoid
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap C D.S hS U'.obj
            (eqToHom (restrict (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP) g).objects_eq.symm).hom
            (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FieldValuedPoint.class C D.S hS U'.obj
              { carrier := D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u
                contained := hK
                toBase := D.groupoid.objects.left.fromSpecResidueField D.u ≫
                  D.groupoid.objects.hom
                value := v }))

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_quasiSplit_of_quasiSplittingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04RW.**  In the quasi-splitting situation of Stacks 04RV there are an
algebraic space `U'`, an étale morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` of algebraic spaces and a point
`u' : Spec κ(u) ⟶ U'` lying over `u : Spec κ(u) ⟶ U` such that the restriction `R' = R|_{U'}`
of `R` to `U'` is quasi-split over `u'`.

`U'` is the object space of the finite part `(R_s/U, e)_fin`, `g` its étale projection, `u'` the
pair `(u, Z_u)` with `Z_u` the open and closed piece of the fibre `F_u = R ×_{s, U} Spec κ(u)`
supported on the identity arrow `e(u)`, and the quasi-splitting is the universal open `Z_univ`
read inside `R|_{U'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiSplit_of_quasiSplittingSituation
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasiSplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left)
    (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u))) :
    ∃ (U' : AlgebraicSpaces C D.S hS)
      (g : U' ⟶ (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP).objects),
      IsEtale C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      ∃ v : U'.obj.obj (Opposite.op
          (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK)),
        (yonedaSchemePointEquiv C hS hU (Opposite.op
            (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK))
            (g.hom.app _ v)).left =
          D.groupoid.objects.left.fromSpecResidueField D.u ∧
        GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsQuasiSplitAt
          (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrict (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP)
            g).groupoid
          ((residueSectionValuedPoint D.groupoid C hS D.u hK U' v).class C D.S hS U'.obj)
declarations.comment: ALL FOUR ASSERTIONS, in Situation 04RV: the algebraic space U', the etale morphism g : U' -> U, the point u' : Spec k(u) -> U' lying over u, and that the restriction R|_{U'} is QUASI-SPLIT over u' -- all four PRODUCED, none assumed. The situation hypothesis is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasiSplittingSituation, which carries the 04RV attribute. The open Z_u of the fibre is the one supported on the identity arrow e(u), which is open and closed and finite over k(u) because s is quasi-finite at e(u), the one geometric hypothesis of Tag 04RV beyond separatedness and local finiteness of type. Beyond Situation 04RV the only hypotheses are that the big fppf site contains the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and Spec k(u), which is this library's standing ambient requirement

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.nonempty_etaleStrongSplitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04RX.**

In the strong splitting situation of Stacks 04RL, with the source in addition flat and locally
of finite presentation, there are a scheme `U'`, a separated étale morphism `g : U' ⟶ U`, and a
point `u'` of `U'` over `u` with `κ(u) = κ(u')`, such that the restriction `R' = R|_{U'}` is
strongly split over `u'`.

The neighbourhood is `U' = (R_s/U, e)_{fin}`, the finite part of Stacks 04RU containing the
unit, with its étale projection; it is a scheme by Stacks 04RI part (2) and Stacks 04RR part
(4), and the projection is separated by Stacks 04RI part (1) and Stacks 04RR part (1).  The
point and the strong splitting are those of Stacks 03FM, the point being recorded as a section
over `Spec κ(u)` whose image under `g` is the canonical morphism `Spec κ(u) ⟶ U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_etaleStrongSplitting
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.StrongSplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left)
    (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u)))
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat D.groupoid.source.left)
    (hfp : AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.source.left) :
    ∃ (U' : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces C D.S hS)
      (g : U' ⟶ (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP).objects),
      U'.obj.IsRepresentable ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      ∃ v : U'.obj.obj (Opposite.op
          (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK)),
        (yonedaSchemePointEquiv C hS hU (Opposite.op
            (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK))
            (g.hom.app _ v)).left =
          D.groupoid.objects.left.fromSpecResidueField D.u ∧
        IsStronglySplitAt
          (restrict (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP) g).groupoid
          ((residueSectionValuedPoint D.groupoid C hS D.u hK U' v).class C D.S hS U'.obj)
declarations.comment:
in Situation 04RL with the source flat and locally of finite presentation: U' is
a SCHEME (asserted as representability of the neighbourhood), U' ⟶ U is SEPARATED as well as
étale, and R|_{U'} is strongly split over a Spec κ(u)-valued point of U' lying over u. The
neighbourhood, its point and the splitting are Stacks 03FM, which this library proves as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_stronglySplit_of_strongSplittingSituation`; the scheme-ness and
the separatedness are Stacks 04RI and Stacks 04RR applied to the finite part (R_s/U, e)_fin,
through its identification with the neighbourhood recorded by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartUniversalOpen.objectsEquiv` and `objectProjection_spec`.
Strong splitting is Stacks 04RK part (1) for the restriction of the REALIZATION of the groupoid
scheme, as in this library's Stacks 03FM and Stacks 04RY; the scheme-level
`Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.StrongSplitting` is not used, the composition of the restricted
realization not being compared with the composition of
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict`. Only flatness and local finite presentation of the
SOURCE are assumed, where the tag asks them of the target too, so the hypotheses are weaker than
the tag's. Beyond Situation 04RL the remaining hypotheses are that the big fppf site contains
the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and Spec κ(u), this library's standing
ambient requirement

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_quasiSplit_separated_scheme_of_quasiSplittingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04RY.**

In the quasi-splitting situation of Stacks 04RV, with the source in addition flat and locally
of finite presentation, there are a scheme `U'`, a separated étale morphism `g : U' ⟶ U`, and a
point `u'` of `U'` over `u` with `κ(u) = κ(u')`, such that `R' = R|_{U'}` is quasi-split over
`u'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiSplit_separated_scheme_of_quasiSplittingSituation
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasiSplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left)
    (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u)))
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat D.groupoid.source.left)
    (hfp : AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.source.left) :
    ∃ (U' : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces C D.S hS)
      (g : U' ⟶ (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP).objects),
      U'.obj.IsRepresentable ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      ∃ v : U'.obj.obj (Opposite.op
          (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK)),
        (yonedaSchemePointEquiv C hS hU (Opposite.op
            (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK))
            (g.hom.app _ v)).left =
          D.groupoid.objects.left.fromSpecResidueField D.u ∧
        IsQuasiSplitAt
          (restrict (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP) g).groupoid
          ((residueSectionValuedPoint D.groupoid C hS D.u hK U' v).class C D.S hS U'.obj) ∧
        ∀ (X' : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver C D.S hS) (ε : U'.obj ≅ yoneda.obj X')
          (gS : X' ⟶ schemeSiteObject C hS hU), yoneda.map gS = ε.inv ≫ g.hom →
          ∃ u' : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme C D.S hS).obj X',
            ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme C D.S hS).map gS).base u' = D.u ∧
            IsIso (((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme C D.S hS).map
              gS).residueFieldMap u')
declarations.comment: ALL FOUR ASSERTIONS PRODUCED, in Situation 04RV with the source flat and locally of finite presentation: U' is a SCHEME (delivered as representability of the neighbourhood), U' -> U is SEPARATED as well as etale, there is a point u' of U' over u with k(u) = k(u') -- recorded both as a Spec k(u)-valued section v of U' over the canonical Spec k(u) -> U, and, on any scheme X' representing U' with any morphism of schemes X' -> U inducing g, as a point u' of X' with image u at which the residue field map is an ISOMORPHISM -- and R|_{U'} is QUASI-SPLIT over u'. Each of the four is constructed, none of them an input. The neighbourhood, the point and the quasi-splitting are Tag 04RW, proved in StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Groupoids/QuasiSplittingEtaleLocalization.lean; the scheme-ness and the separatedness are Tags 04RI and 04RR applied to the finite part (R_s/U, e)_fin. Flatness and local finite presentation are required of the SOURCE alone, where the tag requires them of the target too, so these hypotheses are WEAKER than the tag's. Beyond Situation 04RV the remaining requirements are that the big fppf site contains the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and Spec k(u), this library's standing ambient requirement

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_isAffine_isStronglySplitAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04RZ.**

In the strong splitting situation of Stacks 04RL, with `s` and `t` in addition flat and locally
of finite presentation and with `U` affine, there are an affine scheme `U''`, an étale morphism
`U'' ⟶ U` and a point `u''` of `U''` over `u` with `κ(u) = κ(u'')`, such that the restriction of
`R` to `U''` is strongly split over `u''`.

The étale neighbourhood `U'` of Stacks 04RX is shrunk to an affine one: `U''` is an invariant
affine open of the object scheme of the strong splitting of `R' = R|_{U'}`, so `U'' ⟶ U'` is an
open immersion and the restriction of that splitting to `U''` is a strong splitting of
`R'|_{U''}` over `u''`.  The restriction is taken in two steps, as the restriction of `R'` to
`U''`; its identification with the restriction of `R` along the composite `U'' ⟶ U' ⟶ U` is
Stacks 04MW.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_isStronglySplitAt
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.StrongSplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left) (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u)))
    [IsAffine D.groupoid.objects.left]
    [Flat D.groupoid.source.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.source.left]
    [Flat D.groupoid.target.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.target.left] :
    ∃ (U' : Over D.S) (g : U' ⟶ D.groupoid.objects)
      (R' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction D.groupoid g)
      (U'' : Over D.S) (j : U'' ⟶ R'.groupoid.objects) (u'' : U''.left),
      IsAffine U''.left ∧ IsOpenImmersion j.left ∧
      Etale (j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left ∧
      (j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left.base u'' = D.u ∧
      IsIso ((j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left.residueFieldMap u'') ∧
      ∀ R'' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction R'.groupoid j,
        IsStronglySplitAt R''.groupoid ((eqToHom R''.objects_eq.symm).left.base u'')
declarations.comment:
in Situation 04RL with s, t flat and locally of finite presentation and U affine:
an affine scheme U'', an étale U'' ⟶ U and a point u'' over u with κ(u) = κ(u''), such that
R|_{U''} is strongly split over u''. R|_{U''} is covered in its two-step reading, as the
restriction to U'' of R' = R|_{U'} for the étale neighbourhood U' of Stacks 04RX, rather than as
the restriction of R along the composite U'' ⟶ U' ⟶ U; the identification of the two is
Stacks 04MW, which this library has as the comparison diagram `doubleRestrictionDiagram` and not
as an identification of realizations. The conclusion is stronger than the tag in two respects:
U'' ⟶ U' is an open immersion, not merely étale, and the strong splitting is produced for EVERY
groupoid scheme realizing that restriction. Beyond Situation 04RL the hypotheses are that the big
fppf site contains the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and Spec κ(u), this
library's standing ambient requirement

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_isAffine_isQuasiSplitAt_of_quasiSplittingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04S0.**

In the quasi-splitting situation of Stacks 04RV, with `U` affine and with `s` and `t` flat and
locally of finite presentation, there are a separated étale neighbourhood `U' ⟶ U`, a groupoid
scheme `R'` realizing the restriction `R|_{U'}`, an affine open `U'' ⊆ U'` and a point `u''` of
`U''` over `u` with `κ(u) = κ(u'')`, such that `U'' ⟶ U` is étale and `R|_{U''}` is quasi-split
over `u''` — both when `R|_{U''}` is read as the restriction of `R'` to `U''` and when it is
read, as the tag reads it, as the restriction of `R` along the composite `U'' ⟶ U' ⟶ U`.

Stacks 04RY supplies the neighbourhood and a quasi-splitting of the restriction of the
*realization* of the groupoid scheme; the comparison with the groupoid-scheme notion is
`Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.nonempty_openFiniteSubgroupoid_of_realization`, and the
shrinking to an affine neighbourhood is
`Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_isAffine_isQuasiSplitAt`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_isQuasiSplitAt_of_quasiSplittingSituation
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasiSplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left)
    (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u)))
    [IsAffine D.groupoid.objects.left]
    [Flat D.groupoid.source.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.source.left]
    [Flat D.groupoid.target.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.target.left]
    :
    ∃ (U' : Over D.S) (gp : U' ⟶ D.groupoid.objects)
      (R' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction D.groupoid gp)
      (U'' : Over D.S) (j : U'' ⟶ R'.groupoid.objects) (u'' : U''.left),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated gp.left ∧ Etale gp.left ∧
      IsAffine U''.left ∧ IsOpenImmersion j.left ∧
      Etale (j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left ∧
      (j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left.base u'' = D.u ∧
      IsIso ((j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left.residueFieldMap u'') ∧
      (∀ R'' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction R'.groupoid j,
        IsQuasiSplitAt R''.groupoid ((eqToHom R''.objects_eq.symm).left.base u'')) ∧
      ∀ R''' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction D.groupoid
          (j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects),
        IsQuasiSplitAt R'''.groupoid ((eqToHom R'''.objects_eq.symm).left.base u'')
declarations.comment: ALL ASSERTIONS, in Situation 04RV with U affine and with s and t flat and locally of finite presentation: the separated etale neighbourhood U' -> U, a groupoid scheme R' realizing R|_{U'}, an AFFINE open U'' of U' with a point u'' over u at which the residue field map is an ISOMORPHISM, and the QUASI-SPLITTING of R|_{U''} over u'' -- all PRODUCED. Stacks 04RY is invoked internally as exists_quasiSplit_separated_scheme_of_quasiSplittingSituation; its quasi-splitting is AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.QuasiSplitting of the restriction of the REALIZATION, and it is converted to the groupoid-scheme notion Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.QuasiSplitting by nonempty_openFiniteSubgroupoid_of_realization, which de-realizes the open finite subgroupoid. In two respects the conclusion is STRONGER than the tag: the morphism U'' -> U' is an open immersion, not merely etale, and the quasi-splitting is produced for EVERY groupoid scheme realizing the restriction. R|_{U''} is read both as the restriction of R along the composite U'' -> U' -> U, as the tag reads it, and as the restriction of R' to U''. Beyond Situation 04RV the only requirements are that the big fppf site contain the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and Spec k(u), this library's standing ambient requirement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04S1.** A morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation is
locally surjective for the big fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySurjective_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (_hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (_hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) G)
    (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS a)
    (hflat : HasProperty B S hS (fun _ _ f => IsFlat B S hS f.hom) a ha)
    (hlfp : HasProperty B S hS
      (fun _ _ f => IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) a ha)
    (hsurj : HasProperty B S hS (fun _ _ f => IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) a ha) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_division_isField_quotient_of_isoSpecField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04S4, at an object scheme which is the spectrum of a field.**  A
subgroupoid on the same object scheme whose pre-relation is a monomorphism and whose source and
target maps are *finite* can be divided out, and the quotient is the spectrum of a field.

Over a field the two finite locally free hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_division` reduce to finiteness, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isFinite_of_isoSpecField`, and affineness of the
object scheme is automatic.  The quotient morphism being finite locally free and surjective, its
global functions are a field by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isField_sections_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_of_surjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_division_isField_quotient_of_isoSpecField {S : Scheme.{u}} (G H : GroupoidScheme S)
    (i : GroupoidScheme.Hom H G) (hobj : H.objects = G.objects)
    (hiobj : i.mapObjects = eqToHom hobj) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (e : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k))
    [Mono i.mapArrows]
    [IsFinite H.source.left] [IsFinite H.target.left]
    [Mono (prod.lift H.target H.source)]
    [IsSeparated (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite (prod.lift G.target G.source).left] :
    ∃ D : Division G H i hobj, IsField Γ(D.quotient.left, ⊤)
declarations.comment: all four conclusions, at an object scheme which is the spectrum of a field and with only finiteness assumed of the source and target of the subgroupoid, together with the quotient being the spectrum of a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteFlatQuotient_isAffine_of_mono_groupoidPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 04S4.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid scheme `G` over `S` and
let `(U, P, s|_P, t|_P, c|_P)` be a groupoid scheme `H` mapping to it by a morphism `i` which is
an isomorphism on objects, such that

1. `s|_P, t|_P : P ⟶ U` are finite locally free,
2. `j|_P = (t|_P, s|_P) : P ⟶ U ×_S U` is a monomorphism,
3. `U` is affine, and
4. `j = (t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_S U` is separated and locally quasi-finite (locally of finite type
   with finite fibres; the finite type half is a separate class here).

Then `U/P` is representable by an affine scheme `Ū`, the quotient morphism `U ⟶ Ū` is finite
locally free (and surjective), and `P = U ×_Ū U`; these are the fields of
`Stacks.Groupoids.FiniteFlatQuotient` together with affineness of its quotient scheme.
Moreover `R` is the restriction of a groupoid scheme on `Ū` along the quotient morphism: there
is a groupoid scheme `K` with object scheme `Ū` and a morphism `G ⟶ K` which is the quotient
morphism on objects and whose square of arrow schemes over the pairs of objects is cartesian,
`R = (U ×_S U) ×_{Ū ×_S Ū} R̄`; equivalently, it is fully faithful on the generalized points of
every test scheme.

The source asks in addition that `P ⟶ R` be a monomorphism; this follows from the other
hypotheses (`j ∘ i = (i × i) ∘ j|_P` is a monomorphism) and is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteFlatQuotient_isAffine_of_mono_groupoidPreRelation (G H : GroupoidScheme S)
    (i : GroupoidScheme.Hom H G) [IsIso i.mapObjects]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree H.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree H.target.left]
    [Mono (groupoidPreRelation H)] [IsAffine G.objects.left]
    [IsSeparated (groupoidPreRelation G).left] [LocallyQuasiFinite (groupoidPreRelation G).left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (groupoidPreRelation G).left] :
    ∃ Q : FiniteFlatQuotient H, IsAffine Q.space.left ∧
      ∃ (K : GroupoidScheme S) (he : K.objects = Q.space) (F : GroupoidScheme.Hom G K),
        F.mapObjects = (inv i.mapObjects ≫ Q.quotientMap) ≫ eqToHom he.symm ∧
          IsPullback F.mapArrows (groupoidPreRelation G) (groupoidPreRelation K)
            (prod.map F.mapObjects F.mapObjects) ∧
          ∀ T : Over S, Nonempty (F.evaluation T).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_division
declarations.doc:
A finite locally free subgroupoid equivalence relation on an affine scheme can be
divided out, and a separated locally quasi-finite ambient groupoid descends to the quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_division {S : Scheme.{u}} (G H : GroupoidScheme S)
    (i : GroupoidScheme.Hom H G) (hobj : H.objects = G.objects)
    (hiobj : i.mapObjects = eqToHom hobj)
    [Mono i.mapArrows]
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree H.source.left]
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree H.target.left]
    [Mono (prod.lift H.target H.source)]
    [IsAffine G.objects.left]
    [IsSeparated (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite (prod.lift G.target G.source).left] :
    Nonempty (Division G H i hobj)
declarations.comment: all four conclusions: the affine quotient Ū = U/P as the fppf-sheaf coequalizer, its finite locally free surjective quotient map, the kernel-pair square P = U ×_Ū U, and the descent of the ambient groupoid R to a groupoid on Ū of which it is the restriction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_diag_of_flat_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04S6, condition (5).** Let `F` be a sheaf on the big fppf site of a scheme `S`
whose absolute diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, and suppose there is an algebraic
space `X` over `S` and a morphism `f : X ⟶ F` which is surjective, flat and locally of finite
presentation.  Then `F` is an algebraic space over `S`.

The chart `f` is not assumed to be representable by algebraic spaces; it is so automatically, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_diagonal`, which is what turns the
data of condition (5) into the data of condition (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_diag_of_flat_chart
    {F X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (hdiag : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (diag F))
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ F)
    (hSurj : HasProperty B S hS (surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) f
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_diagonal B S hS hdiag hX f))
    (hFlat : HasProperty B S hS (flatProperty B S hS) f
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_diagonal B S hS hdiag hX f))
    (hLfp : HasProperty B S hS (locallyOfFinitePresentationProperty B S hS) f
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_diagonal B S hS hdiag hX f)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_relativelyRepresentable_diag_of_flat_scheme_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04S6, condition (6).** Let `F` be a sheaf on the big fppf site of a scheme `S`
whose absolute diagonal is representable, and suppose there is a scheme `U` over `S` and a
morphism `f : h_U ⟶ F` which is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation.  Then `F`
is an algebraic space over `S`.

This is condition (5) for the algebraic space `h_U`: a representable diagonal is representable
by algebraic spaces by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces.of_relativelyRepresentable`, and a
representable presheaf is an algebraic space by **Stacks 025Z**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_relativelyRepresentable_diag_of_flat_scheme_chart
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (hdiag : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (diag F))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F)
    (hSurj : HasProperty B S hS (surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) f
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_diagonal B S hS
        (IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces.of_relativelyRepresentable hdiag)
        (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS U) f))
    (hFlat : HasProperty B S hS (flatProperty B S hS) f
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_diagonal B S hS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Bootstrap04S6.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_groupoidScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04S6, condition (2).** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid scheme over `S` whose
object scheme belongs to the big fppf site, such that `s, t` are flat and locally of finite
presentation and `j = (t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_S U` is an equivalence relation. Then the fppf quotient
sheaf `U/R` is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_groupoidScheme
    (site : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : site.Contains S)
    [HasSheafify (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology site S hS) (Type u)]
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) (hU : site.Contains G.objects.left)
    [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source]
    [Flat G.source.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace site S hS
      (Stacks.Groupoids.quotientSheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology site S hS)
        (Over.post site.inclusion) (AlgebraicGeometry.groupoidPreRelation G)).obj
declarations.comment: condition (2): the quotient of a scheme by a flat, locally finitely presented equivalence relation groupoid scheme is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bootstrap04S6QuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04S6, condition (1).** Let `j : R ⟶ U ×_Z U` be an equivalence relation of
algebraic spaces over a presheaf `Z` on the big fppf site of `S`, whose target and source
`t, s : R ⟶ U` are flat and locally of finite presentation. Then the fppf quotient sheaf `U/R`
is an algebraic space.

The proof is the source's: `U` is replaced by an étale atlas `h_{U₀} ⟶ U` (Groupoids in Spaces,
Lemma 046P, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_restrictQuotientSheafMap_chartInSliceMap`); the
restricted relation `R₀ = U₀ ×_U R ×_U U₀` is then an algebraic space with a monomorphism,
locally of finite type, to `U₀ ×_S U₀`, hence representable by Morphisms of Spaces,
Proposition 03XX; and the resulting relation of schemes in the site is condition (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Bootstrap04S6.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_flat_preRelation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bootstrap04S6QuotientSheaf (site : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : site.Contains S) : Bootstrap04S6QuotientSheaf site S hS
declarations.comment: condition (1): the quotient of an algebraic space by a flat, locally finitely presented equivalence relation of algebraic spaces is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBootstrapAlgebraicSpaceAlongFlatSurjection
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a sheaf on the big fppf site of `S`, and suppose there are an algebraic space `X`
over `S` and a morphism `X ⟶ F` which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation. Then `F` is an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBootstrapAlgebraicSpaceAlongFlatSurjection :
    IsBootstrapAlgebraicSpaceAlongFlatSurjection B S hS
declarations.comment: condition (3): a sheaf with a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented chart from an algebraic space, representable by algebraic spaces, is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_flat_scheme_chart
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a sheaf on the big fppf site of `S`, and suppose there are a scheme `U` of the site
and a morphism `h_U ⟶ F` which is representable by algebraic spaces (in particular, one
representable by schemes), surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Then `F` is an
algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_flat_scheme_chart
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f)
    (hSurj : HasProperty B S hS (surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) f hf)
    (hFlat : HasProperty B S hS (flatProperty B S hS) f hf)
    (hLfp : HasProperty B S hS (locallyOfFinitePresentationProperty B S hS) f hf) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.pr₀₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04S7.** For a commuting inner square `G ⋙ P = H ⋙ Q` under the diagram
`𝒜 → ℬ ← 𝒞 → 𝒟 ← ℰ`, the canonical functor `(𝒜 ×_ℬ 𝒞) ×_𝒟 ℰ ⥤ 𝒜 ×_ℱ ℰ` which forgets the
middle factor and transports the two structural isomorphisms into `ℱ`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInSets
declarations.doc:
The 2-category of categories fibred in sets over `𝒞`: the full sub-2-category of the
2-category `BasedCategory 𝒞` of categories over `𝒞` spanned by the categories fibred in sets.
Explicitly:

1. its objects are the categories `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` over `𝒞` that are fibred in sets;
2. its 1-morphisms `(𝒮, p) ⟶ (𝒮', p')` are the functors `G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮'` with `p' ∘ G = p`;
3. its 2-morphisms `t : G ⟶ H` are the morphisms of functors with `p'(t_x) = 𝟙 (p x)` for every
   object `x` of `𝒮`.
declarations.statement: abbrev CatFiberedInSets (𝒞 : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} 𝒞]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInSetoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SA.** A functor `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` is a *category fibred in setoids* if it is
fibred in groupoids and each fibre category `p.Fiber S` is a setoid, i.e. thin (its fibres
are groupoids automatically, by Stacks `003V`).
declarations.statement: class IsFiberedInSetoids (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiberedInSetoids_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SA.** A functor `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` is fibred in setoids if and only if it is fibred in
groupoids (Stacks `003T`) and every fibre category `p.Fiber S` is a setoid in the sense of Stacks
`02XZ`: a groupoid in which every object has exactly one automorphism, the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedInSetoids_iff (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) :
    p.IsFiberedInSetoids ↔
      p.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧ ∀ S : 𝒮, IsSetoidCategory (p.Fiber S)
declarations.comment: Stacks' definition verbatim: fibred in groupoids, and every fibre category is a setoid (`IsSetoidCategory`, Stacks 02XZ).

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProd.proj_isFiberedInSetoids
declarations.doc:
**The 2-fibre product of categories fibred in setoids.** If `𝒳`, `𝒴`, `𝒮` are fibred in
setoids over `𝒞` and
`F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮`, `G : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒮` are 1-morphisms over `𝒞`, then the 2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_𝒮 𝒴`
over `𝒞`, with its structure functor, is again fibred in setoids over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem TwoFibreProd.proj_isFiberedInSetoids
    (hX : pX.IsFiberedInSetoids) (hY : pY.IsFiberedInSetoids) (hS : pS.IsFiberedInSetoids)
    (hF : F ⋙ pS = pX) (hG : G ⋙ pS = pY) :
    (TwoFibreProd.proj pX pY pS F G).IsFiberedInSetoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.existsUnique_twoIso_of_isoClassMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SC (1).** For two 1-morphisms `f, g : 𝒮₁ ⟶ 𝒮₂` of categories fibred in setoids
over `𝒞` with `F(f) = F(g)`, that is inducing the same map on the presheaves of isomorphism
classes of objects, there is a unique 2-isomorphism `f ⟶ g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_twoIso_of_isoClassMap_eq {G H : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒯} (hG : G ⋙ q = p) (hH : H ⋙ q = p)
    (h : isoClassMapOfCompEq hG = isoClassMapOfCompEq hH) :
    ∃! e : G ≅ H, ∀ x : 𝒮, q.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p.obj x)) (e.hom.app x)
declarations.comment: (1): a unique 2-isomorphism between two 1-morphisms with the same image under F.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_oneMorphism_isoClassMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SC (2).** Every morphism `h : F(𝒮₁) ⟶ F(𝒮₂)` of presheaves of isomorphism classes
is `F(f)` for a 1-morphism `f : 𝒮₁ ⟶ 𝒮₂` of categories fibred in setoids over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_oneMorphism_isoClassMap_eq :
    ∃ (G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒯) (hG : G ⋙ q = p), isoClassMapOfCompEq hG = φ
declarations.comment: (2): every map of the associated presheaves comes from a 1-morphism.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassMapEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SC**, final form: for categories `𝒮₁`, `𝒮₂` fibred in setoids over `𝒞`,
`Mor_{Cat/𝒞}(𝒮₁, 𝒮₂)` modulo 2-isomorphism is `Mor_{PSh(𝒞)}(F₁, F₂)`, where `F_i(U)` is the set of
isomorphism classes of objects of the fibre of `𝒮_i` over `U`. The forward map sends a 1-morphism
to the induced map of presheaves; it is surjective by Stacks 04SC (2) and injective by
Stacks 04SC (1).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isoClassMapEquiv :
    _root_.Quotient (twoIsoSetoid p q) ≃ (p.isoClassPresheaf ⟶ q.isoClassPresheaf)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.fiberPresheafIsoIsoClassPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SC (3).** A category fibred in sets `𝒮` is equal to `F(𝒮)`: the presheaf of
isomorphism classes of the fibres of `𝒮` is the presheaf `U ↦ Ob(𝒮_U)` of objects of the fibres,
which is the presheaf that Stacks 02Y2 attaches to `𝒮`. The isomorphism is the quotient map at
each `U`, a bijection because the fibres are discrete, and it is natural because on both sides the
restriction along `f : V ⟶ U` is `x ↦ f^* x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fiberPresheafIsoIsoClassPresheaf (hd : ∀ U : 𝒞, IsDiscrete (p.Fiber U)) :
    p.fiberPresheaf hd ≅ p.isoClassPresheaf
declarations.comment:
(3): for a category fibred in sets the presheaf of isomorphism classes of the fibres
is the presheaf of objects of the fibres, i.e. `𝒮 = F(𝒮)`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoFibreProductIsoClassEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SD.** The presheaf attached by Stacks 04SC to a 2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴` over `𝒞`
is the fibre product of the presheaves attached to `𝒳`, `𝒴` and `𝒵`: at every object `U` of `𝒞`,
`Ob((𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴)_U)/≅ = Ob(𝒳_U)/≅ ×_{Ob(𝒵_U)/≅} Ob(𝒴_U)/≅`, by the bijection sending the class of
an object to the pair of the classes of its components. This is the display to which the source's
proof reduces the lemma.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def twoFibreProductIsoClassEquiv (U : 𝒞) :
    _root_.Quotient
        (isIsomorphicSetoid
          ((TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 F G).Fiber U)) ≃
      {ab : _root_.Quotient (isIsomorphicSetoid (p𝒳.Fiber U)) ×
            _root_.Quotient (isIsomorphicSetoid (p𝒴.Fiber U)) //
          (isoClassMap hF).app (op U) ab.1 = (isoClassMap hG).app (op U) ab.2}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoFibreProductIsoClassMap_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SD**, naturality: the bijection of
`CategoryTheory.Functor.twoFibreProductIsoClassEquiv` commutes with restriction along a morphism
of `𝒞`, so it is an isomorphism of presheaves and not merely a family of bijections.
declarations.statement:
lemma twoFibreProductIsoClassMap_naturality
    [(TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 F G).IsFibered] {V U : 𝒞} (f : V ⟶ U)
    (c : (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 F G).isoClassPresheaf.obj (op U)) :
    (twoFibreProductIsoClassMap hF hG V
        ((TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 F G).isoClassPresheaf.map f.op c)).val =
      (p𝒳.isoClassPresheaf.map f.op (twoFibreProductIsoClassMap hF hG U c).val.fst,
        p𝒴.isoClassPresheaf.map f.op (twoFibreProductIsoClassMap hF hG U c).val.snd)
declarations.comment: Naturality: the bijection is an isomorphism of presheaves.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_oneMorphism_inducing_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SF**, the precise form: given `φ : X ⟶ Y` there is a 1-morphism `G : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` over
`𝒞` which induces `φ` on isomorphism classes of objects, and any 1-morphism inducing `φ` is
related to it by a unique 2-isomorphism. Inducing `φ` is spelled out through the bijections
`\overline{𝒳}(U) ≃ (U ⟶ X)` and `\overline{𝒴}(U) ≃ (U ⟶ Y)` that representability supplies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_oneMorphism_inducing_hom (φ : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ (G : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hG : G ⋙ q = p),
      (∀ (U : 𝒞) (c : p.isoClassPresheaf.obj (op U)),
        hY.equiv U ((isoClassMapOfCompEq hG).app (op U) c) = hX.equiv U c ≫ φ) ∧
      ∀ (H : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hH : H ⋙ q = p),
        (∀ (U : 𝒞) (c : p.isoClassPresheaf.obj (op U)),
          hY.equiv U ((isoClassMapOfCompEq hH).app (op U) c) = hX.equiv U c ≫ φ) →
        ∃! e : G ≅ H, ∀ x : 𝒳, q.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p.obj x)) (e.hom.app x)
declarations.comment:
Given `φ : X ⟶ Y` there is a 1-morphism inducing it, unique up to unique
2-isomorphism.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoIsoQuotientEquivHomOfRepresentableBy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SF.** Let `𝒳`, `𝒴` be categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞` representable by
objects `X`, `Y` of `𝒞`. Then `Mor_{Cat/𝒞}(𝒳, 𝒴)` modulo 2-isomorphism is `Mor_𝒞(X, Y)`. The
bijection is the composite of Stacks 04SC, which identifies the left-hand side with the maps
`\overline{𝒳} ⟶ \overline{𝒴}` of presheaves of isomorphism classes, with the Yoneda step
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassPresheafHomEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def twoIsoQuotientEquivHomOfRepresentableBy :
    _root_.Quotient (twoIsoSetoid p q) ≃ (X ⟶ Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesOverSmallerBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SG.** For a morphism `g : S ⟶ S'` of a big fppf site, the category of
algebraic spaces over `S'` endowed with a morphism to the representable algebraic space of
`S`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev SpacesOverSmallerBase (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S S' : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (hS' : B.Contains S') (g : B.obj hS ⟶ B.obj hS')
declarations.comment: the category of algebraic spaces with a morphism to the smaller base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SG, the forward functor.** An algebraic space over `S` is an algebraic space over
`S'` with a morphism to the representable algebraic space of `S`: the lower-shriek extension, read
in the slice over that representable presheaf.

The structural morphism of the image of `F` sends a section indexed by `ψ : T ⟶ S` to `ψ`; this is
the functor every relative-property statement of Chapters 100 and 101 is written with.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor :
    AlgebraicSpaces B S hS ⥤ SpacesOverSmallerBase B S S' hS hS' g
declarations.comment: the forward functor of the equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctorForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SG, the forward functor is the lower-shriek extension.** Forgetting the structural
morphism to the representable algebraic space of `S` turns
`AlgebraicGeometry.spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor` into the lower-shriek extension of Stacks 03I5
part (2).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctorForgetIso :
    (spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B S S' hS hS' g ⋙
        ObjectProperty.ι (fun X : Over (yoneda.obj (Over.mk g) :
          (BigFppfOver B S' hS')ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) => IsAlgebraicSpace B S' hS' X.left) ⋙
        Over.forget (yoneda.obj (Over.mk g))) ≅
      (ObjectProperty.ι (fun F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u =>
          IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) ⋙ OverShriek.relocalizePresheafFunctor g)
declarations.comment: the forward functor is the lower-shriek extension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spacesOverSmallerBaseEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The category of algebraic spaces over `S` is equivalent to the category of algebraic spaces
over `S'` equipped with a morphism to the representable algebraic space of `S`, the equivalence
being the lower-shriek extension along `g : S ⟶ S'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spacesOverSmallerBaseEquivalence :
    AlgebraicSpaces B S hS ≌ SpacesOverSmallerBase B S S' hS hS' g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_restrict_iff_product
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SH.** The restriction of a presheaf `F'` on the big fppf site of `S'` to the big
fppf site of `S` along `f : S ⟶ S'` is an algebraic space over `S` exactly when the product of
`F'` with the representable presheaf of the object `S →f S'` is an algebraic space over `S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_restrict_iff_product
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S S' : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (hS' : B.Contains S')
    (f : B.obj hS ⟶ B.obj hS') (F' : (BigFppfOver B S' hS')ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict f).obj F') ↔
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S' hS' (yoneda.obj (Over.mk f) ⨯ F')

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiberedInSetoids_and_isoClassPresheaf_iso_isomPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SI.** Let `𝒞` be a category, let `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` be a fibred category, let `U` be an
object of `𝒞` and let `x`, `y` be objects of the fibre category `𝒮_U`. Denote `x`, `y : 𝒞/U ⥤ 𝒮`
also the corresponding 1-morphisms `(a : V ⟶ U) ↦ a^* x` (Stacks 004B). Then

1. the 2-fibre product `𝒮 ×_{𝒮 × 𝒮, (x, y)} 𝒞/U`, whose objects over `a : V ⟶ U` are the triples
   `(z, α : z ≅ a^* x, β : z ≅ a^* y)` with `z` an object and `α`, `β` isomorphisms of `𝒮_V`, is
   fibred in setoids over `𝒞/U`, and
2. `Isom(x, y)` is the presheaf of sets corresponding to that category fibred in setoids
   (Stacks 04SC), namely its presheaf of isomorphism classes of objects of the fibres, the
   identification sending the class of `(z, α, β)` to `β ∘ α⁻¹`.

The second part is an isomorphism of presheaves, hence data: it is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsomPresheafTwoFibreProduct.presheafIso`, pinned by the requirement that
it send the class of `(z, α, β)` to `β ∘ α⁻¹`, which determines it, every class being the class
of such a triple.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isFiberedInSetoids_and_isoClassPresheaf_iso_isomPresheaf
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) [p.IsFibered] {U : 𝒞} (x y : p.Fiber U) :
    PProd (IsomPresheafTwoFibreProduct.proj p x y).IsFiberedInSetoids
      { e : (IsomPresheafTwoFibreProduct.proj p x y).isoClassPresheaf ≅
          p.isomPresheaf x y ⋙ uliftFunctor.{max u₁ v₁ u₂, v₂} //
        ∀ P : IsomPresheafTwoFibreProduct.Tot p x y,
          (e.hom.app (op P.y) (isoClassMk _ ⟨P, rfl⟩)).down.1.1 = P.iso.inv.1 ≫ P.iso.hom.2 }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SK**.

Let `F` be a presheaf of sets on the big fppf site of `S` and let `{S i → S}` be a covering
family of the base. Assume

1. `F` is a sheaf (`hF`);
2. each restriction `F_i = h_{S i} × F` is an algebraic space (`hFi`);
3. the coproduct `∐ F_i` is an algebraic space: `G`, presented by the colimit cofan `hcoprod`
   with legs `ι`, is a coproduct of the `F_i` in sheaves, and it is an algebraic space (`hG`).

Then `F` is an algebraic space.

The coproduct in (3) is given as data because the index type of the covering is of the next
universe, so a coproduct of the `F_i` need not exist in sheaves of `Type u`; any two coproducts
are isomorphic, so this is the source's hypothesis.

The source's proof applies Stacks 04S6 to `∐ F_i ⟶ F`, the base change of `∐ S_i ⟶ S`. Inside
the site this chart is built from a refinement of the covering of size bounded by `S`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isCovering_of_atlas_size_le`; what that lemma asks for is
a bounded étale atlas of the restriction of each `F_i` to an affine open `W` of `S_i`, and
hypothesis (3) is exactly what supplies it. An étale atlas `U` of `∐ F_i` splits along the
coproduct into étale atlases `U_i` of the `F_i`, which are open in `U`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Sheaf.exists_clopen_decomposition_of_isColimit_cofan`). The restriction of
`F_i` to `W` is the base change of `F_i` along `W ⟶ S_i`, so `W ×_{S_i} U_i` is an étale atlas
of it, of size at most `max (size S) (size U)`.

The last step is Stacks 04S6, condition (3), for a chart representable by objects of the site:
a sheaf which receives a representable, surjective, flat, locally finitely presented morphism
from an algebraic space is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_isCovering
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS))))
    (hE : BigFppfOver.IsCovering B S hS ⟨Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)), E⟩)
    (hFi : ∀ i : E.I₀, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (yoneda.obj (E.X i) ⨯ F))
    {G : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)}
    (ι : ∀ i : E.I₀, (⟨yoneda.obj (E.X i) ⨯ F, (hFi i).isSheaf⟩ :
      Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ G)
    (hcoprod : IsColimit (Cofan.mk G ι))
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.obj) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_oneMorphism_inducing_hom
registrations.comment: induced morphism and uniqueness up to unique two-isomorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PresheafOfCategories.elementsMapEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Tag 04SU (e).** The rule `F ↦ 𝒮_F` is fully faithful on presheaves of sets: maps of
presheaves `F ⟶ G` are in bijection with the 1-morphisms `𝒮_F ⥤ 𝒮_G` strictly over `C`, by
`m ↦ El m`.
declarations.comment: (e) maps of presheaves F ⟶ G are the 1-morphisms S_F ⥤ S_G over the base

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.exists_elementsOp_equivalence_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Tag 04SU (f), fibre products.** For maps `α : F ⟶ H` and `β : G ⟶ H` of presheaves of sets
and a fibre product `P = F ×_H G`, the category of elements `𝒮_P` is equivalent to the 2-fibre
product `𝒮_F ×_{𝒮_H} 𝒮_G` over `C`, by an equivalence which is strictly over `C` and whose
composites with the two projections are the 1-morphisms induced by the projections of `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementsOp_equivalence_of_isPullback {α : F ⟶ H} {β : G ⟶ H} {pF : P ⟶ F}
    {pG : P ⟶ G} (h : IsPullback pF pG α β) :
    ∃ e : P.Elementsᵒᵖ ≌
        TwoFibreProductOver (Functor.Elements.π F).leftOp (Functor.Elements.π G).leftOp
          (Functor.Elements.π H).leftOp (NatTrans.mapElements α).op
          (NatTrans.mapElements β).op,
      e.functor ⋙ structureFunctor _ _ _ _ _ = (Functor.Elements.π P).leftOp ∧
      e.functor ⋙ fst _ _ _ _ _ = (NatTrans.mapElements pF).op ∧
      e.functor ⋙ snd _ _ _ _ _ = (NatTrans.mapElements pG).op
declarations.comment: (f) S_{F ×_H G} = S_F ×_{S_H} S_G for maps F → H ← G of presheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.exists_elementsOp_equivalence_of_isLimit_binaryFan
declarations.doc:
**Tag 04SU (f), products.** For a product `P = F × G` of presheaves of sets, the category of
elements `𝒮_P` is equivalent to the 2-fibre product `𝒮_F ×_C 𝒮_G` over `C` (taken along the two
structure functors and the identity of `C`), by an equivalence which is strictly over `C` and
whose composites with the two projections are the 1-morphisms induced by the projections of
`P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementsOp_equivalence_of_isLimit_binaryFan {pF : P ⟶ F} {pG : P ⟶ G}
    (h : IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk pF pG)) :
    ∃ e : P.Elementsᵒᵖ ≌
        TwoFibreProductOver (Functor.Elements.π F).leftOp (Functor.Elements.π G).leftOp
          (𝟭 C) (Functor.Elements.π F).leftOp (Functor.Elements.π G).leftOp,
      e.functor ⋙ structureFunctor _ _ _ _ _ = (Functor.Elements.π P).leftOp ∧
      e.functor ⋙ fst _ _ _ _ _ = (NatTrans.mapElements pF).op ∧
      e.functor ⋙ snd _ _ _ _ _ = (NatTrans.mapElements pG).op
declarations.comment: (f) S_{F × G} = S_F ×_C S_G for presheaves of sets F, G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SV.** A category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` is
*represented by an algebraic space* over `S` if it is equivalent, over that site, to the
category of elements of the sheaf of points of an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.morphismSpaceEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SW.** One-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids represented by `F` and `G`,
modulo two-isomorphism, are morphisms `F ⟶ G` of the representing presheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def morphismSpaceEquiv
    (eX : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒳.val.p (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eY : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒴.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p) :
    Quotient (Functor.twoIsoSetoid 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p) ≃ (F ⟶ G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.morphismSpaceEquiv_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SW.** On every fibre, the forward direction of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.morphismSpaceEquiv` is the map induced by the given one-morphism on
isomorphism classes of objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem morphismSpaceEquiv_map
    (eX : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒳.val.p (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eY : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒴.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (f : {H : 𝒳.val.obj ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj // H ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = 𝒳.val.p})
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : F.obj (op U)) :
    letI : 𝒳.val.p.IsFibered := 𝒳.2.isFibered
    letI : 𝒴.val.p.IsFibered := 𝒴.2.isFibered
    ((Functor.isoClassMap
      (Functor.isFibredOneMorphism_of_isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒴.2 f.2)).app (op U))
      (Functor.isoClassMk 𝒳.val.p
        ((Functor.fiberFunctorOfCompEq eX.inv.w U).obj
          (⟨⟨U, Discrete.mk a⟩, rfl⟩ :
            (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p.Fiber U))) =
    Functor.isoClassMk 𝒴.val.p
      ((Functor.fiberFunctorOfCompEq eY.inv.w U).obj
        (⟨⟨U, Discrete.mk
          ((morphismSpaceEquiv B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F G eX eY (Quotient.mk _ f)).app
            (op U) a)⟩, rfl⟩ :
          (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p.Fiber U))
declarations.comment: induced map on fibre isomorphism classes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsUnique_twoIso_of_morphismSpaceEquiv_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SW.** Two one-morphisms inducing the same morphism of representing presheaves
admit a unique two-isomorphism over the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_twoIso_of_morphismSpaceEquiv_eq
    (eX : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒳.val.p (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eY : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒴.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (f g : {H : 𝒳.val.obj ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj // H ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = 𝒳.val.p})
    (h : morphismSpaceEquiv B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F G eX eY (Quotient.mk _ f) =
      morphismSpaceEquiv B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F G eX eY (Quotient.mk _ g)) :
    ∃! α : f.1 ≅ g.1,
      ∀ x : 𝒳.val.obj, 𝒴.val.p.IsHomLift (𝟙 (𝒳.val.p.obj x)) (α.hom.app x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_inducedSpacesHom_iff_forall_sectionOfObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SW.** A morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces is the one determined by a
1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` over the site if and only if it carries the section of `X` named by every
object `z` of `𝒳` to the section of `Y` named by `f z`.

This is the identification of Stacks 04SW stated as a property of a *given* morphism of algebraic
spaces: it is what pins a morphism of algebraic spaces appearing as a free parameter against a
1-morphism appearing as another, which is the compatibility a statement about "the induced
morphism of algebraic spaces" presupposes. The right-hand condition is the recipe of the source —
an object of `𝒳` over `U` is a section of `X` over `U`, and `f` of it is a section of `Y` over
`U` — and the left-hand side is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.inducedSpacesHom`, the morphism of algebraic spaces that recipe
defines.

The hypotheses are those of the source: `X` and `Y` are algebraic spaces, and `eF`, `eG` are the
equivalences over the site exhibiting `𝒳` and `𝒴` as representable by them. Being equivalent
over the site to a category of elements already makes `p` and `q` fibred in groupoids, so no
such hypothesis is carried.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_inducedSpacesHom_iff_forall_sectionOfObj
    (eF : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver p
      (presheafOfCategories (X.1 ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eG : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver q
      (presheafOfCategories (Y.1 ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hf : f ⋙ q = p) (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    g = inducedSpacesHom B S hS p q eF eG f hf ↔
      ∀ (z : 𝒳) (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (h : p.obj z = W),
        g.hom.app (op W) (PresheafOfCategories.sectionOfObj eF z h) =
          PresheafOfCategories.sectionOfObj eG (f.obj z)
            ((Functor.congr_obj hf z).trans h)
declarations.comment:
the morphism of algebraic spaces determined by a 1-morphism, characterised on
  named sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.morphismSpaceEquiv_eq_inducedSpaceMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SW.** The bijection of morphism spaces takes the 2-isomorphism class of a
1-morphism `Φ : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` over the site to the morphism of representing presheaves that `Φ`
induces: the section of `G` attached to a section of `F` is the one named by the image under `Φ`
of the object naming it.

So the abstract identification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.morphismSpaceEquiv` and the explicit
construction `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.inducedSpaceMap` of Stacks 0GQA are the same map, and a
compatibility expressed through the latter — as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_inducedSpacesHom_iff_forall_sectionOfObj` expresses it — is a
compatibility with the former.

Both sides are computed on named sections: the left by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.morphismSpaceEquiv_app_sectionOfObj`, the right by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.inducedSpaceMap_app_sectionOfObj`, and a morphism of representing
presheaves is determined by those values.
declarations.statement:
theorem morphismSpaceEquiv_eq_inducedSpaceMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (eX : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒳.val.p (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eY : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒴.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (Φ : {H : 𝒳.val.obj ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj // H ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = 𝒳.val.p}) :
    morphismSpaceEquiv B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F G eX eY (Quotient.mk _ Φ) =
      Space.inducedSpaceMap B S hS F G 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p eX eY Φ.1 Φ.2
declarations.comment:
the bijection is the morphism of representing presheaves induced by the
  1-morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.morphismSpaceEquiv_app_sectionOfObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SW.** The morphism `F ⟶ G` of representing presheaves induced by a 1-morphism `Φ`
over the site carries the section of `F` named by an object `z` of `𝒳` to the section of `G`
named by `Φ z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem morphismSpaceEquiv_app_sectionOfObj
    (Φ : {H : 𝒳.val.obj ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj // H ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = 𝒳.val.p})
    (z : 𝒳.val.obj) {W : BigFppfOver B S hS} (h : 𝒳.val.p.obj z = W) :
    (morphismSpaceEquiv B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F G eX eY (Quotient.mk _ Φ)).app (op W)
        (PresheafOfCategories.sectionOfObj eX z h) =
      PresheafOfCategories.sectionOfObj eY (Φ.1.obj z) ((Functor.congr_obj Φ.2 z).trans h)
declarations.comment: value of the induced morphism on a named section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isoClassMap_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SY.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in setoids over the
big fppf site of `S`, whose total objects lie in an arbitrary universe `w`, and let
`a : F ⟶ G` be the map of presheaves of isomorphism classes corresponding to `f`, i.e. sending
the class of `x` to the class of `f x`. Then `a` is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks
02YQ, tested on the universe-lifted scheme-valued points of `G`, since `F` and `G` take values
in `Type w`) if and only if `f` is representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isoClassMap_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_iff
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInSetoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (a : 𝒳.val.p.isoClassPresheaf ⟶ 𝒴.val.p.isoClassPresheaf)
    (ha : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U),
      a.app (op U) (Functor.isoClassMk 𝒳.val.p x) =
        Functor.isoClassMk 𝒴.val.p
          ((Functor.Fiber.mapOfComp 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f)
