            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p f) U).obj x)) :
    Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS
        (Functor.whiskerRight a uliftFunctor.{u}) ↔
      IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (CatFiberedInSetoids.inclusion.map f).hom
declarations.comment: total objects in any universe; `a` tested on universe-lifted points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInSetoids_iff_inertiaProjection_isEquivalence_of_isAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack over the big fppf site of `S` is a stack in setoids if and only if the
canonical projection from its inertia category is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSetoids_iff_inertiaProjection_isEquivalence_of_isAlgebraicStack
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    𝒳.val.p.IsStackInSetoids (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ↔
      (RelativeInertia.π 𝒳.val.p :
        AbsoluteInertia 𝒳.val.p ⥤ 𝒳.val.obj).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInSetoids_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SZ**, the implication (3) ⟹ (1). A category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf
site of `S` which is representable by an algebraic space over `S` is a stack in setoids for the
fppf topology.

The representing presheaf is an fppf sheaf, so the category of its elements is a stack in sets,
and the equivalence over the site that representability provides carries that back to `𝒳`. No
part of the algebraic-stack condition is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSetoids_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
    (h : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳) :
    𝒳.val.p.IsStackInSetoids (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_inertiaProjection_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SZ**, the implication (3) ⟹ (2). For a category fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf site of `S` which is representable by an algebraic space over `S`, the canonical projection
from its inertia category is an equivalence.

This is the implication (3) ⟹ (1) composed with Stacks 04ZM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_inertiaProjection_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace
    (h : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳) :
    (RelativeInertia.π 𝒳.val.p :
      AbsoluteInertia 𝒳.val.p ⥤ 𝒳.val.obj).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInSetoids_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04SZ.** For an algebraic stack `𝒳` over the big fppf site of `S` the following are
equivalent:

1. `𝒳` is a stack in setoids;
2. the canonical 1-morphism `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` from the inertia is an equivalence;
3. `𝒳` is representable by an algebraic space.

The equivalence (1) ⟺ (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInSetoids_iff_inertiaProjection_isEquivalence_of_isAlgebraicStack`,
the implication (3) ⟹ (1) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInSetoids_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace`, and the
implication (1) ⟹ (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isStackInSetoids`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSetoids_tfae (halg : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    List.TFAE
      [𝒳.val.p.IsStackInSetoids (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS),
        (RelativeInertia.π 𝒳.val.p : AbsoluteInertia 𝒳.val.p ⥤ 𝒳.val.obj).IsEquivalence,
        IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_smoothSurjectivePresentation_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T1.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let
`y : (Sch/V)_fppf ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective and smooth. Then there are a scheme `U` over `S`, a
1-morphism `x : (Sch/U)_fppf ⟶ 𝒳` which is surjective and smooth, and a 1-morphism
`a : (Sch/U)_fppf ⟶ (Sch/V)_fppf` making the square `x ≫ f ≅ a ≫ y` 2-commute.

Surjectivity and smoothness are the relative properties of Stacks 03YK for
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smoothMorphismProperty`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smoothSurjectivePresentation_lift
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (_h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : schemeFibredCategory B S hS V ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hy : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS y.hom)
    (hysurj : HasRelativeProperty B S hS (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) y hy)
    (hysmooth : HasRelativeProperty B S hS (Space.smoothMorphismProperty B S hS) y hy) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : schemeFibredCategory B S hS U ⟶ 𝒳)
      (a : schemeFibredCategory B S hS U ⟶ schemeFibredCategory B S hS V)
      (hx : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS x.hom),
      Nonempty (x ≫ f ≅ a ≫ y) ∧
        HasRelativeProperty B S hS (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) x hx ∧
          HasRelativeProperty B S hS (Space.smoothMorphismProperty B S hS) x hx

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProductSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T2, first assertion.** The apex of the canonical 2-commutative square of a
cospan of algebraic stacks over `S` is an algebraic stack. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProduct`, Stacks 04TF, with base the common
target, whose stack and diagonal hypotheses there are two of the clauses of its algebraicity.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProductSquare
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.twoFibreProductSquare.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} f.hom g.hom).pt.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T2, second assertion: the 2-categorical universal property.** The canonical
square of a cospan of algebraic stacks over `S` is a 2-fibre product in the 2-category of
algebraic stacks, and not merely in the ambient 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids:
the square underlying it is the canonical one there, which is a 2-fibre product
unconditionally, and the 2-category of algebraic stacks is a full sub-2-category.

This is also the **right square of Stacks 06PQ**, whose left square is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_cartesianRelativeInertiaSquare`: the right square of the
diagram there is the defining base-change square of the cospan `(π, f)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFinalTwoCommSq_twoFibreProductSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T2, the 2-categorical universal property.** The canonical 2-fibre product square
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProductSquare` of a cospan of algebraic stacks
over `S` is a 2-fibre product in the sense of Stacks 003Q *in the 2-category of algebraic stacks
over* `(Sch/S)_fppf`, not merely in the ambient 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids: a
final object of the 2-category of 2-commutative diagrams over the cospan, any two 1-morphisms into
it being isomorphic by a unique 2-morphism.

That its apex is an algebraic stack is Stacks 04TF; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProduct`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isFinalTwoCommSq_twoFibreProductSquare (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    Bicategory.IsFinalTwoCommSq (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS g f)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProduct
registrations.comment: the 2-fibre product is an algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_groupoidPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T3: every algebraic stack has a presentation.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack
over `S`. Then there are a smooth groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces over `S` and an
equivalence over the big fppf site of `S` from its quotient stack `[U/R]` to `𝒳`.

The groupoid is the self-intersection groupoid of Stacks 04T4 (4) of the presentation of `𝒳` by
a scheme, which is smooth by Stacks 04T5 (1), and the equivalence is the canonical 1-morphism of
Stacks 04T4 (5), which is an equivalence by Stacks 04T5 (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_groupoidPresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Nonempty (GroupoidPresentation B S hS 𝒳.val)
declarations.comment: every algebraic stack has a presentation by a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.tripleEquivComposable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T4 (2).** The canonical equivalence, in the 2-category of categories over the
big fppf site of `S`, between the three-fold 2-fibre product `𝒰 ×_𝒳 𝒰 ×_𝒳 𝒰` and the
category `ℛ ×_{pr₁, 𝒰, pr₀} ℛ` of composable pairs of arrows of the relation. On fibres over
a scheme `T` it sends `((a, b, α), c, β)` to `((a, b, α), (b, c, β))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tripleEquivComposable :
    StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver (tripleProjection B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f)
      (composableProjection B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f)
declarations.comment: part (2): three-fold product as composable arrows

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.tripleEquivComposable_fst
declarations.doc: The comparison of Stacks 04T4 (2) leaves the first relation arrow unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem tripleEquivComposable_fst (x : triple B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    ((tripleEquivComposable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).hom.functor.obj x).x = x.x
declarations.comment: part (2): first arrow of the comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.tripleEquivComposable_last
declarations.doc: The comparison of Stacks 04T4 (2) leaves the final object unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem tripleEquivComposable_last (x : triple B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    ((tripleEquivComposable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).hom.functor.obj x).y.y = x.y
declarations.comment: part (2): last object of the comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.tripleEquivComposable_middle
declarations.doc:
Under the comparison of Stacks 04T4 (2) the second relation arrow starts at the first
arrow's endpoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem tripleEquivComposable_middle (x : triple B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    ((tripleEquivComposable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).hom.functor.obj x).y.x = x.x.y
declarations.comment: part (2): middle object of the comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.tripleEquivComposable_secondIso
declarations.doc:
Under the comparison of Stacks 04T4 (2) the second relation arrow carries the original
second isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem tripleEquivComposable_secondIso (x : triple B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    HEq ((tripleEquivComposable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).hom.functor.obj x).y.iso x.iso
declarations.comment: part (2): second isomorphism of the comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.tripleEquivComposable_middleIso
declarations.doc:
Under the comparison of Stacks 04T4 (2) the identification of the two middle objects is
the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem tripleEquivComposable_middleIso (x : triple B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    HEq ((tripleEquivComposable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).hom.functor.obj x).iso
      (Iso.refl x.x.y)
declarations.comment: part (2): identity at the middle object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.composition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T4 (3).** The outer projection `pr₀₂`, induced through the comparison of part
(2) by the projection of the three-fold product onto its outer two factors: a 1-morphism
from the category of composable pairs to the relation, sending `((a, b, α), (b, c, β))` to
`(a, c, β ∘ α)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def composition :
    BasedCategory.ofFunctor (composableProjection B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) ⥤ᵇ
      (relation B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.composition_fst
declarations.doc: The composite of Stacks 04T4 (3) begins at the first arrow's source.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_fst (x : composable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    ((composition B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).toFunctor.obj x).x = x.x.x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.composition_snd
declarations.doc: The composite of Stacks 04T4 (3) ends at the second arrow's target.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_snd (x : composable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    ((composition B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).toFunctor.obj x).y = x.y.y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.composition_iso
declarations.doc:
On objects the outer arrow of Stacks 04T4 (3) carries the composite of the two
isomorphisms, including the identification of their middle objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_iso (x : composable B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f) :
    HEq ((composition B S hS 𝒰 𝒳 f).toFunctor.obj x).iso
      (x.x.iso ≪≫ f.toFunctor.mapIso x.iso ≪≫ x.y.iso)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relation_of_isAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T4 (1).** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `f : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be a
1-morphism whose source is a category fibred in groupoids representable by an algebraic space over
`S`. Then the self-intersection `ℛ = 𝒰 ×_{f, 𝒳, f} 𝒰` is representable by an algebraic space.

The diagonal of an algebraic stack is representable by algebraic spaces, which is condition (1) of
Stacks 045G; condition (8) of Stacks 045G follows, and instantiated at `𝒯₁ = 𝒯₂ = 𝒰` and
`x = y = f` it is the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relation_of_isAlgebraicStack
    (h𝒴 : Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val)
    (h𝒰 : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒰) :
    Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relation B S hS 𝒰 𝒴 f)
declarations.comment: part (1): the relation is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism `f_can : [U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` of the presentation datum
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.selfIntersectionPresentation` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fullyFaithful_canonicalMap (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Nonempty ((selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).canonicalMap.toFunctor.FullyFaithful)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.relationTarget
declarations.doc:
The target morphism `t : R ⟶ U` of the self-intersection groupoid, read in the category of
algebraic spaces over `S` of Stacks 02X2: the morphism of algebraic spaces named, through Stacks
04SW, by the first projection `pr₀ : ℛ ⟶ 𝒰` of the 2-fibre product.

On a test scheme `T` it sends the isomorphism class of a triple `(a, b, α)` to that of `a`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def relationTarget : R ⟶ U
declarations.comment: part (4): target morphism of the groupoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.relationSource
declarations.doc:
The source morphism `s : R ⟶ U` of the self-intersection groupoid, read in the category of
algebraic spaces over `S` of Stacks 02X2: the morphism of algebraic spaces named, through Stacks
04SW, by the second projection `pr₁ : ℛ ⟶ 𝒰` of the 2-fibre product.

On a test scheme `T` it sends the isomorphism class of a triple `(a, b, α)` to that of `b`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def relationSource : R ⟶ U
declarations.comment: part (4): source morphism of the groupoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.SelfIntersectionPresentation
declarations.doc:
A presentation datum for `f`: a groupoid in algebraic spaces whose object space is the chosen
representing space of `𝒰` and whose arrow space is the chosen representing space of the
self-intersection, together with a morphism from its quotient stack to `𝒳` and a vertical
comparison of that morphism with `f` compatible with descent.
declarations.statement: structure SelfIntersectionPresentation
declarations.comment: parts (4) and (5), the presentation datum: the groupoid and the canonical morphism from its quotient stack, as a structure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.selfIntersectionPresentation
declarations.doc:
The presentation datum of an algebraic stack `𝒳`: the groupoid
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.selfIntersectionGroupoid` over the final algebraic space,
the canonical morphism `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.canonicalMapToStack`, the
comparison `extendsFQuotient` with `f`, and `eU` as the chosen equivalence of the object
fibration.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def selfIntersectionPresentation (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    SelfIntersectionPresentation eU eR
declarations.comment: parts (4) and (5), the construction: that datum built from the declarations of this file and its three predecessors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isSmooth_relationSource_and_relationTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T5 (1).** If the point `f : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` is smooth in the sense of Stacks 04XB, then the
source and target morphisms `s`, `t : R ⟶ U` of the self-intersection groupoid of Stacks 04T4 (4)
are smooth morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_relationSource_and_relationTarget (hf : IsRelativelySmooth B S hS f) :
    Space.IsSmooth B S hS (relationSource eU eR).hom ∧
      Space.IsSmooth B S hS (relationTarget eU eR).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the structure morphisms of the groupoid are smooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.exists_equivalenceOver_canonicalMap_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `f : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism whose source is
represented by an algebraic space `U` and whose self-intersection is represented by an algebraic
space `R`, and suppose that every algebraic space representing a base change of `f` along a
scheme-valued point of `𝒳` has smooth and surjective structural morphism. Then the canonical
1-morphism `f_can : [U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` out of the quotient stack of the groupoid of
`selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳` is the forward 1-morphism of an equivalence over the big
fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equivalenceOver_canonicalMap_of_isSmooth
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (hsmooth : ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒳.val.p = Over.map T.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B T.left.1 T.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map T.hom) 𝒰.val.p 𝒳.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsSmooth B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS T
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B T.left.1 S T.left.2 hS T.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom)
    (hsurj : ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒳.val.p = Over.map T.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B T.left.1 T.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map T.hom) 𝒰.val.p 𝒳.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsSurjective B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS T
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B T.left.1 S T.left.2 hS T.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom) :
    ∃ e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (Stack.quotientStack (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid).p 𝒳.val.p,
      e.hom.functor = (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).canonicalMap.toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isSmooth_selfIntersectionPresentation_source
declarations.doc:
The source morphism `R ⟶ U` of the groupoid in algebraic spaces
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.selfIntersectionPresentation` is smooth when the
presenting 1-morphism `F` is representable by algebraic spaces and smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_selfIntersectionPresentation_source
    (hF : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS F.hom)
    (hsmooth : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (Space.smoothMorphismProperty B S hS) F hF)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Space.IsSmooth B S hS (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.source.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isSmooth_selfIntersectionPresentation_target
declarations.doc:
The target morphism `R ⟶ U` of the groupoid in algebraic spaces
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.selfIntersectionPresentation` is smooth when the
presenting 1-morphism `F` is representable by algebraic spaces and smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_selfIntersectionPresentation_target
    (hF : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS F.hom)
    (hsmooth : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (Space.smoothMorphismProperty B S hS) F hF)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Space.IsSmooth B S hS (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.target.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_pullback_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T6.** The size of a fibre product of schemes is bounded by the maximum of the
sizes of the two factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_pullback_le {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) :
    Scheme.size (pullback f g) ≤ max (Scheme.size X) (Scheme.size Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_le_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
If `f : X ⟶ S` is locally of finite type and `X` is quasi-compact, then
`Scheme.size X ≤ Scheme.size S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.size_le_of_locallyOfFiniteType {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [CompactSpace X] :
    Scheme.size X ≤ Scheme.size S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
Let `F` and `G` be algebraic spaces over `S`, let `H` be an fppf sheaf on the big fppf site of
`S` whose diagonal is representable, and let `f : F ⟶ H` and `g : G ⟶ H`. Then a fibre product
`Z` of `f` and `g` is an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_isPullback
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hHsheaf : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) H)
    (hHdiag : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (diag H))
    {f : F ⟶ H} {g : G ⟶ H} {p : Z ⟶ F} {q : Z ⟶ G} (hZ : IsPullback p q f g) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_representable_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The chosen presheaf fibre product of two algebraic spaces over an fppf sheaf with
representable diagonal is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_representable_diagonal
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ H) (g : G ⟶ H)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hH : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) H)
    (hdiag : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (diag H)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (pullback f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TA.** A smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is flat: on each commuting
square of étale scheme charts the underlying scheme morphism is smooth, hence flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_isSmooth
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_isomPresheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf `Isom(x, y)` of isomorphisms between two objects of the quotient stack of a groupoid
in algebraic spaces, read on the big fppf site of the scheme the test object lies over, is an
algebraic space over that scheme.

Algebraicity is expressed by a pointwise bijection, natural in the test object, with a presheaf
of `Type u` which is an algebraic space: the hom sets of the stackification are not small, so
`Isom(x, y)` itself takes values one universe up.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_isomPresheaf
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (T : BigFppfOver C S hS)
    (x y : (quotientStack G).p.Fiber T) :
    let I := (Over.iteratedSliceBackward T).op ⋙ (quotientStack G).p.isomPresheaf x y
    ∃ F : (BigFppfOver C T.left.1 T.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u,
      IsAlgebraicSpace C T.left.1 T.left.2 F ∧
        ∃ e : ∀ U, I.obj U ≃ F.obj U,
          ∀ ⦃U V⦄ (f : U ⟶ V) (z : I.obj U), e V (I.map f z) = F.map f (e U z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isoClassMap_holdsOnEverySchemePoint_iff_model
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TC.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` as in
Stacks 03YK (stable under base change and fppf local on the target), and let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
1-morphism of categories fibred in setoids over the big fppf site of `S`, with total objects in
an arbitrary universe. Let `F`, resp. `G`, be the presheaf of isomorphism classes of `𝒳`,
resp. `𝒴`, taken through its `Type u` model, and let `a : F ⟶ G` be the map corresponding to
`f`. Then `a` has `P` exactly when `f` has `P` in the relative sense.

The `u`-smallness instances on the presheaves of isomorphism classes say that `F` and `G` are
presheaves of sets on the site, which the source presupposes when it calls them presheaves. As
in the source ("the lemma makes sense by Stacks 04SY"), representability of `a` is not assumed
but derived from representability of `f` by Stacks 04SY.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isoClassMap_holdsOnEverySchemePoint_iff_model
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage B S hS)]
    (a : CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassPresheafModel.{u} 𝒳.val.p ⟶
      CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassPresheafModel.{u} 𝒴.val.p)
    (ha : IsoClassCompatible B S hS f
      (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassPresheafModel.{u} 𝒳.val.p)
      (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassPresheafModel.{u} 𝒴.val.p)
      (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassPresheafModelEquiv.{u} 𝒳.val.p)
      (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassPresheafModelEquiv.{u} 𝒴.val.p) a)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (CatFiberedInSetoids.inclusion.map f).hom) :
    Space.HasProperty B S hS P a
        ((isoClassMap_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_iff_model B S hS f a ha).mpr hf) ↔
      HasRelativeProperty B S hS P (CatFiberedInSetoids.inclusion.map f) hf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isTwoFibreProduct_productSquare
declarations.doc:
The product `𝒳 ×_{(Sch/S)_fppf} 𝒴` of two algebraic stacks over `S` is a product in the
2-category of algebraic stacks over `S`: the canonical square
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.productSquare` over the cospan of structure 1-morphisms
to the final object is a 2-fibre product in that 2-category.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_productSquare (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (productSquare B S hS 𝒳 𝒴)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TF.** Let `𝒵` be a stack in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` whose
diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, let `𝒳` and `𝒴` be algebraic stacks over `S` and
let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵`, `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of stacks in groupoids. Then the 2-fibre product
`𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒵, g} 𝒴` is an algebraic stack over `S`.

The hypothesis on `𝒵` is the stack clause of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack`, i.e.
"stack in groupoids" in both renderings of Stacks 02ZJ; the sieve-indexed conjunct is what Stacks
04TF asks for, and it is what Stacks 026G
(`CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.isStack_structureFunctor`) consumes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProduct
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (f : 𝒳 ⥤ᵇ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⥤ᵇ 𝒵)
    (h𝒵 : 𝒵.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
      𝒵.p.IsStackInGroupoids.{w} (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
    (hdiag : HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.mk 𝒵 h𝒵.2.isFiberedInGroupoids))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor
        (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor 𝒳.p 𝒴.p 𝒵.p f.toFunctor g.toFunctor))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProduct_of_locallySmall
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒵` be a stack in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` whose diagonal is representable
by algebraic spaces, let `𝒳` and `𝒴` be algebraic stacks over `S` whose hom-sets are `u`-small, in
any morphism universes, and let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵`, `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms. Then the 2-fibre product
`𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒵, g} 𝒴` is an algebraic stack over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_twoFibreProduct_of_locallySmall
    (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{v₁, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (𝒴 : BasedCategory.{v₂, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (𝒵 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    [LocallySmall.{u} 𝒳.obj] [LocallySmall.{u} 𝒴.obj]
    (f : 𝒳 ⥤ᵇ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⥤ᵇ 𝒵)
    (h𝒵 : 𝒵.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
      𝒵.p.IsStackInGroupoids.{w} (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
    (hdiag : HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.mk 𝒵 h𝒵.2.isFiberedInGroupoids))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor
        (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor 𝒳.p 𝒴.p 𝒵.p f.toFunctor g.toFunctor))
declarations.comment: the two algebraic factors with locally small morphisms in any universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TH.** A groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces over `B` is *smooth* when
both its source and its target morphism `R ⟶ U` are smooth morphisms of algebraic spaces.

Despite the name this does not say that the quotient stack `[U/R]` is smooth over anything.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSmooth (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS Z) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.GroupoidPresentation
declarations.doc:
A *presentation* of a category `𝒳` over `(Sch/S)_fppf` is a smooth groupoid
`(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces over `S` together with an equivalence of categories over
the site from its quotient stack `[U/R]` to `𝒳`.
declarations.statement: structure GroupoidPresentation (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{v, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothGroupoidAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TJ.** The algebraic stack associated to a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces
`G = (U, R, s, t, c)` over an algebraic space over `S`: the quotient stack `[U/R]` of Stacks
044Q, fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`, together with the proof that it is an
algebraic stack over `S`.

The underlying category over the site is the quotient stack on the nose
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothGroupoidAlgebraicStack_val`); the algebraicity component is
Stacks 04TK.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smoothGroupoidAlgebraicStack
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS A}
    (hG : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth C S hS G) :
    LargeAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS
declarations.comment: the section's construction: the algebraic stack associated to a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces, as one object bundling the quotient stack with its algebraicity. The quotient stack and its fibredness in groupoids are Stacks 044Q; algebraicity is Stacks 04TK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site, and let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a smooth
groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `A` over `S`. Then the quotient stack `[U/R]`
is an algebraic stack over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_isSmooth
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS A}
    (hG : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth C S hS G) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_isSmooth_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TK.** Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site and let
`G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic space over `S`.
Then the quotient stack `[U/R]` is an algebraic stack over `S`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_isSmooth_of_bootstrap` with part
(3) of Stacks 04S6 supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.bootstrap04S6`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_isSmooth_unconditional
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (hG : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth C S hS G) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStackOfAction_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TK** for a group action: if the structure morphism `G ⟶ B` of a group object in
the slice of presheaves over `B` is smooth, then the quotient stack `[X/G]` of Stacks 044Q,
part (2), is an algebraic stack over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStackOfAction_of_isSmooth
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (G X : Over B.obj) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.left) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS X.left)
    (hsm : Space.IsSmooth C S hS G.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStackOfAction B G X hG hX)
declarations.comment: the quotient stack of an action of a smooth group algebraic space

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsSplitFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TL.**
A *split category fibred in groupoids* over `𝒞` is a category fibred in groupoids `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞`
that is isomorphic over `𝒞` to the category `𝒮_F` attached to some presheaf of groupoids
`F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grpd` (Stacks 0049). The source is explicit that isomorphism over `𝒞`, and not merely
equivalence over `𝒞`, is meant.
declarations.statement: def Functor.IsSplitFiberedInGroupoids (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isFiberedInSets_presheafFiberedInSetsProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TM.** For a presheaf `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type*`, the category `𝒮_F = (F.Elements)ᵒᵖ`, whose
objects are the pairs `(U, x)` with `x ∈ F(U)` and whose morphisms `(V, y) ⟶ (U, x)` are the
`f : V ⟶ U` with `f^* x = y`, is fibred in sets over `C` by `p_F : (U, x) ↦ U`: a morphism
`f : V ⟶ U` and an object `(U, x)` have the unique lift `(V, f^* x) ⟶ (U, x)`.
declarations.statement:
instance isFiberedInSets_presheafFiberedInSetsProjection :
    (presheafFiberedInSetsProjection F).IsFiberedInSets

declarations.name: TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_hom_of_localHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TN.** Gluing maps of sheaves. Given an open covering `U : ι → Opens X` of a
topological space `X`, sheaves of sets `F` and `G` on `X`, and local sheaf maps `φ i` on each `U i`
agreeing on all overlaps, there is a unique morphism of sheaves `ψ : F ⟶ G` whose restriction to
each `U i` is `φ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_hom_of_localHom {ι : Type*} {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (U : ι → Opens X) (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤)
    (F G : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) X)
    (φ : (i : ι) → LocalSheafHom F G (U i))
    (hφ : ∀ i j (V : Opens X) (hVi : V ≤ U i) (hVj : V ≤ U j),
      (φ i).app V hVi = (φ j).app V hVj) :
    ∃! ψ : F ⟶ G, ∀ i (V : Opens X) (hV : V ≤ U i),
      ψ.1.app (op V) = (φ i).app V hV

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafMapGluing.maps_of_sheaves_glue
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TQ — Maps of sheaves glue (existence and uniqueness).**

Let `(C, J)` be a site with fiber products, `A` the target category of sheaf values,
`F, G : Sheaf J A`, and let `{ f i : U i → U }` be a covering of `U` in `J`.  Then any
family of maps of restricted sheaves `φ i : F|_{C/U i} ⟶ G|_{C/U i}` that is compatible
on the overlaps `C/(U i ×_U U j)` glues to a unique map `φ : F|_{C/U} ⟶ G|_{C/U}` whose
restriction to each `C/U i` is `φ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem maps_of_sheaves_glue
    (hcov : Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows Ui f) ∈ J U)
    (φ : ∀ i, RestrictedHom J F G (Ui i))
    (hφ : CompatibleOnOverlaps J F G U Ui f φ) :
    ∃! ψ : RestrictedHom J F G U, ∀ i, restrictHomAlong J (f i) F G ψ = φ i

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.essSurj_toDescentData_pseudofunctorOver
declarations.doc:
**Glueing sheaves.** Let `(C, J)` be a site, let `{f i : X i ⟶ S}` be a covering of an object
`S` of `C`, and let `A` be a category with limits of the relevant size. Then every glueing datum
for `A`-valued sheaves with respect to `{f i : X i ⟶ S}` — a sheaf `F i` on each slice site
`C/X i` together with isomorphisms between the restrictions of `F i` and of `F j` over the
overlaps, satisfying the cocycle condition over the triple overlaps — is isomorphic to the
canonical glueing datum of a sheaf `F` on the slice site `C/S`, i.e. there exists such an `F`
together with isomorphisms `F|_{C/X i} ≅ F i` compatible with the given ones over the overlaps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem essSurj_toDescentData_pseudofunctorOver {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type u') [Category.{v'} A]
    [HasLimitsOfSize.{max t u v, max t u v} A] {ι : Type t} {S : C} {X : ι → C} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J S) : ((J.pseudofunctorOver A).toDescentData f).EssSurj

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isEquivalence_toDescentData_pseudofunctorOver
declarations.doc:
**Sheaves on a slice site are glueing data.** Let `(C, J)` be a site, let `{f i : X i ⟶ S}` be
a covering of an object `S` of `C`, and let `A` be a category with limits of the relevant size.
Then the category of `A`-valued sheaves on the slice site `C/S` is equivalent to the category of
glueing data for `A`-valued sheaves with respect to `{f i : X i ⟶ S}` — a sheaf `F i` on each
slice site `C/X i` together with isomorphisms between the restrictions of `F i` and of `F j` over
the overlaps, satisfying the cocycle condition over the triple overlaps — via the functor sending
a sheaf `F` on `C/S` to its canonical glueing datum `(F|_{C/X i})`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_pseudofunctorOver {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type u') [Category.{v'} A]
    [HasLimitsOfSize.{max u v, max u v} A] {ι : Type t} {S : C} {X : ι → C} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J S) : ((J.pseudofunctorOver A).toDescentData f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStack.fullSubcategory
declarations.doc:
Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮` be a stack over the site `(𝒮, J)` and let `P` cut out a full subcategory of
`𝒳`. If `P` is closed under strongly cartesian pullbacks and locally closed, both read fibrewise
through `IsoOverId`, then the restriction of `p` to that full subcategory is a stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStack.fullSubcategory (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒮) (hp : IsStack p J)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳) (h1 : ClosedUnderStronglyCartesian p P)
    (h3 : haveI : p.IsPreFibered := hp.isFibered.toIsPreFibered; LocallyClosed p P J) :
    IsStack (Functor.restrict p P) J

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoTorsor_iff_points
declarations.doc:
A pseudo-torsor is characterized by simple transitivity on the points of every test scheme
over its base presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoTorsor_iff_points
    (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : 𝒞.Contains S)
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (G X : Over B) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X] :
    IsPseudoTorsor G X ↔
      ∀ (T : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (b : yoneda.obj T ⟶ B)
        (x y : (Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶ X),
        ∃! g : (Over.mk b : Over B) ⟶ G, g • x = y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTrivialPseudoTorsor_iff_exists_section
declarations.doc:
A pseudo-torsor is trivial if and only if its structure morphism to the base presheaf has a
section.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivialPseudoTorsor_iff_exists_section
    (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : 𝒞.Contains S)
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (G X : Over B) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X] (hX : IsPseudoTorsor G X) :
    IsTrivialPseudoTorsor G X ↔ ∃ s : B ⟶ X.left, s ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 B
declarations.comment: part (2): trivial iff the structure morphism has a section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPrincipalHomogeneousSpace
declarations.doc:
A *principal homogeneous space* under a group algebraic space `G` over `B` is a pseudo-torsor
which has sections after an fpqc covering of `B`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsPrincipalHomogeneousSpace : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFppfTorsor
declarations.doc: A pseudo-torsor which has sections after an fppf covering of the base.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFppfTorsor : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSyntomicTorsor
declarations.doc: A pseudo-torsor which has sections after a syntomic covering of the base.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSyntomicTorsor : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmoothTorsor
declarations.doc: A pseudo-torsor which has sections after a smooth covering of the base.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSmoothTorsor : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtaleTorsor
declarations.doc:
A pseudo-torsor which has sections after an étale covering of the base; for a principal
homogeneous space this is quasi-isotriviality.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEtaleTorsor : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsZariskiTorsor
declarations.doc:
A pseudo-torsor which has sections after a Zariski covering of the base; for a principal
homogeneous space this is local triviality.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsZariskiTorsor : Prop
declarations.comment: parts (2), (4): Zariski torsor and local triviality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFppfTorsor_iff_siteTorsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04TZ.** An action of a group algebraic space over `S` on an algebraic space over
`S` is an fppf torsor exactly when it is a torsor on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFppfTorsor_iff_siteTorsor
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)))
    (G X : Over (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.left) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left) :
    IsFppfTorsor B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)) hB G X hG hX ↔
      IsSiteTorsor B S hS G X
declarations.comment: the whole statement: the biconditional over the base `S` itself, with the site-side condition read in the sense of Tag 03AH

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isCovering_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a presheaf of sets on the big fppf site of `S` and let `{S i → S}` be a covering
family of the base, and assume

1. `F` is a sheaf (`hF`);
2. each restriction `h_{S i} × F` is an algebraic space (`hFi`);
3. each restriction is of finite type over its member (`hft`).

Then `F` is an algebraic space.

The refinement of the covering by affines over the points of `S`, Stacks 02WQ and the final
appeal to Stacks 04S6 are `AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isCovering_of_atlas_size_le`.
What this proof adds is the bounded atlas it asks for: the restriction of `h_{S i} × F` to an
affine open `W` of `S i` is of finite type over `W`, hence quasi-compact, hence has an affine
étale atlas (Stacks 03H6), which is locally of finite type over `S` and so of size at most
`size (S)` (Stacks 04T7).
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_isCovering_of_isFiniteType
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F)
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS))))
    (hE : BigFppfOver.IsCovering B S hS ⟨Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)), E⟩)
    (hFi : ∀ i : E.I₀, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (yoneda.obj (E.X i) ⨯ F))
    (hft : ∀ i : E.I₀, Space.IsFiniteType B S hS
      (prod.fst : yoneda.obj (E.X i) ⨯ F ⟶ yoneda.obj (E.X i))) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFppfTorsor_of_isFppfCovering_of_modIso
declarations.doc:
**The glued object of Stacks 04U1 is an fppf torsor.**

Let `{Bᵢ ⟶ B}` be an fppf covering of an algebraic space `B` over `S`, let `G` be a group
algebraic space over `B`, and suppose given for each `i` an fppf torsor `Xᵢ` over `Bᵢ` under the
base change of `G`. If `X` is an algebraic space over `B` carrying an action of `G` together
with, for each `i`, an isomorphism `e i` of the base change of `X` to `Bᵢ` with `Xᵢ` which is
equivariant for the base change of `G`, then `X` is an fppf `G`-torsor over `B`.

The base changes of the action on `X` are fppf torsors by transport along the `e i`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFppfTorsor_of_modIso` applied to the inverse isomorphisms), and the
two conditions are fppf local on the base by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFppfTorsor_of_isFppfCovering`.

The existence of `X` from the transition isomorphisms of a descent datum, and so the whole of
Stacks 04U1, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFppfTorsor_of_descentDatum`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFppfTorsor_of_isFppfCovering_of_modIso (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B)
    (G : Over B) [GrpObj G] (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS G.left)
    (X : Over B) [ModObj G X] (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left)
    {I : Type (u + 1)} (Bᵢ : I → (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : ∀ i, Bᵢ i ⟶ B)
    (hBᵢ : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS (Bᵢ i)) (hcov : IsFppfCovering 𝒞 S hS Bᵢ f)
    (Xᵢ : ∀ i, Over (Bᵢ i)) [∀ i, ModObj ((Over.pullback (f i)).obj G) (Xᵢ i)]
    (hXᵢ : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS (Xᵢ i).left)
    (e : ∀ i, (Over.pullback (f i)).obj X ≅ Xᵢ i)
    (he : ∀ i, IsModHom ((Over.pullback (f i)).obj G) (e i).hom)
    (htors : ∀ i, IsFppfTorsor 𝒞 S hS (Bᵢ i) (hBᵢ i) ((Over.pullback (f i)).obj G) (Xᵢ i)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback 𝒞 S hS G.hom (f i) hG (hBᵢ i) hB) (hXᵢ i)) :
    IsFppfTorsor 𝒞 S hS B hB G X hG hX
declarations.comment: the glued object is an fppf torsor; not its existence from the descent datum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFppfTorsor_of_descentDatum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U1.** Let `{f i : Sᵢ ⟶ S}` be a covering family of the big fppf site of `S` and let
`G` be a group algebraic space over `S`. A descent datum `D` of fppf torsors along that family —
for each `i` an fppf torsor `D.x i` over `Sᵢ` under the base change `Gᵢ` of `G`, and for each
`i, j` an equivariant isomorphism `D.φ i j` between the restrictions of `D.x i` and of `D.x j`
to `Sᵢ ×_S Sⱼ`, satisfying the cocycle condition over every `Sᵢ ×_S Sⱼ ×_S Sₖ` — is effective:
there is an fppf `G`-torsor `X` over `S` whose restriction to each `Sᵢ` is isomorphic to `D.x i`,
compatibly with the `D.φ i j`.

The bootstrap theorem Stacks 04S6, condition (3), is used only to see that the glued torsor of
sheaves is an algebraic space; the glueing is Stacks 04UM and the torsor conditions are carried
along by it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFppfTorsor_of_descentDatum
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS (baseYoneda 𝒞 S hS)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda 𝒞 S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (𝒞.obj hS)))))
    {I : Type w} (V : I → BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 (𝒞.obj hS)))
    (hf : Sieve.ofArrows V f ∈ BigFppfOver.topology 𝒞 S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (𝒞.obj hS))))
    (Vij : I → I → BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)
    (pr₁ : ∀ i j, Vij i j ⟶ V i) (pr₂ : ∀ i j, Vij i j ⟶ V j)
    (hVij : ∀ i j, IsPullback (pr₁ i j) (pr₂ i j) (f i) (f j))
    (Vijk : I → I → I → BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)
    (s₁₂ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ Vij i j) (s₂₃ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ Vij j k)
    (hVijk : ∀ i j k, IsPullback (s₁₂ i j k) (s₂₃ i j k) (pr₂ i j) (pr₁ j k))
    (q₁ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ V i) (q₂ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ V j)
    (q₃ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ V k)
    (hq₁ : ∀ i j k, q₁ i j k = s₁₂ i j k ≫ pr₁ i j)
    (hq₂ : ∀ i j k, q₂ i j k = s₁₂ i j k ≫ pr₂ i j)
    (hq₃ : ∀ i j k, q₃ i j k = s₂₃ i j k ≫ pr₂ j k)
    (D : Functor.DescentDatum
      (FppfTorsors.projection (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda 𝒞 S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (𝒞.obj hS)))) G)
      V f Vij pr₁ pr₂ hVij Vijk s₁₂ s₂₃ hVijk q₁ q₂ q₃ hq₁ hq₂ hq₃) :
    D.IsEffective

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.exists_categoryData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U2.** The category of quasi-coherent pairs over `S` exists together with its
projection to the big fppf slice, and its morphisms are exactly the pairs of a morphism of
schemes over `S` and an `f`-map of modules. The description of a hom-set as a disjoint union
of pullback homs then follows by the pullback–pushforward adjunction.
declarations.statement: public theorem exists_categoryData : Nonempty (CategoryData B S hS)

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.homEquivPullbackHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U2.** A hom-set of the category of quasi-coherent pairs is the disjoint union,
over the morphisms `f` of the base, of the morphisms from the pullback of the target module
along `f` to the source module.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def homEquivPullbackHom (A C : Object B S hS) :
    (A ⟶ C) ≃
      Σ f : A.base ⟶ C.base,
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (Object.schemeMap f)).obj C.module ⟶ A.module

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.isStronglyCartesian_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U3.** An arrow of quasi-coherent modules is strongly cartesian if and only if
its canonical pullback comparison map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStronglyCartesian_iff :
    (projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS)).IsStronglyCartesian
      ((projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS)).map m) m ↔
      IsIso ((homEquivPullbackHom A C m).2)

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.finiteTypeProjection_isStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U4.** The projection from the quasi-coherent modules of finite type on the schemes
of the big fppf site over `S` to that site satisfies the three conditions of Stacks 026F: it is a
fibred category, the presheaves `Mor(x, y)` are sheaves, and descent data are effective. Finite
type is preserved by the pullbacks computing the strongly cartesian arrows of Stacks 04U3 and
descends along fppf coverings (Stacks 05AZ), so Stacks 04TU passes the stack of all
quasi-coherent modules, Stacks 03YM, to its full subcategory of modules of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteTypeProjection_isStack (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) :
    Functor.IsStack (finiteTypeProjection B S hS)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: conditions (1), (2) and (3) of Stacks 026F for p_fg, with Stacks 03YM proved, nothing carried

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.essentiallySmall_isFiniteType_and_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
The finite type quasi-coherent sheaves of modules on a ringed space have only a set
of isomorphism classes.

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.small_fiber_finiteTypeSmallProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U6, smallness.** `QCoh_fg,small` is small: its objects over each object of the
base site form a set. The ambient fibre is not set-sized, so this is the content of the cut; see
the implementation notes for why the bound is fibrewise.
declarations.statement:
theorem small_fiber_finiteTypeSmallProjection (T : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS) :
    Small.{u} ((finiteTypeSmallProjection B S hS).Fiber T)
declarations.comment: the selected subcategory is small: its objects over each object of the big fppf site over S form a set

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.fullyFaithful_ι_finiteTypeSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U6 (1), first half.** The inclusion `QCoh_fg,small → QCoh_fg` is fully faithful,
the subcategory being full.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fullyFaithful_ι_finiteTypeSmall :
    (FiniteTypeSmall B S hS).ι.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: clause (1), first half: the inclusion functor is fully faithful

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.essSurj_ι_finiteTypeSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U6 (1), second half.** The inclusion `QCoh_fg,small → QCoh_fg` is essentially
surjective: a canonical representative of its own isomorphism class was kept in every fibre.
declarations.statement: theorem essSurj_ι_finiteTypeSmall : (FiniteTypeSmall B S hS).ι.EssSurj
declarations.comment: clause (1), second half: the inclusion functor is essentially surjective

declarations.name: Stacks.QCoh.isStack_finiteTypeSmallProjection_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U6 (2), unconditionally.** The hypothesis of
`Stacks.QCoh.isStack_finiteTypeSmallProjection` is Stacks 03YM, and that is
`Stacks.QCoh.projection_isStack`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_finiteTypeSmallProjection_unconditional :
    Functor.IsStack (finiteTypeSmallProjection B S hS)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: clause (2): the restricted projection is a stack over the big fppf site over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spaceHomEquivPullbackHom
declarations.doc: The hom-set equation for algebraic spaces over varying representable bases.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spaceHomEquivPullbackHom
    (A C : Comma
      (ObjectProperty.ι (fun F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u =>
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F))
      (yoneda : BigFppfOver B S hS ⥤
        (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)) :
    { e : (A ⟶ C) ≃
        Σ g : A.right ⟶ C.right,
          (Over.mk (ObjectProperty.homMk A.hom : A.left ⟶
            schemeSpace A.right) ⟶ pullbackOver A C g) //
      ∀ m : A ⟶ C, (e m).1 = m.right ∧
        ((e m).2).left ≫
          (ObjectProperty.homMk
            (pullback.snd (schemeSpaceMap (e m).1).hom C.hom) :
              AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS
                (schemeSpaceMap (e m).1) (ObjectProperty.homMk C.hom) ⟶
                C.left) = m.left }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spacesProjection_isStronglyCartesian_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04U9.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over varying schemes is strongly
cartesian if and only if its canonical comparison with the base change of its target is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesProjection_isStronglyCartesian_iff
    {A C : Comma
      (ObjectProperty.ι (fun F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u =>
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F))
      (yoneda : BigFppfOver B S hS ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)} (m : A ⟶ C) :
    (spacesProjection B S hS).IsStronglyCartesian m.right m ↔
      IsIso (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.lift A.hom m.left.hom m.w.symm) :
        A.left ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS
          (schemeSpaceMap m.right) (ObjectProperty.homMk C.hom))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spacesProjection_isFibered
declarations.doc: The projection from algebraic spaces over schemes is a fibred category.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesProjection_isFibered :
    (spacesProjection B S hS).IsFibered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spacesProjection_isMorSheaf
declarations.doc: Morphisms of algebraic spaces over a fixed scheme satisfy fppf descent.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesProjection_isMorSheaf :
    haveI : (spacesProjection B S hS).IsFibered :=
      spacesProjection_isFibered B S hS
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (X Y : (spacesProjection B S hS).Fiber U),
      (spacesProjection B S hS).IsMorSheaf
        (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) U X Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isStack_of_bootstrap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UD.** The projection from finite-type algebraic spaces over varying base schemes
is a stack over the big fppf site of `S`: it satisfies all three conditions of Stacks 026F.

Conditions (1) and (2) are `AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isFibered` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isMorSheaf`. For condition (3), a descent datum is
read in the ambient comma category, where its underlying sheaves glue
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesDescent.nonempty_sheafGlueing`, Stacks 04TR). The glued sheaf is an
algebraic space by Stacks 04U0 over the base of the datum
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesDescent.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isPullback_of_isFiniteType`), which is where
Stacks 04S6 condition (3) and the finite-type hypothesis are spent, so the datum is effective there
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesDescent.SheafGlueing.isEffective`). The descended object is of finite
type over the base because finite type is fppf local on the base
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesDescent.locallyClosed_isFiniteTypeSpace`, Stacks 041U), which brings the
effectivity back to the full subcategory
(`CategoryTheory.Functor.SieveDescentDatum.isEffective_of_isEffective_mapι`).
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isStack_of_bootstrap :
    (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isFibered
declarations.doc:
**Condition (1) of Stacks 04UD.** The projection from finite-type algebraic spaces over
varying schemes to the big fppf site of `S` is a fibred category.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isFibered :
    (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsFibered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isMorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of Stacks 04UD.** Morphisms of finite-type algebraic spaces over a fixed
scheme satisfy fppf descent.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isMorSheaf :
    haveI : (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsFibered :=
      finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isFibered B S hS
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (X Y : (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).Fiber U),
      (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsMorSheaf
        (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) U X Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeSpacesProjection_hasEffectiveDescent
declarations.doc:
Every descent datum of finite-type algebraic spaces relative to an fppf covering sieve of the
big fppf site of `S` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteTypeSpacesProjection_hasEffectiveDescent :
    haveI : (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsFibered :=
      finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isFibered B S hS
    (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).HasEffectiveDescent (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_small_finiteTypeSpaces_stack_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UE.** There is a strictly full subcategory of the stack of finite-type
algebraic spaces over varying base schemes with set-sized fibres whose inclusion is essentially
surjective (and fully faithful, being the inclusion of a full subcategory) and whose restricted
projection is still a stack over the big fppf site of `S`.

The source deduces this from Stacks 04UD,
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeSpacesProjection_isStack_of_bootstrap`, and the replacement of
Stacks 03ZZ, `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStack.exists_small_fullSubcategory`, which applies because
the category of finite-type algebraic spaces is essentially small; that deduction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_small_finiteTypeSpaces_stack`, whose Stacks 04UD input is discharged
here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_finiteTypeSpaces_stack_unconditional :
    ∃ P : ObjectProperty (FiniteTypeSpaces B S hS),
      (∀ T : BigFppfOver B S hS,
        Small.{u} ((P.ι ⋙ finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).Fiber T)) ∧
        P.ι.EssSurj ∧
        (P.ι ⋙ finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsStack
          (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the small stack of finite-type algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_small_finiteTypeSpaces_stack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UE.** Granted that the projection from finite-type algebraic spaces over
varying base schemes is a stack over the big fppf site of `S` — Stacks 04UD, whose condition
(3) this library does not have — there is a strictly full subcategory of it with set-sized
fibres whose inclusion is essentially surjective and whose restricted projection is still a
stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_finiteTypeSpaces_stack (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hp : (finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    ∃ P : ObjectProperty (FiniteTypeSpaces B S hS),
      (∀ T : BigFppfOver B S hS,
        Small.{u} ((P.ι ⋙ finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).Fiber T)) ∧
        P.ι.EssSurj ∧
        (P.ι ⋙ finiteTypeSpacesProjection B S hS).IsStack
          (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the small stack of finite-type algebraic spaces

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UJ.** An object of the category `𝒢-Torsors` of torsors under a sheaf of groups
`𝒢` on a site `(C, J)`: an object `U` of `C` together with a `𝒢|_U`-torsor on the localized
site `C/U`.
declarations.statement: structure SheafOfGroups.Torsors (𝒢 : SheafOfGroups.{w} (C := C) J)

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UJ.** A morphism `(U, F) ⟶ (V, H)` of the category `𝒢-Torsors`: a morphism
`f : U ⟶ V` of `C` together with an isomorphism `α : f^{-1}H ⟶ F` of `𝒢|_U`-torsors. The
isomorphism is recorded through its inverse on total spaces: a map of sheaves on `C` over `f`
which restricts to a bijection from the fibre of `Total F` over each `a : V ⟶ U` to the fibre
of `Total H` over `a ≫ f`.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (T T' : Torsors.{t} 𝒢)

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.instCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UJ.** The torsors under a sheaf of groups `𝒢` on a site `(C, J)` form a category
`𝒢-Torsors`: morphisms compose by composing `f` and `α`.
declarations.statement: instance instCategory : Category (Torsors.{t} 𝒢)

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.projection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UJ.** The functor `p : 𝒢-Torsors ⥤ C` sending a pair `(U, F)` to `U`, which is
how `𝒢-Torsors` is regarded as a category over the site.
declarations.statement: def projection : Torsors.{t} 𝒢 ⥤ C
declarations.comment: the functor p to the site

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.isIso_of_isIso_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UJ.** A morphism of `𝒢-Torsors` whose morphism `f` of the site is an isomorphism
is itself an isomorphism. Every morphism of a fibre category of `p : 𝒢-Torsors ⥤ C` lies over an
identity, so this says that the fibre category over `U` — the category of `𝒢|_U`-torsors — is a
groupoid.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_of_isIso_base : IsIso m

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.projection_effectiveDescent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UK**, condition (3) of Stacks 02ZI: every descent datum for
`p : 𝒢-Torsors ⥤ C` relative to a `J`-covering family with genuine fibre-product overlaps is
effective.

The object over `U` is glued by hand: the sections of its torsor over `(W, β)` are the matching
families which assign, to every factorization of `g ≫ β` through a member `f i` of the covering
family, a section of `D.x i`, compatibly with the restriction maps and with the glueing
isomorphisms of the descent datum. That this is a sheaf is the sheaf condition for the `D.x i`;
that `𝒢` acts simply transitively on it is the simple transitivity on the `D.x i` together with
the sheaf condition for `𝒢`; and that it is locally nonempty follows because each `D.x i` is.
The morphisms `D.x i ⟶ x` send a section of `D.x i` to the matching family it spreads out to,
whose compatibility over the double overlaps is exactly the cocycle condition of the descent
datum, and which recovers the section it came from because of the cocycle condition at
`(i, i, i)`. Effectivity then follows from
`SheafOfGroups.Torsors.isEffective_of_glueing`.

A matching family is indexed by the objects and the morphisms of `C` and by the index set of the
covering family, so it lives in `Type (max u v s t)`: the statement is for torsors whose
sections lie in `Type (max u v s t)`, which is the same bound `max u v s ≤ t` that the route
through Stacks 04TP and 04TS imposes.
declarations.statement:
theorem projection_effectiveDescent {U : C} {I : Type s} (V : I → C) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U)
    (hf : Sieve.ofArrows V f ∈ J U)
    (Vij : I → I → C) (pr₁ : ∀ i j, Vij i j ⟶ V i) (pr₂ : ∀ i j, Vij i j ⟶ V j)
    (hVij : ∀ i j, IsPullback (pr₁ i j) (pr₂ i j) (f i) (f j))
    (Vijk : I → I → I → C)
    (s₁₂ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ Vij i j) (s₂₃ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ Vij j k)
    (hVijk : ∀ i j k, IsPullback (s₁₂ i j k) (s₂₃ i j k) (pr₂ i j) (pr₁ j k))
    (q₁ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ V i) (q₂ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ V j)
    (q₃ : ∀ i j k, Vijk i j k ⟶ V k)
    (hq₁ : ∀ i j k, q₁ i j k = s₁₂ i j k ≫ pr₁ i j)
    (hq₂ : ∀ i j k, q₂ i j k = s₁₂ i j k ≫ pr₂ i j)
    (hq₃ : ∀ i j k, q₃ i j k = s₂₃ i j k ≫ pr₂ j k)
    (D : Functor.DescentDatum (projection : Torsors.{max u v s t} 𝒢 ⥤ C) V f Vij pr₁ pr₂ hVij
      Vijk s₁₂ s₂₃ hVijk q₁ q₂ q₃ hq₁ hq₂ hq₃) :
    D.IsEffective

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.projection_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UK.** The functor `p : 𝒢-Torsors ⥤ C` of Stacks 04UJ is a stack in groupoids
over the site `(C, J)`: it is fibred in groupoids, its `Isom` presheaves are sheaves, and every
descent datum relative to a covering family is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem projection_isStackInGroupoids :
    Functor.IsStackInGroupoids.{s} (projection : Torsors.{max u v s t} 𝒢 ⥤ C) J

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.projection_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UK**, condition (1) of Stacks 02ZI. The functor `p : 𝒢-Torsors ⥤ C` of
Stacks 04UJ is fibred in groupoids: a morphism `f : V ⟶ U` of `C` lifts to the morphism
`(V, f^{-1}F) ⟶ (U, F)` out of the restricted torsor, and a fill-in is unique because the
recorded map of a morphism of `𝒢-Torsors` is a bijection on the sections over each base
morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem projection_isFiberedInGroupoids :
    (projection : Torsors.{t} 𝒢 ⥤ C).IsFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment: condition (1): p is fibred in groupoids

declarations.name: SheafOfGroups.Torsors.projection_isomIsSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UK**, condition (2) of Stacks 02ZI: the presheaves `Isom(x, y)` on `C/U` are
sheaves. For two torsors `x` and `y` over the same object `U` of `C` and a covering family
`{V i → U}` of `U` whose overlaps are genuine fibre products `V i ×_U V j`, a family of
isomorphisms `x|_{V i} ⟶ y|_{V i}` of torsors which agree on the overlaps glues to a unique
isomorphism `x ⟶ y` of `𝒢|_U`-torsors restricting to the given ones.

The glued morphism is produced by the sheaf condition for the torsor `y` on `C/U`: a section of
`x` over an object of `C/U` is, locally on a covering refining `{V i → U}`, the image of a
section of a restriction `x|_{V i}` under the cartesian morphism `x|_{V i} ⟶ x`, and applying
the given isomorphism there prescribes the sought section of `y` locally. The prescriptions
agree because two local factorizations through `f i` and `f j` factor jointly through the fibre
product `V i ×_U V j`, where the hypothesis supplies a single common restriction of the two
isomorphisms. Equivariance for `𝒢` and compatibility with the restriction maps are inherited
pointwise from the given isomorphisms, and the glued morphism is an isomorphism because a
morphism of `𝒢-Torsors` lying over an isomorphism of `C` is one (Stacks 04UJ).
declarations.statement:
theorem projection_isomIsSheaf {U : C} (x y : Torsors.{t} 𝒢)
    (hx : projection.obj x = U) (hy : projection.obj y = U)
    {I : Type s} (V : I → C) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (hf : Sieve.ofArrows V f ∈ J U)
    (Vij : I → I → C) (pr₁ : ∀ i j, Vij i j ⟶ V i) (pr₂ : ∀ i j, Vij i j ⟶ V j)
    (hVij : ∀ i j, IsPullback (pr₁ i j) (pr₂ i j) (f i) (f j))
    (xr : ∀ i, Functor.Restriction projection (f i) x hx)
    (yr : ∀ i, Functor.Restriction projection (f i) y hy)
    (xrij : ∀ i j, Functor.Restriction projection (pr₁ i j ≫ f i) x hx)
    (yrij : ∀ i j, Functor.Restriction projection (pr₁ i j ≫ f i) y hy) :
    Functor.IsomIsSheafFor projection x y hx hy V f Vij pr₁ pr₂ hVij xr yr xrij yrij
declarations.comment: condition (2): the Isom presheaves are sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SheafTorsors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UL.** An object of the category `𝒢/ℬ-Torsors`: an object `U` of the big fppf site
of `S`, a section `b : U ⟶ ℬ` of `ℬ` over `U`, and a `U ×_{b, ℬ} 𝒢`-torsor `F` over `U`.
declarations.statement: structure SheafTorsors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SheafTorsors.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UL.** A morphism `(U, b, F) ⟶ (U', b', F')` of `𝒢/ℬ-Torsors`: a morphism
`f : U ⟶ U'` with `b = b' ∘ f` together with an equivariant identification of `F` with
`f^{-1}F'`.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (T T' : SheafTorsors G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SheafTorsors.instCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UL.** The torsors for a group object `𝒢` over a sheaf `ℬ` form a category
`𝒢/ℬ-Torsors`: morphisms compose by composing `f` and the identification of the total
spaces.
declarations.statement: instance instCategory : Category (SheafTorsors G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SheafTorsors.projection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UL.** The functor `p : 𝒢/ℬ-Torsors ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` sending `(U, b, F)` to `U`,
which is how `𝒢/ℬ-Torsors` is regarded as a category over the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: def projection : SheafTorsors G ⥤ BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS
declarations.comment: the functor p to the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SheafTorsors.isIso_of_isIso_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UL.** A morphism of `𝒢/ℬ-Torsors` whose morphism `f` of the big fppf site is an
isomorphism is itself an isomorphism. Every morphism of a fibre category of
`p : 𝒢/ℬ-Torsors ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` lies over an identity, so this says that the fibre category
over `U` — the disjoint union over the sections `b` of `ℬ` over `U` of the categories of
