For stacks `𝒮` and `𝒮₂` over `(𝒞, J)` with pullbacks `f⁻¹𝒮` and `f⁻¹𝒮₂` given by supplied
stackifications of `u_p 𝒮` and `u_p 𝒮₂` (Stacks 04WJ), the morphism categories

`Mor_{Stacks/𝒞}(𝒮, 𝒮₂)`  and  `Mor_{Stacks/𝒟}(f⁻¹𝒮, f⁻¹𝒮₂)`

are canonically equivalent. The equivalence is the composite of post-composition with the
canonical equivalence `𝒮₂ ⟶ f_*f⁻¹𝒮₂` of clause (1) with the adjunction of Stacks 04WK at
`𝒯 = f⁻¹𝒮₂`; the direction `f⁻¹` is its quasi-inverse.

Both clauses are conditional on being given stackifications, which Stacks 02ZN supplies once
assembled.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivalenceFibredMorPullbackStack :
    Functor.FibredMor p p₂ ≌
      Functor.FibredMor q q₂

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.isStack_forget_iff_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and let `U` be an object of `𝒞`. The localization `j_U : 𝒞/U ⥤ 𝒞` is a
stack over `𝒞` if and only if the representable presheaf `h_U` is a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_forget_iff_isSheaf (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) :
    (Over.forget U).IsStack J ↔ Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj U)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.isStack_of_isStack_comp_forget
declarations.doc:
**Construction B of Stacks 04WV, at the level of stacks, for an arbitrary site.** Let `U` be an
object of `𝒞` whose representable presheaf `h_U` is a sheaf, and let `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞/U` be a functor
whose composite with the localization functor `j_U` is a stack over `(𝒞, J)`. Then `p` itself is a
stack over the site `(𝒞/U, J.over U)`. This is the source's "in this case it is automatically the
case that `p : 𝒯 → 𝒞/U` is a stack over `𝒞/U`".

No fibre products are assumed in `𝒞`: the proof checks the three conditions of Stacks 026F directly.
A covering sieve of `A` in `𝒞/U` is `(overEquiv A).symm R'` for a covering sieve `R'` of `A.left` in
`𝒞`, every object of `𝒞` mapping to `A.left` being automatically over `U`. Condition (1) is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isFibered_of_comp_forget`; condition (2) is
`CategoryTheory.Over.isMorSheaf_of_isMorSheaf_comp_forget`, through the description of sheaves of
morphisms by gluing; and for condition (3) a descent datum for `p` is read as the descent datum
`CategoryTheory.Over.sliceDatum` for `p ⋙ j_U`, whose effectivity gives back that of the original
one by `CategoryTheory.Over.isEffective_of_isEffective_sliceDatum`. **The sheaf hypothesis on `h_U`
is used only there**, to see that the descended object lies over `A`. Compare
`CategoryTheory.Over.isStack_of_comp_forget`, the same statement under `[HasPullbacks 𝒞]`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.basedStackEquivStackPair
declarations.doc:
**Constructions A and B of Stacks 04WV are mutually inverse on objects**, for an arbitrary site
`(𝒞, J)` and an object `U` whose representable presheaf is a sheaf. A pair `(𝒯, p)` carries no
information beyond `p`, because "`p` is a 1-morphism of categories over `𝒞`" says exactly that the
structure functor of `𝒯` is `p ⋙ j_U`; and the two stack conditions agree, by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isStack_comp_forget` in one direction and
`CategoryTheory.Over.isStack_of_isStack_comp_forget` in the other.

Together with `CategoryTheory.Over.stackConstructionHomEquiv` and
`CategoryTheory.Over.stackConstructionHom₂Equiv`, which are bijections on 1-morphisms and on
2-morphisms compatible with identities, composition and whiskering, this exhibits Constructions A
and B as mutually inverse functors of the two 2-categories.
declarations.statement:
def basedStackEquivStackPair :
    BasedStack.{v₁, v₁, max u₁ v₁, max u₁ v₁} (Over U) (J.over U) ≃ StackPair U J hU

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStack_comp_forget
declarations.doc:
**Construction A for stacks.** Let `U` be an object of `𝒞` whose representable presheaf `h_U`
is a sheaf, and let `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞/U` be a stack over the site `(𝒞/U, J.over U)`. Then
`j_! p = p ⋙ j_U : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` is a stack over `(𝒞, J)`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.stackConstructionHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Construction A is bijective on 1-morphisms**, and is the identity on the underlying
functor.
declarations.statement:
def stackConstructionHomEquiv
    (𝒮 𝒮' : BasedStack.{v₁, v₁, max u₁ v₁, max u₁ v₁} (Over U) (J.over U)) :
    (𝒮 ⟶ 𝒮') ≃
      StackPairHom U J hU (stackConstructionA U J hU 𝒮) (stackConstructionA U J hU 𝒮')

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Over.stackConstructionHom₂Equiv
declarations.doc:
**Construction A is bijective on 2-morphisms**, and is the identity on the underlying morphism
of functors.
declarations.statement:
def stackConstructionHom₂Equiv
    {𝒮 𝒮' : BasedStack.{v₁, v₁, max u₁ v₁, max u₁ v₁} (Over U) (J.over U)} (f g : 𝒮 ⟶ 𝒮') :
    (f ⟶ g) ≃ StackPairHom₂ U J hU (stackConstructionHomEquiv U J hU 𝒮 𝒮' f)
      (stackConstructionHomEquiv U J hU 𝒮 𝒮' g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalenceOver_changeBigSiteQuotientEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The canonical 1-morphism `[f⁻¹U/f⁻¹R] ⟶ f⁻¹[U/R]` is an equivalence in the 2-category of
fibred categories over the enlarged localized big fppf site: it has a quasi-inverse strictly over
the site, with vertical unit and counit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceOver_changeBigSiteQuotientEquivalence :
    Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack (changeBigSiteGroupoid B B' h S hS G)).p
      (pullbackQuotientStack h S hS G).p
      (changeBigSiteQuotientEquivalence B B' h S hS G))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `f : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism whose
source is represented by an algebraic space `U` and whose self-intersection is represented by an
algebraic space `R`, and suppose that every algebraic space representing a base change of `f`
along a scheme-valued point of `𝒳` has surjective, flat and locally finitely presented structural
morphism. Then the canonical 1-morphism `f_can : [U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` of the presentation datum
`selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳` is an equivalence over the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_canonicalMap
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (hCover : ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒳.val.p = Over.map T.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B T.left.1 T.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map T.hom) 𝒰.val.p 𝒳.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        let a := algebraicSpaceMap B S hS T
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B T.left.1 S T.left.2 hS T.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)
        (Space.IsSurjective B S hS a.hom ∧ Space.IsFlat B S hS a.hom ∧
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS a.hom)) :
    Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver
      (Stack.quotientStack (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid).p
      𝒳.val.p
      (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).canonicalMap.toFunctor)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isFlat_selfIntersectionPresentation_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WY for the source projection, flatness.** The source morphism `R ⟶ U` of the
groupoid in algebraic spaces of Stacks 04T4 (4) is flat when the presenting 1-morphism is.

The source morphism is induced by the second projection `pr₁` of the self-intersection, which is
the first leg of the leg exchange (Stacks 003Q) of the canonical 2-fibre product square over the
cospan `F`, `F`; so this is Stacks 04XC at flatness, read at that square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_selfIntersectionPresentation_source
    (hF : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS F.hom)
    (hflat : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (g : X ⟶ Y) => Space.IsFlat B S hS g.hom) F hF)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Space.IsFlat B S hS (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.source.hom
declarations.comment: the source projection of a flat presentation is flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isFlat_selfIntersectionPresentation_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WY for the target projection, flatness.** The target morphism `R ⟶ U` of the
groupoid in algebraic spaces of Stacks 04T4 (4) is flat when the presenting 1-morphism is.

The target morphism is induced by the first projection `pr₀` of the self-intersection, which is
the first leg of the canonical 2-fibre product square over the cospan `F`, `F`; so this is Stacks
04XC at flatness, read at that square, with no leg exchange.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_selfIntersectionPresentation_target
    (hF : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS F.hom)
    (hflat : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (g : X ⟶ Y) => Space.IsFlat B S hS g.hom) F hF)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Space.IsFlat B S hS (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.target.hom
declarations.comment: the target projection of a flat presentation is flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_selfIntersectionPresentation_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WY for the source projection, local finite presentation.** The source morphism
`R ⟶ U` of the groupoid in algebraic spaces of Stacks 04T4 (4) is locally of finite presentation
when the presenting 1-morphism is.

This is Stacks 04XC at local finite presentation, read at the leg exchange (Stacks 003Q) of the
canonical 2-fibre product square over the cospan `F`, `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_selfIntersectionPresentation_source
    (hF : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS F.hom)
    (hlfp : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (g : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g.hom) F hF)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.source.hom
declarations.comment: the source projection is locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_selfIntersectionPresentation_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WY for the target projection, local finite presentation.** The target morphism
`R ⟶ U` of the groupoid in algebraic spaces of Stacks 04T4 (4) is locally of finite presentation
when the presenting 1-morphism is.

This is Stacks 04XC at local finite presentation, read at the canonical 2-fibre product square
over the cospan `F`, `F`, with no leg exchange.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_selfIntersectionPresentation_target
    (hF : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS F.hom)
    (hlfp : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (g : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g.hom) F hF)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.target.hom
declarations.comment: the target projection is locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dualNumbers_projections_not_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WY, the dual-number counterexample.** The cover of a point by the spectrum of its
dual numbers is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and neither projection of its
self-fibre product is smooth. So the two projections of a flat presentation locally of finite
presentation are not smooth in general, unlike the smooth case of Stacks 04T5 (1).
declarations.comment: the projections of a flat presentation need not be smooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isFlat_relationSource_and_relationTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WY**, the flatness half of its clause on the structure morphisms of the groupoid.
If the point `f : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` is flat in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK, then the source and target
morphisms `s`, `t : R ⟶ U` of the self-intersection groupoid of Stacks 04T4 (4) are flat
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`.

The source statement is the remark that the conclusion of Stacks 04T5 survives weakening
smoothness of `f` to flatness together with local finite presentation, and that `s` and `t` are
then flat and locally of finite presentation; this is its flatness half.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_relationSource_and_relationTarget
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
    (hP : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (g : F ⟶ G) => Space.IsFlat B S hS g.hom) f hf) :
    Space.IsFlat B S hS (relationSource eU eR).hom ∧
      Space.IsFlat B S hS (relationTarget eU eR).hom
declarations.comment: second clause, flatness half: the structure morphisms of the groupoid are flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relationSource_and_relationTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WY**, the local finite presentation half of its clause on the structure morphisms
of the groupoid. If the point `f : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` is locally of finite presentation in the relative sense
of Stacks 03YK, then the source and target morphisms `s`, `t : R ⟶ U` of the self-intersection
groupoid of Stacks 04T4 (4) are locally of finite presentation.

The source statement is the remark that the conclusion of Stacks 04T5 survives weakening
smoothness of `f` to flatness together with local finite presentation, and that `s` and `t` are
then flat and locally of finite presentation; this is its local finite presentation half. The
flatness half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.isFlat_relationSource_and_relationTarget`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relationSource_and_relationTarget
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
    (hP : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (g : F ⟶ G) =>
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g.hom) f hf) :
    Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
        (relationSource eU eR).hom ∧
      Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
        (relationTarget eU eR).hom
declarations.comment: second clause, lfp half: the structure morphisms are locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRepresentableDiagonal_quotientStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04WZ.** The diagonal of the quotient stack of a groupoid in algebraic spaces over a
scheme of a big fppf site is representable by algebraic spaces.

The diagonal criterion of **Stacks 045G** reduces this to algebraicity of every isomorphism sheaf
of a fibre, which is **Stacks 04TB**; that result in turn rests on Stacks 04SK, whose last step is
the bootstrap theorem.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRepresentableDiagonal_quotientStack
    {C : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : C.Contains S} {A : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS A) :
    HasRepresentableDiagonal C S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.mk (quotientStack G) (isFiberedInGroupoids_quotientStack G))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isRelativelySmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X0, smoothness of the projection.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a smooth
groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S`. Then the canonical projection `π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of
Stacks 044R is smooth in the sense of Stacks 04XB: it is representable by algebraic spaces, and
every algebraic space representing a base change of it along a scheme-valued point of `[U/R]` has
smooth structural morphism.

Only smoothness of the source map `s` is used. The 2-cartesian square of Stacks 04M9 is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.presentation`, built from the representability of the
projection, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representable_quotientStackProjectionHom`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isRelativelySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X0, surjectivity of the projection.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid
in algebraic spaces over `S`. Then the canonical projection `π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of
Stacks 044R is surjective in the sense of Stacks 04XB: every algebraic space representing a base
change of it along a scheme-valued point of `[U/R]` has surjective structural morphism.

No smoothness is needed: the source map of a groupoid is surjective because the identity arrow at
a point of the object space is a preimage of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelySurjective {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} :
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} C S hS
      (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty C S hS)
      (quotientStackProjectionHom G) (representable_quotientStackProjectionHom G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isRelativelySmooth_isSurjective_of_bootstrap04S6
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X0.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces over
`S`. Then the canonical projection `π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R is smooth and surjective in
the sense of Stacks 04XB: it is representable by algebraic spaces, and every algebraic space
representing a base change of it along a scheme-valued point of `[U/R]` has smooth and surjective
structural morphism.

Representability is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representable_quotientStackProjectionHom` (Stacks
04WZ and 045G); everything else is built, the 2-cartesian square of Stacks 04M9 by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.presentation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelySmooth_isSurjective_of_bootstrap04S6 {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B}
    (hG : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth C S hS G) :
    IsRelativelySmooth C S hS (quotientStackProjectionHom G) ∧
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} C S hS
        (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty C S hS)
        (quotientStackProjectionHom G) (representable_quotientStackProjectionHom G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_pullbackStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X2, part (3).** Let `B` be a big fppf site contained in a larger one `B'`, let `S`
be a scheme of `B` and let `f` be the morphism of sites determined by the localized inclusion.
The inverse image `f⁻¹𝒳` of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over the localized big fppf site of `S` is an
algebraic stack over the enlarged localized big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_pullbackStack {B B' : BigFppfSite.{u}}
    (h : IsContained (τ := .fppf) B B') (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    letI : 𝒳.val.p.IsFibered := 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids.isFibered
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B' S (largerContains h hS) (pullbackStack h S hS 𝒳.val)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDeligneMumfordStack_pullbackStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X2, part (4).** Let `B` be a big fppf site contained in a larger one `B'`, let `S`
be a scheme of `B` and let `f` be the morphism of sites determined by the localized inclusion.
The inverse image `f⁻¹𝒳` of a Deligne-Mumford stack `𝒳` over the localized big fppf site of `S`
is a Deligne-Mumford stack over the enlarged localized big fppf site.
The inverse image is a stackification, whose morphisms are not small, so the conclusion is read
with `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsDeligneMumfordStackUniv`, the definition of Stacks 03YO for a
total category in arbitrary universes.

The source's route: a surjective étale atlas of `𝒳` presents it as the quotient stack `[U/R]` of a
groupoid whose source map is étale (Stacks 04T5, and Stacks 04XC at étaleness), the inverse image
of that groupoid has étale source map, `f⁻¹[U/R] = [f⁻¹U/f⁻¹R]` (Stacks 04WX), and the quotient
stack of a groupoid in algebraic spaces with étale source map is presented étale-ly by a scheme
atlas of its object space followed by the canonical projection (Stacks 04X0 at étaleness).
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeligneMumfordStack_pullbackStack {B B' : BigFppfSite.{u}}
    (h : IsContained (τ := .fppf) B B') (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    letI : 𝒳.val.p.IsFibered := 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids.isFibered
    IsDeligneMumfordStackUniv.{u, w} B' S (largerContains h hS) (pullbackStack h S hS 𝒳.val)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pullbackStack_equivalenceOfSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X2, representability by an algebraic space.** A stack over the localized big fppf
site of `S` represented by an algebraic space `F` has inverse image represented by the inverse
image of `F`, that is by `AlgebraicGeometry.changeBigSite` applied to `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackStack_equivalenceOfSpace (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver 𝒳.p
      (presheafOfCategories (F.obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p) :
    letI : 𝒳.p.IsFibered :=
      (StacksRepresentableCFG.isFiberedInGroupoids_of_equivalenceOver e
        (fibredCategory B S hS F.obj).property).isFibered
    Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver (pullbackStack h S hS 𝒳).p
      (presheafOfCategories
        (((changeBigSite B B' h S hS).obj F).obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
declarations.comment: representability by an algebraic space: the inverse image of a stack represented by an algebraic space is represented by the inverse image of that same algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pullbackStack_representableBy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X2, representability by a scheme.** A stack over the localized big fppf site of `S`
represented by a scheme `X` of the smaller site has inverse image represented by the *same*
scheme, read as an object of the larger localized site.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackStack_representableBy (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : BigFppfOver B S hS) (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (e : StacksRepresentableCFG.RepresentableBy 𝒳.p X) :
    letI : 𝒳.p.IsFibered :=
      (StacksRepresentableCFG.isFiberedInGroupoids_of_equivalenceOver e
        (Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.over_forget X)).isFibered
    Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.RepresentableBy (pullbackStack h S hS 𝒳).p
      ((inclusionOver h S hS).obj X : BigFppfOver B' S (largerContains h hS)))
declarations.comment: representability by a scheme: the inverse image of a stack represented by a scheme of the smaller big fppf site is represented by that same scheme, read in the larger one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ChangeOfBigSite.pullbackPseudofunctor
declarations.doc:
**The 2-functor `𝒳 ↦ f⁻¹𝒳`** from the algebraic stacks over `S` for the smaller big fppf site
to those for the larger one. Its value at `𝒳` is `pullbackObj`, equivalent over the larger site to
the inverse image `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pullbackStack` of Stacks 04X2
(`pullbackObjEquivalenceOver`), and its value at a 1-morphism `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is the 1-morphism
`f⁻¹𝒳 ⟶ f⁻¹𝒴` through which `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴 ⥤ f⁻¹𝒴` factors by the universal property of `𝒳 ⥤ f⁻¹𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackPseudofunctor :
    AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS ⥤ᵖ AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B' S (largerContains h hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ChangeOfBigSite.isEquivalence_mapFunctor_pullbackPseudofunctor
declarations.doc:
**The 2-functor `𝒳 ↦ f⁻¹𝒳` induces equivalences of morphism categories**
`Mor(𝒳, 𝒴) ≌ Mor(f⁻¹𝒳, f⁻¹𝒴)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_mapFunctor_pullbackPseudofunctor (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    ((pullbackPseudofunctor h S hS).mapFunctor 𝒳 𝒴).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasChangeBigSitePresentation_of_isPullbackOfAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X3, the "only if" half of the characterization of the essential image.** If `𝒳'`
is equivalent over the enlarged localized big fppf site to the inverse image of an algebraic stack
`𝒳` over the smaller site, then `𝒳'` has a presentation `[U'/R']` with `U'`, `R'` the inverse
images of `U`, `R`.

Stacks 04T5 presents `𝒳` as the quotient stack `[U/R]` of a smooth groupoid, Stacks 04WX
identifies `f⁻¹[U/R]` with `[f⁻¹U / f⁻¹R]`, the inverse image of an equivalence over the
smaller site is an equivalence over the enlarged one, and the inverse image of a smooth groupoid
is smooth. The presentation is the inverse-image groupoid itself, with the identity morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasChangeBigSitePresentation_of_isPullbackOfAlgebraicStack
    (𝒳' : BasedCategory.{v, t} (BigFppfOver B' S (largerContains h hS)))
    (h𝒳' : IsPullbackOfAlgebraicStack.{u, w} h S hS 𝒳') :
    HasChangeBigSitePresentation h S hS 𝒳'
declarations.comment: the characterization of the essential image, 'only if' half: a category over the enlarged localized big fppf site equivalent to the inverse image of an algebraic stack over the smaller one has a presentation by the inverse image of a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces over the smaller site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isPullbackOfAlgebraicStack_of_hasChangeBigSitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X3, the "if" half of the characterization of the essential image.** If `𝒳'` has a
presentation `[U'/R']` with `U'`, `R'` the inverse images of `U`, `R`, then `𝒳'` is equivalent
over the enlarged localized big fppf site to the inverse image of an algebraic stack over the
smaller site.

The isomorphism `G' ≅ f⁻¹G` identifies the quotient stacks (Stacks 046T) and makes `f⁻¹G` smooth;
smoothness then descends to `G`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isSmooth_of_changeBigSiteGroupoid_isSmooth`). The quotient stack of `G` is
an algebraic stack by Stacks 04TK; its small model
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.smallModel` is an object of the 2-category of Stacks 03YP
equivalent to it over the site; and Stacks 04WX identifies the inverse image of the quotient stack
with the quotient stack of the inverse image.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackOfAlgebraicStack_of_hasChangeBigSitePresentation
    (𝒳' : BasedCategory.{v, t} (BigFppfOver B' S (largerContains h hS)))
    (h𝒳' : HasChangeBigSitePresentation h S hS 𝒳') :
    IsPullbackOfAlgebraicStack.{u, w} h S hS 𝒳'
declarations.comment: the characterization of the essential image, 'if' half: a category over the enlarged localized big fppf site with a presentation by the inverse image of a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces over the smaller site is equivalent to the inverse image of an algebraic stack over the smaller site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isPullbackOfAlgebraicStack_iff_hasChangeBigSitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X3, the characterization of the essential image.** A category `𝒳'` over the
enlarged localized big fppf site is equivalent to the inverse image `f⁻¹𝒳` of an algebraic stack
`𝒳` over the smaller site if and only if it has a presentation `[U'/R']` with `U'`, `R'` the
inverse images of `U`, `R` for a groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces over the smaller
site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackOfAlgebraicStack_iff_hasChangeBigSitePresentation
    (𝒳' : BasedCategory.{v, t} (BigFppfOver B' S (largerContains h hS))) :
    IsPullbackOfAlgebraicStack.{u, w} h S hS 𝒳' ↔ HasChangeBigSitePresentation h S hS 𝒳'
declarations.comment: the characterization of the essential image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**The 2-fibre product `𝒳'_S = (Sch/S)_fppf ×_{(Sch/S')_fppf} 𝒳'` of Section 04X4.** For an
algebraic stack `𝒳'` over `S'`, the apex of the canonical 2-fibre product square of the cospan
formed by the structure 1-morphisms of the stack represented by `S/S'` (that is, `(Sch/S)_fppf`
over `S'`) and of `𝒳'` to the final object `(Sch/S')_fppf`. It is an object of the 2-category of
algebraic stacks over `S'`, which is the source's appeal to Lemma 04T2.
declarations.statement:
def changeOfBaseFibreProduct (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS'
declarations.comment:
the 2-fibre product X'_S = (Sch/S)_fppf ×_{(Sch/S')_fppf} X', which is an
  algebraic stack over S' according to Lemma 04T2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProductProjection
declarations.doc:
**The natural 1-morphism `p : 𝒳'_S ⟶ (Sch/S)_fppf` of Section 04X4**: the projection of the
2-fibre product `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProduct` to its first factor, the
stack represented by `S/S'`.
declarations.statement:
def changeOfBaseFibreProductProjection (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    changeOfBaseFibreProduct B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳' ⟶ schemeStack.{u, w} B S' hS' (Over.mk g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProductPair
declarations.doc:
**The pair `(𝒳'_S, p)` of Section 04X4**, as an object of the right-hand 2-category of
Lemma 04X5: an algebraic stack over `S'` with a 1-morphism to the stack represented by
`S/S'`.
declarations.statement:
def changeOfBaseFibreProductPair (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    AlgebraicStackPair.{u, w} B S S' hS hS' g
declarations.comment:
the pair (X'_S, p), an algebraic stack over S' with a 1-morphism to
  (Sch/S)_fppf, i.e. an object of the right-hand side of Lemma 04X5

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase
declarations.doc:
**The algebraic stack over `S` that `(𝒳'_S, p)` corresponds to (Section 04X4).** The image of
the pair `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProductPair` under the inverse of the
bijection on objects of Lemma 04X5, that is, under Construction B.
declarations.statement:
def changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS
declarations.comment:
by Lemma 04X5 the pair (X'_S, p) corresponds in a canonical way to an algebraic
  stack over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionObjEquiv_changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase
declarations.doc:
**The correspondence of Lemma 04X5 carries the algebraic stack over `S` of Section 04X4 back
to `(𝒳'_S, p)`.** Construction A applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase` returns the 2-fibre product `𝒳'_S`
over `S'` together with its natural 1-morphism `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem algebraicStackConstructionObjEquiv_changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase
    (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    algebraicStackConstructionObjEquiv.{u, w} B S S' hS hS' g
        (changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳') =
      changeOfBaseFibreProductPair B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳'
declarations.comment:
the algebraic stack over S corresponds to (X'_S, p) under Lemma 04X5: Construction
  A returns X'_S over S' together with p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase_p
declarations.doc:
The structure functor over `S` of the algebraic stack of Section 04X4 is the natural
1-morphism `p : 𝒳'_S ⟶ (Sch/S)_fppf`, read through the identification of the big fppf site of `S`
with the localization of the big fppf site of `S'` at `S/S'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase_p (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    (changeOfBaseFibreProductOverBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳').val.val.p =
      (changeOfBaseFibreProductProjection B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳').hom.hom.toFunctor ⋙
        (Over.iteratedSliceEquiv (Over.mk g)).functor
declarations.comment: the structure functor of that algebraic stack over S is p

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseAlgebraicStack
registrations.comment:
the introduction's upshot: given a morphism S → S' of base schemes, any
  algebraic stack over S can be viewed as an algebraic stack over S' (Construction A on objects of
  the 2-category of algebraic stacks)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_comp_p_eq_map_of_changeBase
declarations.doc:
**The scheme-valued points of Construction A are those of the original category.** Every
scheme-valued point of `changeBase 𝒳` over the big fppf site of `S'` is a scheme-valued point of
`𝒳` over the big fppf site of `S`, on the same scheme, lying over a morphism to `S` whose
composite with `g` is the structure morphism of the point's base.

This is the content of the source's remark that the statement of Stacks 04X5 makes sense because
`j : (Sch/S)_{fppf} ⟶ (Sch/S')_{fppf}` is the localization functor at `S/S'`: no information about
the base is lost by Construction A. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_changeBase_p_eq_map` it matches up the quantifications over
scheme-valued points in the two sides of the algebraicity criterion.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_comp_p_eq_map_of_changeBase (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{v, t} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (V' : BigFppfOver B S' hS') (y : BigFppfOver B V'.left.1 V'.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.obj)
    (hy : y ⋙ (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳).p = Over.map V'.hom) :
    ∃ h : V'.left ⟶ B.obj hS, y ⋙ 𝒳.p = Over.map h ∧ h ≫ g = V'.hom
declarations.comment: the scheme-valued points of Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_changeBaseFunctor_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 02ZW is unchanged by Construction A.** A 1-morphism of categories over the big fppf
site of `S` is representable by algebraic spaces exactly when the 1-morphism over the big fppf
site of `S'` produced by Construction A is.

This is the second of the four clauses of Stacks 026O, in the form in which the clause is used:
the clause itself is this statement for the diagonal. The proof is the two halves of the source's
remark that `j : (Sch/S)_{fppf} ⟶ (Sch/S')_{fppf}` is the localization functor at `S/S'`. On
points it is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_changeBase_p_eq_map` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_comp_p_eq_map_of_changeBase`, which match up the quantifications
over scheme-valued points of the target. On 2-fibre products it is
`CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.fstEquivalenceOver`, which says that relocalizing the base
does not change the 2-fibre product of a point with the 1-morphism, as an equivalence over the
big fppf site of the point's scheme; so the representing algebraic space is literally the same on
both sides, and no transport of algebraicity along a comparison is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_changeBaseFunctor_iff
    {𝒳 : BasedCategory.{v, t} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    {𝒴 : BasedCategory.{v₂, t₂} (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⥤ᵇ 𝒴) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S' hS' (changeBaseFunctor B S S' hS hS' g f) ↔
      IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f
declarations.comment: representability by algebraic spaces is unchanged by Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_surjective_changeBaseHom_iff
declarations.doc:
**Relative surjectivity is unchanged by Construction A.** A 1-morphism of categories fibred
in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces has the
relative property of Stacks 03YK for surjectivity of morphisms of algebraic spaces exactly when
the 1-morphism over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction A has it.

This is the *surjectivity half of the presentation clause* of Stacks 026O, which is what Stacks
04X5 needs of it: that clause tests surjectivity and smoothness of the structural morphism of
every algebraic space representing a base change of the presentation along a scheme-valued point
of the stack, and for surjectivity that test is exactly
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRelativeProperty` at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty`.

No statement about the lower-shriek extension of Stacks 03I5 part (2) is needed. Stacks 06D7
replaces the relative test by surjectivity on objects, Stacks 06D4, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjectiveOnObjects_changeBaseHom_iff` transfers directly.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeProperty_surjective_changeBaseHom_iff
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom) :
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, v, w, vP} B S' hS' (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S' hS')
        (changeBaseHom B S S' hS hS' g f)
        ((isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_changeBaseFunctor_iff B S S' hS hS' g f.hom).2 hf) ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, v, w, vP} B S hS (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) f hf
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the presentation is unchanged by Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_smooth_changeBaseHom_iff
declarations.doc:
**A relative property tested on étale charts is unchanged by Construction A.** Let `Q` be a
property of morphisms of schemes. A 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces has the relative property of
Stacks 03YK at the every-étale-chart condition of Stacks 03MJ for `Q` exactly when the 1-morphism
over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction A has it.

At `Q = AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth` this is the *smoothness half of the presentation clause* of
Stacks 026O, the other half being
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_surjective_changeBaseHom_iff`; that case is recovered
by applying this statement to `@AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`, since
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smoothMorphismProperty` *is* the every-étale-chart condition at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`. It is stated at a general `Q` because that is what the separation
axioms of Stacks 04YW need of it: for instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite` is the every-étale-chart condition at
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType ⊓ AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`, and nothing in the
argument is about smoothness.

The relative property is written out as the quantifier of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRelativeProperty` rather than through that abbreviation, exactly as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_baseChange` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_of_equivalences` do: the abbreviation carries
`[P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]` and `[P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage B S hS)]`
as instance arguments and neither is available for a general `Q`, while its body uses neither, so
the quantifier is the same proposition carrying no hypothesis on the property.

Unlike surjectivity this really is a statement about the lower-shriek extension of Stacks 03I5
part (2), since smoothness has no objects-level criterion. The two quantifications match up by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_changeBase_p_eq_map` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_comp_p_eq_map_of_changeBase` on scheme-valued points and by
`CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.fstEquivalenceOver` on 2-fibre products, exactly as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_changeBaseFunctor_iff`; so the
representing algebraic space is the same object on both sides, living over the same scheme over
`S`, and what is left is that its structural morphism has `Q` on every étale chart over `S`
exactly when it does over `S'`. That is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor_iff`: the
every-étale-chart condition of Stacks 03MJ for the structural morphism of the image of Stacks
04SG's forward functor does not depend on the base at all.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeProperty_smooth_changeBaseHom_iff (Q : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (_hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom) :
    (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S' hS')
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (changeBaseFiberedInGroupoids B S S' hS hS' g 𝒴).val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (changeBaseFiberedInGroupoids B S S' hS hS' g 𝒴).val.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (changeBaseFiberedInGroupoids B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳).val.p
            (changeBaseFiberedInGroupoids B S S' hS hS' g 𝒴).val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (changeBaseHom B S S' hS hS' g f)))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S' hS' Q
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S' hS' U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S' U.left.2 hS' U.hom).obj
              ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom) ↔
      (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS Q
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj
              ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom)
declarations.comment: smoothness of the presentation is unchanged by Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_diagonalBasedFunctor_changeBase_iff
declarations.doc:
**The diagonal clause of Stacks 026O is unchanged by Construction A.** The diagonal of a
category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` is representable by algebraic spaces
exactly when the diagonal of the category over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction
A is.

The two diagonals are *not* comparable directly: the self-product of `changeBase 𝒳` over the big
fppf site of `S'` has the strictly larger object set of pairs lying over a common `S'`-scheme by
two different morphisms to `S`, so there is no equivalence to transport along. The route taken
instead is Stacks 045G: by its conditions (1), (2) and (3) the clause is equivalent to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRepresentableFromSchemes`, which does transfer
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableFromSchemes_changeBase_iff`), because a 1-morphism out
of a scheme-valued point sees only one morphism to `S` at a time. The equalizer of the two
morphisms, which a direct comparison of the self-products would have to form, is absorbed into the
already-proved equivalence of conditions (2) and (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_diagonalBasedFunctor_changeBase_iff
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S' hS'
        (diagonalBasedFunctor B S' hS' (changeBaseFiberedInGroupoids B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳)) ↔
      IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (diagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: representability of the diagonal is unchanged by Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_factorization_of_isCovering
declarations.doc:
**A point of the big fppf site of `S'` covered by points coming from the site of `S` comes
from the site of `S` itself.** If the structure morphism of every member of a covering family of
`U'` factors through `g`, and the factorizations agree on every pair of morphisms into two
members agreeing over `U'`, then the structure morphism of `U'` factors through `g`, compatibly
with the given factorizations, and the factorization is unique by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isCovering`.

This is the descent input of the stack-in-groupoids clause of Stacks 026O for Construction A: an
object of the total category of `changeBase 𝒳` lying over `U'` lies over an object of the big
fppf site of `S`, so gluing objects along a covering family of `U'` is only possible when
`U'.hom` itself factors through `g`, and nothing short of the sheaf condition for the
representable presheaf of `S` on the big fppf site produces that factorization.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_of_isCovering {U' : BigFppfOver B S' hS'} {I : Type w}
    (Z : I → BigFppfOver B S' hS') (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ U')
    (hf : Sieve.ofArrows Z f ∈ BigFppfOver.topology B S' hS' U')
    (a : ∀ i, (Z i).left ⟶ B.obj hS) (ha : ∀ i, a i ≫ g = (Z i).hom)
    (hcompat : ∀ (i j : I) (Y : B.Schemes) (u : Y ⟶ (Z i).left) (v : Y ⟶ (Z j).left),
      u ≫ (f i).left = v ≫ (f j).left → u ≫ a i = v ≫ a j) :
    ∃ h : U'.left ⟶ B.obj hS, h ≫ g = U'.hom ∧ ∀ i, (f i).left ≫ h = a i
declarations.comment: the descent input of the stack clause of Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_of_changeBase
declarations.doc:
**The stack-in-groupoids clause of Stacks 026O transfers back along Construction A.** If the
category over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction A is a stack in groupoids for
the fppf topology there, then the original category over the big fppf site of `S` is a stack in
groupoids for the fppf topology of that site.

This is one of the two implications of the third of the four clauses of Stacks 026O. Every piece
of data over the site of `S` is read over the site of `S'` — covering families by
`CategoryTheory.Over.mem_over_map_iff`, the fibre-product overlaps by
`CategoryTheory.Over.isPullback_map_iff`, restrictions by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Restriction.overMap`, and descent data field by field — the hypothesis is
applied there, and the conclusion is read back. The one step that is not formal is the object of
the site of `S` that a glued object lies over: the hypothesis produces an object lying over the
image of `U`, which determines its structure morphism only after composition with every member of
the covering family, so `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isCovering` is used to identify it
with `U`.

The converse implication is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_changeBase`, and the two together are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_changeBase_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInGroupoids_of_changeBase (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{v, t} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h : (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳).p.IsStackInGroupoids.{w}
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S' hS')) :
    𝒳.p.IsStackInGroupoids.{w} (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the stack clause transfers back along Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_changeBase_iff
declarations.doc:
**The stack-in-groupoids clause of Stacks 026O is unchanged by Construction A.** A category
over the big fppf site of `S` is a stack in groupoids for the fppf topology there exactly when
the category over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction A is a stack in groupoids
for the fppf topology of that site.

This is the third of the four clauses of Stacks 026O, in full. The clause is read entirely in the
two localized fppf topologies: a covering family of the site of `S` is one of the site of `S'`
and conversely (`CategoryTheory.Over.mem_over_map_iff` and
`CategoryTheory.Over.mem_over_mk`), and the fibre-product overlaps, the restrictions, the fibre
isomorphisms and the descent data all match. The one non-formal ingredient is subcanonicity of
the fppf topology, `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.subcanonical_topology`, which is what pins
down the morphism to `S` carried by an object of the site of `S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInGroupoids_changeBase_iff (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{v, t} (BigFppfOver B S hS)) :
    (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳).p.IsStackInGroupoids.{w}
        (BigFppfOver.topology B S' hS') ↔
      𝒳.p.IsStackInGroupoids.{w} (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the stack clause of Stacks 026O is unchanged by Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_changeBase_iff
declarations.doc:
**The sieve-indexed stack clause of Stacks 026F is unchanged by Construction A.** A category
over the big fppf site of `S` is a stack in the sense of Stacks 026F for the fppf topology there
exactly when the category over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction A is one for
the fppf topology of that site.

Unlike the family-indexed condition this needs no transfer of covering families and descent data
at all: both sides are read through the single statement that the composite of the structure
functor with the localization functor of the big fppf site of `S` is a stack over the whole big
fppf site, by Constructions A and B of Stacks 04WV
(`CategoryTheory.Over.isStack_map_iff`). Subcanonicity of the fppf topology
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.subcanonical_topology`) supplies the sheaf hypothesis of those two
constructions for the representable presheaves of `S` and of `S'`.

The universes are those of Stacks 04X5 itself: Construction B relates two categories over the
same site in the *same* universes, so the total category is taken in the object universe one
above the scheme universe, which is what `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack` is applied
at.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_changeBase_iff (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)) :
    (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳).p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S' hS') ↔
      𝒳.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the sieve-indexed stack clause of Stacks 026O is unchanged by Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_changeBase_iff
declarations.doc:
**The algebraicity criterion of Stacks 04X5.** A category over the big fppf site of `S` is an
algebraic stack over `S` exactly when the category over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by
Construction A is an algebraic stack over `S'`. Together with the object, 1-morphism and
2-morphism equivalences of Stacks 04WV this is what restricts that isomorphism of 2-categories to
algebraic stacks.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack` is not a conjunction of the four clauses of Stacks
026O: the fibred-in-groupoids clause is existentially quantified ahead of the others, which are
stated for the bundled category fibred in groupoids it produces. So the witness is transported
first, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFiberedInGroupoids_changeBase_iff`, and the bundled object on
the `S'` side is then `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseFiberedInGroupoids` of the bundled object
on the `S` side — the same underlying category over the site, paired with a proof of a
proposition, so the two agree definitionally and the remaining clauses can be transported one by
one:

* the stack clause is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_changeBase_iff` in its sieve-indexed half
  and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_changeBase_iff` in its family-indexed half;
* the diagonal clause is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_diagonalBasedFunctor_changeBase_iff`;
* the presentation clause is the pair
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_surjective_changeBaseHom_iff` and
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_smooth_changeBaseHom_iff`, read through
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forall_isSurjective_and_isSmooth_iff_hasRelativeProperty`.

The presentation clause is the only one whose quantifiers move. A presentation of the stack over
`S'` is a 1-morphism out of the category represented by an object `U'` of the site of `S'`, and
its mere existence forces `U'.hom` to factor through `g`, by the rigidity of relocalization
(`CategoryTheory.Over.exists_eq_map_of_comp_map`); the slice of the site of `S'` over `U'` is then
identified with the slice of the site of `S` over that factorization by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorSliceFunctor`, and in the other direction a presentation by `U`
over `S` becomes one by `(Over.map g).obj U` over `S'` through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorSliceInverse`. Neither identification is an equality of
categories, so the relative properties of Stacks 03YK have to be moved across it; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_iff_of_equivalence_source`.

The universes are those of Stacks 04X5: the total category is taken with object universe one
above the scheme universe, which is where Construction B of Stacks 04WV — the one ingredient
whose universes are pinned — applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_changeBase_iff (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S' hS' (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳) ↔
      IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_of_changeBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X5, the algebraic-stack clause in the direction Construction A reflects.** Let
`g : S ⟶ S'` be a morphism of a big fppf site and let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over
the big fppf site of `S`. If the category over the big fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction
A out of `𝒳` is an algebraic stack, then `𝒳` is an algebraic stack over `S`.

All four clauses of Stacks 026O are carried back: see the implementation notes. The descent
universe of the conclusion is free, because the sieve-indexed conjunct of the stack clause does
not depend on it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_of_changeBase
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w'} B S' hS' (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳.val)) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val
declarations.comment: algebraicity transfers back along Construction A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_changeBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X5, the algebraic-stack clause in the direction Construction A produces.** Let
`g : S ⟶ S'` be a morphism of a big fppf site and let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over
the big fppf site of `S`. If `𝒳` is an algebraic stack over `S`, then the category over the big
fppf site of `S'` produced by Construction A out of `𝒳` is an algebraic stack over `S'`.

This is the converse of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_of_changeBase`, and it is the
statement that makes **Stacks 04X6** a definition of an algebraic stack rather than merely of a
category over the big fppf site of `S'`.

Three of the four clauses of Stacks 026O are the already-available biconditionals of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.ChangeOfBase`, read in the forward direction: being fibred
in groupoids is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFiberedInGroupoids_changeBase_iff`, the stack clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_changeBase` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_changeBase_of_isStack`, and the diagonal clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_diagonalBasedFunctor_changeBase_iff`.
The descent universe of the conclusion is free, because the sieve-indexed conjunct of the stack
clause does not depend on it and the family-indexed one is derived from it at any universe.

The presentation clause is easier in this direction than in the reflecting one, and this is the
asymmetry of Construction A working in our favour. Reflection has to *discover* the presenting
object of the site of `S` inside a presentation by an object of the site of `S'`, which is what
forces `CategoryTheory.Over.exists_eq_map_of_comp_map` there. Here the presenting object is
simply pushed forward: a presentation of `𝒳` by `U` becomes a presentation of `changeBase 𝒳` by
`(CategoryTheory.Over.map g).obj U`, the two slices are identified by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorSliceInverse` — which is exactly
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorSliceFunctor` taken in the direction that makes the comparison
isomorphism of Stacks 0457 the identity — and representability and the two relative properties
cross by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_changeBaseFunctor_iff`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_surjective_changeBaseHom_iff` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_smooth_changeBaseHom_iff`, followed by Stacks 0457
and 0459 in the source variable along that identification.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_changeBase
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w'} B S' hS' (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳.val)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseStructureHom_toFunctor
declarations.doc:
The underlying functor of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseStructureHom` is the structure
functor of `𝒳`, read through the inverse of the iterated-slice equivalence. This is the
`object_structure` clause of the correspondence of Stacks 04X5.
declarations.statement:
lemma changeBaseStructureHom_toFunctor (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    (changeBaseStructureHom B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳).hom.toFunctor =
      𝒳.val.val.p ⋙ (Over.iteratedSliceEquiv (Over.mk g)).inverse
declarations.comment: Construction A on 1-morphisms, as a functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionA_val_val
declarations.doc:
The algebraic stack over `S'` underlying Construction A is Construction A of the underlying
category over the big fppf site of `S`. This is the `object_underlying` clause of the
correspondence of Stacks 04X5.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionA_val_val (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    (algebraicStackConstructionA B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳).1.val.val =
      changeBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳.val.val
declarations.comment: Construction A on objects, on the underlying fibred category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionB_p
declarations.doc:
The structure functor produced by Construction B is the pair's 1-morphism to the stack
represented by `S/S'`, read through the iterated-slice equivalence.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionB_p (X : AlgebraicStackPair.{u, w} B S S' hS hS' g) :
    (algebraicStackConstructionB B S S' hS hS' g X).val.val.p =
      X.2.hom.toFunctor ⋙ (Over.iteratedSliceEquiv (Over.mk g)).functor
declarations.comment: Construction B on objects, on the projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionObjEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Constructions A and B of Stacks 04X5 are mutually inverse on objects.** An algebraic stack
over `S` is the same thing as an algebraic stack over `S'` together with a 1-morphism to the stack
represented by `S/S'`.

Both round trips are strict. In one direction nothing has to be done: the pair carries no
information beyond its 1-morphism, and the iterated-slice equivalence composed the other way is
the identity on the nose. In the other the structure functor of the pair's first component has to
be recognized as the 1-morphism followed by the localization functor of `S/S'`, which is what
being a 1-morphism over `S'` says. The two algebraicity conditions agree by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_changeBase_iff`.
declarations.statement:
def algebraicStackConstructionObjEquiv :
    AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS ≃ AlgebraicStackPair.{u, w} B S S' hS hS' g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Constructions A and B of Stacks 04X5 are bijective on 1-morphisms**, and both are the
identity on the underlying functor. In one direction the commutation with the structure functors
is composed with the relocalization functor and with the inverse iterated-slice equivalence; in
the other it is recovered by composing the pair condition with the iterated-slice equivalence,
which cancels on the nose.
declarations.statement:
def algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    (𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) ≃ AlgebraicStackPairHom B S S' hS hS' g
      (algebraicStackConstructionA B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳)
      (algebraicStackConstructionA B S S' hS hS' g 𝒴)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv_val_hom_toFunctor
declarations.doc:
The bijection on 1-morphisms is the identity on the underlying functor. This is the
`hom_underlying` clause of the correspondence of Stacks 04X5; no heterogeneous equality is needed,
the two functors having the same type.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv_val_hom_toFunctor
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (φ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    (algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳 𝒴 φ).val.hom.toFunctor =
      φ.hom.hom.toFunctor
declarations.comment: that bijection, on the underlying functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv_id
declarations.doc: Construction A preserves the identity 1-morphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv_id (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳 𝒳 (𝟙 𝒳) =
      AlgebraicStackPairHom.id B S S' hS hS' g
        (algebraicStackConstructionA B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳)
declarations.comment: that bijection carries the identity to the identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv_comp
declarations.doc: Construction A preserves composition of 1-morphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (φ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (ψ : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) :
    algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳 𝒵 (φ ≫ ψ) =
      AlgebraicStackPairHom.comp B S S' hS hS' g
        (algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳 𝒴 φ)
        (algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒴 𝒵 ψ)
declarations.comment: that bijection is compatible with composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv
declarations.doc:
**Constructions A and B of Stacks 04X5 are bijective on 2-morphisms**, and both are the
identity on the underlying morphism of functors. The only thing to transfer is the condition that
a component lie over an identity, and that is unchanged by the relocalization functor by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isHomLift_overMap_iff`.
declarations.statement:
def algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (φ ψ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    (φ ⟶ ψ) ≃ AlgebraicStackPairHom₂ B S S' hS hS' g
      (algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳 𝒴 φ)
      (algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳 𝒴 ψ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_hom_toNatTrans
declarations.doc:
The bijection on 2-morphisms is the identity on the underlying morphism of functors. This is
the `twoHom_underlying` clause of the correspondence of Stacks 04X5.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_hom_toNatTrans
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {φ ψ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} (η : φ ⟶ ψ) :
    (algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g φ ψ η).hom.toNatTrans =
      η.hom.hom.toNatTrans
declarations.comment: the 2-morphism bijection, on the underlying natural transformation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_id
declarations.doc: Construction A preserves identity 2-morphisms.
declarations.comment: the 2-morphism bijection carries the identity to the identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_comp
declarations.doc: Construction A preserves vertical composition of 2-morphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_comp {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    {φ ψ χ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} (η : φ ⟶ ψ) (θ : ψ ⟶ χ) :
    algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g φ χ (η ≫ θ) =
      algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g φ ψ η ≫
        algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g ψ χ θ
declarations.comment: the 2-morphism bijection is compatible with vertical composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_whiskerLeft
declarations.doc: Construction A preserves left whiskering.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_whiskerLeft
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (a : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) {φ ψ : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵} (η : φ ⟶ ψ) :
    algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g (a ≫ φ) (a ≫ ψ)
        (Bicategory.whiskerLeft a η) =
      Bicategory.whiskerLeft (algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳 𝒴 a).val
        (algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g φ ψ η)
declarations.comment: the 2-morphism bijection is compatible with left whiskering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_whiskerRight
declarations.doc: Construction A preserves right whiskering.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv_whiskerRight
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {φ ψ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} (η : φ ⟶ ψ) (a : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) :
    algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g (φ ≫ a) (ψ ≫ a)
        (Bicategory.whiskerRight η a) =
      Bicategory.whiskerRight (algebraicStackConstructionHom₂Equiv B S S' hS hS' g φ ψ η)
        (algebraicStackConstructionHomEquiv B S S' hS hS' g 𝒴 𝒵 a).val
declarations.comment: the 2-morphism bijection is compatible with right whiskering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.categoryOfAlgebraicStacksOverSmallerBaseScheme
declarations.doc:
**Constructions A and B restrict to mutually inverse isomorphisms on objects, 1-morphisms and
2-morphisms of algebraic stacks.** This is the whole of the correspondence of Stacks 04X5 as a
single object, assembled from the components proved above; the algebraicity criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_changeBase_iff` is what makes its object map well
defined in both directions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def categoryOfAlgebraicStacksOverSmallerBaseScheme :
    AlgebraicStackCorrespondence.{u, w} B S S' hS hS' g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_schemeFibredCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 026O for the big fppf site of a scheme over `S`.** The big fppf site of a scheme
`X` over `S`, read as a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`, is an
algebraic stack.

It is representable by the algebraic space `yoneda.obj X` by Stacks 04SV, so it is a stack in
groupoids and its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces; the identity 1-morphism
presents it, being representable by algebraic spaces by Stacks 02ZZ and surjective and smooth
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.prop_identityPresentation`.

Taken at `X = S/S'` for a morphism `g : S ⟶ S'` of the site, this is the clause of the
2-categorical correspondence of Stacks 04X5 asserting that the base of the right-hand
2-category is itself an algebraic stack over `S'`; the rest of that correspondence is in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/ChangeOfBaseCorrespondence.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_schemeFibredCategory (X : BigFppfOver B S hS) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (schemeFibredCategory B S hS X).val
declarations.comment: the stack of a scheme of the big fppf site is algebraic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseAlgebraicStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X6.** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S`, *viewed as an algebraic stack over `S'`*
along a morphism `g : S ⟶ S'` of the big fppf site: the algebraic stack over `S'` obtained by
applying Construction A of **Stacks 04X5** to `𝒳`.

The underlying category and its structure functor are `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBase`, which
composes the structure functor of `𝒳` with `CategoryTheory.Over.map g`; the content of the
definition is that the result is again an algebraic stack, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_changeBase`.
declarations.statement:
def changeBaseAlgebraicStacks (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    AlgebraicStacks.{u, w'} B S' hS'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X7, the construction.** The *change of base* of a category `𝒳'` over the big fppf
site of `S'` along `g : S ⟶ S'`: the strict pullback of its structure functor along the
relocalization functor of `g`, as a category over the big fppf site of `S`. An object is an object
`U` of the big fppf site of `S` together with an object of `𝒳'` lying over `U/S'`, and the
structure functor is the first projection.
declarations.statement: def baseChange : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeProductEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The image of the change of base under Construction A is the 2-fibre product
`𝒳' ×_{S'} S`.** The identification is strict in one composite: an object of the strict pullback
is carried to the triple consisting of its object of `𝒳'`, its object of the big fppf site of `S`
read in the slice at `S/S'`, and the defining equation of the strict pullback as the comparison
2-cell, and recovering the strict pullback from that triple returns it unchanged. In the other
composite the object of the slice at `S/S'` is only recovered up to the unit of
`CategoryTheory.Over.iteratedSliceEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangeProductEquivalence :
    BasedCategory.Equivalence (changeBase B S S' hS hS' g (baseChange B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳'))
      (baseChangeProduct B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳')
declarations.comment: the change of base is the two-fibre product over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04X7.** The change of base of an algebraic stack over `S'` along `g : S ⟶ S'` is an
algebraic stack over `S`.

Its image under Construction A is the 2-fibre product `𝒳' ×_{S'} S`, hence an algebraic stack
over `S'` by Stacks 04TF; algebraicity is then carried back along Construction A by the direction
of Stacks 04X5 proved in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_of_changeBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_baseChange (h𝒳' : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, u + 1} B S' hS' 𝒳') :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (baseChange B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳')
declarations.comment: the change of base is an algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBase
declarations.doc:
The change of base of an algebraic stack `𝒳'` over `S'` along a morphism `S ⟶ S'` of the big
fppf site: the algebraic stack over `S` whose total category is the strict pullback of the
structure functor of `𝒳'` along the relocalization functor of `g`.
declarations.statement:
def changeOfBase (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeOfBase_twoFibreProductWitness
declarations.doc:
Under the canonical 2-categorical correspondence of Stacks 04X5 between algebraic stacks over
`S` and algebraic stacks over `S'` equipped with a 1-morphism to the stack represented by `S/S'`,
the change of base of `𝒳'` is the 2-fibre product of `𝒳'` and the stack represented by `S/S'`
over the stack represented by the final object `S'/S'`.

The two 1-morphisms to the base are the structure functor of `𝒳'` and the forgetful functor of
`S/S'` read through the iterated-slice equivalence, the apex is the correspondence's image of the
change of base, the second projection is the correspondence's structural 1-morphism and the first
is the projection of the strict pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem changeOfBase_twoFibreProductWitness (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS') :
    Nonempty (ChangeOfBaseTwoFibreProductWitness B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representableMorphismProperties
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04XB.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
preserved by arbitrary base change and local on the target for the fppf precoverage, and let a
1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` representable by
algebraic spaces *have `P`* in the sense of Stacks 03YK
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRelativeProperty`). Then:

1. in a 2-fibre product square over `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` and `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` with `f` representable by
   algebraic spaces and having `P`, the projection to `𝒵` is representable by algebraic spaces
   and has `P`;
2. if `P` is moreover stable under composition, a composite of two 1-morphisms representable by
   algebraic spaces having `P` is representable by algebraic spaces and has `P`, and so is a
   product `𝒳₁ × 𝒳₂ ⟶ 𝒴₁ × 𝒴₂` of two such 1-morphisms;
3. if `P ≤ P'` for a second such property `P'`, a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces
   having `P` has `P'`;
4. each of the following properties of morphisms of algebraic spaces is preserved by arbitrary
   base change and local on the target for the fppf precoverage, so that 1-3 apply to it:
   quasi-compact, quasi-separated, universally closed, universally open, universally
   submersive, universal homeomorphism, surjective, universally injective, locally of finite
   type, locally of finite presentation, finite type, finite presentation, flat, open
   immersion, isomorphism, affine, closed immersion, separated, proper, quasi-affine, integral,
   finite, locally quasi-finite, quasi-finite, syntomic, smooth, unramified, étale, finite
   locally free, monomorphism, immersion, locally separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem representableMorphismProperties :
    (∀ (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)) [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
        [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, t} B S hS)],
      (∀ (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (max (u + 1) w) v}
            (BigFppfOver B S hS))
          (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴) (R : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
          (_ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct R)
          (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom),
          HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P f hf →
          ∃ h : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS R.fst.hom,
            HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P R.fst h) ∧
      (P.IsStableUnderComposition →
        (∀ (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
            (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
            (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
            (hg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom),
            HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P f hf →
            HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P g hg →
            ∃ h : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (f ≫ g).hom,
              HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P (f ≫ g) h) ∧
        (∀ (𝒳₁ 𝒳₂ 𝒴₁ 𝒴₂ : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (max (u + 1) w) v}
              (BigFppfOver B S hS))
            (f₁ : 𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒴₁) (f₂ : 𝒳₂ ⟶ 𝒴₂)
            (hf₁ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f₁.hom)
            (hf₂ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f₂.hom),
            HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P f₁ hf₁ →
            HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P f₂ hf₂ →
            ∃ h : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (productMap f₁ f₂).hom,
              HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P (productMap f₁ f₂) h))) ∧
    (∀ (P P' : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)) [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
        [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, t} B S hS)]
        [P'.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
        [P'.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, t} B S hS)],
      P ≤ P' →
      ∀ (𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
        (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom),
        HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P f hf →
        HasRelativeProperty.{u, _, _, t} B S hS P' f hf) ∧
    (∀ P ∈ ({Space.quasiCompactProperty B S hS,
        Space.quasiSeparatedProperty B S hS,
        Space.universallyClosedProperty B S hS,
        Space.universallyOpenMorphismProperty B S hS,
        Space.universallySubmersiveMorphismProperty B S hS,
        Space.universalHomeomorphismMorphismProperty B S hS,
        Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS,
        Space.universallyInjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom,
        Space.finiteTypeProperty B S hS,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsFlat B S hS f.hom,
        Space.openImmersionProperty B S hS,
        MorphismProperty.isomorphisms (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS),
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom,
        Space.closedImmersionProperty B S hS,
        Space.separatedProperty B S hS,
        Space.properProperty B S hS,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom,
        Space.integralMorphismProperty B S hS,
        Space.finiteMorphismProperty B S hS,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f.hom,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsQuasiFinite B S hS f.hom,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsSyntomic B S hS f.hom,
        Space.smoothMorphismProperty B S hS,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsUnramified B S hS f.hom,
        fun _ _ f => Space.IsEtale B S hS f.hom,
        Space.finiteLocallyFreeMorphismProperty B S hS,
        MorphismProperty.monomorphisms (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS),
        Space.immersionProperty B S hS,
        Space.locallySeparatedMorphismProperty B S hS} :
          Set (MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))),
      P.IsStableUnderBaseChange ∧
        P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, t} B S hS))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_iff_forall_space_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04XC.** A 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`
which is representable by algebraic spaces has the relative property `P` exactly when, for every
2-fibre product square over a 1-morphism out of a stack representable by an algebraic space, the
morphism of representing presheaves induced by the first projection of that square has `P` as a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.

The chosen representing equivalences are universally quantified, so the condition does not depend
on them; and algebraicity of `𝒳` and `𝒴` is not needed, only representability of `f` by algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeProperty_iff_forall_space_baseChange :
    HasRelativeProperty B S hS P f hf ↔
      ∀ (𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
        (_h𝒵 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒵)
        (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴) (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
        (_hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
        (F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
        (eF : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          Q.pt.val.p (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
        (eG : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          𝒵.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p),
        P (ObjectProperty.homMk (representingMap B S hS Q.pt 𝒵 F G eF eG Q.fst) :
          (⟨F, hF⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ (⟨G, hG⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_iff_prop_representingMap_of_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Properties of Stacks, Lemma 04XD.** In the situation above, `f` has the relative property
`P` of Stacks 03YK exactly when the morphism `V ⟶ W` of representing presheaves induced by the
first projection of the square has `P` as a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.

The forward implication is Stacks 04XC and uses no hypothesis on `g`; the backward one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_of_prop_representingMap_of_fppf`.
declarations.statement:
