declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.GroupoidPresentation.exists_baseChangedPresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `g : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by algebraic
spaces and let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation. Then there is a presentation `[U'/R'] ⟶ 𝒳'` whose
presenting groupoid is of the form `(U', R', s', t', c')`: its object space represents
`U' = U ×_𝒳 𝒳'` and its arrow space represents `R' = R ×_𝒳 𝒳'`, where `R` is the
self-intersection `U ×_𝒳 U` of the atlas.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_baseChangedPresentation
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (h𝒳' : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳'.val)
    (hg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom) :
    ∃ (P' : GroupoidPresentation B S hS 𝒳'.val),
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (baseChangedAtlasSquare P g).pt.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (P'.groupoid.objects.obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p) ∧
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (atlasRelationBaseChangeSquare P g).pt.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (P'.groupoid.arrows.obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
declarations.comment: assertions (1) and (2): a groupoid of the form (U', R', s', t', c') and a presentation [U'/R'] -> X'; the 2-commutative square of assertions (3) and (4) is not claimed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.GroupoidPresentation.nonempty_bcSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Y6, assertion (4).** The square

```
[U'/R'] ---ε'---> 𝒳'
   |               |
  [pr]             g
   v               v
 [U/R] ----ε----> 𝒳
```

2-commutes: the presenting 1-morphism of the base-changed presentation followed by `g` is
2-isomorphic, over the big fppf site, to the morphism `[pr]` of quotient stacks induced by `pr`
followed by the presenting 1-morphism of `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_bcSquareIso :
    Nonempty (BasedFunctor.comp
        (baseChangedPresentation P g h𝒳 h𝒳' eU' eR').basedFunctor g.hom ≅
      BasedFunctor.comp (quotientStackPr P g eU' eR' h𝒳 h𝒳') P.basedFunctor)
declarations.comment: assertion (4): the square [U'/R'] -> X' -> X and [U'/R'] -> [U/R] -> X 2-commutes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.GroupoidPresentation.exists_baseChangedPresentationSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Y6, the whole statement.** Let `g : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
over `S` representable by algebraic spaces and let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation. Then there are a
presentation `[U'/R'] ⟶ 𝒳'` of the form `(U', R', s', t', c')` — its object space representing
`U' = U ×_𝒳 𝒳'` and its arrow space representing `R' = R ×_𝒳 𝒳'` — and a morphism of groupoids
`pr : (U', R', s', t', c') ⟶ (U, R, s, t, c)` for which the square

```
[U'/R'] ---ε'---> 𝒳'
   |               |
  [pr]             g
   v               v
 [U/R] ----ε----> 𝒳
```

2-commutes.

The four assertions are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.GroupoidPresentation.exists_baseChangedPresentation`,
`...pr`, `...quotientStackPr` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.GroupoidPresentation.nonempty_bcSquareIso`; this is their conjunction.
The 2-commutativity is a `Nonempty` of an isomorphism of 1-morphisms over the site, an
isomorphism being data while a conjunct must be a proposition — and asserting that a square
2-commutes *is* asserting that such an isomorphism exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_baseChangedPresentationSquare
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (h𝒳' : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳'.val)
    (hg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom) :
    ∃ P' : GroupoidPresentation B S hS 𝒳'.val,
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (baseChangedAtlasSquare P g).pt.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (P'.groupoid.objects.obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p) ∧
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (atlasRelationBaseChangeSquare P g).pt.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (P'.groupoid.arrows.obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p) ∧
      ∃ pr' : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.Hom P'.groupoid P.groupoid,
        Nonempty (BasedFunctor.comp P'.basedFunctor g.hom ≅
          BasedFunctor.comp (quotientStackMap pr') P.basedFunctor)
declarations.comment: the whole statement: assertions (1), (2), (3) and (4) conjoined

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInGroupoids.RepresentablePresentation.isTwoFibreProduct_relationBaseChangeSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Y6.** The canonical `R ×_{s, 𝒰} U'` is a base change of the relation `R` along
`g`: pasted onto the square of `U' = 𝒰 ×_𝒳 𝒳'`, it is a 2-fibre product of the cospan
`(s ≫ f, g)`. This is the `R' = R ×_𝒳 𝒳'` of the statement of the lemma.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_relationBaseChangeSquare :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct
      ((atlasBaseChangeSquare f g).pasteFst (relationBaseChangeSquare f g))
declarations.comment: R' = R ×_𝒳 𝒳' for the canonical squares; no hypothesis carried

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CatFiberedInGroupoids.RepresentablePresentation.nonempty_iso_baseChangedRelationSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Y6.** The displayed chain of the proof, for the canonical 2-fibre products:
`R ×_𝒳 𝒳' = 𝒰 ×_𝒳 𝒰 ×_𝒳 𝒳' = (𝒰 ×_𝒳 𝒳') ×_{𝒳'} (𝒰 ×_𝒳 𝒳')`. The base change of the relation
and the self-intersection of the base-changed atlas are isomorphic as 2-commutative squares over
the triple product, hence compatibly with the projections `pr_R` and `s'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_baseChangedRelationSquare :
    Nonempty ((atlasBaseChangeSquare f g).baseChangedSelfIntersection
        (baseChangedRelationSquare f g) ≅
      (relationSquare f).paste (relationBaseChangeSquare f g))
declarations.comment: R ×_𝒳 𝒳' = U' ×_{𝒳'} U' for the canonical squares; nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointTopology
declarations.doc:
The topology on the points of a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`:
the supremum, over all charts by algebraic spaces, of the topologies coinduced from the point
topologies of the algebraic spaces along the canonical maps.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointTopology
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)) :
    TopologicalSpace (points B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property)
declarations.comment: the underlying topological space of an algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasBasis_nhds_isOpen_isCompact
declarations.doc:
The quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of a point of the space of points of an algebraic
stack over `S` are a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasBasis_nhds_isOpen_isCompact (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property) :
    (nhds x).HasBasis
      (fun W : Set (points B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property) ↦ IsOpen W ∧ IsCompact W ∧ x ∈ W) id
declarations.comment: fundamental system of quasi-compact open neighbourhoods

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.locallyCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
The space of points of an algebraic stack over `S` is locally quasi-compact, that is, a
`LocallyCompactSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyCompactSpace (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    LocallyCompactSpace (points B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiCompactStack
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack over `S` is *quasi-compact* when its space of points, with the topology
`pointTopology`, is a compact space.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsQuasiCompactStack
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (_h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactStack_iff_hasAffineSmoothPresentation
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack is quasi-compact if and only if it has a surjective smooth presentation by
an affine scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactStack_iff_hasAffineSmoothPresentation :
    IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property ↔
      HasAffineSmoothPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasAffineSmoothPresentation_iff_hasQuasiCompactSchemeSmoothPresentation
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack has a surjective smooth presentation by an affine scheme if and only if it
has one by a quasi-compact scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineSmoothPresentation_iff_hasQuasiCompactSchemeSmoothPresentation :
    HasAffineSmoothPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ↔
      HasQuasiCompactSchemeSmoothPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasQuasiCompactSchemeSmoothPresentation_iff_hasQuasiCompactSpaceSmoothPresentation
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack has a surjective smooth presentation by a quasi-compact scheme if and only
if it has one by a quasi-compact algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasQuasiCompactSchemeSmoothPresentation_iff_hasQuasiCompactSpaceSmoothPresentation :
    HasQuasiCompactSchemeSmoothPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ↔
      HasQuasiCompactSpaceSmoothPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasQuasiCompactSpaceSmoothPresentation_iff_hasQuasiCompactStackSurjection
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack has a surjective smooth presentation by a quasi-compact algebraic space if
and only if there is a surjection onto it from a quasi-compact algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasQuasiCompactSpaceSmoothPresentation_iff_hasQuasiCompactStackSurjection :
    HasQuasiCompactSpaceSmoothPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ↔
      HasQuasiCompactStackSurjection.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactStack_of_isOpenSubstackCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YD**, quasi-compactness. An algebraic stack covered by finitely many
quasi-compact open substacks is quasi-compact; in particular a finite disjoint union of
quasi-compact algebraic stacks is quasi-compact, disjointness of the members playing no role.
The points of the substacks cover the points of `𝒳`, so this is the topological fact that a
finite union of quasi-compact subsets is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactStack_of_isOpenSubstackCover
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (𝒰 : ι → OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hcover : IsOpenSubstackCover 𝒳 𝒰)
    (h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 (𝒰 i).property (𝒰 i).isAlgebraic).val
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 (𝒰 i).property (𝒰 i).isAlgebraic).property) :
    IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_scheme_atlas_iff_forall_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YF, the two scheme criteria.** For a property `P` of schemes local in the smooth
topology, an algebraic stack over `S` admits some smooth surjective 1-morphism from the algebraic
stack of a scheme over `S` with `P` exactly when every smooth 1-morphism from the algebraic stack
of a scheme over `S` has source with `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_atlas_iff_forall_scheme
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS P 𝒳 ↔
      HasPropertyOnEverySchemeChart B S hS P 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_scheme_atlas_iff_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YF, the scheme case.** On the algebraic stack of a scheme `U` over `S`, the
existential scheme criterion for a smooth-local property `P` is `P` of the scheme underlying `U`.

One direction is smooth surjective descent along the presentation; the other tests the universal
criterion, which the identity presentation satisfies, at an arbitrary chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_atlas_iff_scheme
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS P (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U) ↔
      P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_scheme_atlas_iff_exists_space_atlas
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack over `S` admits a smooth surjective 1-morphism from the algebraic stack of
a scheme over `S` with `P` exactly when it admits one from the algebraic stack of an algebraic
space over `S` with the étale-local property `P` of Stacks 03E6.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_atlas_iff_exists_space_atlas
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS P 𝒳 ↔
      HasPropertyOnSomeSpaceAtlas B S hS P 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_space_atlas_iff_forall_space
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack over `S` admits a smooth surjective 1-morphism from the algebraic stack of
an algebraic space over `S` with the étale-local property `P` exactly when every smooth
1-morphism from the algebraic stack of an algebraic space over `S` has source with that
property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_space_atlas_iff_forall_space
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSpaceAtlas B S hS P 𝒳 ↔
      HasPropertyOnEverySpaceChart B S hS P 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_space_atlas_iff_space
declarations.doc:
On the algebraic stack of an algebraic space over `S`, the existential algebraic-space
criterion for a smooth-local property `P` is the étale-local property `P` of Stacks 03E6 of that
algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_space_atlas_iff_space
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSpaceAtlas B S hS P (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS F hF) ↔
      Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas
declarations.doc:
**The existential scheme criterion of Stacks 04YF**, and **Stacks 04YG**: the algebraic
stack `𝒳` *has property* `P` when it admits a smooth surjective 1-morphism from the algebraic
stack of a scheme over `S` whose underlying scheme has `P`.

Stacks 04YG defines "`𝒳` has `P`" by any of the four equivalent conditions of Stacks 04YF; this
is the first of them, and the comparisons of Stacks 04YF identify it with the other three.
declarations.statement: abbrev HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tfae_germProperty_at_point
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YI.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `x` be a point of `𝒳`, and let
`P` be a smooth-local property of germs of schemes (**Stacks 04N1**). Then the four conditions
comparing `P` against the smooth charts of `𝒳` through `x` — every scheme chart, some scheme
chart, every algebraic space chart, some algebraic space chart — are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_germProperty_at_point (hP : GermOfScheme.IsSmoothLocal P) :
    [GermPropertyAtEverySchemeChart B S hS 𝒳 x P,
      GermPropertyAtSomeSchemeChart B S hS 𝒳 x P,
      GermPropertyAtEverySpaceChart B S hS 𝒳 x P,
      GermPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart B S hS 𝒳 x P].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.germPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart_algebraicSpaceStack_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YI, the algebraic space addendum.** On the algebraic stack of an algebraic space
`F` over `S` the four conditions say that `F` has property `P` at the corresponding point of `F`,
in the sense of **Stacks 04RC**. The chart realizing the existential condition is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem germPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart_algebraicSpaceStack_iff
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (z : Space.points B S hS F) (P : GermOfScheme.{u} → Prop)
    (hP : GermOfScheme.IsSmoothLocal P) :
    GermPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart B S hS (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS F hF)
        (spacePointMap B S hS F (fibredCategory B S hS F)
          (BasedFunctor.id (fibredCategory B S hS F).val) z) P ↔
      Space.HasPropertyAtPoint B S hS F z P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.germPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart_yoneda_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YI, the representable addendum.** On the algebraic stack of a scheme `U` over `S`
the four conditions say that the germ of `U` at the corresponding scheme point has `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem germPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart_yoneda_iff (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (p : Space.FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) (P : GermOfScheme.{u} → Prop)
    (hP : GermOfScheme.IsSmoothLocal P) :
    GermPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart B S hS
        (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS (yoneda.obj U)
          (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS U))
        (spacePointMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) (fibredCategory B S hS (yoneda.obj U))
          (BasedFunctor.id (fibredCategory B S hS (yoneda.obj U)).val)
          (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U))) P ↔
      P ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U, Space.schemePoint B S hS U p⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasPropertyAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YJ.** Let `P` be a property of germs of schemes which is smooth local (**Stacks
04N1**), let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `x` be a point of `𝒳` (**Stacks 04XG**).
Then `𝒳` *has property* `P` *at* `x` when some smooth chart of `𝒳` by an algebraic space has
property `P` at some point of it lying over `x`, in the sense of **Stacks 04RC**.

The source defines this by any of the four equivalent conditions of **Stacks 04YI**; this is the
fourth of them, and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tfae_germProperty_at_point` identifies it with the
other three for a smooth-local `P`, which is what makes the choice immaterial. As for **Stacks
04RC**, stating this one condition needs neither that hypothesis nor surjectivity of the chart.
Its specializations are the two addenda above:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.germPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart_algebraicSpaceStack_iff` on the algebraic
stack of an algebraic space and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.germPropertyAtSomeSpaceChart_yoneda_iff` on that of a scheme.
declarations.statement: abbrev HasPropertyAtPoint : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YL**, part (1). A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is an *open immersion*
when it is representable by algebraic spaces and is an open immersion in the sense of Stacks
04XB.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsOpenImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YL**, part (2). A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is a *closed immersion*
when it is representable by algebraic spaces and is a closed immersion in the sense of Stacks
04XB.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsClosedImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YL**, part (3). A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is an *immersion* when
it is representable by algebraic spaces and is an immersion in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YM**, part (1). An *open substack* of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is a
strictly full subcategory of `𝒳` which is an algebraic stack and whose canonical inclusion into
`𝒳` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement: structure OpenSubstack (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.ext
declarations.doc: Two open substacks with the same objects are equal.
declarations.statement:
theorem OpenSubstack.ext {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {U V : OpenSubstack 𝒳}
    (h : U.property = V.property) : U = V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fullSubcategoryInclusion_obj
declarations.doc: On objects, the canonical inclusion forgets the membership proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullSubcategoryInclusion_obj (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
    (X : P.FullSubcategory) :
    (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP).hom.hom.toFunctor.obj X = X.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fullSubcategoryInclusion_map
declarations.doc: On morphisms, the canonical inclusion forgets the membership proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullSubcategoryInclusion_map (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
    {X Y : P.FullSubcategory} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP).hom.hom.toFunctor.map f = f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsClosedSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YM**, part (2). A property of the objects of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S`
selects a *closed substack* when it is closed under isomorphism, its full subcategory is an
algebraic stack, and the canonical inclusion of that full subcategory into `𝒳` is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsClosedSubstack (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsLocallyClosedSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YM**, part (3). A property of the objects of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S`
selects a *locally closed substack* when it is closed under isomorphism, its full subcategory is
an algebraic stack, and the canonical inclusion of that full subcategory into `𝒳` is an
immersion.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLocallyClosedSubstack (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isImmersion_quotientStackMap_of_invariantRestrictionBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YN**, the immersion. For a smooth groupoid `G` in algebraic spaces and an invariant
locally closed subspace `Z` of its object space, the 1-morphism `[Z/R_Z] ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044B
is an immersion of algebraic stacks: it is representable by algebraic spaces and an immersion in
the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_quotientStackMap_of_invariantRestrictionBaseChange
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (hG : IsSmooth C S hS G)
    {Z : Subfunctor G.objects.obj} (hZ : IsInvariantLocallyClosed G Z) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS
        (quotientStackMapHom (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).hom).hom ∧
      Stack.IsImmersion C S hS
        (quotientStackMapHom (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).hom)
declarations.comment: the immersion [Z/R_Z] ⟶ [U/R] for an invariant locally closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isOpenImmersion_quotientStackMap_of_invariantRestrictionBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YN**, the open immersion. For a smooth groupoid `G` in algebraic spaces and an
invariant open subspace `Z` of its object space, the 1-morphism `[Z/R_Z] ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044B
is an open immersion of algebraic stacks: it is representable by algebraic spaces and an open
immersion in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_quotientStackMap_of_invariantRestrictionBaseChange
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (hG : IsSmooth C S hS G)
    {Z : Subfunctor G.objects.obj} (hZ : IsInvariantOpen G Z) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS
        (quotientStackMapHom (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).hom).hom ∧
      Stack.IsOpenImmersion C S hS
        (quotientStackMapHom (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).hom)
declarations.comment: the open immersion [Z/R_Z] ⟶ [U/R] for an invariant open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedImmersion_quotientStackMap_of_invariantRestrictionBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YN**, the closed immersion. For a smooth groupoid `G` in algebraic spaces and an
invariant closed subspace `Z` of its object space, the 1-morphism `[Z/R_Z] ⟶ [U/R]` of
Stacks 044B is a closed immersion of algebraic stacks: it is representable by algebraic spaces and
a closed immersion in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_quotientStackMap_of_invariantRestrictionBaseChange
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (hG : IsSmooth C S hS G)
    {Z : Subfunctor G.objects.obj} (hZ : IsInvariantClosed G Z) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS
        (quotientStackMapHom (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).hom).hom ∧
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion C S hS
        (quotientStackMapHom (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).hom)
declarations.comment: the closed immersion [Z/R_Z] ⟶ [U/R] for an invariant closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOver_isGroupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YP, part (1).** For an object `y` of the fibre category of an algebraic stack `𝒳`
over a scheme `T` of the big fppf site of `S`, `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` is a group algebraic space over
`T`: the group object `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` over the base `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.siteTerminalSpace`,
with the group structure `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverGrpObj`, is (on the nose) an
object of the category `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace` of group algebraic spaces
over `T`, and its multiplication is composition of local automorphisms
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceComp`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isomSpaceOver_isGroupAlgebraicSpace (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y) := isomSpaceOverGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 U y
    (∃ G : Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 (siteTerminalSpace B S hS U)
        (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B U.left.1 U.left.2
          (⊤_ (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2))),
        G.obj = Grp.mk (isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)) ∧
      ∀ (Q : Over (siteTerminalSpace B S hS U)) (a b : Q ⟶ isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)
        (V : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ) (t : Q.left.obj V),
        ((CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift a b ≫
          MonObj.mul (X := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)).left.app V) t =
          isomSpaceComp B S hS 𝒳 U y V ((a.left.app V) t) ((b.left.app V) t)
declarations.comment: part (1): Isom(y, y) is a group algebraic space over T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverGrpObj_mul
declarations.doc:
**The group law of `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` is composition of local automorphisms.** On a pair of
sections of `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` over a test object `Q`, the multiplication of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverGrpObj` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceComp`, i.e. reverse categorical composition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isomSpaceOverGrpObj_mul (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U)
    (Q : Over (siteTerminalSpace B S hS U))
    (a b : Q ⟶ isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)
    (V : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ) (t : Q.left.obj V) :
    (letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y) :=
      isomSpaceOverGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 U y;
      ((CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift a b ≫
        MonObj.mul (X := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)).left.app V) t =
      isomSpaceComp B S hS 𝒳 U y V
        ((a.left.app V) t)
        ((b.left.app V) t))
declarations.comment: part (1): the group law is composition of automorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverModObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YP, part (2): the action.** `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` acts on `Isom_𝒳(x, y)` over
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.siteTerminalSpace`, by postcomposition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isomSpaceOverModObj
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (x y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    let G := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y
    let P := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U x y
    letI : GrpObj G := isomSpaceOverGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 U y
    ModObj G P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverModObj_smul
declarations.doc:
**The action of `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` on `Isom_𝒳(x, y)` is postcomposition.** On a section of
`Isom_𝒳(y, y)` and a section of `Isom_𝒳(x, y)` over a test object `Q`, the action of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverModObj` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceSmul`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isomSpaceOverModObj_smul
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (x y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U)
    (Q : Over (siteTerminalSpace B S hS U))
    (g : Q ⟶ isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)
    (p : Q ⟶ isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U x y)
    (V : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ) (t : Q.left.obj V) :
    (letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y) :=
      isomSpaceOverGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 U y;
      letI : ModObj (isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)
        (isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U x y) :=
        isomSpaceOverModObj B S hS 𝒳 U x y;
      ((CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift g p ≫
        ModObj.smul (M := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y)
          (X := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U x y)).left.app V) t) =
      isomSpaceSmul B S hS 𝒳 U x y V ((p.left.app V) t) ((g.left.app V) t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOver_isPseudoTorsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YP, part (2).** `Isom_𝒳(x, y)` is a pseudo-torsor under `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` over `U`:
the shear map `(g, p) ↦ (p ≫ g, p)` is an isomorphism, because for two local isomorphisms
`p, q : x ⟶ y` the unique local automorphism `g` of `y` with `p ≫ g = q` is `p⁻¹ ≫ q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isomSpaceOver_isPseudoTorsor
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    let G := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U y y
    let P := isomSpaceOver B S hS 𝒳 U x y
    letI : GrpObj G := isomSpaceOverGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 U y
    letI : ModObj G P := isomSpaceOverModObj B S hS 𝒳 U x y
    IsPseudoTorsor G P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.automorphismGroupSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YP, part (1).** For an object `y` of the fibre category of an algebraic stack `𝒳`
over a scheme `T` of the big fppf site of `S`, the automorphisms of `y` form a group algebraic
space over `T`: the presheaf `Isom_𝒳(y, y)` is an algebraic space
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_isomSpace`) and it carries the group object structure
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverGrpObj`, whose law is composition of local automorphisms by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverGrpObj_mul`.
declarations.statement:
def automorphismGroupSpace (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 (siteTerminalSpace B S hS U)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B U.left.1 U.left.2
        (⊤_ (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mono_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YQ, part (3).** The relative diagonal of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
the big fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces is a monomorphism: it is
representable by algebraic spaces, and every algebraic space representing one of its base
changes along a scheme-valued point of `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` has monomorphic structural morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    ∃ _hΔ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom),
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p
          = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p
            (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p y
            (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom).toFunctor)
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Mono (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YQ, part (4).** The relative diagonal of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
the big fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces is separated: it is
representable by algebraic spaces, and every algebraic space representing one of its base
changes along a scheme-valued point of `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` has separated structural morphism.

By part (3) that structural morphism is a monomorphism, and a monomorphism of algebraic spaces
is separated (Stacks 042N).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    ∃ _hΔ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom),
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p
          = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p
            (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p y
            (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom).toFunctor)
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsSeparated B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YQ, part (5).** The relative diagonal of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
the big fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces is locally quasi-finite: it
is representable by algebraic spaces, and every algebraic space representing one of its base
changes along a scheme-valued point of `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` has locally quasi-finite structural
morphism.

That structural morphism is a monomorphism by part (3) and its represented base changes are
locally of finite type by part (2) for a representable 1-morphism
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.presheaf_locallyOfFiniteType_relativeDiagonal`), so Stacks 0463
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces :
    ∃ _hΔ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom),
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p
          = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p
            (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p y
            (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom).toFunctor)
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YQ, part (2).** The relative diagonal of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
the big fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces is locally of finite type:
it is representable by algebraic spaces, and every algebraic space representing one of its base
changes along a scheme-valued point of `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` has locally-of-finite-type structural
morphism — the every-étale-chart form of part (1) of Stacks 03XF.

This is read off part (5), the every-chart condition being monotone in the tested property of
scheme morphisms, local finite type being the first conjunct of the meet part (5) is proved at.

The hypothesis is the source's own: Stacks 04YQ asserts all five parts for a 1-morphism
representable by algebraic spaces. The statement asserted for an *arbitrary* 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks is part (2) of **Stacks 04XS**, which rests on Stacks 04XR and is proved in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/RelativeDiagonalFiniteType.lean`; see the implementation
notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces :
    ∃ _hΔ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom),
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p
          = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p
            (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p y
            (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom).toFunctor)
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableMorphism_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
The relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` of a 1-morphism `f` of algebraic stacks
over the big fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces is a *representable*
1-morphism in the sense of Stacks 02Y7 — representable by objects of the site, that is by
schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableMorphism_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳.val.val.p
      (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒳.val 𝒳.val f.hom.hom f.hom.hom).val.p
      (relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom.hom).toFunctor

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.baseChangeDiagonalSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YR.** The structural 2-cell `r ⋙ Δ_{X/Y} ≅ Δ_{U/V} ⋙ (r × r)` of the base-change
square for the diagonal. Both composites have both projections equal to `r = π₁ h s`, so the
2-cell is the canonical one with identity projections.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeDiagonalSquareIso :
    (π₁ h s ⋙ relativeDiagonal h) ≅ (relativeDiagonal (π₂ h s) ⋙ mapDiag h s)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.baseChangeDiagonalSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YR.** The base-change square for the diagonal, over `U = h ⊡ s`: its legs are
`r = π₁ h s : U ⥤ X` and `Δ_{U/V} = relativeDiagonal (π₂ h s) : U ⥤ U ×_V U`, its cospan is
`Δ_{X/Y} = relativeDiagonal h : X ⥤ X ×_Y X` and `r × r = mapDiag h s`, and its structural
2-cell is `baseChangeDiagonalSquareIso`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeDiagonalSquare :
    CatCommSqOver (relativeDiagonal h) (mapDiag h s) (h ⊡ s)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.isEquivalence_baseChangeDiagonalComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YR.** The diagonal is stable under base change: for `h : X ⥤ Y` and `s : V ⥤ Y`,
with `U = X ×_Y V`, `r = π₁ h s` and `g = π₂ h s`, the square
`Δ_{U/V} : U ⥤ U ×_V U`, `r : U ⥤ X` over `Δ_{X/Y} : X ⥤ X ×_Y X`, `r × r : U ×_V U ⥤ X ×_Y X`
is 2-cartesian, i.e. its comparison functor `U ⥤ Δ_{X/Y} ⊡ (r × r)` is an equivalence of
categories. The quasi-inverse is `baseChangeDiagonalInverse`, the unit is an identity by
`baseChangeDiagonalComparison_comp_inverse`, and the counit is
`baseChangeDiagonalCounitIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_baseChangeDiagonalComparison :
    Functor.IsEquivalence (comparison (relativeDiagonal h) (mapDiag h s)
      (baseChangeDiagonalSquare h s))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_tfae :
    List.TFAE
      [IsSeparated B S hS f.hom,
       AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
         (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom
           (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom) :
             𝒳 ⟶ relativeDiagonalTargetStack B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f),
       IsProper B S hS (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom),
       UniversallyClosed B S hS
         (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiCompact_relativeDiagonal_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
If the relative diagonal `Δ_f` of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is of finite
type, then it is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_relativeDiagonal_of_isFiniteType (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (h : Stack.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val f.hom)) :
    Stack.IsQuasiCompact.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFiniteType_relativeDiagonal_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
If the relative diagonal `Δ_f` of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces is quasi-compact, then it is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_relativeDiagonal_of_isQuasiCompact (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom)
    (h : Stack.IsQuasiCompact.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val f.hom)) :
    Stack.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_relativeDiagonal_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YT.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces and write `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` for its relative
diagonal. The following are equivalent, each in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB:

1. `f` is quasi-separated: every algebraic space representing the base change of `f` along a
   scheme-valued point of `𝒴` is quasi-separated over it;
2. `Δ_f` is quasi-compact;
3. `Δ_f` is of finite type.

Condition (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiSeparated`, not Definition 04YW.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_relativeDiagonal_tfae (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    List.TFAE
      [Stack.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom,
       Stack.IsQuasiCompact.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
         (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val f.hom),
       Stack.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
         (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val f.hom)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallySeparated_iff_isImmersion_relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YU.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces. Then `f` is locally separated, in the relative sense of
Stacks 04XB, if and only if its relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` is an immersion
of algebraic stacks, part (3) of Stacks 04YL.

The content is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallySeparated_iff_isImmersion_relativeDiagonal`; the
representability clause that part (3) of Stacks 04YL carries on top of the quantifier of
Stacks 04XB is automatic, by part (1) of Stacks 04XS in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_algebraicStacks`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySeparated_iff_isImmersion_relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks :
    IsLocallySeparated B S hS f.hom ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsImmersion B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YW, the DM condition.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is
*Deligne–Mumford* when its relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and
unramified, the latter in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK: every algebraic space representing
a base change of the diagonal along a scheme-valued point of `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` has unramified
structural morphism.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsDM {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YW, quasi-DM.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *quasi-DM* when its
relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` is locally quasi-finite in the sense of Stacks
04XB.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiDM (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YW, separated.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *separated* when its
relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` is proper in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YW, quasi-separated.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is
*quasi-separated* when its relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, both in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isEquivalence_secondRelativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YY, the implication (2) ⟹ (1).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` whose
second diagonal `Δ_{f, 2}` is an isomorphism is representable by algebraic spaces: the second
diagonal is an isomorphism exactly when `f` is faithful (Stacks 04Z7), and a faithful 1-morphism
of algebraic stacks is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 04Y5).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isEquivalence_secondRelativeDiagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Functor.IsEquivalence (secondRelativeDiagonal B S hS f.hom).hom.toFunctor) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_tfae (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom,
        Functor.IsEquivalence (secondRelativeDiagonal B S hS f.hom).hom.toFunctor,
        Functor.IsEquivalence
          (relativeInertiaStackNeutralSection B S hS f).hom.hom.toFunctor,
        ∀ (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (a : x ⟶ x),
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom).map a = 𝟙 _ → a = 𝟙 x]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEquivalence_secondRelativeDiagonal_iff_relativeInertiaTrivial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YY, the equivalence of parts (2) and (3).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the second diagonal `Δ_{f, 2}` is an isomorphism exactly when the
relative inertia group stack `I_{𝒳/𝒴}` is trivial over `𝒳`, that is, exactly when its neutral
section `e : 𝒳 ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_secondRelativeDiagonal_iff_relativeInertiaTrivial (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    Functor.IsEquivalence (secondRelativeDiagonal B S hS f.hom).hom.toFunctor ↔
      Functor.IsEquivalence
        (relativeInertiaStackNeutralSection B S hS f).hom.hom.toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.relativeInertiaTrivial_iff_isomKernel_trivial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YY, the equivalence of parts (3) and (4).** The relative inertia `I_{𝒳/𝒴}` of a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks is trivial over `𝒳` exactly when, for every scheme `T` and every
`x : T ⟶ 𝒳`, the kernel of `Isom_𝒳(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f ∘ x, f ∘ x)` is trivial — stated as: every
endomorphism of an object of `𝒳` which `f` sends to an identity is an identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeInertiaTrivial_iff_isomKernel_trivial (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    Functor.IsEquivalence
        (relativeInertiaStackNeutralSection B S hS f).hom.hom.toFunctor ↔
      ∀ (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (a : x ⟶ x),
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom).map a = 𝟙 _ → a = 𝟙 x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.secondRelativeDiagonal_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YY, the equivalence of parts (2), (3) and (4).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S` the following are equivalent: the second diagonal `Δ_{f, 2}` is an
isomorphism; the relative inertia `I_{𝒳/𝒴}` is trivial over `𝒳`; the kernel of the map on
`Isom` sheaves attached to any object of `𝒳` over a scheme is trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem secondRelativeDiagonal_tfae (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE
      [Functor.IsEquivalence (secondRelativeDiagonal B S hS f.hom).hom.toFunctor,
        Functor.IsEquivalence
          (relativeInertiaStackNeutralSection B S hS f).hom.hom.toFunctor,
        ∀ (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (a : x ⟶ x),
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom).map a = 𝟙 _ → a = 𝟙 x]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEquivalence_secondRelativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04YY, the implication (1) ⟹ (2).** If a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is
representable by algebraic spaces then its second diagonal `Δ_{f, 2}` is an isomorphism.

By Stacks 04Y5 representability by algebraic spaces makes the underlying functor faithful, and by
Stacks 04Z7 that is exactly the second diagonal being an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_secondRelativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    Functor.IsEquivalence (secondRelativeDiagonal B S hS f.hom).hom.toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_firstRelativeDiagonal_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the
following are equivalent: the first relative diagonal `Δ_{f,1}` is separated; the second relative
diagonal `Δ_{f,2}` is a closed immersion, part (2) of Stacks 04YL; `Δ_{f,2}` is proper;
`Δ_{f,2}` is universally closed — the last two, and the first, in the relative sense of
Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_firstRelativeDiagonal_tfae (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsSeparated B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f).hom,
       AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
         (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)),
       IsProper B S hS
         (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
           (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)).hom,
       UniversallyClosed B S hS
         (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
           (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)).hom]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_firstRelativeDiagonal_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the
following are equivalent: the first relative diagonal `Δ_{f,1}` is quasi-separated; the second
relative diagonal `Δ_{f,2}` is of finite type; `Δ_{f,2}` is quasi-compact — all three in the
relative sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_firstRelativeDiagonal_tfae (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f).hom,
       IsFiniteType B S hS
         (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
           (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)).hom,
       IsQuasiCompact B S hS
         (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
           (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)).hom]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallySeparated_firstRelativeDiagonal_iff_isImmersion_second
declarations.doc:
The first relative diagonal `Δ_{f,1}` of a 1-morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is locally separated, in the relative sense of
Stacks 04XB, if and only if the second relative diagonal `Δ_{f,2}` is an immersion, part (3) of
Stacks 04YL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySeparated_firstRelativeDiagonal_iff_isImmersion_second (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsLocallySeparated B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f).hom ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsImmersion B S hS
        (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_iff_isUnramifiedRelative_diagonals
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z0, part (4).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` — with no
representability hypothesis — is DM, in the sense of Definition 04YW, if and only if its first
relative diagonal `Δ_{f,1} : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` and its second relative diagonal `Δ_{f,2}`,
the relative diagonal of `Δ_{f,1}`, are both unramified in the relative sense of Properties of
Stacks, Section 04XB.

Definition 04YW is representability of `Δ_{f,1}` by algebraic spaces together with Section 04XB
unramifiedness of it; the representability clause is a theorem for a 1-morphism of *algebraic*
stacks — part (1) of Stacks 04XS — so the condition carried here is the Section 04XB clause alone
and the left-hand side is the first conjunct on the right. The second conjunct is unconditionally
true, which is the source's own proof: `Δ_{f,2}` is the relative diagonal of `Δ_{f,1}`, which is
representable by algebraic spaces, so part (3) of Stacks 050E — Stacks 05W6 applied at a diagonal
which is locally of finite type and a monomorphism by parts (2) and (3) of Stacks 04YQ — makes it
unramified with no hypothesis on `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_iff_isUnramifiedRelative_diagonals (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsDM B S hS f ↔
      (IsUnramifiedRelative B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f).hom ∧
        IsUnramifiedRelative B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
          (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDM_iff_isLocallyQuasiFinite_diagonals
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` — with no representability
hypothesis — is quasi-DM, in the sense of Definition 04YW, if and only if its first relative
diagonal `Δ_{f,1} : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` and its second relative diagonal `Δ_{f,2}`, the
relative diagonal of `Δ_{f,1}`, are both locally quasi-finite in the relative sense of Properties
of Stacks, Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_iff_isLocallyQuasiFinite_diagonals (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f ↔
      (IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f).hom ∧
        IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
          (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_iff_isQuasiCompactMorphism_diagonals
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z0, part (2).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` — with no
representability hypothesis — is quasi-separated, in the sense of Definition 04YW, if and only if
its first relative diagonal `Δ_{f,1} : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` and its second relative diagonal
`Δ_{f,2}`, the relative diagonal of `Δ_{f,1}`, are both quasi-compact in the sense of
Definition 050U.

Definition 04YW is the conjunction, at every algebraic space representing a base change of
`Δ_{f,1}` along a scheme-valued point, of quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the
structural morphism, so the left-hand side splits as Section 04XB quasi-compactness of `Δ_{f,1}`
together with Section 04XB quasi-separatedness of `Δ_{f,1}`. Part (2) of Stacks 04YZ, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_relativeDiagonal_iff_isQuasiSeparated` applied to
`Δ_{f,1}`, replaces the second of those by Section 04XB quasi-compactness of `Δ_{f,2}`; and
Stacks 050T, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_iff_baseChange_quasiCompact`, replaces
Section 04XB quasi-compactness of each diagonal by Definition 050U quasi-compactness, which is the
form the statement asks for. Both diagonals are representable by algebraic spaces by part (1) of
Stacks 04XS, so neither application needs a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_iff_isQuasiCompactMorphism_diagonals (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f ↔
      (IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f) ∧
        IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
          (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_iff_universallyClosed_diagonals
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z0, part (1).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` — with no
representability hypothesis — is separated, in the sense of Definition 04YW, if and only if its
first relative diagonal `Δ_{f,1} : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` and its second relative diagonal
`Δ_{f,2}`, the relative diagonal of `Δ_{f,1}`, are both universally closed in the relative sense
of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

Definition 04YW is properness of `Δ_{f,1}`, and properness of a morphism of algebraic spaces is
separatedness, finite type and universal closedness. Universal closedness of `Δ_{f,1}` is the
first conjunct on the right; its separatedness is universal closedness of `Δ_{f,2}` by part (1)
of Stacks 04YZ; it is unconditionally locally of finite type by part (2) of Stacks 04XS; and it
is quasi-compact because it is universally closed, by Stacks 04XW.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_iff_universallyClosed_diagonals (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f ↔
      (UniversallyClosed B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f).hom ∧
        UniversallyClosed B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
          (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)).hom)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.relativeDiagonalSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z1.** The natural isomorphism `σ : Θ ⋙ ρ ≅ π ⋙ Δ_{C/D}` witnessing that the
square 2-commutes; its component at `(a, b, f)` is `(𝟙_{F a}, f⁻¹)`.
declarations.statement:
def relativeDiagonalSquareIso :
    (mapBase F G H ⋙ toRelativeDiagonalTarget F G H) ≅ (toBase F G ⋙ relativeDiagonal H)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.toRelativeDiagonalPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z1.** The functor `A ×_C B ⥤ (A ×_D B) ×_{C ×_D C} C` induced by
`(Θ, π, σ)` into the explicit 2-fibre product of the cospan
`A ×_D B --ρ--> C ×_D C <--Δ_{C/D}-- C`. On objects it sends `(a, b, f)` to
`((a, b, H f), F a, (𝟙_{F a}, f⁻¹))`, and a morphism `(x, y)` to `((x, y), F x)`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.isEquivalence_toRelativeDiagonalPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z1.** The square above is a 2-fibre product diagram: the induced functor
`A ×_C B ⥤ (A ×_D B) ×_{C ×_D C} C` is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toRelativeDiagonalPullback :
    (toRelativeDiagonalPullback F G H).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.isEquivalenceOver_toFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z6.** The 2-commutative square
```
  I_{S/S'} --c--> I_S
     |             |
  F∘π |            | I_F
     v             v
     S' ---e---> I_{S'}
```
is a 2-fibre product in the (2,1)-category of fibred categories over `C`: the canonical
comparison 1-morphism `Θ` to the explicit 2-fibre product `S' ×_{e, I_{S'}, I_F} I_S` is an
equivalence of categories **over `C`**.

The witness produced has `Θ` itself as its underlying functor, so the statement is about
the given comparison functor with its prescribed action on objects and morphisms, and not
merely about the existence of some equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceOver_toFibreProduct :
    Nonempty (IsEquivalenceOver (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p)
      (FibreProduct.structureFunctor p p' F hF) (toFibreProduct p p' F hF))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.toFibreProduct_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Consequence of Stacks 04Z6: the comparison functor `Θ` is an equivalence of the
underlying categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem toFibreProduct_isEquivalence :
    (toFibreProduct p p' F hF).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.squareTwoCommutes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z6, the square.** The 2-commutativity of the square is witnessed by a
natural isomorphism over `C`, `I_F ∘ c ≅ e ∘ (F ∘ π)`. On an object `(x, α)` both
composites are `(F x, id)`, since `F α = id`, so the canonical 2-isomorphism is the
identity.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.full_and_faithful_iff_isEquivalence_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z7.** Let `p𝒮 : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` and `p𝒮' : 𝒮' ⥤ 𝒞` be categories fibred in groupoids and
let `G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮'` be a 1-morphism over `𝒞`. Then `G` is fully faithful if and only if the diagonal
`Δ_G : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒮 ×_{G, 𝒮', G} 𝒮` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_and_faithful_iff_isEquivalence_diagonal (h𝒮 : p𝒮.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (h𝒮' : p𝒮'.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hG : G ⋙ p𝒮' = p𝒮) :
    (G.Full ∧ G.Faithful) ↔ (diagonal hG).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.range_and_isLocallyNoetherianSpace_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z8.** Let `f : X → Y` be a continuous map of topological spaces.
(1) If `X` is Noetherian, then `f(X)` is Noetherian.
(2) If `X` is locally Noetherian and `f` is open, then `f(X)` is locally Noetherian.

Here `f(X)` is `Set.range f` with the subspace topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem NoetherianSpace.range_and_isLocallyNoetherianSpace_range {X Y : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (hf : Continuous f) :
    (NoetherianSpace X → NoetherianSpace (Set.range f)) ∧
      (IsLocallyNoetherianSpace X → IsOpenMap f → IsLocallyNoetherianSpace (Set.range f))

declarations.name: IsSpectralMap.isRetrocompact_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04Z9** (part 2). If `f : X → Y` is continuous and quasi-compact as a map, then its
image `f(X)` is retrocompact in `Y`: it meets every quasi-compact open in a quasi-compact set.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsSpectralMap.isRetrocompact_range
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    {f : X → Y} (hf : IsSpectralMap f) :
    IsRetrocompact (Set.range f)

declarations.name: noetherianSpace_isRetrocompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04ZA** (part 2). Every subset of a Noetherian topological space is retrocompact:
its intersection with any quasi-compact open is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianSpace_isRetrocompact (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X] (E : Set X) : IsRetrocompact E

declarations.name: noetherianSpace_of_isLocallyNoetherianSpace
declarations.doc: A quasi-compact locally Noetherian topological space is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianSpace_of_isLocallyNoetherianSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [CompactSpace X] (hX : IsLocallyNoetherianSpace X) : NoetherianSpace X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_comp_surjective
declarations.doc: If `f` is surjective and `f ≫ q` is quasi-compact, then `q` is quasi-compact.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_isOpenMap_surjective_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Quasi-compactness of a morphism of schemes descends along an open,
surjective morphism of target schemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiCompact_of_isOpenMap_surjective_baseChange
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hopen : IsOpenMap g.base) [Surjective g]
    [QuasiCompact (pullback.snd f g)] : QuasiCompact f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyNoetherianSpace_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04ZF, part (1).** The space of points of a locally Noetherian algebraic space
over `S` is a locally Noetherian topological space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherianSpace_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian X)) :
    IsLocallyNoetherianSpace (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.noetherianSpace_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04ZF, part (2).** The space of points of a quasi-compact locally Noetherian
algebraic space over `S` is a Noetherian topological space.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianSpace_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS F)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian X)) :
    NoetherianSpace (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stacksSober_points_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04ZG, sobriety.** The space of points of a Noetherian algebraic space over `S`
is sober in the sense of Definition 004X: every irreducible closed subset of it has a unique
generic point.

Only quasi-separatedness is used: it makes the space Zariski locally quasi-separated by
Tag 03JX, `(η) ⇒ (ζ)` and Tag 03W7, so Tag 06NJ applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksSober_points_of_isNoetherian (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F) : StacksSober (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.noetherianSpace_points_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04ZG, Noetherianity.** The space of points of a Noetherian algebraic space over
`S` is a Noetherian topological space.

Only quasi-compactness and local Noetherianity are used, which is Tag 04ZF (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianSpace_points_of_isNoetherian (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F) : NoetherianSpace (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stacksSober_and_noetherianSpace_points_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04ZG.** The space of points of a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` is a sober
Noetherian topological space.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksSober_and_noetherianSpace_points_of_isNoetherian
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F) :
    StacksSober (points B S hS F) ∧ NoetherianSpace (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparatedOver_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
If `G` is separated over `S` and `f : F ⟶ G` is separated,
then `F` is separated over `S`.

    (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f) : IsSeparatedOver B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySeparatedOver_of_isLocallySeparated
declarations.doc:
If `G` is locally separated over `S` and `f : F ⟶ G` is
locally separated, then `F` is locally separated over `S`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
If `G` is quasi-separated over `S` and `f : F ⟶ G` is quasi-separated, then `F` is

declarations.doc: If `G` is separated and `f : F ⟶ G` is separated, then `F` is separated.

If `G` is locally separated and `f : F ⟶ G` is locally

If `G` is quasi-separated and `f : F ⟶ G` is quasi-separated, then `F` is

A separated algebraic space over `S` is separated over `S`, that is, an algebraic space

A locally separated algebraic space is locally separated over

theorem isLocallySeparatedOver_of_isAbsolutelyLocallySeparated (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
Every morphism out of an algebraic space which is quasi-separated over `S` is
quasi-separated.

theorem isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver (hF : IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS F)
